AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount.lean_proof:
classical
  let P : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) → Prop := fun σ =>
    ∀ i, F.Adj (eU.symm i) (eW.symm (σ i))
  let E : {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) // P σ} ≃
      {f : U → W // PerfectMatching F U W hUW f} :=
    { toFun := fun σ => ⟨fun u => eW.symm (σ.val (eU u)),
        ⟨(eU.trans (σ.val.trans eW.symm)).bijective, fun u => by
          simpa using σ.property (eU u)⟩⟩
      invFun := fun f => ⟨eU.symm.trans ((Equiv.ofBijective f.val f.property.1).trans eW),
        fun i => by simpa using f.property.2 (eU.symm i)⟩
      left_inv := by
        intro σ
        apply Subtype.ext
        apply Equiv.ext
        intro i
        simp
      right_inv := by
        intro f
        apply Subtype.ext
        funext u
        simp }
  have hterm (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
      (∏ i, if F.Adj (eU.symm i) (eW.symm (σ i)) then (1 : ℝ) else 0) =
        if P σ then 1 else 0 := by
    by_cases h : P σ
    · rw [if_pos h]
      exact Finset.prod_eq_one fun i _ => if_pos (h i)
    · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := not_forall.mp h
      rw [if_neg h]
      exact Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ i) (if_neg hi)
  have hcard : {f : U → W | PerfectMatching F U W hUW f}.ncard =
      (Finset.univ.filter P).card := by
    rw [← Nat.card_coe_set_eq, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
    exact (Fintype.card_congr E).symm.trans (Fintype.card_subtype P)
  rw [← Matrix.permanent_transpose, Matrix.permanent]
  simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply]
  simp_rw [hterm]
  rw [Finset.sum_boole, hcard]
AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (F : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel F.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
    (hUW : Disjoint U W) {n : ℕ} (eU : U ≃ Fin n) (eW : W ≃ Fin n) :
    Matrix.permanent (fun i j : Fin n =>
      if F.Adj (eU.symm i) (eW.symm j) then (1 : ℝ) else 0) =
    ({f : U → W | PerfectMatching F U W hUW f}.ncard : ℝ) := by
AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount.name: AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount
AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
By \noderef{PerfectMatching}, a perfect matching is exactly an edge-respecting
bijection. Mathlib uses $\sum_\sigma\prod_j A_{\sigma(j),j}$.
Replacing $\sigma$ by $\sigma^{-1}$ and reindexing $j=\sigma(i)$ gives
$\sum_\tau\prod_i A_{i,\tau(i)}$.
The product for $\tau$ is one precisely when every chosen pair is an edge,
and otherwise is zero because it has a zero factor. Such permutations
correspond bijectively to matchings by
$f=e_W^{-1}\circ\tau\circ e_U$, with inverse
$\tau=e_W\circ f\circ e_U^{-1}$. The sum of these indicators is their
cardinality. All these operations apply to the empty permutation and map.
\end{proof}
AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}
Let $F$ be a graph on a finite vertex set, let $U,W$ be disjoint subsets,
and choose bijections
$e_U:U\to\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ and $e_W:W\to\mathrm{Fin}(n)$.
Let $A_{ij}$ be one if $F$ joins $e_U^{-1}(i)$ to $e_W^{-1}(j)$ and zero
otherwise. Then the real permanent of $A$ is the natural cardinality,
cast to $\mathbb R$, of the perfect matchings $U\to W$.
\end{lemma}
AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount.title: AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount

AuxiliarySpreadExecution.lean_statement:
theorem AuxiliarySpreadExecution :
    ∀ (d : ENNReal) (D : ℕ), 0 < d → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ (ε C : ENNReal) (N : ℕ),
        0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 ∧ 1 ≤ C ∧ C < ⊤ ∧ 1 ≤ N ∧
        ∀ (r n : ℕ), N ≤ n →
        ∀ {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
          [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
          {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
          {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} [DecidableRel R.Adj]
          (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B),
          (∀ j : Fin r,
            ((Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n ∨
             (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n + 1) ∧
            (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card =
              (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).card) →
          R.maxDegree ≤ D →
          InstanceSuperRegular B ε d → CandidacySuperRegular B A ε d →
          (∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, R.Adj i j → SaturatingSourcePair B i j) →
          ∃ μ : PMF {φ : SimpleGraph.Copy H G // CompatibleEmbedding B A φ},
            VertexSpreadOn (μ.map fun φ => fun x => φ.1 x) (C / n) Set.univ := by

AuxiliarySpreadExecution.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Set $Q=D^2+1$. Apply \noderef{EqualSizeParameterTable} at $(d,D)$ and
choose its sequences $p,\rho,e,\omega,\theta,\zeta,\widehat\zeta$,
certificate $\mathcal K$, numbers $a,M,C$, and cutoff $N_0$. These choices
precede $r$. The certificate has precisely the meaning in
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate}; exposures and rounds remain
independent indices. For $s<Q$, the table gives
$0<e_s\leq e_{s+1}\leq1$. In particular $e_0$ is positive and finite.
Take $\varepsilon=e_0/2$, so $0<\varepsilon<1$ and
$\varepsilon\leq e_0$. Also $1\leq M$ and $2M\leq C$, whence $1\leq C$.
Finiteness of $C$ must not be assumed from notation: take
$k=\max\{N_0,1\}$. The uniform-size conclusion gives $C/k\leq1$.
Since $k$ is positive and finite, cancellation yields $C\leq k<\infty$.
It follows from $2M\leq C$ that $M$ is finite too.

The finite nonempty family $(e_s)_{s<Q}$ has a positive minimum $e_*$.
Choose $N_e\geq1$ with $1/N_e\leq e_*$ and set
$N=\max\{N_0,N_e,1\}$. Thus $n\geq N$ implies
$1/n\leq e_s$ for every $s<Q$. The table's other conclusions remain
valid at every such $n$. In particular $C/n\leq1$ and
$D(1-a)^n\leq1/2$ with $0<a\leq1$.

Fix $r,n,B,A$ as in the statement. Increasing the input error from
$\varepsilon$ to $e_0$ preserves super-regularity. Indeed the tests in
\noderef{RegularPair} become more restrictive while both density bounds
become weaker, and each degree interval in \noderef{SuperRegularPair}
widens. Applying this separately in \noderef{InstanceSuperRegular} and
\noderef{CandidacySuperRegular} gives the input at error $e_0$ needed below.
We check every numerical premise of \noderef{VariableSizeInductionIteration}.
The table gives $p_0=d$, $p_{x+1}=\rho_x(d/2)$ for $x<D$, and the
probability and failure bounds just stated. For $s<Q$ it gives
$e_s\leq e_{s+1}\leq1$, $\omega_{s+1}<e_{s+1}$, and
\[
 2\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+D\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+2D\zeta_s\leq\theta_s.
\]
For every $x\leq D$ it gives $0<\theta_s$, $4\theta_s<\rho_x$ and
$2\zeta_s<\rho_x,1-\rho_x$, and it also gives
$2\zeta_s<d/2,1-d/2$.
For the additive density gap, fix $x<D$. Both $p_x,p_{x+1}$ lie in
$(0,1]$. The table gives $2e_s<p_x-p_{x+1}$, forcing
$p_{x+1}<p_x$. Thus the truncated difference is the ordinary finite real
difference, and our added reciprocal-size bound gives
\[
 p_{x+1}+e_s+1/n\leq p_{x+1}+2e_s<p_x.
\]
This implies the required weak additive inequality, including at round zero.
There is no comparison of two different exposures in this argument.

The certificate's witness-thinning, host-thinning, matching and
matching-existence thresholds are at most $N_0\leq n$ for every
$s<Q,x\leq D$. Its matching constant is at most $M\leq C/2$;
division by two is legitimate since $M,C$ are finite. For every ordered
pair $x,y\leq D$, the Four Graphs threshold is at most $N_0\leq n$
and its exponential constant is at least $a$. These are exactly the
table's threshold clauses, including pairs with $x>y$.
Finally its uniform-size clause and static strict reserve give
\[
 n^{-1}\leq\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+2/n\leq\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+1/(\zeta_sn)\leq\zeta_s,
\]
\[
 \omega_{s+1}+2/n\leq e_{s+1},\qquad
 \omega_{s+1}+1/(e_{s+1}n)\leq e_{s+1}.
\]
These verify all six reserve/output premises of the iteration theorem.
The size, degree, host and candidacy premises are the present hypotheses.
The saturating-pair premise is exactly \noderef{SaturatingSourcePair};
nonedges contain no source edges by the reduced-support field of
\noderef{BlowUpInstance}. No additional source degree assumption is needed.

Apply \noderef{VariableSizeInductionIteration}. It returns a colouring
$c:[r]\to[Q]$ and a law $\mu$ on partial compatible embeddings with full
domain, satisfying the invariant at round $D^2=Q-1$ with the entire last
colour class touched. This is a legal completed last round, not an
invariant at round $Q$. The spread conjunct of
\noderef{ColourRoundInvariant} says that this same law's restrictions to
the full domain are $(C/n)$-vertex-spread. Apply
\noderef{EqualSizeTerminalConversion} with domain equal to the full source
set. Its map produces full compatible Copies, agrees pointwise with each
partial map, and preserves the spread assertion under pushforward. These
are the law and bound required in the conclusion; neither conditioning nor
a further loss of mass occurs.
\end{proof}
AuxiliarySpreadExecution.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}
For every extended nonnegative real $0<d\leq1$ and integer $D\geq0$ there
are $0<\varepsilon<1$, $1\leq C<\infty$ and an integer $N\geq1$, all
chosen before the number of clusters, with this property. For every $r$

saturating matching. Then there is a law on compatible full Copies from
the source to the host whose underlying maps are $(C/n)$-vertex-spread

    (hsecond : (∑ u ∈ U, (d u) ^ 2) ≤
      (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 * (p + δ) ^ 2 + 5 * δ * (U.card : ℝ) ^ 3) :

BalancedDegreeVarianceBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Expanding the square and summing gives
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2
 =\sum_{u\in U}d_u^2-2pq\sum_{u\in U}d_u+np^2q^2.
\]
Since $2pq\ge0$, insert the upper bound for the second moment and the lower bound for the first moment, without requiring $q-5\delta n$ to be nonnegative. Expansion then yields
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2
 \le nq^2(4p\delta+\delta^2)
       +10\delta n^2q\,p(p-\delta)+5\delta n^3.
\]
The assumptions imply $4p\delta+\delta^2\le5\delta$ and
$0\le p(p-\delta)\le p^2\le1$. Also $q^2\le n^2$ and $q\le n$.
The first term is therefore at most $5\delta n^3$, the second is at most
$10\delta n^3$, and the last is $5\delta n^3$. Their sum is the asserted bound.
\end{proof}
BalancedDegreeVarianceBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Balanced restricted-degree variance]
Let $U$ be a finite set of cardinality $n$, let $d_u$ be real numbers indexed by $U$, and let $0\le q\le n$ and $0\le\delta\le p\le1$. Suppose that
\[
 (q-5\delta n)(p-\delta)n\le\sum_{u\in U}d_u,
 \qquad
 \sum_{u\in U}d_u^2\le nq^2(p+\delta)^2+5\delta n^3.
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2\le20\delta n^3.
\]
\end{lemma}

    field_simp

    have h3 : x + 3 ≠ 0 := by linarith

    field_simp

theorem BennettEntropyLowerBound (z : ℝ) (hz : 0 ≤ z) :
    z ^ 2 / (2 * (1 + z / 3)) ≤ (1 + z) * Real.log (1 + z) - z := by
BennettEntropyLowerBound.name: BennettEntropyLowerBound
BennettEntropyLowerBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
On $[0,\infty)$ the quantities $1+x$, $x+3$, and $1+x/3$ are
strictly positive. The identity
\[
 \frac{x^2}{2(1+x/3)}=\frac32\left(x-3+\frac9{x+3}\right)
\]
follows by multiplying by the positive denominators. Define the
difference between the left entropy and this rational expression by
\[
 f(x)=(1+x)\log(1+x)-x-\frac32\left(x-3+\frac9{x+3}\right).
\]
It is differentiable at every $x\ge0$, with
\[
 f'(x)=g(x)=\log(1+x)-\frac32+\frac{27}{2(x+3)^2},\qquad
 g'(x)=\frac1{1+x}-\frac{27}{(x+3)^3}.
\]
Both denominators in $g'$ are positive. Consequently $g'(x)\ge0$
is equivalent to $(x+3)^3\ge27(1+x)$. Their difference is
$x^3+9x^2\ge0$ for $x\ge0$, which proves this sign. The functions
$f$ and $g$ are continuous on $[0,\infty)$, so the mean value theorem
on each compact subinterval shows first that $g$ is nondecreasing.
Since $g(0)=0$, this gives $f'(x)=g(x)\ge0$ on the same half-line.
Applying the mean value theorem once more makes $f$ nondecreasing.
Finally $f(0)=0$ implies $f(z)\ge0$ for every $z\ge0$. Substituting
the displayed rational identity gives the result.
\end{proof}
BennettEntropyLowerBound.tex_statement:
\begin{helper}[Bennett entropy lower bound]
For every real $z\ge0$,
\[
 (1+z)\log(1+z)-z\ge\frac{z^2}{2(1+z/3)}.
\]
\end{helper}
BennettEntropyLowerBound.title: BennettEntropyLowerBound

classical

      intro i j hij
      apply hx
      apply hf₀.1

    let R := {b : B // b ∉ Set.range y}

      dsimp [L]
      rw [Fintype.card_subtype_compl,
        ← Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.ofInjective x hx), Fintype.card_fin, hA]
    have hR : Fintype.card R = n - s := by
      dsimp [R]
      rw [Fintype.card_subtype_compl,
        ← Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.ofInjective y hy), Fintype.card_fin, hB]

      rintro ⟨i, hi⟩
      apply a.2
      refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
      apply f.2.1.1
      exact (f.2.2 i).trans hi

        have hnot : a ∉ Set.range x := by
          rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
          apply b.2
          exact ⟨i, (f.2.2 i).symm.trans ha⟩

      apply Subtype.ext
      funext a
      by_cases ha : a ∈ Set.range x

        exact (f.2.2 i).trans (g.2.2 i).symm
      · exact congrArg (fun e : L ≃ R => (e ⟨a, ha⟩).1) hfg

BijectionCompletionCount.lean_statement:
theorem BijectionCompletionCount {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B]
    (n s : ℕ) (hA : Fintype.card A = n) (hB : Fintype.card B = n)
    (x : Fin s → A) (y : Fin s → B) (hx : Function.Injective x) :
    {f : A → B | Function.Bijective f ∧ ∀ i, f (x i) = y i}.ncard ≤
      (n - s).factorial := by
BijectionCompletionCount.name: BijectionCompletionCount
BijectionCompletionCount.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $E$ be the set of such bijections. If $E$ is empty, its cardinality is zero
and the assertion follows. Otherwise choose $f_0\in E$. If $y(i)=y(j)$,
then $f_0(x(i))=f_0(x(j))$; injectivity of $f_0$ and then of $x$ gives $i=j$.
Thus $y$ is injective. The images of $x$ and $y$ each have $s$ elements,
so $L=A\setminus\operatorname{im}(x)$ and $R=B\setminus\operatorname{im}(y)$
each have $n-s$ elements.

For $f\in E$ and $a\in L$, the equality $f(a)=y(i)=f(x(i))$ would imply
$a=x(i)$, a contradiction. Thus $f$ maps $L$ into $R$ and its restriction
is injective. For $b\in R$, surjectivity of $f$ gives an $a\in A$ with
$f(a)=b$. This $a$ cannot equal $x(i)$, since then $b=y(i)$; hence $a\in L$.
The restriction is therefore a bijection $L\to R$.

The restriction map from $E$ to the set of bijections $L\to R$ is injective:
two extensions with the same restriction agree on $L$, and on its complement
both send $x(i)$ to $y(i)$. For finite sets of size $m=n-s$, there are $m!$
bijections between them: after ordering the domain, successive images have
$m,m-1,\ldots,1$ choices. When $m=0$ there is exactly one empty bijection,
also counted by $0!=1$. Consequently $|E|\leq(n-s)!$.
\end{proof}
BijectionCompletionCount.tex_statement:
\begin{helper}[Counting completions of prescribed images]
Let $A,B$ be finite sets, each of cardinality $n$, let $s$ be a nonnegative integer,
and let $x:\{1,\ldots,s\}\to A$ be injective and $y:\{1,\ldots,s\}\to B$ arbitrary.
There are at most $(n-s)!$ bijections $f:A\to B$ satisfying $f(x(i))=y(i)$ for every $i$.
Here subtraction is natural-number subtraction; injectivity of $x$ implies $s\leq n$.
\end{helper}
BijectionCompletionCount.title: BijectionCompletionCount

theorem BipartiteFactorCutCapacity {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (k : ℕ) :
    (∑ w, ((BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k).capacity
      (BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k).source w : ℤ)) = (k * U.card : ℕ) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset (Option U ⊕ Option W),
      (BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k).source ∈ S →
      (BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k).sink ∉ S →
      ∃ A B : Finset V, A ⊆ U ∧ B ⊆ W ∧
        (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ Finset.univ \ S,
          ((BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k).capacity v w : ℤ)) =
        ((k * A.card +
          (((U \ A) ×ˢ (W \ B)).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).card +
          k * B.card : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
BipartiteFactorCutCapacity.name: BipartiteFactorCutCapacity
BipartiteFactorCutCapacity.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Use the exact copies from \noderef{BipartiteFactorNetwork}. Define $A$ to
be the ambient elements of $U$ whose left copies are outside $S$, and
$B$ to be the ambient elements of $W$ whose right copies are inside $S$.
The copy maps are injective and onto their corresponding parts, so
$A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq W$, and
$S=\{s\}\sqcup(U\setminus A)\sqcup B$, with the copied parts understood.
The source is in $S$ and the sink is outside $S$ by the cut hypotheses.

The only positive capacities, by the network definition, are source-to-left,
left-to-right, and right-to-sink. A source-to-left pair crosses exactly
when its left endpoint lies in $A$, giving $k|A|$. A left-to-right pair
crosses exactly when its endpoints are in $U\setminus A$ and
$W\setminus B$, and has capacity one exactly for a $G$ edge. Because
the subtype copies are exact and injective, these pairs are in bijection
with the ordered edges counted by the displayed middle term; no edge
is duplicated. A right-to-sink pair crosses exactly for a right endpoint
in $B$, giving $k|B|$. All other pairs have capacity zero. Summing these
three disjoint kinds of pairs proves the formula. Finally, exactly the
$|U|$ source-to-left pairs contribute to $\sum_v c(s,v)$, each with
capacity $k$, giving its asserted value. Empty parts and $k=0$ require
no exception to these finite sums.
\end{proof}
BipartiteFactorCutCapacity.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[All cuts of the factor network]
For the network $N$ of \noderef{BipartiteFactorNetwork},
$\sum_v c(s,v)=k|U|$. Every source-side cut $S$ has sets $A\subseteq U$
and $B\subseteq W$ such that
\[
 C(S)=k|A|+e_G(U\setminus A,W\setminus B)+k|B|.
\]
Here $e_G(X,Y)$ counts ordered pairs $(x,y)\in X\times Y$ with $G$-adjacency;
the formula does not require equal part sizes or disjoint ambient sets.
\end{lemma}
BipartiteFactorCutCapacity.title: BipartiteFactorCutCapacity

BipartiteFactorNetwork.lean_proof:
{ source := Sum.inl none
    sink := Sum.inr none
    terminals_distinct := by simp

BipartiteFactorNetwork.lean_statement:
def BipartiteFactorNetwork {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (k : ℕ) :
    FiniteCapacityNetwork (Option U ⊕ Option W) :=
BipartiteFactorNetwork.name: BipartiteFactorNetwork
BipartiteFactorNetwork.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Network for a bipartite regular factor]
Given a simple graph $G$, finite sets $U,W$ of vertices, and $k\in\mathbb N$,
the factor network, in the sense of \noderef{FiniteCapacityNetwork}, has
vertex type $(\{s\}\sqcup U)\sqcup(W\sqcup\{t\})$, implemented as
$\operatorname{Option}(U)\sqcup\operatorname{Option}(W)$.
The source is the left None and the sink the right None; the left and
right Some vertices are exact subtype copies of $U$ and $W$, respectively.
They and the terminals are pairwise disjoint, even if the ambient sets
overlap or are empty. Its capacities are $c(s,u)=k$, $c(w,t)=k$, and
$c(u,w)=1$ if $G$ has the edge $uw$, with every other capacity zero.
Each ordered pair carries exactly one capacity entry, not multiple arcs.
\end{definition}
BipartiteFactorNetwork.title: BipartiteFactorNetwork

      (hab : (BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k).capacity a b = 0)

      f.amount a b = 0 := by

    have h₂ := f.bound b a
    rw [hab, Nat.cast_zero] at h₁
    rw [hba, Nat.cast_zero, f.skew b a] at h₂

theorem BipartiteFlowSaturation {V : Type u} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (k : ℕ)
    (hsize : U.card = W.card)
    (f : FiniteIntegralFlow (BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k))
    (hvalue : (∑ w, f.amount (Sum.inl none) w) = (k * U.card : ℕ)) :
    (∀ u : U, f.amount (Sum.inl none) (Sum.inl (some u)) = (k : ℤ)) ∧
    (∀ w : W, f.amount (Sum.inr (some w)) (Sum.inr none) = (k : ℤ)) ∧
    (∀ (u : U) (w : W),
      0 ≤ f.amount (Sum.inl (some u)) (Sum.inr (some w)) ∧
      f.amount (Sum.inl (some u)) (Sum.inr (some w)) ≤ 1 ∧
      (f.amount (Sum.inl (some u)) (Sum.inr (some w)) = 1 → G.Adj u.val w.val)) ∧
    (∀ u : U, (Finset.univ.filter fun w : W =>
      f.amount (Sum.inl (some u)) (Sum.inr (some w)) = 1).card = k) ∧
    (∀ w : W, (Finset.univ.filter fun u : U =>
      f.amount (Sum.inl (some u)) (Sum.inr (some w)) = 1).card = k) := by
BipartiteFlowSaturation.name: BipartiteFlowSaturation
BipartiteFlowSaturation.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Use the capacity table of \noderef{BipartiteFactorNetwork} and the skew
symmetry and bounds of \noderef{FiniteIntegralFlow}. If both directional
capacities are zero, both net flows are zero. If only the forward
capacity can be positive, its net flow is nonnegative, since its negative
is bounded by the zero reverse capacity. Diagonal net flows are zero by
skew symmetry. Thus the source divergence is the sum of the $n$
source-to-left flows, all in $[0,k]$. Its value is $kn$, so all these
flows equal $k$: if one were less than $k$, its positive integer deficit
would make the sum of the nonnegative deficits strictly positive,
contrary to $nk-\sum_u f(s,u)=0$.

The total divergence over all vertices is zero, since ordered-pair terms
cancel by skew symmetry. Conservation at every nonterminal therefore
says that the sink divergence is $-kn$. Only right-to-sink arcs can
contribute to its negative, so the sum of their nonnegative flows is
$kn$. There are $|W|=n$ of them, each bounded by $k$, and the same
deficit argument saturates every one.

Every middle flow is nonnegative and bounded by its capacity, which is
zero or one. Integrality makes its value zero or one. A value of one
forces capacity one, hence $G$-adjacency. For a fixed left vertex $u$,
the only potentially nonzero outgoing net flows are $f(u,s)=-k$ and
$f(u,w)$ for right vertices $w$. Its conservation equation gives
$\sum_w f(u,w)=k$. A sum of zero-or-one integers counts exactly the
distinct indices where the summand is one, giving the asserted row
count. At a right vertex $w$, conservation similarly gives
$k-\sum_u f(u,w)=0$, proving the column count. The exact subtype copies
ensure that each index represents one ambient vertex; no selected edge
is repeated. For empty parts the pointwise claims are vacuous, and for
$k=0$ the same nonnegative-sum argument gives no selected middle edges.
\end{proof}
BipartiteFlowSaturation.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Saturation and selected middle edges]
Let $U,W$ be finite sets of equal size $n$, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let
$f$ be a feasible integral net flow on the network of
\noderef{BipartiteFactorNetwork} with value $kn$.
Every source-to-left and right-to-sink net flow equals $k$.
For every copied $u\in U,w\in W$, the middle net flow is an integer
between zero and one; if it is one then $uw$ is a $G$ edge.
For each copied $u$, exactly $k$ distinct copied vertices $w$ have middle
flow one, and for each copied $w$, exactly $k$ distinct copied vertices
$u$ have middle flow one.
\end{lemma}
BipartiteFlowSaturation.title: BipartiteFlowSaturation

BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound.lean_proof:
classical
  let e := fun X Y : Finset V => ((X ×ˢ Y).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card
  have hlow : k * A.card ≤ e A W := by
    change k * A.card ≤ ((A.product W).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card
    rw [FilteredProductRowCount]
    calc
      k * A.card = ∑ u ∈ A, k := by simp [Nat.mul_comm]
      _ ≤ ∑ u ∈ A, (W.filter fun w => P u w).card :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun u hu => hrow u (hA hu)
  have htranspose : e A (W \ B) =
      ∑ w ∈ W \ B, (A.filter fun u => P u w).card := by
    simp only [e, Finset.card_eq_sum_ones, Finset.sum_filter,
      Finset.sum_product]
    exact Finset.sum_comm
  have hhigh : e A (W \ B) ≤ k * (W.card - B.card) := by
    rw [htranspose]
    calc
      (∑ w ∈ W \ B, (A.filter fun u => P u w).card) ≤
          ∑ w ∈ W \ B, k := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro w hw
        exact (Finset.card_le_card (Finset.filter_subset_filter _ hA)).trans
          (hcol w (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).1)
      _ = k * (W.card - B.card) := by
        simp [Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hB, Nat.mul_comm]

    change ((A.product (W \ B)).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card +
      ((A.product B).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card =
      ((A.product W).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card
    rw [FilteredProductRowCount, FilteredProductRowCount, FilteredProductRowCount,
      ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro u hu
    simp only [Finset.card_eq_sum_ones, Finset.sum_filter]
    exact Finset.sum_sdiff (f := fun w => if P u w then 1 else 0) hB
  have hb := Finset.card_le_card hB
  by_cases hab : W.card ≤ A.card + B.card
  · have hd : A.card = (A.card + B.card - W.card) + (W.card - B.card) := by omega
    have hm := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => k * x) hd
    simp only [Nat.mul_add] at hm
    dsimp only [e] at hsplit hlow hhigh
    omega
  · have hz : A.card + B.card - W.card = 0 := by omega
    rw [hz, Nat.mul_zero]
    exact Nat.zero_le _
BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (U W : Finset V) (P : V → V → Prop) [DecidableRel P] (k : ℕ)
    (hrow : ∀ u ∈ U, k ≤ (W.filter fun w => P u w).card)
    (hcol : ∀ w ∈ W, (U.filter fun u => P u w).card ≤ k)
    (A B : Finset V) (hA : A ⊆ U) (hB : B ⊆ W) :
    k * (A.card + B.card - W.card) ≤
      ((A ×ˢ B).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card := by
BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound.name: BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound
BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $e(X,Y)$ for the ordered-pair count in the statement. By
\noderef{FilteredProductRowCount},
$e(A,W)=\sum_{u\in A}|\{w\in W:P(u,w)\}|\geq k|A|$.
Counting the pairs with right endpoint in $W\setminus B$ by columns gives
$e(A,W\setminus B)=\sum_{w\in W\setminus B}|\{u\in A:P(u,w)\}|$:
this is the same finite double sum with its summation order exchanged.
Since $A\subseteq U$, each column count is at most its count over $U$,
hence at most $k$. Thus $e(A,W\setminus B)\leq k(|W|-|B|)$.
Partitioning right endpoints into $B$ and $W\setminus B$ gives
$e(A,W)=e(A,B)+e(A,W\setminus B)$. It follows that
$k|A|\leq e(A,B)+k(|W|-|B|)$.
If $|A|+|B|\geq |W|$, then
$|A|=(|A|+|B|-|W|)+(|W|-|B|)$, so cancelling
$k(|W|-|B|)$ yields the desired inequality. Otherwise its left side
is zero and nonnegativity of the pair count proves it. All these counts
include empty sets and $k=0$.
\end{proof}
BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Degree counting inside a rectangle]
Let $U,W$ be finite sets, $P$ a relation between their ambient elements,
and $k\in\mathbb N$. Suppose every $u\in U$ is related to at least $k$
elements of $W$, and every $w\in W$ is related from at most $k$ elements
of $U$. Then for all $A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq W$,
\[
 k\max\{0,|A|+|B|-|W|\}\leq
 |\{(u,w)\in A\times B:P(u,w)\}|.
\]
No equality of part sizes, symmetry of $P$, or disjointness is assumed.
\end{lemma}
BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound.title: BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound

BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion.lean_proof:
classical
  intro V _ _ G _ U W hUW k hsize
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨F, hFG, hU, hW⟩ A hA B hB
    have hcount (T : Finset V) (P : V → Prop) :
        (T.filter P).card = {v | v ∈ T ∧ P v}.ncard := by
      have he : {v | v ∈ T ∧ P v} = (T.filter P : Set V) := by
        ext v
        simp
      rw [he, Set.ncard_coe_finset]
    have hrow : ∀ u ∈ U, k ≤ (W.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card := by
      intro u hu
      rw [hcount, hU u hu]
    have hcol : ∀ w ∈ W, (U.filter fun u => F.Adj u w).card ≤ k := by
      intro w hw
      rw [hcount, hW w hw]
    have h := BipartiteRectangleDegreeBound U W F.Adj k hrow hcol A B hA hB
    rw [← hsize] at h
    refine h.trans (Finset.card_le_card ?_)
    intro p hp
    obtain ⟨hp, hf⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hp
    exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hp, hFG hf⟩
  · intro hrect
    let N := BipartiteFactorNetwork G U W k
    obtain ⟨f, S, hs, ht, hcut, _, hupper⟩ := IntegralFlowTerminalCut N
    obtain ⟨hsource, hformula⟩ := BipartiteFactorCutCapacity G U W k
    obtain ⟨A, B, hA, hB, hformula⟩ := hformula S hs ht
    have hlower := RectangleFactorCutLowerBound G U W k hsize hrect A B hA hB
    have hvalue : (∑ w, f.amount N.source w) = ((k * U.card : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      rw [hcut, hformula] at hupper ⊢
      rw [hsource] at hupper
      exact le_antisymm hupper (by exact_mod_cast hlower)
    obtain ⟨_, _, hmiddle, hrow, hcol⟩ :=
      BipartiteFlowSaturation G U W k hsize f hvalue
    let P : U → W → Prop := fun u w =>
      f.amount (Sum.inl (some u)) (Sum.inr (some w)) = 1
    obtain ⟨F, hFG, hU, hW, _⟩ := BipartiteSelectedEdgeGraph G U W hUW P k
      (fun u w h => (hmiddle u w).2.2 h) hrow hcol
    exact ⟨F, hFG, hU, hW⟩
BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
      (hUW : Disjoint U W) (k : ℕ), U.card = W.card →
      ((∃ F : SimpleGraph V, F ≤ G ∧
          (∀ u ∈ U, {w | w ∈ W ∧ F.Adj u w}.ncard = k) ∧
          (∀ w ∈ W, {u | u ∈ U ∧ F.Adj u w}.ncard = k)) ↔
        ∀ A ⊆ U, ∀ B ⊆ W,
          k * (A.card + B.card - U.card) ≤
            ((A ×ˢ B).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).card) := by
BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion.name: BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion
BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Suppose first that $F$ is such a subgraph.  For $A\subseteq U$ its vertices
send $k|A|$ edges into $W$.  At most $k|W\setminus B|=k(n-|B|)$ of these
can end outside $B$, because every vertex of $W\setminus B$ has degree $k$.
Consequently
$e_G(A,B)\geq e_F(A,B)\geq k(|A|+|B|-n)$; when the expression in
parentheses is negative the asserted inequality is automatic.

Conversely, form a directed network with a source $s$, a sink $t$, arcs
$s\to u$ of capacity $k$ for $u\in U$, arcs $u\to w$ of capacity $1$ for
each edge $uw$ of $G[U,W]$, and arcs $w\to t$ of capacity $k$ for
$w\in W$.  We prove directly that every $s$--$t$ cut has capacity at least
$kn$.  Write the source side of a cut as
$\{s\}\cup (U\setminus A)\cup B$, where $A\subseteq U$ and $B\subseteq W$.
The arcs crossing it have total capacity
\[
 k|A|+e_G(U\setminus A,W\setminus B)+k|B|.
\]
Apply the assumed inequality to $U\setminus A$ and $W\setminus B$.
Their cardinalities sum to $2n-|A|-|B|$, so the middle term is at least
$k\max\{0,n-|A|-|B|\}$.  If $|A|+|B|\leq n$ the displayed cut capacity is
therefore at least $k(|A|+|B|)+k(n-|A|-|B|)=kn$; if
$|A|+|B|\geq n$, its first and last terms already total at least $kn$.

For completeness, the integral max-flow assertion needed here follows by
the augmenting-path algorithm.  Start with the zero integral flow.  As long
as the residual graph has an $s$--$t$ path, augment by the least residual
capacity on that path.  All capacities and all residual capacities are
integers, so every augmentation is by a positive integer and preserves
integrality.  The flow value strictly increases and is bounded by the total
capacity $kn$ out of $s$, hence the procedure terminates.  If it terminates
below $kn$, let $S$ be the vertices reachable from $s$ in the residual
graph.  Every original arc from $S$ to its complement is saturated and
every original arc in the reverse direction carries zero flow.  Summing
flow conservation over $S\setminus\{s\}$ then says that the flow value is
exactly the capacity of this cut, contradicting the cut bound.  Thus an
integral flow of value $kn$ exists.

All $kn$ units leaving $s$ and entering $t$ are then used.  Since each
$U$--$W$ arc has capacity one and the flow is integral, the arcs carrying
one unit form a subgraph of $G[U,W]$.  Flow conservation and saturation of
the source and sink arcs give degree exactly $k$ at every vertex on both
sides, as required.
\end{proof}
BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Bipartite regular-factor cut criterion]
Let $G$ be a finite graph and let $U,W$ be disjoint sets of the same size $n$.
For a natural number $k$, the bipartite graph $G[U,W]$ contains a spanning
$k$-regular subgraph if and only if, for every $A\subseteq U$ and
$B\subseteq W$,
\[
 e_G(A,B)\geq k\max\{0,|A|+|B|-n\}.
\]
Here a spanning $k$-regular subgraph means a subgraph of $G$ in which every
vertex of $U$ has exactly $k$ neighbours in $W$ and every vertex of $W$ has
exactly $k$ neighbours in $U$.
\end{lemma}
BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion.title: BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion

theorem BipartiteSelectedEdgeGraph {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (U W : Finset V) (hUW : Disjoint U W)
    (P : U → W → Prop) [DecidableRel P] (k : ℕ)
    (hG : ∀ (u : U) (w : W), P u w → G.Adj u.val w.val)
    (hrow : ∀ u : U, (Finset.univ.filter fun w : W => P u w).card = k)
    (hcol : ∀ w : W, (Finset.univ.filter fun u : U => P u w).card = k) :
    ∃ F : SimpleGraph V, F ≤ G ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U, {w | w ∈ W ∧ F.Adj u w}.ncard = k) ∧
      (∀ w ∈ W, {u | u ∈ U ∧ F.Adj u w}.ncard = k) ∧
      (∀ (u : U) (w : W), F.Adj u.val w.val ↔ P u w) := by

BipartiteSelectedEdgeGraph.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Define $F\operatorname{.Adj}(a,b)$ to mean either that $a\in U,b\in W$
and their copied pair satisfies $P$, or that $b\in U,a\in W$ and that
copied pair satisfies $P$. This relation is symmetric. A loop would
require the same vertex in both $U$ and $W$, impossible by disjointness;
thus it defines a simple graph. In the first alternative adjacency in
$G$ follows from the support hypothesis, and in the second from that
hypothesis and symmetry of $G$. Hence $F\leq G$.

For $u\in U,w\in W$ the reversed alternative is impossible by
disjointness, so $F\operatorname{.Adj}(u,w)$ is exactly $P(u,w)$.
For a fixed ambient $u\in U$, the map sending a copied selected $w$
to its ambient value is a bijection onto
$\{w\in W:F\operatorname{.Adj}(u,w)\}$. Surjectivity uses that every
element of $W$ has its subtype copy, and injectivity uses equality of
subtypes with the same ambient value. Its domain has cardinality $k$
by the row hypothesis, proving the left degree assertion. The same
argument with the column hypothesis proves the right degree assertion.
The relation selects a set of ordered pairs, not a list with multiplicity;
symmetrization creates exactly one unordered edge for each selected
pair because the parts are disjoint. Empty parts and $k=0$ are included.
\end{proof}
BipartiteSelectedEdgeGraph.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Transporting distinct selected pairs to a simple graph]
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and $U,W$ disjoint finite vertex sets.
Let $P$ be a relation between the exact subtype copies of $U$ and $W$,
and let $k\in\mathbb N$. Suppose every selected pair $P(u,w)$ is a
$G$ edge, each copied $u$ has exactly $k$ distinct selected $w$, and
each copied $w$ has exactly $k$ distinct selected $u$.
There is a simple graph $F\leq G$ whose opposite-part degrees are
exactly $k$ at every vertex in $U$ and $W$, and
$F\operatorname{.Adj}(u,w)\iff P(u,w)$ for all copied $u,w$.
\end{lemma}
BipartiteSelectedEdgeGraph.title: BipartiteSelectedEdgeGraph

classical
  intro Delta ε' d' d hDelta hε' hε'one hd' hd'd hdone
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hεlt, hrefine⟩ := SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement
    Delta ε' d' d hDelta hε' hε'one hd' hd'd hdone
  refine ⟨ε, hε, hεlt, ?_⟩
  intro r
  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ := hrefine r
  refine ⟨n₀, ?_⟩
  intro n hn VH VG _ _ _ _ H G R _ _ _ B A hsizes hH hR hB hA
  obtain ⟨color, hcolorSizes, hcolorIndependent⟩ :=
    EquitableSquareColoring Delta r n hDelta B hH (fun i => (hsizes i).1)
  obtain ⟨H', R', instH', instR', B₀, hHH', hsource₀, hsupport, hdegreeR, hsat₀⟩ :=
    MatchingCompletionExtension Delta r n hDelta B color
      hcolorSizes hcolorIndependent hR
  letI := instH'
  letI := instR'
  have hprojection₀ (x : VH) :
      (finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster x)).1 = B.sourceCluster x :=
    congrArg Prod.fst (hsource₀ x)
  have hfiber₀ (p : Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)) :
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH =>
        B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p).card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH =>
        B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p).card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1 := by
    have heq (x : VH) : B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p ↔
        B.sourceCluster x = p.1 ∧ color x = p.2 := by
      rw [← finProdFinEquiv.symm_apply_eq, hsource₀ x]
      exact ⟨fun h => ⟨congrArg Prod.fst h, congrArg Prod.snd h⟩,
        fun h => Prod.ext h.1 h.2⟩
    simpa only [heq] using hcolorSizes p.1 p.2
  have hunique (x y z : VH) (hxy : H'.Adj x y) (hxz : H'.Adj x z)
      (hyz : B₀.sourceCluster y = B₀.sourceCluster z) : y = z := by
    let p := finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster x)
    let q := finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster y)
    have hp : B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p :=
      (finProdFinEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).symm
    have hq : B₀.sourceCluster y = finProdFinEquiv q :=
      (finProdFinEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).symm
    have hz : B₀.sourceCluster z = finProdFinEquiv q := hyz.symm.trans hq
    have hadj : R'.Adj p q := B₀.reduced_support hxy
    let x₀ : {x : VH // B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p} := ⟨x, hp⟩
    let y₀ : {y : VH // B₀.sourceCluster y = finProdFinEquiv q} := ⟨y, hq⟩
    let z₀ : {y : VH // B₀.sourceCluster y = finProdFinEquiv q} := ⟨z, hz⟩
    rcases hsat₀ p q hadj with ⟨τ, hτ⟩ | ⟨τ, hτ⟩
    · have hy : y₀ = τ x₀ := (hτ x₀ y₀).mp hxy
      have hz : z₀ = τ x₀ := (hτ x₀ z₀).mp hxz
      exact congrArg Subtype.val (hy.trans hz.symm)
    · have hy : x₀ = τ y₀ := (hτ x₀ y₀).mp hxy
      have hz : x₀ = τ z₀ := (hτ x₀ z₀).mp hxz
      exact congrArg Subtype.val (τ.injective (hy.symm.trans hz))
  have hdegreeH : H'.maxDegree ≤ Delta ^ 3 := by
    apply H'.maxDegree_le_of_forall_degree_le
    intro x
    let p := finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster x)
    let f : H'.neighborSet x → R'.neighborSet p := fun y =>
      ⟨finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster y.1), B₀.reduced_support y.2⟩
    have hf : Function.Injective f := by
      intro y z heq
      apply Subtype.ext
      apply hunique x y.1 z.1 y.2 z.2
      exact finProdFinEquiv.symm.injective (congrArg Subtype.val heq)
    calc
      H'.degree x = Fintype.card (H'.neighborSet x) :=
        (SimpleGraph.card_neighborSet_eq_degree H' x).symm
      _ ≤ Fintype.card (R'.neighborSet p) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
      _ = R'.degree p := SimpleGraph.card_neighborSet_eq_degree R' p
      _ ≤ R'.maxDegree := R'.degree_le_maxDegree p
      _ ≤ Delta ^ 3 := hdegreeR
  obtain ⟨G', instG', B', A', hG', hsource, hhost, hallowed, hfibers, hsuper, hcan⟩ :=
    hn₀ n hn B A B₀ hsizes hHH' hprojection₀
      (fun p q hpq => (hsupport p q).mp hpq) hfiber₀ hB hA
  letI := instG'
  refine ⟨H', G', R', instH', instG', instR', B', A', hHH', hG',
    hallowed, ?_, hhost, hfibers, hsupport, hdegreeH, hdegreeR, hsuper, hcan, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    rw [hsource x]
    exact hprojection₀ x
  · intro p q hpq
    have hmap : B'.sourceCluster = B₀.sourceCluster := funext hsource
    unfold SaturatingSourcePair
    rw [hmap]
    exact hsat₀ p q hpq

theorem BlowUpReductionToAuxiliary :

      0 < d' → d' < d ^ 2 / 2 → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ ε : ENNReal, 0 < ε ∧ ε < ε' ∧
      ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ,
      ∀ (n : ℕ), n₀ ≤ n →
      ∀ {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
        [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
        {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
        [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel R.Adj]
        (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B),
        (∀ i,
          (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = i).card = n ∧
          (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = i).card = n) →
        H.maxDegree ≤ Delta → R.maxDegree ≤ Delta →
        InstanceLowerSuperRegular B ε d → CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d →
        ∃ (H' : SimpleGraph VH) (G' : SimpleGraph VG)
          (R' : SimpleGraph (Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)))
          (_ : DecidableRel H'.Adj) (_ : DecidableRel G'.Adj) (_ : DecidableRel R'.Adj)
          (B' : BlowUpInstance (r * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G'
            (R'.comap finProdFinEquiv.symm)) (A' : CandidacySystem B'),
          H ≤ H' ∧ G' ≤ G ∧
          (∀ {x v}, A'.allowed x v → A.allowed x v) ∧
          (∀ x, (finProdFinEquiv.symm (B'.sourceCluster x)).1 = B.sourceCluster x) ∧
          (∀ v, (finProdFinEquiv.symm (B'.hostCluster v)).1 = B.hostCluster v) ∧
          (∀ p,
            let X := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B'.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p
            let V := Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B'.hostCluster v = finProdFinEquiv p
            X.card = V.card ∧
              (X.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ X.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1)) ∧
          (∀ p q, R'.Adj p q ↔ R.Adj p.1 q.1) ∧
          H'.maxDegree ≤ Delta ^ 3 ∧ R'.maxDegree ≤ Delta ^ 3 ∧
          InstanceSuperRegular B' ε' d' ∧ CandidacySuperRegular B' A' ε' d' ∧
          ∀ p q, R'.Adj p q →
            SaturatingSourcePair B' (finProdFinEquiv p) (finProdFinEquiv q) := by

BlowUpReductionToAuxiliary.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Apply \noderef{EquitableSquareColoring} to every $X_i$.  It gives a single refinement map whose fibers $X_{i,j}$ have the asserted two possible sizes and are $2$-independent.  In particular, between any two refined source parts the old graph $H$ is a matching, and it is empty when the corresponding original indices form a nonedge of $R$.

Apply \noderef{MatchingCompletionExtension} to this refinement.  It constructs $H'\supseteq H$ and the graph $R'$ having exactly the displayed support, completes every old refined matching to one saturating its smaller side, adds no edge across a refined nonedge, preserves the refined source partition, and proves $\Delta(R')\leq\Delta^3$.  Each vertex of $H'$ has at most one neighbor in each refined source part adjacent to its own part, because every such pair is a matching.  The number of those adjacent parts is its degree in $R'$, and hence $\Delta(H')\leq\Delta(R')\leq\Delta^3$.

Now use \noderef{SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement}.  Its support hypothesis follows from the forward implication in the exact equivalence
\[
 (i,j)(i',j')\in E(R')\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad ii'\in E(R)
\]
provided by \noderef{MatchingCompletionExtension}.  Its threshold is chosen after $\Delta,\varepsilon',d',d$ and before $n$, exactly as required here.  It partitions each $V_i$ into parts $V_{i,j}$ with $|V_{i,j}|=|X_{i,j}|$, without changing the source refinement, and simultaneously restricts every relevant host pair and every candidacy graph.  The output consists of graphs $G'\subseteq G$ and $A'^{i,j}\subseteq A^i[X_{i,j},V_{i,j}]$ for which all host pairs on $R'$ and all candidacy graphs are $(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular.  The spanning extraction used there is supplied by \noderef{SuperRegularSubgraph}; \noderef{RegularSubgraph} supplies the corresponding regular extraction component before the minimum-degree cleanup.

Because both refined cluster maps project to the old maps, their fibers form disjoint unions equal to $X_i$ and $V_i$, not merely subsets of those clusters.  None of the host/candidacy restrictions changes $H'$, $R'$, or the source partition, so the containment, exact support, degree, size, emptiness, and saturating-matching conclusions from the first two steps all remain true.  Collecting these data gives the asserted refined blow-up instance and every listed property.
\end{proof}
BlowUpReductionToAuxiliary.title: BlowUpReductionToAuxiliary

theorem BlowupOrderMargins (η C₀ C' : ENNReal) (k : ℕ)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hηhalf : η ≤ 1 / 2)
    (hC₀ : 1 ≤ C₀) (hC₀top : C₀ < ⊤) (hC'top : C' < ⊤)
    (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ∃ C : ENNReal, 1 ≤ C ∧ C < ⊤ ∧ C₀ ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (Nbal Nred Nexec : ℕ), ∃ N : ℕ,
      ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → Nbal ≤ n ∧ C / n ≤ 1 ∧
        ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ENNReal) ≤ (1 - η) * n →
          (1 - η) * n < (m : ENNReal) + 1 →
          Nred ≤ m ∧ Nexec ≤ m / k ∧ C' / (m / k : ℕ) ≤ C / n := by

BlowupOrderMargins.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $b=1-\eta$. Since $0<\eta\leq1/2$, $1/2\leq b<1$ and $b$ is finite.
Choose
\[
 C=\max\{C_0,1,4kC'/b\}.
\]
Every quantity in this maximum is finite and $b>0$, so $1\leq C<\infty$
and $C_0\leq C$. This choice depends on none of the three thresholds.
After they are given, choose an integer $N\geq\max\{N_{\rm bal},1\}$
large enough that, for every $n\geq N$,
\[
 n\geq C,\qquad bn\geq2(k+1),\qquad
 bn-1\geq N_{\rm red},\qquad bn/(2k)\geq\max\{N_{\rm exec},1\}.
\]
Such an integer exists by the Archimedean property, since $b>0$, $k>0$
and all the constants displayed are finite real numbers. The first inequality
implies $C/n\leq1$ because $n\geq1$.
Fix any $m$ with the stated floor inequalities and write $u=\lfloor m/k\rfloor$.
The second floor inequality gives $m>bn-1$. Natural division gives
$u>m/k-1$. Consequently
\[
 u>(bn-1)/k-1=(bn-(k+1))/k\geq bn/(2k).
\]
The last comparison follows from $bn\geq2(k+1)$. Thus $u\geq1$,
$u\geq N_{\rm exec}$, and $m\geq N_{\rm red}$. Both denominators below
are positive. Monotonicity of division and $2kC'/b\leq C$ give
\[
 C'/u\leq 2kC'/(bn)\leq C/n.
\]
This calculation is valid also when $C'=0$. Since all its terms are finite,
it is equally a calculation in extended nonnegative reals. These are all
the required conclusions.
\end{proof}
BlowupOrderMargins.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}
Let $0<\eta\leq1/2$, let $1\leq C_0<\infty$ and $C'<\infty$ be extended
nonnegative reals, and let $k\geq1$ be an integer. There is a finite
$C\geq C_0,1$, chosen before any order thresholds, such that for every
three integers $N_{\rm bal},N_{\rm red},N_{\rm exec}$ there is $N$ with the
following property. For every integer $n\geq N$, one has
$n\geq N_{\rm bal}$ and $C/n\leq1$. For every natural number $m$ satisfying
\[
 m\leq(1-\eta)n<m+1,
\]
one also has
\[
 m\geq N_{\rm red},\qquad \lfloor m/k\rfloor\geq N_{\rm exec},\qquad
 \frac{C'}{\lfloor m/k\rfloor}\leq\frac Cn.
\]
All casts, products and quotients in these inequalities are in the extended
nonnegative reals; $\lfloor m/k\rfloor$ denotes natural-number division.
\end{lemma}

theorem BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S T : Finset V)
    (hST : Disjoint S T) {y : ℕ} (eS : S ≃ Fin y) (eT : T ≃ Fin y) :
    ((∃ i : Fin y, (T.filter fun w => G.Adj (eS.symm i) w).card = 0) →
      {f : S → T | PerfectMatching G S T hST f}.ncard = 0) ∧
    ((∀ i : Fin y, 0 < (T.filter fun w => G.Adj (eS.symm i) w).card) →
      ({f : S → T | PerfectMatching G S T hST f}.ncard : ℝ) ≤
        ∏ i : Fin y, Real.rpow
          ((T.filter fun w => G.Adj (eS.symm i) w).card.factorial : ℝ)
          (((T.filter fun w => G.Adj (eS.symm i) w).card : ℝ)⁻¹)) := by
BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct.name: BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct
BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Form the natural-number matrix $A_{ij}=1$ when
$G(e_S^{-1}(i),e_T^{-1}(j))$ holds and $A_{ij}=0$ otherwise.
Every entry is either zero or one, which is exactly the hypothesis
\texttt{ZeroOneMatrix} of the checked imported theorem
\texttt{EntropyMethodsFormalization.BregmanMinc}. Its row support is
$\{j:A_{ij}=1\}$; the bijection $e_T^{-1}$ identifies this set with the
neighbors of $e_S^{-1}(i)$ in $T$, so its cardinality is $r_i$.

Casting the permanent from natural numbers to real numbers commutes with
its finite sum of finite products. The cast matrix is the real zero-one
adjacency matrix. By \noderef{AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount}, its
permanent is $m$, with perfect matchings interpreted as in
\noderef{PerfectMatching}. Thus the natural-number permanent also equals
$m$, since the natural-to-real map is injective. Apply the zero-row branch
of the imported Bregman--Minc theorem when a row support is empty, and
its positive-row branch otherwise. These give respectively $m=0$ and
the stated product inequality. No entropy argument is required locally.
\end{proof}
BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Matching row-degree product]
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $S,T$ be disjoint finite sets, and
let $e_S:S\to\{0,\ldots,y-1\}$ and $e_T:T\to\{0,\ldots,y-1\}$ be
bijections. Put $r_i=|\{w\in T:G(e_S^{-1}(i),w)\}|$ and let $m$ be
the number of perfect matchings from $S$ to $T$. If some $r_i=0$, then
$m=0$. If every $r_i>0$, then
\[
 m\le\prod_{i=0}^{y-1}(r_i!)^{1/r_i}.
\]
The empty product is one, so the positive-row assertion includes $y=0$.
\end{lemma}
BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct.title: BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct

    calc

      _ = E.card := Fintype.card_coe E

    let e : Y j ≃ {v // v ∈ S.filter fun v => f v = j} :=
      { toFun := fun v => ⟨v.val.val, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨v.val.property, v.property⟩⟩
        invFun := fun v => ⟨⟨v.val, (Finset.mem_filter.mp v.property).1⟩,

        left_inv := fun _ => rfl
        right_inv := fun _ => rfl }

    Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le
      ((hX j).trans ((hroom j).le.trans_eq (hY j).symm))
  let slots (j : J) : X j ↪ Y j := (hslots j).some
  -- Assemble the binwise slot injections without choosing a default bin.
  let g : E ↪ S :=
    (((Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv (fun v : E => b v.val)).symm.toEmbedding).trans
      (Function.Embedding.sigmaMap (Function.Embedding.refl J) slots)).trans
      (Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv (fun v : S => f v.val)).toEmbedding

    (slots (b v.val) ⟨v, rfl⟩).property

    intro v hv

    have hH : H.card ≤ E.card := by

theorem CapacityPreservingReassignment {V J : Type*}
    [Fintype V] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq J]
    (S E : Finset V) (hES : E ⊆ S) (f b : V → J)
    (hroom : ∀ j, E.card < (S.filter fun v => f v = j).card) :
    ∃ f' : V → J,
      (∀ v ∉ S, f' v = f v) ∧
      (∀ v ∈ E, f' v = b v) ∧
      (∀ j, (S.filter fun v => f' v = j).card =
        (S.filter fun v => f v = j).card) ∧
      (∀ j, ((S.filter fun v => f' v = j) ∆
        (S.filter fun v => f v = j)).card ≤ 2 * E.card) := by
CapacityPreservingReassignment.name: CapacityPreservingReassignment
CapacityPreservingReassignment.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $e=|E|$, $s_j=|S_j|$, $a_j=|E\cap S_j|$, and
$b_j=|\{v\in E:b(v)=j\}|$. The bins partition $S$, so
$\sum_j a_j=\sum_j b_j=e$; each of $a_j,b_j$ is at most $e<s_j$.
Remove all exceptional vertices from their old bins and put them
in their prescribed bins. Retain ordinary vertices provisionally.
Bin $j$ now has $s_j-a_j+b_j$ vertices, an excess $b_j-a_j$.
For each bin of positive excess choose exactly $b_j-a_j$ of its
ordinary vertices and remove them. This is possible because the
number of ordinary vertices is $s_j-a_j\geq b_j-a_j$.
The total number removed is
$D=\sum_{b_j>a_j}(b_j-a_j)\leq\sum_j b_j=e$.
As the signed excesses sum to zero, this is also the sum of deficits
of the negative-excess bins. Partition the removed set into pieces
of these deficit sizes and place each piece in its deficit bin.
Such a partition exists by listing this finite set and cutting the
list at the cumulative deficit sizes. All bins now have size $s_j$,
and no exceptional vertex was moved away from its prescribed bin.
Define $f'$ by this partition on $S$ and by $f$ elsewhere.

In a fixed bin, exceptional membership changes in at most
$a_j+b_j$ places. Ordinary membership changes in just one direction:
exactly $|b_j-a_j|$ ordinary vertices are removed or received.
Thus its symmetric difference has size at most
$a_j+b_j+|b_j-a_j|=2\max(a_j,b_j)\leq2e$.
If $J$ is empty, a map $V\to J$ forces $V$ empty and all conclusions
are vacuous. If $E$ is empty, the construction leaves every bin
unchanged. These cases require no division or positive size claim.
\end{proof}
CapacityPreservingReassignment.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Capacity-preserving reassignment of exceptions]
Let $V,J$ be finite types, $E\subseteq S\subseteq V$, and let
$f,b:V\to J$. Assume $|E|$ is strictly smaller than every old bin
$S_j=\{v\in S:f(v)=j\}$. There is a map $f':V\to J$, equal to
$f$ outside $S$ and equal to $b$ on $E$, whose bins in $S$ have the
same sizes as before, and each new bin has symmetric difference
of size at most $2|E|$ from its old bin.
\end{lemma}
CapacityPreservingReassignment.title: CapacityPreservingReassignment

    have hk := fun i => (hN' i).2.1
    have hloss := fun i => (hN' i).2.2.1
    have hsmall := fun i => (hN' i).2.2.2.1
    have hdegree := fun i => (hN' i).2.2.2.2.1
    have hthreshold := fun i => (hN' i).2.2.2.2.2.1
    have hhostdegree := fun i => (hN' i).2.2.2.2.2.2.1
    have hcanddegree := fun i => (hN' i).2.2.2.2.2.2.2
    obtain ⟨X, hXcount, _, hE⟩ :=
      ClusterwiseDeletionBuffer B m k Delta hEq hm hk hH hR
    let E := Finset.univ.filter fun x => x ∉ X ∧ ∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y
    let S := X ∪ E
    have hXloss (i : Fin r) :
        ((X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤ 3 * ε * n := by
      rw [hXcount i]
      exact hloss i
    have hbuffer (i : Fin r) :
        ((E.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤
          4 * Delta * Delta * ε * n := by
      have hcast : ((E.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤
          (Delta : ENNReal) * Delta * k := by
        exact_mod_cast hE i
      calc
        _ ≤ (Delta : ENNReal) * Delta * k := hcast
        _ ≤ (Delta : ENNReal) * Delta * (4 * ε * n) := by gcongr
        _ = 4 * Delta * Delta * ε * n := by ac_rfl
    have hSsmall (i : Fin r) :
        ((S.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤
          a * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} := by
      change (((X ∪ E).filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤ _
      rw [Finset.filter_union]
      have hc := Finset.card_union_le (X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i)
        (E.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i)
      have hc' : (((X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i) ∪
          (E.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i)).card : ENNReal) ≤
          ((X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) +
          ((E.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) := by
        exact_mod_cast hc
      calc
        _ ≤ _ := hc'
        _ ≤ 3 * ε * n + 4 * Delta * Delta * ε * n :=
          add_le_add (hXloss i) (hbuffer i)
        _ = (3 + 4 * Delta * Delta) * ε * n := by simp only [add_mul]
        _ ≤ _ := hsmall i
    obtain ⟨hreg, hsizea, hinit⟩ :=
      RebalancingRestrictionEstimates B A n ε d a hεa hhost hcand hsize hdegree
    obtain ⟨Bs, As, hsm, hvm, ham, hrange, hsreg, hsH, hsR,
      hssmall, hssize, hsinit⟩ :=
      RestrictedSmallBlowUpInterface B A S Delta n a (d / 2) hreg hH hR hSsmall
        hsizea (fun x _ => hinit x)
    letI : DecidableRel As.allowed := fun _ _ => Classical.propDecidable _
    obtain ⟨_, hpartial⟩ := hp n ((le_max_left _ _).trans hn)
      Bs As hsreg hsH hsR hssmall hssize hsinit
    let T : Finset {x // x ∈ S} := Finset.univ.filter fun x => x.1 ∈ X
    obtain ⟨ν, hν⟩ := hpartial T
    have hnonempty (x : VH) : ∃ v, A.allowed x v := by
      have hnpos : 0 < (n : ENNReal) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < n)
      have hmul : 0 < (d / 2) * n := by positivity
      have hpos := hmul.trans_le (hinit x)
      have hc : 0 < Set.ncard {v : VG | A.allowed x v} := by exact_mod_cast hpos
      exact (Set.ncard_pos (Set.toFinite _)).mp hc
    let g : VH → VG := fun x => Classical.choose (hnonempty x)
    obtain ⟨μ, hμ, hreserve⟩ := RestrictedPartialEmbeddingTransport B A S X
      Finset.subset_union_left Bs As ham T (by intro x; simp [T]) g (C / n) (d' * n) ν hν
    refine ⟨m, hfloor, hceil, X, μ, hμ, ?_⟩
    intro f hf
    obtain ⟨Br, Ar, hsource, hhostmap, hallowed, hleft, hright, hremoved⟩ :=
      RebalancingResidualGeometry B A X f m hEq hm hXcount
    have himageloss (i : Fin r) :
        (((X.image f.toFun).filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).card : ENNReal) ≤
          3 * ε * n := by
      rw [hremoved i]
      exact hXloss i
    have hresHost : InstanceLowerSuperRegular Br ε' d' :=
      RebalancingResidualHost B A X f Br m ε d ε' d' (3 * ε * n)
        hhostmap hright hhost himageloss hthreshold
        ((le_add_right le_rfl).trans hdensity) hhostdegree
    have hJ : 4 * Delta * Delta * ε * n ≤ (8 * Delta * Delta * ε) * m := by
      calc
        _ = (8 * Delta * Delta * ε) * ((n : ENNReal) / 2) := by
          simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
          have htwo : (2⁻¹ : ENNReal) * 8 = 4 := by
            calc
              _ = (2⁻¹ : ENNReal) * (2 * 4) := by norm_num
              _ = ((2⁻¹ : ENNReal) * 2) * 4 := (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
              _ = 4 := by rw [ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel (by norm_num) (by norm_num), one_mul]
          calc
            4 * Delta * Delta * ε * n = (Delta : ENNReal) * Delta * ε * n * 4 := by ac_rfl
            _ = (Delta : ENNReal) * Delta * ε * n * ((2 : ENNReal)⁻¹ * 8) := by rw [htwo]
            _ = _ := by ac_rfl
        _ ≤ _ := by gcongr
    have hrho : (d' - ε') * m ≤ d' * n := by
      exact mul_le_mul' tsub_le_self (by exact_mod_cast hmn)
    have hresCand : CandidacyLowerSuperRegular Br Ar ε' d' :=
      RebalancingResidualCandidacy B A X f Br Ar m ε d ε' d'
        (3 * ε * n) (4 * Delta * Delta * ε * n) (8 * Delta * Delta * ε) (d' * n)
        hsource hhostmap hallowed hleft hright hEq hcand hXloss himageloss hbuffer
        hJ hε' hε'top hthreshold hdensity hcanddegree hrho
        (fun x hx hy => hreserve f hf x
          (Finset.mem_union_right X (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ x, hx, hy⟩)) hx)
    exact ⟨Br, Ar, hsource, hhostmap, hallowed, hleft, hright, hresHost, hresCand⟩

theorem ClusterRebalancing :
    ∀ (Delta : ℕ) (d : ENNReal), 1 ≤ Delta → 0 < d → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ d₀' : ENNReal, 0 < d₀' ∧ d₀' < d ∧
      ∀ d' : ENNReal, 0 < d' → d' ≤ d₀' →
        ∃ epsilon₀' : ENNReal, 0 < epsilon₀' ∧
        ∀ epsilon' : ENNReal, 0 < epsilon' → epsilon' ≤ epsilon₀' →
          ∃ epsilon₀ : ENNReal, 0 < epsilon₀ ∧
          ∀ epsilon : ENNReal, 0 < epsilon → epsilon ≤ epsilon₀ →
            ∃ C₀ : ENNReal, 1 ≤ C₀ ∧ C₀ < ⊤ ∧
            ∀ C : ENNReal, C₀ ≤ C →
              ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → C / n ≤ 1 →
              ∀ {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
                [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
                {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG}
                [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
                {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} [DecidableRel R.Adj]
                (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
                [DecidableRel A.allowed],
                H.maxDegree ≤ Delta → R.maxDegree ≤ Delta →
                InstanceLowerSuperRegular B epsilon d →
                CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A epsilon d →
                (∀ i, Fintype.card {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i} =
                  Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i}) →
                (∀ i, (1 - epsilon) * n ≤
                    Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} ∧
                  (Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} : ENNReal) ≤
                    (1 + epsilon) * n) →
                ∃ m : ℕ, (m : ENNReal) ≤ (1 - epsilon) * n ∧
                  (1 - epsilon) * n < (m : ENNReal) + 1 ∧
                ∃ X : Finset VH, ∃ μ : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X),
                  VertexSpreadOn
                    (μ.map (fun f => fun x : {x : VH // x ∈ X} => f.toFun x.1))
                    (C / n) Set.univ ∧
                  ∀ f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X, μ f ≠ 0 →
                    let Y := {x : VH // x ∉ X}
                    let W := {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}
                    ∃ Br : BlowUpInstance r Y W
                        (H.induce {x : VH | x ∉ X})
                        (G.induce {v : VG | v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) R,
                    ∃ Ar : CandidacySystem Br,
                      (∀ x : Y, Br.sourceCluster x = B.sourceCluster x.1) ∧
                      (∀ v : W, Br.hostCluster v = B.hostCluster v.1) ∧
                      (∀ (x : Y) (v : W), Ar.allowed x v ↔
                        (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x.1 v.1) ∧
                      (∀ i, Fintype.card {x : Y // Br.sourceCluster x = i} =
                        m) ∧
                      (∀ i, Fintype.card {v : W // Br.hostCluster v = i} =
                        m) ∧
                      InstanceLowerSuperRegular Br epsilon' d' ∧
                      CandidacyLowerSuperRegular Br Ar epsilon' d' := by

ClusterRebalancing.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Fix $\Delta,d$, and put $\widehat d=d/2$. This is positive and at most
$1$, so the principal statement of \noderef{PartialEmbedding} supplies
$b>0$ with $b<\widehat d$. Put $d'_0=\min\{d/4,b/2\}$.
Both entries are positive, and $d'_0\leq d/4\leq d/2<d$.
For $0<d'\leq d'_0$ we have both $d'\leq d/4$ and $d'\leq b$.
The same principal statement, at output reserve $d'$, supplies a finite
positive input-error cutoff $a_0$. Choose
$a=\min\{1/4,a_0/2\}$. Then $0<a\leq1/4$ and $a\leq a_0$.

Apply \noderef{RebalancingLossMargins} at $(\Delta,d,d',a)$.
It supplies $\varepsilon'_0>0$ bounded by $\min\{1/4,d'/2\}$ and,
for each admissible $\varepsilon'$, a positive $\varepsilon_0$.
Fix admissible $\varepsilon$, and let $n_a$ be its numerical order
threshold from that node. Independently apply the principal statement
of \noderef{PartialEmbedding} at input error $a$, not $\varepsilon$,
and output reserve $d'$. It supplies a finite $C_0\geq1$.
These choices are independent of $r$ and use no constants from the proof
of that theorem.

If $C=\infty$, choose $n_0=4$ for every $r$.
For $n\geq4$ the condition $C/n\leq1$ is impossible, since division
of $\infty$ by the finite scalar $n$ is $\infty$.
For finite $C\geq C_0$, let $n_p$ be the order threshold supplied by
\noderef{PartialEmbedding} at $(\Delta,\widehat d,d',a,C)$.
For every $r$ choose $n_0=\max\{n_a,n_p\}$; allowing an $r$-dependent
threshold does not require introducing $r$ into any earlier cutoff.

Fix $n\geq n_0$ and an instance satisfying the assumptions. Write
$N_i=|V_i|=|X_i|$. The numerical node supplies integers $m,k$ with
\[
 m\leq(1-\varepsilon)n<m+1,\qquad n/2\leq m\leq n,\qquad n\geq4,
 \qquad k\leq4\varepsilon n.
\]
In particular $m=\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)n\rfloor$.
Its window implications give, for every $i$,
\[
\begin{gathered}
 m\leq N_i,\quad N_i-m\leq k,\quad N_i-m\leq3\varepsilon n,\quad
 (3+4\Delta^2)\varepsilon n\leq aN_i,\\
 (d/2)n\leq(d-\varepsilon)N_i,\qquad
 \varepsilon N_i\leq\varepsilon'm,\\
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)N_i-3\varepsilon n,\qquad
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)N_i-3\varepsilon n
                                     -4\Delta^2\varepsilon n,\\
 (d'-\varepsilon')+8\Delta^2\varepsilon/\varepsilon'\leq d-\varepsilon.
\end{gathered}
\]
It also supplies $\varepsilon\leq a$ and $\varepsilon'<\infty$.
Thus every floor, ceiling, strict-threshold transfer, density loss,
and degree margin used below has a statement-level source.

Apply \noderef{ClusterwiseDeletionBuffer} with $m,k,\Delta$, using equal
fibers, $m\leq N_i$, $N_i-m\leq k$, and the original two maximum-degree
bounds. It gives a deterministic $X$ with the exact filtered count
$|X\cap X_i|=N_i-m$. Substituting the numerical loss bound gives
$|X\cap X_i|\leq3\varepsilon n$. For the exact external buffer
\[
 E=\{x\notin X:\exists y\in X,\ xy\in E(H)\},\qquad S=X\cup E,
\]
the same theorem gives $|E\cap X_i|\leq\Delta^2k$. Casting this natural-number
inequality to the nonnegative scalars and using $k\leq4\varepsilon n$ yields
$|E\cap X_i|\leq\Delta^2k\leq4\Delta^2\varepsilon n$.
Filtering $X\cup E$ by its cluster commutes with union, and the cardinality
of a union is at most the sum of the cardinalities. Consequently
\[
 |S\cap X_i|\leq |X\cap X_i|+|E\cap X_i|
 \leq3\varepsilon n+4\Delta^2\varepsilon n
 =(3+4\Delta^2)\varepsilon n\leq aN_i.
\]
In particular the entire external buffer is
included in the restricted source, while only $X$ will be embedded.

Apply \noderef{RebalancingRestrictionEstimates} with the original
host and candidacy lower-super-regularity, $\varepsilon\leq a$,
the original size window, and $(d/2)n\leq(d-\varepsilon)N_i$.
It supplies host lower-$(a,d/2)$-regularity, the host-size window
with error $a$, and at least $(d/2)n$ original candidates at every
original source vertex. These are not degree-only substitutes for
regularity. Together with the two original degree bounds and
$|S\cap X_i|\leq aN_i$, they verify every assumption of
\noderef{RestrictedSmallBlowUpInterface}. That node supplies $B_S,A_S$
on the literal source subtype $S$, with unchanged host and reduced
graphs, restricted source map, unchanged host map, exact original
candidacy relation, and all numerical premises of
\noderef{PartialEmbedding} at $(\Delta,d/2,a,n)$.

Use the partial conclusion of \noderef{PartialEmbedding} on $B_S,A_S$
and the subset $T=\{x\in S:x\in X\}$. It gives a law $\nu$ on partial
compatible maps with reserve at least $d'n$ at every vertex of
$S\setminus T$, whose total-map law on $S$ is $(C/n)$-spread.
For every original vertex $x$ the candidate-degree bound is strictly
positive, because $d/2>0$ and $n\geq4$. Hence choose an original candidate
$g(x)$ once and for all (the choice is the empty function if the source
is empty). Apply \noderef{RestrictedPartialEmbeddingTransport} with
this $g$, the exact restricted candidacy equivalence, $X\subseteq S$,
the defining equivalence for $T$, $q=C/n$, and $\rho=d'n$.
It supplies the ambient partial law $\mu$ with spread on its restrictions
to $X$, and reserve $d'n$ on every vertex of $S\setminus X$, in particular
every vertex of $E$, for every supported ambient map. The transport
identifies the updated candidate sets in both directions and removes
exactly the same image. It claims spread only on $X$, not on the fixed
ignored ambient values.

Fix $f$ with $\mu(f)\ne0$. Apply \noderef{RebalancingResidualGeometry}
with equal original fibers, $m\leq N_i$, and $|X\cap X_i|=N_i-m$.
It constructs $B_r,A_r$ on the literal source and host complements,
the induced graphs, and the unchanged reduced graph. Its two cluster
maps are the restrictions of the originals; its allowed relation is
exactly the ambient \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy} relation, in both directions.
Both residual fibers have size $m$, and it also proves
$|f(X)\cap V_i|=|X\cap X_i|\leq3\varepsilon n$.

For the host apply \noderef{RebalancingResidualHost} with
$L=3\varepsilon n$. The exact host-map identity and host fiber size
come from geometry, original host super-regularity is assumed, and
the removed-host bound was just proved. Its threshold-transfer
and degree-margin hypotheses are exactly the displayed numerical
bounds. Its density hypothesis follows by discarding the nonnegative
$8\Delta^2\varepsilon/\varepsilon'$ term. This proves
host lower-$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regularity for $B_r$.

For candidacy apply \noderef{RebalancingResidualCandidacy} with
\[
 L=3\varepsilon n,\quad J=4\Delta^2\varepsilon n,\quad
 \eta=8\Delta^2\varepsilon,\quad \rho=d'n.
\]
The exact residual interfaces and both fiber sizes are supplied by
geometry; equal original fibers and original candidacy super-regularity
are assumptions. The source and host deletion bounds are at most $L$,
and the external-buffer estimate proved above gives the exceptional count at most $J$.
Since $m\geq n/2$, we have $J\leq\eta m$.
Positivity of $\varepsilon'$ is assumed and its finiteness was supplied
by the numerical node. Threshold transfer, density loss, and the full
right-degree margin are exactly the numerical bounds displayed above.
Finally $m\leq n$ and $d'-\varepsilon'\leq d'$ give
$(d'-\varepsilon')m\leq d'n=\rho$; every external-buffer vertex has
that reserve by the transported law. Thus every hypothesis is checked.
The candidacy node applies exceptional-row slicing, including ordinary
row equality and the right-degree buffer loss, and transports edge
counts, density, neighborhood counts, and fiber sizes to the literal
residual subtypes. It yields candidacy
lower-$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regularity. These two regularity
conclusions and the exact geometry give the required conclusion
for every supported $f$.
\end{proof}
ClusterRebalancing.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Cluster rebalancing]
For every integer $\Delta\geq1$ and $0<d\leq1$, there is $0<d'_0<d$ such that, for every $0<d'\leq d'_0$, there is $\varepsilon'_0>0$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon'\leq\varepsilon'_0$, there is $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$, there is a finite $C_0$ with $1\leq C_0<\infty$ such that the following holds for $C\geq C_0$ (with $C/n\leq1$), every $r$, and every sufficiently large $n$ (depending also on $r$).

Let $(H,G,R,(X_i)_{i\in[r]},(V_i)_{i\in[r]},(A^i)_{i\in[r]})$ be a lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular blow-up instance with lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular candidacy graphs.  Suppose $\Delta(H),\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$, $|X_i|=|V_i|$, and
\[
 (1-\varepsilon)n\leq |V_i|\leq(1+\varepsilon)n
 \qquad(i\in[r]).
\]
Then there are a deterministic set $X\subseteq V(H)$ and a probability distribution on partial compatible embeddings $f:H[X]\hookrightarrow G$ whose restrictions $f|_X:X\to V(G)$ form a $(C/n)$-vertex-spread law (with all of $V(G)$ allowed), such that every $f$ in its support has the following property.  Thus, for any distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_s\in X$ and arbitrary $v_1,\ldots,v_s\in V(G)$, the probability that $f(x_j)=v_j$ for every $j$ is at most $(C/n)^s$.  On the literal residual vertex sets $V(H)\setminus X$ and $V(G)\setminus f(X)$, the induced graphs $H-X$ and $G-f(X)$, the unchanged reduced graph $R$, the exact residual fibers $X_i\setminus X$ and $V_i\setminus f(X)$, and the updated candidacy relation $A_f$ form a lower-$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular blow-up instance with lower-$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular candidacy graphs.  Moreover, for every $i$,
\[
 |X_i\setminus X|=|V_i\setminus f(X)|=\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)n\rfloor.
\]
Here ``exact'' means that the residual cluster maps are restrictions of the original maps and that a residual pair $(x,v)$ is allowed if and only if it belongs to \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}.
\end{lemma}

classical
  have hchoose : ∀ i : Fin r, ∃ S : Finset VH,
      S ⊆ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i) ∧
      S.card = Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - m := by
    intro i
    apply Finset.exists_subset_card_eq
    rw [← Fintype.card_subtype, hEq i]
    exact Nat.sub_le _ _
  choose S hSsub hScard using hchoose
  let X := Finset.univ.biUnion S
  have hScluster : ∀ i x, x ∈ S i → B.sourceCluster x = i := by
    intro i x hx
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hSsub i hx)).2
  have hfilter : ∀ i, X.filter (fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i) = S i := by
    intro i
    ext x
    constructor

      obtain ⟨hxX, hxi⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hx
      obtain ⟨j, _, hxj⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hxX
      have hji : j = i := (hScluster j x hxj).symm.trans hxi
      simpa only [hji] using hxj
    · intro hx
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨i, Finset.mem_univ i, hx⟩, hScluster i x hx⟩
  have hXcard : ∀ i, (X.filter (fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i)).card ≤ k := by
    intro i
    rw [hfilter i, hScard i]
    exact hk i
  refine ⟨X, ?_, hXcard, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    rw [hfilter i, hScard i]
  · dsimp only
    intro i
    let Y := (R.neighborFinset i).biUnion
      (fun j => X.filter (fun y => B.sourceCluster y = j))
    have hYcard : Y.card ≤ Δ * k := by
      calc
        Y.card ≤ (R.neighborFinset i).card * k :=
          Finset.card_biUnion_le_card_mul _ _ _ (fun j _ => hXcard j)
        _ ≤ Δ * k := Nat.mul_le_mul_right k
          ((R.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree i).le.trans
            ((R.degree_le_maxDegree i).trans hR))
    have hbuffer :
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => x ∉ X ∧ ∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y).filter
          fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i) ⊆ Y.biUnion (fun y => H.neighborFinset y) := by
      intro x hx
      obtain ⟨hxbuf, hxi⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hx
      obtain ⟨y, hyX, hxy⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxbuf).2.2
      have hij : R.Adj i (B.sourceCluster y) := by
        simpa only [hxi] using B.reduced_support hxy
      have hyY : y ∈ Y := Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
        ⟨B.sourceCluster y, (R.mem_neighborFinset i _).mpr hij,
          Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hyX, rfl⟩⟩
      exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
        ⟨y, hyY, (H.mem_neighborFinset y x).mpr (H.adj_symm hxy)⟩
    calc
      _ ≤ (Y.biUnion (fun y => H.neighborFinset y)).card := Finset.card_le_card hbuffer
      _ ≤ Y.card * Δ := Finset.card_biUnion_le_card_mul _ _ _ (fun y _ =>
        (H.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree y).le.trans
          ((H.degree_le_maxDegree y).trans hH))
      _ ≤ (Δ * k) * Δ := Nat.mul_le_mul_right Δ hYcard
      _ = Δ * Δ * k := by ac_rfl

theorem ClusterwiseDeletionBuffer {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG}
    {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R)
    (m k Δ : ℕ) [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel R.Adj]
    (hEq : ∀ i, Fintype.card {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i} =
      Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i})
    (hm : ∀ i, m ≤ Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i})
    (hk : ∀ i, Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - m ≤ k)
    (hH : H.maxDegree ≤ Δ) (hR : R.maxDegree ≤ Δ) :
    ∃ X : Finset VH,
      (∀ i, (X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card =
        Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - m) ∧
      (∀ i, (X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card ≤ k) ∧
      let X' := Finset.univ.filter fun x => x ∉ X ∧ ∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y
      ∀ i, (X'.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card ≤ Δ * Δ * k := by

ClusterwiseDeletionBuffer.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Clusterwise deletion and its external buffer]
Let a finite blow-up instance have equally large source and host clusters.  Fix natural numbers $m,k,\Delta$.  Suppose $m\leq |V_i|$, $|V_i|-m\leq k$ for every $i$, and $\Delta(H),\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$.  Then there is $X\subseteq V(H)$ such that
\[
 |X\cap X_i|=|V_i|-m\leq k\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
For its external neighbor buffer
\[
 X'=\{x\notin X:N_H(x)\cap X\ne\varnothing\}
\]
one moreover has $|X'\cap X_i|\leq\Delta^2k$ for every $i$.  In particular, taking $m=\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)n\rfloor$ and $k=3\varepsilon n$ gives exactly the deletion sizes and the $3\varepsilon\Delta^2n$ buffer bound used in the paper (whenever the displayed real bounds imply the corresponding integral inequalities).
\end{lemma}
ClusterwiseDeletionBuffer.title: ClusterwiseDeletionBuffer

CodegreeWindowTransfer.lean_proof:
have hk : (k : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.natCast_ne_top k
  have ha : (a : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.natCast_ne_top a
  have hak' : (a : ENNReal) ≤ k := by exact_mod_cast hak
  have hpa : p * k ≤ (a : ENNReal) + ε * k := by
    apply tsub_le_iff_right.mp
    simpa only [ENNReal.sub_mul (fun _ _ => hk)] using halower
  have hqc : q * a ≤ (c : ENNReal) + ε * a := by
    apply tsub_le_iff_right.mp
    simpa only [ENNReal.sub_mul (fun _ _ => ha)] using hclower
  have hqe : q * (ε * k) ≤ ε * k := by
    simpa only [one_mul] using mul_le_mul_right' hq (ε * k)
  constructor
  · rw [ENNReal.sub_mul (fun _ _ => hk)]
    apply tsub_le_iff_right.mpr
    calc
      p * q * k = q * (p * k) := by ring
      _ ≤ q * ((a : ENNReal) + ε * k) := mul_le_mul_left' hpa q
      _ = q * a + q * (ε * k) := mul_add _ _ _
      _ ≤ ((c : ENNReal) + ε * a) + ε * k := add_le_add hqc hqe
      _ ≤ ((c : ENNReal) + ε * k) + ε * k :=
        add_le_add (add_le_add le_rfl (mul_le_mul_left' hak' ε)) le_rfl
      _ = (c : ENNReal) + 2 * ε * k := by ring
  · calc
      (c : ENNReal) ≤ (q + ε) * a := hcupper
      _ = q * a + ε * a := add_mul _ _ _
      _ ≤ q * ((p + ε) * k) + ε * k :=
        add_le_add (mul_le_mul_left' haupper q) (mul_le_mul_left' hak' ε)
      _ = p * q * k + q * (ε * k) + ε * k := by ring
      _ ≤ p * q * k + ε * k + ε * k := add_le_add (add_le_add le_rfl hqe) le_rfl
      _ = (p * q + 2 * ε) * k := by ring
CodegreeWindowTransfer.lean_statement:
theorem CodegreeWindowTransfer (ε p q : ENNReal) (k a c : ℕ)
    (_hε : ε ≤ 1) (_hp : p ≤ 1) (hq : q ≤ 1) (hak : a ≤ k)
    (halower : (p - ε) * k ≤ a) (haupper : (a : ENNReal) ≤ (p + ε) * k)
    (hclower : (q - ε) * a ≤ c) (hcupper : (c : ENNReal) ≤ (q + ε) * a) :
    (p * q - 2 * ε) * k ≤ c ∧ (c : ENNReal) ≤ (p * q + 2 * ε) * k := by
CodegreeWindowTransfer.name: CodegreeWindowTransfer
CodegreeWindowTransfer.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Multiplication of a truncated difference by a finite nonnegative integer distributes over truncated subtraction.
Thus the two lower bounds give $pk\leq a+\varepsilon k$ and $qa\leq c+\varepsilon a$.
Since $q\leq1$ and $a\leq k$, monotonicity and distributivity give
\[
 pqk=q(pk)\leq q(a+\varepsilon k)
 =qa+q\varepsilon k\leq c+\varepsilon a+\varepsilon k
 \leq c+2\varepsilon k.
\]
The defining order property of truncated subtraction yields $(pqk-2\varepsilon k)_+\leq c$; distributing the finite factor $k$ gives the required lower bound.
For the upper bound,
\[
 c\leq(q+\varepsilon)a=qa+\varepsilon a
 \leq q(p+\varepsilon)k+\varepsilon k
 =pqk+q\varepsilon k+\varepsilon k
 \leq(pq+2\varepsilon)k.
\]
No cancellation or division by a parameter occurs, so the argument includes zero values of every parameter and of $k$.
\end{proof}
CodegreeWindowTransfer.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Transfer of neighborhood bounds to a codegree window]
Let $\varepsilon,p,q\in[0,1]$, and let $k,a,c$ be nonnegative integers with $a\leq k$.
Suppose
\[
 (p-\varepsilon)_+k\leq a\leq(p+\varepsilon)k,
 \qquad(q-\varepsilon)_+a\leq c\leq(q+\varepsilon)a.
\]
Then $(pq-2\varepsilon)_+k\leq c\leq(pq+2\varepsilon)k$.
The subscript $+$ denotes truncated subtraction, $(x-y)_+=\max\{x-y,0\}$.
\end{lemma}
CodegreeWindowTransfer.title: CodegreeWindowTransfer
