ColourRoundMatchingRecords.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The map $y\mapsto\mathrm{inl}(y)$ is injective with image $U$ by its
definition, giving $e$. Each member of $K$ uniquely has the form
$\mathrm{inr}(w)$ with $w\in V_i$; define $v$ to be this $w$.
Equality of its values gives equality of the original sum vertices,
so $v$ is injective. These give the first two identities.

Choose a fixed perfect matching $\sigma_*$, which exists by assumption,
and choose $y_*\in Y$. Then $v(\sigma_*(e(y_*)))$ is a host vertex.
For each matching $\sigma$ define a total function on source vertices
by $v(\sigma(e(y)))$ on $Y$ and this fixed host vertex off $Y$.
Its restriction to $Y$ is injective, by injectivity of $e$ and $v$
and the bijectivity clause of \noderef{PerfectMatching}.
The matching-edge clause of \noderef{PerfectMatching} puts each
matching edge in $F\subseteq A_f^i$.
The source/host sum tags force the forward orientation in the
symmetrization, so it is an allowed edge of the updated candidacy
system at $(X,f)$ by \noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster} and
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}. Finally $Y$ is independent by the source-independent
clause of \noderef{BlowUpInstance}; the graph-homomorphism condition on
$Y$ is therefore vacuous. These verify every field of
\noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding}, giving the record $\ell(\sigma)$.
If two records are equal, their values on every $y\in Y$ are equal.
Injectivity of $v$ and surjectivity of $e$ recover the two matching
functions. By \noderef{PerfectMatching}, the remaining fields assert
bijectivity and edge membership and are propositions, so proof
irrelevance identifies them. Thus
$\ell$ is injective.

The definitions of the domains give $X'=X\cup Y$: membership is the
disjunction of old membership and source-cluster equality with $i$.
For a tested $j$, the edge $ij$ implies $j\ne i$.
Since $j\notin S$ and $c(j)\ge t$, its source cluster meets neither
$X$ nor $Y$, and hence does not meet $X'$.
For any $z\in X'$, \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} supplies
$A.\mathrm{allowed}(z,h(z))$ from compatibility of $h$; the cluster-respecting
clause of \noderef{CandidacySystem} then implies that $h(z)$ belongs to the
host cluster of $z$. No such $z$ has cluster $j$, so the full host
cluster $V_j$ is disjoint from $h(X')$. This proves both exact part
equalities, including the reverse inclusions: every vertex of these
full clusters is genuinely unused.

Consider a forward edge of $T^j_\sigma$, written
$\mathrm{inl}(y)\mathrm{inr}(w)$. Its old-candidacy premise, by
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster} and \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}, gives
the two cluster equalities, $A.\mathrm{allowed}(y,w)$, and every
adjacency requirement to $f(X)$. The preceding unused-part argument
gives $y\notin X'$ and $w\notin h(X')$.
For a neighbour $z\in X'$ of $y$, split according to $X'=X\cup Y$.
If $z\in X$, the old requirement and $h(z)=f(z)$ give
$G(w,h(z))$.
If $z\in Y$, put $u=e(z)$. Symmetry of the source graph gives
$H(z,y)$, so the defining new constraint of $T^j_\sigma$ supplies
$\sigma(u)=\mathrm{inr}(z')$ and $G(z',w)$.
The second and third displayed identities imply
$z'=v(\sigma(e(z)))=\ell(\sigma)(z)=h(z)$.
Symmetry of the host graph then gives $G(w,h(z))$.
Thus every new updated-candidacy constraint holds, so the forward edge
belongs to $A_h^j$. The reverse orientation follows by symmetry of
both symmetrized graphs. Consequently $T^j_\sigma\subseteq A_h^j$.
The argument uses only the stated agreements of $h$ and therefore
applies to every compatible agreeing lift, not just a chosen extension.
\end{proof}
ColourRoundMatchingRecords.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Matching records and true updated containment]
Let $B$ be a blow-up instance and $A$ a candidacy system, and let $c$
be a colouring into $q$ colours. Fix $t,S,i$ with $c(i)=t$ and $i\notin S$.
Let $X$ consist exactly of the source vertices whose cluster has colour
less than $t$ or belongs to $S$, and let $f$ be a compatible partial
embedding on $X$. Put $Y=X_i$, assume $Y\ne\varnothing$, and put
$U=\mathrm{inl}(Y)$, $K=\mathrm{inr}(V_i)$.
Let $X'$ consist exactly of the source vertices whose cluster has colour
less than $t$ or belongs to $S\cup\{i\}$.
For any ambient graph $F$ contained in the symmetrized old updated
candidacy graph $A_f^i$, with disjoint parts $U,K$ and a perfect matching,
there are a bijection $e:Y\to U$, an injection $v:K\to V(G)$, and an
injection $\ell$ from its perfect matchings to compatible partial
embedding records on $Y$ for $A_f$, such that
\[
 e(y)=\mathrm{inl}(y),\qquad
 \mathrm{inr}(v(k))=k,\qquad
 \ell(\sigma)(y)=v(\sigma(e(y))).
\]
For every matching $\sigma$, every compatible partial embedding $h$ on
$X'$ agreeing with $f$ on $X$ and $\ell(\sigma)$ on $Y$, and every $j$
with $ij\in E(R)$, $j\notin S$, $c(j)\ge t$, the graph $T^j_\sigma$
defined by symmetrizing
\[
 \mathrm{inl}(y)\mathrm{inr}(w)\in E(A_f^j),\quad
 \forall u\in U,\quad
 [u=\mathrm{inl}(x),\ xy\in E(H)]\Longrightarrow
 [\sigma(u)=\mathrm{inr}(z),\ zw\in E(G)]
\]
is contained in the true updated candidacy graph $A_h^j$ at $(X',h)$.
Moreover the source part outside $X'$ is exactly $\mathrm{inl}(X_j)$,
and the host part outside $h(X')$ is exactly $\mathrm{inr}(V_j)$.
\end{lemma}

classical
  have widen (W : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG))
      (L Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG)) (a b d : ENNReal) (hab : a ≤ b)
      (hW : @SuperRegularPair (VH ⊕ VG) _ W (Classical.decRel _) L Q a d) :
      @SuperRegularPair (VH ⊕ VG) _ W (Classical.decRel _) L Q b d := by

          R.Adj j k) := by
      apply Finset.ext
      intro k
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.notMem_empty,
        or_false]
      exact and_congr (processed k) Iff.rfl
    have hold := hwitness f hf j hjuntouched hjold

    rcases hold with ⟨hex, _, W, hW, hreg⟩

theorem ColourRoundReset
    {r q : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel R.Adj]
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (colour : Fin r → Fin q) (epsilon density : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (D : ℕ) (C : ENNReal) (n round : ℕ)
    (X : Finset VH) (μ : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X))
    (hnext : round + 1 < q) (hepsilon : epsilon round ≤ epsilon (round + 1))
    (hμ : ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon density D C n round
      (Finset.univ.filter fun j : Fin r => (colour j).val = round) X μ) :
    ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon density D C n (round + 1) ∅ X μ := by
ColourRoundReset.name: ColourRoundReset
ColourRoundReset.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
We verify every clause of \noderef{ColourRoundInvariant}.  This is the
round-boundary argument of \texttt{paper/r2-colour-round-addendum.tex},
lines 241--271 and 333--341, restricted to boundaries with $t+1<q$.
Put $P=\{k:c(k)<t\}\cup B_t$ and $P'=\{k:c(k)<t+1\}$.
For each cluster $k$, natural-number arithmetic gives
\[
 k\in P\ \Longleftrightarrow\ c(k)<t\text{ or }c(k)=t
       \ \Longleftrightarrow\ c(k)<t+1
       \ \Longleftrightarrow\ k\in P'.
\]
Thus $P=P'$, including when $B_t$ is empty.  Applying this equality to
the source-cluster index of every source vertex proves that the old domain
clause is exactly the new domain clause, with the same $X$.
The degree bound and square-colouring clauses are unchanged, the new touched
set is empty and hence contained in the next colour class, and the new
round is legal by $t+1<q$.  The law and its restriction maps are unchanged,
so its vertex-spread clause, interpreted by \noderef{VertexSpreadOn},
is the old clause without any change of probability law.

Fix $f\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$ and a cluster $j$ for which the new witness
clause is required, namely $c(j)\geq t+1$.  Then $j\notin B_t$ and
$c(j)\geq t$, so the old invariant supplies its witness.  Its old and new
exposure finsets are equal, not just equicardinal:
\[
 \{k\in P:R.Adj(j,k)\}=\{k\in P':R.Adj(j,k)\}.
\]
Let their common cardinality be $x_j$.  The old bound $x_j\leq D$ therefore
remains valid, and the density is the very same $p_{x_j}$.
The new touched-neighbour finset is empty, so its cardinality is zero and
in particular at most one.

The partial embedding $f$ itself is unchanged, in the same type with domain
$X$, as in \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding}.  Consequently $f(X)$,
the unused source part of cluster $j$, and its unused host part are all
unchanged.  Unfolding \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy} shows that every allowed
pair is unchanged: it tests the same domain exclusion, image exclusion,
original allowed pair, and adjacency to every $f(x')$ with $x'\in X$.
Hence \noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster} gives the identical updated graph
of cluster $j$ before and after the reset.  The witness graph $W$ supplied
by the old invariant is therefore still contained in that same graph on
the same two parts $L,Q$.

If $N_R(j)\cap B_t$ is nonempty, this old witness already has error
$\varepsilon_{t+1}$, exactly the new error because the new touched set is
empty.  Keep its super-regularity assertion unchanged.  If the intersection
is empty, the old witness has error $\varepsilon_t$.  Write
$a=\varepsilon_t$, $b=\varepsilon_{t+1}$, and $d=p_{x_j}$, so $a\leq b$.
We check directly that its $(a,d)$-super-regularity implies
$(b,d)$-super-regularity.
By \noderef{RegularPair}, for subsets $U\subseteq L$ and $V\subseteq Q$
with $|U|>b|L|$ and $|V|>b|Q|$, monotonicity of multiplication gives
$|U|>a|L|$ and $|V|>a|Q|$.  The old regularity supplies
$d-a\leq d_W(U,V)\leq d+a$.
Truncated subtraction is antitone in its second argument and addition is
monotone, so
\[
 d-b\leq d-a\leq d_W(U,V)\leq d+a\leq d+b.
\]
This proves the new regularity, with the strict thresholds as required by
the definition.  For each $u\in L$, the old left degree bounds of
\noderef{SuperRegularPair} give
\[
 (d-b)|Q|\leq(d-a)|Q|\leq\deg_W(u,Q)
       \leq(d+a)|Q|\leq(d+b)|Q|.
\]
For each $v\in Q$, the identical monotonicities give the right degree bounds
\[
 (d-b)|L|\leq(d-a)|L|\leq\deg_W(v,L)
       \leq(d+a)|L|\leq(d+b)|L|.
\]
These inequalities use the extended nonnegative-real arithmetic of the
definitions and remain valid if a part is empty or a parameter is infinite.
Together they prove the new super-regularity of the unchanged $W$.
Thus only previously untouched witnesses have had their error weakened;
all witness, domain, colouring, degree, exposure, and spread clauses hold
with the same $X$ and $\mu$.  This proves the claimed next-round invariant.
There is no assertion at round $q$, since the hypothesis excludes it.
\end{proof}
ColourRoundReset.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Reset between consecutive colour rounds]
Let $B$ be a blow-up instance with finite source and host vertex sets,
candidacy system $A$, and reduced graph $R$ on $[r]$.  Fix a colouring
$c:[r]\to[q]$, sequences $\varepsilon,p:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty]$,
$D\in\mathbb N$, $C\in[0,\infty]$, and $n,t\in\mathbb N$.
Let $B_t=\{j:c(j)=t\}$, $X$ be a finite source-vertex set, and $\mu$ a
specified law on compatible partial embeddings with domain $X$.
Assume $t+1<q$, $\varepsilon_t\leq\varepsilon_{t+1}$, and the completed-class
invariant $\mathcal I(t,B_t;X,\mu)$ of \noderef{ColourRoundInvariant}, with
parameters $(\varepsilon,p,D,C,n)$.  Then the same domain and the same law
satisfy
\[
 \mathcal I(t+1,\varnothing;X,\mu).
\]
\end{lemma}

      (fun j => ⟨(P.witness_density _ (heJ j).le).1, P.host_density_lower⟩)
      (fun j => ⟨hp _ (heJ j).le, hd⟩)
      (enlarge _ _ _ _ _ _ P.inner_reserve.le h12) h13 h23
  refine ⟨F, F13, W23, ?_, hF, ?_, fun sigma hs j => htransport j sigma hs⟩
  · intro x v hxv
    obtain ⟨_, hh | hh⟩ := hxv
    · exact hsub hh.2.2.1
    · exact (hsub hh.2.2.1).symm
  · intro j
    refine ⟨hU, hK, hnear j, hUK, (hdisj j).1, (hdisj j).2, hF,

      enlarge _ _ _ _ _ _ hetheta (h23 j), ?_⟩
    intro x hx v hv hxv
    have hh :
        (rho (exposure j) * (d / 2) - 2 * eta round) * (Z j).card ≤
          (((Z j).filter fun z => (F13 j).Adj x z ∧ (W23 j).Adj v z).card : ENNReal) ∧

theorem ColourRoundRetainedTriplets
    {r q : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel R.Adj]
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (colour : Fin r → Fin q)
    (theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (D : ℕ) (d C a : ENNReal) (n round : ℕ)
    (P : ColourRoundStepParameters D q d C a n round
      theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi)
    (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hsizes : ∀ j : Fin r,
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n ∨
       (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n + 1) ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).card)
    (hhost : InstanceSuperRegular B (epsilon 0) d)
    (hsource : ∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, R.Adj i j → SaturatingSourcePair B i j)
    (touched : Finset (Fin r)) (X : Finset VH)
    (mu : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X))
    (hinv : ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon density D C n round touched X mu)
    (i : Fin r) (hi : (colour i).val = round) (hiS : i ∉ touched)
    (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X) (hf : f ∈ mu.support) :
    let Y := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = i
    let K0 := Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = i
    let U := Y.image (Sum.inl : VH → VH ⊕ VG)
    let K := K0.image (Sum.inr : VG → VH ⊕ VG)
    let J := {j : Fin r // R.Adj i j ∧ j ∉ touched ∧ round ≤ (colour j).val}
    let Z : J → Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := fun j =>
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).image Sum.inr
    let exposure := fun j : Fin r => (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin r =>
      ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ touched) ∧ R.Adj j k).card
    let Ai := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
      ∃ y : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl y ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧
        (y, v) ∈ UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X f i
    ∃ (F : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG)) (F13 F23 : J → SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG)),
      F ≤ Ai ∧
      @SuperRegularPair _ _ F (Classical.decRel _) U K (theta round) (rho (exposure i)) ∧
      (∀ j, @NearEqualRegularTriplet _ _ _ F (F13 j) (F23 j)
        (Classical.decRel _) (Classical.decRel _) (Classical.decRel _)
        U K (Z j) Y.card (theta round) (rho (exposure i))
          (rho (exposure j)) (d / 2)) ∧
      (∀ sigma : U → K, Function.Bijective sigma → ∀ j : J,
        let I := @MatchingInducedGraph _ _ _ (F13 j) (F23 j)
          (Classical.decRel _) (Classical.decRel _) U K (Z j) sigma
        let L := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inl : U → U ⊕ Z j)
        let Q := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inr : Z j → U ⊕ Z j)
        @SuperRegularPair _ _ I (Classical.decRel _) L Q
          (omega (round + 1)) (rho (exposure j) * (d / 2)) →
        let Vj := (Finset.univ.filter fun y : VH => B.sourceCluster y = j).image
          (Sum.inl : VH → VH ⊕ VG)
        let T := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
          ∃ y : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl y ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧
            (y, v) ∈ UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X f j ∧
            ∀ u : U, (∃ x : VH, (u : VH ⊕ VG) = Sum.inl x ∧ H.Adj x y) →
              ∃ w : VG, (sigma u : VH ⊕ VG) = Sum.inr w ∧ G.Adj w v
        ∃ W : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG), W ≤ T ∧
          @SuperRegularPair _ _ W (Classical.decRel _) Vj (Z j)
            (epsilon (round + 1)) (rho (exposure j) * (d / 2))) := by

ColourRoundRetainedTriplets.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Apply \noderef{ColourRoundWitnessThinnings} with the given instance,
parameters, invariant and supported partial embedding. Write $x=e_i$.
It supplies $x\le D$, independently $e_j<D$ for every $j\in\mathcal J$,
a contained current pair $W_{12}$ of parameters $(\xi_t,\rho_x)$,
and future families $O_j,W_j,J_j$. On the full future parts,
$O_j\subseteq A_f^j$ has parameters $(\varepsilon_t,p_{e_j})$,
$W_j\subseteq O_j$ has parameters $(\xi_t,\rho_{e_j})$, and
$J_j\subseteq H_0$ on the full host parts has parameters $(\xi_t,d/2)$.
This helper proves the exact witness-part identities, both threshold
bounds at every application, and the universe and host-copy adapters.
It uses the supplied guarantees, not an assertion of certificate existence.

For each $j\in\mathcal J$, apply
\noderef{ColourRoundSourceWitnessAssembly}, with $y=e_j<D$,
the given saturating source pair, the supplied cluster sizes, and
$O_j,W_j,J_j$. It gives a graph $F_{13}^j$ on $U,Z_j$ with parameters
$(\zeta_t,\rho_{e_j})$, and the precise deterministic transport into
$T^j_\sigma$ in the conclusion, for every successful bijection $\sigma$.
The source adapter treats both injection orientations, the two
one-point complements, artificial-row deletion, and genuine-row
restoration using the stored old witness. Choose these finitely many
test graphs together, and set $F_{23}^j=J_j$.

We now prove simultaneous retention and triplet verification.
Error enlargement preserves super-regularity by
\noderef{SuperRegularPair} and \noderef{RegularPair}: for errors
$b\le c$, a rectangle larger than $c$ times each part is also larger
than $b$ times each part; its lower bound $d-b$ is at least $d-c$
and its upper bound $d+b$ is at most $d+c$. The degree windows enlarge
by the same inequalities. By the inner-reserve field of
\noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters}, $\xi_t<\zeta_t$, so enlarge
$W_{12}$ and each $F_{23}^j$ to error $\zeta_t$.

The parts $U,K$ have the same size $m=|Y|$, since their copy maps
are injective and source and host cluster sizes agree.
Each $|Z_j|$ is $n$ or $n+1$, as is $m$, giving exactly the three
near-equal alternatives. The source and host copies are disjoint.
Also $K\cap Z_j=\varnothing$, because $ij\in E(R)$ implies $i\ne j$,
whereas a vertex belonging to both host fibers would give $i=j$.
The projection $\mathcal J\to N_R(i)$ is injective; the degree clause
of \noderef{ColourRoundInvariant} therefore gives
$|\mathcal J|\le D$.

The density fields in \noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters} give
$2\zeta_t<\rho_{e_j}$ and $2\zeta_t<d/2$, and their upper counterparts
give $\rho_{e_j}<1$ and $d/2<1$. Indeed
$0\le2\zeta_t<1-\rho_{e_j}$ implies $\rho_{e_j}<1$, and likewise for
$d/2$. Moreover $\zeta_t\le2\zeta_t<1-d/2\le1$.
The degree-loss field implies $\zeta_t\le\theta_t$.
Define $F$ to be the \noderef{SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph} of
$W_{12},F_{13}^j,F_{23}^j$, with constant test error $\zeta_t$ and
densities $\rho_{e_j},d/2$.
For the two finite-sum hypotheses of
\noderef{NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity}, use
\[
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\sqrt{\zeta_t}
   =|\mathcal J|\sqrt{\zeta_t}\le D\sqrt{\zeta_t},\qquad
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\zeta_t
   =|\mathcal J|\zeta_t\le D\zeta_t.
\]
The regularity-loss and degree-loss fields give respectively
$\zeta_t+\sum_j\sqrt{\zeta_t}\le\theta_t$ and
$\zeta_t+2\sum_j\zeta_t\le\theta_t$.
The square-root field gives $2\sqrt{\zeta_t}\le\theta_t$.
All size, disjointness, density, error and super-regularity premises
of that theorem have now been checked. Its conclusion proves the full
$(\theta_t,\rho_x)$ super-regularity of $F$ on $U,K$.
Every edge of $F$ is an edge of $W_{12}$, in either orientation, so
$F\subseteq W_{12}\subseteq A_f^i$.

Since $0\le\zeta_t\le1$, we have $\zeta_t\le\sqrt{\zeta_t}$, hence
$2\zeta_t\le\theta_t$. For a retained edge from $U$ to $K$, the
reverse orientation in the defining symmetrization of $F$ is excluded
by $U\cap K=\varnothing$. Thus its defining test gives, for every $j$,
the codegree window
$(\rho_{e_j}d/2\pm2\zeta_t)|Z_j|$, with the actual future part size.
Enlarge this window to error $\theta_t$, and enlarge the two test-pair
errors from $\zeta_t$ to $\theta_t$. Together with the checked part
sizes, disjointness and retained super-regularity, these are precisely
all clauses of \noderef{NearEqualRegularTriplet}.
The deterministic transport supplied earlier has no hypothesis about
the retained graph $F$ and remains valid for every bijection $\sigma$.
It is therefore exactly the final conclusion of the lemma.
\end{proof}
ColourRoundRetainedTriplets.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Deterministic retained triplet family]
Let $B,A,c,\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\xi,D,d,C,a,n,t$
be a blow-up instance, candidacy system, colouring, parameter sequences and
scalars, with a \noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters} record at these parameters
and $n\ge1$. Assume each source cluster has size $n$ or $n+1$ and the same
size as its host cluster; the original host pairs are
$(\varepsilon_0,d)$-super-regular; every reduced edge is a
\noderef{SaturatingSourcePair}; and
\noderef{ColourRoundInvariant} holds for $(t,S,X,\mu)$.
Fix $i$ with $c(i)=t$, $i\notin S$, and $f\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$.
Write $Y=X_i$, $K_0=V_i$, $U=\{\mathrm{inl}(y):y\in Y\}$,
$K=\{\mathrm{inr}(v):v\in K_0\}$, and
\[
 \mathcal J=\{j:ij\in E(R),\ j\notin S,\ c(j)\ge t\},\qquad
 Z_j=\{\mathrm{inr}(v):v\in V_j\},\quad
 V'_j=\{\mathrm{inl}(y):y\in X_j\}.
\]
Let $e_j=|N_R(j)\cap(\{k:c(k)<t\}\cup S)|$, and let $A_f^j$ be
the graph on the ambient source/host sum whose edges are precisely the
symmetrized pairs $\mathrm{inl}(y)\mathrm{inr}(v)$ with
$(y,v)\in\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}$ at $(B,A,X,f,j)$.
There are graphs $F,F_{13}^j,F_{23}^j$ on this ambient sum such that
$F\subseteq A_f^i$, the pair $(F;U,K)$ is
$(\theta_t,\rho_{e_i})$-super-regular, and for every $j\in\mathcal J$
the three graphs form a \noderef{NearEqualRegularTriplet} on
$(U,K,Z_j)$ at size $|Y|$ with parameters
$(\theta_t,\rho_{e_i},\rho_{e_j},d/2)$.
Moreover, for any bijection $\sigma:U\to K$, if its matching-induced
intersection of $F_{13}^j$ and $F_{23}^j$ on the canonical subtype copies
of $U,Z_j$ is $(\omega_{t+1},\rho_{e_j}d/2)$-super-regular, there is a graph
$W_j$ on the ambient sum with
\[
 W_j\subseteq T^j_\sigma,\qquad
 (W_j;V'_j,Z_j)\text{ is }(\varepsilon_{t+1},\rho_{e_j}d/2)
 \text{-super-regular}.
\]
Here $T^j_\sigma$ is the symmetrization of the relation
\[
 \mathrm{inl}(y),\mathrm{inr}(v):\quad
 \mathrm{inl}(y)\mathrm{inr}(v)\in E(A_f^j),\quad
 \forall u\in U,\quad
 \bigl[u=\mathrm{inl}(x),\ xy\in E(H)\bigr]
 \Longrightarrow
 \bigl[\sigma(u)=\mathrm{inr}(w),\ wv\in E(G)\bigr].
\]
This conclusion is deterministic; it asserts no matching probability law.
\end{lemma}

ColourRoundSourceWitnessAssembly.lean_proof:
classical
  dsimp only
  let L := fun k : Fin r =>
    (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = k).image
      (Sum.inl : VH → VH ⊕ VG)
  let Q := fun k : Fin r =>
    (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = k).image
      (Sum.inr : VG → VH ⊕ VG)
  let U := L i
  let K := Q i
  let V := L j
  let Z := Q j
  let Aj := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
    ∃ x : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl x ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧
      (x, v) ∈ UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X f j
  let H0 : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
    ∃ v w : VG, p = Sum.inr v ∧ s = Sum.inr w ∧ G.Adj v w
  intro hOA hWO hJH hO hW
  letI : DecidableRel O.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  letI : DecidableRel W.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  letI : DecidableRel J.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  let M : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
    ∃ x z : VH, p = Sum.inl x ∧ s = Sum.inl z ∧ H.Adj x z
  have adjM (x z : VH) : M.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inl z) ↔ H.Adj x z := by
    simp only [M, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj, Sum.inl.injEq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, hh | hh⟩
      · obtain ⟨x', z', rfl, rfl, hh⟩ := hh; exact hh
      · obtain ⟨x', z', rfl, rfl, hh⟩ := hh; exact hh.symm
    · intro hh
      exact ⟨fun he => H.ne_of_adj hh (Sum.inl_injective he),
        Or.inl ⟨x, z, rfl, rfl, hh⟩⟩
  let e (k : Fin r) : {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = k} ≃ L k :=
    Equiv.ofBijective
      (fun x => ⟨Sum.inl x.val, Finset.mem_image.mpr
        ⟨x.val, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, x.property⟩, rfl⟩⟩)
      ⟨by
        intro x z he
        exact Subtype.ext (Sum.inl_injective (congrArg Subtype.val he)), by
        intro z
        obtain ⟨x, hx, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp z.property
        exact ⟨⟨x, (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).2⟩, Subtype.ext he⟩⟩
  have coeE (k : Fin r) (x : {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = k}) :
      (e k x : VH ⊕ VG) = Sum.inl x.val := rfl
  have source :
      (∃ t : U ↪ V, ∀ u : U, ∀ v : V, M.Adj u v ↔ v = t u) ∨
      (∃ t : V ↪ U, ∀ u : U, ∀ v : V, M.Adj u v ↔ u = t v) := by
    rcases hsource with ⟨t, ht⟩ | ⟨t, ht⟩
    · let t' : U ↪ V := (e i).symm.toEmbedding.trans (t.trans (e j).toEmbedding)
      refine Or.inl ⟨t', ?_⟩
      intro u v
      have hh := ht ((e i).symm u) ((e j).symm v)
      have hm := adjM ((e i).symm u).val ((e j).symm v).val
      rw [← coeE, ← coeE, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hm
      rw [hm, hh]
      exact ⟨fun he => by simpa only [t', Function.Embedding.trans_apply,
        Equiv.toEmbedding_apply, ← he, Equiv.apply_symm_apply],
        fun he => by
          apply (e j).injective
          simpa only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] using he⟩
    · let t' : V ↪ U := (e j).symm.toEmbedding.trans (t.trans (e i).toEmbedding)
      refine Or.inr ⟨t', ?_⟩
      intro u v
      have hh := ht ((e i).symm u) ((e j).symm v)
      have hm := adjM ((e i).symm u).val ((e j).symm v).val
      rw [← coeE, ← coeE, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hm
      rw [hm, hh]
      exact ⟨fun he => by simpa only [t', Function.Embedding.trans_apply,
        Equiv.toEmbedding_apply, ← he, Equiv.apply_symm_apply],
        fun he => by
          apply (e i).injective
          simpa only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] using he⟩
  have cardL (k : Fin r) : (L k).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = k).card :=
    Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Sum.inl_injective
  have cardQ (k : Fin r) : (Q k).card = (L k).card := by
    rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Sum.inr_injective, cardL]
    exact (hsizes k).2.symm
  have sizeU : U.card = n ∨ U.card = n + 1 := by rw [cardL]; exact (hsizes i).1
  have sizeV : V.card = n ∨ V.card = n + 1 := by rw [cardL]; exact (hsizes j).1
  have sourceHost (s t : Fin r) : Disjoint (L s) (Q t) := by
    apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro z hzL hzQ
    obtain ⟨x, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hzL
    obtain ⟨v, _, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hzQ
    cases he
  have hKZ : Disjoint K Z := by
    apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro z hzK hzZ
    obtain ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hzK
    obtain ⟨w, hw, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hzZ
    have he' := Sum.inr_injective he
    subst w
    exact R.ne_of_adj hij
      (((Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2).symm.trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hw).2)
  have heta : eta round ≤ 1 := by
    have htwo : eta round ≤ 2 * eta round := by
      calc
        eta round ≤ eta round + eta round := le_add_right le_rfl
        _ = 2 * eta round := by ring
    exact htwo.trans (P.host_density_upper.le.trans tsub_le_self)
  have hp : rho y ≤ 1 :=
    (tsub_pos_iff_lt.mp ((zero_le _).trans_lt (P.witness_density y hy.le).2)).le
  have hd : d / 2 ≤ 1 :=
    (tsub_pos_iff_lt.mp ((zero_le _).trans_lt P.host_density_upper)).le
  have hph : rho y * (d / 2) ≤ 1 := by
    calc
      rho y * (d / 2) ≤ 1 * 1 := mul_le_mul' hp hd
      _ = 1 := one_mul _
  have heps : epsilon round ≤ 1 := P.error_monotone.trans P.error_unit
  have complement (A B : Finset (VH ⊕ VG)) (t : A ↪ B)
      (hcard : B.card = A.card + 1) :
      ∃ z ∈ B, ∃ tau : A ≃ B.erase z, ∀ x, (tau x : VH ⊕ VG) = (t x : VH ⊕ VG) := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
      let S := Finset.univ.image fun x : A => (t x : VH ⊕ VG)
      have hS : S ⊆ B := by
        intro x hx
        obtain ⟨a, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
        exact (t a).property
      have hsize : S.card = A.card := by
        rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective]
        · simp
        · intro a b he
          exact t.injective (Subtype.ext he)
      have hdiff : (B \ S).card = 1 := by
        rw [Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hS, hsize, hcard]; omega
      obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.mp hdiff
      have hzB : z ∈ B := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp (hz.symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self z)).1
      have hzS : z ∉ S := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp (hz.symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self z)).2
      have image : S = B.erase z := by
        ext x
        constructor
        · intro hx
          exact Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨fun he => hzS (he ▸ hx), hS hx⟩
        · intro hx
          obtain ⟨hne, hxB⟩ := Finset.mem_erase.mp hx
          by_contra hxS
          have hh : x ∈ B \ S := Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hxB, hxS⟩
          rw [hz, Finset.mem_singleton] at hh
          exact hne hh
      let g : A → B.erase z := fun x => ⟨t x, image ▸
        Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩⟩
      have hg : Function.Bijective g := by
        constructor
        · intro x y he
          exact t.injective (Subtype.ext
            (congrArg (fun z : B.erase _ => (z : VH ⊕ VG)) he))
        · intro y
          have hyS : (y : VH ⊕ VG) ∈ S := image.symm ▸ y.property
          obtain ⟨x, _, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hyS
          exact ⟨x, Subtype.ext he⟩
      exact ⟨z, hzB, Equiv.ofBijective g hg, fun _ => rfl⟩
  have assembled : ∃ F13 : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG),
      @SuperRegularPair _ _ F13 (Classical.decRel _) U Z (eta round) (rho y) ∧
      (∀ sigma : U → K, Function.Bijective sigma →
        let I := @MatchingInducedGraph _ _ _ F13 J (Classical.decRel _) _ U K Z sigma
        let LP := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inl : U → U ⊕ Z)
        let QP := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inr : Z → U ⊕ Z)
        @SuperRegularPair _ _ I (Classical.decRel _) LP QP
          (omega (round + 1)) (rho y * (d / 2)) →
        let Anew := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v z =>
          v ∈ V ∧ z ∈ Z ∧ O.Adj v z ∧
            ∀ u : U, M.Adj u v → H0.Adj (sigma u) z
        ∃ Wnew : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG), Wnew ≤ Anew ∧
          @SuperRegularPair _ _ Wnew (Classical.decRel _) V Z
            (epsilon (round + 1)) (rho y * (d / 2))) := by
    by_cases heq : U.card = V.card
    · have equiv : ∃ tau : U ≃ V, ∀ u : U, ∀ v : V, M.Adj u v ↔ v = tau u := by

theorem ColourRoundSourceWitnessAssembly
    {r q : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (D : ℕ) (d C a : ENNReal) (n round y : ℕ)
    (P : ColourRoundStepParameters D q d C a n round
      theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi)
    (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hy : y < D)
    (i j : Fin r) (hij : R.Adj i j)
    (hsource : SaturatingSourcePair B i j)
    (hsizes : ∀ k : Fin r,
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = k).card = n ∨
       (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = k).card = n + 1) ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = k).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = k).card)
    (X : Finset VH) (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)
    (O W J : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG)) :
    let U := (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = i).image
      (Sum.inl : VH → VH ⊕ VG)
    let K := (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = i).image
      (Sum.inr : VG → VH ⊕ VG)
    let V := (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).image
      (Sum.inl : VH → VH ⊕ VG)
    let Z := (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).image
      (Sum.inr : VG → VH ⊕ VG)
    let Aj := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
      ∃ x : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl x ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧
        (x, v) ∈ UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X f j
    let H0 : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
      ∃ v w : VG, p = Sum.inr v ∧ s = Sum.inr w ∧ G.Adj v w
    O ≤ Aj → W ≤ O → J ≤ H0 →
    @SuperRegularPair _ _ O (Classical.decRel _) V Z
      (epsilon round) (density y) →
    @SuperRegularPair _ _ W (Classical.decRel _) V Z (xi round) (rho y) →
    ∃ F13 : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG),
      @SuperRegularPair _ _ F13 (Classical.decRel _) U Z (eta round) (rho y) ∧
      (∀ sigma : U → K, Function.Bijective sigma →
        let I := @MatchingInducedGraph _ _ _ F13 J
          (Classical.decRel _) (Classical.decRel _) U K Z sigma
        let L := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inl : U → U ⊕ Z)
        let Q := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inr : Z → U ⊕ Z)
        @SuperRegularPair _ _ I (Classical.decRel _) L Q
          (omega (round + 1)) (rho y * (d / 2)) →
        let T := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
          ∃ x : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl x ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧
            (x, v) ∈ UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X f j ∧
            ∀ u : U, (∃ z : VH, (u : VH ⊕ VG) = Sum.inl z ∧ H.Adj z x) →
              ∃ w : VG, (sigma u : VH ⊕ VG) = Sum.inr w ∧ G.Adj w v
        ∃ Wnew : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG), Wnew ≤ T ∧
          @SuperRegularPair _ _ Wnew (Classical.decRel _) V Z
            (epsilon (round + 1)) (rho y * (d / 2))) := by

ColourRoundSourceWitnessAssembly.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $m=|U|=|K|$ and $k=|V|=|Z|$. The copied-part equalities follow
from injectivity of the sum injections and the assumed cluster-size
equalities. Each of $m,k$ belongs to $\{n,n+1\}$. The parts $U,K,Z$
are pairwise disjoint: source and host copies are disjoint, and the
two host clusters are disjoint since $ij\in E(R)$ implies $i\ne j$.
Also $V$ and $Z$ are disjoint.
Let $M$ have exactly the source edges on source copies and no other
edges. Its adjacency between copied source vertices is precisely that
of $H$. By \noderef{SaturatingSourcePair}, in one orientation there
is an injection between the source cluster subtypes whose graph is
exactly the source-pair edges. The maps from those subtypes to $U,V$
are equivalences: every vertex in the displayed image part has a
unique preimage under $\mathrm{inl}$. Conjugate the injection by these
equivalences. We obtain either an injection $U\to V$ with
$M(u,v)$ equivalent to $v=\tau(u)$, or an injection $V\to U$ with
$M(u,v)$ equivalent to $u=\tau(v)$.

Here are the parameter checks, all from
\noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters}, using $y\le D$.
Its witness density bounds give $0<\rho_y<1$: the lower bound is
$2\zeta_t<\rho_y$, and the upper bound follows from
$0\le2\zeta_t<1-\rho_y$. The host bounds similarly give
$0<d/2<1$, and give $\zeta_t\le2\zeta_t<1-d/2\le1$.
Thus $\rho_y(d/2)\le1$. We have
$\xi_t<\zeta_t$, $1/n\le\xi_t$,
$\xi_t+2/n\le\zeta_t$ and
$\xi_t+1/(\zeta_t n)\le\zeta_t$.
Also $\omega_{t+1}<\varepsilon_{t+1}\le1$,
$\omega_{t+1}+2/n\le\varepsilon_{t+1}$ and
$\omega_{t+1}+1/(\varepsilon_{t+1}n)\le\varepsilon_{t+1}$.
Finally $\varepsilon_t\le\varepsilon_{t+1}\le1$.

If $m=k$, the injection in either orientation is surjective, since its
image has the domain cardinality and the finite codomain has that same
cardinality. It therefore gives an equivalence $U\simeq V$, inverted
if its orientation was $V\to U$. In the inverted case,
$u=\tau(v)$ is equivalent to $v=\tau^{-1}(u)$ by applying the inverse.
Apply \noderef{EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport} with error
enlargements $\xi_t\le\zeta_t$ and
$\omega_{t+1}\le\varepsilon_{t+1}$.

If $m=k+1$, the cluster-size alternatives force $k=n$ and $m=n+1$.
There cannot be an injection $U\to V$, since injectivity would give
$m\le k$. The injection $V\to U$ has image of size $n$, so its
complement in $U$ has exactly one element $u_0$. Its range is therefore
exactly $U\setminus\{u_0\}$, yielding an equivalence
$V\simeq U\setminus\{u_0\}$ with the original adjacency equivalence.
Apply \noderef{CurrentExtraSourceWitnessTransport}, supplying every
inner, integer and outer reserve checked above. This produces the
full-current-part test graph, with an artificial row at $u_0$, and its
transport deletes that artificial row.

If $k=m+1$, necessarily $m=n$, $k=n+1$, and only the injection
$U\to V$ is possible. Its image has a singleton complement $v_0$,
and gives an equivalence $U\simeq V\setminus\{v_0\}$.
The adjacency equivalence also shows that $v_0$ has no source neighbour
in $U$, since $v_0$ lies outside the image.
Apply \noderef{FutureExtraSourceWitnessTransport}. Supply the stored
old witness $O$ with its stated parameters
$(\varepsilon_t,p_y)$, not just its thinning $W$.
Because $y<D$, the density update and gap fields give
$p_{y+1}=\rho_y(d/2)$ and
$\rho_y(d/2)+\varepsilon_t+1/n\le p_y$.
This is its old-row gap hypothesis. All other reserves have already
been checked. Its transport restores a subset of the genuine unmatched
old row after testing the smaller part.
These three cases exhaust $m,k\in\{n,n+1\}$.

In every case the cited transport supplies the asserted $F_{13}$ and,
for each successful bijection, a contained super-regular graph on the
full parts $V,Z$ inside the symmetrization of
$v\in V$, $z\in Z$, $O(v,z)$ and
$\forall u\in U, M(u,v)\Rightarrow H_0(\sigma(u),z)$.
This auxiliary graph is contained in $T_\sigma$, as follows.
In the forward orientation, write $v=\mathrm{inl}(x)$ and
$z=\mathrm{inr}(a)$ by their part memberships.
The edge $O(v,z)$ belongs to $A_f^j$. The reverse alternative in the
symmetrization defining $A_f^j$ is impossible on a source/host pair;
hence $(x,a)$ belongs to the displayed updated candidacy cluster.
For any $u=\mathrm{inl}(b)$ with $H(b,x)$, the definition of $M$
gives $M(u,v)$. The auxiliary constraint gives
$H_0(\sigma(u),z)$. Since $\sigma(u)\in K$, it is
$\mathrm{inr}(w)$ for some $w$. The host-edge definition of $H_0$,
using symmetry of $G$ for its reverse alternative, yields $G(w,a)$.
This proves the required true constraint. The reverse orientation of
an auxiliary edge follows by symmetry of $T_\sigma$.
Transitivity of graph containment now gives the claimed
$W_{\mathrm{new}}\subseteq T_\sigma$, without changing its
super-regularity, its parameters or its exact parts.
\end{proof}
ColourRoundSourceWitnessAssembly.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Source-matching assembly of a future test]
Let $B,A$ be a blow-up instance and candidacy system, and let
$\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\xi,D,d,C,a,n,t$
carry a \noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters} record. Assume $n\ge1$,
$y<D$, every source cluster has size $n$ or $n+1$ and equals its host
cluster in size. Fix $ij\in E(R)$ and assume
\noderef{SaturatingSourcePair} for $(B,i,j)$.
For a partial compatible embedding $f$ on $X$, put
$U=\mathrm{inl}(X_i)$, $K=\mathrm{inr}(V_i)$,
$V=\mathrm{inl}(X_j)$, $Z=\mathrm{inr}(V_j)$.
Let $A_f^j$ symmetrize the copied pairs belonging to
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster} at $(B,A,X,f,j)$, and let $H_0$
have exactly the original host edges on host copies and no other edges.
Suppose $O,W,J$ are ambient graphs with
$O\subseteq A_f^j$, $W\subseteq O$, $J\subseteq H_0$, and
\[
 (O;V,Z)\text{ is }(\varepsilon_t,p_y)\text{-super-regular},\qquad
 (W;V,Z)\text{ is }(\xi_t,\rho_y)\text{-super-regular}.
\]
There is a graph $F_{13}$ whose pair on $U,Z$ is
$(\zeta_t,\rho_y)$-super-regular. For every bijection $\sigma:U\to K$,
if the \noderef{MatchingInducedGraph} of $F_{13},J$ on the canonical
subtype copies of $U,Z$ is
$(\omega_{t+1},\rho_y d/2)$-super-regular, there is an ambient graph
$W_{\mathrm{new}}$ on the full parts $V,Z$, contained in the
symmetrization $T_\sigma$ of
\[
 \mathrm{inl}(x),\mathrm{inr}(v):\quad
 (x,v)\in\mathrm{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}(B,A,X,f,j),\quad
 \forall u\in U,\quad
 [u=\mathrm{inl}(z),\ zx\in E(H)]\Longrightarrow
 [\sigma(u)=\mathrm{inr}(w),\ wv\in E(G)],
\]
and $(W_{\mathrm{new}};V,Z)$ is
$(\varepsilon_{t+1},\rho_y d/2)$-super-regular.
\end{lemma}

ColourRoundStepParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Numerical data for one colour round]
For $D,q,d,C,a,n,t$ and sequences $\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,
\omega,\xi$, a colour-round step parameter record consists of a certificate
$\mathcal C$ of \noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate} at
$(D,q,d,\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\xi)$, together with the
following inequalities. It records $t<q$,
$\varepsilon_t\le\varepsilon_{t+1}\le1$, $0<a\le1$, $C/n\le1$, and
$D(1-a)^n\le1/2$. Its simultaneous-test reserves are
\[
2\sqrt{\zeta_t}\le\theta_t,\quad
\zeta_t+D\sqrt{\zeta_t}\le\theta_t,\quad
\zeta_t+2D\zeta_t\le\theta_t.
\]
For every $x\le D$ it records $0<\theta_t$, $4\theta_t<\rho_x$,
$2\zeta_t<\rho_x$, $2\zeta_t<1-\rho_x$; it also records
$2\zeta_t<d/2$ and $2\zeta_t<1-d/2$.
For $x<D$ it records $p_{x+1}=\rho_xd/2$ and
$p_{x+1}+\varepsilon_t+1/n\le p_x$.
It records $\omega_{t+1}<\varepsilon_{t+1}$,
\[
1/n\le\xi_t<\zeta_t,\quad \xi_t+2/n\le\zeta_t,\quad
\xi_t+1/(\zeta_t n)\le\zeta_t.
\]
For every $x\le D$ it records
$\omega_{t+1}+2/n\le\varepsilon_{t+1}$ and
$\omega_{t+1}+1/(\varepsilon_{t+1}n)\le\varepsilon_{t+1}$.
Finally, for every $x\le D$ the certificate's witness-thinning,
host-thinning, matching-spread and matching-existence thresholds are at
most $n$, and its matching constant is at most $C/2$. For every ordered
pair $x,y\le D$, its Four-Graphs threshold is at most $n$ and its
Four-Graphs constant is at least $a$. This is a record of numerical
data and their bounds, not an additional theorem assumption.
\end{definition}

  · intro j hij
    let E := Finset.univ.filter fun k =>
      ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ touched) ∧ R.Adj j k
    have hiE : i ∉ E := by
      simp only [E, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, hi,
        lt_self_iff_false, false_or, hiS, false_and, not_false_eq_true]
    have eqE : (Finset.univ.filter fun k =>
        ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ insert i touched) ∧ R.Adj j k) =
        insert i E := by
      ext k
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_insert, E]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hk | (rfl | hk), hjk⟩
        · exact Or.inr ⟨Or.inl hk, hjk⟩
        · exact Or.inl rfl
        · exact Or.inr ⟨Or.inr hk, hjk⟩
      · rintro (rfl | ⟨hk, hjk⟩)
        · exact ⟨Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), R.symm hij⟩
        · exact ⟨hk.imp id Or.inr |> Or.imp id id, hjk⟩
    have hsub : insert i E ⊆ Finset.univ.filter fun k => R.Adj j k := by
      intro k hk
      rcases Finset.mem_insert.mp hk with rfl | hk
      · exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, R.symm hij⟩
      · exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, (Finset.mem_filter.mp hk).2.2⟩
    have hbound := (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans (hdegree j)
    rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hiE] at hbound
    exact ⟨by change E.card < D; omega,
      by rw [eqE, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hiE]⟩

theorem ColourRoundUntouchedGeometry
    {r q : ℕ} (R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)) [DecidableRel R.Adj]
    (colour : Fin r → Fin q) (D round : ℕ) (touched : Finset (Fin r))
    (i : Fin r)
    (hdegree : ∀ j, (Finset.univ.filter fun k => R.Adj j k).card ≤ D)
    (hcolour : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, u ≠ v →
      (R.Adj u v ∨ ∃ k, R.Adj u k ∧ R.Adj k v) → colour u ≠ colour v)
    (htouched : ∀ j ∈ touched, (colour j).val = round)
    (hi : (colour i).val = round) (hiS : i ∉ touched) :
    (touched.filter fun k => R.Adj i k) = ∅ ∧
    (∀ j, R.Adj i j → (touched.filter fun k => R.Adj j k) = ∅) ∧
    (∀ j, ((insert i touched).filter fun k => R.Adj j k).card ≤ 1) ∧
    (∀ j, R.Adj i j →
      (Finset.univ.filter fun k =>
        ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ touched) ∧ R.Adj j k).card < D ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun k =>
        ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ insert i touched) ∧ R.Adj j k).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun k =>
          ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ touched) ∧ R.Adj j k).card + 1) := by

ColourRoundUntouchedGeometry.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
If $s\in S\cap N_R(i)$, the edge $is$ contradicts $c(s)=c(i)$.
If $s\in S\cap N_R(j)$ with $ij\in E(R)$, then $s\ne i$ because
$i\notin S$, and the walk $i,j,s$ contradicts the same equality of
colours. Two distinct neighbours of any vertex that lie in $S\cup\{i\}$
also have the same colour and are joined by a two-edge walk. Thus there
cannot be two such neighbours.
The vertex $i$ is not in the set counted by $e_j$: its colour is $t$ and
it is not in $S$. Adding it to $S$ adds exactly this one neighbour of
$j$ and changes no other membership condition. The resulting neighbour
set has size $e_j+1$ and is contained in $N_R(j)$, so $e_j+1\le D$.
This gives the asserted strict bound and the exact increment.
\end{proof}
ColourRoundUntouchedGeometry.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Untouched witnesses and independent exposure counts]
Let $R$ be a finite reduced graph of maximum degree at most $D$, and let
$c:V(R)\to[q]$ separate distinct vertices joined by an edge or a two-edge
walk. Let $S\subseteq c^{-1}(t)$ and $i\in c^{-1}(t)\setminus S$.
Then $N_R(i)\cap S=\varnothing$, and $N_R(j)\cap S=\varnothing$ for
every $j\in N_R(i)$. Every vertex has at most one neighbour in
$S\cup\{i\}$. Write
$e_j=|\{k:(c(k)<t\text{ or }k\in S),\ jk\in E(R)\}|$.
For every $j\in N_R(i)$, $e_j<D$, and replacing $S$ by $S\cup\{i\}$
changes $e_j$ to exactly $e_j+1$. No comparison with $e_i$ is asserted.
\end{lemma}

theorem ColourRoundWitnessThinnings
    {r q : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel R.Adj]
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (colour : Fin r → Fin q)
    (theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (D : ℕ) (d C a : ENNReal) (n round : ℕ)
    (P : ColourRoundStepParameters D q d C a n round
      theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi)
    (hsizes : ∀ j : Fin r,
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n ∨
       (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n + 1) ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).card)
    (hhost : InstanceSuperRegular B (epsilon 0) d)
    (touched : Finset (Fin r)) (X : Finset VH)
    (mu : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X))
    (hinv : ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon density D C n round touched X mu)
    (i : Fin r) (hi : (colour i).val = round) (hiS : i ∉ touched)
    (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X) (hf : f ∈ mu.support) :
    let L := fun j : Fin r =>
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).image
        (Sum.inl : VH → VH ⊕ VG)
    let Q := fun j : Fin r =>
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).image
        (Sum.inr : VG → VH ⊕ VG)
    let J := {j : Fin r // R.Adj i j ∧ j ∉ touched ∧ round ≤ (colour j).val}
    let exposure := fun j : Fin r => (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin r =>
      ((colour k).val < round ∨ k ∈ touched) ∧ R.Adj j k).card
    let Aj := fun j : Fin r => SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>

ColourRoundWitnessThinnings.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Unpack \noderef{ColourRoundInvariant}. Its degree, square-colouring and
touched-colour clauses meet all hypotheses of
\noderef{ColourRoundUntouchedGeometry} at $i$. Thus the touched-neighbour
sets of $i$ and every $j\in\mathcal J$ are empty, and $e_j<D$ for each
such $j$. The invariant separately gives $e_i\le D$. No comparison of
$e_i$ and $e_j$ is made.

For any $j\notin S$ with $c(j)\ge t$, the exact domain clause says that
a vertex $x\in X_j$ cannot belong to $X$: membership would say
$c(j)<t$ or $j\in S$, both impossible. If a vertex $v\in V_j$ were
$f(x)$ for $x\in X$, compatibility in
\noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} and the cluster-respecting clause
of \noderef{CandidacySystem} would give
$B.\mathrm{sourceCluster}(x)=B.\mathrm{hostCluster}(v)=j$.
This contradicts the preceding exclusion. Hence $V_j\cap f(X)$ is empty.
The two finite parts in the witness clause of
\noderef{ColourRoundInvariant} are therefore exactly $L_j$ and $Q_j$,
not merely subsets: each copy in the full cluster satisfies the unused
condition, and every vertex in a witness part is by its definition a
copy in that cluster. Since the touched-neighbour set is empty, its
conditional witness error is $\varepsilon_t$. Select its graph $O_j$,
with containment in $A_f^j$ as defined by
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}. The same argument gives $O_i$.

The source and host injections into the sum preserve cardinalities and
have disjoint images. Thus $|L_j|=|Q_j|\in\{n,n+1\}$, so both
near-equal inequalities hold. The witness threshold in
\noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters} at $(t,e_j)$ is at most $n$ and
hence at most both part sizes. Its round bound is $t<q$; the invariant
provides the required exposure bound separately for each call.
Apply the witness-thinning guarantee of
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate} through
\noderef{FiniteSuperRegularThinning}. This adapter uses an equivalence
with a lifted finite ordinal in the guarantee's universe, preserves
both exact parts and sizes, and pulls back containment. It supplies
$W_j\subseteq O_j$ with parameters $(\xi_t,\rho_{e_j})$, and supplies
$W_{12}\subseteq O_i\subseteq A_f^i$ with parameters
$(\xi_t,\rho_{e_i})$.

For each $j\in\mathcal J$, the host clusters $V_i,V_j$ are disjoint:
the reduced edge implies $i\ne j$, while a common vertex would have
both cluster labels. Their sizes belong to $\{n,n+1\}$, giving both
near-equal inequalities. The host threshold from
\noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters} is at most $n$, hence at most
both sizes. The input super-regularity is the $ij$ clause of
\noderef{InstanceSuperRegular}. Apply the host-thinning guarantee of
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate}, again through
\noderef{FiniteSuperRegularThinning}, obtaining a graph $T_j\subseteq G$
with $(\xi_t,d/2)$ super-regularity on $V_i,V_j$.
Let $J_j$ have precisely the edges
$\mathrm{inr}(v)\mathrm{inr}(w)$ for $vw\in E(T_j)$, symmetrized
on the ambient sum. Its containment in $H_0$ follows edgewise from
$T_j\subseteq G$, in either orientation. For host vertices its
adjacency is equivalent to that of $T_j$: the forward implication
uses symmetry in the reversed orientation, and the backward implication
uses looplessness to satisfy the unequal-endpoint condition of the
symmetrization. Apply \noderef{SuperRegularPairEmbedding} with the
injective host map $\mathrm{inr}$. Its exact neighbourhood and rectangle
count identities give the desired super-regularity on $Q_i,Q_j$.
Choose these finitely many graphs together to obtain all families.
\end{proof}
ColourRoundWitnessThinnings.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Contained thinnings of the full untouched witnesses]
Let $B,A,c,\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\xi,D,d,C,a,n,t$
be an instance, candidacy system, colouring, sequences and scalars, with a
\noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters} record at these parameters.
Assume every source cluster has size $n$ or $n+1$ and equals its host
cluster in size, the original host pairs are
$(\varepsilon_0,d)$-super-regular, and
\noderef{ColourRoundInvariant} holds for $(t,S,X,\mu)$.
Fix $i$ with $c(i)=t$, $i\notin S$, and $f\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$.
Let $L_j=\mathrm{inl}(X_j)$, $Q_j=\mathrm{inr}(V_j)$ be the full copied
clusters, let
$\mathcal J=\{j:ij\in E(R),j\notin S,c(j)\ge t\}$, and put
$e_j=|N_R(j)\cap(\{k:c(k)<t\}\cup S)|$.
On the source/host sum let $A_f^j$ be the symmetrization of
$\mathrm{inl}(x)\mathrm{inr}(v)$ for
$(x,v)\in\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}$ at $(B,A,X,f,j)$,
and let $H_0$ have exactly the original host edges on host copies and
no edges incident to source copies.
Then $e_i\le D$ and $e_j<D$ for every $j\in\mathcal J$.
There are graphs $W_{12}$ and families $O_j,W_j,J_j$ on the ambient sum
with $W_{12}\subseteq A_f^i$ and
$(W_{12};L_i,Q_i)$ $(\xi_t,\rho_{e_i})$-super-regular, and, for each
$j\in\mathcal J$,
\[
 O_j\subseteq A_f^j,\quad
 (O_j;L_j,Q_j)\text{ is }(\varepsilon_t,p_{e_j})\text{-super-regular},
 \quad W_j\subseteq O_j,\quad
 (W_j;L_j,Q_j)\text{ is }(\xi_t,\rho_{e_j})\text{-super-regular},
\]
\[
 J_j\subseteq H_0,\qquad
 (J_j;Q_i,Q_j)\text{ is }(\xi_t,d/2)\text{-super-regular}.
\]
\end{lemma}

theorem CompleteRowPadding {V W : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (Gp : SimpleGraph W)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel Gp.Adj]
    (e : V ↪ W) (L Q : Finset V) (D : Finset W)
    (ε η d : ENNReal)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hbudget : ε ≤ η * η) (hη : η ≤ 1) (hd : d ≤ 1)
    (hdis : Disjoint (L.map e) D)
    (hsize : ((L.map e) ∪ D).card = Q.card)
    (hcopy : ∀ x ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ Q, Gp.Adj (e x) (e y) ↔ G.Adj x y)
    (hcomplete : ∀ z ∈ D, ∀ y ∈ Q, Gp.Adj z (e y))
    (hreg : LowerSuperRegularPair G L Q ε d) :
    LowerSuperRegularPair Gp ((L.map e) ∪ D) (Q.map e) η d := by
CompleteRowPadding.name: CompleteRowPadding
CompleteRowPadding.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $M=|L|$, $K=|D|$, and $N=|Q|=M+K$. The budgets give $0<\eta$ and $\varepsilon\leq\eta$. If $d\leq\eta$, all required lower bounds are zero, so assume $\eta<d$. All parameters are then finite.

For tested subsets $S\subseteq e(L)\cup D$ and $T\subseteq e(Q)$, write $S=e(S_0)\cup S_D$ disjointly and $T=e(T_0)$, with $S_0\subseteq L$, $S_D\subseteq D$, and $T_0\subseteq Q$. Their thresholds are $|S|>\eta N$ and $|T_0|>\eta N$, so both cardinalities are positive. Exact adjacency and complete dummy rows give the edge count
$E_{F^+}(S,T)=E_F(S_0,T_0)+|S_D||T_0|$.
If $|S_0|>\varepsilon M$, the right threshold also exceeds $\varepsilon N$. The lower-regularity clause of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}, expressed by \noderef{LowerRegularPair} and \noderef{PairDensity}, gives $E_F(S_0,T_0)\geq(d-\varepsilon)|S_0||T_0|$. As $d-\eta\leq d-\varepsilon$ and $d-\eta\leq1$, the displayed edge count is at least $(d-\eta)|S||T_0|$.
Otherwise $|S_0|\leq\varepsilon M\leq\varepsilon N\leq\eta^2N<\eta|S|$. Consequently $|S_D|\geq(1-\eta)|S|\geq(d-\eta)|S|$, and the complete rows alone give the same bound. Divide by the positive finite rectangle cardinality to obtain lower regularity. Empty parts admit no tested rectangle and require no division.

For an old left vertex its degree is unchanged and at least $(d-\varepsilon)N\geq(d-\eta)N$; a dummy has degree $N$. A right vertex has its old degree plus $K$, at least $(d-\varepsilon)M+K\geq(d-\eta)(M+K)$, because the difference is $(\eta-\varepsilon)M+(1-d+\eta)K\geq0$. These are exactly the two degree clauses of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}.
\end{proof}
CompleteRowPadding.title: CompleteRowPadding

def CrossEdgeRetention {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (L R : Finset V) (ω : V × V → Bool) : SimpleGraph V :=
CrossEdgeRetention.name: CrossEdgeRetention
CrossEdgeRetention.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Spanning cross-edge retention]
Given $G,L,R$ and $\omega:V\times V\to\{0,1\}$, define $G_\omega$ on
the original vertex set $V$ by
\[
vw\in E(G_\omega)\iff vw\in E(G)\text{ and }
\bigl((v\in L,w\in R,\omega_{(v,w)}=1)
\text{ or }(w\in L,v\in R,\omega_{(w,v)}=1)\bigr).
\]
The adjacency relation is symmetric and irreflexive. When the parts are
disjoint, this retains each undirected cross edge using its unique
$L$-to-$R$ coordinate and deletes every other edge.
\end{definition}
CrossEdgeRetention.title: CrossEdgeRetention

    simp [CrossEdgeRetention, hv, hw, hwL]

    unfold IndependentRetentionCount
    apply congrArg Finset.card

    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨hpU, hpW⟩, hp⟩
      exact ⟨⟨⟨hpU, hpW⟩, (ha _ _ (hU hpU) (hW hpW)).mp hp |>.1⟩,
        (ha _ _ (hU hpU) (hW hpW)).mp hp |>.2⟩

  · intro v hv
    unfold IndependentRetentionCount
    rw [Finset.filter_filter]
    have he : ((({v} : Finset V).product R).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2 ∧ ω p = true) =
        ({v} : Finset V).product (R.filter fun w => (CrossEdgeRetention G L R ω).Adj v w) := by
      ext p
      simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨rfl, hw⟩, hp⟩

      · rintro ⟨rfl, hw, hp⟩

    simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.card_product, Finset.card_singleton, one_mul]

        (L.filter fun v => (CrossEdgeRetention G L R ω).Adj v w).product {w} := by
      ext p
      simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨hv, rfl⟩, hp⟩
        exact ⟨⟨hv, (ha _ _ hv hw).mpr hp⟩, rfl⟩
      · rintro ⟨⟨hv, hp⟩, rfl⟩
        exact ⟨⟨hv, rfl⟩, (ha _ _ hv hw).mp hp⟩

open scoped Classical

theorem CrossEdgeRetentionCounts {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (L R : Finset V)
    (hLR : Disjoint L R) (ω : V × V → Bool) :
    CrossEdgeRetention G L R ω ≤ G ∧
    (∀ (U : Finset V), U ⊆ L → ∀ (W : Finset V), W ⊆ R →
      (((U.product W).filter fun p => (CrossEdgeRetention G L R ω).Adj p.1 p.2).card) =
        IndependentRetentionCount ((U.product W).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2) ω) ∧
    (∀ v ∈ L,
      (R.filter fun w => (CrossEdgeRetention G L R ω).Adj v w).card =
        IndependentRetentionCount ((({v} : Finset V).product R).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2) ω) ∧
    (∀ w ∈ R,
      (L.filter fun v => (CrossEdgeRetention G L R ω).Adj v w).card =
        IndependentRetentionCount ((L.product {w}).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2) ω) := by
CrossEdgeRetentionCounts.name: CrossEdgeRetentionCounts
CrossEdgeRetentionCounts.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Every retained adjacency includes an original adjacency, proving containment
by \noderef{CrossEdgeRetention}. If $u\in L,w\in R$, disjointness gives
$w\notin L$. The reversed alternative in that definition is therefore
impossible, and retained adjacency is exactly original adjacency together
with $\omega_{(u,w)}=1$. Thus the ordered-edge set on $U\times W$ is
precisely the original ordered-edge set filtered by this coordinate test.
Its cardinality is $K_{A(U,W)}$ by \noderef{IndependentRetentionCount}.
For a left vertex, $w\mapsto(v,w)$ is a bijection between retained
neighbors and retained coordinates in $A(\{v\},R)$. For a right vertex,
$v\mapsto(v,w)$ is the analogous bijection, using symmetry of adjacency.
These bijections prove the two degree identities, without identifying the
sizes of the two parts.
\end{proof}
CrossEdgeRetentionCounts.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Exact counts on the common retention sample]
Let $L,R$ be disjoint parts of $G$, and let $G_\omega$ be the graph of
\noderef{CrossEdgeRetention}. Then $G_\omega\subseteq G$.
Writing $A(U,W)=\{(u,w)\in U\times W:uw\in E(G)\}$ and using the
count of \noderef{IndependentRetentionCount}, for every $U\subseteq L$,
$W\subseteq R$ we have
\[
e_{G_\omega}(U,W)=K_{A(U,W)}(\omega).
\]
For every $v\in L$ and $w\in R$ the two degree identities are
\[
\deg_{G_\omega}(v;R)=K_{A(\{v\},R)}(\omega),\qquad
\deg_{G_\omega}(w;L)=K_{A(L,\{w\})}(\omega).
\]
\end{lemma}

theorem CrossPairSubgraphAssembly {V I : Type*}
    [Fintype V] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq I]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (R : SimpleGraph I)
    (f : V → I) (η c : ENNReal)
    (hpair : ∀ p q, R.Adj p q →
      ∃ F : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
        F ≤ G ∧
        (∀ ⦃u v⦄, F.Adj u v →
          (f u = p ∧ f v = q) ∨ (f u = q ∧ f v = p)) ∧
        SuperRegularPair F (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p)

    ∃ G' : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G'.Adj,
      G' ≤ G ∧
      (∀ ⦃u v⦄, G'.Adj u v → R.Adj (f u) (f v)) ∧
      (∀ p q, R.Adj p q →
        SuperRegularPair G' (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p)
          (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = q) η c) := by

CrossPairSubgraphAssembly.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Choose a linear ordering of the finite index type, for example by
an enumeration, and for every unordered edge $\{p,q\}$ select just
one of the supplied graphs, using the orientation $p<q$.
Let $G'$ be the union of their edge relations. Each selected relation
is symmetric and irreflexive; so is their union. Each relation is
contained in $G$, and each of its edges has endpoint fibers equal
to its selected index pair. Hence $G'\subseteq G$ and its edges
project to edges of $R$.

For a fixed edge $pq$ and vertices $u\in f^{-1}(p)$,
$v\in f^{-1}(q)$, any selected graph contributing the edge $uv$
must have unordered index pair exactly $\{p,q\}$: this follows
from its crossing support and uniqueness of the values $f(u),f(v)$.
Conversely the selected graph for this pair contributes all its
edges to $G'$. Thus on this pair the assembled graph agrees
exactly with that one selected graph. In particular every opposite
degree count and every subset ordered-edge count is identical;
so are the densities by \noderef{PairDensity}. Transfer along this
agreement using \noderef{SuperRegularPairEmbedding}, with the identity
map on the vertex type, the selected graph as source, and $G'$ as target.
The identity is injective, its images of the two finite fibers are
the fibers themselves, and the crossing-edge equivalence just proved
is exactly the embedding's adjacency hypothesis. The parameters
$\eta,c$ are unchanged. If the tested
orientation is the one selected, the supplied
\noderef{SuperRegularPair} assertion applies directly. In the other
orientation its two degree clauses exchange places, and the
regularity assertion exchanges the two subset variables. Their
densities are equal, because coordinate swap is a bijection of
the corresponding ordered-edge sets. Thus the same assertion holds
in both orientations. Empty fiber tests and truncated or infinite
scalar endpoints cause no additional issue: agreement is equality
of the counts, not an estimate or real-number conversion.
\end{proof}
CrossPairSubgraphAssembly.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Assembly of contained crossing subgraphs]
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, $R$ a simple graph on a finite index
type, and $f$ assign each vertex of $G$ an index. Suppose for every
ordered edge $pq$ of $R$ there is a graph $F\subseteq G$, with
edges only crossing the fibers of $p,q$, which is
$(\eta,c)$-super-regular on those fibers. There is a graph
$G'\subseteq G$ on the original vertex type, supported only on
$R$-edges between fibers, whose pair on every edge of $R$ is
$(\eta,c)$-super-regular.
\end{lemma}
CrossPairSubgraphAssembly.title: CrossPairSubgraphAssembly

classical
  -- Relabelling preserves every rectangle and both neighbourhood cardinalities.
  have relabel : ∀ {A B : Type _} [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B]
      (G : SimpleGraph A) (D : SimpleGraph B)
      [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel D.Adj]
      (L R : Finset A) (L' R' : Finset B) (f : A → B) (e d : ENNReal),
      Set.InjOn f L → Set.InjOn f R → L.image f = L' → R.image f = R' →
      (∀ x ∈ L, ∀ z ∈ R, G.Adj x z ↔ D.Adj (f x) (f z)) →
      SuperRegularPair G L R e d → SuperRegularPair D L' R' e d := by
    intro A B _ _ G D _ _ L R L' R' f e d injL injR imageL imageR adj hG
    have cardL : L'.card = L.card := by
      rw [← imageL]
      exact Finset.card_image_iff.mpr injL
    have cardR : R'.card = R.card := by
      rw [← imageR]
      exact Finset.card_image_iff.mpr injR
    have pull : ∀ (P Q : Finset A) (X : Finset B),
        Q = P.filter (fun x => f x ∈ X) → X ⊆ P.image f → Q.image f = X := by
      intro P Q X hQ hX
      subst Q
      ext x
      simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨y, ⟨_, hx⟩, rfl⟩
        exact hx
      · intro hx
        obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp (hX hx)
        exact ⟨y, ⟨hy, hx⟩, rfl⟩
    have edges : ∀ X ⊆ L, ∀ Y ⊆ R,
        ((X.product Y).filter fun q => G.Adj q.1 q.2).card =
        (((X.image f).product (Y.image f)).filter fun q => D.Adj q.1 q.2).card := by
      intro X hX Y hY
      apply Finset.card_bij (fun q _ => (f q.1, f q.2))
      · intro q hq
        obtain ⟨hq, ha⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hq
        obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hq
        exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr
          ⟨Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨q.1, hx, rfl⟩,
           Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨q.2, hy, rfl⟩⟩,
          (adj _ (hX hx) _ (hY hy)).mp ha⟩
      · intro q hq r hr he
        have hq' := Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).1
        have hr' := Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hr).1
        exact Prod.ext (injL (hX hq'.1) (hX hr'.1) (congrArg Prod.fst he))
          (injR (hY hq'.2) (hY hr'.2) (congrArg Prod.snd he))
      · intro q hq
        obtain ⟨hq, ha⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hq
        obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hq
        obtain ⟨x, hx, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
        obtain ⟨y, hy, hf⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hy
        refine ⟨(x, y), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hx, hy⟩, ?_⟩,

        (a : A → Prop) (b : B → Prop) [DecidablePred a] [DecidablePred b],

        (P.filter a).card = ((P.image f).filter b).card := by
      intro P hinj a b _ _ hab
      apply Finset.card_bij (fun x _ => f x)
      · intro x hx
        obtain ⟨hx, ha⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hx
        exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr
          ⟨Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, (hab x hx).mp ha⟩
      · intro x hx y hy he
        exact hinj (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).1 (Finset.mem_filter.mp hy).1 he
      · intro y hy
        obtain ⟨hy, hb⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hy
        obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hy
        exact ⟨x, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hx, (hab x hx).mpr hb⟩, rfl⟩
    rcases hG with ⟨hr, hl, hh⟩
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro X hX Y hY hx hy
      let X0 := L.filter (fun x => f x ∈ X)
      let Y0 := R.filter (fun y => f y ∈ Y)
      have hX0 : X0 ⊆ L := Finset.filter_subset _ _
      have hY0 : Y0 ⊆ R := Finset.filter_subset _ _
      have imX : X0.image f = X := pull L X0 X rfl (by simpa only [imageL] using hX)
      have imY : Y0.image f = Y := pull R Y0 Y rfl (by simpa only [imageR] using hY)
      have cx : X.card = X0.card := by
        rw [← imX]
        exact Finset.card_image_iff.mpr (injL.mono hX0)
      have cy : Y.card = Y0.card := by
        rw [← imY]
        exact Finset.card_image_iff.mpr (injR.mono hY0)
      have density : PairDensity G X0 Y0 = PairDensity D X Y := by
        unfold PairDensity
        rw [edges X0 hX0 Y0 hY0, imX, imY, cx, cy]

      rw [cardR, cy] at hy
      simpa only [density] using hr X0 hX0 Y0 hY0 hx hy
    · intro x hx
      rw [← imageL] at hx
      obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
      have hc := counts R injR (fun z => G.Adj u z) (fun z => D.Adj (f u) z)

      simpa only [cardR, ← hc] using hl u hu
    · intro z hz
      rw [← imageR] at hz
      obtain ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
      have hc := counts L injL (fun x => G.Adj x w) (fun x => D.Adj x (f w))
        (fun x hx => adj x hx w hw)
      rw [imageL] at hc
      simpa only [cardL, ← hc] using hh w hw
  let U0 := U.erase u0
  have hU0 : U0.card = n := by
    simp only [U0, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hu0, hU, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
  have hU0Z : Disjoint U0 Z := hUZ.mono_left (Finset.erase_subset _ _)
  have hu0Z : u0 ∉ Z := Finset.disjoint_left.mp hUZ hu0
  let G : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun x z =>
    ∃ v : V, ∃ w : Z, x = tau v ∧ z = w ∧ W.Adj v w
  letI : DecidableRel G.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adjG : ∀ v : V, ∀ z : Z, G.Adj (tau v) z ↔ W.Adj v z := by
    intro v z
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, hh | hh⟩
      · obtain ⟨v', w, hv, hw, ha⟩ := hh
        have he : v = v' := tau.injective (Subtype.ext hv)
        have hz : z = w := Subtype.ext hw
        simpa only [he, hz] using ha
      · obtain ⟨v', w, hv, hw, _⟩ := hh
        exact False.elim (Finset.disjoint_left.mp hU0Z (tau v').property (hv ▸ z.property))
    · intro ha
      refine ⟨?_, Or.inl ⟨v, z, rfl, rfl, ha⟩⟩
      intro he
      exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp hU0Z (tau v).property (he ▸ z.property)
  let f : S ⊕ T → S ⊕ T := fun x => if hx : x ∈ V then tau ⟨x, hx⟩ else x
  have fe : ∀ v : V, f v = tau v := by intro v; simp [f, v.property]
  have fz : ∀ z ∈ Z, f z = z := by
    intro z hz
    have hv : z ∉ V := fun hv => Finset.disjoint_left.mp hVZ hv hz
    simp only [f, dif_neg hv]
  have injV : Set.InjOn f V := by
    intro x hx y hy he
    have hh : tau ⟨x, hx⟩ = tau ⟨y, hy⟩ := Subtype.ext
      (by simpa only [← fe ⟨x, hx⟩, ← fe ⟨y, hy⟩] using he)

  have injZ : Set.InjOn f Z := by
    intro x hx y hy he
    simpa only [fz x hx, fz y hy] using he
  have imV : V.image f = U0 := by
    ext x
    constructor
    · intro hx
      obtain ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
      rw [fe ⟨v, hv⟩]
      exact (tau ⟨v, hv⟩).property
    · intro hx
      obtain ⟨v, he⟩ := tau.surjective ⟨x, hx⟩
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨v, v.property, (fe v).trans (congrArg Subtype.val he)⟩

    ext z
    constructor
    · intro hz
      obtain ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz

    rw [hZ]

    rw [hZ]
    have hh : (k : ENNReal) ≤ (n : ENNReal) :=

  letI : DecidableRel D.Adj := Classical.decRel _

    intro x z hxz
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj] at hxz ⊢
    exact ⟨hxz.1, hxz.2.elim (fun hh => Or.inl (Or.inl hh))
      (fun hh => Or.inr (Or.inl hh))⟩
  have rowD : ∀ z ∈ Z, D.Adj u0 z ↔ z ∈ N := by
    intro z hz
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]

    have he : (Z.filter fun z => D.Adj u0 z) = N := by
      ext z

        fun hz => ⟨hNZ hz, (rowD z (hNZ hz)).mpr hz⟩⟩
    rw [he, hNk]
  obtain ⟨N', F, _, _, _, _, _, haway, hF⟩ :=
    FutureExtraVertexStability n k xi eta p hn hxi heta hp hinner hinnerReg G D U0 Z u0
      hU0Z (Finset.notMem_erase _ _) hu0Z hU0 (Or.inl hZ) hGD
      (by rw [rowCount]) hkLower hkUpper hG
  letI : DecidableRel F.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adjF : ∀ v : V, ∀ z : Z, F.Adj (tau v) z ↔ W.Adj v z := by
    intro v z
    exact (haway _ _ (Finset.mem_erase.mp (tau v).property).1
      (fun he => hu0Z (he ▸ z.property))).trans (adjG v z)
  refine ⟨F, ?_, adjF, ?_⟩
  · simpa only [U0, Finset.insert_erase hu0] using hF
  intro sigma hsigma
  dsimp only
  intro hI
  let I := @MatchingInducedGraph (S ⊕ T) _ _ F J (Classical.decRel _) _ U K Z sigma
  letI : DecidableRel I.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  let L : Finset (U ⊕ Z) := Finset.univ.image Sum.inl
  let R : Finset (U ⊕ Z) := Finset.univ.image Sum.inr
  let a : U := ⟨u0, hu0⟩
  let L0 := L.erase (Sum.inl a)
  have disjLR : Disjoint L R := by
    apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro q hq hr
    obtain ⟨u, _, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hq
    obtain ⟨z, _, hf⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hr
    exact Sum.inl_ne_inr (he.trans hf.symm)
  have haL : Sum.inl a ∈ L := by simp [L]
  have cardL : L.card = n + 1 := by
    rw [Finset.card_image_iff.mpr (by intro x _ y _ he; exact Sum.inl.inj he)]
    simpa only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_coe] using hU
  have cardR : R.card = n := by
    rw [Finset.card_image_iff.mpr (by intro x _ y _ he; exact Sum.inr.inj he)]
    simpa only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_coe] using hZ
  have hdeleted : SuperRegularPair I L0 R eps (p * h) :=
    MatchingInducedLeftRowDeletion n omega eps (p * h) hn homega heps hph
      houter houterReg I L R (Sum.inl a) disjLR haL cardL (Or.inl cardR) hI
  let up : U0 → U := fun u => ⟨u, Finset.mem_of_mem_erase u.property⟩
  have left : ∀ q ∈ L0, ∃ u : U0, q = Sum.inl (up u) := by
    intro q hq
    obtain ⟨hne, hq⟩ := Finset.mem_erase.mp hq
    obtain ⟨u, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hq
    have hu : (u : S ⊕ T) ≠ u0 := by
      intro he
      exact hne (congrArg Sum.inl (Subtype.ext he))
    exact ⟨⟨u, Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hu, u.property⟩⟩, rfl⟩
  have inLeft : ∀ u : U0, Sum.inl (up u) ∈ L0 := by
    intro u
    apply Finset.mem_erase.mpr
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · intro he
      exact (Finset.mem_erase.mp u.property).1 (congrArg Subtype.val (Sum.inl.inj he))
    · simp [L]
  have right : ∀ q ∈ R, ∃ z : Z, q = Sum.inr z := by
    intro q hq
    obtain ⟨z, _, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hq
    exact ⟨z, he.symm⟩
  let Wnew : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v z =>
    ∃ u : U0, ∃ w : Z, v = tau.symm u ∧ z = w ∧
      F.Adj u w ∧ J.Adj (sigma (up u)) w
  letI : DecidableRel Wnew.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adjNew : ∀ u : U0, ∀ z : Z,
      Wnew.Adj (tau.symm u) z ↔ F.Adj u z ∧ J.Adj (sigma (up u)) z := by
    intro u z
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, hh | hh⟩
      · obtain ⟨u', w, hu, hw, ha⟩ := hh
        have he : u = u' := tau.symm.injective (Subtype.ext hu)
        have hz : z = w := Subtype.ext hw
        simpa only [he, hz] using ha
      · obtain ⟨u', w, hv, _, _⟩ := hh
        exact False.elim (Finset.disjoint_left.mp hVZ (tau.symm u').property (hv ▸ z.property))
    · intro ha
      refine ⟨?_, Or.inl ⟨u, z, rfl, rfl, ha⟩⟩
      intro he
      exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp hVZ (tau.symm u).property (he ▸ z.property)
  let g : U ⊕ Z → S ⊕ T := Sum.elim
    (fun u => if hu : (u : S ⊕ T) ∈ U0 then tau.symm ⟨u, hu⟩ else u) Subtype.val
  have gu : ∀ u : U0, g (Sum.inl (up u)) = tau.symm u := by
    intro u
    simp only [g, Sum.elim_inl, up, u.property, dif_pos]
    apply congrArg (fun u : U0 => (tau.symm u).val)
    exact Subtype.ext rfl
  have gz : ∀ z : Z, g (Sum.inr z) = z := by intro z; rfl
  have injL0 : Set.InjOn g L0 := by
    intro q hq r hr he
    obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := left q hq
    obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := left r hr
    have huv : u = v := tau.symm.injective (Subtype.ext (by simpa only [gu] using he))
    exact congrArg (fun u => Sum.inl (up u)) huv
  have injR : Set.InjOn g R := by
    intro q hq r hr he
    obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := right q hq
    obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := right r hr
    exact congrArg Sum.inr (Subtype.ext he)
  have imageL0 : L0.image g = V := by
    ext v
    constructor
    · intro hv
      obtain ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hv
      obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := left q hq
      rw [gu]
      exact (tau.symm u).property
    · intro hv
      obtain ⟨u, he⟩ := tau.symm.surjective ⟨v, hv⟩
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨Sum.inl (up u), inLeft u,
        (gu u).trans (congrArg Subtype.val he)⟩
  have imageR : R.image g = Z := by
    ext z
    constructor
    · intro hz
      obtain ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
      obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := right q hq
      exact w.property
    · intro hz
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨Sum.inr ⟨z, hz⟩, by simp [R], rfl⟩
  have adjI : ∀ u : U, ∀ z : Z,
      I.Adj (Sum.inl u) (Sum.inr z) ↔ F.Adj u z ∧ J.Adj (sigma u) z := by
    intro u z
    simp only [I, MatchingInducedGraph, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj,
      Sum.inl_ne_inr, Sum.inr_ne_inl, Sum.inl.injEq, Sum.inr.injEq,
      false_and, exists_false, or_false]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, x, w, rfl, rfl, ha⟩
      exact ha
    · intro ha
      refine ⟨?_, u, z, rfl, rfl, ha⟩
      intro he
      cases he
  have hnew : SuperRegularPair Wnew V Z eps (p * h) := by
    apply relabel I Wnew L0 R V Z g eps (p * h) injL0 injR imageL0 imageR
    · intro q hq r hr
      obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := left q hq
      obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := right r hr
      rw [gu, gz, adjNew, adjI]
    · exact hdeleted
  refine ⟨Wnew, ?_, hnew⟩
  intro v z hvz
  rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj] at hvz ⊢
  refine ⟨hvz.1, ?_⟩
  have forward : ∀ v z : S ⊕ T,
      (∃ u : U0, ∃ w : Z, v = tau.symm u ∧ z = w ∧
        F.Adj u w ∧ J.Adj (sigma (up u)) w) →
      v ∈ V ∧ z ∈ Z ∧ O.Adj v z ∧
        ∀ x : U, M.Adj x v → H.Adj (sigma x) z := by
    rintro v z ⟨u, w, rfl, rfl, hfu, hju⟩
    have genuine : W.Adj (tau.symm u) w := by
      apply (adjF (tau.symm u) w).mp
      simpa only [tau.apply_symm_apply] using hfu
    refine ⟨(tau.symm u).property, w.property, hWO genuine, ?_⟩
    intro x hm
    have he : x = up u := Subtype.ext (by
      simpa only [tau.apply_symm_apply] using (hM x (tau.symm u)).mp hm)
    simpa only [he] using hJH hju
  exact hvz.2.elim (fun hh => Or.inl (forward v z hh))
    (fun hh => Or.inr (forward z v hh))
CurrentExtraSourceWitnessTransport.lean_statement:
theorem CurrentExtraSourceWitnessTransport
    {S T : Type*} [Fintype S] [Fintype T] [DecidableEq S] [DecidableEq T]
    (U K V Z : Finset (S ⊕ T)) (n : ℕ) (u0 : S ⊕ T)
    (M O W J H : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T))
    [DecidableRel W.Adj] [DecidableRel J.Adj]
    (tau : V ≃ (U.erase u0)) (xi eta omega eps p h : ENNReal)
    (hUK : Disjoint U K) (hUZ : Disjoint U Z) (hKZ : Disjoint K Z)
    (hVZ : Disjoint V Z) (hu0 : u0 ∈ U)
    (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hU : U.card = n + 1) (hK : K.card = n + 1)
    (hV : V.card = n) (hZ : Z.card = n)
    (hM : ∀ u : U, ∀ v : V, M.Adj u v ↔ (u : S ⊕ T) = tau v)
    (hWO : W ≤ O) (hJH : J ≤ H)
    (hp : p ≤ 1) (hph : p * h ≤ 1)
    (hxi : xi < eta) (heta : eta ≤ 1) (hinteger : (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ xi)
    (hinner : xi + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ eta)
    (hinnerReg : xi + 1 / (eta * (n : ENNReal)) ≤ eta)
    (homega : omega < eps) (heps : eps ≤ 1)
    (houter : omega + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ eps)
    (houterReg : omega + 1 / (eps * (n : ENNReal)) ≤ eps)
    (hW : SuperRegularPair W V Z xi p) :
    ∃ F : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T),
      @SuperRegularPair (S ⊕ T) _ F (Classical.decRel _) U Z eta p ∧
      (∀ v : V, ∀ z : Z, F.Adj (tau v) z ↔ W.Adj v z) ∧
      (∀ sigma : U → K, Function.Bijective sigma →
        let I := @MatchingInducedGraph (S ⊕ T) _ _ F J (Classical.decRel _) _ U K Z sigma
        let L := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inl : U → U ⊕ Z)
        let R := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inr : Z → U ⊕ Z)
        @SuperRegularPair (U ⊕ Z) _ I (Classical.decRel _) L R omega (p * h) →
        let Anew := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v z =>
          v ∈ V ∧ z ∈ Z ∧ O.Adj v z ∧
            ∀ u : U, M.Adj u v → H.Adj (sigma u) z
        ∃ Wnew : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T), Wnew ≤ Anew ∧
          @SuperRegularPair (S ⊕ T) _ Wnew (Classical.decRel _) V Z eps (p * h)) := by
