CurrentExtraSourceWitnessTransport.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Pull $W[V,Z]$ back to $U\setminus\{u_0\},Z$ using $\tau^{-1}$ and
restrict the pulled-back graph to these two parts. The bijection preserves
degrees, rectangle cardinalities, and edge counts, so the pair is still
$(\xi,p)$-super-regular by \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.
Put $\ell=\lfloor pn\rfloor$. Since $0\le p\le1$ and $n\ge1$,
$0\le\ell\le n$. Moreover $pn-1<\ell\le pn$ and
$\eta n\ge\xi n\ge1$, so
$(p-\eta)n\le\ell\le(p+\eta)n$.
Choose an $\ell$-subset $N$ of $Z$ and form an auxiliary ambient graph
by adjoining the row $u_0N$ to the pulled-back graph, with no other
edges incident to $u_0$. The old graph is contained in this auxiliary
ambient graph and the available row has exactly $\ell$ vertices.
Apply \noderef{FutureExtraVertexStability} with residual size $n$,
row size $\ell$, errors $\xi,\eta$, density $p$, and that auxiliary
ambient graph. Its row-degree inequalities are those just proved; its
two slack hypotheses and unit bounds are displayed assumptions.
It produces the desired $F$. The unchanged-edge conclusion preserves
all genuine pulled-back rows. This construction gives no source image
for $u_0$; its row is artificial.

Fix $\sigma$ and a successful induced graph. Its left part has $n+1$
vertices, its right part has $n$, and its artificial left vertex is the
subtype copy of $u_0$. Apply
\noderef{MatchingInducedLeftRowDeletion} with errors $\omega,e$ and
density $ph$; all its degree, size, unit, and slack hypotheses are exactly
the displayed assumptions. The resulting graph on the residual left
part and the full right part is $(e,ph)$-super-regular.
Restrict $\sigma$ to the residual left part and restrict its host part
to $K\setminus\{\sigma(u_0)\}$. Bijectivity of $\sigma$ makes this
restriction a bijection: injectivity forbids another preimage of
$\sigma(u_0)$, and surjectivity supplies the unique preimage of every
other host vertex. The restricted matching-induced graph is exactly the
deleted graph, after relabelling its subtype copies.

Define $W_{\rm new}$ to have the edges $vz$ with
$\tau(v)z\in F$ and $\sigma(\tau(v))z\in J$, and their reverses.
Using the residual source bijection $\tau^{-1}$, apply
\noderef{MatchingInducedUpdatedCandidacyTransport} to the restricted
matching and this target graph. The complete bipartite graph on the
residual source and host parts makes that bijection a perfect matching
as defined in \noderef{PerfectMatching}. The target adjacency
equivalence is definitional. The two exact-image equivalences are
$v\in V\Longleftrightarrow\exists u\in U\setminus\{u_0\},
v=\tau^{-1}(u)$ and the identity equivalence on $Z$.
Thus $W_{\rm new}[V,Z]$ is $(e,ph)$-super-regular.
For each of its edges the genuine-row identity and $W\subseteq O$
give $vz\in O$, while $J\subseteq H$ gives the constraint from
$\tau(v)$. The source-matching equivalence says this is the only
constraint from $U$. Hence $W_{\rm new}\subseteq T_\sigma$.
The artificial row was deleted and is neither transported nor restored.
\end{proof}
CurrentExtraSourceWitnessTransport.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Artificial current row, deletion, and contained transport]
Let $U,K,V,Z$ lie in a finite disjoint-union ambient set, with
$U\cap K=U\cap Z=K\cap Z=V\cap Z=\varnothing$,
$|U|=|K|=n+1$, $|V|=|Z|=n$, and $n\ge1$. Let $u_0\in U$ and let
$\tau:V\to U\setminus\{u_0\}$ be a bijection such that
$uv\in M\Longleftrightarrow u=\tau(v)$ on $U\times V$.
Assume $W\subseteq O$, $J\subseteq H$, and $W[V,Z]$ is
$(\xi,p)$-super-regular. Suppose $p\le1$, $ph\le1$, and
\[
1/n\le\xi<\eta\le1,\quad
\xi+2/n\le\eta,\quad \xi+1/(\eta n)\le\eta,
\]
\[
\omega<e\le1,\quad \omega+2/n\le e,\quad
\omega+1/(en)\le e.
\]
There is an $(\eta,p)$-super-regular graph $F[U,Z]$ with
$\tau(v)z\in F\Longleftrightarrow vz\in W$ on $V\times Z$.
For every bijection $\sigma:U\to K$, if the matching-induced graph on
subtype copies of $U,Z$, with edges $uz\in F$ and $\sigma(u)z\in J$,
is $(\omega,ph)$-super-regular, the graph
\[
T_\sigma:\quad vz\in E(T_\sigma)\Longleftrightarrow
v\in V,\ z\in Z,\ vz\in O,\quad
\forall u\in U\ (uv\in M\Rightarrow\sigma(u)z\in H),
\]
symmetrized as a simple graph, contains a spanning
$(e,ph)$-super-regular graph on $V,Z$.
\end{lemma}

classical
  intro V _ _ G _ U W n δ p η hn hk _ hη hδp hp hδn hhier hbad
  have hpfin : p ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hp
  have hδfin : δ ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top hpfin hδp
  have hηfin : η ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hη
  have hnNat : 0 < n := by
    by_contra h
    have : n = 0 := by omega
    simp [this] at hδn
  have hnpos : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hnNat
  have hδpR : δ.toReal ≤ p.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_mono hpfin hδp
  have hpR : p.toReal ≤ 1 := by simpa using ENNReal.toReal_mono ENNReal.one_ne_top hp
  have hδnR : 1 ≤ δ.toReal * (n : ℝ) := by
    simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_one, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
      using ENNReal.toReal_mono (ENNReal.mul_ne_top hδfin (by simp)) hδn
  have hhierR : 20 * δ.toReal ≤ η.toReal ^ 5 := by
    simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_pow]
      using ENNReal.toReal_mono (ENNReal.pow_ne_top hηfin) hhier
  have hδpos : 0 < δ.toReal := by
    nlinarith only [hδnR, hnpos, ENNReal.toReal_nonneg (a := δ)]
  have hηpos : 0 < η.toReal := by
    by_contra h
    have : η.toReal = 0 := le_antisymm (not_lt.mp h) ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
    rw [this] at hhierR
    norm_num at hhierR
    linarith only [hhierR, hδpos]
  let bad := (W ×ˢ W).filter fun z =>
    ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * n ∨
    ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.2).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * n ∨
    (p + δ) ^ 2 * n < ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1 ∧ G.Adj u z.2).card : ENNReal)
  have hbadR : (bad.card : ℝ) ≤ 5 * δ.toReal * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    simpa only [bad, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat,
      ENNReal.toReal_natCast, ENNReal.toReal_pow] using
      ENNReal.toReal_mono (by finiteness) hbad
  -- Each low-degree vertex contributes a full row of exceptional ordered pairs.
  let L := W.filter fun w => ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u w).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * n
  have hrows : L ×ˢ W ⊆ bad := by
    intro z hz
    rcases Finset.mem_product.mp hz with ⟨hz1, hz2⟩
    rcases Finset.mem_filter.mp hz1 with ⟨hzW, hzlow⟩
    exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hzW, hz2⟩, Or.inl hzlow⟩
  have hLsmall : (L.card : ℝ) ≤ 5 * δ.toReal * n := by
    have hcount := Finset.card_le_card hrows
    rw [Finset.card_product, hk] at hcount
    have hcountR : (L.card : ℝ) * n ≤ (bad.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hcount
    nlinarith only [hcountR, hbadR, hnpos]
  intro U' hU' W' hW' hUlarge hWlarge
  have hUlargeR : η.toReal * (n : ℝ) < U'.card := by
    simpa only [hn, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using
      (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mpr hUlarge
  have hWlargeR : η.toReal * (n : ℝ) < W'.card := by
    simpa only [hk, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using
      (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mpr hWlarge
  have hqpos : (0 : ℝ) < W'.card := lt_trans (mul_pos hηpos hnpos) hWlargeR
  have hU'pos : (0 : ℝ) < U'.card := lt_trans (mul_pos hηpos hnpos) hUlargeR
  have hqn : (W'.card : ℝ) ≤ U.card := by
    have hc := Finset.card_le_card hW'
    rw [hk] at hc
    rw [hn]
    exact_mod_cast hc
  let d : V → ℝ := fun u => (W'.filter fun w => G.Adj u w).card
  let r : V → ℝ := fun w => (U.filter fun u => G.Adj u w).card
  let c : V × V → ℝ := fun z => (U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1 ∧ G.Adj u z.2).card
  have hfirstCount : (∑ u ∈ U, d u) = ∑ w ∈ W', r w := by
    simp only [d, r, Finset.card_eq_sum_ones, Nat.cast_sum,
      Finset.sum_filter, Nat.cast_ite, Nat.cast_one, Nat.cast_zero]
    exact Finset.sum_comm
  have hgoodDegree : ∀ w ∈ W' \ L, (p.toReal - δ.toReal) * (n : ℝ) ≤ r w := by
    intro w hw
    have hwlow : ¬ ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u w).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * n := by
      intro h
      exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).2 (Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨hW' (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).1, h⟩)
    have := ENNReal.toReal_mono (by simp) (le_of_not_gt hwlow)
    simpa only [r, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le hδp hpfin,
      ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using this
  -- This signed lower bound is valid even when the cardinality surrogate is negative.
  have hfirst : ((W'.card : ℝ) - 5 * δ.toReal * n) *
      (p.toReal - δ.toReal) * n ≤ ∑ u ∈ U, d u := by
    have hnum : (W'.card : ℝ) - 5 * δ.toReal * n ≤ ((W' \ L).card : ℝ) := by
      have hc : (W'.card : ℝ) ≤ ((W' \ L).card : ℝ) + L.card := by
        exact_mod_cast (Finset.card_le_card_sdiff_add_card (s := W') (t := L))
      linarith only [hc, hLsmall]
    rw [hfirstCount]

      _ ≤ ((W' \ L).card : ℝ) * ((p.toReal - δ.toReal) * n) := by
        simpa only [mul_assoc] using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hnum
          (mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hδpR) hnpos.le)
      _ = ∑ w ∈ W' \ L, ((p.toReal - δ.toReal) * n) := by simp
      _ ≤ ∑ w ∈ W' \ L, r w := Finset.sum_le_sum hgoodDegree
      _ ≤ ∑ w ∈ W', r w := Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
        Finset.sdiff_subset (fun _ _ _ => Nat.cast_nonneg _)
  have hsecondCount : (∑ u ∈ U, (d u) ^ 2) = ∑ z ∈ W' ×ˢ W', c z := by
    dsimp only [d, c]
    exact_mod_cast OrderedTwoPathCount U W' G.Adj
  have hcommon : ∀ z, c z ≤ (n : ℝ) := by
    intro z
    dsimp only [c]
    exact_mod_cast ((Finset.card_le_card (Finset.filter_subset _ _)).trans_eq hn)
  have hgoodCommon : ∀ z ∈ W' ×ˢ W', z ∉ bad →
      c z ≤ (p.toReal + δ.toReal) ^ 2 * n := by
    intro z hz hnot

theorem DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      (U W : Finset V) (n : ℕ) (δ p η : ENNReal),
      U.card = n → W.card = n → Disjoint U W → η ≤ 1 →
      δ ≤ p → p ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ δ * n → 20 * δ ≤ η ^ 5 →
      (((W ×ˢ W).filter fun z =>
          ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * n ∨
          ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.2).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * n ∨
          (p + δ) ^ 2 * n <
            ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1 ∧ G.Adj u z.2).card : ENNReal)).card : ENNReal)
        ≤ 5 * δ * n ^ 2 →
      RegularPair G U W η p := by
DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion.name: DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion
DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Call an ordered pair exceptional when one of the three displayed inequalities fails, and let $E\subseteq W^2$ be the set of exceptional ordered pairs.  Thus $|E|\le5\delta n^2$.  Let
\[
 D=\{w\in W:\deg(w)<(p-\delta)n\},\qquad d=|D|.
\]
Every $w\in D$ makes all $n$ pairs $(w,w')$, $w'\in W$, exceptional.  These rows are disjoint, so $dn\le |E|\le5\delta n^2$.  The hypothesis $1\le\delta n$ implies $n>0$, and hence
\[
 d\le5\delta n.                                                   \tag{1}
\]

Fix $C\subseteq W$, put $c=|C|$, and put $r_u=|N(u)\cap C|$ for $u\in U$.  Expanding the square, double-counting edges using \noderef{FilteredProductRowCount}, and double-counting ordered length-two paths using \noderef{OrderedTwoPathCount} gives the exact identity
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}(r_u-pc)^2
 =\sum_{w,w'\in C}|N(w)\cap N(w')|-2pc\sum_{w\in C}\deg(w)+p^2c^2n. \tag{2}
\]
For every nonexceptional pair in $C^2$ use the assumed codegree bound.  For an exceptional pair use the trivial bound $n$, charging this on top of the same nonnegative baseline.  Since $|E\cap C^2|\le5\delta n^2$, this gives
\[
 \sum_{w,w'\in C}|N(w)\cap N(w')|
 \le c^2(p+\delta)^2n+5\delta n^3.                                \tag{3}
\]
This includes diagonal pairs: a nonexceptional diagonal satisfies the codegree hypothesis, while an exceptional diagonal is included in the exceptional-pair charge.

At most $d$ vertices of $C$ lie in $D$, so the number of vertices of $C\setminus D$ is at least $c-d$. Since $(p-\delta)n\ge0$, summing their degree lower bounds gives
\[
 \sum_{w\in C}\deg(w)\ge(c-d)(p-\delta)n.                         \tag{4}
\]
This remains valid if $c-d<0$, since all degrees are nonnegative.
Insert (3) and (4) into (2), expand $(p+\delta)^2$, and cancel the two positive copies of $p^2c^2n$ against the leading negative term.  This gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{u\in U}(r_u-pc)^2
 &\le 4p\delta c^2n+\delta^2c^2n+5\delta n^3
       +2p^2cdn-2pcd\delta n\\
 &\le 4\delta n^3+\delta n^3+5\delta n^3+10\delta n^3\\
 &\le20\delta n^3.                                                \tag{5}
\end{align*}
Indeed, $c\le n$ and $p\le1$ bound the first term by $4\delta n^3$; $\delta\le p\le1$ bounds the second by $\delta n^3$; and (1), $c\le n$, and $p\le1$ bound $2p^2cdn$ by $10\delta n^3$.  The last term in the first line is nonpositive, so discarding it is valid.  Thus every term in the expansion is accounted for. Equivalently, applying \noderef{BalancedDegreeVarianceBound} to (3) and to the weaker first-moment bound $(c-5\delta n)(p-\delta)n$ obtained from (1) and (4) gives (5).

Now let $A\subseteq U$ and $C\subseteq W$ have $a=|A|>\eta n$ and $c>\eta n$. Cauchy--Schwarz on $A$ bounds the square of the sum by $a\sum_{u\in A}(r_u-pc)^2$. Since the summands are nonnegative and $A\subseteq U$, this square sum is at most the square sum over $U$. Applying (5) gives
\[
 |e(A,C)-pac|=\left|\sum_{u\in A}(r_u-pc)\right|
 \le\sqrt{a\,20\delta n^3}
 \le\sqrt{a\eta^5n^3}\le\eta ac.                                \tag{6}
\]
For the last inequality, square both sides and cancel $\eta^2a$; what remains is $\eta^3n^3\le ac^2$, which follows from $a,c>\eta n$. The edge count in (6) is the row sum by \noderef{FilteredProductRowCount}. Dividing (6) by $ac>0$ gives $p-\eta\le e(A,C)/(ac)\le p+\eta$ for every permitted $A,C$. The parameters are finite since $\delta\le p\le1$ and $\eta\le1$. Thus these real inequalities give the extended-nonnegative density inequalities in \noderef{RegularPair}; if $\eta>p$, the lower bound uses truncated subtraction and is just $0\le e(A,C)/(ac)$. This proves the assertion.
\end{proof}
DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Degree--codegree criterion]
Let $B=(U,W)$ be a balanced bipartite graph with $|U|=|W|=n$.  Let $0<\delta\le p\le1$, $0<\eta\le1$, $\delta n\ge1$, and suppose $\eta^5\ge20\delta$.  If all but at most $5\delta n^2$ ordered pairs $(w,w')\in W^2$ satisfy
\[
 \deg(w),\deg(w')\ge(p-\delta)n,
 \qquad |N(w)\cap N(w')|\le(p+\delta)^2n,
\]
then $(U,W)$ is $(\eta,p)$-regular.
\end{lemma}
DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion.title: DegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion

theorem DirectedReachabilitySimplePath {V : Type*} (R : V → V → Prop)
    {a b : V} (hab : Relation.ReflTransGen R a b) (hne : a ≠ b) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (p : Fin (n + 1) → V),
      0 < n ∧ Function.Injective p ∧ p 0 = a ∧ p (Fin.last n) = b ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, R (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ) := by
DirectedReachabilitySimplePath.name: DirectedReachabilitySimplePath
DirectedReachabilitySimplePath.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
We first show by induction on a finite directed walk that its endpoints
can be joined by a list with no repeated vertices. A length-zero walk
at $b$ gives the singleton list $[b]$. For the induction step, suppose
the first step is from $c$ to $d$, and a repetition-free list from $d$
to $b$ has already been obtained. If $c$ does not occur in that list,
prepend $c$. The new first step is the given directed step, all later
steps are unchanged, and no repetition is introduced. If $c$ occurs,
write the list as a prefix followed by $c$ and a suffix. Discard the
prefix and retain the list starting at that occurrence of $c$.
Its last vertex is still $b$, its steps are original directed steps,
and it remains repetition-free. This completes the induction.
Apply this construction to the walk from $a$ to $b$. Its list is
nonempty and cannot be a singleton, since its endpoints are distinct.
Write its length as $n+1$, with $n>0$, and let $p(i)$ be its vertex
at index $i$. The absence of repetitions gives injectivity, and the
list's first vertex, last vertex, and adjacent-step conditions give
the asserted endpoint and directed-step identities.
\end{proof}
DirectedReachabilitySimplePath.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Removing repetitions from a directed residual walk]
Let $R$ be a directed relation on a type $V$, and let $a\ne b$.
If $b$ is reachable from $a$ by a finite sequence of $R$-steps
(allowing the length-zero sequence), then there exist $n>0$ and an
injective sequence $p:\{0,\ldots,n\}\to V$ with $p(0)=a$,
$p(n)=b$, and $R(p(i),p(i+1))$ for every $0\le i<n$.
No symmetry of $R$ is assumed.
\end{lemma}
DirectedReachabilitySimplePath.title: DirectedReachabilitySimplePath

ElementarySymmetricExtremaStep.name: ElementarySymmetricExtremaStep
ElementarySymmetricExtremaStep.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
If all entries are equal, take $b=a$. Then $c$ is that common entry,
both variances are zero, and both other claims are equalities. In
particular this treats $n=1$ without choosing distinct indices.
Otherwise choose indices $i,j$ attaining the minimum and maximum.
Their values satisfy $a_i<a_j$: otherwise the minimum equals the
maximum and every entry between them is equal, contradicting
nonconstancy. In particular $i\ne j$. Put $m=(a_i+a_j)/2$ and
$b=\operatorname{update}(\operatorname{update}(a,i,m),j,m)$.
The two entries at $i,j$ are $m$, and all other entries are unchanged,
which gives the operation certificate. Put $R=a_j-a_i>0$. By
\noderef{ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging}, $b$ is nonnegative, has the
same sum, its subset product sum does not decrease, and
\[
 \sum_t(b_t-c)^2=V-R^2/2,
 \qquad V=\sum_t(a_t-c)^2.
\]
Summing $a_i\le a_t\le a_j$ and dividing by $n>0$ gives
$a_i\le c\le a_j$. For every $t$ this implies
$-R\le a_t-c\le R$, hence $(a_t-c)^2\le R^2$.
Summing yields $V\le nR^2$. Since $2n>0$, we obtain
$V/(2n)\le R^2/2$. Consequently
\[
 \sum_t(b_t-c)^2=V-R^2/2
 \le V-V/(2n)=\left(1-\frac1{2n}\right)V,
\]
as claimed.
\end{proof}
ElementarySymmetricExtremaStep.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Extrema averaging contracts variance]
Let $n>0$, let $k\ge0$ be an integer, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be
nonnegative real numbers. Write $c=(\sum_t a_t)/n$. There exists a
vector $b$ with the following operation certificate: either $a$ is
constant and $b=a$, or there are distinct indices $i,j$ such that
\[
 a_i\le a_t\le a_j\quad\text{for every }t,\qquad a_i<a_j,
 \qquad
 b=\operatorname{update}(\operatorname{update}(a,i,m),j,m),
 \quad m=(a_i+a_j)/2.
\]
Here $\operatorname{update}(a,i,m)$ replaces entry $i$ by $m$ and
leaves every other entry unchanged. Thus in the nonconstant case $b$
is exactly the vector obtained by averaging a minimum and a maximum
entry. In both cases $b$ is nonnegative, has the same total sum as $a$,
and satisfies
\[
 \sum_{|A|=k}\prod_{t\in A}a_t
 \le \sum_{|A|=k}\prod_{t\in A}b_t,
 \qquad
 \sum_t(b_t-c)^2\le\left(1-\frac1{2n}\right)\sum_t(a_t-c)^2.
\]
The subset sums range over subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
\end{lemma}

open scoped BigOperators Topology

theorem ElementarySymmetricMean (n k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (a : Fin n → ℝ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 ≤ a i) :
    (∑ A ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard k, ∏ i ∈ A, a i) /
      (n.choose k : ℝ) ≤ ((∑ i, a i) / (n : ℝ)) ^ k := by
ElementarySymmetricMean.name: ElementarySymmetricMean
ElementarySymmetricMean.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $e_k(a)$ for the subset sum in the statement and $\bar a$ for the
arithmetic mean. For $k=0$ both sides are one. For $n=1$ both permitted
values of $k$ give equality. Assume $n\ge2$, $k\ge1$.
Holding all entries except two entries $b,c$ fixed, group the subsets
according as they contain neither, one, or both of these entries. This
gives
\[
 e_k(a)=E_k+(b+c)E_{k-1}+bcE_{k-2},
\]
where $E_j$ is the $j$-subset product sum of the other $n-2$ entries,
defined to be zero for $j<0$ or $j>n-2$. Each $E_j$ is nonnegative.
Replacing $b,c$ by $(b+c)/2,(b+c)/2$ preserves their sum and increases
their product by $(b-c)^2/4$. Therefore it does not decrease $e_k$,
preserves the mean, and preserves nonnegativity.

Starting from $a$, apply \noderef{ElementarySymmetricExtremaStep}
at each step. Its operation certificate says that a constant vector
is left unchanged; otherwise the next vector is obtained by averaging
distinct minimum and maximum entries. Each step preserves
nonnegativity and the mean, and does not decrease $e_k$. Let
$V_r=\sum_i(a_i^{(r)}-\bar a)^2$. If the range at step $r$ is $R_r$,
\noderef{ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging} gives
$V_{r+1}=V_r-R_r^2/2$ in the nonconstant case. In the constant case
both variances and $R_r$ are zero, so the same identity holds.
Since every entry and the mean lie between the
smallest and largest entries, $V_r\le nR_r^2$. Hence
\[
 0\le V_{r+1}\le(1-1/(2n))V_r.
\]
Induction gives $V_r\le(1-1/(2n))^rV_0\to0$.
For each $i$, $|a_i^{(r)}-\bar a|\le\sqrt{V_r}$, so the entire finite
vector converges to the constant vector $(\bar a,\ldots,\bar a)$.
The finite sum of finite products $e_k$ is a continuous polynomial.
Because it never decreased along this sequence,
$e_k(a)\le e_k(\bar a,\ldots,\bar a)=\binom n k\bar a^k$.
Finally $\binom n k>0$ for $k\le n$, so division proves the claim.
\end{proof}
ElementarySymmetricMean.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Elementary-symmetric mean inequality]
For $n>0$, $0\le k\le n$, and nonnegative real entries $a_1,\ldots,a_n$,
\[
 {1\over\binom n k}\sum_{\substack{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\\|A|=k}}
       \prod_{i\in A}a_i
 \le\left({1\over n}\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\right)^k.
\]
Empty products and zeroth powers equal one.
\end{lemma}
ElementarySymmetricMean.title: ElementarySymmetricMean

classical

  have hbj : b j = m := by simp [b]

    simp [b, hti, htj]

open scoped BigOperators

theorem ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging (n k : ℕ) (a : Fin n → ℝ)
    (ha : ∀ t, 0 ≤ a t) (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    let m := (a i + a j) / 2
    let b := Function.update (Function.update a i m) j m
    (∀ t, 0 ≤ b t) ∧ (∑ t, b t) = (∑ t, a t) ∧
      (∑ A ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard k, ∏ t ∈ A, a t) ≤
        (∑ A ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard k, ∏ t ∈ A, b t) ∧
      (∀ c : ℝ, (∑ t, (b t - c) ^ 2) =
        (∑ t, (a t - c) ^ 2) - (a i - a j) ^ 2 / 2) := by
ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging.name: ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging
ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The new entries $m$ are nonnegative, and their sum $2m=a_i+a_j$
is the old sum of the two changed entries. Every other entry is unchanged,
which proves nonnegativity and preservation of the total sum.
For $k=0$ the only subset is empty and both product sums equal one.
For $k=1$ the product sum is the total sum of the entries, so the
claimed inequality is equality.

For $k\ge2$, put $S=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i,j\}$ and
$E_r=\sum_{A\subseteq S,\ |A|=r}\prod_{t\in A}a_t$ for each
nonnegative integer $r$. In particular these sums are zero if $r>|S|$.
Partition the $k$-subsets into those containing neither $i$ nor $j$,
only $i$, only $j$, and both. Removing the indicated indices gives
bijections with the $k$-, $(k-1)$-, $(k-1)$-, and $(k-2)$-subsets
of $S$, respectively. In each bijection the product is multiplied
by $1,a_i,a_j$, or $a_i a_j$, respectively. Thus the old product sum is
\[
 E_k+(a_i+a_j)E_{k-1}+a_i a_j E_{k-2}.
\]
The entries on $S$ are unchanged, so the new product sum is
$E_k+2mE_{k-1}+m^2E_{k-2}$. Their difference is
\[
 (m^2-a_i a_j)E_{k-2}
 =\frac{(a_i-a_j)^2}{4}E_{k-2}\ge0,
\]
because every product defining $E_{k-2}$ is nonnegative.
No negative-index sum is used in either small-$k$ case.

Finally all terms of the squared-deviation sums except the two at
$i,j$ cancel. Expanding those two terms gives
\[
 2(m-c)^2-(a_i-c)^2-(a_j-c)^2
 =-\frac{(a_i-a_j)^2}{2},
\]
which proves the last assertion for every $c$.
\end{proof}
ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[One pair-averaging step]
Let $a=(a_t)_{t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}}$ have nonnegative real entries, let
$i\ne j$, and let $k\ge0$ be an integer. Put $m=(a_i+a_j)/2$, and let
$b$ agree with $a$ except that $b_i=b_j=m$. Then $b$ has nonnegative
entries, $\sum_t b_t=\sum_t a_t$, and
\[
 \sum_{|A|=k}\prod_{t\in A}a_t
 \le \sum_{|A|=k}\prod_{t\in A}b_t.
\]
Moreover, for every real $c$,
\[
 \sum_t(b_t-c)^2=\sum_t(a_t-c)^2-\frac{(a_i-a_j)^2}{2}.
\]
All subsets in the displayed sums are subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
\end{lemma}
ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging.title: ElementarySymmetricPairAveraging

      exact (mul_le_mul_left' he 2).trans_lt (hgap y hy)
  let cert : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta Q d
      theta p epsilon rho zeta omega hatZeta := {
    witnessThinningThreshold := fun s x => (pkg (input s)).witnessThinningThreshold 0 x
    hostThinningThreshold := fun s => (pkg (input s)).hostThinningThreshold 0
    fourGraphsConstant := fun s x y => (pkg (input s)).fourGraphsConstant 0 x y
    fourGraphsThreshold := fun s x y => (pkg (input s)).fourGraphsThreshold 0 x y
    matchingConstant := fun s x => (pkg (input s)).matchingConstant 0 x
    matchingThreshold := fun s x => (pkg (input s)).matchingThreshold 0 x
    matchingExistenceThreshold := fun s x => (pkg (input s)).matchingExistenceThreshold 0 x
    witnessThinningGuarantee := by
      intro s hs x hx V _ _ G _ L R hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR hG
      exact (pkg (input s)).witnessThinningGuarantee 0 (by norm_num) x hx G L R
        hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR
        (SuperRegularErrorMonotone G L R _ _ _ (hepscut s hs) hG)
    hostThinningGuarantee := by
      intro s hs V _ _ G _ L R hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR hG
      exact (pkg (input s)).hostThinningGuarantee 0 (by norm_num) G L R
        hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR
        (SuperRegularErrorMonotone G L R _ _ _ (hepszero s hs) hG)
    fourGraphsPositive := by
      intro s hs x y hx hy
      exact (pkg (input s)).fourGraphsPositive 0 (by norm_num) x y hx hy
    fourGraphsGuarantee := by
      intro s hs x y hx hy
      exact (pkg (input s)).fourGraphsGuarantee 0 (by norm_num) x y hx hy
    matchingConstantAtLeastOne := by
      intro s hs x hx
      exact (pkg (input s)).matchingConstantAtLeastOne 0 (by norm_num) x hx
    matchingExistenceGuarantee := by
      intro s hs x hx
      exact (pkg (input s)).matchingExistenceGuarantee 0 (by norm_num) x hx

      intro s hs x hx
      exact (pkg (input s)).matchingGuarantee 0 (by norm_num) x hx

  refine ⟨epsilon, omega, theta, zeta, hatZeta, cert, hround, ?_⟩
  intro s x hs hx
  obtain ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, hfin⟩ := hdata (input s)

theorem EqualSizeBackwardCertificates (d : ENNReal) (Delta : ℕ)
    (p rho : ℕ → ENNReal) (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1)
    (hdens : ∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
      0 < p x ∧ p x ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < rho x ∧ rho x < p x)
    (hgaps : ∀ y, y < Delta → 0 < p y - p (y + 1)) :
    ∃ (epsilon omega theta zeta hatZeta : ℕ → ENNReal)
      (cert : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta (Delta ^ 2 + 1) d
        theta p epsilon rho zeta omega hatZeta),
      (∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
        0 < epsilon s ∧ epsilon s < hatZeta s ∧ hatZeta s < zeta s ∧
        0 < theta s ∧ 0 < omega (s + 1) ∧
        omega (s + 1) < epsilon (s + 1) ∧ epsilon s ≤ epsilon (s + 1) ∧
        epsilon (s + 1) ≤ 1 ∧
        2 * (zeta s) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta s ∧
        zeta s + Delta * (zeta s) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta s ∧
        zeta s + 2 * Delta * zeta s ≤ theta s ∧
        (∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
          4 * theta s < rho x ∧
          2 * zeta s < rho x ∧ 2 * zeta s < 1 - rho x) ∧
        2 * zeta s < d / 2 ∧ 2 * zeta s < 1 - d / 2 ∧
        (∀ y, y < Delta → 2 * epsilon s < p y - p (y + 1))) ∧
      (∀ s x, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 → x ≤ Delta →
        cert.matchingConstant s x ≠ ⊤) := by

EqualSizeBackwardCertificates.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Set $\varepsilon_Q=1/2$. Since $Q\geq1$, round zero exists even when
$\Delta=0$. Process $s=Q-1,Q-2,\ldots,0$.
At each step $0<\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1$ has already been fixed.
Apply \noderef{EqualSizeOneRoundChoices} with $e=\varepsilon_{s+1}$
and the given exposure data. Write its outputs as
$\omega_{s+1},\theta_s,\zeta_s,\widehat\zeta_s,b_s,K_s$.
These satisfy all three displayed square-root and linear budgets, all
the required density and complementary-density reserves, and
\[
 0<b_s<\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s,\quad
 b_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1},\quad
 0<\omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1},\quad
 2b_s<p_y-p_{y+1}.
\]
For $s>0$ set $\varepsilon_s=b_s/2$. The number $b_s$ is finite:
$2\zeta_s<\rho_0<p_0\leq1$ implies
$\zeta_s<\infty$, and $b_s<\zeta_s$.
Thus $0<\varepsilon_s<b_s<\widehat\zeta_s$ and
$\varepsilon_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1$.
Also $2\varepsilon_s\leq2b_s<p_y-p_{y+1}$.
This supplies exactly the hypothesis on $\varepsilon_s$ needed for
the next backward step. There is no circular choice: the step-$s$
certificate uses $b_s$, not the still-to-be-fixed initial error.

At step zero all the $b_s$ for $s<Q$ are known and positive finite.
After selecting $K_0$, set
\[
 \varepsilon_0=\tfrac12\min_{s<Q} b_s.
\]
The finite minimum is positive because $Q\geq1$. It gives
$0<\varepsilon_0\leq b_0/2<b_0<\widehat\zeta_0$,
$\varepsilon_0\leq\varepsilon_1$, and every round-zero gap inequality.
Crucially $\varepsilon_0\leq b_s$ for every $s<Q$.
Every already chosen $\omega_{s+1}$ has the same next-round error as
when $K_s$ was chosen; in particular altering the initial error does
not alter any output-error choice. This completes the scalar assertions,
including the value $\varepsilon_Q$ needed by the last round.

We now assemble actual guarantees rather than attach names to thresholds.
For $s<Q$ use the round-zero thresholds and constants of $K_s$ as
the round-$s$ data of $\mathcal K$.
Given a witness that is $(\varepsilon_s,p_x)$-super-regular with
$x\leq\Delta$, we have $\varepsilon_s\leq b_s$.
By \noderef{SuperRegularErrorMonotone} it is $(b_s,p_x)$-super-regular.
Apply the witness-thinning guarantee of $K_s$ to the same graph and
the same disjoint parts, preserving both lower cardinality bounds and
both near-equality inequalities. The supplied spanning subgraph is
$(\widehat\zeta_s,\rho_x)$-super-regular, exactly as required.
For a host pair that is $(\varepsilon_0,d)$-super-regular, use
$\varepsilon_0\leq b_s$ and the same monotonicity lemma, then apply
the host-thinning guarantee of $K_s$. It returns the required spanning
$(\widehat\zeta_s,d/2)$-super-regular graph. Thus the single initial
error is below every host-thinning cutoff, not merely round zero's.

The Four Graphs guarantee of $K_s$ has input error $\theta_s$,
ordered density triple $(\rho_x,\rho_y,d/2)$, and output error
$\omega_{s+1}$, which are exactly the parameters of the desired field.
Transfer this guarantee and its positivity and at-most-one constant field
for every independent pair $x,y\leq\Delta$. No inequality between the
exposures is used. Transfer the matching-existence and matching-spread
guarantees unchanged: both use error $\theta_s$ and density $\rho_x$.
Transfer $1\leq M_{s,x}$ and the finiteness of $M_{s,x}$ from
\noderef{EqualSizeOneRoundChoices}. These fill every guarantee field of
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate}.

Extend $\theta,\zeta,\widehat\zeta$ by $1$ at indices $s\geq Q$;
retain $\varepsilon_Q=1/2$ and extend $\varepsilon$ by $1/2$ above $Q$.
Set $\omega_0=1/2$ and extend $\omega$ by $1/2$ above $Q$.
Define unused certificate data by zero thresholds, Four Graphs constant
$1/2$, and matching constant $1$. The required fields are restricted to
$s<Q$ and the stated exposures, so these extensions introduce no new
obligations. All the applications above are polymorphic in the same
universe of finite vertex types as the certificate, and retain the
decidable instances of their input graphs; no proof-local auxiliary
result is transported across nodes. Finite sums, finite subtypes, and
lifted finite vertex types are covered by choosing that common universe
before applying the one-round lemma. All choices involve only the given
scalar data and $\Delta$, never the reduced-graph order $r$.
\end{proof}
EqualSizeBackwardCertificates.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Backward colour-round certificates]
Fix $0<d\leq1$, $\Delta\in\mathbb N$, and total exposure sequences
$p,\rho$ with $0<p_x\leq1$ and $0<\rho_x<p_x$ for $x\leq\Delta$,
and $p_y-p_{y+1}>0$ for $y<\Delta$. Put $Q=\Delta^2+1$.
There are total sequences $\varepsilon,\omega,\theta,\zeta,\widehat\zeta$
and an induction application certificate $\mathcal K$ of
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate} with parameters
$(\Delta,Q,d,\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\widehat\zeta)$.
For each $s<Q$ they satisfy
\[
 0<\varepsilon_s<\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s,\quad0<\theta_s,
 \quad0<\omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1,
 \quad\varepsilon_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1},
\]
\[
 2\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+\Delta\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+2\Delta\zeta_s\leq\theta_s.
\]
For every $x\leq\Delta$ one has
$4\theta_s<\rho_x$, $2\zeta_s<\rho_x$, and
$2\zeta_s<1-\rho_x$. Furthermore $2\zeta_s<d/2$,
$2\zeta_s<1-d/2$, and $2\varepsilon_s<p_y-p_{y+1}$ for $y<\Delta$.
Every matching constant $\mathcal K.\mathrm{matchingConstant}(s,x)$
with $s<Q$ and $x\leq\Delta$ is finite.
\end{lemma}

classical
  let Q := Delta ^ 2 + 1
  letI : Nonempty (Fin Q) := ⟨⟨0, by dsimp [Q]; omega⟩⟩
  let A := Fin Q × (Fin (Delta + 1) × Fin (Delta + 1))
  let B := Fin Q × Fin (Delta + 1)
  let f : A → ENNReal := fun i => cert.fourGraphsConstant i.1 i.2.1 i.2.2
  let g : B → ENNReal := fun i => cert.matchingConstant i.1 i.2
  let a := min 1 (Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty f)
  let M := max 1 (Finset.univ.sup g)
  let C := 2 * M
  have ha : 0 < a := by
    refine lt_min (by norm_num) ((Finset.lt_inf'_iff _).mpr ?_)
    intro i _
    exact (cert.fourGraphsPositive i.1 i.1.isLt i.2.1 i.2.2
      (by omega) (by omega)).1
  have ha1 : a ≤ 1 := min_le_left _ _
  have haconst (s x y : ℕ) (hs : s < Q) (hx : x ≤ Delta) (hy : y ≤ Delta) :
      a ≤ cert.fourGraphsConstant s x y := by
    exact (min_le_right _ _).trans
      (Finset.inf'_le f (Finset.mem_univ (⟨⟨s, hs⟩, ⟨x, by omega⟩, ⟨y, by omega⟩⟩ : A)))
  have hM : 1 ≤ M := le_max_left _ _
  have hMconst (s x : ℕ) (hs : s < Q) (hx : x ≤ Delta) :
      cert.matchingConstant s x ≤ M := by
    exact (Finset.le_sup (f := g) (Finset.mem_univ (⟨⟨s, hs⟩, ⟨x, by omega⟩⟩ : B))).trans

    intro i _

      cert.hostThinningThreshold s ≤ Ncert ∧
      cert.matchingThreshold s x ≤ Ncert ∧
      cert.matchingExistenceThreshold s x ≤ Ncert ∧
      cert.fourGraphsThreshold s x y ≤ Ncert := by
    have h := Finset.le_sup (f := fun i : A =>
      max (cert.witnessThinningThreshold i.1 i.2.1)
        (max (cert.hostThinningThreshold i.1)

            (max (cert.matchingExistenceThreshold i.1 i.2.1)

  have hpadding (i : Fin Q) : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,

      (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ zeta i - hatZeta i ∧
      hatZeta i + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ zeta i ∧
      hatZeta i + 1 / (zeta i * (n : ENNReal)) ≤ zeta i ∧

open Filter

theorem EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds (Delta : ℕ) (d : ENNReal)
    (p rho epsilon omega theta zeta hatZeta : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (cert : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta (Delta ^ 2 + 1) d
      theta p epsilon rho zeta omega hatZeta)
    (hreserves : ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
      0 < hatZeta s ∧ hatZeta s < zeta s ∧ zeta s ≠ ⊤ ∧
      omega (s + 1) < epsilon (s + 1) ∧ epsilon (s + 1) ≤ 1)
    (hfinite : ∀ s x, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 → x ≤ Delta →
      cert.matchingConstant s x ≠ ⊤) :
    ∃ (a M C : ENNReal) (n₀ : ℕ),
      0 < a ∧ a ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ M ∧ 2 * M ≤ C ∧
      (∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
        (∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
          a ≤ cert.fourGraphsConstant s x x ∧
          cert.matchingConstant s x ≤ M ∧
          cert.witnessThinningThreshold s x ≤ n₀ ∧
          cert.hostThinningThreshold s ≤ n₀ ∧
          cert.matchingThreshold s x ≤ n₀ ∧
          cert.matchingExistenceThreshold s x ≤ n₀) ∧
        (∀ x y, x ≤ Delta → y ≤ Delta →
          a ≤ cert.fourGraphsConstant s x y ∧
          cert.fourGraphsThreshold s x y ≤ n₀)) ∧
      (∀ n, n₀ ≤ n →
        C / (n : ENNReal) ≤ 1 ∧ Delta * (1 - a) ^ n ≤ (2 : ENNReal)⁻¹ ∧
        ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
          (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ hatZeta s ∧
          (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ zeta s - hatZeta s ∧
          hatZeta s + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ zeta s ∧
          hatZeta s + 1 / (zeta s * (n : ENNReal)) ≤ zeta s ∧
          omega (s + 1) + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ epsilon (s + 1) ∧
          omega (s + 1) + 1 / (epsilon (s + 1) * (n : ENNReal)) ≤
            epsilon (s + 1)) := by
EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds.name: EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds
EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $S=\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$ and $X=\{0,\ldots,\Delta\}$.
Both are finite and nonempty, also when $\Delta=0$.
By the constant fields of \noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate},
every $a_{s,x,y}=\mathcal K.\mathrm{fourGraphsConstant}(s,x,y)$ is
positive and at most one, and every
$M_{s,x}=\mathcal K.\mathrm{matchingConstant}(s,x)$ is at least one.
The latter are finite by hypothesis. Set
\[
 a=\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{a_{s,x,y}:s\in S,\ x,y\in X\}\bigr),
 \quad
 M=\max\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{M_{s,x}:s\in S,\ x\in X\}\bigr),
 \quad C=2M.
\]
The finite minimum is positive and at most one, and the finite maximum
is finite and at least one. Thus $a,M,C$ are finite, and they satisfy
all required constant comparisons, including those with $y=x$.
Let $N_{\rm cert}$ be the maximum of zero and all the finitely many
certificate thresholds in the asserted index ranges. Each such
threshold is a natural number, so this maximum exists.

For each $s\in S$ set
\[
 r_s=\zeta_s-\widehat\zeta_s,\qquad
 q_s=\varepsilon_{s+1}-\omega_{s+1}.
\]
Since $\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s<\infty$, $r_s$ is positive finite;
also $\zeta_s$ and $\widehat\zeta_s$ are positive finite.
The other strict inequality gives
$0<\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1$ and
$0\leq\omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}<\infty$, hence $q_s$ is positive
finite. All subtractions here therefore agree with ordinary real
subtraction, and the products $\zeta_s r_s$ and
$\varepsilon_{s+1}q_s$ are positive finite. In particular all the real
numbers in the following finite set are finite:
\[
 \{1,C\}\cup\bigcup_{s\in S}
 \left\{\frac1{\widehat\zeta_s},\frac1{r_s},
 \frac2{r_s},\frac1{\zeta_s r_s},
 \frac2{q_s},\frac1{\varepsilon_{s+1}q_s}\right\}.
\]
Use the Archimedean property to choose a natural number $N_{\rm pad}$
at least every member of this set. We identify finite extended real
numbers with their real values only after the finiteness checks above.
For $n\geq N_{\rm pad}$, $n\geq1$ and $n\geq C$, so $C/n\leq1$.
For each $s\in S$, multiplication or division by the indicated positive
finite denominators gives
\[
 1/n\leq\widehat\zeta_s,\quad1/n\leq r_s,
 \quad2/n\leq r_s,\quad1/(\zeta_s n)\leq r_s,
 \quad2/n\leq q_s,\quad
 1/(\varepsilon_{s+1}n)\leq q_s.
\]
Adding $\widehat\zeta_s$ to the third and fourth inequalities gives
the two inner padding bounds; adding $\omega_{s+1}$ to the last two
gives the two output padding bounds. The first inequality is the
explicit inner reserve, independent of the second inequality about the
gap $r_s$; neither has been inferred from the other.

It remains to bound the geometric failure term. If $\Delta=0$, it is
zero for every $n$. If $a=1$, it is zero for every $n\geq1$.
Otherwise $0<a<1$. Write $b=1-a\in(0,1)$ and
$u=a/(1-a)>0$. An elementary induction gives
$(1+u)^n\geq1+nu$: the induction step multiplies by $1+u$ and
uses the nonnegative additional term $nu^2$.
Since $1+u=1/b$ and $u\geq a$, inversion gives
\[
 b^n\leq\frac1{1+nu}\leq\frac1{1+na}.
\]
Choose an integer $N_{\rm decay}\geq2\Delta/a$ by the Archimedean
property, which applies because $a>0$ is finite. For every
$n\geq N_{\rm decay}$ one has
$2\Delta\leq na\leq1+na$, so
\[
 \Delta(1-a)^n\leq\frac{\Delta}{1+na}\leq\frac12.
\]
In the two immediate cases take $N_{\rm decay}=1$.

Finally set $n_0=\max(N_{\rm cert},N_{\rm pad},N_{\rm decay})$.
Every certificate threshold is at most $n_0$. For every $n\geq n_0$
the preceding arguments establish each of the claimed inequalities.
All choices are functions only of the finite parameter and certificate
data and $\Delta$; no reduced-graph order or instance occurs.
\end{proof}
EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Common constants and uniform order bounds]
Put $Q=\Delta^2+1$ and let $\mathcal K$ be an induction application
certificate with parameters
$(\Delta,Q,d,\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\widehat\zeta)$
in the sense of \noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate}.
Assume that for $s<Q$,
\[
 0<\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s<\infty,\qquad
 \omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1,
\]
and every $\mathcal K$-matching constant at $s<Q$, $x\leq\Delta$ is
finite. Then there are $0<a\leq1\leq M$, $C\geq2M$, and
$n_0\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $s<Q$ and $x,y\leq\Delta$,
\[
 a\leq\mathcal K.\mathrm{fourGraphsConstant}(s,x,y),\qquad
 \mathcal K.\mathrm{matchingConstant}(s,x)\leq M,
\]
and each witness-thinning, host-thinning, matching-spread,
matching-existence, and Four Graphs threshold at these indices is at
most $n_0$. For every $n\geq n_0$ and $s<Q$,
\[
 C/n\leq1,\qquad \Delta(1-a)^n\leq\tfrac12,
\]
\[
 n^{-1}\leq\widehat\zeta_s,\quad
 n^{-1}\leq\zeta_s-\widehat\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+2/n\leq\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+1/(\zeta_s n)\leq\zeta_s,
\]
\[
 \omega_{s+1}+2/n\leq\varepsilon_{s+1},\qquad
 \omega_{s+1}+1/(\varepsilon_{s+1}n)\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

EqualSizeOneRoundChoices.lean_proof:
classical
  -- An anchored finite minimum also works for empty indexing types and top caps.
  have small {I : Type} [Fintype I] (c : ENNReal) (hc : 0 < c)
      (f : I → ENNReal) (hf : ∀ i, 0 < f i) :
      ∃ a : ENNReal, 0 < a ∧ a < c ∧ a < 1 ∧ ∀ i, a < f i := by
    let v := min c (min 1 (Finset.univ.inf f))
    have hv : 0 < v := lt_min hc (lt_min (by norm_num)
      ((Finset.lt_inf_iff (by simp : (0 : ENNReal) < ⊤)).mpr (fun i _ => hf i)))
    have hv1 : v ≤ 1 := (min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_left _ _)
    have hav : v / 2 < v := ENNReal.half_lt_self hv.ne'
      (ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hv1)
    refine ⟨v / 2, ENNReal.div_pos hv.ne' (by norm_num),
      hav.trans_le (min_le_left _ _), hav.trans_le hv1, ?_⟩
    intro i
    exact hav.trans_le ((min_le_right _ _).trans
      ((min_le_right _ _).trans (Finset.inf_le (Finset.mem_univ i))))
  let X := Fin (Delta + 1)
  have hx (i : X) : (i : ℕ) ≤ Delta := by have := i.isLt; omega
  have hp (i : X) := hdens i (hx i)
  have hr (i : X) : rho i < 1 := (hp i).2.2.2.trans_le (hp i).2.1
  have hrtop (i : X) : rho i ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top (hr i).le
  have hdtop : d ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hd1
  have hhalf : 0 < d / 2 := ENNReal.div_pos hd.ne' (by norm_num)
  have hhalf1 : d / 2 < 1 := by
    calc
      d / 2 ≤ 1 / 2 := by gcongr
      _ < 1 := by norm_num
  have hc (i : X × X) := NearEqualFourGraphs (rho i.1) (rho i.2) (d / 2)
    (hp i.1).2.2.1 (hr i.1).le (hp i.2).2.2.1 (hr i.2).le hhalf hhalf1.le
  choose outCap houtCap houtput using hc
  obtain ⟨omega, homega, homegae, homega1, homegaCap⟩ := small e he outCap houtCap
  have hinputs (i : X × X) := houtput i omega homega (homegaCap i).le
  choose inCap hinCap hinput using hinputs
  obtain ⟨theta, htheta, _, htheta1, hthetaCap⟩ := small 1 (by norm_num)
    (fun i : X × X => min (inCap i) (rho i.1 / 8))
    (fun i => lt_min (hinCap i) (ENNReal.div_pos (hp i.1).2.2.1.ne' (by norm_num)))
  have hthetaIn (i : X × X) : theta ≤ inCap i :=
    (hthetaCap i).le.trans (min_le_left _ _)
  have hthetaRho (i : X) : 4 * theta < rho i := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    have ht : theta < rho i / 8 := (hthetaCap (i, i)).trans_le (min_le_right _ _)
    have htf : theta ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top htheta1.le
    have htr := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal htf
      (ENNReal.div_ne_top (hrtop i) (by norm_num))).mpr ht
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (hrtop i)).mp
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] at *
    have hrr := ENNReal.toReal_pos (hp i).2.2.1.ne' (hrtop i)
    nlinarith only [htr, hrr]
  have hexp (i : X × X) := hinput i theta htheta (hthetaIn i)
  choose expCap hexpCap hexponential using hexp
  have ha (i : X × X) := small (expCap i) (hexpCap i)
    (fun _ : Fin 0 => (1 : ENNReal)) (fun _ => by norm_num)
  choose a hapos haCap ha1 haunused using ha
  have hfour (i : X × X) := hexponential i (a i) (hapos i) (haCap i).le
  choose fourN hfourGuarantee using hfour
  have hspread (i : X) := UniformPerfectMatchingSpread theta (rho i)
    htheta (hthetaRho i) (hr i).le
  choose M hM hMtop matchN hmatch using hspread
  have htwo (i : X) : 2 * theta < rho i :=
    (mul_le_mul_left (by norm_num : (2 : ENNReal) ≤ 4) theta).trans_lt (hthetaRho i)
  have hcount (i : X) := MatchingEnumeration theta (rho i) htheta (htwo i) (hr i).le
  choose existN hexist using hcount
  have hthetatop : theta ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top htheta1.le
  have hhalfTop : d / 2 ≠ ⊤ := by finiteness
  have hhalfD : d / 2 < d := ENNReal.half_lt_self hd.ne' hdtop
  have hcomp (i : X) : 0 < 1 - rho i := tsub_pos_iff_lt.mpr (hr i)
  have hhostcomp : 0 < 1 - d / 2 := tsub_pos_iff_lt.mpr hhalf1
  let cap := min (theta / (2 * (Delta + 1)))
    (min (theta / (1 + 2 * Delta)) (min ((d / 2) / 20) ((1 - d / 2) / 4)))
  have hcap : 0 < cap := by
    dsimp [cap]
    refine lt_min (ENNReal.div_pos htheta.ne' (by finiteness))
      (lt_min (ENNReal.div_pos htheta.ne' (by finiteness))
      (lt_min (ENNReal.div_pos hhalf.ne' (by norm_num))
        (ENNReal.div_pos hhostcomp.ne' (by norm_num))))
  obtain ⟨h, hh, hhcap, hh1, hhx⟩ := small cap hcap
    (fun i : X => min (rho i / 20) ((1 - rho i) / 4))
    (fun i => lt_min (ENNReal.div_pos (hp i).2.2.1.ne' (by norm_num))
      (ENNReal.div_pos (hcomp i).ne' (by norm_num)))
  have hhtop : h ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hh1.le
  have hhA : h < theta / (2 * (Delta + 1)) := hhcap.trans_le (min_le_left _ _)
  have hhB : h < theta / (1 + 2 * Delta) :=
    hhcap.trans_le ((min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_left _ _))
  have hhD : h < (d / 2) / 20 := hhcap.trans_le
    ((min_le_right _ _).trans ((min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_left _ _)))
  have hhDc : h < (1 - d / 2) / 4 := hhcap.trans_le
    ((min_le_right _ _).trans ((min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_right _ _)))
  have hhR (i : X) : h < rho i / 20 := (hhx i).trans_le (min_le_left _ _)
  have hhRc (i : X) : h < (1 - rho i) / 4 := (hhx i).trans_le (min_le_right _ _)
  let zeta := h ^ 2
  let hatZeta := zeta / 2
  have hzetapos : 0 < zeta := ENNReal.pow_pos hh 2
  have hzetatop : zeta ≠ ⊤ := by dsimp [zeta]; finiteness
  have hhatpos : 0 < hatZeta := ENNReal.div_pos hzetapos.ne' (by norm_num)
  have hhattop : hatZeta ≠ ⊤ := by dsimp [hatZeta]; finiteness
  have hhatlt : hatZeta < zeta := ENNReal.half_lt_self hzetapos.ne' hzetatop
  have hzle : zeta ≤ h := by
    dsimp [zeta]
    rw [pow_two]
    simpa using mul_le_mul_right hh1.le h
  have hroot : zeta ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ = h :=
    ENNReal.pow_rpow_inv_natCast (by norm_num : (2 : ℕ) ≠ 0) h
  -- All arithmetic below is in the finite real part of ENNReal.
  have hRpos : 0 < h.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hh.ne' hhtop
  have hR1 : h.toReal < 1 := by
    simpa using (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop ENNReal.one_ne_top).mpr hh1
  have hRA : h.toReal < theta.toReal / (2 * ((Delta : ℝ) + 1)) := by
    have H := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop (by finiteness)).mpr hhA
    simpa using H
  have hRB : h.toReal < theta.toReal / (1 + 2 * (Delta : ℝ)) := by
    have H := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop (by finiteness)).mpr hhB
    simpa using H
  have hthetaR : 0 < theta.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos htheta.ne' hthetatop
  have hAp : 0 < 2 * ((Delta : ℝ) + 1) := by positivity
  have hBp : 0 < 1 + 2 * (Delta : ℝ) := by positivity
  have hAmul := (lt_div_iff₀ hAp).mp hRA
  have hBmul := (lt_div_iff₀ hBp).mp hRB
  have hrootBudget : 2 * zeta ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    rw [hroot]
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hthetatop).mp
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat]
    have hD0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Delta := Nat.cast_nonneg _
    nlinarith only [hAmul, hRpos, hD0]
  have hsumBudget : zeta + Delta * zeta ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    rw [hroot]
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hthetatop).mp
    rw [ENNReal.toReal_add hzetatop (by finiteness)]
    simp only [zeta, ENNReal.toReal_pow,
      ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
    have hD0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Delta := Nat.cast_nonneg _
    have hs : h.toReal ^ 2 ≤ h.toReal := by nlinarith
    nlinarith only [hAmul, hRpos, hD0, hs]
  have hlinearBudget : zeta + 2 * Delta * zeta ≤ theta := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hthetatop).mp
    rw [ENNReal.toReal_add hzetatop (by finiteness)]
    simp only [zeta, ENNReal.toReal_pow,
      ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat]
    have hD0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Delta := Nat.cast_nonneg _
    have hs : h.toReal ^ 2 ≤ h.toReal := by nlinarith
    have H := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hs (by positivity : 0 ≤ 1 + 2 * (Delta : ℝ))
    nlinarith only [hBmul, H]
  have hsmallR (i : X) : 2 * zeta < rho i ∧
      2 * zeta < 1 - rho i ∧ 10 * hatZeta < rho i := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    have H := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop
      (ENNReal.div_ne_top (hrtop i) (by norm_num))).mpr (hhR i)
    have J := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop (by finiteness)).mpr (hhRc i)
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] at H J
    have hs : h.toReal ^ 2 ≤ h.toReal := by nlinarith
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (hrtop i)).mp
      simp only [zeta, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_pow]
      nlinarith only [H, hs, hRpos]
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by finiteness)).mp
      simp only [zeta, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_pow]
      nlinarith only [J, hs, hRpos]
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (hrtop i)).mp
      simp only [hatZeta, zeta, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat,
        ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_pow]
      nlinarith only [H, hs, hRpos]
  have hsmallD : 2 * zeta < d / 2 ∧ 2 * zeta < 1 - d / 2 ∧
      10 * hatZeta < d / 2 := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    have H := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop (by finiteness)).mpr hhD
    have J := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hhtop (by finiteness)).mpr hhDc
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] at H J
    have hs : h.toReal ^ 2 ≤ h.toReal := by nlinarith
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) hhalfTop).mp
      simp only [zeta, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat,
        ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_div]
      nlinarith only [H, hs, hRpos]
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by finiteness)).mp
      simp only [zeta, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_pow]
      nlinarith only [J, hs, hRpos]
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) hhalfTop).mp
      simp only [hatZeta, zeta, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat,
        ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_pow]
      nlinarith only [H, hs, hRpos]
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hbcap, hb1, hbgap⟩ := small (min e (hatZeta / 16))
    (lt_min he (ENNReal.div_pos hhatpos.ne' (by norm_num)))
    (fun i : Fin Delta => (p i - p (i + 1)) / 4)
    (fun i => ENNReal.div_pos (hgaps i i.isLt).ne' (by norm_num))
  have hbtop : b ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hb1.le
  have hbe : b ≤ e := hbcap.le.trans (min_le_left _ _)
  have hb16 : b ≤ hatZeta / 16 := hbcap.le.trans (min_le_right _ _)
  have hbhat : b < hatZeta := by
    apply (hbcap.trans_le (min_le_right _ _)).trans_le
    calc
      hatZeta / 16 ≤ hatZeta * 1 := by
        change hatZeta * (16 : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ hatZeta * 1
        gcongr
        norm_num
      _ = hatZeta := mul_one _
  have hgap (y : ℕ) (hy : y < Delta) : 2 * b < p y - p (y + 1) := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    have H := hbgap ⟨y, hy⟩
    have hg : p y - p (y + 1) ≠ ⊤ := by
      apply ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top
      exact tsub_le_self.trans (hdens y (by omega)).2.1
    have H' := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hbtop (by finiteness)).mpr H
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) hg).mp
    simp only [ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] at *
    have hp' := ENNReal.toReal_pos (hgaps y hy).ne' hg
    nlinarith only [H', hp']
  let xi := hatZeta / 16
  have hxi : 0 < xi := ENNReal.div_pos hhatpos.ne' (by norm_num)
  have hbudget (D r : ENNReal) (hD : 0 < D) (hDt : D ≠ ⊤) (hrD : r ≤ D) :
      4 * ((r / D) * b + xi) ≤ hatZeta := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    have hratio : r / D ≤ 1 := (ENNReal.div_le_iff hD.ne' hDt).mpr (by simpa using hrD)
    have H : 4 * (b + xi) ≤ hatZeta := by
      apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by dsimp [xi]; finiteness) hhattop).mp
      have hbR := (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal
        hbtop (by finiteness)).mpr hb16
      rw [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_add
        hbtop (by dsimp [xi]; finiteness)]
      simp only [xi, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_div] at *
      have hhat0 : 0 ≤ hatZeta.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
      linarith only [hbR, hhat0]
    apply le_trans _ H
    gcongr
    simpa using mul_le_mul_left hratio b
  have hwitness (i : X) := QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning b (p i) (rho i) hatZeta xi
    hb hbhat (hp i).2.2.1 (hp i).2.2.2 (hp i).2.1 hxi
    (hbudget (p i) (rho i) (hp i).1
      (ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top (hp i).2.1) (hp i).2.2.2.le)
    (hsmallR i).2.2
  choose witnessN hwitnessGuarantee using hwitness
  obtain ⟨hostN, hhostGuarantee⟩ := QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning b d (d / 2) hatZeta xi
    hb hbhat hhalf hhalfD hd1 hxi (hbudget d (d / 2) hd hdtop hhalfD.le) hsmallD.2.2
  let extN (f : X → ℕ) (x : ℕ) := if H : x ≤ Delta then f ⟨x, by omega⟩ else 0
  let extC (f : X → ENNReal) (x : ℕ) :=
    if H : x ≤ Delta then f ⟨x, by omega⟩ else 1
  let extPairN (f : X × X → ℕ) (x y : ℕ) :=
    if H : x ≤ Delta ∧ y ≤ Delta then f (⟨x, by omega⟩, ⟨y, by omega⟩) else 0
  let extPairC (f : X × X → ENNReal) (x y : ℕ) :=
    if H : x ≤ Delta ∧ y ≤ Delta then f (⟨x, by omega⟩, ⟨y, by omega⟩) else 1 / 2
  let K : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta 1 d
      (fun _ => theta) p (fun _ => b) rho (fun _ => zeta)
      (fun _ => omega) (fun _ => hatZeta) := {
    witnessThinningThreshold := fun round x => if round = 0 then extN witnessN x else 0
    hostThinningThreshold := fun round => if round = 0 then hostN else 0
    fourGraphsConstant := fun round x y => if round = 0 then extPairC a x y else 1 / 2
    fourGraphsThreshold := fun round x y => if round = 0 then extPairN fourN x y else 0
    matchingConstant := fun round x => if round = 0 then extC M x else 1
    matchingThreshold := fun round x => if round = 0 then extN matchN x else 0
    matchingExistenceThreshold := fun round x => if round = 0 then extN existN x else 0
    witnessThinningGuarantee := by
      intro round hround x hx V _ _ G _ L R hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR hG
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      simp only [extN, dif_pos hx] at hL hR
      exact hwitnessGuarantee ⟨x, by omega⟩ G L R hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR hG
    hostThinningGuarantee := by
      intro round hround V _ _ G _ L R hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR hG
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      exact hhostGuarantee G L R hLR hL hR hnearL hnearR hG
    fourGraphsPositive := by
      intro round hround x y hx hy
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      simp only [extPairC, dif_pos (And.intro hx hy)]
      exact ⟨hapos (⟨x, by omega⟩, ⟨y, by omega⟩),
        (ha1 (⟨x, by omega⟩, ⟨y, by omega⟩)).le⟩
    fourGraphsGuarantee := by
      intro round hround x y hx hy V _ _ F₁₂ F₁₃ F₂₃ _ _ _ W₁ W₂ W₃ m hm ht h₁₂ hM
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      simp only [extPairN, dif_pos (And.intro hx hy)] at hm
      simp only [extPairC, dif_pos (And.intro hx hy)]
      exact hfourGuarantee (⟨x, by omega⟩, ⟨y, by omega⟩)
        F₁₂ F₁₃ F₂₃ W₁ W₂ W₃ m hm ht h₁₂ hM
    matchingConstantAtLeastOne := by
      intro round hround x hx
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      simp only [extC, dif_pos hx]
      exact hM ⟨x, by omega⟩
    matchingExistenceGuarantee := by
      intro round hround x hx V _ _ G _ U W hUW m hm hU hW hG
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      simp only [extN, dif_pos hx] at hm
      have H := hexist ⟨x, by omega⟩ G U W hUW m hm hU hW hG
      have hbase : 0 < rho x - 2 * theta := tsub_pos_iff_lt.mpr (htwo ⟨x, by omega⟩)
      have hpositive : 0 < (rho x - 2 * theta) ^ m * (m.factorial : ENNReal) :=
        ENNReal.mul_pos (ENNReal.pow_pos hbase m).ne'
          (by exact_mod_cast (Nat.factorial_pos m).ne')
      have hcard : 0 < ({f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}.ncard : ENNReal) :=
        hpositive.trans_le H
      have hnat : 0 < {f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}.ncard := by
        exact_mod_cast hcard
      obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Set.nonempty_of_ncard_ne_zero hnat.ne'
      exact ⟨⟨f, hf⟩⟩
    matchingGuarantee := by
      intro round hround x hx V _ _ G _ U W hUW m hm hU hW hG hnonempty
      have hr0 : round = 0 := by omega
      subst round
      simp only [extN, dif_pos hx] at hm
      simp only [extC, dif_pos hx]
      have H := hmatch ⟨x, by omega⟩ G U W hUW m hm hU hW hG hnonempty
      let mu := (UniformPerfectMatching G U W hUW hnonempty).map Subtype.val
      let inclusion (f : U → W) (u : U) : V := (f u : V)
      have hlaw :
          (UniformPerfectMatching G U W hUW hnonempty).map (fun f u => (f.val u : V)) =
            mu.map inclusion := by
        rw [PMF.map_comp]
        rfl
      rw [hlaw]
      refine ⟨H.1, ?_⟩
      intro s xx yy hinj _
      rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_map_apply]
      by_cases hy : ∀ i, yy i ∈ W
      · let yr (i : Fin s) : W := ⟨yy i, hy i⟩
        have hevent : inclusion ⁻¹' CylinderEvent xx yy = CylinderEvent xx yr := by
          ext f
          constructor
          · intro hf i
            exact Subtype.ext (hf i)
          · intro hf i
            exact congrArg Subtype.val (hf i)
        rw [hevent]
        exact H.2 s xx yr hinj (fun _ => Set.mem_univ _)
      · have hevent : inclusion ⁻¹' CylinderEvent xx yy = ∅ := by
          apply Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr
          intro f hf
          apply hy
          intro i
          have hi : (f (xx i) : V) = yy i := hf i
          rw [← hi]
          exact (f (xx i)).property
        rw [hevent]
        simp
  }
  refine ⟨omega, theta, zeta, hatZeta, b, K, hb, hbhat, hhatlt,
    htheta, homega, homegae, hbe, hrootBudget, hsumBudget, hlinearBudget,
    ?_, hsmallD.1, hsmallD.2.1, hgap, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    exact ⟨hthetaRho ⟨x, by omega⟩, (hsmallR ⟨x, by omega⟩).1,
      (hsmallR ⟨x, by omega⟩).2.1⟩

EqualSizeOneRoundChoices.lean_statement:
theorem EqualSizeOneRoundChoices (d : ENNReal) (Delta : ℕ)
    (p rho : ℕ → ENNReal) (e : ENNReal)
    (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1) (he : 0 < e) (he1 : e ≤ 1)
    (hdens : ∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
      0 < p x ∧ p x ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < rho x ∧ rho x < p x)
    (hgaps : ∀ y, y < Delta → 0 < p y - p (y + 1)) :
    ∃ (omega theta zeta hatZeta b : ENNReal)
      (K : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta 1 d
        (fun _ => theta) p (fun _ => b) rho (fun _ => zeta)
        (fun _ => omega) (fun _ => hatZeta)),
      0 < b ∧ b < hatZeta ∧ hatZeta < zeta ∧
      0 < theta ∧ 0 < omega ∧ omega < e ∧ b ≤ e ∧
      2 * zeta ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta ∧
      zeta + Delta * zeta ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta ∧
      zeta + 2 * Delta * zeta ≤ theta ∧
      (∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
        4 * theta < rho x ∧ 2 * zeta < rho x ∧ 2 * zeta < 1 - rho x) ∧
      2 * zeta < d / 2 ∧ 2 * zeta < 1 - d / 2 ∧
      (∀ y, y < Delta → 2 * b < p y - p (y + 1)) ∧
      (∀ x, x ≤ Delta → K.matchingConstant 0 x ≠ ⊤) := by
EqualSizeOneRoundChoices.name: EqualSizeOneRoundChoices
EqualSizeOneRoundChoices.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
All quantities used below are finite real numbers: $d\leq1$,
$0<\rho_x<p_x\leq1$, and $0<e\leq1$.
In particular $0<d/2<1$ and $0<\rho_x<1$.
For each ordered pair $x,y\leq\Delta$, apply
\noderef{NearEqualFourGraphs} to $(\rho_x,\rho_y,d/2)$.
Its six density hypotheses hold by these inequalities. Write $u_{xy}>0$
for its output-error cap. Take $\omega$ to be one half of the minimum
of $e$, $1$, and all $u_{xy}$ (allowing an infinite cap does not affect
this minimum). The index set is finite and nonempty, including when
$\Delta=0$. Hence $0<\omega<e$ and $\omega\leq u_{xy}$.
Only now use the output-error universal quantifier in Four Graphs:
for each pair it supplies a positive input-error cap $v_{xy}$ at
this fixed $\omega$.

Let $\theta$ be one half of the minimum of $1$, all $v_{xy}$,
and all $\rho_x/8$. Then $\theta>0$, $\theta\leq v_{xy}$, and
$4\theta\leq\rho_x/4<\rho_x$.
At this fixed input error, Four Graphs supplies an exponential-constant
cap $c_{xy}>0$. Set $a_{xy}=\min(1,c_{xy})/2$.
Thus $0<a_{xy}\leq1$ and $a_{xy}\leq c_{xy}$; apply its last
universal quantifier at $a_{xy}$ and record the resulting order threshold
and probability guarantee. This follows the output-error, input-error,
exponential-constant quantifier order exactly. Both exposure coordinates
range independently over the full set $\{0,\ldots,\Delta\}$.

For each $x\leq\Delta$, apply \noderef{UniformPerfectMatchingSpread}
at $(\theta,\rho_x)$: $\theta>0$, $4\theta<\rho_x$, and
$\rho_x\leq1$ verify its hypotheses. Record its finite constant
$M_x\geq1$, threshold, and spread guarantee. Its map to matching
functions is exactly the map to ambient-vertex-valued functions in the
certificate, after composing with the right-subtype inclusion.
Explicitly, unfold \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} and \noderef{CylinderEvent}.
For each cylinder of ambient prescriptions $y_i$, if any
$y_i$ is outside the right part its mass is zero; otherwise form the
right-subtype prescriptions with these values. Their cylinder is the
preimage of the ambient cylinder under the inclusion, so the same
$(M_x/m)^k$ bound holds. The constraint $M_x/m\leq1$ is unchanged.
Apply \noderef{MatchingEnumeration} at $(\theta,\rho_x)$, since
$2\theta\leq4\theta<\rho_x$. Its lower bound
$(\rho_x-2\theta)^m m!$ is positive: the base is positive and finite,
its natural power is positive also for $m=0$, and $m!>0$.
Consequently the finite set of perfect matchings has positive cardinality,
so a matching exists. Record this threshold and existence guarantee.

Choose a positive real $h$ strictly below each of
\[
 1,\quad\frac{\theta}{2(\Delta+1)},\quad
 \frac{\theta}{1+2\Delta},\quad
 \min_{x\leq\Delta}\frac{\rho_x}{20},\quad
 \min_{x\leq\Delta}\frac{1-\rho_x}{4},\quad
 \frac{d/2}{20},\quad\frac{1-d/2}{4}.
\]
Every entry is positive, so half their minimum is a valid explicit
choice. Set $\zeta=h^2$ and $\widehat\zeta=\zeta/2$.
Since $0<h<1$, $\zeta\leq h$ and $\sqrt\zeta=h$.
It follows that
\[
 2\sqrt\zeta=2h<\theta,\qquad
 \zeta+\Delta\sqrt\zeta\leq(\Delta+1)h<\theta,\qquad
 \zeta+2\Delta\zeta\leq(1+2\Delta)h<\theta.
\]
Also $2\zeta\leq2h<\rho_x,1-\rho_x,d/2,1-d/2$, and
$10\widehat\zeta=5h^2\leq5h<\rho_x,d/2$.
These verify all the claimed padding reserves, including the strict
inner gap $\zeta-\widehat\zeta>0$.

Let $b$ be half the minimum of $e$, $\widehat\zeta/16$, and the
finitely many $(p_y-p_{y+1})/4$ for $y<\Delta$.
When $\Delta=0$ omit the last family. Thus
$0<b<\widehat\zeta$, $b\leq e$, and
$2b\leq(p_y-p_{y+1})/4<p_y-p_{y+1}$.
Put $\xi=\widehat\zeta/16>0$.
For each witness take $(D,\rho)=(p_x,\rho_x)$; for each host take
$(D,\rho)=(d,d/2)$. In each case $0<\rho<D\leq1$ and
$\rho/D\leq1$; division is ordinary division because $D$ is finite
and positive. Hence
\[
 4\bigl((\rho/D)b+\xi\bigr)
 \leq4\bigl(\widehat\zeta/16+\widehat\zeta/16\bigr)
 =\widehat\zeta/2\leq\widehat\zeta.
\]
Together with $0<b<\widehat\zeta$, $\xi>0$, and
$10\widehat\zeta<\rho$, this checks every scalar hypothesis of
\noderef{QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning}. Apply it separately to
each witness density and to the host density, and record the resulting
thresholds and actual spanning-subgraph conclusions, including their
disjointness, two size cutoffs, and both near-equality assumptions.

Use the recorded data at round zero to fill the fields of $K$:
the thinning thresholds and conclusions just obtained, the constants
$a_{xy}$ and their Four Graphs thresholds and conclusions, and the
constants $M_x$, matching thresholds, existence thresholds, and their
guarantees. All fields are required only at round zero and exposures
at most $\Delta$. Extend the data functions elsewhere by zero thresholds,
Four Graphs constant $1/2$, and matching constant $1$; no guarantee is
required there. The two constant comparison fields hold because
$0<a_{xy}\leq1$ and $M_x\geq1$. This constructs exactly
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate} with the displayed parameters.
All graph guarantees are uniform in finite vertex types. One may first
choose their scalar data at the universe of the intended certificate
(including finite sums and subtype copies); the statements impose no
vertex-count dependence on these choices. These are applications of the
displayed universal graph guarantees, not transport of an auxiliary
proof-local result. None of the choices uses $r$.
\end{proof}
EqualSizeOneRoundChoices.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous choices for one colour round]
Fix $0<d\leq1$, $\Delta\in\mathbb N$, total exposure sequences $p,\rho$,
and $0<e\leq1$. Assume $0<p_x\leq1$, $0<\rho_x<p_x$ for
$x\leq\Delta$, and $p_y-p_{y+1}>0$ for $y<\Delta$.
There are scalars $\omega,\theta,\zeta,\widehat\zeta,b$ and a
certificate $K$ in the sense of \noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate},
with degree bound $\Delta$, certified round bound $1$, host density $d$,
and parameter sequences
\[
 t_s=\theta,\quad D_x=p_x,\quad \beta_s=b,\quad
 \rho_x=\rho_x,\quad \eta_s=\zeta,\quad
 \omega_s=\omega,\quad \xi_s=\widehat\zeta.
\]
They satisfy
\[
 0<b<\widehat\zeta<\zeta,\quad 0<\theta,\quad
 0<\omega<e,\quad b\leq e,
\]
\[
 2\sqrt\zeta\leq\theta,\quad
 \zeta+\Delta\sqrt\zeta\leq\theta,\quad
 \zeta+2\Delta\zeta\leq\theta,
\]
and, for every $x\leq\Delta$,
\[
 4\theta<\rho_x,\quad 2\zeta<\rho_x,\quad
 2\zeta<1-\rho_x.
\]
Also $2\zeta<d/2$, $2\zeta<1-d/2$, and
$2b<p_y-p_{y+1}$ for every $y<\Delta$.
Every $K$-matching constant at round zero and exposure $x\leq\Delta$
is finite. Thus $K$ contains actual witness and host thinnings at input
error $b$, and Four Graphs data for every ordered pair $x,y\leq\Delta$.
\end{lemma}
EqualSizeOneRoundChoices.title: EqualSizeOneRoundChoices

intro d Delta hd hd1
  obtain ⟨p, rho, hp0, hdens, hrec, hgaps⟩ :=
    ExposureDensityRecursion d Delta hd hd1
  obtain ⟨epsilon, omega, theta, zeta, hatZeta, cert, hround, hfinite⟩ :=
    EqualSizeBackwardCertificates d Delta p rho hd hd1 hdens hgaps
  have hreserves : ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
      0 < hatZeta s ∧ hatZeta s < zeta s ∧ zeta s ≠ ⊤ ∧
      omega (s + 1) < epsilon (s + 1) ∧ epsilon (s + 1) ≤ 1 := by
    intro s hs
    obtain ⟨he, heh, hhz, ht, ho, hoe, hemono, he1,
      hroot, hsum, hlinear, hsmall, hdhalf, hdcomp, hgap⟩ := hround s hs
    have hz1 : zeta s ≤ 1 := by
      calc
        zeta s ≤ 2 * zeta s := by
          simpa using mul_le_mul_right' (by norm_num : (1 : ENNReal) ≤ 2) (zeta s)
        _ ≤ rho 0 := (hsmall 0 (Nat.zero_le Delta)).2.1.le
        _ ≤ 1 := (hdens 0 (Nat.zero_le Delta)).2.2.2.le.trans
          (hdens 0 (Nat.zero_le Delta)).2.1
    exact ⟨he.trans heh, hhz, ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hz1, hoe, he1⟩
  obtain ⟨a, M, C, n₀, ha, ha1, hM, hC, hthresholds, horder⟩ :=
    EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds Delta d p rho epsilon omega theta zeta hatZeta
      cert hreserves hfinite
  exact ⟨p, rho, epsilon, omega, theta, zeta, hatZeta, cert,
    a, M, C, n₀, hp0, hdens, hrec, hround, ha, ha1, hM, hC, hthresholds, horder⟩
EqualSizeParameterTable.lean_statement:
theorem EqualSizeParameterTable :
    ∀ (d : ENNReal) (Delta : ℕ), 0 < d → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ (p rho epsilon omega theta zeta hatZeta : ℕ → ENNReal)
        (cert : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta (Delta ^ 2 + 1) d
          theta p epsilon rho zeta omega hatZeta)
        (a M C : ENNReal) (n₀ : ℕ),
        p 0 = d ∧
        (∀ x, x ≤ Delta → 0 < p x ∧ p x ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < rho x ∧ rho x < p x) ∧
        (∀ x, x < Delta → p (x + 1) = rho x * (d / 2)) ∧
        (∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
          0 < epsilon s ∧ epsilon s < hatZeta s ∧ hatZeta s < zeta s ∧
          0 < theta s ∧ 0 < omega (s + 1) ∧
          omega (s + 1) < epsilon (s + 1) ∧ epsilon s ≤ epsilon (s + 1) ∧
          epsilon (s + 1) ≤ 1 ∧
          2 * (zeta s) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta s ∧
          zeta s + Delta * (zeta s) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta s ∧
          zeta s + 2 * Delta * zeta s ≤ theta s ∧
          (∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
            4 * theta s < rho x ∧
            2 * zeta s < rho x ∧ 2 * zeta s < 1 - rho x) ∧
          2 * zeta s < d / 2 ∧ 2 * zeta s < 1 - d / 2 ∧
          (∀ y, y < Delta → 2 * epsilon s < p y - p (y + 1))) ∧
        0 < a ∧ a ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ M ∧ 2 * M ≤ C ∧
        (∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
          (∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
            a ≤ cert.fourGraphsConstant s x x ∧
            cert.matchingConstant s x ≤ M ∧
            cert.witnessThinningThreshold s x ≤ n₀ ∧
            cert.hostThinningThreshold s ≤ n₀ ∧
            cert.matchingThreshold s x ≤ n₀ ∧
            cert.matchingExistenceThreshold s x ≤ n₀) ∧
          (∀ x y, x ≤ Delta → y ≤ Delta →
            a ≤ cert.fourGraphsConstant s x y ∧
            cert.fourGraphsThreshold s x y ≤ n₀)) ∧
        (∀ n, n₀ ≤ n →
          C / (n : ENNReal) ≤ 1 ∧ Delta * (1 - a) ^ n ≤ (2 : ENNReal)⁻¹ ∧
          ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
            (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ hatZeta s ∧
            (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ zeta s - hatZeta s ∧
            hatZeta s + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ zeta s ∧
            hatZeta s + 1 / (zeta s * (n : ENNReal)) ≤ zeta s ∧
            omega (s + 1) + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ epsilon (s + 1) ∧
            omega (s + 1) + 1 / (epsilon (s + 1) * (n : ENNReal)) ≤
              epsilon (s + 1)) := by

EqualSizeParameterTable.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Apply \noderef{ExposureDensityRecursion} to $d,\Delta$ to obtain
$p,\rho$ with $p_0=d$, the stated recursion, all density inequalities,
and every positive exposure gap $p_y-p_{y+1}$.

Apply \noderef{EqualSizeBackwardCertificates} to these sequences.
It gives the five round-indexed sequences and the actual induction
application certificate, all inequalities (A1)--(A2), and finite
matching constants throughout the required index ranges. Its construction
uses \noderef{EqualSizeOneRoundChoices} for each backward step: the
single-round packages use all ordered exposure pairs, and each thinning
has already been supplied by the quantitative thinning theorem. The
initial error is chosen below every host cutoff, not only its own
round's cutoff.

To apply \noderef{EqualSizeCommonOrderBounds}, verify its reserves
explicitly. For $s<Q$, $0<\varepsilon_s<\widehat\zeta_s$ implies
$\widehat\zeta_s>0$, and $\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s$ is already supplied.
Exposure zero is always available and gives
\[
 \zeta_s\leq2\zeta_s<\rho_0<p_0\leq1;
\]
hence $\zeta_s$ is finite. Finally
$\omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1$ and the finiteness of each matching
constant are outputs of the backward-certificate lemma.
The common-order lemma therefore provides $a,M,C,n_0$, all threshold
comparisons, (A3), and every bound in (A4a)--(A4b), including the separate
inner reserve $1/n\leq\widehat\zeta_s$. This proves all the required
conjuncts.

The exposure sequences were fixed from $d,\Delta$, the backward choices
use only these sequences and the $Q=\Delta^2+1$ rounds, and the common
constants and order cutoff use only the resulting finite data.
Thus no choice depends on $r$ or on a graph instance. The construction
also covers $\Delta=0$, retains $\varepsilon_Q$ for the last round, and
extends every sequence and certificate-data function to all natural
indices as stated in the backward-certificate lemma.
\end{proof}
EqualSizeParameterTable.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Finite colour-round parameter construction]
Fix $0<d\leq1$ and $\Delta\in\mathbb N$, and put $Q=\Delta^2+1$.
There are exposure-indexed densities $p_x,\rho_x$, round-indexed errors
$\varepsilon_s,\omega_{s+1},\theta_s,\zeta_s,\widehat\zeta_s$, an induction
application certificate $\mathcal K$ with certified round bound $Q$ in the
sense of \noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate}, constants $0<a\leq1\leq M$ and
$C\geq2M$, and $n_0\in\mathbb N$ with the following properties.
One has $p_0=d$ and, for $x\leq\Delta$,
\[
 0<\rho_x<p_x\leq1,\qquad
 p_{x+1}=\rho_x(d/2)\quad(x<\Delta).
\]
For every $s<Q$,
\[
 0<\varepsilon_s<\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s,\quad0<\theta_s,\quad
 0<\omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1,\quad
 \varepsilon_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1},
\]
\[
 2\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+\Delta\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+2\Delta\zeta_s\leq\theta_s,                 \tag{A1}
\]
and, for every $x\leq\Delta$ and $y<\Delta$,
\[
 4\theta_s<\rho_x,\quad 2\zeta_s<\rho_x,\quad
 2\zeta_s<1-\rho_x,\quad 2\zeta_s<d/2,\quad
 2\zeta_s<1-d/2,\quad 2\varepsilon_s<p_y-p_{y+1}.       \tag{A2}
\]
The certificate simultaneously supplies, for every $s<Q$ and every ordered
pair $x,y\leq\Delta$, the witness and host spanning-thinning conclusions,
the near-equal Four Graphs conclusion with input error $\theta_s$ and output
error $\omega_{s+1}$, perfect-matching existence, and uniform-matching
spread, exactly as specified in \noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate}.
Writing its constants and thresholds as
$a_{s,x,y},N^{\rm FG}_{s,x,y},M_{s,x},N^{\rm mat}_{s,x},
N^{\rm exist}_{s,x},N^{\rm wit}_{s,x},N^{\rm host}_s$, one has
\[
 a\leq a_{s,x,y},\qquad M_{s,x}\leq M,
\]
and every displayed threshold is at most $n_0$.  Thus one $\theta_s$ works
for all ordered exposure pairs, without any comparison between $x$ and $y$.
Finally, for every $n\geq n_0$ and $s<Q$,
\[
 \Delta(1-a)^n\leq\tfrac12,\qquad C/n\leq1,             \tag{A3}
\]
\[
 n^{-1}\leq\widehat\zeta_s,\quad
 n^{-1}\leq\zeta_s-\widehat\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+2/n\leq\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+1/(\zeta_sn)\leq\zeta_s,             \tag{A4a}
\]
\[
 \omega_{s+1}+2/n\leq\varepsilon_{s+1},\qquad
 \omega_{s+1}+1/(\varepsilon_{s+1}n)\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}. \tag{A4b}
\]
\end{lemma}

EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport.lean_proof:
classical
  have enlarge : ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T)) (P Q : Finset (S ⊕ T))
      (a b d : ENNReal), a ≤ b →
      @SuperRegularPair _ _ G (Classical.decRel _) P Q a d →
      @SuperRegularPair _ _ G (Classical.decRel _) P Q b d := by
    intro G P Q a b d hab hG
    rcases hG with ⟨hr, hl, hh⟩
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro X hX Y hY hx hy
      obtain ⟨lo, hi⟩ := hr X hX Y hY
        (lt_of_le_of_lt (mul_le_mul_left hab _) hx)
        (lt_of_le_of_lt (mul_le_mul_left hab _) hy)
      exact ⟨(tsub_le_tsub_left hab d).trans lo, hi.trans (add_le_add_right hab d)⟩
    · intro x hx
      exact ⟨(mul_le_mul_left (tsub_le_tsub_left hab d) _).trans (hl x hx).1,
        (hl x hx).2.trans (mul_le_mul_left (add_le_add_right hab d) _)⟩
    · intro y hy
      exact ⟨(mul_le_mul_left (tsub_le_tsub_left hab d) _).trans (hh y hy).1,
        (hh y hy).2.trans (mul_le_mul_left (add_le_add_right hab d) _)⟩
  let F : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun x z =>
    ∃ u : U, ∃ w : Z, x = u ∧ z = w ∧ W.Adj (tau u) w
  letI : DecidableRel F.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adjF : ∀ u : U, ∀ z : Z, F.Adj u z ↔ W.Adj (tau u) z := by
    intro u z
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, hh | hh⟩
      · obtain ⟨v, w, hv, hw, ha⟩ := hh
        have huv : u = v := Subtype.ext hv
        have hzw : z = w := Subtype.ext hw
        simpa only [huv, hzw] using ha
      · obtain ⟨v, w, hv, hw, _⟩ := hh
        exact False.elim (Finset.disjoint_left.mp hUZ v.property (hv ▸ z.property))
    · intro ha
      refine ⟨?_, Or.inl ⟨u, z, rfl, rfl, ha⟩⟩
      intro he
      exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp hUZ u.property (he ▸ z.property)
  let f : S ⊕ T → S ⊕ T := fun x => if hx : x ∈ U then tau ⟨x, hx⟩ else x
  have fe : ∀ u : U, f u = tau u := by intro u; simp [f, u.property]
  have finj : Set.InjOn f U := by
    intro x hx y hy he
    have he' : tau ⟨x, hx⟩ = tau ⟨y, hy⟩ :=
      Subtype.ext (by simpa only [← fe ⟨x, hx⟩, ← fe ⟨y, hy⟩] using he)
    exact congrArg Subtype.val (tau.injective he')
  have imageU : U.image f = V := by
    ext v
    constructor
    · intro hv
      obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hv
      rw [fe ⟨u, hu⟩]
      exact (tau ⟨u, hu⟩).property
    · intro hv
      obtain ⟨u, he⟩ := tau.surjective ⟨v, hv⟩
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨u, u.property, (fe u).trans (congrArg Subtype.val he)⟩
  have cardU : V.card = U.card := by
    rw [← imageU]
    exact Finset.card_image_iff.mpr finj
  have adj : ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ z ∈ Z, F.Adj x z ↔ W.Adj (f x) z := by
    intro x hx z hz
    simpa only [fe ⟨x, hx⟩] using adjF ⟨x, hx⟩ ⟨z, hz⟩
  have counts : ∀ (P : Finset (S ⊕ T)) (g : S ⊕ T → S ⊕ T)
      (hinj : Set.InjOn g P) (a b : S ⊕ T → Prop)
      [DecidablePred a] [DecidablePred b],
      (∀ x ∈ P, a x ↔ b (g x)) →
      (P.filter a).card = ((P.image g).filter b).card := by
    intro P g hinj a b _ _ hab
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun x _ => g x)
    · intro x hx
      obtain ⟨hx, ha⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hx
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, (hab x hx).mp ha⟩
    · intro x hx y hy he
      exact hinj (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).1 (Finset.mem_filter.mp hy).1 he
    · intro y hy
      obtain ⟨hy, hb⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hy
      obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hy
      exact ⟨x, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hx, (hab x hx).mpr hb⟩, rfl⟩

      ((X.product Y).filter fun q => F.Adj q.1 q.2).card =

    intro X hX Y hY
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun q _ => (f q.1, q.2))
    · intro q hq
      obtain ⟨hq, ha⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hq
      obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hq
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr
        ⟨Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨q.1, hx, rfl⟩, hy⟩, (adj _ (hX hx) _ (hY hy)).mp ha⟩
    · intro q hq r hr he
      have hq' := Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).1
      have hr' := Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hr).1
      have he2 := congrArg Prod.snd he

      obtain ⟨hq, ha⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hq
      obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hq
      obtain ⟨x, hx, he⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
      refine ⟨(x, q.2), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hx, hy⟩, ?_⟩,

      exact (adj _ (hX hx) _ (hY hy)).mpr (by simpa only [he] using ha)
  have hF : @SuperRegularPair _ _ F (Classical.decRel _) U Z xi p := by
    rcases hW with ⟨hr, hl, hh⟩
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro X hX Y hY hx hy
      have cx : (X.image f).card = X.card := Finset.card_image_iff.mpr (finj.mono hX)
      have hXV : X.image f ⊆ V := by
        rw [← imageU]
        exact Finset.image_mono f hX

        unfold PairDensity
        rw [edges X hX Y hY, cx]
      rw [density]

      have hc : (Z.filter fun z => F.Adj x z).card =

        ext z

      have hf : f x ∈ V := by rw [← imageU]; exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
