      have hc := counts U f finj (fun x => F.Adj x z) (fun x => W.Adj x z)
        (fun x hx => adj x hx z hz)
      rw [imageU] at hc
      simpa only [cardU, ← hc] using hh z hz
  refine ⟨F, enlarge F U Z xi eta p hxi hF, adjF, ?_⟩
  intro sigma hsigma
  dsimp only
  intro hI
  let Wnew : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v z =>
    ∃ u : U, ∃ w : Z, v = tau u ∧ z = w ∧ F.Adj u w ∧ J.Adj (sigma u) w
  letI : DecidableRel Wnew.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adjNew : ∀ u : U, ∀ z : Z,
      Wnew.Adj (tau u) z ↔ F.Adj u z ∧ J.Adj (sigma u) z := by
    intro u z
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, hh | hh⟩
      · obtain ⟨v, w, hv, hw, ha⟩ := hh
        have huv : u = v := tau.injective (Subtype.ext hv)
        have hzw : z = w := Subtype.ext hw
        simpa only [huv, hzw] using ha
      · obtain ⟨v, w, hv, hw, _⟩ := hh

      refine ⟨?_, Or.inl ⟨u, z, rfl, rfl, ha⟩⟩

    intro he

    intro v
    constructor
    · intro hv
      obtain ⟨u, he⟩ := tau.surjective ⟨v, hv⟩
      exact ⟨u, (congrArg Subtype.val he).symm⟩
    · rintro ⟨u, rfl⟩
      exact (tau u).property
  have partZ : ∀ z : S ⊕ T, z ∈ Z ↔ ∃ w : Z, z = w := by
    intro z
    exact ⟨fun hz => ⟨⟨z, hz⟩, rfl⟩, by rintro ⟨w, rfl⟩; exact w.property⟩
  letI : DecidableRel M.Adj := Classical.decRel _

    M B F J Wnew V Z omega (p * h) hUK hB hM adjNew partV partZ hI
  refine ⟨Wnew, ?_, enlarge Wnew V Z omega eps (p * h) homega transported⟩
  intro v z hvz
  rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj] at hvz ⊢
  refine ⟨hvz.1, ?_⟩
  have forward : ∀ (v z : S ⊕ T),
      (∃ u : U, ∃ w : Z, v = tau u ∧ z = w ∧ F.Adj u w ∧ J.Adj (sigma u) w) →
      v ∈ V ∧ z ∈ Z ∧ O.Adj v z ∧

    rintro v z ⟨u, w, rfl, rfl, hfu, hju⟩

theorem EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport
    {S T : Type*} [Fintype S] [Fintype T] [DecidableEq S] [DecidableEq T]
    (U K V Z : Finset (S ⊕ T)) (m : ℕ)
    (M O W J H : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T))
    [DecidableRel W.Adj] [DecidableRel J.Adj]
    (tau : U ≃ V) (xi eta omega eps p h : ENNReal)
    (hUK : Disjoint U K) (hUZ : Disjoint U Z) (hKZ : Disjoint K Z)
    (hVZ : Disjoint V Z)
    (hU : U.card = m) (hK : K.card = m) (hV : V.card = m) (hZ : Z.card = m)
    (hM : ∀ u : U, ∀ v : V, M.Adj u v ↔ v = tau u)
    (hWO : W ≤ O) (hJH : J ≤ H)
    (hxi : xi ≤ eta) (homega : omega ≤ eps)
    (hW : SuperRegularPair W V Z xi p) :
    ∃ F : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T),
      @SuperRegularPair (S ⊕ T) _ F (Classical.decRel _) U Z eta p ∧
      (∀ u : U, ∀ z : Z, F.Adj u z ↔ W.Adj (tau u) z) ∧
      (∀ sigma : U → K, Function.Bijective sigma →
        let I := @MatchingInducedGraph (S ⊕ T) _ _ F J (Classical.decRel _) _ U K Z sigma
        let L := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inl : U → U ⊕ Z)
        let R := Finset.univ.image (Sum.inr : Z → U ⊕ Z)
        @SuperRegularPair (U ⊕ Z) _ I (Classical.decRel _) L R omega (p * h) →
        let Anew := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v z =>
          v ∈ V ∧ z ∈ Z ∧ O.Adj v z ∧
            ∀ u : U, M.Adj u v → H.Adj (sigma u) z
        ∃ Wnew : SimpleGraph (S ⊕ T), Wnew ≤ Anew ∧
          @SuperRegularPair (S ⊕ T) _ Wnew (Classical.decRel _) V Z eps (p * h)) := by
EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport.name: EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport
EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Define $F$ to have just the edges $uz$ with $u\in U,z\in Z$ and
$\tau(u)z\in W$, and their reverses. Disjointness excludes loops and
ambiguity between the two orientations. The bijection $\tau$ preserves
every degree on the opposite side and every edge count in a tested
rectangle: the rectangle $A\times B$ corresponds to
$\tau(A)\times B$, with unchanged cardinalities. Thus the degree and
regularity inequalities in \noderef{SuperRegularPair} hold with error
$\xi$ and hence with error $\eta$. Error enlargement decreases the lower
bounds, increases the upper bounds, and only restricts the sets tested for
regularity.

For a given $\sigma$, define $W_{\rm new}$ to have just the edges
$\tau(u)z$ for which $uz\in F$ and $\sigma(u)z\in J$, and their
reverses. It is not defined to be $T_\sigma$. On these edges, $W\subseteq O$
gives the old constraint and $J\subseteq H$ gives the new constraint.
The source-matching equivalence says that $u$ is the only vertex of $U$
adjacent in $M$ to $\tau(u)$. Therefore all the new constraints hold and
$W_{\rm new}\subseteq T_\sigma$.

Apply \noderef{MatchingInducedUpdatedCandidacyTransport} with the
source bijection $\tau$, the graph $W_{\rm new}$ as its target graph,
and the complete bipartite graph on $U,K$ as its matching graph. The
bijection $\sigma$ is a perfect matching of that graph in the sense of
\noderef{PerfectMatching}. The target adjacency equivalence is precisely
the definition of $W_{\rm new}$, not an equality with $T_\sigma$.
The required part conditions are the two equivalences
$v\in V\Longleftrightarrow\exists u\in U\ v=\tau(u)$ and
$z\in Z\Longleftrightarrow\exists w\in Z\ z=w$.
Both follow from bijectivity and the identity on $Z$.
Transport gives error $\omega$ on the exact parts $V,Z$. Enlarge that
error to $e$ by the degree and rectangle inequalities just described.
This proves the required spanning contained witness.
\end{proof}
EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Equal-size pullback and contained transport]
In a finite disjoint-union ambient vertex set, let $U,K,V,Z$ have size
$m$, with $U\cap K=U\cap Z=K\cap Z=V\cap Z=\varnothing$.
Let $M,O,W,J,H$ be graphs and let $\tau:U\to V$ be a bijection such that
$uv\in M$ if and only if $v=\tau(u)$, for $u\in U,v\in V$.
Assume $W\subseteq O$, $J\subseteq H$, $\xi\le\eta$, $\omega\le e$,
and $W[V,Z]$ is $(\xi,p)$-super-regular.
There is a graph $F$ with $F[U,Z]$ $(\eta,p)$-super-regular and
$uz\in F\Longleftrightarrow\tau(u)z\in W$ on $U\times Z$.
For every bijection $\sigma:U\to K$, if the graph on subtype copies of
$U,Z$ with edges $uz\in F$ and $\sigma(u)z\in J$ is
$(\omega,ph)$-super-regular, then the graph
\[
 T_\sigma:\quad vz\in E(T_\sigma)\Longleftrightarrow
 v\in V,\ z\in Z,\ vz\in O,\quad
 \forall u\in U\ (uv\in M\Rightarrow\sigma(u)z\in H),
\]
symmetrized as a simple graph, contains a spanning
$(e,ph)$-super-regular graph on $V,Z$.
\end{lemma}
EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport.title: EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport

EqualSizeTerminalConversion.lean_statement:
theorem EqualSizeTerminalConversion
    {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (X : Finset VH) (μ : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X))
    (b : ENNReal) (hX : X = Finset.univ)
    (hspread : VertexSpreadOn
      (μ.map fun f => fun x : {x : VH // x ∈ X} => f.toFun x.1) b Set.univ) :
    ∃ F : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X →
        {φ : SimpleGraph.Copy H G // CompatibleEmbedding B A φ},
      (∀ f x, (F f).1 x = f.toFun x) ∧
      VertexSpreadOn ((μ.map F).map fun φ => fun x => φ.1 x) b Set.univ := by
EqualSizeTerminalConversion.name: EqualSizeTerminalConversion
EqualSizeTerminalConversion.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Every source vertex belongs to $X$. For any partial embedding $f$,
injectivity on $X$ from \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} is therefore
global injectivity. Its edge-preservation field applies to every source
edge and supplies a graph homomorphism into $G$. Together these form a
\texttt{SimpleGraph.Copy}; no reflection of host edges is asserted or
needed. The compatibility field applies to every source vertex and is
exactly \noderef{CompatibleEmbedding}. Define $F(f)$ by these fields
with underlying function $f.toFun$. This constructs $F$ on every input,
not only on the support of $\mu$, and proves the displayed pointwise equality.

Let $e:X\simeq V_H$ be the bijection given by inclusion; its inverse
sends $x$ to $\langle x,x\in X\rangle$, using $X=V_H$.
The underlying full map of $F(f)$ is the restricted map of $f$ composed
with $e^{-1}$. Fix $s\in\mathbb N$, an injective map
$x:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to V_H$, and any prescribed host map
$v:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to V_G$. The map $e^{-1}\circ x$ is injective.
For each input $f$, the conditions
\[
 F(f)(x(k))=v(k)\quad\text{for every }k
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 f(e^{-1}(x(k)))=v(k)\quad\text{for every }k
\]
are identical. By \noderef{CylinderEvent}, these cylinders have the
same inverse image in the law on partial embeddings. The pushforward
mass formula, summing the original masses over each fibre, therefore
gives equal cylinder probabilities, including when $s=0$.
The assumed restriction-law bound gives probability at most $b^s$.
Also $b\leq1$ is part of the same \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} assumption.
These are precisely the two required clauses for the full underlying-map
law of $\mu\mathbin{\mathrm{map}}F$. Thus both maps and spread are
preserved, independently of how the full-domain law was obtained.
\end{proof}
EqualSizeTerminalConversion.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Full-domain terminal conversion]
Let $B$ be a finite blow-up instance with candidacy system $A$, let
$X\subseteq V_H$ be a finite set with $X=V_H$, and let $\mu$ be any law on
\noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} with domain $X$. Suppose the law of
the restricted maps $x\in X\mapsto f(x)$ is $b$-vertex-spread on the whole
host vertex set in the sense of \noderef{VertexSpreadOn}.
There is a map $F$ from these partial embeddings to full injective graph
homomorphisms $H\hookrightarrow G$ satisfying \noderef{CompatibleEmbedding},
such that $F(f)(x)=f(x)$ for every $f$ and every $x\in V_H$.
The pushforward $\mu\mathbin{\mathrm{map}}F$ has $b$-vertex-spread
underlying maps on the whole host vertex set.
\end{lemma}

classical
  intro Delta r n hDelta VH VG _ _ _ H G R _ B hmax hcluster
  let X : Fin r -> Type _ := fun i => {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i}

    SimpleGraph.fromRel fun x y => exists z : VH, H.Adj x.1 z ∧ H.Adj y.1 z

    (H.degree_le_maxDegree x).trans hmax

    rw [Nat.le_sub_one_iff_lt (by positivity)]
    rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborSet_eq_degree]

          exists z : VH, H.Adj x.1 z ∧ H.Adj y.1.1 z := by
        have hy : (Q i).Adj x y.1 := y.2
        exact ((SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj _ _ _).mp hy).2.elim id fun h =>
          ⟨h.choose, h.choose_spec.2, h.choose_spec.1⟩

      have hchooseZ (y : (Q i).neighborSet x) :

        exact Classical.choose_spec (hcommon y)

  let c : (i : Fin r) -> X i -> Fin (Delta ^ 2) := fun i =>
    Classical.choose (hcolor i)

theorem EquitableSquareColoring :
    ∀ (Delta r n : ℕ), 1 ≤ Delta →
      ∀ {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH]
        {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
        [DecidableRel H.Adj] (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R),
        H.maxDegree ≤ Delta →
        (∀ i, (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = i).card = n) →
        ∃ color : VH → Fin (Delta ^ 2),
          (∀ i j,
            let s := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH =>
              B.sourceCluster x = i ∧ color x = j
            s.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ s.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1) ∧
          ∀ {x y}, B.sourceCluster x = B.sourceCluster y → color x = color y →
            x ≠ y → ¬ H.Adj x y ∧ ¬ ∃ z, H.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj y z := by

classical

      exact ⟨S, fun w hw => (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hS hw)).1,
        fun w hw => (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hS hw)).2, fun _ => hcard⟩
    · exact ⟨∅, by simp, by simp, fun h => (hu h).elim⟩
  have hchooseW : ∀ w : V, ∃ S : Finset V,

    intro w
    by_cases hw : w ∈ BW

        fun u hu => (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hS hu)).2, fun _ => hcard⟩

  choose SW hSWsub hSWadj hSWcard using hchooseW
  have hdis : ∀ v ∈ U, v ∉ W := fun v hv hw => Finset.disjoint_left.mp hUW hv hw

    (u ∈ BU ∧ v ∈ SU u) ∨ (u ∈ BW ∧ v ∈ SW u)

    intro u v h
    rcases h with h | h
    · exact hSUadj u v h.2
    · exact hSWadj u v h.2
  let G : SimpleGraph V :=
    { Adj := fun u v => F.Adj u v ∨ E u v ∨ E v u
      symm := by
        intro u v huv
        rcases huv with huv | huv | huv
        · exact Or.inl huv.symm
        · exact Or.inr (Or.inr huv)
        · exact Or.inr (Or.inl huv)
      loopless := by
        constructor
        intro u huv
        rcases huv with huv | huv | huv
        · exact F.loopless.irrefl u huv
        · exact H.loopless.irrefl u (hEH u u huv)
        · exact H.loopless.irrefl u (hEH u u huv) }

    intro u v huv

    intro u hu

    have hu0 := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hu).2

    constructor

      obtain ⟨hwW, huw⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hw

        · exact (hdis u huU (hW₀ hf.1)).elim

      · exact (hu0 (hSWsub w hs.2)).elim

  have hexW : ∀ w ∈ BW, U.filter (fun u => G.Adj w u) = SW w := by
    intro w hw
    have hwW := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).1
    have hw0 := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).2

      obtain ⟨huU, hwu⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hu

      · rcases hFs hf with hf | hf

        · exact (hdis w (hU₀ hf.2) hwW).elim
      · exact (hw0 (hSUsub u hs.2)).elim
      · exact hs.2
    · intro hu
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hU₀ (hSWsub w hu),
        ((hcross u (hU₀ (hSWsub w hu)) w hwW).mpr
          (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hw, hu⟩))).symm⟩
  have hcoreU : ∀ u ∈ U₀,

    constructor
    · apply Finset.card_le_card
      intro u hu
      obtain ⟨hu0, hf⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hu
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hU₀ hu0, hFG hf⟩

        obtain ⟨huU, hg⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hu
        by_cases hu0 : u ∈ U₀

        · exact Finset.mem_union_right _ (Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨huU, hu0⟩)

  exact ⟨G, inferInstance, hGH, hFG, hagree,
    fun u hu => (congrArg Finset.card (hexU u hu)).trans (hSUcard u hu),
    fun w hw => (congrArg Finset.card (hexW w hw)).trans (hSWcard w hw),
    hcoreU, hcoreW⟩
ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension.lean_statement:
theorem ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H F : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel F.Adj]
    (U W U₀ W₀ : Finset V) (k : ℕ)
    (hUW : Disjoint U W) (hU₀ : U₀ ⊆ U) (hW₀ : W₀ ⊆ W)
    (hFH : F ≤ H)
    (hFs : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, F.Adj u v →
      (u ∈ U₀ ∧ v ∈ W₀) ∨ (u ∈ W₀ ∧ v ∈ U₀))
    (hNU : ∀ u ∈ U \ U₀, k ≤ (W₀.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card)
    (hNW : ∀ w ∈ W \ W₀, k ≤ (U₀.filter fun u => H.Adj w u).card) :
    ∃ G : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G.Adj,
      G ≤ H ∧ F ≤ G ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U₀, ∀ w ∈ W₀, G.Adj u w ↔ F.Adj u w) ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U \ U₀, (W.filter fun w => G.Adj u w).card = k) ∧
      (∀ w ∈ W \ W₀, (U.filter fun u => G.Adj w u).card = k) ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U₀,
        (W₀.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card ≤ (W.filter fun w => G.Adj u w).card ∧
        (W.filter fun w => G.Adj u w).card ≤
          (W₀.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card + (W \ W₀).card) ∧
      (∀ w ∈ W₀,
        (U₀.filter fun u => F.Adj w u).card ≤ (U.filter fun u => G.Adj w u).card ∧
        (U.filter fun u => G.Adj w u).card ≤
          (U₀.filter fun u => F.Adj w u).card + (U \ U₀).card) := by
ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension.name: ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension
ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For each exceptional vertex choose a $k$-element subset of its neighbors
in the opposite core. Such a subset exists by the cardinality hypothesis.
Add all chosen edges, in both orientations, to $F$ to obtain $G$.
All added edges belong to $H$, which proves containment and looplessness;
including both orientations proves symmetry. Finite adjacency is decidable.
An added edge has exactly one exceptional endpoint, since the other endpoint
is in the opposite core and the full parts are disjoint. In particular no
added edge joins two core vertices, so $G$ agrees with $F$ on the core.
The support hypothesis on $F$ gives an exceptional vertex no old neighbors.
No other exceptional vertex can prescribe an edge incident to it, because
every prescribed opposite endpoint is in a core. Its opposite-part neighbor
set is therefore exactly its chosen set, of size $k$.
For a core vertex in $U_0$, all old neighbors lie in $W_0$, all such edges
are retained, and every new opposite-part neighbor lies in $W\setminus W_0$.
Its neighbor set is thus contained in the union of its old neighbor set
with $W\setminus W_0$. Taking cardinalities proves the two bounds.
The identical argument for a vertex in $W_0$ proves the other bounds.
\end{proof}
ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Extending a core by exceptional rows]
Let $H,F$ be finite simple graphs on the same vertex set, and let
$U,W$ be disjoint finite sets with $U_0\subseteq U,W_0\subseteq W$.
Suppose $F\subseteq H$ and every edge of $F$ joins $U_0$ to $W_0$.
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Suppose each vertex of $U\setminus U_0$
has at least $k$ neighbors in $W_0$ in $H$, and each vertex of
$W\setminus W_0$ has at least $k$ neighbors in $U_0$ in $H$.
There is a simple graph $F\subseteq G\subseteq H$ on the same vertex set
which agrees with $F$ between $U_0,W_0$, gives each exceptional vertex
exactly $k$ neighbors in the opposite full part, and satisfies
\[
\deg_F(u,W_0)\leq\deg_G(u,W)\leq\deg_F(u,W_0)+|W\setminus W_0|
\quad(u\in U_0),
\]
and the analogous inequalities with $U,W$ exchanged.
\end{lemma}
ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension.title: ExceptionalCoreEdgeExtension

      ε' * ((L₀ \ D_L).card : ENNReal))

      (d - ε) * (R₀.card : ENNReal) - (D_R.card : ENNReal))
    (hRightDegree : (d' - ε') * ((L₀ \ D_L).card : ENNReal) ≤
      (d - ε) * (L₀.card : ENNReal) - (D_L.card : ENNReal) -

      (d' - ε') * ((R₀ \ D_R).card : ENNReal) ≤

ExceptionalLeftLowerSuperRegular.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $e_J(S,T)$ for the number of ordered edges from $S$ to $T$ in a graph
$J$, as in \noderef{PairDensity}.  We verify separately the three clauses of
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}.

First consider an ordinary vertex $x\in L\setminus E$.  Lower
$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regularity of $(L_0,R_0)$ gives
\[
 |N_{G_0}(x)\cap R_0|\geq(d-\varepsilon)|R_0|.
\]
Passing from $R_0$ to the exact residual part $R=R_0\setminus D_R$ deletes at
most $|D_R|$ of these neighbors.  The exact ordinary-row equality between
$G$ and $G_0$ on $R$ and the first degree-margin inequality therefore give
\[
 |N_G(x)\cap R|\geq(d-\varepsilon)|R_0|-|D_R|
 \geq(d'-\varepsilon')|R|.
\]
For $x\in E$ the same conclusion is precisely the exceptional-row hypothesis.
Thus every vertex of $L$ has the required degree into $R$.

Next fix $y\in R$.  In $G_0$ it has at least
$(d-\varepsilon)|L_0|$ neighbors in $L_0$.  At most $|D_L|$ of these lie in
the deleted left part.  On the remaining ordinary rows $L\setminus E$, the
adjacency relation is unchanged; discarding all $|E|$ exceptional rows covers
every possible further loss caused by the update.  Consequently
\[
 |N_G(y)\cap L|\geq(d-\varepsilon)|L_0|-|D_L|-|E|
 \geq(d'-\varepsilon')|L|.
\]
This proves the right-degree clause.

It remains to prove lower regularity rather than assume it.  Take
$S\subseteq L$ and $T\subseteq R$ with
$|S|>\varepsilon'|L|$ and $|T|>\varepsilon'|R|$.  The two threshold-transfer
inequalities imply $|S|>\varepsilon|L_0|$ and
$|T|>\varepsilon|R_0|$.  Lower regularity of the original pair, which is part
of its lower-super-regularity, hence yields
\[
 e_{G_0}(S,T)\geq(d-\varepsilon)|S||T|.
\]
Every ordered edge whose left endpoint is in $S\setminus E$ is preserved in
$G$, so at most $|S\cap E||T|\leq |E||T|$ ordered edges can be lost.  Since
$|E|\leq\eta|L|$ and $|S|>\varepsilon'|L|$, positivity of $\varepsilon'$ gives
$|E|/|S|\leq\eta/\varepsilon'$.  Dividing by $|S||T|$ gives
\[
 d_G(S,T)\geq d-\varepsilon-\frac{\eta}{\varepsilon'}
 \geq d'-\varepsilon',
\]
where the last inequality is the density-margin hypothesis.  Thus $(L,R)$ is
lower $(\varepsilon',d')$-regular.  This regularity conclusion and the two
degree conclusions are exactly the three clauses of
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}, completing the proof.
\end{proof}
ExceptionalLeftLowerSuperRegular.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Exceptional-row slicing for a candidacy pair]
Let $(L_0,R_0)$ be a lower $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular pair in a graph $G_0$.  Let $D_L\subseteq L_0$ and $D_R\subseteq R_0$, put
\[
 L=L_0\setminus D_L,\qquad R=R_0\setminus D_R,
\]
and let $E\subseteq L$.  Let $G$ be an updated graph such that, for every $x\in L\setminus E$ and $y\in R$,
\[
 xy\in E(G)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad xy\in E(G_0).
\]
Suppose that $0<\varepsilon'<\infty$, $|E|\leq\eta|L|$, and
\[
 \varepsilon|L_0|\leq\varepsilon'|L|,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon|R_0|\leq\varepsilon'|R|,
 \qquad
 (d'-\varepsilon')+\frac{\eta}{\varepsilon'}\leq d-\varepsilon.
\]
Suppose also that
\[
 (d'-\varepsilon')|R|\leq (d-\varepsilon)|R_0|-|D_R|
\]
and
\[
 (d'-\varepsilon')|L|\leq (d-\varepsilon)|L_0|-|D_L|-|E|.
\]
Finally, suppose that every exceptional vertex $x\in E$ has at least
$(d'-\varepsilon')|R|$ neighbors in $R$ in $G$.  Then $(L,R)$ is lower
$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular in $G$.
\end{lemma}

theorem ExceptionalRectangleDensity
    {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (F G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel F.Adj] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (U W U₀ W₀ : Finset V) (n : ℕ) (c h η : ℝ)
    (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hh : 0 < h) (hhc : h ≤ c / 100)
    (hη : 0 < η) (h3 : 3 * h < η)
    (hbudget : 2 * h + 4 * h / η < η) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hbadU : ((U \ U₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n)
    (hbadW : ((W \ W₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n)
    (hagree : ∀ u ∈ U₀, ∀ w ∈ W₀, G.Adj u w ↔ F.Adj u w)
    (hrect : ∀ A ⊆ U₀, ∀ B ⊆ W₀, h * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
      h * n < (B.card : ℝ) → |(F.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) - c| ≤ 2 * h) :
    ∀ X ⊆ U, ∀ Y ⊆ W, η * n < (X.card : ℝ) →
      η * n < (Y.card : ℝ) → |(G.edgeDensity X Y : ℝ) - c| < η := by

ExceptionalRectangleDensity.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $X_0=X\cap U_0$, $Y_0=Y\cap W_0$, and write
$a=|X|,b=|Y|,a_0=|X_0|,b_0=|Y_0|$.
Since $X\setminus U_0\subseteq U\setminus U_0$, we have
$a-a_0\leq2hn$, and similarly $b-b_0\leq2hn$.
The size tests and $3h<\eta$ imply $a_0,b_0>hn>0$.
In particular all four tested sets are nonempty.
The number of positions outside $X_0\times Y_0$ is
$R=ab-a_0b_0\geq0$. Because $a_0\leq a,b_0\leq b$,
\[
R=(a-a_0)b+a(b-b_0)-(a-a_0)(b-b_0)
\leq2hn(a+b)\leq(4h/\eta)ab.
\]
For the last bound multiply $a,b>\eta n$ by $2h/\eta>0$,
and then by $b,a$, respectively, and add the resulting inequalities.
Let $e_0$ count the edges of $F$ in $X_0\times Y_0$, and let $e$ count
the edges of $G$ in $X\times Y$.
Agreement on the core gives $e_0\leq e\leq e_0+R$.
By \noderef{PairDensityReal}, the core density hypothesis, multiplied by
$a_0b_0>0$, gives
$(c-2h)a_0b_0\leq e_0\leq(c+2h)a_0b_0$.
Here $0<c-2h<1$, using $h\leq c/100$, $h>0$, and $c<1$.
Consequently
\[
e\geq(c-2h)(ab-R)\geq(c-2h)ab-R
\geq(c-2h-4h/\eta)ab,
\]
whereas $a_0b_0\leq ab$ gives
$e\leq(c+2h)ab+R\leq(c+2h+4h/\eta)ab$.
Divide by $ab>0$ and apply \noderef{PairDensityReal} to the full rectangle.
The budget $2h+4h/\eta<\eta$ yields the claimed strict density bound.
\end{proof}
ExceptionalRectangleDensity.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Density after exceptional-position changes]
Let $F,G$ be simple graphs on the same vertex set, and let $U,W,U_0,W_0$ be finite vertex
sets. Let $n>0$ be an integer and let real numbers satisfy
$0<c<1$, $0<h\leq c/100$, $0<\eta$, $3h<\eta$, and
$2h+4h/\eta<\eta$. Suppose
$|U\setminus U_0|,|W\setminus W_0|\leq2hn$, and $G$ agrees with $F$
between $U_0,W_0$. Suppose
$|d_F(A,B)-c|\leq2h$ for every $A\subseteq U_0,B\subseteq W_0$
with $|A|,|B|>hn$.
Then $|d_G(X,Y)-c|<\eta$ for all $X\subseteq U,Y\subseteq W$
with $|X|,|Y|>\eta n$.
\end{lemma}

    exact tsub_pos_iff_lt.mpr hdecrease
ExposureDensityRecursion.lean_statement:
theorem ExposureDensityRecursion (d : ENNReal) (Delta : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1) :
    ∃ p rho : ℕ → ENNReal,
      p 0 = d ∧
      (∀ x, x ≤ Delta → 0 < p x ∧ p x ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < rho x ∧ rho x < p x) ∧
      (∀ x, x < Delta → p (x + 1) = rho x * (d / 2)) ∧
      (∀ x, x < Delta → 0 < p x - p (x + 1)) := by
ExposureDensityRecursion.name: ExposureDensityRecursion
ExposureDensityRecursion.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For every nonnegative integer $x$ set $p_x=d(d/4)^x$ and
$\rho_x=p_x/2$. These are finite positive numbers since $0<d\leq1$.
Because $d/4\leq1$, one has $p_x\leq1$; division of the positive finite
$p_x$ by two gives $0<\rho_x<p_x$. Direct multiplication gives
$p_{x+1}=p_xd/4=\rho_x(d/2)$. Since $d/2\leq1$,
$p_{x+1}\leq\rho_x<p_x$, so truncated subtraction agrees with ordinary
positive subtraction and $p_x-p_{x+1}>0$. These formulas define the
sequences even beyond $\Delta$. When $\Delta=0$ the gap and recursion
requirements are empty and the assertions at exposure zero still hold.
\end{proof}
ExposureDensityRecursion.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Exposure densities and their positive gaps]
For $0<d\leq1$ and $\Delta\in\mathbb N$, there are total sequences
$p,\rho:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty]$ such that $p_0=d$,
$0<p_x\leq1$ and $0<\rho_x<p_x$ for $x\leq\Delta$,
$p_{x+1}=\rho_x(d/2)$ for $x<\Delta$, and
$p_x-p_{x+1}>0$ for $x<\Delta$.
\end{lemma}
ExposureDensityRecursion.title: ExposureDensityRecursion

ExtendUpdatedPartialEmbedding.lean_proof:
let h : VH → VG := fun z => if z ∈ X then f.toFun z else g.toFun z
  have hX : ∀ x ∈ X, h x = f.toFun x := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [h, if_pos hx]
  have hY : ∀ y ∈ Y, h y = g.toFun y := by
    intro y hy
    have hyX : y ∉ X := fun hx => Finset.disjoint_left.mp hXY hx hy
    simp only [h, if_neg hyX]
  refine ⟨{ toFun := h, injOn := ?_, map_adj := ?_, compatible := ?_ }, hX, hY⟩
  · intro x hx y hy heq
    change x ∈ X ∪ Y at hx
    change y ∈ X ∪ Y at hy
    rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hx with hx | hx <;>
      rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hy with hy | hy
    · rw [hX x hx, hX y hy] at heq
      exact f.injOn hx hy heq
    · rw [hX x hx, hY y hy] at heq
      exact False.elim ((g.compatible y hy).2.1
        (Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hx, heq⟩))
    · rw [hY x hx, hX y hy] at heq
      exact False.elim ((g.compatible x hx).2.1
        (Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨y, hy, heq.symm⟩))
    · rw [hY x hx, hY y hy] at heq
      exact g.injOn hx hy heq
  · intro x y hx hy hadj
    rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hx with hx | hx <;>
      rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hy with hy | hy
    · rw [hX x hx, hX y hy]
      exact f.map_adj hx hy hadj
    · rw [hX x hx, hY y hy]
      exact G.symm ((g.compatible y hy).2.2.2 x hx (H.symm hadj))
    · rw [hY x hx, hX y hy]
      exact (g.compatible x hx).2.2.2 y hy hadj
    · rw [hY x hx, hY y hy]
      exact g.map_adj hx hy hadj
  · intro z hz
    rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hz with hz | hz
    · rw [hX z hz]
      exact f.compatible z hz
    · rw [hY z hz]
      exact (g.compatible z hz).2.2.1

theorem ExtendUpdatedPartialEmbedding {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (X Y : Finset VH) (hXY : Disjoint X Y)
    (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)
    (g : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f) Y) :
    ∃ h : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A (X ∪ Y),
      (∀ x ∈ X, h.toFun x = f.toFun x) ∧
      (∀ y ∈ Y, h.toFun y = g.toFun y) := by

have linear : ∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a →
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 4 * n * Real.exp (-a * (n : ℝ)) < 1 / 4 := by
    intro a ha
    have hscale : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => a * (n : ℝ)) atTop atTop :=
      tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop.const_mul_atTop ha
    have hlim : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => 4 * n * Real.exp (-a * (n : ℝ)))
        atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      have ht := ((Real.tendsto_pow_mul_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero 1).comp hscale).const_mul
        (4 / a)
      convert ht using 1
      · ext n
        simp only [Function.comp_def, pow_one]
        field_simp
      · simp
    exact hlim.eventually_lt_const (by norm_num)
  have quadratic : ∀ b : ℝ, 0 < b →
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n *
        Real.exp (-b * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) < 1 / 4 := by
    intro b hb
    have hlarge : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (Real.log 4 + 1) / b ≤ (n : ℝ) :=
      tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop.eventually_ge_atTop _
    have hlim : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => 2 * Real.exp (-(n : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa using (Real.tendsto_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero.comp
        tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop).const_mul (2 : ℝ)
    filter_upwards [hlarge, hlim.eventually_lt_const (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 4)]
      with n hlarge hsmall
    have hlin := (div_le_iff₀ hb).mp hlarge
    have hprod := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hlin (Nat.cast_nonneg n : (0 : ℝ) ≤ n)
    have hexp : (n : ℝ) * Real.log 4 - b * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ -(n : ℝ) := by
      nlinarith only [hprod]
    calc
      2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-b * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)
          = 2 * Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log 4 - b * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
        rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Real.exp_add, Real.exp_nat_mul,
          Real.exp_log (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 4)]
        ring
      _ ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-(n : ℝ)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hexp) (by norm_num)
      _ < 1 / 4 := hsmall
  have h₁ := linear (c ^ 2 / 8) (by positivity)
  have h₂ := quadratic (h ^ 4 / 8) (by positivity)
  have h₃ := linear (2 * h ^ 2) (by positivity)
  have h₄ := quadratic (2 * h ^ 4) (by positivity)
  have hfloor : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 1 / h ≤ (n : ℝ) :=
    tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop.eventually_ge_atTop _
  have hall : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      1 ≤ h * (n : ℝ) ∧
      4 * n * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) < 1 / 4 ∧
      2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) < 1 / 4 ∧
      4 * n * Real.exp (-2 * h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ)) < 1 / 4 ∧
      2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-2 * h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) < 1 / 4 := by
    filter_upwards [hfloor, h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄] with n hf h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have hf' := (div_le_iff₀ hh).mp hf
      simpa only [mul_comm] using hf'
    · convert h₁ using 1 <;> congr 2 <;> ring
    · convert h₂ using 1 <;> congr 2 <;> ring
    · convert h₃ using 1 <;> congr 2 <;> ring
    · convert h₄ using 1 <;> congr 2 <;> ring
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := hall.exists_forall_of_atTop
  refine ⟨max 1 (max M N), le_max_left _ _,
    (le_max_left M N).trans (le_max_right _ _), ?_⟩
  intro n hn
  exact hN n (((le_max_right M N).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans hn)
ExtractionTailCutoffs.lean_statement:
open Filter
open scoped Topology

theorem ExtractionTailCutoffs (c h : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (hc : 0 < c) (hh : 0 < h) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n₀ ∧ M ≤ n₀ ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
        1 ≤ h * (n : ℝ) ∧
        4 * n * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) < 1 / 4 ∧
        2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) < 1 / 4 ∧
        4 * n * Real.exp (-2 * h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ)) < 1 / 4 ∧
        2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-2 * h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) < 1 / 4 := by
ExtractionTailCutoffs.name: ExtractionTailCutoffs
ExtractionTailCutoffs.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
All four expressions are positive for $n\geq1$. For $a>0$,
$\log(4n)-an$ tends to $-\infty$: indeed
$\log n/n\to0$, so eventually $\log n\leq an/2$, and then
$\log(4n)-an\leq\log4-an/2$.
This applies with $a=c^2/8>0$ and $a=2h^2>0$ to the first and
third expressions. For $b>0$, the logarithm of
$2\,4^n e^{-bn^2}$ is $\log2+n\log4-bn^2$.
For $n\geq2\log4/b$, it is at most $\log2-bn^2/2$, which
tends to $-\infty$. Apply this with $b=h^4/8>0$ and
$b=2h^4>0$ to the second and fourth expressions. Thus each
logarithm is eventually strictly less than $\log(1/4)$, and
monotonicity of the exponential gives the four required strict bounds.
Choose integer cutoffs for these four eventual statements. Their
maximum, enlarged to include $M$, $1$, and $\lceil1/h\rceil$, is
$n_0$. For every $n\geq n_0$, multiplication of $n\geq1/h$ by
$h>0$ gives $hn\geq1$, and all four eventual bounds remain valid.
Every choice depends only on $c,h,M$.
\end{proof}
ExtractionTailCutoffs.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform extraction tail cutoffs]
For real $c,h>0$ and an integer $M\geq0$, there is an integer
$n_0\geq\max\{1,M\}$ such that, for every integer $n\geq n_0$,
$hn\geq1$ and each of
\[
4n e^{-c^2n/8},\qquad 2\,4^n e^{-h^4n^2/8},\qquad
4n e^{-2h^2n},\qquad 2\,4^n e^{-2h^4n^2}
\]
is strictly less than $1/4$.
\end{lemma}
ExtractionTailCutoffs.title: ExtractionTailCutoffs

FactorialRootExceptionalProduct.lean_proof:
classical
  let a : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => Real.rpow (n.factorial : ℝ) (n : ℝ)⁻¹
  have apos (n : ℕ) : 0 < a n := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by positivity) _
  have ratio (m y : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hmy : m ≤ y) :
      a m / a y ≤ (m : ℝ) / y * Real.exp ((Real.log y + 1) / m) := by
    have hy : 0 < y := hm.trans_le hmy
    have hmR : 0 < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
    have hyR : 0 < (y : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hy
    have hlogs : Real.log m ≤ Real.log y := Real.log_le_log hmR (by exact_mod_cast hmy)
    have hu : Real.log (m.factorial : ℝ) / m ≤
        Real.log m - 1 + (Real.log y + 1) / m := by
      apply (div_le_iff₀ hmR).2
      have hb := (LogFactorialBounds m hm).2
      have hid : (Real.log m - 1 + (Real.log y + 1) / m) * m =
          (m : ℝ) * Real.log m - m + Real.log y + 1 := by field_simp; ring
      rw [hid]
      linarith
    have hl : Real.log y - 1 ≤ Real.log (y.factorial : ℝ) / y := by
      apply (le_div_iff₀ hyR).2
      nlinarith [(LogFactorialBounds y hy).1]
    have hlog : Real.log (m.factorial : ℝ) / m - Real.log (y.factorial : ℝ) / y ≤
        Real.log ((m : ℝ) / y) + (Real.log y + 1) / m := by
      rw [Real.log_div hmR.ne' hyR.ne']
      linarith
    dsimp [a]
    rw [Real.rpow_def_of_pos (by positivity), Real.rpow_def_of_pos (by positivity),
      ← Real.exp_sub]
    simp only [← div_eq_mul_inv]
    calc
      _ ≤ Real.exp (Real.log ((m : ℝ) / y) + (Real.log y + 1) / m) :=
        Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hlog
      _ = _ := by rw [Real.exp_add, Real.exp_log (div_pos hmR hyR)]
  let x := D + 2 * θ
  let γ := Real.log ((x + θ) / x) - θ * Real.log (1 / x)
  have hx : 0 < x := by dsimp [x]; positivity
  have hxθ : 0 < x + θ := by positivity
  have hx1 : x < 1 := by dsimp [x]; linarith
  have hlogx : Real.log x < 0 := Real.log_neg hx hx1
  have hγ : 0 < γ := by
    have hl : 0 < Real.log (1 / x) := Real.log_pos ((one_lt_div hx).2 hx1)
    have he : 2 ≤ Real.exp 1 := by linarith [Real.add_one_le_exp 1]
    have hmax : x * Real.log (1 / x) ≤ 1 / Real.exp 1 := by
      have ht := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos (one_div_pos.mpr hx) (Real.exp_pos 1))
      rw [Real.log_div (by positivity) (Real.exp_ne_zero 1), Real.log_exp] at ht
      have ht' := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ht hx.le
      have hid : x * (1 / x / Real.exp 1 - 1) = 1 / Real.exp 1 - x := by field_simp
      rw [hid] at ht'
      nlinarith
    have hhalf : x * Real.log (1 / x) ≤ 1 / 2 :=
      hmax.trans (one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by norm_num) he)
    have hsmall : (x + θ) * Real.log (1 / x) < 1 := by
      have hθx : θ < x / 2 := by dsimp [x]; linarith
      nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hθx hl]
    have hstrict := Real.log_lt_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos hx hxθ)
      (show x / (x + θ) ≠ 1 by
        intro h; have := (div_eq_one_iff_eq hxθ.ne').1 h; linarith)
    rw [Real.log_div hx.ne' hxθ.ne'] at hstrict
    have hstrict' : θ / (x + θ) < Real.log ((x + θ) / x) := by
      rw [Real.log_div hxθ.ne' hx.ne']
      have hid : x / (x + θ) - 1 = -(θ / (x + θ)) := by field_simp; ring
      rw [hid] at hstrict
      linarith
    have habs : θ * Real.log (1 / x) < θ / (x + θ) := by
      apply (lt_div_iff₀ hxθ).2
      nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hsmall hθ]
    dsimp [γ]
    linarith
  have threshold : ∃ y₀ : ℕ, 0 < y₀ ∧ ∀ y : ℕ, y₀ ≤ y →
      1 / (y : ℝ) ≤ θ ∧ (Real.log y + 1) / (θ * y) ≤ γ / 2 := by
    have hcast : Tendsto (fun y : ℕ => (y : ℝ)) atTop atTop := tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop
    have hinv : Tendsto (fun y : ℕ => 1 / (y : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
      tendsto_const_nhds.div_atTop hcast
    have hlog : Tendsto (fun y : ℕ => Real.log y / (θ * y)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa using (Real.tendsto_pow_log_div_mul_add_atTop θ 0 1 hθ.ne').comp hcast
    have hone : Tendsto (fun y : ℕ => 1 / (θ * y)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
      tendsto_const_nhds.div_atTop (hcast.const_mul_atTop hθ)
    have hdelta : Tendsto (fun y : ℕ => (Real.log y + 1) / (θ * y)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
      simpa only [zero_add, ← add_div] using hlog.add hone
    have he : ∀ᶠ y : ℕ in atTop,
        1 ≤ y ∧ 1 / (y : ℝ) < θ ∧ (Real.log y + 1) / (θ * y) < γ / 2 := by
      filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 1, hinv.eventually_lt_const hθ,
        hdelta.eventually_lt_const (show 0 < γ / 2 by positivity)] with y hy hi hd
      exact ⟨hy, hi, hd⟩
    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀⟩ := eventually_atTop.1 he
    exact ⟨y₀, (hy₀ y₀ le_rfl).1, fun y hy =>
      ⟨(hy₀ y hy).2.1.le, (hy₀ y hy).2.2.le⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, hthreshold⟩ := threshold
  refine ⟨y₀, hy₀, ?_⟩
  intro y hyy₀ r hr hry hbad
  have hy : 0 < y := hy₀.trans_le hyy₀
  have hyR : 0 < (y : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hy
  have hy1 : 1 ≤ (y : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hy
  have hlogy : 0 ≤ Real.log y := Real.log_nonneg hy1
  obtain ⟨hinv, hδγ⟩ := hthreshold y hyy₀
  let δ := (Real.log y + 1) / (θ * y)
  have hδ : 0 ≤ δ := div_nonneg (by linarith) (by positivity)
  have hθy : 1 ≤ θ * y := (div_le_iff₀ hyR).1 hinv
  have controlled (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hmy : m ≤ y)
      (hlow : θ * y ≤ (m : ℝ)) (hupp : (m : ℝ) / y ≤ x) :
      a m / a y ≤ x * Real.exp δ := by
    apply (ratio m y hm hmy).trans
    apply mul_le_mul hupp _ (Real.exp_pos _).le hx.le
    apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_left (by linarith) (by positivity) hlow
  have hordinary (i : Fin y) (hi : ¬ (D + θ) * (y : ℝ) < (r i : ℝ)) :
      a (r i) / a y ≤ x * Real.exp δ := by
    by_cases hlarge : θ * y ≤ (r i : ℝ)
    · apply controlled (r i) (hr i) (hry i) hlarge
      apply (div_le_iff₀ hyR).2
      have : (r i : ℝ) ≤ (D + θ) * y := le_of_not_gt hi
      dsimp [x]
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg hθ.le hyR.le]
    · let s := Nat.ceil (θ * (y : ℝ))
      have hs : 0 < s := Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (by positivity)
      have hslow : θ * y ≤ (s : ℝ) := Nat.le_ceil _
      have hsup : (s : ℝ) < θ * y + 1 := Nat.ceil_lt_add_one (by positivity)
      have hsyR : (s : ℝ) ≤ (y : ℝ) := by
        have : 2 * θ < 1 := by linarith
        nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right this hyR]
      have hsy : s ≤ y := by exact_mod_cast hsyR
      have hrs : r i ≤ s := by
        have : (r i : ℝ) ≤ (s : ℝ) := (not_le.mp hlarge).le.trans hslow
        exact_mod_cast this
      have hsupx : (s : ℝ) / y ≤ x := by
        apply (div_le_iff₀ hyR).2
        dsimp [x]
        nlinarith [mul_nonneg hD.le hyR.le]
      exact (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (FactorialRootMonotone (r i) s (hr i) hrs)
        (apos y).le).trans (controlled s hs hsy hslow hsupx)
  let bad : Finset (Fin y) := Finset.univ.filter fun i => (D + θ) * (y : ℝ) < (r i : ℝ)
  let t : Fin y → ℝ := fun i => if i ∈ bad then 0 else Real.log x + δ
  have hrow (i : Fin y) : a (r i) ≤ a y * Real.exp (t i) := by
    by_cases hi : i ∈ bad
    · simp only [t, if_pos hi, Real.exp_zero, mul_one]
      exact FactorialRootMonotone (r i) y (hr i) (hry i)
    · have hni : ¬ (D + θ) * (y : ℝ) < (r i : ℝ) := by simpa [bad] using hi
      have hh := (div_le_iff₀ (apos y)).1 (hordinary i hni)
      simpa [t, hi, Real.exp_add, Real.exp_log hx, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc] using hh
  have hsum : ∑ i, t i = ((y : ℝ) - bad.card) * (Real.log x + δ) := by
    have ht (i : Fin y) : t i = (Real.log x + δ) -
        (if i ∈ bad then Real.log x + δ else 0) := by
      dsimp [t]; split_ifs <;> ring
    simp_rw [ht]
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    simp [Finset.sum_ite_mem, sub_mul]
    ring
  have hk : (bad.card : ℝ) ≤ θ * y := hbad
  have hk0 : 0 ≤ (bad.card : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg _
  have hexponent : ((y : ℝ) - bad.card) * (Real.log x + δ) ≤
      (y : ℝ) * Real.log (x + θ) := by
    have hsign := mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (sub_nonneg.mpr hk) hlogx.le
    have hδsign := mul_nonneg hk0 hδ
    have habs : (1 - θ) * Real.log x + δ ≤ Real.log (x + θ) := by
      have hδγ' : δ ≤ γ := hδγ.trans (by linarith)
      dsimp [γ] at hδγ'
      rw [Real.log_div hxθ.ne' hx.ne', Real.log_div one_ne_zero hx.ne', Real.log_one] at hδγ'
      nlinarith
    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left habs hyR.le]
  have hprod : (∏ i : Fin y, a (r i)) ≤ a y ^ y * Real.exp (∑ i, t i) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∏ i : Fin y, (a y * Real.exp (t i)) :=
        Finset.prod_le_prod (fun i _ => (apos (r i)).le) (fun i _ => hrow i)
      _ = _ := by rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib, ← Real.exp_sum]; simp
  have hpow : a y ^ y = (y.factorial : ℝ) :=
    Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow (by positivity) hy.ne'
  have hfinal : Real.exp (∑ i, t i) ≤ (D + 3 * θ) ^ y := by
    rw [hsum]
    have hh := Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hexponent
    rw [Real.exp_nat_mul, Real.exp_log hxθ] at hh
    have hxid : x + θ = D + 3 * θ := by dsimp [x]; ring
    simpa only [hxid] using hh
  change (∏ i : Fin y, a (r i)) ≤ _
  rw [hpow] at hprod
  exact hprod.trans (by simpa [mul_comm] using
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hfinal (Nat.cast_nonneg y.factorial))
FactorialRootExceptionalProduct.lean_statement:
open Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

theorem FactorialRootExceptionalProduct (D θ : ℝ)
    (hD : 0 < D) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hc : D + 3 * θ < 1) :
    ∃ y₀ : ℕ, 0 < y₀ ∧ ∀ (y : ℕ), y₀ ≤ y →
      ∀ (r : Fin y → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < r i) → (∀ i, r i ≤ y) →
        ((((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin y)).filter fun i =>
          (D + θ) * (y : ℝ) < (r i : ℝ)).card : ℝ) ≤ θ * (y : ℝ)) →
        (∏ i : Fin y, Real.rpow (Nat.factorial (r i) : ℝ) ((r i : ℝ)⁻¹)) ≤
          (D + 3 * θ) ^ y * (y.factorial : ℝ) := by
FactorialRootExceptionalProduct.name: FactorialRootExceptionalProduct
FactorialRootExceptionalProduct.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $a_r=(r!)^{1/r}$ for positive integers $r$.
This sequence is increasing: $a_r\le a_{r+1}$ is equivalent, after
raising to the positive power $r(r+1)$ and cancelling $(r!)^r$, to
$r!\le(r+1)^r$, which follows by bounding each factor by $r+1$.
For $1\le r\le y$, comparison of the increasing function $\log t$ with
its integrals over $[1,r]$ gives
\[
 r\log r-r\le\log(r!)\le r\log r-r+\log r+1.
\]
Indeed the lower bound follows from
$\sum_{j=2}^r\log j\ge\int_1^r\log t\,dt=r\log r-r+1$,
and the upper bound follows from
$\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}\log j\le\int_1^r\log t\,dt$ after adding $\log r$.
Consequently
\[
 \frac{a_r}{a_y}\le\frac r y
       \exp\left(\frac{\log y+1}{r}\right).                 \tag{1}
\]

Set $x=D+2\theta$ and
$\gamma=\log((x+\theta)/x)-\theta\log(1/x)$.
We have $0<x<x+\theta<1$ and $\theta<x/2$.
To see $\gamma>0$, integrating $1/t$ over $[x,x+\theta]$ gives
$\log(1+\theta/x)>\theta/(x+\theta)$.
The function $t\log(1/t)$ on $(0,1)$ has maximum $1/e$ (differentiate:
its derivative is $\log(1/t)-1$). Thus
$(x+\theta)\log(1/x)<(3/2)x\log(1/x)\le3/(2e)<1$,
and hence $\theta/(x+\theta)>\theta\log(1/x)$.
The elementary strict inequality $e>3/2$ follows, for example, by
integrating $\exp t\ge1$ over $[0,1]$ to obtain $e\ge2$.

Choose $y_0$ large enough that for all integers $y\ge y_0$,
$y>0$, $1/y\le\theta$, and
\[
 \delta_y:=\frac{\log y+1}{\theta y}\le\gamma/2.             \tag{2}
\]
This is possible since $\log y/y\to0$ and $1/y\to0$.
For completeness the former limit follows from
$\log y=\int_1^y t^{-1}dt\le\int_1^y t^{-1/2}dt
=2(\sqrt y-1)$ for $y\ge1$. These choices use only $D,\theta$.

For an exceptional index, monotonicity gives $a_{r_i}/a_y\le1$.
For a nonexceptional index with $r_i\ge\theta y$, (1) gives
$a_{r_i}/a_y\le(D+\theta)e^{\delta_y}\le xe^{\delta_y}$.
For a remaining index put $s=\lceil\theta y\rceil$.
Then $1\le s$, $r_i\le s$, and
$\theta y\le s\le\theta y+1\le2\theta y<y$,
the last inequality following from $3\theta<1$.
Apply monotonicity and (1) to $s$; since $s/y\le2\theta\le x$,
the same bound $a_{r_i}/a_y\le xe^{\delta_y}$ follows.
Thus all nonexceptional rows satisfy this bound and
\[
 \frac{\prod_i a_{r_i}}{y!}
 \le(xe^{\delta_y})^{y-k}
 =\exp((y-k)\log x+(y-k)\delta_y)
 \le\exp\bigl(y((1-\theta)\log x+\delta_y)\bigr).           \tag{3}
\]
Here $a_y^y=y!$, $\log x<0$, $k\le\theta y$, and
$0\le k\le y$, $\delta_y\ge0$ justify the last inequality even
when $xe^{\delta_y}$ is greater than one.
Finally
\[
 (1-\theta)\log x+\delta_y
 \le\log x+\theta\log(1/x)+\gamma
 =\log(x+\theta).
\]
Substituting this in (3), exponentiating, and multiplying by the
positive number $y!$ proves the claim.
\end{proof}
FactorialRootExceptionalProduct.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Factorial-root product with exceptional rows]
For real numbers $D>0$ and $\theta>0$ with $D+3\theta<1$, there is an
integer $y_0>0$ such that for every integer $y\ge y_0$ and positive
integers $r_0,\ldots,r_{y-1}\le y$, if
\[
 k:=|\{i:r_i>(D+\theta)y\}|\le\theta y,
\]
then
\[
 \prod_{i=0}^{y-1}(r_i!)^{1/r_i}\le(D+3\theta)^y y!.
\]
The threshold depends only on $D$ and $\theta$.
\end{lemma}
FactorialRootExceptionalProduct.title: FactorialRootExceptionalProduct

FactorialRootMonotone.lean_proof:
have step (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
      Real.rpow (n.factorial : ℝ) (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤
        Real.rpow ((n + 1).factorial : ℝ) ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
    have hnR : 0 < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hfac : 0 ≤ (n.factorial : ℝ) := by positivity
    have hroot : 0 ≤ Real.rpow (n.factorial : ℝ) (n : ℝ)⁻¹ :=
      Real.rpow_nonneg hfac _
    have hbound : Real.rpow (n.factorial : ℝ) (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ (n + 1 : ℕ) := by
      apply (Real.rpow_inv_le_iff_of_pos hfac (by positivity) hnR).2
      rw [Real.rpow_natCast]
      exact_mod_cast (Nat.factorial_le_pow n).trans
        (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (Nat.le_succ n) n)
    apply (Real.le_rpow_inv_iff_of_pos hroot (by positivity) (by positivity)).2
    have hpower : (Real.rpow (n.factorial : ℝ) (n : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ n =
        (n.factorial : ℝ) := Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow hfac (Nat.ne_of_gt hn)
    rw [Real.rpow_natCast, pow_succ, hpower, Nat.factorial_succ,
      Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one]
    simpa [mul_comm] using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbound hfac
  induction y, hmy using Nat.le_induction with
  | base => exact le_rfl
  | succ y hmy ih => exact ih.trans (step y (hm.trans_le hmy))
FactorialRootMonotone.lean_statement:
theorem FactorialRootMonotone (m y : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hmy : m ≤ y) :
    Real.rpow (m.factorial : ℝ) (m : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤
      Real.rpow (y.factorial : ℝ) (y : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
FactorialRootMonotone.name: FactorialRootMonotone
FactorialRootMonotone.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
First fix a positive integer $n$ and put $a=(n!)^{1/n}$.
Every factor in $n!=\prod_{j=1}^n j$ is at most $n+1$, so
$n!\le(n+1)^n$. Since $a\ge0$ and $a^n=n!$, taking the
positive $n$th root gives $a\le n+1$. Consequently
\[
 a^{n+1}=a^n a=n!a\le n!(n+1)=(n+1)!.
\]
Taking the positive $(n+1)$st root proves
$(n!)^{1/n}\le((n+1)!)^{1/(n+1)}$.
Starting at $n=m$ and applying this adjacent inequality successively
for $n=m,m+1,\ldots,y-1$ gives the desired inequality by transitivity.
When $m=y$, the assertion is equality, so no adjacent step is required.
\end{proof}
FactorialRootMonotone.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of positive factorial roots]
For positive integers $m$ and $y$ with $m\le y$,
\[
 (m!)^{1/m}\le (y!)^{1/y}.
\]
\end{lemma}
FactorialRootMonotone.title: FactorialRootMonotone

FiberwiseCapacityRefinement.lean_proof:
classical
  let f : X → V := fun x => (e (a x) ⟨x, rfl⟩).val
  have hf (x : X) : b (f x) = a x := (e (a x) ⟨x, rfl⟩).property
  have hfiber (x : X) (i : I) (h : a x = i) :
      f x = (e i ⟨x, h⟩).val := by
    subst i
    rfl
  have hfi : Function.Injective f := by
    intro x y h
    have hi : a x = a y := (hf x).symm.trans ((congrArg b h).trans (hf y))
    have hey := hfiber y (a x) hi.symm
    exact congrArg Subtype.val ((e (a x)).injective (Subtype.ext (h.trans hey)))
  let d : V → J := fun v => if h : ∃ x, f x = v then c h.choose else j₀
  have hd (x : X) : d (f x) = c x := by
    dsimp [d]
    rw [dif_pos ⟨x, rfl⟩]
    exact congrArg c (hfi (Classical.choose_spec (show ∃ y, f y = f x from ⟨x, rfl⟩)))
  refine ⟨d, fun i j => Fintype.card_le_of_injective
    (fun x => (⟨f x.val, (hf x.val).trans x.property.1,
      (hd x.val).trans x.property.2⟩ : {v : V // b v = i ∧ d v = j})) ?_⟩
  intro x y h
  exact Subtype.ext (hfi (congrArg Subtype.val h))
FiberwiseCapacityRefinement.lean_statement:
theorem FiberwiseCapacityRefinement
    {I J X V : Type*} [Fintype X] [Fintype V] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq J]
    (a : X → I) (b : V → I) (c : X → J) (j₀ : J)
    (e : ∀ i, {x : X // a x = i} ↪ {v : V // b v = i}) :
    ∃ d : V → J, ∀ i j,
      Fintype.card {x : X // a x = i ∧ c x = j} ≤
        Fintype.card {v : V // b v = i ∧ d v = j} := by
FiberwiseCapacityRefinement.name: FiberwiseCapacityRefinement
FiberwiseCapacityRefinement.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For $x\in X$, define $f(x)$ to be the underlying vertex of
$e_{a(x)}(x)$.  Then $b(f(x))=a(x)$.
If $f(x)=f(y)$, applying $b$ gives $a(x)=a(y)=i$.
Both images can therefore be compared in the same fiber $b^{-1}(i)$,
where injectivity of $e_i$ gives $x=y$.  Thus $f:X\to V$ is injective.
For $v\in f(X)$, let $x$ be its unique preimage and set $d(v)=c(x)$.
For $v\notin f(X)$, set $d(v)=j_0$.  This defines $d$ on all of $V$,
and $d(f(x))=c(x)$ for every $x$.
Consequently $f$ restricts to an injection from
$\{x:a(x)=i,c(x)=j\}$ to $\{v:b(v)=i,d(v)=j\}$.
The cardinality inequality for this injection gives the assertion at
every pair $(i,j)$.  Empty fibers give empty restricted injections, and
unused host vertices are covered by the default color.
\end{proof}
FiberwiseCapacityRefinement.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Refining finite capacities by colors]
Let $X,V$ be finite sets, $I,J$ be index sets, $a:X\to I$ and
$b:V\to I$ be total maps, $c:X\to J$ be a coloring, and $j_0\in J$.
Suppose that for every $i\in I$ an injection
$e_i:a^{-1}(i)\to b^{-1}(i)$ is given.
Then there is a total map $d:V\to J$ such that, for every $i\in I,j\in J$,
\[
 |\{x:a(x)=i,\ c(x)=j\}|\leq
 |\{v:b(v)=i,\ d(v)=j\}|.
\]
No equality of the original capacities, nonempty fiber, or ordering of
$V$ is required.
\end{lemma}
FiberwiseCapacityRefinement.title: FiberwiseCapacityRefinement

theorem FilteredProductRowCount {A B : Type*} [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B]
    (U : Finset A) (W : Finset B) (P : A → B → Prop) [DecidableRel P] :
    ((U.product W).filter fun p => P p.1 p.2).card =
      ∑ x ∈ U, (W.filter fun y => P x y).card := by
FilteredProductRowCount.name: FilteredProductRowCount
FilteredProductRowCount.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Counting a relation by rows]
Let $U\subseteq A$ and $W\subseteq B$ be finite sets, and let $P$ be a relation on $A\times B$.
Then
\[
 |\{(x,y)\in U\times W:P(x,y)\}|=
 \sum_{x\in U}|\{y\in W:P(x,y)\}|.
\]
\end{lemma}
FilteredProductRowCount.title: FilteredProductRowCount

source : V
  sink : V
  terminals_distinct : source ≠ sink
  capacity : V → V → ℕ
FiniteCapacityNetwork.name: FiniteCapacityNetwork
FiniteCapacityNetwork.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Finite integer-capacity network]
For a finite vertex type $V$, a finite integer-capacity network consists of
distinct vertices $s,t\in V$ and a function $c:V\times V\to\mathbb N$.
The vertices $s,t$ are the source and sink. A zero capacity represents an
absent arc. Capacities are finite natural numbers; parallel arcs are not
separately represented. A source-side cut is a subset $S$ with $s\in S$
and $t\notin S$, and its capacity is
$C(S)=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{w\notin S}c(v,w)$.
\end{definition}
FiniteCapacityNetwork.title: FiniteCapacityNetwork

FiniteGreedySpreadLaw.lean_proof:
classical
  let b : U → V := fun u => (hT u).choose
  let extend (A : Finset U) (f : A → V) : U → V :=
    fun u => if hu : u ∈ A then f ⟨u, hu⟩ else b u
  have extend_on (A : Finset U) (f : A → V) (u : A) :
      extend A f u = f u := by simp [extend, u.property]
  have reference_independent (A : Finset U) (f : A → V) (g : U → V)
      (hg : ∀ u : A, g u = f u) : Good A (extend A f) ↔ Good A g := by
    apply hlocal A (extend A f) g
    intro u hu
    exact (extend_on A f ⟨u, hu⟩).trans (hg ⟨u, hu⟩).symm
  have uniform_spread (L : Finset V) (hL : L.Nonempty)
      (hLq : 1 / (L.card : ENNReal) ≤ q) :
      VertexSpreadOn ((PMF.uniformOfFinset L hL).map
        (fun v => fun _ : Unit => v)) q Set.univ := by
    refine ⟨hq, ?_⟩
    intro s x y hx _
    have hs : s ≤ 1 := by
      simpa using Fintype.card_le_of_injective x hx
    cases s with
    | zero =>
      have hevent : CylinderEvent x y = Set.univ := by ext f; simp [CylinderEvent]
      rw [hevent, pow_zero]
      exact le_of_eq ((PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff _ _).mpr (Set.subset_univ _))
    | succ s =>
      have hs0 : s = 0 := by omega
      subst s
      rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_map_apply]
      have hevent : (fun v => fun _ : Unit => v) ⁻¹' CylinderEvent x y = {y 0} := by
        ext v
        simp [CylinderEvent, Fin.forall_fin_one]
      rw [hevent]
      calc
        _ = ((L.filter fun v => v ∈ ({y 0} : Set V)).card : ENNReal) /
            (L.card : ENNReal) := by
          convert PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFinset_apply hL {y 0} using 1
          congr 2
          apply congrArg Finset.card
          ext v
          simp
        _ ≤ q ^ (0 + 1) := by
          have hcard : (L.filter (fun v => v ∈ ({y 0} : Set V))).card ≤ 1 := by
            calc
              _ ≤ ({y 0} : Finset V).card := Finset.card_le_card (by
                intro v hv
                simpa using (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2)
              _ = 1 := Finset.card_singleton _
          have hcard' : ((L.filter (fun v => v ∈ ({y 0} : Set V))).card : ENNReal) ≤ 1 :=
            by exact_mod_cast hcard
          simpa only [Nat.zero_add, pow_one] using
            (ENNReal.div_le_div_right hcard' (L.card : ENNReal)).trans hLq
  have prefixes : ∀ (G : Finset U → (U → V) → Prop),
      (∀ A f g, (∀ u ∈ A, f u = g u) → (G A f ↔ G A g)) →
      (∀ f, G ∅ f) →
      ∀ (K : ∀ A : Finset U, (A → V) → U → Finset V),
      (∀ A f z, z ∉ A →
        (K A f z).Nonempty ∧ 1 / ((K A f z).card : ENNReal) ≤ q ∧
          (G A (extend A f) → ∀ v ∈ K A f z,
            G (insert z A) (Function.update (extend A f) z v))) →
      ∀ A : Finset U, ∃ ν : PMF (A → V),
        VertexSpreadOn ν q Set.univ ∧
        ∀ f ∈ ν.support, G A (extend A f) := by
    intro G hGloc hGzero K hK A
    induction A using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty =>
      let f0 : (∅ : Finset U) → V := fun u => False.elim (Finset.notMem_empty _ u.property)
      refine ⟨PMF.pure f0, ⟨hq, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
      · intro s x y hx hy
        cases s with
        | zero =>
          have hevent : CylinderEvent x y = Set.univ := by ext f; simp [CylinderEvent]
          rw [hevent, pow_zero]
          exact le_of_eq ((PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff _ _).mpr (Set.subset_univ _))
        | succ s => exact False.elim (Finset.notMem_empty _ (x 0).property)
      · intro f hf
        exact hGzero _
    | @insert z A hz ih =>
      obtain ⟨ν, hν, hvalid⟩ := ih
      let L (f : A → V) := K A f z
      have hL (f : A → V) : (L f).Nonempty := (hK A f z hz).1
      have hLq (f : A → V) : 1 / ((L f).card : ENNReal) ≤ q := (hK A f z hz).2.1
      have hLG (f : A → V) := (hK A f z hz).2.2
      let κ (f : A → V) : PMF (Unit → V) :=
        (PMF.uniformOfFinset (L f) (hL f)).map (fun v => fun _ => v)
      have hκ (f : A → V) : VertexSpreadOn (κ f) q Set.univ :=
        uniform_spread (L f) (hL f) (hLq f)
      let e : (insert z A : Finset U) ≃ (A ⊕ Unit) :=
        { toFun := fun u => if hu : u.val = z then Sum.inr () else
            Sum.inl ⟨u.val, (Finset.mem_insert.mp u.property).resolve_left hu⟩
          invFun := Sum.elim (fun u => ⟨u.val, Finset.mem_insert_of_mem u.property⟩)
            (fun _ => ⟨z, Finset.mem_insert_self z A⟩)
          left_inv := by
            intro u
            dsimp
            split
            · rename_i hu
              exact Subtype.ext hu.symm
            · rfl
          right_inv := by
            intro u
            cases u with
            | inl u =>
              have hu : u.val ≠ z := by intro he; exact hz (he ▸ u.property)
              simp [hu]
            | inr u => cases u; simp }
      let joint : PMF ((A ⊕ Unit) → V) :=
        ν.bind fun f => (κ f).map (Sum.elim f)
      let out : PMF (↥(insert z A) → V) :=
        joint.map (fun k => k ∘ e.toFun)
      refine ⟨out, ?_, ?_⟩
      · exact VertexSpreadRestriction e.toEmbedding (VertexSpreadSequential ν κ q hν hκ)
      · intro f hf
        obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hf
        obtain ⟨g, hg, hkg⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_bind_iff _ _ _).mp hk
        obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hkg
        obtain ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp ha
        have hvL : v ∈ L g := (PMF.mem_support_uniformOfFinset_iff _ _).mp hv
        have hgood := hLG g (hvalid g hg) v hvL
        apply (hGloc (insert z A) _ _ ?_).mp hgood
        intro u hu
        by_cases huz : u = z
        · subst u
          simp [extend, e]
        · have huA : u ∈ A := (Finset.mem_insert.mp hu).resolve_left huz
          simp [extend, e, hu, huA, huz]
  intro S
  let K (A : Finset U) (f : A → V) (z : U) : Finset V :=
    if hz : z ∉ A then
      if hf : Good A (extend A f) then (hstep A (extend A f) z hz hf).choose
      else T z
    else T z
  have hK : ∀ A f z, z ∉ A →
      (K A f z).Nonempty ∧ 1 / ((K A f z).card : ENNReal) ≤ q ∧
        (Good A (extend A f) → ∀ v ∈ K A f z,
          Good (insert z A) (Function.update (extend A f) z v)) := by
    intro A f z hz
    by_cases hf : Good A (extend A f)
    · simpa only [K, dif_pos hz, dif_pos hf] using
        ⟨(hstep A (extend A f) z hz hf).choose_spec.1,
          (hstep A (extend A f) z hz hf).choose_spec.2.1,
          fun _ => (hstep A (extend A f) z hz hf).choose_spec.2.2⟩
    · simp only [K, dif_pos hz, dif_neg hf]
      exact ⟨hT z, hTq z, fun h => False.elim (hf h)⟩
  obtain ⟨ν, hν, hvalid⟩ := prefixes Good hlocal hzero K hK S
  -- The complement law has constant kernels, independently uniform in T(z).
  let C : Finset U := Finset.univ \ S
  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, _⟩ := prefixes (fun _ _ => True)
    (fun _ _ _ _ => Iff.rfl) (fun _ => trivial)
    (fun _ _ z => T z) (fun _ _ z _ => ⟨hT z, hTq z, fun _ _ _ => trivial⟩) C
  let eU : U ≃ (S ⊕ C) :=
    { toFun := fun u => if hu : u ∈ S then Sum.inl ⟨u, hu⟩
        else Sum.inr ⟨u, by simp [C, hu]⟩
      invFun := Sum.elim Subtype.val Subtype.val
      left_inv := by intro u; dsimp; split <;> rfl
      right_inv := by
        intro u
        cases u with
        | inl u => simp [u.property]
        | inr u =>
          have hu : u.val ∉ S := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp u.property).2
          simp [hu] }
  let joint : PMF ((S ⊕ C) → V) := ν.bind fun f => ρ.map (Sum.elim f)
  let total : PMF (U → V) := joint.map (fun f => f ∘ eU)
  have htotal : VertexSpreadOn total q Set.univ :=
    VertexSpreadRestriction eU.toEmbedding (VertexSpreadSequential ν (fun _ => ρ) q hν (fun _ => hρ))
  have total_valid : ∀ f ∈ total.support, Good S f := by
    intro f hf
    obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hf
    obtain ⟨g, hg, hkg⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_bind_iff _ _ _).mp hk
    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hkg
    apply (reference_independent S g _ ?_).mp (hvalid g hg)
    intro u
    simp [eU, u.property]
  obtain ⟨f0, hf0⟩ := total.support_nonempty
  let pack : (U → V) → {f : U → V // Good S f} := fun f =>
    if hf : f ∈ total.support then ⟨f, total_valid f hf⟩
    else ⟨f0, total_valid f0 hf0⟩
  have projected : (total.map pack).map Subtype.val = total := by
    rw [PMF.map_comp]
    have heq : total.map (Subtype.val ∘ pack) = total.map id := by
      apply PMF.ext
      intro f
      simp only [PMF.map_apply]
      apply tsum_congr
      intro g
      by_cases hg : g ∈ total.support
      · simp only [Function.comp_apply, pack, dif_pos hg, id_eq]
        split_ifs <;> rfl
      · have hg0 : total g = 0 := by simpa only [PMF.mem_support_iff, not_not] using hg
        simp [hg0]
    exact heq.trans (PMF.map_id total)
  refine ⟨total.map pack, ?_⟩
  rw [projected]
  exact htotal
FiniteGreedySpreadLaw.lean_statement:
theorem FiniteGreedySpreadLaw {U V : Type*} [Fintype U] [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq U] [DecidableEq V]
    (q : ENNReal) (hq : q ≤ 1)
    (T : U → Finset V) (hT : ∀ u, (T u).Nonempty)
    (hTq : ∀ u, 1 / ((T u).card : ENNReal) ≤ q)
    (Good : Finset U → (U → V) → Prop)
    (hlocal : ∀ S f g, (∀ u ∈ S, f u = g u) → (Good S f ↔ Good S g))
    (hzero : ∀ f, Good ∅ f)
    (hstep : ∀ S f z, z ∉ S → Good S f →
      ∃ L : Finset V, L.Nonempty ∧ 1 / (L.card : ENNReal) ≤ q ∧
        ∀ v ∈ L, Good (insert z S) (Function.update f z v)) :
    ∀ S : Finset U, ∃ μ : PMF {f : U → V // Good S f},
      VertexSpreadOn (μ.map Subtype.val) q Set.univ := by
FiniteGreedySpreadLaw.name: FiniteGreedySpreadLaw
FiniteGreedySpreadLaw.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
First choose $b(u)\in T(u)$ for every $u$. These choices define a total
map $b$ even if $U$ is empty; no element of $V$ is needed in the empty
case. For a map $h:S\to V$, let $e_S(h)$ be the total map equal to
$h$ on $S$ and equal to $b$ outside $S$. The locality assumption
implies that whether $\mathrm{Good}(S,e_S(h))$ holds is independent
of these outside values. Call such a restricted map $h$ valid.

Fix the prescribed $S$ and list its vertices without repetition as
$z_1,\ldots,z_m$. Put $S_t=\{z_1,\ldots,z_t\}$.
We construct a law on functions $S_t\to V$ which is $q$-spread and
whose positive-mass functions are valid. For $t=0$, use the point
mass on the unique empty function. By \noderef{CylinderEvent}, its
only cylinders are of length zero, with mass $1=q^0$; an injective
positive-length prescription into the empty domain is impossible.
Validity follows from the empty
set assumption applied to $b$. Together with $q\leq1$, these cylinder
checks establish \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} on the whole codomain $V$.

Suppose the law on $S_t$ has been constructed. For every valid
function $h:S_t\to V$, apply the extension assumption to
$e_{S_t}(h)$ and $z=z_{t+1}$ and choose a corresponding set $L_h$.
On the singleton block $\{z\}$ choose its value uniformly in $L_h$.
For every invalid $h$, define the kernel instead by uniform choice
in $T(z)$. This defines a kernel for every prefix function, including
all functions of mass zero. Both choice sets are nonempty. By
Mathlib's \texttt{PMF.toOuterMeasure\_uniformOfFinset\_apply}, the probability of a prescribed
value $v$ is zero if $v$ is outside the choice set and otherwise is
its reciprocal cardinality, which is at most $q$. Mapping the chosen
value to a function on the singleton does not change this probability,
since evaluation at its sole element is an inverse to that map.
Every kernel on the singleton block is therefore $q$-spread by
\noderef{VertexSpreadOn}, using the cylinders of \noderef{CylinderEvent}:
the empty cylinder has mass one, a one-point cylinder has the bound
just proved, and an injective prescription of length at least two on
a singleton does not exist. Its scalar condition $q\leq1$ is assumed.

Apply \noderef{VertexSpreadSequential} with first source type $S_t$,
second source type $\{z\}$, and target type $V$. Its bind and map
give a $q$-spread law on functions on their disjoint sum. Identify this
sum with $S_{t+1}$ by sending each old vertex to itself and the sole
new vertex to $z$. This is a bijection because $z\notin S_t$. By
\noderef{CylinderEvent}, under precomposition by its inverse a cylinder
corresponds to a cylinder with the same number of prescriptions and
injective sources. The resulting cylinder probabilities are equal and
the scalar condition $q\leq1$ is unchanged, so
\noderef{VertexSpreadOn} is preserved.

To check support, suppose an extended function has positive mass.
All spaces are finite, so the bind and map formulas express its mass
as a finite sum of products of prefix masses and conditional masses.
If this sum is positive, at least one product is positive. Thus its
prefix has positive mass and is valid, and its new value belongs to
$L_h$: a value outside the uniform choice set has mass zero by
\texttt{PMF.toOuterMeasure\_uniformOfFinset\_apply}. The extension assumption makes
$e_{S_t}(h)[z\mapsto v]$ good on $S_{t+1}$. This total map agrees on
$S_{t+1}$ with the extension of the actual restricted function, so
locality makes that restricted function valid. The invalid-prefix
fallback is consequently never used at a positive-mass prefix.
This proves both induction assertions, yielding a law on $S$.

Next list the vertices of $U\setminus S$. Append their values one at
a time using independent uniform choices in their sets $T(u)$.
Each kernel is constant as a function of the prefix, hence is defined
on every prefix, and has the same singleton spread bound as above.
Repeated applications of \noderef{VertexSpreadSequential} and the
same cylinder-preserving bijections give a law $\nu$ on total maps
$U\to V$ satisfying \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} on the whole codomain.
Appending values never changes the restriction
to $S$. Therefore every positive-mass total map satisfies
$\mathrm{Good}(S,f)$ by the locality assumption and the established
validity of its restriction. This is why independent random values,
rather than the deterministic values of $b$, were used for the
stored completion: the desired bound concerns all source vertices.

For completeness, package this law into the subtype without changing
its projected law. The finite support
$P=\{f:\nu(f)\ne0\}$ is nonempty because the masses sum to one.
Every $f\in P$ has a proof of $\mathrm{Good}(S,f)$. Choose $f_0\in P$.
Map a total map $f$ to $\langle f,\mathrm{Good}(S,f)\rangle$ when
it belongs to $P$, and map it to the packaged $f_0$ otherwise. This
is a total function to the asserted subtype. Let $\mu$ be its
pushforward of $\nu$. For every event $E$ of total maps, the mass
of its preimage under the subtype projection is
\[
 \sum_{f\in P}\nu(f)\mathbf1_E(f)
       +\sum_{f\notin P}0\mathbf1_E(f_0)=\nu(E).
\]
Thus the projected law is exactly $\nu$. In particular, taking $E$ to
be each cylinder of \noderef{CylinderEvent} preserves every cylinder
bound, and the scalar condition $q\leq1$ is unchanged. Hence the
projected law satisfies \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} on the whole codomain
$V$. If $U$ is empty this construction is the point mass on
the empty map, even if $V$ is empty. If $S$ is empty but $U$ is not,
only the independent-completion steps are performed. Both cases
are covered by the same reasoning.
\end{proof}
FiniteGreedySpreadLaw.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Finite greedy law with random total-map completion]
Let $U,V$ be finite sets, $q\in[0,1]$ an extended nonnegative real,
and $T(u)\subseteq V$ a nonempty finite set for every $u\in U$,
with $1/|T(u)|\leq q$. Let $\mathrm{Good}(S,f)$ be a predicate on
finite subsets $S\subseteq U$ and total maps $f:U\to V$ satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ and $g$ agree on $S$, then
$\mathrm{Good}(S,f)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{Good}(S,g)$.
\item $\mathrm{Good}(\varnothing,f)$ holds for every total map $f$.
\item Whenever $z\notin S$ and $\mathrm{Good}(S,f)$, there is a
nonempty finite set $L\subseteq V$ with $1/|L|\leq q$ such that
$\mathrm{Good}(S\cup\{z\},f[z\mapsto v])$ for every $v\in L$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for every $S\subseteq U$ there is a PMF on the subtype of total
maps satisfying $\mathrm{Good}(S,f)$ whose projection to total maps
is $q$-vertex-spread on all of $V$, in the sense of
\noderef{VertexSpreadOn}.
\end{lemma}
FiniteGreedySpreadLaw.title: FiniteGreedySpreadLaw

FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail.lean_proof:
classical
  by_cases hz : s = ∅
  · subst s
    simp only [Finset.sum_empty, abs_zero, not_lt.mpr ht, Set.setOf_false,
      measureReal_empty]
    positivity
  have hsum := HasSubgaussianMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun hi hs
  let c : ℝ≥0 := ⟨N / 4, by positivity⟩
  have hc : ((∑ _i ∈ s, (1 / 4 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) ≤ (c : ℝ) := by
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, NNReal.coe_mul, NNReal.coe_natCast,
      NNReal.coe_div, NNReal.coe_one, NNReal.coe_ofNat]
    change (s.card : ℝ) * (1 / 4) ≤ N / 4
    linarith
  have hbig : HasSubgaussianMGF (fun ω => ∑ i ∈ s, X i ω) c μ := by
    refine ⟨hsum.integrable_exp_mul, fun u => ?_⟩
    exact (hsum.mgf_le u).trans (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by
      exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hc (sq_nonneg u))
        (by norm_num)))
  have hupper := hbig.measure_ge_le ht
  have hlower := hbig.neg.measure_ge_le ht
  have hsub : {ω | t < |∑ i ∈ s, X i ω|} ⊆
      {ω | t ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, X i ω} ∪ {ω | t ≤ -(∑ i ∈ s, X i ω)} := by
    intro ω hω
    change t < |∑ i ∈ s, X i ω| at hω
    rcases (lt_abs.mp hω) with hω | hω
    · exact Or.inl (le_of_lt hω)
    · exact Or.inr hω.le
  have hden : -t ^ 2 / (2 * (c : ℝ)) = -2 * t ^ 2 / N := by
    change -t ^ 2 / (2 * (N / 4)) = -2 * t ^ 2 / N
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [hden] at hupper hlower
  exact (measureReal_mono hsub).trans
    ((measureReal_union_le _ _).trans (by simpa [two_mul] using add_le_add hupper hlower))
FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail.lean_statement:
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

theorem FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail
    {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (s : Finset ι)
    (hi : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hs : ∀ i ∈ s, HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) (1 / 4) μ)
    (N t : ℝ) (hN : 0 < N) (hr : (s.card : ℝ) ≤ N) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    μ.real {ω | t < |∑ i ∈ s, X i ω|} ≤
      2 * Real.exp (-2 * t ^ 2 / N) := by
FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail.name: FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail
FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
If $s$ is empty the sum is zero, and the asserted event is empty.
Otherwise the independent-sum subgaussian theorem gives parameter
$|s|/4$ to the sum $S$. Since $|s|\leq N$, its exponential bound is
also bounded by $\exp(Nu^2/8)$, so $S$ has parameter $N/4$.
The checked subgaussian Chernoff inequality gives
$\mu(S\geq t)\leq\exp(-t^2/(2(N/4)))$.
Negation preserves the subgaussian parameter, so the same inequality
applies to $-S$. The event $|S|>t$ lies in the union of these two
weak-tail events. Subadditivity of probability and
$-t^2/(2(N/4))=-2t^2/N$ give the assertion. These arguments do not
require the random variables to have identical distributions.
\end{proof}
FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Finite independent subgaussian tail]
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure, let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be independent
real random variables, and let $s\subseteq I$ be finite. Suppose each
$X_i$ with $i\in s$ has centered subgaussian parameter $1/4$, meaning
$\mathbb E e^{uX_i}\leq e^{u^2/8}$ for every real $u$, with the
exponentials integrable. If $0<N$, $|s|\leq N$, and $t\geq0$, then
\[
 \mu\left(\left|\sum_{i\in s}X_i\right|>t\right)
 \leq 2\exp(-2t^2/N).
\]
\end{lemma}
FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail.title: FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail
