open scoped Classical symmDiff

theorem HostExceptionalCorrection {r k : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}
    [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (σ : VH → Fin r × Fin k) (f : VG → Fin r × Fin k)
    (ε d : ENNReal) (n : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hn : 2 * k ≤ n)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / (8 * (k : ENNReal) ^ 2)) (hd : d ≤ 1)
    (hσ : ∀ x, (σ x).1 = B.sourceCluster x)
    (hf : ∀ v, (f v).1 = B.hostCluster v)
    (hcard : ∀ i,
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card = n ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).card = n)
    (hsize : ∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / k ∨
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / k + 1)
    (hcapacity : ∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card)
    (hcand : CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d) :
    ∃ f' : VG → Fin r × Fin k,
      (∀ v, (f' v).1 = B.hostCluster v) ∧
      (∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card) ∧
      (∀ p, (((Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p) ∆
          (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p)).card : ENNReal) ≤
        2 * k * ε * n) ∧
      (∀ v, (d - 2 * ε) *
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = f' v).card : ENNReal) ≤
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = f' v ∧ A.allowed x v).card : ENNReal)) := by
HostExceptionalCorrection.name: HostExceptionalCorrection
HostExceptionalCorrection.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
If $d\leq2\varepsilon$, retain $f$; the requested lower bound is
zero and every symmetric difference is empty. Otherwise all
parameters are finite and $d-2\varepsilon>0$; work with real values.
For a source bin $X_{ij}=\sigma^{-1}(i,j)$ define
\[
 E_{ij}=\{v\in V_i:\deg_A(v,X_{ij})<(d-2\varepsilon)|X_{ij}|\},
 \quad E_i=\bigcup_j E_{ij},\quad e_i=|E_i|.
\]
The floor estimate $m\geq n/(2k)$ implies
$|X_{ij}|\geq m>\varepsilon n$.
If $|E_{ij}|>\varepsilon n$, the two tagged sets constitute a
valid lower-regularity test in the original candidacy graph.
Every degree defining $E_{ij}$ is strictly below
$(d-2\varepsilon)|X_{ij}|$, so summing these finitely many
inequalities gives density strictly below $d-2\varepsilon$.
This contradicts density at least $d-\varepsilon$, furnished by
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular} and
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}, with
\noderef{LowerRegularPair} and \noderef{PairDensity}.
Therefore $|E_{ij}|\leq\varepsilon n$ and
$e_i\leq k\varepsilon n<m$, since $\varepsilon<1/(8k^2)$.

Every host vertex $v\in V_i$ has a suitable bin with degree at
least $(d-\varepsilon)|X_{ij}|$. Indeed, if none did, summing
the strict reverse inequalities over the partition of $X_i$ would
give total candidacy degree strictly below $(d-\varepsilon)n$,
contrary to the host-side minimum-degree clause of
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular} and
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}. The fibers partition $X_i$
because $\sigma$ has the stated projection. Select a suitable index
for each member of $E_i$.

Apply \noderef{CapacityPreservingReassignment} on $V_i$, using
the second coordinate of $f$, exceptional set $E_i$, and the selected
indices. Every old capacity is at least $m>e_i$, so its room
hypothesis holds. It preserves all capacities, puts each exception
in its selected suitable bin, and changes each bin in at most
$2e_i\leq2k\varepsilon n$ positions. Do this independently on
the disjoint original host clusters and attach their unchanged first
coordinates. This defines $f'$ globally with the asserted projection.
A nonexceptional vertex has degree at least
$(d-2\varepsilon)|X_{ij}|$ into every source bin of its cluster;
an exceptional vertex in its selected bin has the stronger bound
$(d-\varepsilon)|X_{ij}|$. These establish the requested bound
for every host vertex. Tagging bijects the relevant neighbors, so the
ordinary relation counts are exactly those used by the predicates.
Conversion back to extended nonnegative reals preserves these finite
positive lower bounds. If $r=0$, the given cluster maps force empty
vertex types and the empty map supplies all assertions.
\end{proof}
HostExceptionalCorrection.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Suitable-bin correction of exceptional host vertices]
Let $k\geq1$, $n\geq2k$, $0<\varepsilon<1/(8k^2)$, and $d\leq1$.
Let $B,A$ be a blow-up instance and candidacy system whose original
source and host clusters all have size $n$ and whose candidacy pairs
are lower $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular. Suppose $\sigma$ refines
the source map into $k$ fibers per original cluster of sizes
$m$ or $m+1$, $m=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$, and $f$ refines the host
map with those exact capacities. There is a corrected host map $f'$
with the same projection and capacities, for which each bin has
symmetric difference of size at most $2k\varepsilon n$ from its
old bin, and each host vertex $v$ has at least
$(d-2\varepsilon)|\sigma^{-1}(f'(v))|$ candidates in the source
bin to which it is assigned. Lower endpoints are truncated at zero.
\end{lemma}

open Filter
open scoped Topology

theorem HostRefinementParameters (k N : ℕ) (η θ : ℝ)
    (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
    ∃ e : ℝ, 0 < e ∧ e < η ∧ e < 1 ∧ e < 1 / (8 * (k : ℝ) ^ 2) ∧
      (4 * (k : ℝ) ^ 2 + 2) * e ≤ θ ∧ 2 * k * e ≤ θ ∧
      ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
        2 * k ≤ n ∧ N ≤ n / k ∧
        2 * (r : ℝ) * k * (r + 1) * n *
          Real.exp (-((e / (2 * k)) ^ 2 / (2 * (1 + e / (6 * k)))) * n) < 1 := by
HostRefinementParameters.name: HostRefinementParameters
HostRefinementParameters.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Take $e=\min\{\eta/2,\theta/(8k^2),1/(16k^2)\}$.
All three entries are positive. Since $k\geq1$,
$4k^2+2\leq8k^2$ and $2k\leq8k^2$; these inequalities give
the two non-strict margins. The first entry gives $e<\eta<1$;
the last gives $e<1/(8k^2)$.
Set $c=(e/(2k))^2/(2(1+e/(6k)))>0$. For each fixed $r$, the
function $2rk(r+1)n\exp(-cn)$ tends to zero as $n$ tends to infinity.
For instance $x\exp(-x)\to0$ with $x=cn$, and the prefactor
becomes the fixed constant $2rk(r+1)/c$. Choose an integer $M$
above which this function is less than one. Then
$n_0=\max\{2k,kN,M\}$ gives all three assertions; $kN\leq n$
implies $N\leq\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ because $k>0$.
When $r=0$ the tail expression is zero for every $n$ and this
same construction still works. Thus $e$ is selected before $r$;
only the order cutoff can depend on $r$. The positive rate here is
the weaker hypergeometric rate actually used in host sampling.
\end{proof}
HostRefinementParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Parameters for host refinement]
For an integer $k\geq1$, an integer extraction cutoff $N$, and real
numbers $0<\eta<1$, $0<\theta$, there is $e>0$, depending only on
$k,\eta,\theta$, such that
\[
 e<\eta,\quad e<1,\quad e<1/(8k^2),\quad
 (4k^2+2)e\leq\theta,\quad 2ke\leq\theta.
\]
For every integer $r\geq0$ there is $n_0$ such that for all $n\geq n_0$,
$n\geq2k$, $\lfloor n/k\rfloor\geq N$, and
\[
 2rk(r+1)n\exp\left(-\frac{(e/(2k))^2}{2(1+e/(6k))}n\right)<1.
\]
\end{lemma}

HypergeometricExponentialMoment.lean_proof:
classical
  obtain ⟨M, _hMsub, hM⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq
    (show t ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).card by simpa using ht)
  let a : Fin n → ℝ := fun i => if i ∈ M then Real.exp l else 1
  let m : ℝ := (s : ℝ) * t / n
  let z : ℝ := (t : ℝ) / n * (Real.exp l - 1)
  have hnR : 0 < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hc : 0 < (n.choose s : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.choose_pos hs
  have ha : ∀ i, 0 ≤ a i := by
    intro i
    dsimp [a]
    split_ifs <;> positivity
  have hraw := WeightedSubsetIntersectionSum n s hs M (Real.exp l)
  rw [hM] at hraw

      (∑ x ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
        HypergeometricMass n s t x * Real.exp (l * (x : ℝ))) =
      (∑ A ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard s,
        ∏ i ∈ A, a i) / (n.choose s : ℝ) := by
    rw [show (∑ A ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard s,
      ∏ i ∈ A, a i) = _ from hraw, Finset.sum_div]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro x hx
    by_cases hxs : x ≤ s
    · simp only [HypergeometricMass, if_pos hxs]
      rw [show l * (x : ℝ) = (x : ℝ) * l by ring, Real.exp_nat_mul]
      field_simp [hc.ne']
    · simp [HypergeometricMass, hxs]
  have hsum : (∑ i, a i) = (n : ℝ) + (t : ℝ) * (Real.exp l - 1) := by
    have hf : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).filter (fun i => i ∈ M) = M := by
      ext i

    have hg : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).filter (fun i => i ∉ M) =

      simp

      rw [Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ M)]
      simp [hM]
    dsimp [a]
    rw [Finset.sum_ite, hf, hg]
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hM, hcard, mul_one]

    rw [hsum]
    dsimp [z]
    field_simp [hnR.ne']

    exact div_nonneg (Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i _ => ha i)) hnR.le

      congr 1
      dsimp [m, z]

HypergeometricExponentialMoment.lean_statement:
theorem HypergeometricExponentialMoment (n s t : ℕ)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hs : s ≤ n) (ht : t ≤ n) (l : ℝ) :
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), HypergeometricMass n s t x *
      Real.exp (l * ((x : ℝ) - (s : ℝ) * t / n)) ≤
    Real.exp (((s : ℝ) * t / n) * (Real.exp l - 1 - l)) := by
HypergeometricExponentialMoment.name: HypergeometricExponentialMoment
HypergeometricExponentialMoment.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Take an $n$-element set with a distinguished $t$-subset. Assign weight
$e^\lambda$ to a distinguished element and weight one to every other
element. These weights are strictly positive for every real $\lambda$.
An $s$-subset containing $x$ distinguished elements has weight
$e^{\lambda x}$; there are
$\binom t x\binom{n-t}{s-x}$ such subsets for $x\le s$.
For $x>s$ there are none. A binomial coefficient is zero if its lower
index exceeds its upper index, so this counting formula also excludes
$x>t$ and $s-x>n-t$. Every $s$-subset is counted once, and its distinguished
count lies in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. Consequently the subset-product sum divided
by $\binom n s$ equals
$\sum_{x=0}^n H(n,s,t,x)e^{\lambda x}$, using
\noderef{HypergeometricMass}.

Apply \noderef{ElementarySymmetricMean} with $k=s$ to these weights.
Their arithmetic mean is $1-p+pe^\lambda$, where $p=t/n\in[0,1]$.
It follows that
\[
 \sum_{x=0}^n H(n,s,t,x)e^{\lambda x}
 \le (1+p(e^\lambda-1))^s
 \le \exp(sp(e^\lambda-1)).
\]
For the last inequality use $1+z\le e^z$ for every real $z$ with
$z=p(e^\lambda-1)$. The left base is positive, since it is an average
of positive weights, so raising both sides to the natural power $s$
preserves the inequality. Multiplying by $e^{-\lambda m}>0$, and using
$sp=m$, proves the assertion. No step assumes $\lambda\ge0$; in
particular the same argument applies to the negative moment needed for
the lower tail. If $s=0$ it gives equality, without a division by $s$.
\end{proof}
HypergeometricExponentialMoment.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Centered hypergeometric exponential moment]
Let $n>0$, $s,t\le n$ be natural numbers and $m=st/n$ in real arithmetic.
For every real $\lambda$, including negative values,
\[
 \sum_{x=0}^n H(n,s,t,x)e^{\lambda(x-m)}
 \le \exp\bigl(m(e^\lambda-1-\lambda)\bigr),
\]
where $H$ is \noderef{HypergeometricMass}.
\end{lemma}
HypergeometricExponentialMoment.title: HypergeometricExponentialMoment

HypergeometricMass.lean_proof:
if x ≤ s then

HypergeometricMass.lean_statement: noncomputable def HypergeometricMass (n s t x : ℕ) : ℝ :=
HypergeometricMass.name: HypergeometricMass
HypergeometricMass.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Hypergeometric masses]
For natural numbers $n,s,t,x$, define the real number
\[
 H(n,s,t,x)=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle {\binom t x\binom{n-t}{s-x}\over\binom n s},&x\le s,\\
 0,&x>s.
 \end{cases}
\]
Natural-number subtraction is truncated and real division by zero is
defined to be zero. In applications $s,t\le n$, so the denominator is
positive. When $s,t\le n$, these are the masses for the number of marked elements in a
uniform $s$-subset of an $n$-element set with $t$ marked elements. The
explicit $x\le s$ condition prevents truncated subtraction from assigning
a spurious mass to $x>s$.
\end{definition}
HypergeometricMass.title: HypergeometricMass

HypergeometricTwoTail.lean_proof:
classical

  let u : ℝ := η * n

  have hmass (x : ℕ) : 0 ≤ HypergeometricMass n s t x := by
    unfold HypergeometricMass
    split_ifs <;> positivity
  have hmnonneg : 0 ≤ m := by dsimp [m]; positivity

    dsimp [m]
    rw [div_le_iff₀ hnR]

        HypergeometricMass n s t x) = 0 := by

      intro x hx

        HypergeometricMass n s t x ≤ Real.exp (-a) *
          (HypergeometricMass n s t x * Real.exp (l * ((x : ℝ) - m))) := by

            Real.exp (l * ((x : ℝ) - m) - a) := by

        _ = _ := by
          rw [show l * ((x : ℝ) - m) - a = -a + l * ((x : ℝ) - m) by ring,
            Real.exp_add]
          ring
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ x ∈ S, Real.exp (-a) *
          (HypergeometricMass n s t x * Real.exp (l * ((x : ℝ) - m))) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum hterm
      _ = Real.exp (-a) * (∑ x ∈ S,
          HypergeometricMass n s t x * Real.exp (l * ((x : ℝ) - m))) :=
        (Finset.mul_sum ..).symm
      _ ≤ Real.exp (-a) * (∑ x ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          HypergeometricMass n s t x * Real.exp (l * ((x : ℝ) - m))) := by
        apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (Real.exp_nonneg _)
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hS
        intro x _ _
        exact mul_nonneg (hmass x) (Real.exp_nonneg _)
      _ ≤ Real.exp (-a) * Real.exp (m * (Real.exp l - 1 - l)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (HypergeometricExponentialMoment n s t hn hs ht l)
          (Real.exp_nonneg _)

  let U := (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun x : ℕ => m + u ≤ (x : ℝ))

      Real.exp (-(u ^ 2 / (2 * (m + u / 3)))) := by
    let z : ℝ := u / m

    have hl : 0 < l := Real.log_pos (by dsimp [z]; linarith [div_pos hu hmpos])
    have hexp : Real.exp l = 1 + z := Real.exp_log (by linarith)

      intro x hx
      have hxU := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).2

      linarith)

      rw [hexp, ← huz]
      dsimp [l]
      ring
    have hden : 0 < 1 + z / 3 := by positivity
    have hid : m * (z ^ 2 / (2 * (1 + z / 3))) =
        u ^ 2 / (2 * (m + u / 3)) := by
      dsimp [z]
      field_simp
    apply htail.trans
    apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
    rw [he]
    rw [hid] at hscale
    linarith
  have hlower : (∑ x ∈ L, HypergeometricMass n s t x) ≤
      Real.exp (-(u ^ 2 / (2 * m))) := by
    let l : ℝ := -u / m
    have hl : l < 0 := div_neg_of_neg_of_pos (neg_neg_of_pos hu) hmpos

HypergeometricTwoTail.lean_statement:
theorem HypergeometricTwoTail (n s t : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hs : s ≤ n) (ht : t ≤ n) (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∑ x ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter
      (fun x : ℕ => η * n < |(x : ℝ) - (s : ℝ) * t / n|),
      HypergeometricMass n s t x ≤
    2 * Real.exp (-(η ^ 2 / (2 * (1 + η / 3))) * n) := by
HypergeometricTwoTail.name: HypergeometricTwoTail
HypergeometricTwoTail.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
All masses are nonnegative, since their binomial coefficients are
nonnegative and $\binom n s>0$. Put $u=\eta n>0$ and first assume $m>0$.
For $\lambda>0$ and $x\ge m+u$,
$1\le e^{\lambda(x-m-u)}$. Multiply by the mass and sum; enlarging to all
$0\le x\le n$ preserves the inequality. By
\noderef{HypergeometricExponentialMoment} this yields
\[
 \sum_{x\ge m+u}H(n,s,t,x)
 \le \exp(m(e^\lambda-1-\lambda)-\lambda u).
\]
Here and below sums are restricted to $0\le x\le n$.
Take $\lambda=\log(1+u/m)>0$. The exponent becomes $-mh(u/m)$, where
$h(z)=(1+z)\log(1+z)-z$. For $z\ge0$,
\[
 h(z)\ge {z^2\over2(1+z/3)}.
\]
Indeed the difference has value and derivative zero at zero, and second
derivative $1/(1+z)-27/(z+3)^3\ge0$, because
$(z+3)^3-27(z+1)=z^3+9z^2\ge0$. Integrating the second derivative from
zero, then the first derivative, proves the inequality. Thus the upper
tail is at most $e^{-u^2/(2(m+u/3))}$.

For $\lambda<0$ and $x\le m-u$, one has
$1\le e^{\lambda(x-m+u)}$. Multiplying by the mass and enlarging the
sum to all $x$, the same cited moment lemma bounds the
lower tail by $\exp(m(e^\lambda-1-\lambda)-\lambda(-u))$.
For $\lambda\le0$ one has $e^\lambda-1-\lambda\le\lambda^2/2$:
the difference $q(\lambda)=\lambda^2/2-e^\lambda+1+\lambda$ has
$q(0)=q'(0)=0$ and $q''(\lambda)=1-e^\lambda\ge0$ on this half-line.
Integration towards zero gives $q'(\lambda)\le0$ and $q(\lambda)\ge0$.
Choosing $\lambda=-u/m$ therefore bounds the lower tail by
$e^{-u^2/(2m)}$.

Since $s,t\le n$, $m\le n$ and $m+u/3\le n(1+\eta/3)$.
The upper bound is at most $\exp(-\eta^2n/(2(1+\eta/3)))$;
the lower bound is at most $\exp(-\eta^2n/2)$, which is no larger.
The strict deviation event is contained in the union of these two
non-strict tails, so summing their bounds gives the assertion.

If $m=0$, positivity of $n$ implies $s=0$ or $t=0$.
From \noderef{HypergeometricMass}, if $s=0$ only $x=0$ has nonzero mass;
if $t=0$ the coefficient $\binom0x$ excludes every $x>0$.
In either case the mass at zero is one and $m=0$. The strict deviation
sum is therefore zero, proving the assertion in this case as well.
\end{proof}
HypergeometricTwoTail.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Two hypergeometric tails]
For $n>0$, $s,t\le n$, and a positive real number $\eta$, put $m=st/n$.
The masses of \noderef{HypergeometricMass} satisfy
\[
 \sum_{\substack{0\le x\le n\\|x-m|>\eta n}} H(n,s,t,x)
 \le2\exp\left(-{\eta^2n\over2(1+\eta/3)}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}
HypergeometricTwoTail.title: HypergeometricTwoTail

IndependentEdgeSample.lean_statement:
open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

noncomputable def IndependentEdgeSample (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι]
    (q : ℝ≥0) (hq : q ≤ 1) : Measure (ι → Bool) :=
IndependentEdgeSample.name: IndependentEdgeSample
IndependentEdgeSample.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Common independent retention sample]
For a finite index set $I$ and $q\in[0,1]$, let
$\Omega=\{0,1\}^{I}$, with its discrete sigma algebra, and define
$\mu_q=\bigotimes_{i\in I}\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)$.
Equivalently, the mass of $\omega$ is
$\prod_{i\in I}(q\text{ if }\omega_i=1,\;1-q\text{ otherwise})$.
The same sample $\omega$ is used for every retention test. For a graph on
$V$ we use $I=V\times V$; only coordinates oriented from $L$ to $R$
are used, so disjointness of $L,R$ assigns exactly one coordinate to
each undirected cross edge. Unused coordinates have no effect on the graph.
\end{definition}
IndependentEdgeSample.title: IndependentEdgeSample

IndependentRetentionConcentration.lean_proof:
classical

      IsProbabilityMeasure (IndependentEdgeSample ι q hq) ∧
      iIndepFun (fun i (ω : ι → Bool) => (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ))
        (IndependentEdgeSample ι q hq) ∧
      (∀ i : ι, ∫ ω, (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ) ∂(IndependentEdgeSample ι q hq) = q) ∧
      (∀ i : ι, HasSubgaussianMGF (fun ω : ι → Bool =>
        (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ) - q) (1 / 4) (IndependentEdgeSample ι q hq)) := by
    simpa only [IndependentEdgeSample] using
      (IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw (fun _ : ι => q) (fun _ => hq))

    have ht : 0 < ξ * (m : ℝ) := mul_pos hξ (by exact_mod_cast hm)
    simp [hIempty, IndependentRetentionCount, not_lt_of_ge ht.le]
  have hkpos : (0 : ℝ) < I.card := by exact_mod_cast Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hk

  have hix : iIndepFun X μ := hi.comp (fun _ x => x - (q : ℝ))
    (fun _ => measurable_id.sub_const (q : ℝ))

IndependentRetentionConcentration.lean_statement:
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

theorem IndependentRetentionConcentration {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (q : ℝ≥0) (hq : q ≤ 1) (I : Finset ι) (m : ℕ)
    (hm : 0 < m) (hI : I.card ≤ m) (ξ : ℝ) (hξ : 0 < ξ) :
    IndependentEdgeSample ι q hq
      {ω | ξ * m < |(IndependentRetentionCount I ω : ℝ) - (q : ℝ) * I.card|} ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-2 * ξ ^ 2 * m)) := by
IndependentRetentionConcentration.name: IndependentRetentionConcentration
IndependentRetentionConcentration.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $k=|I|$ and $t=\xi m>0$. If $k=0$, the count is zero by
\noderef{IndependentRetentionCount}, so the failure event is empty and
its probability is zero. Suppose $k>0$. By
\noderef{IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw} specialized to the constant
coordinate probabilities $q_i=q$, the coordinates have expectations $q$,
and $X_i-q$ are independent centered
sub-Gaussian variables with parameters $1/4$. Independence is preserved
under coordinatewise translation and negation. The count definition gives
$K_I-qk=\sum_{i\in I}(X_i-q)$, and
$qk-K_I=\sum_{i\in I}(-(X_i-q))$. Negation preserves the same MGF bound:
substitute $-u$ for $u$ in that bound.

Apply the checked Mathlib theorem
\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF.measure\_sum\_ge\_le\_of\_iIndepFun}:
for independent variables with parameters $c_i$ and $t\geq0$, it bounds
the real probability of $t\leq\sum_iY_i$ by
$\exp(-t^2/(2\sum_i c_i))$. Here $\sum_{i\in I}c_i=k/4$, so each of
the two non-strict tail events has probability at most
$\exp(-2t^2/k)$. The strict absolute-value failure event is contained
in their union; subadditivity therefore bounds its probability by
$2\exp(-2\xi^2m^2/k)$. Since $0<k\leq m$, we have $m^2/k\geq m$.
Multiplication by $-2\xi^2$ reverses this inequality, and monotonicity
of the exponential gives the claimed bound.

All events are measurable because the sample space is finite and
discrete. By the probability clause of
\noderef{IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw} with the same constant-coordinate specialization,
every event measure is at most one and thus finite. Its real conversion
is therefore reversible: $\operatorname{ofReal}(\mu(E).\operatorname{toReal})
=\mu(E)$. Applying the monotone map $\operatorname{ofReal}$ to the real
tail and union inequalities proves precisely the stated extended-real
inequality. No division by a zero summand count is used.
\end{proof}
IndependentRetentionConcentration.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Two-sided concentration for one retention test]
Let $I$ be a subset of a finite coordinate set, $0\leq q\leq1$,
$m$ a positive integer with $|I|\leq m$, and $\xi>0$. Under the common
law of \noderef{IndependentEdgeSample}, the count of
\noderef{IndependentRetentionCount} satisfies
\[
\mu_q\{\omega:|K_I(\omega)-q|I||>\xi m\}
\leq 2\exp(-2\xi^2 m).
\]
The bound is interpreted as an extended nonnegative real.
\end{lemma}
IndependentRetentionConcentration.title: IndependentRetentionConcentration

IndependentRetentionCount.lean_statement: def IndependentRetentionCount {ι : Type*} (I : Finset ι) (ω : ι → Bool) : ℕ :=
IndependentRetentionCount.name: IndependentRetentionCount
IndependentRetentionCount.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Retained coordinate count]
For a finite set $A$ of coordinates and a Boolean sample $\omega$, put
$K_A(\omega)=|\{i\in A:\omega_i=1\}|$.
In particular $K_\varnothing=0$.
\end{definition}
IndependentRetentionCount.title: IndependentRetentionCount

classical

  letI := hμ
  have hi : iIndepFun (fun i (ω : ι → Bool) => (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) μ := by
    exact iIndepFun_pi (fun _ =>
      (measurable_of_countable (fun b : Bool => (if b then 1 else 0 : ℝ))).aemeasurable)
  have he (i : ι) : ∫ ω, (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ) ∂μ = q i := by
    have hp := measurePreserving_eval (fun i => (PMF.bernoulli (q i) (hq i)).toMeasure) i
    rw [← PMF.bernoulli_expectation (hq i), ← hp.map_eq]
    have hf : (fun b : Bool => (if b then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) =
        (fun b => cond b 1 0) := by ext b; cases b <;> rfl

    rw [← hf]

  refine ⟨hμ, hi, he, ?_⟩
  intro i
  have hb : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 :=

  have hs := hasSubgaussianMGF_of_mem_Icc
    (measurable_of_countable (fun ω : ι → Bool => (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ))).aemeasurable hb

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

theorem IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (q : ι → ℝ≥0) (hq : ∀ i, q i ≤ 1) :
    let μ := Measure.pi (fun i => (PMF.bernoulli (q i) (hq i)).toMeasure)
    IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧
      iIndepFun (fun i (ω : ι → Bool) => (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) μ ∧
      (∀ i, ∫ ω, (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ) ∂μ = q i) ∧
      (∀ i, HasSubgaussianMGF (fun ω : ι → Bool =>
        (if ω i then 1 else 0 : ℝ) - q i) (1 / 4) μ) := by
IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw.name: IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw
IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Each Bernoulli law is a probability measure, including $q_i=0$ and $q_i=1$,
so its finite product is a probability measure. Evaluation at coordinate
$i$ preserves measure to that coordinate's Bernoulli law. Consequently
the integral of its indicator is the Bernoulli expectation $q_i$.
The coordinate functions are measurable, and functions of distinct
coordinates in a product measure are independent. Each indicator takes
values in $[0,1]$. Mathlib's proved Hoeffding lemma
\texttt{hasSubgaussianMGF\_of\_mem\_Icc} therefore gives the centered
indicator parameter $(1-0)^2/4=1/4$. These are exactly the claimed
independence, expectation, and moment-generating-function conclusions.
\end{proof}
IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Independent unequal Bernoulli law]
Let $I$ be a finite index type and let $q_i\in[0,1]$ be nonnegative real
numbers. On $\Omega=\{0,1\}^I$ put the product of the Bernoulli laws with
success probabilities $q_i$. This is a probability measure; the coordinate
indicators $X_i$ are independent, $\mathbb E X_i=q_i$, and every centered
indicator $X_i-q_i$ has subgaussian moment-generating-function parameter
$1/4$, that is, for every real $s$,
\[
 \mathbb E\exp(s(X_i-q_i))\leq\exp(s^2/8).
\]
\end{lemma}
IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw.title: IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw

          ((UniformPerfectMatching G U W hUW h).map fun f u => (f.val u : V))
          (matchingConstant round x / m) Set.univ
InductionApplicationCertificate.lean_statement:
structure InductionApplicationCertificate
    (Delta Q : ℕ) (d : ENNReal)
    (t D beta rho eta omega xi : ℕ → ENNReal) where
InductionApplicationCertificate.name: InductionApplicationCertificate
InductionApplicationCertificate.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}
Fix $\Delta,Q\in\mathbb N$, $d\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}$, and
sequences $\theta,p,\eta,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\xi:\mathbb N\to
\mathbb R_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}$.  An \emph{induction application
certificate} consists of threshold functions
$N^{\rm wit}:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ and $N^{\rm host}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$,
constant functions $a:\mathbb N^3\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}$ and
$M:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}$, and threshold functions
$N^{\rm FG}:\mathbb N^3\to\mathbb N$ and
$N^{\rm mat},N^{\rm exist}:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$, having all of the following
properties.  The functions are total, but the guarantees below are required
only in the finite certified range $s<Q$; their values at $s\geq Q$ are
arbitrary.

For every round $s<Q$ and every $x\leq\Delta$, every finite ambient vertex type $V$ with decidable
equality, every graph $G$ on $V$ with decidable adjacency, and all finite
parts $L,R\subseteq V$, if
\[
 L\cap R=\varnothing,\quad N^{\rm wit}_{s,x}\leq |L|,\quad
 N^{\rm wit}_{s,x}\leq |R|,\quad |L|\leq |R|+1,\quad |R|\leq |L|+1,
\]
and $G[L,R]$ is $(\eta_s,p_x)$-super-regular, then there is a graph $G'$ on
the same ambient type such that $G'\subseteq G$ and $G'[L,R]$ is
$(\xi_s,\rho_x)$-super-regular.  Under the same quantification, if
\[
 L\cap R=\varnothing,\quad N^{\rm host}_s\leq |L|,\quad
 N^{\rm host}_s\leq |R|,\quad |L|\leq |R|+1,\quad |R|\leq |L|+1,
\]
and $G[L,R]$ is $(\eta_0,d)$-super-regular, then there is a graph $G'$ on
the same ambient type such that $G'\subseteq G$ and $G'[L,R]$ is
$(\xi_s,d/2)$-super-regular.  Here $\xi_s$ is the inner reserve below the
post-padding error $\zeta_s$; the certificate records the thinning
conclusion, while the induction step records the quantitative slack from
$\xi_s$ to $\zeta_s$.  In each conclusion the graph is spanning on
the specified parts because its vertex type and the parts themselves are
unchanged.

For every round $s<Q$ and every ordered pair $x,y\leq\Delta$, one has $0<a_{s,x,y}\leq1$.  Moreover, consider any
finite ambient vertex type $V$ with decidable equality, any three graphs
$F_{12},F_{13},F_{23}$ on $V$ with decidable adjacency, finite parts
$W_1,W_2,W_3\subseteq V$, and $m\in\mathbb N$ with
$N^{\rm FG}_{s,x,y}\leq m$.  Suppose the parts are pairwise disjoint,
\[
 |W_1|=|W_2|=m,\qquad m\leq |W_3|+1,qquad |W_3|\leq m+1,
\]
the pairs $(W_1,W_2)$ in $F_{12}$, $(W_1,W_3)$ in $F_{13}$, and
$(W_2,W_3)$ in $F_{23}$ are respectively
\[
 (\theta_s,\rho_x),\qquad (\theta_s,\rho_y),\qquad (\theta_s,d/2)
\]
super-regular, and every edge $vu\in E(F_{12})$ with $v\in W_1$ and
$u\in W_2$ satisfies
\[
 (\rho_y(d/2)-\theta_s)|W_3|
 \leq |N_{F_{13}}(v)\cap N_{F_{23}}(u)\cap W_3|
 \leq (\rho_y(d/2)+\theta_s)|W_3|.
\]
Thus the full near-equal $(\theta_s,\rho_x,\rho_y,d/2)$-regular-triplet
hypothesis holds.  For every proof $h_{12}$ that $W_1$ and $W_2$ are
disjoint and every witness that the type
\[
 \mathcal M=\{\sigma:W_1\to W_2:\sigma\text{ is a perfect matching of }
 F_{12}[W_1,W_2]\text{ relative to }h_{12}\}
\]
is nonempty, let $\mu$ be the uniform probability mass function on
$\mathcal M$.  For $\sigma\in\mathcal M$, let $A_\sigma$ be the graph on the
disjoint union $W_1\sqcup W_3$ in which the left copy of $v\in W_1$ is
adjacent to the right copy of $w\in W_3$ exactly when
$vw\in E(F_{13})$ and $\sigma(v)w\in E(F_{23})$.  Then the outer measure
induced by $\mu$ satisfies
\[
 1-(1-a_{s,x,y})^m\leq
 \mu^{*}\!\left(\left\{\sigma\in\mathcal M:
 A_\sigma[W_1,W_3]\text{ is }
 (\omega_{s+1},\rho_y(d/2))\text{-super-regular}\right\}\right),
\]
where the displayed parts of $A_\sigma$ are the full left and right copies
in $W_1\sqcup W_3$.

Finally, for every round $s<Q$ and $x\leq\Delta$, one has $M_{s,x}\geq1$.  For every finite
ambient vertex type $V$ with decidable equality, every graph $G$ on $V$ with
decidable adjacency, disjoint finite parts $U,W\subseteq V$, and
$m\in\mathbb N$, suppose that
\[
 N^{\rm mat}_{s,x}\leq m,\qquad |U|=m,\qquad |W|=m,
\]
$G[U,W]$ is $(\theta_s,\rho_x)$-super-regular, and the type $\mathcal P$ of
perfect matchings $f:U\to W$ of $G[U,W]$ is nonempty.  If $\nu$ is the
uniform probability mass function on $\mathcal P$, then the pushforward of
$\nu$ along $f\mapsto (u\mapsto f(u))$, viewing each subtype-valued matching
as an ordinary map $U\to V$, is $(M_{s,x}/m)$-vertex-spread on the whole
codomain $V$.

The certificate also supplies this nonemptiness rather than assuming it:
under the same ambient quantification, if
\[
 N^{\rm exist}_{s,x}\leq m,\qquad |U|=|W|=m,
 \qquad G[U,W]\text{ is }(\theta_s,\rho_x)\text{-super-regular},
\]
then the type $\mathcal P$ of perfect matchings is nonempty.  Thus the
existence witness needed to form the uniform law is a certified output for
every retained pair above the recorded threshold.
\end{definition}

IntegralFlowAugmentation.lean_proof:
classical
  let r (i : Fin p.length) : ℤ :=
    (N.capacity (p.vertex i.castSucc) (p.vertex i.succ) : ℤ) -
      f.amount (p.vertex i.castSucc) (p.vertex i.succ)
  let S := Finset.univ.image r
  have hS : S.Nonempty := by
    exact ⟨r ⟨0, p.positive⟩, Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨⟨0, p.positive⟩, by simp, rfl⟩⟩
  let δ := S.min' hS
  have hδ : 0 < δ := by
    obtain ⟨i, _, hi⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp (Finset.min'_mem S hS)
    have hr := p.residual i
    dsimp [r] at hi
    dsimp [δ]
    rw [← hi]
    exact sub_pos.mpr hr
  have hδr (i : Fin p.length) : δ ≤ r i :=
    Finset.min'_le S (r i) (Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨i, by simp, rfl⟩)
  let C (v w : V) : ℤ :=
    ((Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin p.length =>
      p.vertex i.castSucc = v ∧ p.vertex i.succ = w).card : ℤ)
  have hCnonneg (v w : V) : 0 ≤ C v w := by
    dsimp [C]
    positivity
  have hCle (v w : V) : C v w ≤ 1 := by
    have hc : (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin p.length =>
        p.vertex i.castSucc = v ∧ p.vertex i.succ = w).card ≤ 1 := by
      apply Finset.card_le_one.mpr
      intro i hi j hj
      have he : i.castSucc = j.castSucc := p.injective
        ((Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2.1.trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2.1.symm)
      exact Fin.castSucc_injective _ he
    dsimp [C]
    exact_mod_cast hc
  let a (v w : V) := f.amount v w + δ * (C v w - C w v)
  have habound (v w : V) : a v w ≤ (N.capacity v w : ℤ) := by
    by_cases hc : C v w = 0
    · dsimp [a]
      have hb := f.bound v w
      have hn := hCnonneg w v
      nlinarith
    · have hpos : 0 < (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin p.length =>
          p.vertex i.castSucc = v ∧ p.vertex i.succ = w).card := by
        by_contra hn
        have hz : (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin p.length =>
            p.vertex i.castSucc = v ∧ p.vertex i.succ = w).card = 0 := by omega
        exact hc (by simp [C, hz])
      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Finset.card_pos.mp hpos
      obtain ⟨hv, hw⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2
      have hr := hδr i
      dsimp [r] at hr
      rw [hv, hw] at hr
      have hf := hCle v w
      have hb := hCnonneg w v
      dsimp [a]
      nlinarith
  have hCsum (v w : V) : C v w =
      ∑ i : Fin p.length, if p.vertex i.castSucc = v ∧ p.vertex i.succ = w
        then (1 : ℤ) else 0 := by
    simp [C, Finset.sum_boole]
  have hdepart (v : V) : (∑ w, C v w) =
      ∑ i : Fin p.length, if p.vertex i.castSucc = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0 := by
    simp_rw [hCsum]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    by_cases h : p.vertex i.castSucc = v <;> simp [h]
  have harrive (v : V) : (∑ w, C w v) =
      ∑ i : Fin p.length, if p.vertex i.succ = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0 := by
    simp_rw [hCsum]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    by_cases h : p.vertex i.succ = v <;> simp [h]
  have htel (b : Fin (p.length + 1) → ℤ) :
      (∑ i : Fin p.length, b i.castSucc) - (∑ i : Fin p.length, b i.succ) =
        b 0 - b (Fin.last p.length) := by
    have h₁ := Fin.sum_univ_castSucc b
    have h₂ := Fin.sum_univ_succ b
    linarith
  have harow (v : V) : (∑ w, a v w) = (∑ w, f.amount v w) +
      δ * ((if N.source = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0) -
        (if N.sink = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0)) := by
    simp only [a, Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum,
      Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hdepart, harrive]
    rw [htel (fun j => if p.vertex j = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0)]
    rw [p.start, p.finish]
  let g : FiniteIntegralFlow N := {
    amount := a
    skew := by
      intro v w
      dsimp [a]
      rw [f.skew v w]
      ring
    bound := habound
    conserve := by
      intro v hs ht
      rw [harow, f.conserve v hs ht]
      simp [Ne.symm hs, Ne.symm ht] }
  refine ⟨δ, g, hδ, hδr, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro v w
    rfl
  · change (∑ w, a N.source w) = _
    rw [harow]
    simp [Ne.symm N.terminals_distinct]
IntegralFlowAugmentation.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem IntegralFlowAugmentation {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    {N : FiniteCapacityNetwork V} (f : FiniteIntegralFlow N)
    (p : SimpleResidualPath f) :
    ∃ (δ : ℤ) (g : FiniteIntegralFlow N),
      0 < δ ∧
      (∀ i : Fin p.length,
        δ ≤ (N.capacity (p.vertex i.castSucc) (p.vertex i.succ) : ℤ) -
          f.amount (p.vertex i.castSucc) (p.vertex i.succ)) ∧
      (∀ v w, g.amount v w = f.amount v w + δ *
        (((Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin p.length =>
          p.vertex i.castSucc = v ∧ p.vertex i.succ = w).card : ℤ) -
         ((Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin p.length =>
          p.vertex i.castSucc = w ∧ p.vertex i.succ = v).card : ℤ))) ∧
      (∑ w, g.amount N.source w) = (∑ w, f.amount N.source w) + δ := by
IntegralFlowAugmentation.name: IntegralFlowAugmentation
IntegralFlowAugmentation.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
By \noderef{SimpleResidualPath}, the $m$ residual capacities are positive
integers and $m>0$. Let $\delta$ be their minimum. This minimum exists
because there are finitely many and at least one; it is a positive integer
and is no greater than each residual capacity. Define $g$ by the displayed
formula. Its values are integers. Interchanging $v,w$ negates the change,
so skew symmetry follows from \noderef{FiniteIntegralFlow}.

Injectivity of $p$ implies that each directed pair occurs at most once.
An edge and its reverse cannot both occur: such occurrences would repeat
both endpoints, whereas their positions in an injective sequence are
unique. Consecutive vertices are distinct. Thus the change on any pair is
either $0$, $\delta$, or $-\delta$. On a forward path edge, the choice of
$\delta$ gives $g(v,w)\leq c(v,w)$. On a reverse path edge the flow
decreases, so its upper capacity bound is preserved. On other pairs the
bound is unchanged. This checks all upper bounds, and skew symmetry also
checks all lower bounds.

At an internal path vertex $p(j)$, $0<j<m$, its outgoing sum gains
$\delta$ on the pair to $p(j+1)$ and loses $\delta$ on the pair to
$p(j-1)$, and changes on no other pair. Its divergence is unchanged.
Vertices outside the path have unchanged divergence as well. The only
remaining path vertices are the distinct terminals. The source occurs
only as $p(0)$ and gains $\delta$ on its sole outgoing path step, with
no incoming path step. The sink has the opposite change. Hence every
required conservation equation is preserved and the value increases
by exactly $\delta$.
\end{proof}
IntegralFlowAugmentation.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Integral augmentation along a simple residual path]
Let $f$ be a feasible integral flow on a finite integer-capacity network
with distinct terminals, and let $p(0),\ldots,p(m)$ be a simple residual
source-to-sink path, as in \noderef{SimpleResidualPath}.
There are an integer $\delta>0$ and a feasible integral flow $g$ such that
$\delta\leq c(p(i),p(i+1))-f(p(i),p(i+1))$ for every $i<m$,
\[
g(v,w)=f(v,w)+\delta\bigl(
 |\{i<m:p(i)=v,\ p(i+1)=w\}|-
 |\{i<m:p(i)=w,\ p(i+1)=v\}|\bigr),
\qquad |g|=|f|+\delta.
\]
\end{lemma}
IntegralFlowAugmentation.title: IntegralFlowAugmentation

IntegralFlowCutIdentity.lean_proof:
have hcancel : (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ S, f.amount v w) =
      -(∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ S, f.amount v w) := by
    calc
      _ = ∑ w ∈ S, ∑ v ∈ S, f.amount v w := Finset.sum_comm
      _ = ∑ w ∈ S, ∑ v ∈ S, -f.amount w v := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro w hw
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro v hv
        exact f.skew v w
      _ = _ := by simp only [Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  have hz : (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ S, f.amount v w) = 0 := by omega
  have hdiv : (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w, f.amount v w) = ∑ w, f.amount N.source w := by
    apply Finset.sum_eq_single N.source
    · intro v hv hne
      exact f.conserve v hne (fun he => ht (he ▸ hv))
    · intro hnot
      exact (hnot hs).elim
  have hsplit : (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w, f.amount v w) =
      (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ S, f.amount v w) +
      ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ Finset.univ \ S, f.amount v w := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro v hv
    have h := Finset.sum_sdiff (f := f.amount v) (Finset.subset_univ S)
    simpa only [add_comm] using h.symm
  rw [hz, zero_add, hdiv] at hsplit
  exact hsplit
IntegralFlowCutIdentity.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem IntegralFlowCutIdentity {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    {N : FiniteCapacityNetwork V} (f : FiniteIntegralFlow N)
    (S : Finset V) (hs : N.source ∈ S) (ht : N.sink ∉ S) :
    (∑ w, f.amount N.source w) =
      ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ Finset.univ \ S, f.amount v w := by
IntegralFlowCutIdentity.name: IntegralFlowCutIdentity
IntegralFlowCutIdentity.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Sum the divergence $\sum_w f(v,w)$ over $v\in S$. By conservation in
\noderef{FiniteIntegralFlow}, each term except the source term is zero:
the sink is outside $S$, and any other vertex in $S$ is neither terminal.
The sum is therefore $|f|$. Split each inner sum into $w\in S$ and
$w\notin S$. The sum over $S\times S$ is zero: the bijection
$(v,w)\mapsto(w,v)$ negates every summand by skew symmetry, so this
integer sum is its own negative and hence zero. Equivalently diagonal
terms are zero and off-diagonal terms cancel in pairs. Removing that
sum gives the asserted identity.
\end{proof}
IntegralFlowCutIdentity.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Net flow across a cut]
Let $f$ be a feasible integral flow on a finite network with distinct
terminals, as in \noderef{FiniteIntegralFlow}. For every subset $S$ with
$s\in S$ and $t\notin S$,
\[
 |f|=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{w\notin S} f(v,w).
\]
\end{lemma}
IntegralFlowCutIdentity.title: IntegralFlowCutIdentity

IntegralFlowTerminalCut.lean_proof:
classical
  let value (f : FiniteIntegralFlow N) : ℤ := ∑ w, f.amount N.source w
  let M : ℤ := ∑ w, (N.capacity N.source w : ℤ)
  have hbound (f : FiniteIntegralFlow N) : value f ≤ M := by
    exact Finset.sum_le_sum (fun w _ => f.bound N.source w)
  have hterminal : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ f : FiniteIntegralFlow N,
      0 ≤ value f → (M - value f).toNat = n →
      ∃ g : FiniteIntegralFlow N, 0 ≤ value g ∧ ¬Nonempty (SimpleResidualPath g) := by
    intro n
    induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | h n ih =>
      intro f hf hn
      by_cases hp : Nonempty (SimpleResidualPath f)
      · obtain ⟨p⟩ := hp
        obtain ⟨δ, g, hδ, _, _, hval⟩ := IntegralFlowAugmentation f p
        change value g = value f + δ at hval
        have hg : 0 ≤ value g := by omega
        have hfb := hbound f
        have hgb := hbound g
        have hsmall : (M - value g).toNat < n := by omega
        exact ih (M - value g).toNat hsmall g hg rfl
      · exact ⟨f, hf, hp⟩
  let zero : FiniteIntegralFlow N := {
    amount := fun _ _ => 0
    skew := by intros; simp
    bound := by intros; positivity
    conserve := by intros; simp }
  have hzero : 0 ≤ value zero := by simp [value, zero]
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hno⟩ := hterminal (M - value zero).toNat zero hzero rfl
  let R (v w : V) : Prop := f.amount v w < (N.capacity v w : ℤ)
  let S : Finset V := Finset.univ.filter (Relation.ReflTransGen R N.source)
  have hmem (v : V) : v ∈ S ↔ Relation.ReflTransGen R N.source v := by
    simp [S]
  have hs : N.source ∈ S := (hmem _).mpr .refl
  have hclosed (v w : V) (hv : v ∈ S) (hr : R v w) : w ∈ S :=
    (hmem _).mpr ((hmem _).mp hv |>.tail hr)
  have ht : N.sink ∉ S := by
    intro ht
    obtain ⟨n, p, hpos, hinj, hstart, hfinish, hres⟩ :=
      DirectedReachabilitySimplePath R ((hmem _).mp ht) N.terminals_distinct
    exact hno ⟨{
      length := n
      positive := hpos
      vertex := p
      injective := hinj
      start := hstart
      finish := hfinish
      residual := hres }⟩
  have heq (v w : V) (hv : v ∈ S) (hw : w ∉ S) :
      f.amount v w = (N.capacity v w : ℤ) := by
    have hn : ¬R v w := fun hr => hw (hclosed v w hv hr)
    exact le_antisymm (f.bound v w) (le_of_not_gt hn)
  refine ⟨f, S, hs, ht, ?_, hf, hbound f⟩
  rw [IntegralFlowCutIdentity f S hs ht]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro v hv
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro w hw
  exact heq v w hv (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).2
IntegralFlowTerminalCut.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem IntegralFlowTerminalCut {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (N : FiniteCapacityNetwork V) :
    ∃ (f : FiniteIntegralFlow N) (S : Finset V),
      N.source ∈ S ∧ N.sink ∉ S ∧
      (∑ w, f.amount N.source w) =
        ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ Finset.univ \ S, (N.capacity v w : ℤ) ∧
      0 ≤ (∑ w, f.amount N.source w) ∧
      (∑ w, f.amount N.source w) ≤ ∑ w, (N.capacity N.source w : ℤ) := by
IntegralFlowTerminalCut.name: IntegralFlowTerminalCut
IntegralFlowTerminalCut.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The capacities in \noderef{FiniteCapacityNetwork} are finite nonnegative
integers. The zero function satisfies \noderef{FiniteIntegralFlow}: it is
skew symmetric, is bounded above by every capacity, and has zero divergence.
For any feasible flow, summing its upper bounds at the source gives
$|f|\leq M:=\sum_w c(s,w)$, a finite nonnegative integer.

Start at zero. If a simple residual source-to-sink path exists, apply
\noderef{IntegralFlowAugmentation}. This preserves feasibility and
increases the integer value by at least one. This process must stop
within $M$ augmentations: after $r$ augmentations its value is at least
$r$, and a further augmentation from value $M$ contradicts the bound.
More formally, induction on the nonnegative integer $M-|f|$ gives a
terminal flow reachable from any intermediate flow: without a path it
is already terminal, and with a path augmentation decreases this integer
strictly. Starting at zero therefore gives a terminal $f$ with
$0\leq |f|\leq M$ and no simple residual source-to-sink path.

Let $S$ consist of vertices reachable from $s$ by finite residual walks,
including the length-zero walk. It is a finite subset because the vertex
type is finite, and it contains $s$. A residual walk from $s$ to $t$
would give a simple path: if a vertex repeats at positions $i<j$, delete
the segment after position $i$ through position $j$. The adjoining step
is still a residual step because the vertices at $i,j$ agree. This
shortens the walk and preserves its endpoints. Repetition removal
terminates as lengths decrease, producing an injective walk. Distinct
terminals ensure its length is positive. It is therefore a path in the
precise sense of \noderef{SimpleResidualPath}, contrary to terminality.
Thus $t\notin S$.

For $v\in S,w\notin S$ there is no residual step from $v$ to $w$,
since appending such a step would make $w$ reachable. Consequently
$f(v,w)\geq c(v,w)$, and the flow bound gives equality. Apply
\noderef{IntegralFlowCutIdentity} and replace each crossing net flow
by its capacity. This gives $|f|=C(S)$ as required. When $M=0$ the same
argument starts and stops at the zero flow; no positive-capacity path
can be augmented without contradicting the value bound.
\end{proof}
IntegralFlowTerminalCut.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Termination and a tight residual cut]
Every finite integer-capacity network with distinct terminals admits a
feasible integral flow $f$ and a subset $S$ containing $s$ and excluding
$t$ such that
\[
 |f|=C(S),\qquad 0\leq |f|\leq\sum_w c(s,w).
\]
Here network, flow, and cut capacity have the meanings in
\noderef{FiniteCapacityNetwork} and \noderef{FiniteIntegralFlow}.
\end{lemma}
IntegralFlowTerminalCut.title: IntegralFlowTerminalCut

LogFactorialBounds.lean_proof:
induction n, hn using Nat.le_induction with
  | base => norm_num
  | succ n hn ih =>
    have hnR : 0 < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hsR : 0 < (n : ℝ) + 1 := by positivity
    have hu := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos hsR hnR)
    have hl := Real.one_sub_inv_le_log_of_pos (div_pos hsR hnR)
    rw [Real.log_div hsR.ne' hnR.ne'] at hu hl
    have hu' : (n : ℝ) * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log n) ≤ 1 := by
      have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hu hnR.le
      field_simp at this
      nlinarith
    have hl' : 1 ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log n) := by
      have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hl hsR.le
      simp only [inv_div] at this
      field_simp at this
      nlinarith
    rw [Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.cast_mul,
      Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity)]
    push_cast
    constructor <;> nlinarith [ih.1, ih.2]
LogFactorialBounds.lean_statement:
theorem LogFactorialBounds (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (n : ℝ) * Real.log n - n ≤ Real.log (n.factorial : ℝ) ∧
    Real.log (n.factorial : ℝ) ≤
      (n : ℝ) * Real.log n - n + Real.log n + 1 := by
LogFactorialBounds.name: LogFactorialBounds
LogFactorialBounds.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For every positive real number $z$ the tangent-line inequality for the
logarithm gives $\log z\le z-1$. Applying this inequality to $1/z$
also gives $1-1/z\le\log z$.
For completeness, the tangent-line inequality follows because the
function $z-1-\log z$ has derivative $1-1/z$, which is nonpositive
on $(0,1]$ and nonnegative on $[1,\infty)$; its value at $1$ is zero.
For a positive integer $n$, put
$q_n=\log(n+1)-\log n=\log((n+1)/n)$.
The two inequalities just proved yield
\[
 n q_n\le1,\qquad (n+1)q_n\ge1.
\]
We now prove the two factorial bounds simultaneously by induction.
At $n=1$, they read $-1\le0\le0$.
If the lower bound holds at $n$, then
\[
 \log((n+1)!)\ge n\log n-n+\log(n+1)
 \ge (n+1)\log(n+1)-(n+1),
\]
where the second inequality is precisely $nq_n\le1$.
If the upper bound holds at $n$, then
\[
 \log((n+1)!)\le n\log n-n+\log n+1+\log(n+1)
 \le (n+1)\log(n+1)-(n+1)+\log(n+1)+1,
\]
where the second inequality is precisely $(n+1)q_n\ge1$.
Here both induction steps use $(n+1)!=(n+1)n!$ and positivity of
its factors to take logarithms. This completes the induction.
\end{proof}
LogFactorialBounds.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Elementary logarithmic factorial bounds]
For every positive integer $n$,
\[
 n\log n-n\le\log(n!)\le n\log n-n+\log n+1.
\]
\end{lemma}
LogFactorialBounds.title: LogFactorialBounds

theorem LowerRegularBadRows {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (L R S : Finset V) (ε d : ENNReal)
    (hreg : LowerRegularPair G L R ε d) (hS : S ⊆ R)
    (hsize : ε * R.card < S.card) :
    ((L.filter fun v => ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) <
      (d - ε) * S.card).card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * L.card := by
LowerRegularBadRows.name: LowerRegularBadRows
LowerRegularBadRows.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $T$ be the displayed bad-row set and suppose $\varepsilon|L|<|T|$.
The strict thresholds imply that $T$ and $S$ are nonempty, so
$|T||S|$ is positive and finite. By \noderef{FilteredProductRowCount},
the ordered edge count is $\sum_{v\in T}|N_G(v)\cap S|$.
Every summand is strictly below $(d-\varepsilon)_+|S|$; summing over
the nonempty finite set $T$ therefore gives a strict upper bound
$(d-\varepsilon)_+|T||S|$ on the edge count. Division by the positive
finite denominator gives $d_G(T,S)<(d-\varepsilon)_+$, with density
as defined in \noderef{PairDensity}. But $T\subseteq L$, $S\subseteq R$,
and both strict thresholds hold, so \noderef{LowerRegularPair} gives
$d_G(T,S)\geq(d-\varepsilon)_+$. This contradiction proves the bound.
The argument does not require upper regularity or positive $\varepsilon$.
If the truncated lower endpoint is infinite, the strict sum inequality
and division still hold in the extended nonnegative reals; the
denominator remains positive and finite.
\end{proof}
LowerRegularBadRows.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Bad rows of a lower-regular pair]
Let $G$ be a graph, $L,R,S$ finite vertex sets, and $\varepsilon,d$ extended
nonnegative reals. Suppose $G[L,R]$ is lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-regular,
$S\subseteq R$, and $\varepsilon|R|<|S|$. Then
\[
 |\{v\in L:|N_G(v)\cap S|<(d-\varepsilon)_+|S|\}|
       \leq\varepsilon|L|.
\]
Here subtraction is truncated subtraction, as in
\noderef{LowerRegularPair}.
\end{lemma}
LowerRegularBadRows.title: LowerRegularBadRows

theorem LowerRegularRestriction {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W U' W' : Finset V)
    (ε θ d : ENNReal) (hU : U' ⊆ U) (hW : W' ⊆ W) (hεθ : ε ≤ θ)
    (hUthreshold : ε * (U.card : ENNReal) ≤ θ * (U'.card : ENNReal))
    (hWthreshold : ε * (W.card : ENNReal) ≤ θ * (W'.card : ENNReal))
    (hreg : LowerRegularPair G U W ε d) :
    LowerRegularPair G U' W' θ d := by
LowerRegularRestriction.name: LowerRegularRestriction
LowerRegularRestriction.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For any $S\subseteq U'$, $T\subseteq W'$ above the strict
$\theta$ thresholds, the assumptions imply
$|S|>\varepsilon|U|$ and $|T|>\varepsilon|W|$.
Apply the definition in \noderef{LowerRegularPair} to these sets
inside $U,W$. It gives density at least $d-\varepsilon$.
Monotonicity of truncated subtraction and $\varepsilon\leq\theta$
give $d-\theta\leq d-\varepsilon$, proving the required lower bound.
This proof makes no positivity, finiteness, or nonempty-set assumption
beyond the displayed strict tests.
\end{proof}
LowerRegularRestriction.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Threshold transfer to restricted parts]
Let $(U,W)$ in $G$ be lower $(\varepsilon,d)$-regular,
$U'\subseteq U$, $W'\subseteq W$, and $\varepsilon\leq\theta$.
Assume $\varepsilon|U|\leq\theta|U'|$ and
$\varepsilon|W|\leq\theta|W'|$. Then $(U',W')$ is lower
$(\theta,d)$-regular. The parameters may be extended nonnegative
reals and all subtraction is truncated.
\end{lemma}
LowerRegularRestriction.title: LowerRegularRestriction

LowerSuperRegularDeletionSlicing.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Lower-super-regular slicing after deletion]
Let $(U,W)$ be lower $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular in a graph $G$, and delete sets $D_U\subseteq U$ and $D_W\subseteq W$.  Suppose the residual pair $(U\setminus D_U,W\setminus D_W)$ is lower $(\varepsilon',d')$-regular and

\qquad
(d'-\varepsilon')|U\setminus D_U|\leq(d-\varepsilon)|U|-|D_U|.
\]
Then the residual pair is lower $(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular.
\end{lemma}

    Finset.card_image_of_injective S hinj
  have density (P Q : Finset V) (hP : P ⊆ L) (hQ : Q ⊆ R) :
      PairDensity H (P.image e) (Q.image e) = PairDensity G P Q := by
    have edges :
        (((P.image e).product (Q.image e)).filter fun p => H.Adj p.1 p.2) =
        ((P.product Q).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).image (Prod.map e e) := by
      change (((P.image e) ×ˢ (Q.image e)).filter _) = _
      rw [← Finset.prodMap_image_product, Finset.filter_image]
      congr 1
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro p hp
      obtain ⟨hp, hq⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hp
      exact hadj p.1 (hP hp) p.2 (hQ hq)
    unfold PairDensity
    rw [edges, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (hinj.prodMap hinj), card, card]
  have left (x : V) (hx : x ∈ L) :
      ((R.image e).filter fun y => H.Adj (e x) y).card =
        (R.filter fun y => G.Adj x y).card := by
    rw [Finset.filter_image]
    have hh : R.filter (fun y => H.Adj (e x) (e y)) =
        R.filter (fun y => G.Adj x y) :=
      Finset.filter_congr fun y hy => hadj x hx y hy
    rw [hh, card]
  have right (y : V) (hy : y ∈ R) :
      ((L.image e).filter fun x => H.Adj x (e y)).card =
        (L.filter fun x => G.Adj x y).card := by
    rw [Finset.filter_image]
    have hh : L.filter (fun x => H.Adj (e x) (e y)) =
        L.filter (fun x => G.Adj x y) :=
      Finset.filter_congr fun x hx => hadj x hx y hy

    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩

      let Q0 := R.filter fun x => e x ∈ Q

      simpa only [card, right b hb] using hG.2.2 b hb

      have hsQ : Q.image e ⊆ R.image e := Finset.image_subset_image hQ

LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding.lean_statement:
theorem LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding
    {V W : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq W]
    (e : V → W) (hinj : Function.Injective e)
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (L R : Finset V) (eps d : ENNReal)
    (hadj : ∀ x ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ R, H.Adj (e x) (e y) ↔ G.Adj x y) :
    LowerSuperRegularPair G L R eps d ↔
    LowerSuperRegularPair H (L.image e) (R.image e) eps d := by
LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding.name: LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding
LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Injectivity preserves the cardinality of every finite set. For any
$P\subseteq L,Q\subseteq R$, the map $(x,y)\mapsto(e(x),e(y))$
is a bijection from the ordered $G$-edges of $P\times Q$ to the
ordered $H$-edges of $e(P)\times e(Q)$. Consequently their densities
are equal by \noderef{PairDensity}, including empty sets.
For subsets $A\subseteq e(L),B\subseteq e(R)$, take
$P=\{x\in L:e(x)\in A\}$ and $Q=\{y\in R:e(y)\in B\}$.
Their images are exactly $A,B$, and their sizes are therefore the
same. The strict size thresholds in \noderef{LowerRegularPair}
are unchanged, so its density lower bound transfers.
For each $x\in L$, the map $e$ also bijects its neighbors in $R$
with the neighbors of $e(x)$ in $e(R)$. For each $y\in R$ it
bijects the neighbors in $L$ in the other orientation. Transfer both
degree lower bounds in \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}, using
$|e(L)|=|L|$ and $|e(R)|=|R|$. Together with the transferred
lower regularity these are exactly the required three clauses.
Conversely, apply the target's subset bounds to $e(P),e(Q)$ for
each source test $P,Q$, and its degree bounds to $e(x),e(y)$.
The same bijections and cardinality identities give all source clauses.
\end{proof}
LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Transport of a lower super-regular pair]
Let $e:V\to W$ be injective, let $G,H$ be simple graphs, and let
$L,R\subseteq V$ be finite. Suppose that, for $x\in L,y\in R$,
$H(e(x),e(y))$ holds if and only if $G(x,y)$ holds.
Then $(L,R)$ is lower $(\epsilon,d)$-super-regular in $G$ if and only if
$(e(L),e(R))$ is lower $(\epsilon,d)$-super-regular in $H$.
The parameters may be extended nonnegative reals.
\end{lemma}
LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding.title: LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding

intro Delta r n hDelta VH VG _ _ _ H G R _ _ B color _htwoSizes htwo hR
  classical
  let P := Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)
  let E : P ≃ Fin (r * Delta ^ 2) := finProdFinEquiv
  let part : VH → P := fun x => (B.sourceCluster x, color x)
  let X (p : P) := {x : VH // part x = p}
  have hleft (p q : P) (x : X p) (y z : X q)
      (hxy : H.Adj x.val y.val) (hxz : H.Adj x.val z.val) : y = z := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    by_contra hne
    have hp : part y.val = part z.val := y.property.trans z.property.symm
    exact (htwo (congrArg Prod.fst hp) (congrArg Prod.snd hp) hne).2
      ⟨x.val, H.symm hxy, H.symm hxz⟩
  have hright (p q : P) (x y : X p) (z : X q)
      (hxz : H.Adj x.val z.val) (hyz : H.Adj y.val z.val) : x = y := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    by_contra hne
    have hp : part x.val = part y.val := x.property.trans y.property.symm
    exact (htwo (congrArg Prod.fst hp) (congrArg Prod.snd hp) hne).2
      ⟨z.val, hxz, hyz⟩

      (∀ x y, H.Adj x.val y.val → C x y) ∧
      ((∃ τ : X p ↪ X q, ∀ x y, C x y ↔ y = τ x) ∨
       (∃ τ : X q ↪ X p, ∀ x y, C x y ↔ x = τ y)) := by
    by_cases hcard : Fintype.card (X p) ≤ Fintype.card (X q)
    · obtain ⟨τ, hτ⟩ := FinitePartialMatchingCompletion
        (fun x : X p => fun y : X q => H.Adj x.val y.val)
        (hleft p q) (hright p q) hcard
      exact ⟨fun x y => y = τ x, fun x y h => (hτ x y h).symm,
        Or.inl ⟨τ, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩⟩
    · obtain ⟨τ, hτ⟩ := FinitePartialMatchingCompletion
        (fun y : X q => fun x : X p => H.Adj x.val y.val)
        (fun y x z h₁ h₂ => hright p q x z y h₁ h₂)
        (fun y z x h₁ h₂ => hleft p q x y z h₁ h₂)
        (Nat.le_of_lt (Nat.lt_of_not_ge hcard))
      exact ⟨fun x y => x = τ y, fun x y h => (hτ y x h).symm,
        Or.inr ⟨τ, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩⟩
  choose C hCold hC using hcomplete
  -- Only the completion indexed by the increasing ordered pair is used.
  let H' : SimpleGraph VH :=
    { Adj := fun x y => R.Adj (B.sourceCluster x) (B.sourceCluster y) ∧
        ((E (part x) < E (part y) ∧
          C (part x) (part y) ⟨x, rfl⟩ ⟨y, rfl⟩) ∨
         (E (part y) < E (part x) ∧
          C (part y) (part x) ⟨y, rfl⟩ ⟨x, rfl⟩))
      symm := by
        intro x y h
        exact ⟨R.symm h.1, h.2.symm⟩
      loopless := by
        constructor
        intro x h
        exact R.loopless.irrefl _ h.1 }
  let R' : SimpleGraph P :=
    { Adj := fun p q => R.Adj p.1 q.1
      symm := fun _ _ h => R.symm h
      loopless := ⟨fun _ h => R.loopless.irrefl _ h⟩ }
  have hle : H ≤ H' := by
    intro x y hxy
    have hr := B.reduced_support hxy
    have hne : E (part x) ≠ E (part y) := by
      intro h
      have hp := E.injective h
      exact R.ne_of_adj hr (congrArg Prod.fst hp)
    refine ⟨hr, ?_⟩
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with h | h
    · exact Or.inl ⟨h, hCold _ _ _ _ hxy⟩
    · exact Or.inr ⟨h, hCold _ _ _ _ (H.symm hxy)⟩
  have hAdj (p q : P) (hr : R'.Adj p q) (hlt : E p < E q)
      (x : X p) (y : X q) : H'.Adj x.val y.val ↔ C p q x y := by
    rcases x with ⟨x, hx⟩
    rcases y with ⟨y, hy⟩
    subst p
    subst q
    change (R.Adj (B.sourceCluster x) (B.sourceCluster y) ∧
      ((E (part x) < E (part y) ∧ _) ∨ (E (part y) < E (part x) ∧ _))) ↔ _
    simp only [show R.Adj (B.sourceCluster x) (B.sourceCluster y) from hr,
      hlt, not_lt_of_ge (le_of_lt hlt), true_and, false_and, or_false]
  obtain ⟨e⟩ : Nonempty (∀ i, {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i} ↪
      {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i}) := by
    exact ⟨fun i => (Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le (B.capacity i)).some⟩
  let j₀ : Fin (Delta ^ 2) := ⟨0, by positivity⟩
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := FiberwiseCapacityRefinement
    B.sourceCluster B.hostCluster color j₀ e
  let B' : BlowUpInstance (r * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G
      (R'.comap E.symm) :=
    { sourceCluster := fun x => E (part x)
      hostCluster := fun v => E (B.hostCluster v, d v)
      source_independent := by
        intro i x hx y hy _ hxy
        have hp : part x = part y := E.injective (hx.trans hy.symm)
        exact R.ne_of_adj hxy.1 (congrArg Prod.fst hp)
      capacity := by
        intro t
        let es : {x : VH // E (part x) = t} ≃
            {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = (E.symm t).1 ∧
              color x = (E.symm t).2} :=
          Equiv.subtypeEquivRight (fun _ =>
            E.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply.trans Prod.ext_iff)
        let ev : {v : VG // E (B.hostCluster v, d v) = t} ≃
            {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = (E.symm t).1 ∧
              d v = (E.symm t).2} :=
          Equiv.subtypeEquivRight (fun _ =>
            E.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply.trans Prod.ext_iff)
        exact (Fintype.card_congr es).le.trans
          ((hd (E.symm t).1 (E.symm t).2).trans (Fintype.card_congr ev).symm.le)
      reduced_support := by
        intro x y hxy
        change R'.Adj (E.symm (E (part x))) (E.symm (E (part y)))
        simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hxy.1 }
  let ef (p : P) : X p ≃ {x : VH // B'.sourceCluster x = E p} :=
    Equiv.subtypeEquivRight (fun x => by
      change part x = p ↔ E (part x) = E p
      exact ⟨congrArg E, fun h => E.injective h⟩)
  have hsat (p q : P) (hr : R'.Adj p q) (hlt : E p < E q) :
      SaturatingSourcePair B' (E p) (E q) := by
    rcases hC p q with ⟨τ, hτ⟩ | ⟨τ, hτ⟩
    · refine Or.inl ⟨((ef p).symm.toEmbedding.trans τ).trans (ef q).toEmbedding, ?_⟩
      intro x y
      change H'.Adj x.val y.val ↔ y = (ef q) (τ ((ef p).symm x))
      exact ((hAdj p q hr hlt ((ef p).symm x) ((ef q).symm y)).trans
        (hτ _ _)).trans (ef q).symm.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply
    · refine Or.inr ⟨((ef q).symm.toEmbedding.trans τ).trans (ef p).toEmbedding, ?_⟩
      intro x y
      change H'.Adj x.val y.val ↔ x = (ef p) (τ ((ef q).symm y))
      exact ((hAdj p q hr hlt ((ef p).symm x) ((ef q).symm y)).trans
        (hτ _ _)).trans (ef p).symm.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply
  have hsatSymm (i j : Fin (r * Delta ^ 2))
      (h : SaturatingSourcePair B' i j) : SaturatingSourcePair B' j i := by
    rcases h with ⟨τ, hτ⟩ | ⟨τ, hτ⟩
    · exact Or.inr ⟨τ, fun x y => (H'.adj_comm _ _).trans (hτ y x)⟩
    · exact Or.inl ⟨τ, fun x y => (H'.adj_comm _ _).trans (hτ y x)⟩
  have hdegree : R'.maxDegree ≤ Delta ^ 3 := by
    apply R'.maxDegree_le_of_forall_degree_le
    intro p
    let en : R'.neighborSet p ≃ R.neighborSet p.1 × Fin (Delta ^ 2) :=
      { toFun := fun q => (⟨q.val.1, q.property⟩, q.val.2)
        invFun := fun q => ⟨(q.1.val, q.2), q.1.property⟩
        left_inv := fun _ => rfl
        right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
    calc
      R'.degree p = Fintype.card (R'.neighborSet p) :=
        (R'.card_neighborSet_eq_degree p).symm
      _ = Fintype.card (R.neighborSet p.1 × Fin (Delta ^ 2)) := Fintype.card_congr en
      _ = R.degree p.1 * Delta ^ 2 := by
        rw [Fintype.card_prod, R.card_neighborSet_eq_degree, Fintype.card_fin]
      _ ≤ Delta * Delta ^ 2 :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ ((R.degree_le_maxDegree p.1).trans hR)
      _ = Delta ^ 3 := by rw [pow_succ]; exact Nat.mul_comm _ _
  refine ⟨H', R', inferInstance, inferInstance, B', hle, ?_, ?_, hdegree, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    exact E.symm_apply_apply (part x)
  · intro p q
    rfl
  · intro p q hr
    by_cases hlt : E p < E q
    · exact hsat p q hr hlt
    · have hne : E p ≠ E q := fun h => R'.ne_of_adj hr (E.injective h)
      exact hsatSymm _ _ (hsat q p (R'.symm hr) (lt_of_le_of_ne (le_of_not_gt hlt) hne.symm))
MatchingCompletionExtension.lean_statement:
theorem MatchingCompletionExtension :
    ∀ (Delta r n : ℕ), 1 ≤ Delta →
      ∀ {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH]
        {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
        [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel R.Adj]
        (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R)
        (color : VH → Fin (Delta ^ 2)),
        (∀ i j,
          let s := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH =>
            B.sourceCluster x = i ∧ color x = j
          s.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ s.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1) →
        (∀ {x y}, B.sourceCluster x = B.sourceCluster y → color x = color y →
          x ≠ y → ¬ H.Adj x y ∧ ¬ ∃ z, H.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj y z) →
        R.maxDegree ≤ Delta →
        ∃ (H' : SimpleGraph VH) (R' : SimpleGraph (Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)))
          (_ : DecidableRel H'.Adj) (_ : DecidableRel R'.Adj)
          (B' : BlowUpInstance (r * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G
            (R'.comap finProdFinEquiv.symm)),
          H ≤ H' ∧
          (∀ x, finProdFinEquiv.symm (B'.sourceCluster x) =
            (B.sourceCluster x, color x)) ∧
          (∀ p q, R'.Adj p q ↔ R.Adj p.1 q.1) ∧
          R'.maxDegree ≤ Delta ^ 3 ∧
          ∀ p q, R'.Adj p q →
            SaturatingSourcePair B'
              (finProdFinEquiv p)
              (finProdFinEquiv q) := by
MatchingCompletionExtension.name: MatchingCompletionExtension
MatchingCompletionExtension.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $k=\Delta^2$, and write $a_H$ and $a_G$ for the source and host
cluster maps of $B$ from \noderef{BlowUpInstance}.  Thus
$X_i=a_H^{-1}(i)$ and $V_i=a_G^{-1}(i)$, and these fibers partition
their respective vertex sets, with $|X_i|\leq|V_i|$ for every $i$.
Let $P=[r]\times[k]$, and put $X_p=X_{i,j}$ for $p=(i,j)$.
Every source vertex belongs to the unique part indexed by
$(a_H(x),c(x))$.

We first construct the refined host map, independently of adding source
edges.  For each $i$, choose an injection $e_i:X_i\to V_i$ using the
capacity inequality.  Explicitly, enumerate the two finite sets as
$x_1,\ldots,x_a$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_b$, where $a\leq b$, and send
$x_\ell$ to $v_\ell$ for $1\leq\ell\leq a$.  For $a=0$ this is the
empty injection.  There are only finitely many indices, so make these
choices for all $i$.  Since $1\leq\Delta$, we have $k\geq1$; fix a
distinguished color $j_0\in[k]$ (the element $0$ of $\mathrm{Fin}(k)$
in Lean).

Apply \noderef{FiberwiseCapacityRefinement} to the total maps
$a_H,a_G,c$, the injections $e_i$, and the default color $j_0$.
It gives a total host coloring $d$ such that, on defining
\[
 V_{i,j}=\{v:a_G(v)=i,\ d(v)=j\},
\]
we have $|X_{i,j}|\leq|V_{i,j}|$ for every pair $(i,j)$.
These sets are pairwise disjoint: membership in two of them forces both
indices to agree, since $a_G$ and $d$ are functions.  Every $v\in V_i$
belongs to $V_{i,d(v)}$, so they partition $V_i$; over all $i$ they
partition the whole host vertex set.  The cited capacity-refinement
statement does not presume $|X_i|=|V_i|$, and applies to empty fibers.
If $V_i$ is empty, original capacity forces $X_i$ to be empty as well.

Define $R'$ on $P$ by $R'.\mathrm{Adj}((i,j),(i',j'))$ if and only if
$R.\mathrm{Adj}(i,i')$.  Symmetry follows from symmetry of $R$, and a
loop would give a loop of $R$, so this is a simple graph.  For an edge
$pq$ of $R'$, the original parts of $p$ and $q$ are distinct, so $X_p$
and $X_q$ are disjoint.  The graph $H[X_p,X_q]$ is a matching: if
$x_1,x_2\in X_p$ were distinct and adjacent to the same $y\in X_q$,
they would have the same original cluster and color and would share
the neighbor $y$, contradicting the stated hypothesis.  Applying that
hypothesis to two distinct vertices of $X_q$ excludes a common neighbor
on the $X_p$ side.  For any $p,q$ with $R'.\mathrm{Adj}(p,q)$ false,
an $H$-edge between their parts would contradict the reduced-support
field of \noderef{BlowUpInstance}; thus no such edge exists.

Order $P$ by the images of its elements under
$E=\texttt{finProdFinEquiv}:P\simeq\mathrm{Fin}(rk)$.
Represent each unordered edge uniquely as $(p,q)$ with $E(p)<E(q)$.
For this representative, choose $S=X_p,T=X_q$ if $|X_p|\leq|X_q|$;
otherwise choose $S=X_q,T=X_p$.  In particular, a tie is always
resolved in favor of $X_p$.  Let $M\subseteq S\times T$ be the
original adjacency relation.  The two uniqueness conditions just
proved, together with $|S|\leq|T|$, are exactly the hypotheses of
\noderef{FinitePartialMatchingCompletion}.  Its conclusion gives an
injection $\tau:S\to T$ retaining every pair of $M$.
Use precisely the graph of $\tau$ as the completed bipartite relation
$C_{p,q}$.  It is a matching saturating $S$: every $s$ has partner
$\tau(s)$, uniqueness on $S$ is functional uniqueness, and uniqueness
on $T$ is injectivity of $\tau$.  Every original edge is retained by
the cited conclusion.  Empty parts are permitted by that statement.
The argument works for arbitrary finite part sizes, hence in particular
for the given floor and floor-plus-one sizes, including zero.

Choose this completion once for each unordered edge of $R'$, and let
$H'$ have all edges of $H$ together with all the added edges.
More explicitly, vertices $x,y$, in parts $p,q$ respectively, are
adjacent precisely when $R'.\mathrm{Adj}(p,q)$ and either
$E(p)<E(q)$ with $(x,y)\in C_{p,q}$, or $E(q)<E(p)$ with
$(y,x)\in C_{q,p}$.
This defines a simple graph: the added pairs have endpoints in
disjoint parts and are treated as unordered pairs, so adjacency is
symmetric and there are no loops.  The refined source parts partition
the source vertex set.  Thus the unordered pair of parts containing
the endpoints of an edge is unique.  Completions for different
unordered pairs cannot add an edge between the parts of another pair.
It follows that $H'[X_p,X_q]$ is exactly the chosen completed matching
for each edge $pq$ of $R'$, and is empty for every nonedge.  Also
$H\leq H'$ by its definition.  The adjacency relations of $R'$ and
$H'$ are decidable: the former uses the given decidable adjacency of
$R$, and the latter is membership in a finite union of the given old
edges and the finite lists of new edges.  Classical finite choices
above require no additional hypothesis on the host vertex type.

To construct the precise blow-up instance in the conclusion, let
\[
 E:\mathrm{Fin}(r)\times\mathrm{Fin}(k)\ \simeq
   \mathrm{Fin}(rk)
\]
be the bijection \texttt{finProdFinEquiv}.  Use the reduced graph
$\widetilde R=R'.\mathrm{comap}(E^{-1})$, whose adjacency at $u,w$ is
$R'.\mathrm{Adj}(E^{-1}(u),E^{-1}(w))$, and define the two cluster maps by
\[
 a'_H(x)=E(a_H(x),c(x)),\qquad
 a'_G(v)=E(a_G(v),d(v)).
\]
Both maps are total.  Since $E$ is bijective, the source fiber at
$E(i,j)$ is exactly $X_{i,j}$ and the host fiber there is exactly
$V_{i,j}$.  We now verify every field of \noderef{BlowUpInstance}.
First, each source fiber is independent in $H'$: it is a subset of
the original independent $X_i$, hence has no old $H$-edge, and every
added edge joins parts over distinct original clusters, hence cannot
have both endpoints in that fiber.  Second, its capacity inequality
is the injection inequality already proved.  This checks every index
of $\mathrm{Fin}(rk)$ because it is $E(i,j)$ for a unique pair.
Third, if $xy$ is an old edge, original reduced support gives
$R.\mathrm{Adj}(a_H(x),a_H(y))$, which gives
$R'.\mathrm{Adj}((a_H(x),c(x)),(a_H(y),c(y)))$.  If it is an added
edge, its pair of source parts was an edge of $R'$ by construction.
In either case this is exactly
$\widetilde R.\mathrm{Adj}(a'_H(x),a'_H(y))$, by the inverse identities
for $E$.  This verifies reduced support.  These are all the fields;
the host graph remains $G$, and \noderef{BlowUpInstance} requires no
further edge condition on $G$.  Denote the resulting instance by $B'$.
The inverse identity also gives
$E^{-1}(B'.\mathrm{sourceCluster}(x))=(a_H(x),c(x))$, as required.
For each edge $pq$ of $R'$, identifying the fibers at $E(p),E(q)$
with $X_p,X_q$ transports the completed injection $\tau$ to those
fibers.  The exact adjacency description gives the first disjunct
of \noderef{SaturatingSourcePair} if $X_p$ was chosen as $S$, and the
second disjunct if $X_q$ was chosen as $S$.

Finally, the neighbors of $(i,j)$ in $R'$ are precisely the pairs
$(i',j')$ with $i'\in N_R(i)$ and arbitrary $j'\in[k]$.  The bijection
with $N_R(i)\times[k]$ gives
\[
 d_{R'}(i,j)=d_R(i)k\leq\Delta k=\Delta^3,
\]
where $d_R(i)\leq\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$.  Taking the maximum over the
finite vertex set proves $\Delta(R')\leq\Delta^3$.
If $r=0$, the original cluster maps have empty codomain, so both
source and host vertex sets are empty.  The constructions of the
injections and both refined maps above are then empty constructions;
$R'$ is the graph on the empty product index set and has maximum
degree zero, while all field and matching assertions are vacuous.
Thus this case also satisfies the conclusion.  The degree estimate
corrects the symbol $R$ in line 396 of the manuscript.
\end{proof}
MatchingCompletionExtension.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous matching completion]
Let $\Delta,r,n$ be nonnegative integers with $1\leq\Delta$, and let
$B=(H,G,R,(X_i)_{i\in[r]},(V_i)_{i\in[r]})$ be a finite blow-up
instance in the sense of \noderef{BlowUpInstance}.  Let
$c\colon V(H)\to[\Delta^2]$ be a coloring of the source vertices.  Suppose that every fiber
\[
 X_{i,j}=\{x\in X_i:c(x)=j\}
\]
has cardinality $\lfloor n/\Delta^2\rfloor$ or $\lfloor n/\Delta^2\rfloor+1$, and that whenever distinct vertices $x,y$ lie in the same original source cluster and satisfy $c(x)=c(y)$, they are nonadjacent in $H$ and have no common neighbor in $H$.  If $\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$, then there are graphs $H'\supseteq H$ and $R'$ on $[r]\times[\Delta^2]$ and a refined blow-up instance with source clusters $X_{i,j}$ such that
\[
 (i,j)(i',j')\in E(R')\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad ii'\in E(R),
\]
$\Delta(R')\leq\Delta^3$, and $H'[X_{i,j},X_{i',j'}]$ is a saturating matching in the sense of \noderef{SaturatingSourcePair} for every edge of $R'$.  No edge is added between a pair corresponding to a nonedge of $R'$.
\end{lemma}
MatchingCompletionExtension.title: MatchingCompletionExtension

MatchingConcentrationCorrection.lean_proof:
Real.log ((d + ε + 3 * Real.sqrt ε) / (d - 2 * ε)) -
    3 * Real.sqrt ε * Real.log (min (d + ε + 3 * Real.sqrt ε) 1)
MatchingConcentrationCorrection.lean_statement: noncomputable def MatchingConcentrationCorrection (d ε : ℝ) : ℝ :=
MatchingConcentrationCorrection.name: MatchingConcentrationCorrection
MatchingConcentrationCorrection.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Logarithmic matching-count correction]
For real $d,\varepsilon$ define
\[
 L(d,\varepsilon)=\log{d+\varepsilon+3\sqrt\varepsilon\over d-2\varepsilon}
 -3\sqrt\varepsilon\log\min(d+\varepsilon+3\sqrt\varepsilon,1).
\]
The square root and logarithm are the total real functions: square root
of a negative number is zero, $\log0=0$, and the logarithm of a negative
number is the logarithm of its absolute value; division by zero is zero.
In applications $d>2\varepsilon>0$, so every
logarithm argument in this formula is positive. Thus $e^{L(d,\varepsilon)}$
is the correction factor for the loss from small rectangles and the
ratio of upper and lower matching-count densities.
\end{definition}
MatchingConcentrationCorrection.title: MatchingConcentrationCorrection

MatchingConcentrationCorrectionAbsorptio.lean_proof:
have hD : ContinuousAt (fun e : ℝ => d + e + 3 * Real.sqrt e) 0 := by fun_prop
  have hden : ContinuousAt (fun e : ℝ => d - 2 * e) 0 := by fun_prop
  have hquot := hD.div hden (by simpa using hd.ne')
  have hlog := hquot.log (by simp [hd.ne'])
  have hmin := hD.min (continuousAt_const (y := (1 : ℝ)))
  have hminlog := hmin.log (by simpa [min_eq_left hd1] using hd.ne')
  have hcont : ContinuousAt (MatchingConcentrationCorrection d) 0 :=
    hlog.sub (((continuousAt_const (y := (3 : ℝ))).mul
      Real.continuous_sqrt.continuousAt).mul hminlog)
  have hzero : MatchingConcentrationCorrection d 0 = 0 := by
    simp [MatchingConcentrationCorrection, hd.ne']
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · simpa only [hzero] using hcont.continuousWithinAt.tendsto
  · intro γ hγ
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hnear⟩ := Metric.continuousAt_iff.mp hcont γ hγ
    let ε₀ := min (r / 2) (min (1 / 32) (d / 8))
    have hε₀ : 0 < ε₀ := by
      dsimp [ε₀]
      exact lt_min (by positivity) (lt_min (by norm_num) (by positivity))
    have hεr : ε₀ ≤ r / 2 := min_le_left _ _
    have hεsmall : ε₀ ≤ 1 / 32 := le_trans (min_le_right _ _) (min_le_left _ _)
    have hεd : ε₀ ≤ d / 8 := le_trans (min_le_right _ _) (min_le_right _ _)
    obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := exists_nat_gt (2 * Real.log 2 / γ)
    refine ⟨ε₀, hε₀, by linarith, by linarith, N + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
    intro ε hε hεle
    have hL : MatchingConcentrationCorrection d ε ≤ γ := by
      have hdist : dist ε 0 < r := by
        rw [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero, abs_of_pos hε]
        linarith
      have hbound := hnear hdist
      rw [hzero, Real.dist_eq, sub_zero] at hbound
      exact le_trans (le_abs_self _) hbound.le
    refine ⟨hL, ?_⟩
    intro n hn
    have hNn : (N : ℝ) ≤ n := by
      exact_mod_cast le_trans (Nat.le_succ N) hn
    have hlarge : Real.log 2 ≤ γ * (n : ℝ) / 2 := by
      have hfrac := lt_of_lt_of_le hN hNn
      have hmul := (div_lt_iff₀ hγ).mp hfrac
      linarith
    have htwo : (2 : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (γ * (n : ℝ) / 2) := by
      calc
        (2 : ℝ) = Real.exp (Real.log 2) := (Real.exp_log (by norm_num)).symm
        _ ≤ _ := Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hlarge
    calc
      _ ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-(γ * (n : ℝ))) := by
        apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (by norm_num)
        apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
        nlinarith [show (0 : ℝ) ≤ n from Nat.cast_nonneg n]
      _ ≤ Real.exp (γ * (n : ℝ) / 2) * Real.exp (-(γ * (n : ℝ))) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right htwo (Real.exp_pos _).le
      _ = Real.exp (-γ / 2) ^ n := by
        rw [← Real.exp_add, ← Real.exp_nat_mul]
        congr 1
        ring
