    apply (mul_lt_mul_iff_of_pos_left (sq_pos_of_pos hηpos)).mp
    calc
      _ ≤ _ := hcenterScaled
      _ < η.toReal ^ 5 * (m : ℝ) * (W'.card : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
        apply mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right _ (sq_pos_of_pos hqpos)
        exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right
          (by linarith only [hhierR, hδpos] : 23 * δ.toReal < η.toReal ^ 5) hmpos
      _ = _ := by ring
  have hcs : (∑ u ∈ U', (d u - p.toReal * W'.card)) ^ 2 ≤
      (U'.card : ℝ) * (∑ u ∈ U, (d u - p.toReal * W'.card) ^ 2) := by
    have hc := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq U'
      (fun u => d u - p.toReal * W'.card) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
    simp only [mul_one, one_pow, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul] at hc
    have hs : (∑ u ∈ U', (d u - p.toReal * W'.card) ^ 2) ≤
        ∑ u ∈ U, (d u - p.toReal * W'.card) ^ 2 :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hU' (fun _ _ _ => sq_nonneg _)
    exact hc.trans (by simpa [mul_comm] using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hs hU'pos.le)
  have hsumsq : (∑ u ∈ U', (d u - p.toReal * W'.card)) ^ 2 <
      (η.toReal * (U'.card : ℝ) * W'.card) ^ 2 := by
    calc
      _ ≤ _ := hcs
      _ < (U'.card : ℝ) * (η.toReal ^ 3 * (m : ℝ) * (W'.card : ℝ) ^ 2) :=
        mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hcenterStrict hU'pos
      _ < (η.toReal * (U'.card : ℝ) * W'.card) ^ 2 := by
        have := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hUlargeR
          (show 0 < η.toReal ^ 2 * (U'.card : ℝ) * (W'.card : ℝ) ^ 2 by positivity)
        convert this using 1 <;> ring
  have hsumbound : |∑ u ∈ U', (d u - p.toReal * W'.card)| <
      η.toReal * (U'.card : ℝ) * W'.card := by
    exact (sq_lt_sq₀ (abs_nonneg _) (by positivity)).mp (by simpa using hsumsq)
  have hsumId : (∑ u ∈ U', (d u - p.toReal * W'.card)) =
      (∑ u ∈ U', d u) - (U'.card : ℝ) * p.toReal * W'.card := by
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
    ring
  have hedgeCount : (((U' ×ˢ W').filter fun z => G.Adj z.1 z.2).card : ℝ) =
      ∑ u ∈ U', d u := by
    dsimp only [d]
    exact_mod_cast FilteredProductRowCount U' W' G.Adj
  have hdensityR : (PairDensity G U' W').toReal =
      (∑ u ∈ U', d u) / ((U'.card : ℝ) * W'.card) := by
    simp only [PairDensity, ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_mul,
      ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
    exact congrArg (fun x : ℝ => x / ((U'.card : ℝ) * W'.card)) hedgeCount
  have hlowerR : p.toReal - η.toReal ≤ (PairDensity G U' W').toReal := by
    rw [hdensityR]
    apply (le_div_iff₀ (mul_pos hU'pos hqpos)).mpr
    have := (abs_lt.mp hsumbound).1
    rw [hsumId] at this
    nlinarith only [this]
  have hupperR : (PairDensity G U' W').toReal ≤ p.toReal + η.toReal := by
    rw [hdensityR]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ (mul_pos hU'pos hqpos)).mpr
    have := (abs_lt.mp hsumbound).2
    rw [hsumId] at this
    nlinarith only [this]
  have hUne : (U'.card : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast (show U'.card ≠ 0 by exact_mod_cast hU'pos.ne')
  have hWne : (W'.card : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast (show W'.card ≠ 0 by exact_mod_cast hqpos.ne')
  have hdensityfin : PairDensity G U' W' ≠ ⊤ := by
    exact ENNReal.div_ne_top (by simp) (mul_ne_zero hUne hWne)
  constructor
  · by_cases hηp : η ≤ p
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hdensityfin).mp
      simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le hηp hpfin] using hlowerR
    · simpa only [tsub_eq_zero_of_le (le_of_not_ge hηp)] using
        (zero_le (PairDensity G U' W'))
  · apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal hdensityfin (by finiteness)).mp
    simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_add hpfin hηfin] using hupperR
NearEqualDegreeCodegreeRegularityCriteri.lean_statement:
theorem NearEqualDegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      (U W : Finset V) (m : ℕ) (δ p η : ENNReal),
      U.card = m → (W.card + 1 = m ∨ W.card = m ∨ W.card = m + 1) →
      Disjoint U W → η ≤ 1 → δ ≤ p → p ≤ 1 →
      2 ≤ m → 1 ≤ δ * m → 32 * δ ≤ η ^ 5 →
      (((W ×ˢ W).filter fun z =>
          ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * m ∨
          ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.2).card : ENNReal) < (p - δ) * m ∨
          (p + δ) ^ 2 * m <
            ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1 ∧ G.Adj u z.2).card : ENNReal)).card : ENNReal)
        ≤ 6 * δ * (W.card : ENNReal) ^ 2 →
      RegularPair G U W η p := by
NearEqualDegreeCodegreeRegularityCriteri.name: NearEqualDegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion
NearEqualDegreeCodegreeRegularityCriteri.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
First, $\eta>0$: otherwise $32\delta\leq\eta^5=0$ would give
$\delta=0$, contrary to $1\leq\delta m$.  Write $k=|W|$ and let
$U'\subseteq U$ and $W'\subseteq W$ satisfy $|U'|>\eta m$ and
$|W'|>\eta k$.  Put $q=|W'|$.  The assumptions $m\geq2$ and
$k\in\{m-1,m,m+1\}$ imply $k\geq1$, so $q>\eta k>0$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-equal-ratio}
 t\coloneqq \frac{k}{q}<\frac1\eta.
\end{equation}

Let $L\subseteq W$ be the set of vertices having fewer than
$(p-\delta)m$ neighbors in $U$.  For every $w\in L$ and every $z\in W$,
the ordered pair $(w,z)$ is bad by the endpoint condition.  These
$|L|k$ ordered pairs are distinct, whence
\[
 |L|k\leq 6\delta k^2
 \quad\text{and therefore}\quad |L|\leq6\delta k.
\]
Every vertex in $W'\setminus L$ has at least $(p-\delta)m$ neighbors in
$U$.  Thus, writing $S_1=e(U,W')$, we obtain the explicit first-moment
bound
\begin{align*}
 S_1
 &=\sum_{w\in W'}|N_G(w)\cap U|\\
 &\geq |W'\setminus L|(p-\delta)m\\
 &\geq (q-6\delta k)(p-\delta)m.
\end{align*}
The last inequality remains valid when $q-6\delta k<0$, since its
right-hand side is then nonpositive while $S_1\geq0$.

For the second moment put $d_u=|N_G(u)\cap W'|$.  Double-counting
ordered length-two paths with middle vertex in $U$ gives
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}d_u^2
 =\sum_{(w,w')\in W'^2}|N_G(w)\cap N_G(w')\cap U|.
\]
There are at most $6\delta k^2$ bad ordered pairs in the restricted set
$W'^2$.  Every good summand is at most $(p+\delta)^2m$, while every bad
summand is at most $m$.  Consequently, with
$S_2=\sum_{u\in U}d_u^2$,
\[
 S_2\leq (p+\delta)^2mq^2+6\delta k^2m
 =mq^2\bigl((p+\delta)^2+6\delta t^2\bigr).
\]
Since $p\geq0$, the lower bound on $S_1$ may be substituted into the
negative first-moment term in the centered second moment.  Expanding it
line by line and using $k=tq$ yields
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2
 &=S_2-2pqS_1+mp^2q^2\\
 &\leq mq^2\bigl((p+\delta)^2+6\delta t^2
       -2p(p-\delta)(1-6\delta t)+p^2\bigr)\\
 &=mq^2\bigl(4p\delta+\delta^2
       +12p\delta(p-\delta)t+6\delta t^2\bigr).
\end{align*}
Here $0\leq\delta\leq p\leq1$, so
$4p\delta+\delta^2\leq5\delta$ and
$12p\delta(p-\delta)t\leq12\delta t$.  By
\eqref{eq:near-equal-ratio} and $0<\eta\leq1$, it follows that
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2
 &<\delta mq^2\left(5+\frac{12}{\eta}
                         +\frac6{\eta^2}\right)\\
 &\leq \frac{23\delta}{\eta^2}mq^2
 \leq \frac{23}{32}\eta^3mq^2
 <\eta^3mq^2,
\end{align*}
where the penultimate inequality is exactly $32\delta\leq\eta^5$.

Suppose now that the density between $U'$ and $W'$ differed from $p$
by more than $\eta$.  Since
$e(U',W')=\sum_{u\in U'}d_u$, this says
\[
 \left|\sum_{u\in U'}(d_u-pq)\right|>\eta|U'|q.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz, followed by $|U'|>\eta m$, then gives
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2
 \geq\sum_{u\in U'}(d_u-pq)^2
 \geq\frac{\left(\sum_{u\in U'}(d_u-pq)\right)^2}{|U'|}
 >\eta^2|U'|q^2
 >\eta^3mq^2.
\]
This contradicts the preceding upper bound.  Hence every admissible
$(U',W')$ has density in $[p-\eta,p+\eta]$, which is precisely
\noderef{RegularPair}.
\end{proof}

  intro d₁₂ d₁₃ d₂₃ hd₁₂ hd₁₂1 hd₁₃ hd₁₃1 hd₂₃ hd₂₃1

  refine ⟨min e (min θD θC), lt_min he (lt_min hθD hθC), ?_⟩

  have hεD : ε ≤ θD := hεsmall.trans ((min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_left _ _))

  obtain ⟨hεδ, hεη, hεd, hεx, hεy, hS, hT, hS₂, hT₂, hlo, hhi, hpoly⟩ :=

  obtain ⟨cC, hcC, NC, hcommon⟩ := hcommon ε hε hεC

  have hc : c < 1 := max_lt hcD hcC
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀, habsorb⟩ := FourGraphsPolynomialLossAbsorption c hc

  intro a ha haa
  obtain ⟨NA, hNA, hAbs⟩ := habsorb a ha haa
  have hp : d₁₃ * d₂₃ ≤ 1 := by simpa using mul_le_mul' hd₁₃1 hd₂₃1

NearEqualFourGraphs.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $q=d_{13}d_{23}$ and first choose $0<\varepsilon'_0\leq1$.
Fix $0<\varepsilon'\leq\varepsilon'_0$, and put $k=|W_3|$.
Use \noderef{NearEqualFourGraphsParameters} with $\eta=\varepsilon'$
to obtain positive finite $\delta,\zeta,e$, with
$\delta\leq\min(q,\varepsilon')$, $32\delta\leq(\varepsilon')^5$,
and all the degree, set-size, and polynomial windows stated there for
every $0\leq\varepsilon\leq e$.
Invoke \noderef{UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration}, always with matching
density $d_{12}$ and additive error $\zeta$, first with lower set-density
bounds $d_{13}/2,d_{23}/2$, and then with lower bounds
$(d_{13}/2)^2,(d_{23}/2)^2$.  Let $\theta_{\rm deg}>0$ and
$\theta_{\rm cod}>0$ be the two admissible input-error thresholds supplied
by that node.

Choose $\varepsilon_0=\min(e,\theta_{\rm deg},\theta_{\rm cod})>0$.
For every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$, the parameter lemma gives
\[
 2\varepsilon<\min(d_{12},d_{13},d_{23}),\qquad
 \varepsilon\leq\min(\delta,\varepsilon'),
\]
as well as $d_{ij}/2\leq d_{ij}-\varepsilon$ and
$(d_{ij}/2)^2\leq(d_{ij}-2\varepsilon)^2$ for $ij=13,23$.
Its two sharp degree inequalities are
\[
 q-\delta\leq(d_{13}-\varepsilon)(d_{23}-\varepsilon)-\zeta,
 \qquad
 (d_{13}+\varepsilon)(d_{23}+\varepsilon)+\zeta\leq q+\delta.
\]
Its polynomial window is
\[
 (d_{13}+2\varepsilon)^2(d_{23}+2\varepsilon)^2+\zeta
 \leq(q+\delta)^2.
\tag{1}
\]

Fix any $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$.  The two concentration
invocations now apply.  Take the larger of their size thresholds and the
larger of their exponential constants, calling the latter $c<1$; increasing
a constant below $1$ only weakens the asserted upper bound.  Thus one $c$
and one threshold work for every vertex-neighborhood and good-codegree set
used below.  Denote this common size threshold by $N_*$.  The relation
$|k-m|\leq1$ gives explicitly
\[
 m-1\leq k\leq m+1,
 \qquad 1-m^{-1}\leq k/m\leq1+m^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
We will use the upper inequality in the union bounds.  The degree windows
below retain their actual opposite-part cardinalities, and the near-equal
regularity criterion itself accepts $k\in\{m-1,m,m+1\}$, so no unrecorded
replacement of $k$ by $m$ is needed.  The perfect-matching witness in the
statement makes the uniform distribution well-defined.

The adjacency and cardinality identifications on the copied graph
are supplied by \noderef{MatchingInducedGraphIdentities}.
For $v\in W_1$, the matching edge $v\sigma(v)$ lies in $F_{12}$.
The last clause of \noderef{NearEqualRegularTriplet}, normalized by the actual $k$, gives deterministically
\[
 \deg_{A_\sigma}(v)=(q\pm\varepsilon)k.
\tag{3}
\]
For $w\in W_3$, put $S=N_{F_{13}}(w)\cap W_1$ and $T=N_{F_{23}}(w)\cap W_2$.  Both sets are normalized by $m$, because their opposite parts are $W_1,W_2$, and
\[
 \deg_{A_\sigma}(w)=|\sigma(S)\cap T|.
\]
Super-regularity gives $|S|=(d_{13}\pm\varepsilon)m$ and
$|T|=(d_{23}\pm\varepsilon)m$. The lower endpoints are at least
$(d_{13}/2)m,(d_{23}/2)m$, respectively, so the first concentration
invocation applies. Its center $|S||T|/m$ lies between
$(d_{13}-\varepsilon)(d_{23}-\varepsilon)m$ and
$(d_{13}+\varepsilon)(d_{23}+\varepsilon)m$.
The two sharp degree inequalities above put the concentration interval
inside $[(q-\delta)m,(q+\delta)m]$.
\noderef{MatchingInducedDegreeConcentration} makes precisely these
estimates simultaneous, with failure at most $kc^m$.
In particular every such $w$ has at least $(q-\delta)m$ neighbors,
exactly the criterion's lower-degree condition. Also $\delta\leq\varepsilon'$
puts these degrees in the final super-regularity window.

On the $W_1$ side, (3) is already normalized by the actual opposite-part
size $k$, and $\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon'$ puts it in the
required $(q\pm\varepsilon')k$ window.  Thus no replacement of $k$ by $m$
is made in either final degree condition.

For regularity, apply \noderef{NearEqualRegularPairGoodCodegrees} to $F_{13}[W_1,W_3]$ and $F_{23}[W_2,W_3]$.  At most $6\varepsilon k^2$ ordered pairs of $W_3^2$ are bad for one of the two input graphs.  For any remaining $(w,w')$, take the two common-neighborhood sets $S\subseteq W_1$ and $T\subseteq W_2$.  Their sizes are at most $(d_{13}+2\varepsilon)^2m$ and $(d_{23}+2\varepsilon)^2m$.  Set-image concentration and (1) imply
\[
 |N_{A_\sigma}(w)\cap N_{A_\sigma}(w')|
 =|\sigma(S)\cap T|\leq(q+\delta)^2m
\]
except with probability $c^m$.  Here the good-codegree lower bounds are at
least $(d_{13}-2\varepsilon)^2m\geq(d_{13}/2)^2m$ and
$(d_{23}-2\varepsilon)^2m\geq(d_{23}/2)^2m$, so the second concentration
invocation really applies; its conclusion differs from $|S||T|/m$ by at
most $\zeta m$, while (1) gives the displayed upper bound.
Applying \noderef{MatchingInducedCodegreeConcentration} to these two
exceptional-set bounds, the squared lower set-size bounds, (1), and the
second concentration invocation gives the following simultaneous event.

There are at most $k^2\leq(m+1)^2$ good ordered pairs, with diagonal pairs
retained. A union bound makes their concentration estimates simultaneous. On that event, every pair
which is good in both input graphs satisfies the displayed codegree bound,
and the retained vertex estimate gives the criterion's $(q-\delta)m$ lower
degree bound.  Hence only the at most $6\varepsilon k^2\leq6\delta k^2$
input-bad ordered pairs are bad for the output.  We have
$0\leq\delta\leq q\leq1$, $\varepsilon'\leq1$, $1\leq\delta m$, and
$32\delta\leq(\varepsilon')^5$ by the choices above. Therefore the
deterministic adapter \noderef{MatchingInducedSuperRegularCertificate},
which applies \noderef{NearEqualDegreeCodegreeRegularityCriterion} with
exactly these sizes and exceptional-pair allowance, combines this regularity
estimate with the two degree sides to prove $(\varepsilon',q)$-super-regularity
in the sense of \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.

The first union bound has $k$ events and the second has $k^2$ events, so the
total failure probability is explicitly
\[
 kc^m+k^2c^m\leq\bigl((m+1)+(m+1)^2\bigr)c^m.
\]
Use \noderef{FourGraphsPolynomialLossAbsorption} to select $a_0>0$
after $\varepsilon$ and the common $c$ have been fixed. For every
$0<a\leq a_0$ it supplies a threshold above which the last display is
at most $(1-a)^m$, including when $c=0$. Take $n_0$ at least this
threshold and $N_*$, and at least $2$ and $1/\delta$ (rounded up).
Then $1\leq\delta m$ for every $m\geq n_0$, as needed above.
Thus the success probability is at least $1-(1-a)^m$.
All thresholds and both union bounds used only
$k\leq m+1$ and $|k-m|\leq1$, so they are uniform for
$k=m-1,m,m+1$, as required.
\end{proof}
NearEqualFourGraphs.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Near-equal Four Graphs lemma]
For all $0<d_{12},d_{13},d_{23}\leq1$ there exists $\varepsilon'_0>0$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon'\leq\varepsilon'_0$, there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$, there exists $a_0>0$ such that, for every $0<a\leq a_0$, there exists $n_0$ with the following property.  Let $m\geq n_0$, let $|W_1|=|W_2|=m$, and let $|W_3|\in\{m-1,m,m+1\}$.  If $(F_{12},F_{13},F_{23})$ is a near-equal $(\varepsilon,d_{12},d_{13},d_{23})$-regular triplet in the sense of \noderef{NearEqualRegularTriplet}, then, for every witness that $F_{12}[W_1,W_2]$ has a perfect matching and a uniformly random such matching $\sigma$ in the sense of \noderef{UniformPerfectMatching},
\[
 \Pr\bigl[A_\sigma\text{ is }(\varepsilon',d_{13}d_{23})\text{-super-regular on }W_1,W_3\bigr]
 \geq1-(1-a)^m,
\]
where $A_\sigma$ is \noderef{MatchingInducedGraph}.  The constants and failure bound are uniform over all three permitted values of $|W_3|$.
\end{lemma}

NearEqualFourGraphsParameters.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
All input numbers are finite. Work in the nonnegative reals and take
\[
 \delta=\min\{q/8,\eta/4,\eta^5/128\},\quad
 \zeta=\min\{\delta/4,q\delta/4\},\quad
 e=\min\{1/2,\delta/8,d_{12}/4,d_{13}/8,d_{23}/8,q\delta/64\}.
\]
Every entry of each minimum is strictly positive. The required bounds on
$\delta,e$ follow immediately. Fix $0\leq\varepsilon\leq e$ and write
$x=d_{13},y=d_{23}$. Then $\varepsilon\leq x/8,y/8$ gives both
lower set-density bounds and both squared lower bounds, and gives
$2\varepsilon<x,y$. Also $2\varepsilon\leq d_{12}/2<d_{12}$.
Since $x,y\leq1$ and $\varepsilon\leq1/2$,
\[
 (x-\varepsilon)(y-\varepsilon)
 =q-(x+y)\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2\geq q-2\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 (x+\varepsilon)(y+\varepsilon)\leq q+3\varepsilon.
\]
Here $2\varepsilon+\zeta\leq\delta/2$ and
$3\varepsilon+\zeta\leq5\delta/8\leq\delta$, proving the two
degree windows (and $q\geq\delta$ removes any ambiguity about their
lower endpoints). For the last window,
\[
 (x+2\varepsilon)^2\leq x^2+6\varepsilon,\qquad
 (y+2\varepsilon)^2\leq y^2+6\varepsilon,
\]
because $4x\varepsilon+4\varepsilon^2\leq6\varepsilon$.
Multiplication gives an upper bound
$q^2+12\varepsilon+36\varepsilon^2\leq q^2+30\varepsilon$.
Consequently
\[
 30\varepsilon+\zeta\leq(30/64+1/4)q\delta
 <2q\delta\leq2q\delta+\delta^2.
\]
Adding $q^2$ proves the required polynomial inequality. Embedding these
finite nonnegative real choices into the extended nonnegative reals
preserves all the stated arithmetic operations and inequalities.
\end{proof}
NearEqualFourGraphsParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Four Graphs parameter windows]
For $0<d_{12},d_{13},d_{23}\leq1$ and $0<\eta\leq1$, put
$q=d_{13}d_{23}$. There exist positive finite numbers $\delta,\zeta,e$
such that $\delta\leq q$, $\delta\leq\eta$,

\[
 \varepsilon\leq\min(\delta,\eta),\qquad
 2\varepsilon<\min(d_{12},d_{13},d_{23}),
\]
\[
 d_{13}/2\leq d_{13}-\varepsilon,\quad
 d_{23}/2\leq d_{23}-\varepsilon,\quad
 (d_{13}/2)^2\leq(d_{13}-2\varepsilon)^2,\quad
 (d_{23}/2)^2\leq(d_{23}-2\varepsilon)^2,
\]
and the following sharp degree and codegree windows hold:
\[
 q-\delta\leq(d_{13}-\varepsilon)(d_{23}-\varepsilon)-\zeta,
 \qquad (d_{13}+\varepsilon)(d_{23}+\varepsilon)+\zeta\leq q+\delta,
\]
\[
 (d_{13}+2\varepsilon)^2(d_{23}+2\varepsilon)^2+\zeta
 \leq(q+\delta)^2.
\]

\end{lemma}

theorem NearEqualRegularPairGoodCodegrees :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      (U W : Finset V) (m : ℕ) (ε d : ENNReal),
      U.card = m → (W.card + 1 = m ∨ W.card = m ∨ W.card = m + 1) →
      2 ≤ m → 2 * ε < d → SuperRegularPair G U W ε d →
      (((W ×ˢ W).filter fun z =>
          let C := (U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1 ∧ G.Adj u z.2).card
          (C : ENNReal) < (d - 2 * ε) ^ 2 * m ∨
            (d + 2 * ε) ^ 2 * m < (C : ENNReal)).card : ENNReal) ≤
        3 * ε * (W.card : ENNReal) ^ 2 := by
NearEqualRegularPairGoodCodegrees.name: NearEqualRegularPairGoodCodegrees
NearEqualRegularPairGoodCodegrees.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $m\geq2$, we have $m>0$.
Apply \noderef{SuperRegularCodegreeExceptionalBound} to the given
super-regular pair, with $n=m=|U|$ and $2\varepsilon<d$.
It bounds the bad ordered pairs in precisely the stated window by
$2\varepsilon|W|^2\leq3\varepsilon|W|^2$.
The helper allows arbitrary $|W|$, so the near-equal size hypothesis
requires no additional adjustment.  Throughout, the window is
normalized by the actual opposite-part size $|U|=m$.
\end{proof}
NearEqualRegularPairGoodCodegrees.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Good codegrees in a near-equal regular pair]
Let $|U|=m\geq2$ and $|W|\in\{m-1,m,m+1\}$.  If $(U,W)$ is $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular and $2\varepsilon<d$, then at most
$3\varepsilon|W|^2$ ordered pairs $(w,w')\in W^2$ have their common-neighborhood size in $U$ outside
\[
 [(d-2\varepsilon)^2m,(d+2\varepsilon)^2m].
\]
All degree and codegree windows are thus normalized by the actual opposite-part size $m=|U|$.
\end{lemma}

W₁.card = m ∧ W₂.card = m ∧

  Disjoint W₁ W₂ ∧ Disjoint W₁ W₃ ∧ Disjoint W₂ W₃ ∧
  SuperRegularPair F₁₂ W₁ W₂ ε d₁₂ ∧
  SuperRegularPair F₁₃ W₁ W₃ ε d₁₃ ∧
  SuperRegularPair F₂₃ W₂ W₃ ε d₂₃ ∧
  ∀ v ∈ W₁, ∀ u ∈ W₂, F₁₂.Adj v u →
    (d₁₃ * d₂₃ - ε) * W₃.card ≤

    ((W₃.filter fun z => F₁₃.Adj v z ∧ F₂₃.Adj u z).card : ENNReal) ≤

def NearEqualRegularTriplet {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (F₁₂ F₁₃ F₂₃ : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel F₁₂.Adj] [DecidableRel F₁₃.Adj] [DecidableRel F₂₃.Adj]
    (W₁ W₂ W₃ : Finset V) (m : ℕ) (ε d₁₂ d₁₃ d₂₃ : ENNReal) : Prop :=
NearEqualRegularTriplet.name: NearEqualRegularTriplet
NearEqualRegularTriplet.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}
Let $W_1,W_2,W_3$ be pairwise disjoint finite vertex sets with $|W_1|=|W_2|=m$ and $|W_3|\in\{m-1,m,m+1\}$.  For $1\leq i<j\leq3$, let $(W_i,W_j)$ be $(\varepsilon,d_{ij})$-super-regular in $F_{ij}$ in the sense of \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.  The triple is a near-equal $(\varepsilon,d_{12},d_{13},d_{23})$-regular triplet if every edge $vu\in E(F_{12})$, with $v\in W_1$ and $u\in W_2$, satisfies
\[
 (d_{13}d_{23}-\varepsilon)|W_3|\leq
 |N_{F_{13}}(v)\cap N_{F_{23}}(u)\cap W_3|
 \leq(d_{13}d_{23}+\varepsilon)|W_3|.
\]
In particular, both the common-neighborhood window and all degree windows involving $W_3$ are normalized by the actual cardinality $|W_3|$, while the matching pair has the common size $m$.
\end{definition}

theorem NearEqualRetentionThreshold (ξ h : ℝ) (hξ : 0 < ξ) (hh : 0 < h) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n₀ ∧ ∀ a b : ℕ,
      n₀ ≤ a → n₀ ≤ b → a ≤ b + 1 → b ≤ a + 1 →
      ENNReal.ofReal
        (2 * (a + b : ℝ) * Real.exp (-2 * ξ ^ 2 * min (a : ℝ) b) +
         2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (a + b) * Real.exp (-2 * ξ ^ 2 * h ^ 2 * a * b)) < 1 := by
NearEqualRetentionThreshold.name: NearEqualRetentionThreshold
NearEqualRetentionThreshold.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $k=2\xi^2>0$, $c=kh^2>0$ and $s=\min(a,b)$. The two
near-equal inequalities imply $\max(a,b)\leq s+1$, hence
$a+b\leq2s+1$; also $ab\geq s^2$. For $s\geq1$, the degree term is
at most $6s e^{-ks}$.

For $x>0$, the nonnegative power series for $e^x$ gives
$e^x\geq x^3/6$ and $e^x\geq x^2/2$. Consequently
$6s e^{-ks}\leq36/(k^3s^2)$. Choose an integer $n_0\geq1$ strictly
larger than each of
\[
\sqrt{72/k^3},\qquad 4\log(2)/c,\qquad 8/c.
\]
Such an integer exists by the Archimedean property, and this choice is
independent of $a,b$ or any graph. The first inequality makes the
degree term strictly smaller than $1/2$ whenever $s\geq n_0$.

For the rectangle term use $2^{a+b}=e^{(a+b)\log2}$. It is at most
$4e^{2s\log2-cs^2}$. Since $s>4\log(2)/c$, we have
$2s\log2\leq cs^2/2$. The term is therefore at most
$4e^{-cs^2/2}$. The inequality $e^x\geq x^2/2$ applied to
$x=cs^2/2>0$ bounds this by $32/(c^2s^4)$.
Since $s>8/c$ and $s\geq1$, we have
$c^2s^4\geq c^2s^2>64$, so the rectangle term is strictly smaller
than $1/2$. The sum of the two nonnegative terms is strictly smaller
than one. For a nonnegative real $B$, $\operatorname{ofReal}(B)<1$
is equivalent to $B<1$, proving the displayed assertion.
\end{proof}
NearEqualRetentionThreshold.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform numerical threshold for near-equal retention tests]
For real $\xi,h>0$, there exists an integer $n_0\geq1$ such that for
all integers $a,b\geq n_0$ with $a\leq b+1$ and $b\leq a+1$,
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\left(
 2(a+b)e^{-2\xi^2\min(a,b)}
 +2\,2^{a+b}e^{-2\xi^2h^2ab}\right)<1.
\]
The threshold depends only on $\xi,h$.
\end{lemma}
NearEqualRetentionThreshold.title: NearEqualRetentionThreshold

            ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hpT, hpS⟩, K.symm hpAdj⟩
        · intro p _ q _ hpq
          exact Prod.swap_injective hpq
        · intro p hp
          obtain ⟨hpTS, hpAdj⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hp
          obtain ⟨hpT, hpS⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hpTS
          exact ⟨p.swap, Finset.mem_filter.mpr
            ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hpS, hpT⟩, K.symm hpAdj⟩, rfl⟩
      simp only [PairDensity, hcount, mul_comm]
    have lowSwap (L R : Finset V)
        (h : LowerSuperRegularPair G L R (ENNReal.ofReal θr) d) :
        LowerSuperRegularPair G R L (ENNReal.ofReal θr) d := by
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro S hS T hT hScard hTcard
        simpa only [densitySwap G S T] using h.1 T hT S hS hTcard hScard
      · intro w hw
        simpa only [G.adj_comm] using h.2.2 w hw
      · intro u hu
        simpa only [G.adj_comm] using h.2.1 u hu
    have highSwap (K : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel K.Adj] (L R : Finset V)
        (h : SuperRegularPair K L R η c) : SuperRegularPair K R L η c := by
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro S hS T hT hScard hTcard
        simpa only [densitySwap K S T] using h.1 T hT S hS hTcard hScard
      · intro w hw
        simpa only [K.adj_comm] using h.2.2 w hw
      · intro u hu
        simpa only [K.adj_comm] using h.2.1 u hu
    have ordered : ∀ (L R : Finset V), Disjoint L R →
        (L.card = m ∨ L.card = m + 1) → (R.card = m ∨ R.card = m + 1) →
        L.card ≤ R.card → LowerSuperRegularPair G L R (ENNReal.ofReal θr) d →
        ∃ F : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
          F ≤ G ∧ (∀ ⦃x y⦄, F.Adj x y →
            (x ∈ L ∧ y ∈ R) ∨ (x ∈ R ∧ y ∈ L)) ∧
          SuperRegularPair F L R η c := by
      intro L R hLR hL hR hle hlowLR
      -- Keep only crossing edges and pad the smaller part when necessary.
      let e : V ↪ Option V := ⟨Option.some, Option.some_injective V⟩
      let D : Finset (Option V) := if L.card < R.card then {none} else ∅
      let Lp := (L.map e) ∪ D
      let Rp := R.map e
      let Gp : SimpleGraph (Option V) := {
        Adj := fun x y => match x, y with
          | some x, some y => G.Adj x y ∧
              ((x ∈ L ∧ y ∈ R) ∨ (x ∈ R ∧ y ∈ L))
          | none, some y => L.card < R.card ∧ y ∈ R
          | some x, none => L.card < R.card ∧ x ∈ R
          | none, none => False
        symm := by
          intro x y hxy
          cases x with
          | none => cases y with
            | none => exact hxy
            | some y => exact hxy
          | some x =>
            cases y with
            | none => exact hxy
            | some y =>
              exact ⟨G.symm hxy.1, hxy.2.elim
                (fun h => Or.inr ⟨h.2, h.1⟩) (fun h => Or.inl ⟨h.2, h.1⟩)⟩
        loopless := ⟨by intro x; cases x <;> simp⟩ }
      letI : DecidableRel Gp.Adj := Classical.decRel _
      have hD : Disjoint (L.map e) D := by
        dsimp [D]
        split_ifs <;> simp [e]
      have hLp : Lp.card = R.card := by
        have hnear : R.card ≤ L.card + 1 := by omega
        dsimp [Lp]
        rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hD, Finset.card_map]
        dsimp [D]
        split_ifs with hlt
        · simp only [Finset.card_singleton]; omega
        · simp only [Finset.card_empty, add_zero]; omega
      have hRp : Rp.card = R.card := Finset.card_map _
      have hcopy : ∀ x ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ R, Gp.Adj (e x) (e y) ↔ G.Adj x y := by
        intro x hx y hy
        change (G.Adj x y ∧ _) ↔ G.Adj x y
        exact and_iff_left (Or.inl ⟨hx, hy⟩)
      have hcomplete : ∀ z ∈ D, ∀ y ∈ R, Gp.Adj z (e y) := by
        intro z hz y hy
        dsimp [D] at hz
        split_ifs at hz with hlt
        · have hz0 : z = none := Finset.mem_singleton.mp hz
          subst z
          exact ⟨hlt, hy⟩
        · simp at hz
      have hpad : LowerSuperRegularPair Gp Lp Rp (ENNReal.ofReal β) d :=
        CompleteRowPadding G Gp e L R D (ENNReal.ofReal θr) (ENNReal.ofReal β) d
          (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hθr) hθbudget hβ1 hd1 hD hLp hcopy hcomplete hlowLR
      have hdis : Disjoint Lp Rp := by
        apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
        intro z hzL hzR
        obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp hzR
        rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hzL with hz | hz
        · obtain ⟨x, hx, hxy⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp hz
          have heq : x = y := e.injective hxy
          exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp hLR (heq ▸ hx) hy
        · dsimp [D] at hz
          split_ifs at hz <;> simp [e] at hz
      have hsupport : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, Gp.Adj x y →
          (x ∈ Lp ∧ y ∈ Rp) ∨ (x ∈ Rp ∧ y ∈ Lp) := by
        intro x y hxy
        cases x with
        | none =>
          cases y with
          | none => exact False.elim hxy
          | some y =>
            exact Or.inl ⟨Finset.mem_union_right _ (by simp [D, hxy.1]),
              Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨y, hxy.2, rfl⟩⟩
        | some x =>
          cases y with
          | none =>
            exact Or.inr ⟨Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨x, hxy.2, rfl⟩,
              Finset.mem_union_right _ (by simp [D, hxy.1])⟩
          | some y =>
            rcases hxy.2 with hh | hh
            · exact Or.inl ⟨Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨x, hh.1, rfl⟩),
                Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨y, hh.2, rfl⟩⟩
            · exact Or.inr ⟨Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨x, hh.1, rfl⟩,
                Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨y, hh.2, rfl⟩)⟩
      -- Extraction requires the two parts to cover its vertex type.
      let S := {z : Option V // z ∈ Lp ∪ Rp}
      let Ls : Finset S := Finset.univ.filter fun z => z.val ∈ Lp
      let Rs : Finset S := Finset.univ.filter fun z => z.val ∈ Rp
      let Gs : SimpleGraph S := Gp.comap Subtype.val
      letI : DecidableRel Gs.Adj := Classical.decRel _
      have images (T : Finset (Option V)) (hT : T ⊆ Lp ∪ Rp) :
          (Finset.univ.filter fun z : S => z.val ∈ T).image Subtype.val = T := by
        ext z
        simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          exact hx
        · intro hz
          exact ⟨⟨z, hT hz⟩, hz, rfl⟩
      have hLs : Ls.image Subtype.val = Lp := images Lp Finset.subset_union_left
      have hRs : Rs.image Subtype.val = Rp := images Rp Finset.subset_union_right
      have hLc : Ls.card = R.card := by
        rw [← hLp, ← hLs, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective]
      have hRc : Rs.card = R.card := by
        rw [← hRp, ← hRs, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective]
      have hdisS : Disjoint Ls Rs := by
        apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
        intro x hx hy
        exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp hdis (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).2 (Finset.mem_filter.mp hy).2
      have hcoverS : Ls ∪ Rs = Finset.univ := by
        apply Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall.mpr
        intro x
        simpa only [Ls, Rs, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_filter,
          Finset.mem_univ, true_and] using x.property
      have hsupportS : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, Gs.Adj x y →
          (x ∈ Ls ∧ y ∈ Rs) ∨ (x ∈ Rs ∧ y ∈ Ls) := by
        intro x y hxy
        simpa only [Ls, Rs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
          using hsupport hxy
      have hlowS : LowerSuperRegularPair Gs Ls Rs (ENNReal.ofReal β) d := by
        apply (LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding Subtype.val Subtype.val_injective Gs Gp
          Ls Rs (ENNReal.ofReal β) d (fun _ _ _ _ => Iff.rfl)).mpr
        simpa only [hLs, hRs] using hpad
      have extractionInput (α : ENNReal) (hαtop : α ≠ ⊤) (hβα : ENNReal.ofReal β ≤ α) :
          LowerSuperRegularPair Gs Ls Rs α (ENNReal.ofReal q + α) := by
        have hend : ENNReal.ofReal q + α - α = ENNReal.ofReal q :=
          ENNReal.add_sub_cancel_right hαtop
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro A hA B hB hsizeA hsizeB
          rw [hend]
          exact hqβd.trans (hlowS.1 A hA B hB
            ((mul_le_mul_left hβα _).trans_lt hsizeA)
            ((mul_le_mul_left hβα _).trans_lt hsizeB))
        · intro x hx
          rw [hend]
          exact (mul_le_mul_left hqβd _).trans (hlowS.2.1 x hx)
        · intro y hy
          rw [hend]
          exact (mul_le_mul_left hqβd _).trans (hlowS.2.2 y hy)
      have hRm : m ≤ R.card := by omega
      have hextracted : ∃ F : SimpleGraph S, ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
          F ≤ Gs ∧ SuperRegularPair F Ls Rs (ENNReal.ofReal τ) c := by
        rw [← hqc]
        first
        | exact hexu Gs Ls Rs R.card (hNu.trans (hNm.trans hRm)) hLc hRc
            hdisS hcoverS hsupportS (extractionInput αu hαutop hβu)
        | exact hexv Gs Ls Rs R.card (hNv.trans (hNm.trans hRm)) hLc hRc
            hdisS hcoverS hsupportS (extractionInput αv hαvtop hβv)
      obtain ⟨Fs, hFsdec, hFsGs, hFsreg⟩ := hextracted
      letI : DecidableRel Fs.Adj := hFsdec
      let inc : S ↪ Option V := ⟨Subtype.val, Subtype.val_injective⟩
      let Fp := Fs.map inc
      letI : DecidableRel Fp.Adj := Classical.decRel _
      have hFpGp : Fp ≤ Gp := (SimpleGraph.map_le_iff_le_comap inc Fs Gp).mpr hFsGs
      have hFpReg : SuperRegularPair Fp Lp Rp (ENNReal.ofReal τ) c := by
        have hh := SuperRegularPairEmbedding inc inc.injective Fs Fp Ls Rs
          (ENNReal.ofReal τ) c (fun _ _ _ _ => SimpleGraph.map_adj_apply) hFsreg
        change SuperRegularPair Fp (Ls.image Subtype.val) (Rs.image Subtype.val)
          (ENNReal.ofReal τ) c at hh
        simpa only [hLs, hRs] using hh
      have hdelete : SuperRegularPair Fp (L.map e) (R.map e) η c := by
        have hh := SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion Fp Lp Rp (L.map e) (R.map e)
          m τ η.toReal c.toReal hτ.le hrη hrη1.le hrc.le hrc1
          (by dsimp [τ]; linarith) hm hfloor
          Finset.subset_union_left (by rfl)
          (by simpa only [Finset.card_map] using (show m ≤ L.card by omega))
          (by simpa only [Finset.card_map] using hRm)
          (by rw [hLp, Finset.card_map]; omega)
          (by change Rp.card ≤ Rp.card + 1; omega)
          (by simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hctop] using hFpReg)
        simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hηtop, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hctop] using hh
      -- Pulling back along `some` removes the dummy and isolates the ambient remainder.
      let F := Fp.comap e
      letI : DecidableRel F.Adj := Classical.decRel _
      have hFG : F ≤ G := by
        intro x y hxy
        have hh := hFpGp hxy
        exact hh.1
      have hFsupport : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, F.Adj x y →
          (x ∈ L ∧ y ∈ R) ∨ (x ∈ R ∧ y ∈ L) := by
        intro x y hxy
        exact (hFpGp hxy).2
      have density (A B : Finset V) :
          PairDensity Fp (A.map e) (B.map e) = PairDensity F A B := by
        unfold PairDensity
        simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod]
        rw [← Finset.prodMap_map_product, Finset.filter_map, Finset.card_map,
          Finset.card_map, Finset.card_map]
        rfl
      have countLeft (x : V) :
          ((R.map e).filter fun y => Fp.Adj (e x) y).card =
          (R.filter fun y => F.Adj x y).card := by
        rw [Finset.filter_map, Finset.card_map]
        rfl
      have countRight (y : V) :
          ((L.map e).filter fun x => Fp.Adj x (e y)).card =
          (L.filter fun x => F.Adj x y).card := by
        rw [Finset.filter_map, Finset.card_map]
        rfl
      refine ⟨F, inferInstance, hFG, hFsupport, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro A hA B hB hsizeA hsizeB
        have hh := hdelete.1 (A.map e) (Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hA)
          (B.map e) (Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hB)
          (by simpa only [Finset.card_map] using hsizeA)
          (by simpa only [Finset.card_map] using hsizeB)
        simpa only [density] using hh
      · intro x hx
        have hh := hdelete.2.1 (e x) (Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)
        simpa only [Finset.card_map, countLeft] using hh
      · intro y hy
        have hh := hdelete.2.2 (e y) (Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩)
        simpa only [Finset.card_map, countRight] using hh
    rcases le_total U.card W.card with hle | hle
    · exact ordered U W hUW hU hW hle hlow
    · obtain ⟨F, hFdec, hFG, hFsupport, hFreg⟩ :=
        ordered W U hUW.symm hW hU hle (lowSwap U W hlow)
      letI : DecidableRel F.Adj := hFdec
      exact ⟨F, hFdec, hFG, fun _ _ h => (hFsupport h).elim Or.inr Or.inl,
        highSwap F W U hFreg⟩
NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction.lean_statement:
universe u v

theorem NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction (η c d : ENNReal)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η < 1) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hcd : c < d ^ 2 / 2) (hd1 : d ≤ 1) :
    ∃ θ : ENNReal, ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < θ ∧ θ < η ∧ 1 ≤ N ∧
      (∀ {V : Type u} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
        (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (m : ℕ),
        N ≤ m → Disjoint U W →
        (U.card = m ∨ U.card = m + 1) →
        (W.card = m ∨ W.card = m + 1) →
        LowerSuperRegularPair G U W θ d →
        ∃ F : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
          F ≤ G ∧
          (∀ ⦃u v⦄, F.Adj u v →
            (u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ W) ∨ (u ∈ W ∧ v ∈ U)) ∧
          SuperRegularPair F U W η c) ∧
      (∀ {V : Type v} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
        (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (m : ℕ),
        N ≤ m → Disjoint U W →
        (U.card = m ∨ U.card = m + 1) →
        (W.card = m ∨ W.card = m + 1) →
        LowerSuperRegularPair G U W θ d →
        ∃ F : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
          F ≤ G ∧
          (∀ ⦃u v⦄, F.Adj u v →
            (u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ W) ∨ (u ∈ W ∧ v ∈ U)) ∧
          SuperRegularPair F U W η c) := by
NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction.name: NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction
NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The hypotheses imply that all three parameters are finite,
$0<d\leq1$ and $0<c<1/2$. Work with their real values. Put
$q=\sqrt{2c}$, $g=(d-q)/4$, and $\tau=\eta/4$.
Then $0<q<d\leq1$ and $g>0$. By \noderef{SuperRegularSubgraph},
choose $0<\alpha<\tau$ and a cutoff $N_1$ for extraction with
input density $q$ and output error $\tau$. The same parameters may
be required for two vertex universes at once: take the minimum of
their two supplied errors and the maximum of their two cutoffs.
Weakening an input error only strengthens the required degree and
subset hypotheses, so each supplied extraction still applies.
Choose $0<\theta<\min\{\eta,\alpha/4,g\}$ and an integer
$N\geq\max\{1,N_1,2/\alpha,1/(\alpha g),8/\eta\}$.
These choices precede $G,U,W,m$.

First restrict $G$ to its crossing edges on $U\cup W$, and regard
this graph as a graph on the subtype $U\cup W$. Cardinalities,
opposite-part degrees, and densities of subsets of the two parts are
unchanged. This follows directly from the ordered-edge count in
\noderef{PairDensity}: inclusion of the subtype is a bijection on
each part and on its ordered crossing edges.
The hypotheses of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} give degree
at least $(d-\theta)$ times the opposite size and density at least
$d-\theta$ whenever both subset sizes exceed their $\theta$ thresholds.

If the two sizes are equal, tests above the $\alpha$ thresholds
are above the $\theta$ thresholds, and $d-\theta>q$.
Thus the restricted graph meets the minimum-degree and density
hypotheses of \noderef{SuperRegularSubgraph}: its lower
$(\alpha,q+\alpha)$-regularity is exactly density at least $q$
on those tests, by \noderef{LowerRegularPair}. Extraction yields
error $\tau$ and density $q^2/2=c$. Weakening the error to $\eta$
preserves all degree inequalities and makes the tested family smaller,
by \noderef{RegularPair} and \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.

Suppose next the sizes are $m$ and $h=m+1$, with $U$ the smaller
part. Add one new vertex to $U$ and join it to every vertex of $W$.
The padded parts cover their enlarged vertex set and have size $h$.
Original vertices of $U$ have degree at least $(d-\theta)h>qh$;
the new vertex has degree $h\geq qh$. A vertex of $W$ has degree
at least $(d-\theta)m+1\geq q(m+1)$, since $d-\theta>q$ and $q<1$.
For padded tests $S,T$ of sizes greater than $\alpha h$, put
$S_0=S\setminus\{*\}$. Then
$|S_0|>\alpha(m+1)-1\geq\alpha m/2>\theta m$
and $|T|>\alpha h>\theta h$. The original lower-regularity
test applies, and, even discarding the new edges,
\[
 d_{\rm pad}(S,T)\geq(d-\theta)|S_0|/|S|
 \geq d-\theta-1/|S|>d-\theta-1/(\alpha h)
 \geq d-\theta-g>q.
\]
Here $0<d-\theta\leq1$ and the choice of $N$ were used.
Apply \noderef{SuperRegularSubgraph} to the padded graph.

Delete the new vertex from the extracted graph. Degrees from $U$
to $W$ are unchanged. Degrees from $W$ to $U$ lose at most one,
and therefore lie between $(c-\tau)(m+1)-1$ and
$(c+\tau)(m+1)$. Their error relative to $m$ is at most
$\tau+2/m\leq\eta/2<\eta$, since $c<1/2$, $\tau<1/4$,
and $m\geq8/\eta$. Tests of sizes greater than $\eta m$ and
$\eta(m+1)$ exceed the padded $\tau(m+1)$ thresholds:
$\eta m>\tau(m+1)$ for $m\geq1$. Their edges are unchanged
by deletion, so their densities lie within $\tau$ of $c$ and hence
within $\eta$. These are precisely the clauses of
\noderef{SuperRegularPair}. If $W$ was the smaller part, interchange
the parts in this argument; ordered-edge density is symmetric because
swapping coordinates bijects the two ordered-edge sets.

Finally extend the extracted graph by isolated vertices to the original
ambient type. Its edges are original crossing edges of $G$, and all
tested counts are unchanged. No dummy vertex remains. The real and
extended inequalities agree because every quantity is finite. Input
$d-\theta$ is positive. An output real lower endpoint that is negative
corresponds to truncated endpoint zero and is automatic; otherwise it
is the identical lower bound just proved. This proves the extended
statement as well, including both degree orientations.
\end{proof}
NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Contained extraction on equal or consecutive parts]
Let $0<\eta<1$, $0<c<d^2/2$, and $d\leq1$, in extended
nonnegative reals. There are $0<\theta<\eta$ and an integer $N\geq1$,
depending only on these parameters, such that the following holds.
If $G$ is a finite simple graph, $U,W$ are disjoint, both sizes belong
to $\{m,m+1\}$ with $m\geq N$, and $(U,W)$ is lower
$(\theta,d)$-super-regular, then there is a graph $F$ on the original
vertex set, contained in $G$, with edges only between $U$ and $W$, for
which $(U,W)$ is $(\eta,c)$-super-regular. Neither coverage of the
ambient vertex set nor absence of other edges in $G$ is required.
\end{lemma}
NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction.title: NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction

NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity.lean_proof:
intro V K _ _ _ F₁₂ F₁₃ F₂₃ _ _ _ W₁ W₂ W₃ m ε₀ η δ ε d₁₃ d₂₃
    h₁₂ _hdisj hW₁ hW₂ hnear hε₀ hε hregsum hdegsum _hpositive hd hF₁₂ hF₁₃ hF₂₃
  classical
  let F := SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph F₁₂ F₁₃ F₂₃ W₁ W₂ h₁₂ W₃ ε d₁₃ d₂₃
  letI : DecidableRel F.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  change SuperRegularPair F W₁ W₂ η δ
  let good (k : K) (x v : V) :=
    (d₁₃ k * d₂₃ k - 2 * ε k) * (W₃ k).card ≤
      (((W₃ k).filter fun z => (F₁₃ k).Adj x z ∧ (F₂₃ k).Adj v z).card : ENNReal) ∧
    (((W₃ k).filter fun z => (F₁₃ k).Adj x z ∧ (F₂₃ k).Adj v z).card : ENNReal) ≤
      (d₁₃ k * d₂₃ k + 2 * ε k) * (W₃ k).card
  have hchar (x : V) (hx : x ∈ W₁) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ W₂) :
      F.Adj x v ↔ F₁₂.Adj x v ∧ ∀ k, good k x v := by
    change (x ≠ v ∧
      ((x ∈ W₁ ∧ v ∈ W₂ ∧ F₁₂.Adj x v ∧ ∀ k, good k x v) ∨
       (v ∈ W₁ ∧ x ∈ W₂ ∧ F₁₂.Adj v x ∧ ∀ k, good k v x))) ↔ _

    · rintro ⟨_, h | h⟩
      · exact ⟨h.2.2.1, h.2.2.2⟩
      · exact False.elim (Finset.disjoint_left.mp h₁₂ h.1 hv)
    · intro h
      exact ⟨F₁₂.ne_of_adj h.1, Or.inl ⟨hx, hv, h.1, h.2⟩⟩
  have hcharRight (v : V) (hv : v ∈ W₂) (x : V) (hx : x ∈ W₁) :

  -- A finite union bound for the original elements discarded by any test.
  have hcount {A : Type _} [DecidableEq A] (S : Finset A)
      (edge : A → Prop) (test : K → A → Prop)
      [DecidablePred edge] [∀ k, DecidablePred (test k)] :
      ((S.filter edge).card : ENNReal) ≤
        ((S.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) +
          ∑ k, ((S.filter fun a => ¬ test k a).card : ENNReal) := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
      let E := S.filter edge
      let D := E.filter fun a => ¬ ∀ k, test k a
      have hpartition : (S.filter edge).card =
          (S.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card + D.card := by
        simpa only [E, D, Finset.filter_filter] using
          (Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := E) (fun a => ∀ k, test k a)).symm
      have hsub : D ⊆ Finset.univ.biUnion (fun k => S.filter fun a => ¬ test k a) := by
        intro a ha
        obtain ⟨haE, hanot⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := not_forall.mp hanot
        exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨k, Finset.mem_univ _,
          Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨(Finset.mem_filter.mp haE).1, hk⟩⟩
      have hD : D.card ≤ ∑ k, (S.filter fun a => ¬ test k a).card :=
        (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans Finset.card_biUnion_le
      rw [hpartition, Nat.cast_add]
      apply add_le_add le_rfl
      exact_mod_cast hD
  have hpartner (G H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel H.Adj]
      (L R T : Finset V) (ε p q : ENNReal)
      (hε : ε ≤ 1) (hp : p ≤ 1) (hq : q ≤ 1)
      (hG : SuperRegularPair G L T ε p) (hH : RegularPair H R T ε q) :
      ∀ x ∈ L,
        ((R.filter fun v => ¬ ((p * q - 2 * ε) * T.card ≤
          ((T.filter fun z => G.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) ∧
          ((T.filter fun z => G.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) ≤
            (p * q + 2 * ε) * T.card)).card : ENNReal) ≤ 2 * ε * R.card := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
      intro x hx
      by_cases hT : T = ∅
      · simp [hT]
      have hk : T.card ≠ 0 := fun hz => hT (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hz)
      let C (v : V) := (T.filter fun z => G.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj v z).card
      let bad (v : V) := ¬ ((p * q - 2 * ε) * T.card ≤ (C v : ENNReal) ∧
        (C v : ENNReal) ≤ (p * q + 2 * ε) * T.card)
      change ((R.filter bad).card : ENNReal) ≤ 2 * ε * R.card
      let S := T.filter fun z => G.Adj x z
      have hS : S ⊆ T := Finset.filter_subset _ _
      have hSk : S.card ≤ T.card := Finset.card_le_card hS
      obtain ⟨halower, haupper⟩ := hG.2.1 x hx
      change (p - ε) * T.card ≤ (S.card : ENNReal) at halower
      change (S.card : ENNReal) ≤ (p + ε) * T.card at haupper
      have hC (v : V) : (S.filter fun z => H.Adj v z).card = C v := by
        simp only [S, C, Finset.filter_filter]
      have hca (v : V) : C v ≤ S.card := by
        rw [← hC v]
        exact Finset.card_filter_le _ _
      by_cases hsmall : (S.card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * T.card
      · have hempty : R.filter bad = ∅ := by
          apply Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff.mpr
          intro v _hv hbad
          exact hbad (SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow ε p q T.card S.card
            (C v) hk hε hp hq halower hsmall (hca v))
        simp only [hempty, Finset.card_empty, Nat.cast_zero, zero_le]
      · have hlarge : ε * T.card < S.card := lt_of_not_ge hsmall
        let Tminus := R.filter fun v =>
          ((S.filter fun z => H.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) < (q - ε) * S.card
        let Tplus := R.filter fun v =>
          (q + ε) * S.card < ((S.filter fun z => H.Adj v z).card : ENNReal)
        have hminus : (Tminus.card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * R.card :=
          RegularPairLowerTail H R T S ε q hε hq hH hS hlarge
        have hplus : (Tplus.card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * R.card :=
          RegularPairUpperTail H R T S ε q hε hq hH hS hlarge
        have hsubset : R.filter bad ⊆ Tminus ∪ Tplus := by
          intro v hv
          obtain ⟨hvR, hvbad⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hv
          by_cases hm : v ∈ Tminus
          · exact Finset.mem_union_left _ hm
          by_cases ht : v ∈ Tplus
          · exact Finset.mem_union_right _ ht
          have hlower : (q - ε) * S.card ≤ (C v : ENNReal) := by
            have hnot : ¬ ((S.filter fun z => H.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) <
                (q - ε) * S.card := by
              intro hlt
              exact hm (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hvR, hlt⟩)
            simpa only [hC v] using le_of_not_gt hnot
          have hupper : (C v : ENNReal) ≤ (q + ε) * S.card := by
            have hnot : ¬ (q + ε) * S.card <
                ((S.filter fun z => H.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) := by
              intro hlt
              exact ht (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hvR, hlt⟩)
            simpa only [hC v] using le_of_not_gt hnot
          exact False.elim (hvbad (CodegreeWindowTransfer ε p q T.card S.card
            (C v) hε hp hq hSk halower haupper hlower hupper))
        calc
          ((R.filter bad).card : ENNReal) ≤ (Tminus ∪ Tplus).card := by
            exact_mod_cast Finset.card_le_card hsubset
          _ ≤ (Tminus.card : ENNReal) + Tplus.card := by
            exact_mod_cast Finset.card_union_le Tminus Tplus
          _ ≤ ε * R.card + ε * R.card := add_le_add hminus hplus
          _ = 2 * ε * R.card := by ring
  have hrow (x : V) (hx : x ∈ W₁) (k : K) :
      ((W₂.filter fun v => ¬ good k x v).card : ENNReal) ≤ 2 * ε k * W₂.card :=
    hpartner (F₁₃ k) (F₂₃ k) W₁ W₂ (W₃ k) (ε k)
      (d₁₃ k) (d₂₃ k) (hε k).1 (hd k).1 (hd k).2 (hF₁₃ k) (hF₂₃ k).1 x hx
  have hcol (v : V) (hv : v ∈ W₂) (k : K) :
      ((W₁.filter fun x => ¬ good k x v).card : ENNReal) ≤ 2 * ε k * W₁.card := by
    have h := hpartner (F₂₃ k) (F₁₃ k) W₂ W₁ (W₃ k) (ε k)
      (d₂₃ k) (d₁₃ k) (hε k).1 (hd k).2 (hd k).1 (hF₂₃ k) (hF₁₃ k).1 v hv
    simpa only [good, mul_comm (d₂₃ k) (d₁₃ k), and_comm] using h
  have hdegree (A : Finset V) (edge : V → Prop) (test : K → V → Prop)
      [DecidablePred edge] [∀ k, DecidablePred (test k)]
      (hlower : (δ - ε₀) * A.card ≤ ((A.filter edge).card : ENNReal))
      (hupper : ((A.filter edge).card : ENNReal) ≤ (δ + ε₀) * A.card)
      (hbad : ∀ k, ((A.filter fun a => ¬ test k a).card : ENNReal) ≤ 2 * ε k * A.card) :
      (δ - η) * A.card ≤ ((A.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) ∧
      ((A.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) ≤ (δ + η) * A.card := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
      have hsum : (∑ k, ((A.filter fun a => ¬ test k a).card : ENNReal)) ≤
          (2 * ∑ k, ε k) * A.card := by
        calc
          _ ≤ ∑ k, 2 * ε k * A.card := Finset.sum_le_sum fun k _ => hbad k
          _ = (2 * ∑ k, ε k) * A.card := by rw [← Finset.sum_mul, ← Finset.mul_sum]
      have hlost := (hcount A edge test).trans (add_le_add le_rfl hsum)
      constructor
      · rw [ENNReal.sub_mul (fun _ _ => ENNReal.natCast_ne_top A.card)]
        apply tsub_le_iff_right.mpr
        have hbase : δ * A.card ≤ ((A.filter edge).card : ENNReal) + ε₀ * A.card := by
          apply tsub_le_iff_right.mp
          simpa only [ENNReal.sub_mul (fun _ _ => ENNReal.natCast_ne_top A.card)] using hlower
        calc
          δ * A.card ≤ ((A.filter edge).card : ENNReal) + ε₀ * A.card := hbase
          _ ≤ (((A.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) +
              (2 * ∑ k, ε k) * A.card) + ε₀ * A.card := add_le_add hlost le_rfl
          _ = ((A.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) +
              (ε₀ + 2 * ∑ k, ε k) * A.card := by ring
          _ ≤ ((A.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) + η * A.card :=
            add_le_add le_rfl (mul_le_mul_right' hdegsum _)
      · have hsub : A.filter (fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a) ⊆ A.filter edge := by
          intro a ha
          obtain ⟨haA, hae, _⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
          exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨haA, hae⟩
        have hc : ((A.filter fun a => edge a ∧ ∀ k, test k a).card : ENNReal) ≤
            (A.filter edge).card := by exact_mod_cast Finset.card_le_card hsub
        exact hc.trans (hupper.trans (mul_le_mul_right' (add_le_add le_rfl hε₀) _))
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · apply RegularityAfterDensityLoss F₁₂ F W₁ W₂ ε₀ δ η
      (∑ k, (ε k) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹) hε₀ hregsum hF₁₂.1
    intro U hU Z hZ hsizeU hsizeZ
    have heq : (U.product Z).filter (fun p => F.Adj p.1 p.2) =
        (U.product Z).filter (fun p => F₁₂.Adj p.1 p.2 ∧ ∀ k, good k p.1 p.2) := by
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro p hp
      obtain ⟨hpU, hpZ⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hp
      exact hchar p.1 (hU hpU) p.2 (hZ hpZ)
    have hsub : (U.product Z).filter (fun p => F.Adj p.1 p.2) ⊆
        (U.product Z).filter (fun p => F₁₂.Adj p.1 p.2) := by
      intro p hp
      obtain ⟨hpUZ, hpF⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hp
      obtain ⟨hpU, hpZ⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hpUZ
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hpUZ, ((hchar p.1 (hU hpU) p.2 (hZ hpZ)).mp hpF).1⟩
    have hmono : PairDensity F U Z ≤ PairDensity F₁₂ U Z := by
      apply ENNReal.div_le_div_right
      exact_mod_cast Finset.card_le_card hsub
    refine ⟨hmono, ?_⟩
    let den : ENNReal := (U.card : ENNReal) * Z.card
    have hbad (k : K) :
        (((U.product Z).filter fun p => ¬ good k p.1 p.2).card : ENNReal) / den ≤
          (ε k) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
      apply OneIndexBadPairCounting (F₁₃ k) (F₂₃ k) W₁ W₂ (W₃ k) m (ε k)
        (d₁₃ k) (d₂₃ k) hW₁ hW₂ (hnear k) (hε k).1 (hd k).1 (hd k).2
        (hF₁₃ k) (hF₂₃ k) U hU Z hZ
      · exact (mul_le_mul_right' (hε k).2 (m : ENNReal)).trans_lt (by simpa only [hW₁] using hsizeU)
      · exact (mul_le_mul_right' (hε k).2 (m : ENNReal)).trans_lt (by simpa only [hW₂] using hsizeZ)
    have hsum : (∑ k, (((U.product Z).filter fun p => ¬ good k p.1 p.2).card : ENNReal)) / den ≤
        ∑ k, (ε k) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
      simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv, Finset.sum_mul] using Finset.sum_le_sum (fun k _ => hbad k)
    have hbound := ENNReal.div_le_div_right
      (hcount (U.product Z) (fun p => F₁₂.Adj p.1 p.2) (fun k p => good k p.1 p.2)) den
    rw [← heq, ENNReal.add_div] at hbound
    have hloss : PairDensity F₁₂ U Z ≤ PairDensity F U Z + ∑ k, (ε k) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ :=
      hbound.trans (add_le_add le_rfl hsum)
    apply tsub_le_iff_right.mpr
    simpa only [add_comm] using hloss
  · intro x hx
    have heq : W₂.filter (fun v => F.Adj x v) =
        W₂.filter (fun v => F₁₂.Adj x v ∧ ∀ k, good k x v) := by
      exact Finset.filter_congr fun v hv => hchar x hx v hv
    rw [heq]
    exact hdegree W₂ (fun v => F₁₂.Adj x v) (fun k v => good k x v)
      (hF₁₂.2.1 x hx).1 (hF₁₂.2.1 x hx).2 (hrow x hx)
  · intro v hv
    have heq : W₁.filter (fun x => F.Adj x v) =
        W₁.filter (fun x => F₁₂.Adj x v ∧ ∀ k, good k x v) := by
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro x hx
      simpa only [F.adj_comm v x, F₁₂.adj_comm v x] using hcharRight v hv x hx
    rw [heq]
    exact hdegree W₁ (fun x => F₁₂.Adj x v) (fun k x => good k x v)
      (hF₁₂.2.2 v hv).1 (hF₁₂.2.2 v hv).2 (hcol v hv)
NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity.lean_statement:
theorem NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity :
    ∀ {V K : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Fintype K]
      (F₁₂ : SimpleGraph V) (F₁₃ F₂₃ : K → SimpleGraph V)
      [DecidableRel F₁₂.Adj] [∀ k, DecidableRel (F₁₃ k).Adj]
      [∀ k, DecidableRel (F₂₃ k).Adj]
      (W₁ W₂ : Finset V) (W₃ : K → Finset V) (m : ℕ)
      (ε₀ η δ : ENNReal) (ε d₁₃ d₂₃ : K → ENNReal),
      (h₁₂ : Disjoint W₁ W₂) →
      (∀ k, Disjoint W₁ (W₃ k) ∧ Disjoint W₂ (W₃ k)) →
      W₁.card = m → W₂.card = m →
      (∀ k, (W₃ k).card + 1 = m ∨ (W₃ k).card = m ∨ (W₃ k).card = m + 1) →
      ε₀ ≤ η → (∀ k, ε k ≤ 1 ∧ 2 * (ε k) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ η) →
      ε₀ + ∑ k, (ε k) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ η →
      ε₀ + 2 * ∑ k, ε k ≤ η →
      (∀ k, 2 * ε k < d₁₃ k ∧ 2 * ε k < d₂₃ k) →
      (∀ k, d₁₃ k ≤ 1 ∧ d₂₃ k ≤ 1) →
      SuperRegularPair F₁₂ W₁ W₂ ε₀ δ →
      (∀ k, SuperRegularPair (F₁₃ k) W₁ (W₃ k) (ε k) (d₁₃ k)) →
      (∀ k, SuperRegularPair (F₂₃ k) W₂ (W₃ k) (ε k) (d₂₃ k)) →
      let F := SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph F₁₂ F₁₃ F₂₃ W₁ W₂ h₁₂ W₃ ε d₁₃ d₂₃
      letI : DecidableRel F.Adj := Classical.decRel _
      SuperRegularPair F W₁ W₂ η δ := by
NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity.name: NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity
NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Call the retained graph $F$.  Its defining relation makes it a subgraph of
$F'_{12}$ supported on $W_1\times W_2$.

Fix $x\in W_1$ and $k\in K$, and put
$S=N_{F_{13}^k}(x)\cap W_3^k$.  Super-regularity gives
$|S|=(d_{13}^k\pm\varepsilon_k)|W_3^k|$ and
$|S|>\varepsilon_k|W_3^k|$, since $2\varepsilon_k<d_{13}^k$.
Regularity of $F_{23}^k[W_2,W_3^k]$ implies that fewer than
$\varepsilon_k|W_2|$ vertices of $W_2$ have degree into $S$ below
$(d_{23}^k-\varepsilon_k)|S|$, and fewer than that many have degree above
$(d_{23}^k+\varepsilon_k)|S|$: either contrary exceptional set, together
with $S$, would violate regularity.  Every remaining $v$ therefore has
\[
 |N_{F_{13}^k}(x)\cap N_{F_{23}^k}(v)\cap W_3^k|
 =(d_{13}^kd_{23}^k\pm2\varepsilon_k)|W_3^k|,
\]
using only that both densities are at most one.  Thus the $k$th test deletes
at most $2\varepsilon_k|W_2|$ partners of $x$.  The symmetric argument for
fixed $v\in W_2$ deletes at most $2\varepsilon_k|W_1|$ partners.  Summing
over $k$, and then using
$\varepsilon_0+2\sum_k\varepsilon_k\leq\eta$, converts the original
$(\delta\pm\varepsilon_0)$ degree windows into
$(\delta\pm\eta)$ windows on both sides.  Notice that no conversion between
$m$ and $|W_3^k|$ occurred.

For regularity, take $U\subseteq W_1$ and $Z\subseteq W_2$ with
$|U|>\eta|W_1|$ and $|Z|>\eta|W_2|$.  For fixed $k$, apply
\noderef{OneIndexBadPairCounting} to the two super-regular pairs with third
part $W_3^k$.  Its proof and statement normalize the two endpoint sets by
$|W_1|=|W_2|=m$ and all third-part degrees by the actual $|W_3^k|$; hence
the hypothesis $2\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}\leq\eta$ shows that at most a
$\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}$ proportion of $U\times Z$ fails the $k$th displayed
test.  A union bound gives
\[
 0\leq d_{F'_{12}}(U,Z)-d_F(U,Z)
 \leq\sum_k\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}.
\]
Apply \noderef{RegularityAfterDensityLoss} with this last sum as the density
loss.  Its hypotheses are exactly $\varepsilon_0\leq\eta$ and
$\varepsilon_0+\sum_k\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}\leq\eta$, so $F$ is
$(\eta,\delta)$-regular.  Together with the two degree calculations this is
precisely $(\eta,\delta)$-super-regularity.
\end{proof}
NearEqualVaryingGoodEdgeSuperRegularity.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Near-equal varying-error simultaneous good-edge retention]
Let $W_1,W_2$ be disjoint sets of size $m$, and let a finite set $K$ index
sets $W_3^k$ with $|W_3^k|\in\{m-1,m,m+1\}$, each disjoint from $W_1,W_2$.
Suppose $F'_{12}[W_1,W_2]$ is $(\varepsilon_0,\delta)$-super-regular and,
for every $k$, the pairs $F_{13}^k[W_1,W_3^k]$ and
$F_{23}^k[W_2,W_3^k]$ are $(\varepsilon_k,d_{13}^k)$- and
$(\varepsilon_k,d_{23}^k)$-super-regular. Assume
$\varepsilon_k\leq1$, $2\varepsilon_k<d_{13}^k,d_{23}^k\leq1$, and
\[
 \varepsilon_0\leq\eta,\qquad2\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}\leq\eta,
 \qquad \varepsilon_0+\sum_k\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}\leq\eta,
 \qquad \varepsilon_0+2\sum_k\varepsilon_k\leq\eta.
\]
Retain an edge $xv$ of $F'_{12}$ precisely when, for every $k$,
\[
 |N_{F_{13}^k}(x)\cap N_{F_{23}^k}(v)\cap W_3^k|
 =(d_{13}^kd_{23}^k\pm2\varepsilon_k)|W_3^k|.
\]
Then the retained graph on $(W_1,W_2)$ is $(\eta,\delta)$-super-regular.
Every displayed window is normalized by the actual part $W_3^k$.
\end{lemma}

let q : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x ^ 2 / 2 - Real.exp x + 1 + x
  have hd (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt q (x + 1 - Real.exp x) x := by
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 2).div_const 2).sub
      (Real.hasDerivAt_exp x)).add_const 1 |>.add (hasDerivAt_id x) using 1
    simp
    ring
  have hanti : Antitone q := antitone_of_hasDerivAt_nonpos hd (by
    intro x
    change x + 1 - Real.exp x ≤ 0
    have := Real.add_one_le_exp x
    linarith)
  have h := hanti hl
  simp only [q, Real.exp_zero] at h
  nlinarith

NegativeExponentialQuadraticBound.name: NegativeExponentialQuadraticBound
NegativeExponentialQuadraticBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $q(x)=x^2/2-e^x+1+x$. This function is differentiable on the
real line and $q'(x)=x+1-e^x$. The elementary exponential tangent
inequality $1+x\le e^x$ gives $q'(x)\le0$ for every real $x$.
The mean value theorem therefore makes $q$ antitone on the real line.
Since $\lambda\le0$, $q(\lambda)\ge q(0)=0$. Expanding this last
inequality gives the asserted bound.
\end{proof}

\[
 e^\lambda-1-\lambda\le\lambda^2/2.
\]
\end{helper}

    exact (ENNReal.sub_eq_of_eq_add_rev' ENNReal.one_ne_top hsum.symm).symm
  have hpow : (1 - a) ^ n ≤ 1 :=
    pow_le_one₀ (zero_le _) tsub_le_self
  have hfail (k : ι) : μ.toOuterMeasure (G k)ᶜ ≤ (1 - a) ^ n := by
    rw [hcompl]
    calc
      1 - μ.toOuterMeasure (G k) ≤ 1 - (1 - (1 - a) ^ n) :=
        tsub_le_tsub_left (hmap k) 1
      _ = (1 - a) ^ n := ENNReal.sub_sub_cancel ENNReal.one_ne_top hpow
  have hbad : μ.toOuterMeasure Eᶜ ≤ (2 : ENNReal)⁻¹ := by
    calc
      μ.toOuterMeasure Eᶜ = μ.toOuterMeasure (⋃ k, (G k)ᶜ) := by
        change μ.toOuterMeasure (⋂ k, G k)ᶜ = _
        rw [Set.compl_iInter]
      _ ≤ ∑ k, μ.toOuterMeasure (G k)ᶜ :=
        MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion_fintype_le μ.toOuterMeasure _
      _ ≤ ∑ _k : ι, (1 - a) ^ n := Finset.sum_le_sum fun k _ => hfail k

        mul_le_mul_right' (by exact_mod_cast hcard) _

    ENNReal.sub_eq_of_eq_add_rev' ENNReal.one_ne_top ENNReal.inv_two_add_inv_two.symm

    calc
      (2 : ENNReal)⁻¹ = 1 - (2 : ENNReal)⁻¹ := hhalf.symm

    by_contra h

        (Set.disjoint_left.2 fun σ hσ hσE => h ⟨σ, hσE, hσ⟩)

theorem OneClusterExtension :

      SuperRegularPair F₁₂ W₁ W₂ ε₁₂ d₁₂ →

        let μ := μ₀.map Subtype.val
        VertexSpreadOn μ (C / (2 * n)) Set.univ →
        (∀ k,
          1 - (1 - a) ^ n ≤ μ₀.toOuterMeasure {σ |
            letI : DecidableRel
                (MatchingInducedGraph (F₁₃ k) (F₂₃ k) W₁ W₂ (W₃ k) σ).Adj :=
              Classical.decRel _
            let L : Finset (W₁ ⊕ W₃ k) := Finset.univ.image Sum.inl
            let R : Finset (W₁ ⊕ W₃ k) := Finset.univ.image Sum.inr
            SuperRegularPair
              (MatchingInducedGraph (F₁₃ k) (F₂₃ k) W₁ W₂ (W₃ k) σ)
              L R (εOut k) (d₁₃ k * d₂₃ k)}) →
        ∃ E : Set (W₁ → W₂),

            letI : DecidableRel

              Classical.decRel _
            let L : Finset (W₁ ⊕ W₃ k) := Finset.univ.image Sum.inl
            let R : Finset (W₁ ⊕ W₃ k) := Finset.univ.image Sum.inr

              (MatchingInducedGraph (F₁₃ k) (F₂₃ k) W₁ W₂ (W₃ k) σ)
              L R (εOut k) (d₁₃ k * d₂₃ k)) ∧

OneClusterExtension.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $B_k=E_k^c$. The map from the perfect-matching subtype to maps
$W_1\to W_2$ is injective and $\mu$ is, by definition, the pushforward of
$\mu_0$ along this map. Moreover, membership in $E_k$ is the same predicate
before and after forgetting the perfect-matching proof. Hence the assumed
$\mu_0$ bound gives $\mu(E_k)\geq1-(1-a)^n$, and therefore
$\mu(B_k)\leq(1-a)^n$, for every $k$. Since $K$ is finite, the union bound gives
\[
 \mu(E^c)=\mu\Bigl(\bigcup_{k\in K}B_k\Bigr)
 \leq\sum_{k\in K}\mu(B_k)
 \leq |K|(1-a)^n
 \leq\Delta(1-a)^n\leq\tfrac12.
\]
Consequently $\mu(E)\geq1/2$.  In particular $E$ has positive probability, so it contains an element of the finite support of $\mu$ and the conditional distribution is defined.

Apply \noderef{VertexSpreadConditioning} directly to the assumed $(C/(2n))$-vertex-spread law, with $q=C/(2n)$ and $p=1/2$.  Since
\[
 \frac{C/(2n)}{1/2}=\frac Cn,
\]
that lemma shows that the conditional law is $(C/n)$-vertex-spread because the hypothesis $C/n\leq1$ is exactly its required parameter-range inequality.  By the definition of $E$, every matching in the support of this conditional law makes all the graphs $A^k_\sigma$ simultaneously $(\varepsilon',d_{13}^kd_{23}^k)$-super-regular.  Thus conditioning preserves all the simultaneous good-event conclusions while incurring only the stated factor-two spread loss.
\end{proof}
OneClusterExtension.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[One-cluster extension]
Let $F_{12}$ be an $(\varepsilon_{12},d_{12})$-super-regular graph between equal parts $W_1,W_2$ of size $n$, and let $K$ index at most $\Delta$ future neighbor clusters $W_3^k$. For every $k\in K$, suppose $(F_{12},F_{13}^k,F_{23}^k)$ is a near-equal $(\varepsilon_{\rm in}(k),d_{12},d_{13}^k,d_{23}^k)$-regular triplet in the sense of \noderef{NearEqualRegularTriplet}; thus $|W_3^k|\in\{n-1,n,n+1\}$ and all conditions involving $W_3^k$ use its actual cardinality. Assume that $F_{12}$ has a perfect matching. Let $\mu_0$ be the uniform law on its perfect matchings and let $\mu$ be the pushforward law after forgetting the proof that a map is a perfect matching. Assume:
\[
 |K|\leq\Delta,\qquad \Delta(1-a)^n\leq\tfrac12,
 \qquad 0<\varepsilon_{12},\quad4\varepsilon_{12}<d_{12}\leq1,
 \qquad C/n\leq1,
\]
that $\mu$ is $(C/(2n))$-vertex-spread, and that for every $k$ the Four Graphs good event
\[
 E_k=\{\sigma:A^k_\sigma\text{ is }(\varepsilon_{\rm out}(k),d_{13}^kd_{23}^k)\text{-super-regular}\}
\]
has $\mu_0$-probability at least $1-(1-a)^n$. Then the simultaneous good event $E=\bigcap_{k\in K}E_k$, viewed as an event of maps $W_1\to W_2$, has $\mu$-probability at least $1/2$, and the law of $\sigma$ conditioned on $E$ is $(C/n)$-vertex-spread. Here each $A^k_\sigma$ is \noderef{MatchingInducedGraph}. No comparison between $\varepsilon_{12}$ and the values $\varepsilon_{\rm in}(k)$ is assumed.
\end{lemma}

        (((U.product W).filter fun p =>
          ¬ ((d₁₃ * d₂₃ - 2 * ε) * W₃.card ≤
              (((W₃.filter fun z => F₁₃.Adj p.1 z ∧ F₂₃.Adj p.2 z).card : ENNReal)) ∧

OneIndexBadPairCounting.name: OneIndexBadPairCounting
OneIndexBadPairCounting.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $s=\sqrt\varepsilon$ and $k=|W_3|$. The strict size
assumptions imply $|U|,|W|>0$, since $2sn\geq0$. In particular,
the denominator $|U||W|$ in the asserted proportion is positive.
If $W_3=\varnothing$, every common-neighborhood cardinality is zero.
Both endpoints $(d_{13}d_{23}-2\varepsilon)k$ and
$(d_{13}d_{23}+2\varepsilon)k$ are also zero, so every pair satisfies
the window. There are no bad pairs, and the asserted proportion is
$0\leq s$. Henceforth assume $W_3\ne\varnothing$, so $k>0$.

All three parameters are finite, because they lie between zero and one.
We may therefore do ordinary real arithmetic, interpreting a subtraction
in the nonnegative-reals statements as
$(a-b)_+=\max\{a-b,0\}$. Fix $x\in W_1$, put
$S=N_{F_{13}}(x)\cap W_3$, and write $a=|S|$. The degree clause of
\noderef{SuperRegularPair} gives
\[
 (d_{13}-\varepsilon)_+k\leq a\leq(d_{13}+\varepsilon)k,
 \qquad 0\leq a\leq k.
\]
In particular, the signed real inequalities
$d_{13}k-\varepsilon k\leq a\leq d_{13}k+\varepsilon k$
hold, including when $d_{13}<\varepsilon$.

First suppose $a>\varepsilon k$. For $v\in W_2$, write
$c_v=|N_{F_{23}}(v)\cap S|$, and define the two exceptional sets
\[
 T_- =\{v\in W_2:c_v<(d_{23}-\varepsilon)_+a\},\qquad
 T_+ =\{v\in W_2:c_v>(d_{23}+\varepsilon)a\}.
\]
We show $|T_-|\leq\varepsilon n$. Otherwise
$|T_-|>\varepsilon|W_2|$, and both $T_-$ and $S$ exceed the
thresholds in \noderef{RegularPair}, which applies to $F_{23}$ by
\noderef{SuperRegularPair}. Both sets are nonempty. By the ordered
edge-count definition in \noderef{PairDensity},
\[
 d_{F_{23}}(T_-,S)
 =\frac{\sum_{v\in T_-}c_v}{|T_-|a}
 <(d_{23}-\varepsilon)_+.
\]
Here the strict inequality follows by summing the defining strict
inequalities over the nonempty set $T_-$ and dividing by the positive
number $|T_-|a$. This contradicts the regularity lower bound.
The same reasoning for $T_+$ gives $|T_+|\leq\varepsilon n$:
if its size were larger, its density with $S$ would be strictly greater
than $d_{23}+\varepsilon$, contradicting the regularity upper bound.
These arguments remain valid for $\varepsilon=0$; if a lower-tail
endpoint is zero then that tail is empty because $c_v\geq0$.

For $v\notin T_-\cup T_+$ we have
$(d_{23}-\varepsilon)_+a\leq c_v\leq(d_{23}+\varepsilon)a$.
Together with $a\leq k$, the lower bound implies the following signed
real inequalities:
\[
 \begin{split}
 c_v&\geq d_{23}a-\varepsilon a
      \geq d_{23}a-\varepsilon k\\
    &\geq d_{13}d_{23}k-d_{23}\varepsilon k-\varepsilon k
      \geq(d_{13}d_{23}-2\varepsilon)k.
 \end{split}
\]
Since $c_v\geq0$ as well, this proves
$c_v\geq(d_{13}d_{23}-2\varepsilon)_+k$.
For the upper bound, similarly,
\[
 \begin{split}
 c_v&\leq d_{23}a+\varepsilon a
      \leq d_{23}a+\varepsilon k\\
    &\leq d_{13}d_{23}k+d_{23}\varepsilon k+\varepsilon k
      \leq(d_{13}d_{23}+2\varepsilon)k.
 \end{split}
\]
Both chains use $0\leq d_{23}\leq1$. Also,
$N_{F_{23}}(v)\cap S$ is exactly the common neighborhood in $W_3$.
Thus every bad partner of $x$ belongs to $T_-\cup T_+$, whose size
is at most $2\varepsilon n$.

Now suppose $a\leq\varepsilon k$. Combining this with the degree lower
bound gives $(d_{13}-\varepsilon)_+k\leq\varepsilon k$.
Since $k>0$, cancellation yields
$(d_{13}-\varepsilon)_+\leq\varepsilon$.
If $d_{13}\leq\varepsilon$ then $d_{13}\leq2\varepsilon$ directly;
otherwise the truncated difference is $d_{13}-\varepsilon$, and adding
$\varepsilon$ again gives $d_{13}\leq2\varepsilon$.
Consequently $d_{13}d_{23}\leq d_{13}\leq2\varepsilon$, so the lower
window endpoint is zero. Every $v\in W_2$ has
\[
 0\leq c_v\leq a\leq\varepsilon k
       \leq(d_{13}d_{23}+2\varepsilon)k.
\]
There are no bad partners in this case. We have therefore proved that
every row $x\in W_1$ has at most $2\varepsilon n$ bad partners.

For completeness, the column bound follows by the same two cases, fixing
$v\in W_2$ and taking $S'=N_{F_{23}}(v)\cap W_3$ instead.
Its degree bounds come from \noderef{SuperRegularPair} for $F_{23}$.
If $|S'|>\varepsilon k$, define the lower and upper exceptional sets
in $W_1$ using $(d_{13}-\varepsilon)_+|S'|$ and
$(d_{13}+\varepsilon)|S'|$; \noderef{RegularPair} for $F_{13}$,
with the density sum from \noderef{PairDensity}, bounds each by
$\varepsilon n$. The displayed window chains now have $d_{13}$
in place of the multiplier $d_{23}$ and give the same product window.
If $|S'|\leq\varepsilon k$, cancel the same positive $k$ in its
degree lower bound to obtain $d_{23}\leq2\varepsilon$, and every
intersection lies in the window. Thus every column also has at most
$2\varepsilon n$ bad partners.

Let $B$ denote the number of bad pairs in $U\times W$. Summing the row
bound over $x\in U$ (and restricting each row to $W$) gives
$B\leq2\varepsilon n|U|$. If $s=0$, then $\varepsilon=s^2=0$,
so $B=0$ and the proportion is zero. If $s>0$, then
$\varepsilon=s^2$ and the strict size bound for $W$ gives
\[
 2\varepsilon n= s(2sn)<s|W|.
\]
Dividing $B\leq2\varepsilon n|U|$ by the positive $|U||W|$
therefore gives
$B/(|U||W|)\leq2\varepsilon n/|W|<s$, proving the claimed
non-strict bound. The calculation retains the actual size $k$ throughout;
no equality $k=n$, nor any positive lower bound on $k$ beyond the
explicit nonempty branch, has been used.
\end{proof}
OneIndexBadPairCounting.title: OneIndexBadPairCounting

    Finset.sum_mul_sum, Finset.sum_product]
  calc
    _ = ∑ w ∈ W, ∑ u ∈ U, ∑ z ∈ W,
        (if P u w then 1 else 0) * (if P u z then 1 else 0) :=
      Finset.sum_comm

        (if P u w then 1 else 0) * (if P u z then 1 else 0) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro w hw
      exact Finset.sum_comm
    _ = _ := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro w hw
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

theorem OrderedTwoPathCount {A B : Type*} [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B]
    (U : Finset A) (W : Finset B) (P : A → B → Prop) [DecidableRel P] :
    (∑ u ∈ U, (W.filter fun w => P u w).card ^ 2) =
      ∑ z ∈ W ×ˢ W, (U.filter fun u => P u z.1 ∧ P u z.2).card := by
OrderedTwoPathCount.name: OrderedTwoPathCount
OrderedTwoPathCount.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Both sides count triples $(u,w,z)\in U\times W\times W$ for which
$P(u,w)$ and $P(u,z)$ hold. For a fixed $u$, the two endpoints can be
chosen independently from its related elements of $W$, giving the square
on the left; no distinctness condition is imposed. For a fixed ordered
pair $(w,z)$, the allowed middle elements are exactly the elements counted
on the right. Equivalently, expand both sides as the finite sum of
$\mathbf1_{P(u,w)}\mathbf1_{P(u,z)}$ over all such triples and interchange
the three finite summations. This proves the identity, including the
diagonal terms.
\end{proof}
OrderedTwoPathCount.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Counting ordered two-edge paths]
Let $U\subseteq A$ and $W\subseteq B$ be finite sets and let $P$ be a relation
between $A$ and $B$. Then
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}|\{w\in W:P(u,w)\}|^2
 =\sum_{(w,z)\in W^2}|\{u\in U:P(u,w)\text{ and }P(u,z)\}|.
\]
The ordered pairs on the right include pairs with $w=z$.
\end{lemma}
OrderedTwoPathCount.title: OrderedTwoPathCount

PaddedSource.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}
For a blow-up instance with source clusters $X_i$ and host clusters $V_i$, its padded source vertex set is
\[
 V(H)^+=V(H)\sqcup\coprod_{i\in[r]}[\,|V_i|-|X_i|\,].
\]
The second summand consists of dummy vertices, with exactly $|V_i|-|X_i|$ dummy vertices assigned to cluster $i$.  The difference is nonnegative by the capacity clause in \noderef{BlowUpInstance}.

PairDensity.lean_statement:
noncomputable def PairDensity {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)

PairDensity.name: PairDensity
PairDensity.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}
For a simple graph $G$ on an arbitrary vertex type and arbitrary finite vertex subsets $U,W$, let $e_G(U,W)$ be the number of ordered pairs $(u,w)\in U\times W$ with $uw\in E(G)$.  The sets may overlap.  The density of the ordered pair is
\[
d_G(U,W)=\frac{e_G(U,W)}{|U||W|},
\]
with value $0$ when either part is empty.  The regularity applications in the paper specialize this definition to disjoint parts.
\end{definition}

    exact ENNReal.div_ne_top (by simp) hden

    simp only [PairDensity, ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_mul,
      ENNReal.toReal_natCast]

      (((A.product B).filter fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) /

theorem PairDensityReal {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (A B : Finset V)
    (hA : A.Nonempty) (hB : B.Nonempty) :
    PairDensity G A B ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (PairDensity G A B).toReal = (G.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) ∧
      (G.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) =
        (((A.product B).filter fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) /
          ((A.card : ℝ) * (B.card : ℝ)) := by
PairDensityReal.name: PairDensityReal
PairDensityReal.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Nonemptiness makes both cardinalities positive, so their product is
nonzero. The finite numerator divided by this nonzero finite denominator
is finite. Applying the real-value map to the quotient in
\noderef{PairDensity} gives the displayed real quotient. Expanding
Mathlib's edge-density definition gives the same filtered Cartesian
product and the same denominator, first in $\mathbb Q$ and then in
$\mathbb R$. Thus the two densities agree.
\end{proof}
PairDensityReal.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Real density adapter]
For a simple graph $G$ and nonempty finite vertex sets $A,B$, the value
$\operatorname{PairDensity}(G,A,B)$ of \noderef{PairDensity} is finite.
Its real value equals Mathlib's rational edge density, viewed in $\mathbb R$,
and both equal
\[
 \frac{|\{(a,b)\in A\times B:G(a,b)\}|}{|A||B|}.
\]
\end{lemma}
