PartialEmbedding.lean_proof:
classical
  intro Δ d hd hd1
  let a := d * (d / 2) ^ Δ
  obtain ⟨d₀', hd₀', hd₀'d, hp⟩ := PartialEmbeddingParameters Δ d hd hd1
  refine ⟨d₀', hd₀', hd₀'d, ?_⟩
  intro d' hd' hd'₀
  obtain ⟨ε₀, hε₀, hε₀top, hp⟩ := hp d' hd' hd'₀
  refine ⟨ε₀, hε₀, hε₀top, ?_⟩
  intro ε hε hε₀'
  obtain ⟨C₀, hC₀, hC₀top, hp⟩ := hp ε hε hε₀'
  refine ⟨C₀, hC₀, hC₀top, ?_⟩
  intro C hC hCtop
  obtain ⟨n₀, hp⟩ := hp C hC hCtop
  refine ⟨n₀, ?_⟩
  intro n hn₀
  obtain ⟨hn, hεhalf, hεd, ha, had, hpower, hthreshold, hloss,
    hd'a, hCa, hCtwo, hq, hrecip, hfallback⟩ := hp n hn₀
  intro r VH VG _ _ _ _ H G _ _ R _ B A _ hreg hdeg hR hsmall hhost hinit
  let q := C / n
  have hloss' : ε * (1 + ε) ≤ a / 2 := by
    calc
      ε * (1 + ε) = 1 * ε * (1 + ε) := by simp
      _ ≤ (Δ + 1 : ENNReal) * ε * (1 + ε) := by
        gcongr
        exact_mod_cast (Nat.le_add_left 1 Δ)
      _ ≤ a / 2 := hloss
  have hd'a' : d' ≤ a / 2 :=
    hd'a.trans (ENNReal.div_le_div le_rfl (by norm_num : (2 : ENNReal) ≤ 4))
  let Good : Finset VH → (VH → VG) → Prop := fun S f =>
    ∃ e : GreedyPartialEmbedding B A d ε n S, e.toFun = f
  have transfer : ∀ S f g, (∀ x ∈ S, f x = g x) → Good S f → Good S g := by
    intro S f g hfg he
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := he
    have heq : ∀ x ∈ S, e.toFun x = g x := fun x hx =>
      (congrFun he x).trans (hfg x hx)
    refine ⟨{
      toPartialCompatibleEmbedding := {
        toFun := g
        injOn := ?_
        map_adj := ?_
        compatible := ?_ }
      raw_bound := ?_ }, rfl⟩
    · intro x hx y hy hxy
      apply e.injOn hx hy
      rw [heq x hx, heq y hy]
      exact hxy
    · intro x y hx hy hxy
      rw [← heq x hx, ← heq y hy]
      exact e.map_adj hx hy hxy
    · intro x hx
      rw [← heq x hx]
      exact e.compatible x hx
    · intro x hx
      have hraw : RawCandidates B A S e.toFun x = RawCandidates B A S g x := by
        ext v
        simp only [RawCandidates, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨hv, he'⟩
          refine ⟨hv, ?_⟩
          intro y hy hxy
          rw [← heq y hy]
          exact he' y hy hxy
        · rintro ⟨hv, he'⟩
          refine ⟨hv, ?_⟩
          intro y hy hxy
          rw [heq y hy]
          exact he' y hy hxy
      rw [← hraw]
      exact e.raw_bound x hx
  have hlocal : ∀ S f g, (∀ x ∈ S, f x = g x) → (Good S f ↔ Good S g) := by
    intro S f g hfg
    exact ⟨transfer S f g hfg, transfer S g f (fun x hx => (hfg x hx).symm)⟩
  have hzero : ∀ f, Good ∅ f := by
    intro f
    refine ⟨{
      toPartialCompatibleEmbedding := {
        toFun := f
        injOn := by simp
        map_adj := by simp
        compatible := by simp }
      raw_bound := ?_ }, rfl⟩
    intro x hx
    simpa [RawCandidates, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card'] using hinit x
  let T : VH → Finset VG := fun x =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = B.sourceCluster x
  have hTcard (x : VH) : (T x).card =
      Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = B.sourceCluster x} := by
    simp [T, Fintype.card_subtype]
  have hTbound (x : VH) : 0 < (T x).card ∧ 1 / ((T x).card : ENNReal) ≤ q := by
    apply hfallback
    simpa only [hTcard] using (hhost (B.sourceCluster x)).1
  have hstep : ∀ S f z, z ∉ S → Good S f →
      ∃ L : Finset VG, L.Nonempty ∧ 1 / (L.card : ENNReal) ≤ q ∧
        ∀ v ∈ L, Good (insert z S) (Function.update f z v) := by
    intro S f z hz he
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := he
    obtain ⟨L, hL, hLsize, hLstep⟩ := GreedyPartialEmbeddingStep Δ d ε a n hn ha
      hpower hthreshold hloss B A hreg hdeg hsmall (fun i => (hhost i).2) S e z hz
    refine ⟨L, hL, hrecip L.card hLsize, ?_⟩
    intro v hv
    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hLstep v hv
    exact ⟨g, hg.trans (congrArg (fun f => Function.update f z v) he)⟩
  have law (X : Finset VH) : ∃ μ : PMF {f : VH → VG // Good X f},
      VertexSpreadOn (μ.map Subtype.val) q Set.univ :=
    FiniteGreedySpreadLaw q hq T (fun x => Finset.card_pos.mp (hTbound x).1)
      (fun x => (hTbound x).2) Good hlocal hzero hstep X
  constructor
  · obtain ⟨μ, hμ⟩ := law Finset.univ
    let pack : {f : VH → VG // Good Finset.univ f} →
        {φ : SimpleGraph.Copy H G // CompatibleEmbedding B A φ} := fun u =>
      let e := Classical.choose u.property
      ⟨{
         toHom := {
           toFun := e.toFun
           map_rel' := fun hxy => e.map_adj (Finset.mem_univ _) (Finset.mem_univ _) hxy }
         injective' := fun x y hxy => e.injOn (Finset.mem_univ x) (Finset.mem_univ y) hxy },
       fun x => e.compatible x (Finset.mem_univ x)⟩
    refine ⟨μ.map pack, ?_⟩
    have hm : (μ.map pack).map (fun φ x => φ.1 x) = μ.map Subtype.val := by
      rw [PMF.map_comp]
      congr 1
      funext u
      exact Classical.choose_spec u.property
    rw [hm]
    exact hμ
  · intro X
    obtain ⟨μ, hμ⟩ := law X
    let pack : {f : VH → VG // Good X f} →
        {f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X // ∀ x, x ∉ X →
          d' * n ≤ Set.ncard {v : VG | (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x v}} := fun u =>
      let e := Classical.choose u.property
      ⟨e.toPartialCompatibleEmbedding,
       GreedyPartialEmbeddingReserve Δ d ε a d' n hpower hloss' hd'a' B A hdeg hsmall
         (fun i => (hhost i).2) X e⟩
    refine ⟨μ.map pack, ?_⟩
    have hm : (μ.map pack).map (fun f => f.val.toFun) = μ.map Subtype.val := by
      rw [PMF.map_comp]
      congr 1
      funext u
      exact Classical.choose_spec u.property
    rw [hm]
    exact hμ
PartialEmbedding.lean_statement:
theorem PartialEmbedding :
    ∀ (Δ : ℕ) (d : ENNReal), 0 < d → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ d₀' : ENNReal, 0 < d₀' ∧ d₀' < d ∧
      ∀ d' : ENNReal, 0 < d' → d' ≤ d₀' →
        ∃ ε₀ : ENNReal, 0 < ε₀ ∧ ε₀ < ⊤ ∧
        ∀ ε : ENNReal, 0 < ε → ε ≤ ε₀ →
          ∃ C₀ : ENNReal, 1 ≤ C₀ ∧ C₀ < ⊤ ∧
          ∀ C : ENNReal, C₀ ≤ C → C < ⊤ →
            ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
            ∀ {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
              [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
              {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG}
              [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
              {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} [DecidableRel R.Adj]
              (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
              [DecidableRel A.allowed],
              InstanceLowerRegular B ε d → H.maxDegree ≤ Δ → R.maxDegree ≤ Δ →
              (∀ i, (Fintype.card {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i} : ENNReal) ≤
                ε * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i}) →
              (∀ i, (1 - ε) * n ≤
                  Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} ∧
                (Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} : ENNReal) ≤
                  (1 + ε) * n) →
              (∀ x, d * n ≤ Set.ncard {v : VG | A.allowed x v}) →
              (∃ μ : PMF {φ : SimpleGraph.Copy H G // CompatibleEmbedding B A φ},
                VertexSpreadOn
                  (μ.map fun φ x => φ.1 x) (C / n) Set.univ) ∧
              (∀ X : Finset VH,
                ∃ μ : PMF {f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X //
                    ∀ x, x ∉ X →
                      d' * n ≤ Set.ncard
                        {v : VG | (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x v}},
                  VertexSpreadOn
                    (μ.map fun f => f.val.toFun) (C / n) Set.univ) := by
PartialEmbedding.name: PartialEmbedding
PartialEmbedding.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Apply \noderef{PartialEmbeddingParameters} to $\Delta,d$ and use its
$d'_0,\varepsilon_0,C_0,n_0$ in precisely the quantifier order in the
statement. Fix the subsequent parameters, $n\geq n_0$, and an instance
satisfying the hypotheses. Put $a=d(d/2)^\Delta$ and $q=C/n$.
The parameter lemma gives $n>0$, $q\leq1$, $0<a\leq d$,
$\varepsilon\leq1/2$, the power floor
$a\leq d(d-\varepsilon)^k$ for $k\leq\Delta$, and
\[
 \varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)<a,\quad
 (\Delta+1)\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)\leq a/2,\quad d'\leq a/4.
\]
Since $\Delta+1\geq1$, the loss bound also gives
$\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)\leq a/2$, and $d'\leq a/2$.
All parameter choices are independent of $r$ and the graphs.

For a total map $f:V(H)\to V(G)$ define $\mathrm{Good}(S,f)$ to mean
that $f$ is the underlying map of a greedy state on $S$ from
\noderef{GreedyPartialEmbedding}. We check the three invariant
hypotheses of the finite law construction explicitly.
First, goodness depends only on values on $S$. Indeed, injectivity
on $S$, edge preservation inside $S$, and compatibility on $S$ use
only those values by \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding}.
For an unembedded $x$, the raw set from \noderef{RawCandidates}
uses only images of vertices in $S$. Its cardinality is consequently
unchanged when the map is changed outside $S$, as is the exposure
count $|S\cap N_H(x)|$. Thus the raw-bound field of the greedy state
is unchanged too. This proves both directions of the locality
equivalence by transporting the state to the new total map.

Second, every total map is good on the empty set. The three partial
compatibility requirements are vacuous. The raw set is the original
candidate set, its exposure count is zero, and its raw bound is
exactly the assumed inequality $dn\leq|\{v:A(x,v)\}|$.

Third, let $z\notin S$ and let $f$ be good on $S$.
Apply \noderef{GreedyPartialEmbeddingStep} to a witnessing state.
Its hypotheses are the parameter inequalities above, host lower
regularity, the degree bound on $H$, source-cluster smallness, and
the upper host-size bound. It gives a nonempty legal set $L$ of
size at least $(a/2)n$, and for every $v\in L$ a good state on
$S\cup\{z\}$ with total map exactly $f[z\mapsto v]$.
The reciprocal-cardinality clause of
\noderef{PartialEmbeddingParameters} gives $1/|L|\leq q$.
In particular this step bounds bad rows by lower regularity and
removes occupied images within the single source cluster; it does
not introduce any loss depending on $|S|$ or $r$.

For each source vertex $u$, take the fallback set $T(u)=V_{c(u)}$.
The lower host-size hypothesis gives
$|T(u)|\geq(1-\varepsilon)n$. The other reciprocal-cardinality
clause of \noderef{PartialEmbeddingParameters} shows that $T(u)$
is nonempty and $1/|T(u)|\leq q$. We have now checked every
hypothesis of \noderef{FiniteGreedySpreadLaw}. For every prescribed
$X$ it supplies a PMF on total maps good on $X$ whose projected law
is $q$-vertex-spread on all of $V(G)$. Its proof uses the checked
uniform probabilities of Mathlib's \texttt{PMF.toOuterMeasure\_uniformOfFinset\_apply} and
the full joint-cylinder result of \noderef{VertexSpreadSequential}:
kernels have a spread bound even at zero-mass invalid prefixes, and
stored values outside $X$ are appended independently and uniformly
from $T(u)$, rather than deterministically fixed.

For each good map in this law choose a witnessing greedy state.
By \noderef{GreedyPartialEmbeddingReserve}, its underlying partial
compatible embedding has at least $d'n$ updated candidates for
every $x\notin X$. The hypotheses of that reserve lemma are the
power floor, $\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)\leq a/2$, $d'\leq a/2$,
the source degree bound, cluster smallness, and the upper host-size
bound, all established above. Moreover, completing stored values
outside $X$ cannot change the updated graph by
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCongruence}, since the maps agree on $X$.
Every candidate for $x$ lies in $V_{c(x)}$ by
\noderef{CandidacySystem}, so the restriction in
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster} removes no additional candidate
for this $x$.

Push the law forward to the subtype of partial compatible embeddings
with these reserve proofs. Choosing the witness and adding the
proofs does not change its underlying total map: by the definition
of goodness, that map is exactly the original good map. The
projection of the pushforward back to total maps is therefore the
original projected law. Every cylinder probability is identical,
giving the partial conclusion with full joint spread on total maps.

For the full conclusion apply the same finite-law construction with
$X=V(H)$. Every witnessing state is injective on the whole source,
preserves every source edge, and satisfies $A(x,f(x))$ for every $x$.
It therefore gives a graph copy which is compatible in the sense of
\noderef{CompatibleEmbedding}. Push forward to these compatible
copies. Once again the underlying total maps are unchanged, so
their projected law has the same cylinders and the same spread bound.

If the source is empty, the construction uses the unique empty map
and no fallback fiber, even if the host is empty. If $X$ is empty
but the source is not, only the independent completion is performed,
and the initial degree bound gives the reserve. When $\Delta=0$,
the exposure count is always zero and $a=d$; the parameter and
extension lemmas use $\Delta+1$, not division by $\Delta$, and
remain valid. Thus all stated endpoint cases are included.
\end{proof}
PartialEmbedding.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Partial embedding lemma]
For every $\Delta\in\mathbb N$ and $0<d\leq1$, there is $0<d'_0<d$ such that, for every $0<d'\leq d'_0$, there is a finite real $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$, there is a finite real $C_0\geq1$ such that, for every finite real $C\geq C_0$, there is $n_0\in\mathbb N$ with the following property for every integer $n\geq n_0$. All scalar parameters in this hierarchy are finite real numbers.

Let $(H,G,R,(X_i)_{i\in[r]},(V_i)_{i\in[r]},(A^i)_{i \in [r]})$ be a finite blow-up instance with candidacy graphs.  Suppose it is host-lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-regular in the sense of \noderef{InstanceLowerRegular}, $\Delta(H),\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$, $|X_i|\leq\varepsilon|V_i|$, and $(1-\varepsilon)n\leq|V_i|\leq(1+\varepsilon)n$ for every $i$.  Suppose also that every $x\in X_i$ has at least $dn$ candidates in $A^i$.

Then there is a probability distribution on compatible embeddings $\varphi:H\hookrightarrow G$ whose underlying maps are $(C/n)$-vertex-spread on the whole codomain $V(G)$ in the sense of \noderef{VertexSpreadOn}.  Moreover, for every $X\subseteq V(H)$ there is such a $(C/n)$-vertex-spread distribution on partial compatible embeddings $f:H[X]\hookrightarrow G$ for which every unembedded vertex $x$ has at least $d'n$ candidates in its restricted updated candidacy graph $A_f^i$ from \noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}, where $x\in X_i$.
\end{lemma}
PartialEmbedding.title: PartialEmbedding

PartialEmbeddingParameters.lean_proof:
lift d to ℝ≥0 using ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hd1
  norm_cast at hd hd1
  let a : ℝ≥0 := d * (d / 2) ^ Δ
  have ha : 0 < a := by dsimp [a]; positivity
  have ha_d : a ≤ d := by
    have hhalf : d / 2 ≤ 1 := by rify at hd1 ⊢; linarith
    exact (mul_le_mul_right (pow_le_one₀ (zero_le _) hhalf) d).trans_eq (mul_one d)
  have ha1 : a ≤ 1 := ha_d.trans hd1
  have hquarter : a / 4 < d := by
    have h : a / 4 < a := by rify at ha ⊢; linarith
    exact h.trans_le ha_d
  refine ⟨↑(a / 4), by exact_mod_cast (show 0 < a / 4 by positivity),
    by simpa [a] using (ENNReal.coe_lt_coe.mpr hquarter), ?_⟩
  intro d' hd' hd'a
  lift d' to ℝ≥0 using ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.coe_ne_top hd'a
  norm_cast at hd' hd'a
  let e : ℝ≥0 := min (1 / 2) (min (d / 2) (min (d' / 4) (a / (8 * (Δ + 1)))))
  have he : 0 < e := by dsimp [e]; positivity
  refine ⟨↑e, by exact_mod_cast he, ENNReal.coe_lt_top, ?_⟩
  intro ε hε hεe
  lift ε to ℝ≥0 using ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.coe_ne_top hεe
  norm_cast at hε hεe
  obtain ⟨hεhalf, hεd, hεd', hεa⟩ :
      ε ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ ε ≤ d / 2 ∧ ε ≤ d' / 4 ∧ ε ≤ a / (8 * (Δ + 1)) := by
    simpa only [e, le_min_iff] using hεe
  have hloss : (Δ + 1 : ℝ≥0) * ε ≤ a / 8 := by
    have h := (le_div_iff₀ (show (0 : ℝ≥0) < 8 * (Δ + 1) by positivity)).mp hεa
    rify at h ⊢
    nlinarith only [h]
  have hepsLoss : ε ≤ a / 8 := by
    have hD1 : (1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ Δ + 1 := by simp
    exact (le_mul_of_one_le_left (zero_le ε) hD1).trans hloss

    rify at hεhalf hepsLoss ha ⊢

  have htotal : (Δ + 1 : ℝ≥0) * ε * (1 + ε) ≤ a / 2 := by
    rify at hεhalf hloss ⊢
    have hprod := mul_le_mul hloss (show (1 : ℝ) + ε ≤ 3 / 2 by linarith)

    intro k hk
    have hbase : d / 2 ≤ d - ε := by
      exact le_tsub_of_add_le_left (by rify at hεd ⊢; linarith)
    have hhalf : d / 2 ≤ 1 := by rify at hd1 ⊢; linarith
    exact mul_le_mul_right ((pow_le_pow_of_le_one (zero_le _) hhalf hk).trans
      (pow_le_pow_left₀ (zero_le _) hbase k)) d
  let c : ℝ≥0 := max 1 (max (2 / a) (max (2 / d') (1 / ε)))
  have hc1 : 1 ≤ c := le_max_left _ _
  have hca : 2 / a ≤ c := (le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)
  have htwo : 2 ≤ 2 / a := (le_div_iff₀ ha).mpr (by simpa using mul_le_mul_right ha1 2)
  refine ⟨↑c, by exact_mod_cast hc1, ENNReal.coe_lt_top, ?_⟩
  intro C hC hCtop
  lift C to ℝ≥0 using hCtop.ne
  norm_cast at hC
  have hCa : 2 / a ≤ C := hca.trans hC
  have hC2 : 2 ≤ C := htwo.trans hCa
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := exists_nat_ge C
  refine ⟨max 1 m, ?_⟩
  intro n hn
  have hn1 : 1 ≤ n := (le_max_left _ _).trans hn
  have hnpos : 0 < n := by omega
  have hnN : (0 : ℝ≥0) < n := by exact_mod_cast hnpos
  have hCn : C ≤ n := hm.trans (by exact_mod_cast ((le_max_right 1 m).trans hn))
  have hlegal : ∀ t : ℕ, a / 2 * n ≤ (t : ℝ≥0) →
      1 / (t : ℝ≥0) ≤ C / n := by
    intro t ht
    have htN : (0 : ℝ≥0) < t := lt_of_lt_of_le (by positivity) ht
    have hCan : 2 ≤ C * a := (div_le_iff₀ ha).mp hCa
    have hmult : (n : ℝ≥0) ≤ C * t := by
      have h := mul_le_mul_right ht C
      rify at h hCan ⊢
      have h' := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hCan (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ n by positivity)
      nlinarith only [h, h']
    exact (div_le_div_iff₀ htN hnN).mpr (by simpa using hmult)
  have hfallback : ∀ t : ℕ, (1 - ε) * n ≤ (t : ℝ≥0) →
      0 < t ∧ 1 / (t : ℝ≥0) ≤ C / n := by
    intro t ht

      le_tsub_of_add_le_left (by rify at hεhalf ⊢; linarith)
    have htHalf : (n : ℝ≥0) / 2 ≤ t := by
      simpa [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm] using (mul_le_mul_left hhalf (n : ℝ≥0)).trans ht
    have htN : (0 : ℝ≥0) < t := lt_of_lt_of_le (by positivity) htHalf
    have htpos : 0 < t := by exact_mod_cast htN
    refine ⟨htpos, (div_le_div_iff₀ htN hnN).mpr ?_⟩
    have hmult := mul_le_mul_left hC2 (t : ℝ≥0)
    rify at htHalf hmult ⊢
    nlinarith only [htHalf, hmult]
  have haE : (↑a : ENNReal) = (↑d : ENNReal) * (↑d / 2) ^ Δ := by
    norm_cast
  change 0 < n ∧ _
  rw [← haE]
  refine ⟨hnpos, ?_, by exact_mod_cast hεd,
    by exact_mod_cast ha, by exact_mod_cast ha_d, ?_,
    by exact_mod_cast hstrict, by exact_mod_cast htotal, by exact_mod_cast hd'a,
    ?_, by exact_mod_cast hC2, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simpa only [ENNReal.coe_div (by norm_num : (2 : ℝ≥0) ≠ 0),
      ENNReal.coe_one, ENNReal.coe_ofNat] using ENNReal.coe_le_coe.mpr hεhalf
  · intro k hk
    exact_mod_cast hpower k hk
  · simpa only [ENNReal.coe_div ha.ne', ENNReal.coe_ofNat] using
      ENNReal.coe_le_coe.mpr hCa
  · change (↑C : ENNReal) / (↑(n : ℝ≥0)) ≤ 1
    rw [← ENNReal.coe_div (p := C) hnN.ne']
    exact_mod_cast ((div_le_one₀ hnN).mpr hCn)
  · intro t ht
    have ht' : a / 2 * n ≤ (t : ℝ≥0) := by exact_mod_cast ht
    have htN : (0 : ℝ≥0) < t := lt_of_lt_of_le (by positivity) ht'
    change (↑(1 : ℝ≥0) : ENNReal) / ↑(t : ℝ≥0) ≤ (↑C : ENNReal) / ↑(n : ℝ≥0)
    rw [← ENNReal.coe_div (p := 1) htN.ne', ← ENNReal.coe_div (p := C) hnN.ne']
    exact_mod_cast hlegal t ht'
  · intro t ht
    have ht' : (1 - ε) * n ≤ (t : ℝ≥0) := by exact_mod_cast ht
    obtain ⟨htpos, hbound⟩ := hfallback t ht'
    have htN : (0 : ℝ≥0) < t := by exact_mod_cast htpos
    refine ⟨htpos, ?_⟩
    change (↑(1 : ℝ≥0) : ENNReal) / ↑(t : ℝ≥0) ≤ (↑C : ENNReal) / ↑(n : ℝ≥0)
    rw [← ENNReal.coe_div (p := 1) htN.ne', ← ENNReal.coe_div (p := C) hnN.ne']
    exact_mod_cast hbound

open scoped NNReal

theorem PartialEmbeddingParameters (Δ : ℕ) (d : ENNReal) (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1) :
    let a := d * (d / 2) ^ Δ
    ∃ d₀' : ENNReal, 0 < d₀' ∧ d₀' < d ∧
      ∀ d' : ENNReal, 0 < d' → d' ≤ d₀' →
        ∃ ε₀ : ENNReal, 0 < ε₀ ∧ ε₀ < ⊤ ∧
        ∀ ε : ENNReal, 0 < ε → ε ≤ ε₀ →
          ∃ C₀ : ENNReal, 1 ≤ C₀ ∧ C₀ < ⊤ ∧
          ∀ C : ENNReal, C₀ ≤ C → C < ⊤ →
            ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
              0 < n ∧ ε ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ ε ≤ d / 2 ∧
              0 < a ∧ a ≤ d ∧
              (∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ Δ → a ≤ d * (d - ε) ^ k) ∧
              ε * (1 + ε) < a ∧
              (Δ + 1 : ENNReal) * ε * (1 + ε) ≤ a / 2 ∧
              d' ≤ a / 4 ∧ 2 / a ≤ C ∧ 2 ≤ C ∧ C / n ≤ 1 ∧
              (∀ t : ℕ, a / 2 * n ≤ (t : ENNReal) → 1 / (t : ENNReal) ≤ C / n) ∧
              (∀ t : ℕ, (1 - ε) * n ≤ (t : ENNReal) →
                0 < t ∧ 1 / (t : ENNReal) ≤ C / n) := by
PartialEmbeddingParameters.name: PartialEmbeddingParameters
PartialEmbeddingParameters.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The assumptions make $d$ finite. Put $a=d(d/2)^\Delta$ and $d'_0=a/4$.
Since $0<d/2\leq1/2$, its $\Delta$th power is positive and at most
one, including when $\Delta=0$. Thus $0<a\leq d\leq1$ and
$0<a/4<d$. Fix $0<d'\leq a/4$ and choose
\[
 \varepsilon_0=\min\{1/2,d/2,d'/4,a/(8(\Delta+1))\}.
\]
All four entries are positive and finite, so the same holds for their
minimum. For $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$, choose
\[
 C_0=\max\{1,2/a,2/d',1/\varepsilon\}.
\]
Its entries are finite and it is at least one. Given finite $C\geq C_0$,
choose an integer $n_0\geq\max\{1,C\}$, using the Archimedean
property on the finite real representative of $C$. Then $n\geq n_0$
implies $n>0$, $C\leq n$, and $C/n\leq1$.
Because $\varepsilon\leq d/2$, the truncated difference is the ordinary
nonnegative difference and satisfies $d-\varepsilon\geq d/2$.
For $k\leq\Delta$ we have
$(d-\varepsilon)^k\geq(d/2)^k\geq(d/2)^\Delta$; the second
inequality uses $0<d/2\leq1$. Multiplication by $d$ gives the power
bound. Also $1+\varepsilon\leq3/2$ and
$(\Delta+1)\varepsilon\leq a/8$, so
\[
 (\Delta+1)\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)\leq3a/16\leq a/2.
\]
Since $\Delta+1\geq1$, the same bound $3a/16$ holds for
$\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)$, and it is strictly less than $a$
because $a>0$. Finally $d'\leq a/4$ was imposed, $C\geq2/a$ follows
from $C\geq C_0$, and $a\leq1$ gives $2/a\geq2$.
For $t\geq(a/2)n$, the lower bound is positive, so reciprocation gives
$1/t\leq2/(an)\leq C/n$. For $t\geq(1-\varepsilon)n$, we have
$t\geq n/2>0$ because $\varepsilon\leq1/2$; consequently
$1/t\leq2/n\leq C/n$.
Every computation is on finite nonnegative real representatives, where
the field operations agree with extended nonnegative real operations
because every denominator used is positive. The choices depend only
on the parameters quantified earlier, never on a graph or on $r$.
\end{proof}
PartialEmbeddingParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Parameters for the partial-embedding construction]
Fix $\Delta\in\mathbb N$ and $0<d\leq1$, and put $a=d(d/2)^\Delta$.
There is $0<d'_0<d$ such that for every $0<d'\leq d'_0$ there is
$0<\varepsilon_0<\infty$ such that for every
$0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$ there is $1\leq C_0<\infty$
such that for every $C_0\leq C<\infty$ there is $n_0\in\mathbb N$
with the following inequalities for every integer $n\geq n_0$:
\[
\begin{gathered}
 n>0,\quad \varepsilon\leq\tfrac12,\quad\varepsilon\leq d/2,
 \quad 0<a\leq d,\\
 a\leq d(d-\varepsilon)_+^k\quad(0\leq k\leq\Delta),\\
 \varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)<a,\qquad
 (\Delta+1)\varepsilon(1+\varepsilon)\leq a/2,\\
 d'\leq a/4,\qquad 2/a\leq C,\qquad 2\leq C,
 \qquad C/n\leq1.
\end{gathered}
\]
In addition, every natural number $t\geq(a/2)n$ satisfies
$1/t\leq C/n$, and every natural number $t\geq(1-\varepsilon)_+n$
is positive and satisfies $1/t\leq C/n$.
All scalars are extended nonnegative reals; the displayed bounds force
them to be finite, and the subtraction is truncated subtraction.
\end{lemma}
PartialEmbeddingParameters.title: PartialEmbeddingParameters

PerfectMatchingBijectionBound.lean_proof:
classical
  let e : A ≃ B := Fintype.equivOfCardEq (by simpa using hA.trans hB.symm)
  let encode : {f : A → B // PerfectMatching G A B hAB f} → (A ≃ B) :=
    fun f => Equiv.ofBijective f.1 f.2.1
  have hi : Function.Injective encode := by
    intro f g h
    apply Subtype.ext
    exact congrArg (fun e : A ≃ B => e.toFun) h
  have hc := Fintype.card_le_of_injective encode hi
  rw [Fintype.card_equiv e, Fintype.card_coe, hA] at hc
  simpa only [← Nat.card_coe_set_eq, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] using hc

theorem PerfectMatchingBijectionBound
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (A B : Finset V) (hAB : Disjoint A B) (y : ℕ)
    (hA : A.card = y) (hB : B.card = y) :
    {f : A → B | PerfectMatching G A B hAB f}.ncard ≤ y.factorial := by
PerfectMatchingBijectionBound.name: PerfectMatchingBijectionBound
PerfectMatchingBijectionBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
By \noderef{PerfectMatching}, a perfect matching is a bijective function
from $A$ to $B$ satisfying the edge condition. Forgetting the edge condition
is injective into the set of bijections. Choose any bijection between the
two equal-size sets; composition identifies their bijections with the
permutations of $A$. A set of size $y$ has exactly $y!$ permutations:
successively choosing images gives $y(y-1)\cdots1$, and the empty set
has one permutation. Taking cardinalities proves the bound.
\end{proof}
PerfectMatchingBijectionBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[The elementary matching upper bound]
For finite disjoint vertex sets $A,B$ of equal size $y$ in a finite graph
$G$, the number of perfect matchings from $A$ to $B$ is at most $y!$.
This includes $y=0$.
\end{lemma}
PerfectMatchingBijectionBound.title: PerfectMatchingBijectionBound

classical

  let X (i : Fin r) := {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i}

    simpa only [F, Fintype.card_subtype] using (hcard i).2
  have hX (i : Fin r) : Fintype.card (X i) = n := by
    simpa only [X, Fintype.card_subtype] using (hcard i).1
  let e (i : Fin r) : F i ≃ X i := Fintype.equivOfCardEq ((hF i).trans (hX i).symm)
  let S (p : Fin r × Fin k) : Finset (F p.1) :=
    Finset.univ.filter fun v => σ (e p.1 v).val = p
  have hS (p : Fin r × Fin k) : (S p).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card := by
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun v _ => (e p.1 v).val)
    · intro v hv
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2⟩
    · intro v _ w _ h
      exact (e p.1).injective (Subtype.ext h)
    · intro x hx
      have hxσ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).2
      have hxB : B.sourceCluster x = p.1 := by rw [← hproj x, hxσ]
      refine ⟨(e p.1).symm ⟨x, hxB⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
      · simp [S, hxσ]
      · simp
  have hsum (i : Fin r) : ∑ j : Fin k, (S (i, j)).card = n := by
    have hsplit (j : Fin k) :
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).filter
          fun x => (σ x).2 = j) = (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = (i, j)) := by
      ext x
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Prod.ext_iff, hproj]
    simp_rw [hS, ← hsplit]
    simpa only [Finset.mem_univ, Finset.filter_true, (hcard i).1] using
      Finset.sum_card_fiberwise_eq_card_filter
        (Finset.univ.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i) Finset.univ
        (fun x => (σ x).2)

  have hnR : 0 < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hnpos
  have hkR : 0 < (k : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hkpos
  have hεfinite : ε ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hε1

  have heR : 0 < ε.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hε.ne' hεfinite

  have hsubcount (i : Fin r) (Q : VG → Prop) [DecidablePred Q] :

      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, v.property⟩,

    · intro v _ w _ h
      exact Subtype.ext h
    · intro v hv
      obtain ⟨hv, hQ⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hv
      exact ⟨⟨v, (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2⟩,
        Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hQ⟩, rfl⟩
  let C : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p q =>

theorem PrescribedHostPartitionSample {r k : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}

    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R)
    (A : CandidacySystem B) (σ : VH → Fin r × Fin k)
    (ε d : ENNReal) (n : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hn : 2 * k ≤ n)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hd : d ≤ 1)
    (hproj : ∀ x, (σ x).1 = B.sourceCluster x)
    (hcard : ∀ i,
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card = n ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).card = n)
    (hsize : ∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / k ∨
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / k + 1)
    (hhost : InstanceLowerSuperRegular B ε d)
    (hcand : CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d)
    (htail : 2 * (r : ℝ) * k * (r + 1) * n *
      Real.exp (-((ε.toReal / (2 * k)) ^ 2 /
        (2 * (1 + ε.toReal / (6 * k)))) * n) < 1) :
    ∃ f : VG → Fin r × Fin k,
      (∀ v, (f v).1 = B.hostCluster v) ∧
      (∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card) ∧
      (∀ x j, (d - 2 * ε) *
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = (B.sourceCluster x, j)).card : ENNReal) ≤
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun v =>
          f v = (B.sourceCluster x, j) ∧ A.allowed x v).card : ENNReal)) ∧
      (∀ v i j, R.Adj (B.hostCluster v) i →
        (d - 2 * ε) * ((Finset.univ.filter fun w => f w = (i, j)).card : ENNReal) ≤
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun w => f w = (i, j) ∧ G.Adj v w).card : ENNReal)) := by

PrescribedHostPartitionSample.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The source fibers partition each original source cluster, by the
projection identity, so their prescribed sizes $s_{ij}$ sum to $n$.
For each original host cluster choose a uniform permutation and cut
it into consecutive blocks of those sizes. This gives an ordered
partition of exactly the prescribed capacities. Each block is a
uniform $s_{ij}$-subset: for any fixed such subset the number of
permutations placing it in those positions is $s_{ij}!(n-s_{ij})!$,
independent of the subset. The finite product of these probability
spaces over the original clusters gives simultaneous partitions;
no independence between the subsequent failure events is claimed.

For a fixed source vertex, or a fixed host vertex and a supported
opposite original cluster, its neighbors form a fixed subset $T$
of that cluster, of size $t\leq n$. By
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}, \noderef{InstanceLowerSuperRegular},
and the degree clauses of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair},
$t\geq(d-\varepsilon)n$ if $d>\varepsilon$; otherwise the required
output lower bound is already zero. Tagged candidacy degrees equal
the ordinary relation counts, because the map $v\mapsto\mathrm{inr}(v)$
bijections the tested candidates and the opposite tagged neighbors.
The reversed branch of the symmetric relation graph introduces no
additional candidates, since its endpoints have opposite tags.

By \noderef{UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw}, the block intersection
count $Z$ has masses $H(n,s_{ij},t,x)$ for $0\leq x\leq n$.
The elementary floor bound $m\geq n/k-1\geq n/(2k)$ gives
$\varepsilon s_{ij}\geq an$. Apply
\noderef{HypergeometricTwoTail} with parameter $a>0$.
It bounds the probability that $|Z-s_{ij}t/n|>an$ by
$2\exp(-cn)$. The failure $Z<(d-2\varepsilon)s_{ij}$,
when its threshold is positive, implies
$s_{ij}t/n-Z>\varepsilon s_{ij}\geq an$; hence it is among
these strictly bounded deviations. If the threshold is nonpositive,
failure is impossible. This uses exactly the exponent in that
checked tail, not a sharper sampling estimate.

There are $rkn$ source/bin tests and at most $r^2kn$ directed
host/bin tests. The union bound makes their total failure
probability at most $2rk(r+1)n\exp(-cn)<1$.
Thus at least one outcome has no failure. Its partitions define
$f$ and give the asserted projection and capacities. Every host
test was imposed on every original vertex of the relevant cluster,
so the estimates remain available for vertices later reassigned.
If $r=0$, the two cluster maps force both vertex types empty; the
unique empty map proves the result without sampling.
All parameters are finite: $d\leq1$, $\varepsilon<1$.
Converting back to extended nonnegative reals gives the same counts
and inequalities when endpoints are nonnegative, and gives the
automatic zero lower bound otherwise.
\end{proof}
PrescribedHostPartitionSample.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous degree estimates for prescribed host capacities]
Let $k\geq1$, $n\geq2k$, $0<\varepsilon<1$, $d\leq1$.
Let $B$ be a blow-up instance with $r$ source and host clusters of
size $n$, and $A$ its candidacy system. Suppose the host and candidacy
pairs are lower $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular. Let
$\sigma:V(H)\to[r]\times[k]$ project to the original source map,
with each fiber of size $m$ or $m+1$, where $m=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$.
Put $a=\varepsilon/(2k)$ and
$c=a^2/(2(1+\varepsilon/(6k)))$, using finite real values.
If $2rk(r+1)n\exp(-cn)<1$, there is a host map
$f:V(G)\to[r]\times[k]$ projecting to the original host map and
with each fiber size exactly the corresponding $\sigma$-fiber size,
such that every original source vertex has at least
$(d-2\varepsilon)|f^{-1}(i,j)|$ candidates in every bin of its
original cluster $i$, and every original host vertex $v$ has at least
$(d-2\varepsilon)|f^{-1}(i,j)|$ neighbors in every bin of every
cluster $i$ adjacent to its original cluster in $R$.
Lower endpoints are truncated at zero.
\end{lemma}

theorem ProductPermutationIntersectionTail {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (F : I → Type*) [∀ i, Fintype (F i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (F i)]
    (i : I) (S T : Finset (F i)) (n : ℕ) (hcard : Fintype.card (F i) = n)
    (hn : 0 < n) (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    (((Finset.univ : Finset (∀ j, Equiv.Perm (F j))).filter
      fun (ω : ∀ j, Equiv.Perm (F j)) =>
        a * n < |(((S.image (ω i)) ∩ T).card : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ) * T.card / n|).card : ℝ) /
        (Fintype.card (∀ j, Equiv.Perm (F j)) : ℝ) ≤

ProductPermutationIntersectionTail.name: ProductPermutationIntersectionTail
ProductPermutationIntersectionTail.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
By \noderef{ProductPermutationSubsetLaw}, the fraction on the left is
the fraction of $|S|$-subsets $U$ of $F_i$ for which
$\bigl||U\cap T|-|S||T|/n\bigr|>an$.
The integer $|U\cap T|$ lies between $0$ and $n$, since
$U\cap T\subseteq T\subseteq F_i$. Partition this event according
to that integer $x$. By \noderef{UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw},
the fraction of all $|S|$-subsets giving the value $x$ is
$H(n,|S|,|T|,x)$. The required fraction is therefore exactly the sum
of these masses over $0\leq x\leq n$ with
$|x-|S||T|/n|>an$. Both subset sizes are at most $n$.
Applying \noderef{HypergeometricTwoTail} with these sizes and the
positive parameter $a$ bounds that sum by the displayed quantity.
All events use the original product-permutation space; no independence
of intersection counts is asserted or needed.
\end{proof}
ProductPermutationIntersectionTail.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Intersection tails for product-permutation blocks]
Let $I$ be finite and let $F_j$ be finite sets. Fix $i\in I$ with
$|F_i|=n>0$, subsets $S,T\subseteq F_i$, and a real number $a>0$.
For $\Omega=\prod_{j\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(F_j)$, one has
\[
\frac{|\{\omega\in\Omega:
 \bigl||\omega_i(S)\cap T|-|S||T|/n\bigr|>an\}|}{|\Omega|}
\leq 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{a^2n}{2(1+a/3)}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

        τ.apply_symm_apply ω⟩

  have htotal : Fintype.card Ω = K.card * c := by
    calc
      _ = ∑ U ∈ K, ((Finset.univ : Finset Ω).filter fun ω => b ω = U).card := by
        simpa using (Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
          (s := (Finset.univ : Finset Ω)) (t := K) (f := b) (fun ω _ => hb ω))
      _ = K.card * c := Finset.sum_const_nat hfiber
  have hevent : ((Finset.univ : Finset Ω).filter fun ω => P (b ω)).card =
      (K.filter P).card * c := by
    calc
      _ = ∑ U ∈ K.filter P,
          ((Finset.univ : Finset Ω).filter fun ω => b ω = U).card := by
        rw [Finset.sum_card_fiberwise_eq_card_filter]
        congr 1
        ext ω
        simp [hb]
      _ = (K.filter P).card * c :=
        Finset.sum_const_nat (fun U hU => hfiber U (Finset.mem_filter.mp hU).1)
  change _ / (Fintype.card Ω : ℝ) = _
  rw [hevent, htotal, Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_mul]
  exact mul_div_mul_right _ _ (by exact_mod_cast hc.ne' : (c : ℝ) ≠ 0)

open scoped BigOperators
open scoped Classical

theorem ProductPermutationSubsetLaw {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (F : I → Type*) [∀ i, Fintype (F i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (F i)]
    (i : I) (S : Finset (F i)) (P : Finset (F i) → Prop) :
    (((Finset.univ : Finset (∀ j, Equiv.Perm (F j))).filter
      fun (ω : ∀ j, Equiv.Perm (F j)) => P (S.image (ω i))).card : ℝ) /
        (Fintype.card (∀ j, Equiv.Perm (F j)) : ℝ) =
    ((((Finset.univ : Finset (F i)).powersetCard S.card).filter P).card : ℝ) /
      (((Finset.univ : Finset (F i)).powersetCard S.card).card : ℝ) := by
ProductPermutationSubsetLaw.name: ProductPermutationSubsetLaw
ProductPermutationSubsetLaw.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $b(\omega)=\omega_i(S)$ and let $K$ be the family of $|S|$-subsets
of $F_i$. Every $b(\omega)$ belongs to $K$. Put
$c=|\{\omega:b(\omega)=S\}|$, which is positive because the identity
permutation in every coordinate is one such outcome.
For $U\in K$, choose a bijection from $S$ onto $U$. Since their
complements in the same finite set have equal size as well, extend it
to a permutation $\pi$ of $F_i$. Thus $\pi(S)=U$.
Postcomposition with $\pi$ in coordinate $i$, leaving all other
coordinates unchanged, defines a bijection $\tau$ of $\Omega$;
its inverse postcomposes that coordinate with $\pi^{-1}$.
It satisfies $b(\tau\omega)=\pi(b(\omega))$. Injectivity of $\pi$
therefore gives $b(\tau\omega)=U$ if and only if $b(\omega)=S$.
Consequently every fiber of $b$ over $K$ has exactly $c$ elements.
Counting all fibers gives $|\Omega|=|K|c$, and counting the fibers
over those $U$ satisfying $P$ gives $|\{\omega:P(b(\omega))\}|=
|\{U\in K:P(U)\}|c$. Division and cancellation of $c>0$ prove the
identity. Both denominators are positive, since $S\in K$ and
$\Omega$ contains the identity outcome.
\end{proof}
ProductPermutationSubsetLaw.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Subset marginals of product permutations]
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $F_i$ be finite sets for $i\in I$, and put
$\Omega=\prod_{j\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(F_j)$. Fix $i\in I$, a subset
$S\subseteq F_i$, and any predicate $P$ on subsets of $F_i$. Then
\[
 \frac{|\{\omega\in\Omega:P(\omega_i(S))\}|}{|\Omega|}
 =\frac{|\{U\subseteq F_i:|U|=|S|,\ P(U)\}|}
 {|\{U\subseteq F_i:|U|=|S|\}|}.
\]
In particular, the image of $S$ under the $i$th coordinate of a uniform
product permutation is a uniform subset of its prescribed size.
\end{lemma}
ProductPermutationSubsetLaw.title: ProductPermutationSubsetLaw

QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning.lean_statement:
open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

theorem QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning :
    ∀ β D ρ η ξ : ENNReal,
      0 < β → β < η → 0 < ρ → ρ < D → D ≤ 1 →
      0 < ξ → 4 * ((ρ / D) * β + ξ) ≤ η → 10 * η < ρ →
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
        (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (L R : Finset V),
        Disjoint L R → n₀ ≤ L.card → n₀ ≤ R.card →
        L.card ≤ R.card + 1 → R.card ≤ L.card + 1 →
        SuperRegularPair G L R β D →
        ∃ G' : SimpleGraph V, G' ≤ G ∧
          @SuperRegularPair V _ G' (Classical.decRel _) L R η ρ := by
QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning.name: QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning
QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
First apply \noderef{ThinningRealParameters}: all parameters are finite. Indeed $D\leq1$, $\rho<D$,
$\eta\leq10\eta<\rho$, and $\beta<\eta$ establish finiteness of
$D,\rho,\eta,\beta$. Also
$\xi\leq\lambda\beta+\xi\leq4(\lambda\beta+\xi)\leq\eta$ establishes
finiteness of $\xi$. Positivity and finiteness permit real conversions
throughout the following argument. Put $q=\rho/D$ in the real numbers;
then $0<q<1$, $qD=\rho$, and the budget hypothesis gives
$q\beta+\xi\leq\eta/4\leq\eta$. Also $\beta<\eta<\rho<D$.

Apply \noderef{NearEqualRetentionThreshold} with the positive real
conversions of $\xi,\eta$ to choose $n_0\geq1$, before choosing any
vertex type or graph. On a graph with admissible parts, use
\noderef{IndependentEdgeSample} on $V\times V$ with probability $q$.
This is one probability measure by \noderef{IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw}
specialized to the constant coordinate probabilities $q_i=q$.
By \noderef{RetentionBadEventUnion}, the event failing
\noderef{RetentionCountControl} has measure at most
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\bigl(
2(|L|+|R|)e^{-2\xi^2\min(|L|,|R|)}
+2\,2^{|L|+|R|}e^{-2\xi^2\eta^2|L||R|}\bigr)<1.
\]
The strict inequality is the chosen numerical threshold and uses both
near-equal inequalities. If no outcome had count control, this failure
event would be the whole sample space and have measure one, a
contradiction. Choose an outcome $\omega$ with count control, and set
$G'=G_\omega$ using \noderef{CrossEdgeRetention}. This graph has the
original vertex set. By \noderef{CrossEdgeRetentionCounts} it is
contained in $G$, and its rectangle and degree counts are exactly
the retained coordinate counts tested in count control.

For $v\in L$ take $m=|R|$, $a=\deg_G(v;R)$ and
$b=\deg_{G'}(v;R)$. The original super-regularity hypothesis supplies
$(D-\beta)m\leq a\leq(D+\beta)m$ by \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.
The coordinate bijection $w\mapsto(v,w)$ shows that the original
coordinate set has size $a$, and the degree identity just cited gives
$|b-qa|\leq\xi m$ from count control. Apply
\noderef{ThinningCountInterval} to obtain
$(\rho-\eta)|R|\leq b\leq(\rho+\eta)|R|$.
For $w\in R$, use $m=|L|$ and the bijection $v\mapsto(v,w)$;
symmetry identifies the original adjacency count with
$\deg_G(w;L)$. The same transfer proves the right-degree interval.

Finally take $U\subseteq L,W\subseteq R$ with
$|U|>\eta|L|$, $|W|>\eta|R|$. These subsets are nonempty, since
$\eta>0$ and the parts have size at least one. Because $\beta<\eta$,
they also satisfy the original $\beta$-thresholds. Thus the regularity
clause of \noderef{SuperRegularPair} gives
$D-\beta\leq d_G(U,W)\leq D+\beta$.
By \noderef{PairDensity}, $d_G(U,W)=e_G(U,W)/m$, where
$m=|U||W|$ is positive and finite. Multiplication by $m$ preserves
and reflects each inequality (also for extended nonnegative endpoints),
so
\[
(D-\beta)|U||W|\leq e_G(U,W)\leq(D+\beta)|U||W|.
\]
Count control and the exact rectangle identity give
$|e_{G'}(U,W)-qe_G(U,W)|\leq\xi|U||W|$. Apply
\noderef{ThinningCountInterval} with $m=|U||W|$ to obtain
$(\rho-\eta)m\leq e_{G'}(U,W)\leq(\rho+\eta)m$.
Dividing both inequalities by the same positive finite $m$, and using
the density formula of \noderef{PairDensity} for $G'$, gives
$\rho-\eta\leq d_{G'}(U,W)\leq\rho+\eta$.
This is precisely the regularity clause; together with the two degree
intervals it proves \noderef{SuperRegularPair}. Every normalization
used the actual opposite-part size. No equality of the part sizes or
graph-dependent threshold was used.
\end{proof}
QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Quantitative spanning super-regular thinning]
Let $0<\beta<\eta$, $0<\rho<D\leq1$, and $\xi>0$. Put $\lambda=\rho/D$ and assume
\[
4(\lambda\beta+\xi)\leq\eta\quad\text{and}\quad 10\eta<\rho.
\]
There is $n_0$ such that the following holds. If $L,R$ are disjoint, both have size at least $n_0$, their sizes differ by at most one, and $G[L,R]$ is $(\beta,D)$-super-regular in the sense of \noderef{SuperRegularPair}, then $G$ contains a spanning subgraph $G'$ for which $G'[L,R]$ is $(\eta,\rho)$-super-regular.
\end{lemma}
QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning.title: QuantitativeSuperRegularThinning

    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (S : Finset VH) (f : VH → VG) (x : VH) : Finset VG := by
RawCandidates.name: RawCandidates
RawCandidates.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Raw candidates]
For a blow-up instance $B$, a candidacy system $A$, a finite embedded
set $S$, and a total map $f:V(H)\to V(G)$, define
\[
 D_S^f(x)=\{v\in V(G):A(x,v),\quad
                  G(v,f(y))\text{ for every }y\in S\cap N_H(x)\}.
\]
This is a finite set, denoted $\operatorname{RawCandidates}(B,A,S,f,x)$.
In particular it does not remove the occupied images $f(S)$.
\end{definition}

  have hkR := hkle

  rify at hd hd1 hd' hdd ha hε' hε hequarter hedquarter heaK hee' hedK hedensity hen hK hΔpos
  have hnR : (4 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn4
  have hnnonneg : (0 : ℝ) ≤ n := Nat.cast_nonneg n

      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hNhalf ha.le]
  have hdegbase : (d : ℝ) / 2 ≤ ((d : ℝ) - ε) * (1 - (ε : ℝ)) := by
    nlinarith only [hedquarter, mul_nonneg (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε by positivity)
      (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε by positivity),
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hd1 (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε by positivity)]
  have hdegree : (d / 2 : ℝ≥0) * n ≤ (d - ε) * N := by
    rify [hed]
    have hde : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) - ε := sub_nonneg.mpr (by exact_mod_cast hed)
    nlinarith only [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hdegbase hnnonneg,
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hNloR hde]
  have htransfer : ε * (N : ℝ≥0) ≤ ε' * m := by
    have hmhalfR := hmhalf
    rify at hmhalfR ⊢
    nlinarith only [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hNtwo hε.le,
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hee' hnnonneg,
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmhalfR hε'.le]
  have hstrongadd : (d' - ε') * (m : ℝ≥0) +
      4 * Δ * Δ * ε * n + 3 * ε * n ≤ (d - ε) * N := by
    have hdegreeR := hdegree
    have hmnR : (m : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hmn
    rify [he'd, hed] at hdegreeR ⊢
    have hbound : ((d' : ℝ) - ε') * m ≤ (d : ℝ) / 4 * n := by
      have : (d' : ℝ) - ε' ≤ (d : ℝ) / 4 := by linarith only [hdd, hε'.le]
      have hmnonneg : (0 : ℝ) ≤ m := Nat.cast_nonneg m
      nlinarith only [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right this hmnonneg,
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmnR (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ (d : ℝ) / 4 by positivity)]
    have hKn := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hdK hnnonneg
    dsimp [K] at hKn
    push_cast at hKn
    nlinarith only [hbound, hKn, hdegreeR]
  have hstrong : (d' - ε') * (m : ℝ≥0) ≤
      (d - ε) * N - 3 * ε * n - 4 * Δ * Δ * ε * n := by
    -- The additive bound justifies both truncated subtractions.
    apply le_tsub_of_add_le_right
    apply le_tsub_of_add_le_right
    exact hstrongadd
  have hweak : (d' - ε') * (m : ℝ≥0) ≤ (d - ε) * N - 3 * ε * n :=
    hstrong.trans (tsub_le_self)
  refine ⟨hmN, hlossk, hloss, ?_, hdegree, htransfer, hweak, ?_⟩
  · simpa only [K, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_ofNat] using hsmall
  · simpa only [Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_ofNat] using hstrong
RebalancingLossMargins.lean_statement:
open scoped NNReal ENNReal

theorem RebalancingLossMargins (Δ : ℕ) (d d' a : ENNReal)
    (hΔ : 1 ≤ Δ) (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1)
    (hd' : 0 < d') (hd'd : d' ≤ d / 4) (ha : 0 < a) (haquarter : a ≤ 1 / 4) :
    ∃ ε₀' : ENNReal, 0 < ε₀' ∧ ε₀' ≤ min (1 / 4) (d' / 2) ∧
    ∀ ε' : ENNReal, 0 < ε' → ε' ≤ ε₀' →
      ∃ ε₀ : ENNReal, 0 < ε₀ ∧
      ∀ ε : ENNReal, 0 < ε → ε ≤ ε₀ →
        ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
        ∃ m k : ℕ,
          4 ≤ n ∧ ε ≤ a ∧ ε ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ ε ≤ d / 4 ∧ ε' < ⊤ ∧
          (m : ENNReal) ≤ (1 - ε) * n ∧
          (1 - ε) * n < (m : ENNReal) + 1 ∧
          (n : ENNReal) / 2 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ n ∧
          (k : ENNReal) ≤ 4 * ε * n ∧
          (d' - ε') + (8 * Δ * Δ * ε) / ε' ≤ d - ε ∧
          ∀ N : ℕ, (1 - ε) * n ≤ N → (N : ENNReal) ≤ (1 + ε) * n →
            m ≤ N ∧ N - m ≤ k ∧ ((N - m : ℕ) : ENNReal) ≤ 3 * ε * n ∧
            (3 + 4 * Δ * Δ) * ε * n ≤ a * N ∧
            (d / 2) * n ≤ (d - ε) * N ∧
            ε * N ≤ ε' * m ∧
            (d' - ε') * m ≤ (d - ε) * N - 3 * ε * n ∧
            (d' - ε') * m ≤ (d - ε) * N - 3 * ε * n - 4 * Δ * Δ * ε * n := by

RebalancingLossMargins.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
All input scalars are finite: $d\leq1$, $d'\leq d/4$, and $a\leq1/4$.
Work in their ordinary real representatives. Put $K=3+4\Delta^2$ and choose
\[
 \varepsilon'_0=\min\{1/4,d'/2\},\qquad
 \varepsilon_0=\min\{1/4,d/4,a,a/(2K),\varepsilon'/4,
                    d/(4K),d\varepsilon'/(32\Delta^2)\}.
\]
Every entry is strictly positive, since $\Delta\geq1$; hence both minima
are strictly positive. Fix admissible $\varepsilon$ and take
$n_0=\max\{4,\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil\}$. Then $n\geq n_0$ implies
$\varepsilon n\geq1$. Set $m=\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)n\rfloor$ and
$k=\lceil3\varepsilon n\rceil$. The floor inequalities give
$m\leq(1-\varepsilon)n<m+1$, and
$m\geq(1-\varepsilon)n-1\geq3n/4-1\geq n/2$; also $m\leq n$.
For $N$ in the stated window, $m\leq N$, and
$N-m\leq2\varepsilon n+1\leq3\varepsilon n\leq k$.
The ceiling inequality gives $k\leq3\varepsilon n+1\leq4\varepsilon n$.

The window yields $n/2\leq N\leq2n$. Therefore
$K\varepsilon n\leq an/2\leq aN$ and
$\varepsilon N\leq2\varepsilon n\leq\varepsilon'n/2\leq\varepsilon'm$.
Since $\varepsilon\leq d/4$ and $d\leq1$,
\[
 (d-\varepsilon)(1-\varepsilon)
 =d-(d+1)\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2
 \geq d-2\varepsilon\geq d/2.
\]
Multiplying by $n$ proves the candidate-degree bound. Moreover
\[
 (d-\varepsilon)N-K\varepsilon n
 \geq(d/2-K\varepsilon)n\geq(d/4)n
 \geq(d'-\varepsilon')m.
\]
Here $K\varepsilon\leq d/4$, $d'\leq d/4$, and $m\leq n$ justify the
last two comparisons. This proves the stronger degree margin; omitting
the nonnegative buffer loss proves the other. The stronger inequality
also shows that its subtractions do not cross zero, so the same assertions
hold for truncated subtraction. Finally
$8\Delta^2\varepsilon/\varepsilon'\leq d/4$, whence
$(d'-\varepsilon')+8\Delta^2\varepsilon/\varepsilon'\leq d'+d/4
\leq d/2\leq d-\varepsilon$. Returning to extended nonnegative reals
preserves every displayed inequality and proves the claim.
\end{proof}
RebalancingLossMargins.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Floor, ceiling, and loss margins]
Fix $\Delta\geq1$, $0<d\leq1$, $0<d'\leq d/4$, and $0<a\leq1/4$.
There exists $0<\varepsilon'_0\leq\min\{1/4,d'/2\}$ such that for each
$0<\varepsilon'\leq\varepsilon'_0$ there is $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that,
for each $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
there are integers $m,k\geq0$ satisfying $n\geq4$,
$\varepsilon\leq a,1/4,d/4$, $\varepsilon'<\infty$, and
\[
 m\leq(1-\varepsilon)n<m+1,\qquad n/2\leq m\leq n,
 \qquad k\leq4\varepsilon n,
 \qquad (d'-\varepsilon')+8\Delta^2\varepsilon/\varepsilon'\leq d-\varepsilon.
\]
For every integer $N$ in the window $(1-\varepsilon)n\leq N\leq(1+\varepsilon)n$,
\[
 m\leq N,\quad N-m\leq k,\quad N-m\leq3\varepsilon n,\quad
 (3+4\Delta^2)\varepsilon n\leq aN,\quad
 (d/2)n\leq(d-\varepsilon)N,\quad \varepsilon N\leq\varepsilon'm,
\]
and both degree margins hold:
\[
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)N-3\varepsilon n,
 \qquad
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)N-3\varepsilon n-4\Delta^2\varepsilon n.
\]
All cutoffs depend only on the displayed scalar parameters, not on the
number of clusters. Subtractions are nonnegative-real truncated subtraction.
\end{lemma}

RebalancingResidualCandidacy.lean_proof:
classical
  let left (P : VH → Prop) : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) :=
    Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ P x
  let right (P : VG → Prop) : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) :=
    Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ P v
  have mem_left (P : VH → Prop) (z) : z ∈ left P ↔
      ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ P x := by
    simp only [left, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  have mem_right (P : VG → Prop) (z) : z ∈ right P ↔
      ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ P v := by
    simp only [right, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  have left_map (P : VH → Prop) : left P =
      (Finset.univ.filter P).map Function.Embedding.inl := by
    ext z
    cases z <;> simp [left]
  have right_map (P : VG → Prop) : right P =
      (Finset.univ.filter P).map Function.Embedding.inr := by
    ext z
    cases z <;> simp [right]
  have left_card (P : VH → Prop) :
      (left P).card = (Finset.univ.filter P).card := by
    rw [left_map, Finset.card_map]
  have right_card (P : VG → Prop) :
      (right P).card = (Finset.univ.filter P).card := by
    rw [right_map, Finset.card_map]
  let Aup := UpdatedCandidacy B A X f
  let g₀ : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p q =>
    ∃ x v, p = Sum.inl x ∧ q = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed x v
  let g : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p q =>
    ∃ x v, p = Sum.inl x ∧ q = Sum.inr v ∧ Aup.allowed x v
  letI : DecidableRel g₀.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  letI : DecidableRel g.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adj₀ (x : VH) (v : VG) :
      g₀.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inr v) ↔ A.allowed x v := by
    simp [g₀, SimpleGraph.fromRel]
  have adj (x : VH) (v : VG) :
      g.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inr v) ↔ Aup.allowed x v := by
    simp [g, SimpleGraph.fromRel]
  let e : ({x : VH // x ∉ X} ⊕ {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) ↪ (VH ⊕ VG) :=
    (Function.Embedding.subtype _).sumMap (Function.Embedding.subtype _)
  let gr : SimpleGraph ({x : VH // x ∉ X} ⊕ {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) :=
    SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p q =>
      ∃ x v, p = Sum.inl x ∧ q = Sum.inr v ∧ Ar.allowed x v
  letI : DecidableRel gr.Adj := Classical.decRel _
  have adjr (x) (v) : gr.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inr v) ↔ Ar.allowed x v := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, h | h⟩
      · obtain ⟨x', v', hx, hv, ha⟩ := h
        cases Sum.inl.inj hx
        cases Sum.inr.inj hv
        exact ha
      · obtain ⟨x', v', hx, _, _⟩ := h
        cases hx
    · exact fun h => ⟨Sum.inl_ne_inr, Or.inl ⟨x, v, rfl, rfl, h⟩⟩
  have reflect (p q) : gr.Adj p q ↔ g.Adj (e p) (e q) := by
    cases p with
    | inl x =>
      cases q with
      | inl y => simp [gr, g, e, SimpleGraph.fromRel]
      | inr v =>
        change gr.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inr v) ↔
          g.Adj (Sum.inl x.1) (Sum.inr v.1)
        rw [adjr, adj]
        exact hallowed x v
    | inr v =>
      cases q with
      | inl x =>
        rw [gr.adj_comm, g.adj_comm]
        change gr.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inr v) ↔
          g.Adj (Sum.inl x.1) (Sum.inr v.1)
        rw [adjr, adj]
        exact hallowed x v
      | inr w => simp [gr, g, e, SimpleGraph.fromRel]
  intro i
  let L₀ := left (fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i)
  let Q₀ := right (fun v => B.hostCluster v = i)
  let DL := left (fun x => x ∈ X ∧ B.sourceCluster x = i)
  let DQ := right (fun v => v ∈ X.image f.toFun ∧ B.hostCluster v = i)
  let E := left (fun x => x ∉ X ∧ (∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y) ∧ B.sourceCluster x = i)
  let lr : Finset ({x : VH // x ∉ X} ⊕ {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) :=
    Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ Br.sourceCluster x = i
  let qr : Finset ({x : VH // x ∉ X} ⊕ {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) :=
    Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ Br.hostCluster v = i
  have mem_lr (z) : z ∈ lr ↔ ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ Br.sourceCluster x = i := by
    simp only [lr, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  have mem_qr (z) : z ∈ qr ↔ ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ Br.hostCluster v = i := by
    simp only [qr, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  have hL₀ : L₀.card = Fintype.card {x // B.sourceCluster x = i} := by
    dsimp only [L₀]
    rw [left_card, Fintype.card_subtype]
    congr 1
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
  have hQ₀ : Q₀.card = Fintype.card {v // B.hostCluster v = i} := by
    dsimp only [Q₀]
    rw [right_card, Fintype.card_subtype]
    congr 1
    ext v
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
  have hDL : DL ⊆ L₀ := by
    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨x, rfl, hx⟩ := (mem_left _ _).mp hz
    rw [mem_left]
    exact ⟨x, rfl, hx.2⟩
  have hDQ : DQ ⊆ Q₀ := by
    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨v, rfl, hv⟩ := (mem_right _ _).mp hz
    rw [mem_right]
    exact ⟨v, rfl, hv.2⟩
  have hE : E ⊆ L₀ \ DL := by
    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨x, rfl, hx⟩ := (mem_left _ _).mp hz
    simpa only [L₀, DL, Finset.mem_sdiff, mem_left, Sum.inl.injEq,
      exists_eq_left', hx.1, hx.2.2, false_and, not_false_eq_true, and_self]
  have hDLcard : (DL.card : ENNReal) ≤ L := by
    have heq : DL = (X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).map
        Function.Embedding.inl := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp only [DL, mem_left, Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter,
        Function.Embedding.inl_apply, Sum.inl.injEq, Sum.inr_ne_inl, false_and,
        exists_false, exists_eq_right, exists_eq_left', reduceCtorEq, and_false]
    simpa only [heq, Finset.card_map] using hX i
  have hDQcard : (DQ.card : ENNReal) ≤ L := by
    have heq : DQ = ((X.image f.toFun).filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).map
        Function.Embedding.inr := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp only [DQ, mem_right, Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter,
        Function.Embedding.inr_apply, Sum.inr.injEq, Sum.inl_ne_inr, false_and,
        exists_false, exists_eq_right, exists_eq_left', reduceCtorEq, and_false]
    simpa only [heq, Finset.card_map] using himage i
  have hEcard : (E.card : ENNReal) ≤ J := by
    have heq : E = ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => x ∉ X ∧ ∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y).filter
        fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).map Function.Embedding.inl := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp only [E, mem_left, Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Function.Embedding.inl_apply, Sum.inl.injEq,
        Sum.inr_ne_inl, false_and, exists_false, exists_eq_right, exists_eq_left',
        reduceCtorEq, and_false]
      simp only [and_assoc]
    simpa only [heq, Finset.card_map] using hbuffer i
  have imageL : lr.map e = L₀ \ DL := by
    ext z
    cases z with
    | inl x =>
      simp only [Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_sdiff]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨z, hz, hzx⟩
        cases z with
        | inl a =>
          have ha : a.1 = x := Sum.inl.inj hzx
          subst x
          have hai : B.sourceCluster a.1 = i := by
            simpa only [mem_lr, Sum.inl.injEq, exists_eq_left', hsource] using hz
          simp only [L₀, DL, mem_left, Sum.inl.injEq, exists_eq_left']
          exact ⟨hai, fun h => a.2 h.1⟩
        | inr v => cases hzx
      · intro hx
        have hx' : B.sourceCluster x = i ∧ x ∉ X := by
          simp only [L₀, DL, mem_left, Sum.inl.injEq, exists_eq_left'] at hx
          exact ⟨hx.1, fun h => hx.2 ⟨h, hx.1⟩⟩
        refine ⟨Sum.inl ⟨x, hx'.2⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
        simp only [mem_lr, Sum.inl.injEq, exists_eq_left', hsource]
        exact hx'.1
    | inr v => simp [lr, L₀, DL, left, e]
  have imageQ : qr.map e = Q₀ \ DQ := by
    ext z
    cases z with
    | inr v =>
      simp only [Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_sdiff]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨z, hz, hzv⟩
        cases z with
        | inr a =>
          have ha : a.1 = v := Sum.inr.inj hzv
          subst v
          have hai : B.hostCluster a.1 = i := by
            simpa only [mem_qr, Sum.inr.injEq, exists_eq_left', hhost] using hz
          simp only [Q₀, DQ, mem_right, Sum.inr.injEq, exists_eq_left']
          exact ⟨hai, fun h => a.2 h.1⟩
        | inl x => cases hzv
      · intro hv
        have hv' : B.hostCluster v = i ∧ v ∉ X.image f.toFun := by
          simp only [Q₀, DQ, mem_right, Sum.inr.injEq, exists_eq_left'] at hv
          exact ⟨hv.1, fun h => hv.2 ⟨h, hv.1⟩⟩
        refine ⟨Sum.inr ⟨v, hv'.2⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
        simp only [mem_qr, Sum.inr.injEq, exists_eq_left', hhost]
        exact hv'.1
    | inl x => simp [qr, Q₀, DQ, right, e]
  have hlr : lr.card = m := by
    have heq : lr = (Finset.univ.filter fun x => Br.sourceCluster x = i).map
        Function.Embedding.inl := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp only [mem_lr, Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Function.Embedding.inl_apply, Sum.inl.injEq,
        Sum.inr_ne_inl, false_and, exists_false, exists_eq_right, exists_eq_left',
        reduceCtorEq, and_false]
    rw [heq, Finset.card_map, ← Fintype.card_subtype]
    exact hleft i
  have hqr : qr.card = m := by
    have heq : qr = (Finset.univ.filter fun v => Br.hostCluster v = i).map
        Function.Embedding.inr := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp only [mem_qr, Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Function.Embedding.inr_apply, Sum.inr.injEq,
        Sum.inl_ne_inr, false_and, exists_false, exists_eq_right, exists_eq_left',
        reduceCtorEq, and_false]
    rw [heq, Finset.card_map, ← Fintype.card_subtype]
    exact hright i
  have hL : (L₀ \ DL).card = m := by rw [← imageL, Finset.card_map, hlr]
  have hQ : (Q₀ \ DQ).card = m := by rw [← imageQ, Finset.card_map, hqr]
  have hRows : ∀ z ∈ (L₀ \ DL) \ E, ∀ w ∈ Q₀ \ DQ,
      g.Adj z w ↔ g₀.Adj z w := by
    intro z hz w hw
    obtain ⟨x, rfl, hxi⟩ := (mem_left _ _).mp
      (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hz).1).1
    obtain ⟨v, rfl, hvi⟩ := (mem_right _ _).mp (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).1
    have hx : x ∉ X := by
      simpa only [DL, mem_left, Sum.inl.injEq, exists_eq_left', hxi, and_true] using
        (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hz).1).2
    have hv : v ∉ X.image f.toFun := by
      simpa only [DQ, mem_right, Sum.inr.injEq, exists_eq_left', hvi, and_true] using
        (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hw).2
    have hn : ¬ ∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y := by
      simpa only [E, mem_left, Sum.inl.injEq, exists_eq_left', hx, hxi, true_and,
        and_true, not_false_eq_true] using (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hz).2
    rw [adj, adj₀]
    constructor
    · exact fun h => h.2.2.1
    · intro h
      exact ⟨hx, hv, h, fun y hy hxy => False.elim (hn ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩)⟩
  have exceptional : ∀ z ∈ E, (d' - ε') * ((Q₀ \ DQ).card : ENNReal) ≤
      (((Q₀ \ DQ).filter fun w => g.Adj z w).card : ENNReal) := by
    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨x, rfl, hx⟩ := (mem_left _ _).mp hz
    have candidates : ((Q₀ \ DQ).filter fun w => g.Adj (Sum.inl x) w) =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v => Aup.allowed x v).map Function.Embedding.inr := by
      ext w
      cases w with
      | inl y => simp [Q₀, DQ, right]
      | inr v =>
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_map,
          Function.Embedding.inr_apply, Sum.inr.injEq, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨_, hav⟩
          exact ⟨v, (adj x v).mp hav, rfl⟩
        · rintro ⟨v', hav, rfl⟩
          have hvi : B.hostCluster v' = i :=
            (Aup.cluster_respecting hav).symm.trans hx.2.2
          refine ⟨?_, (adj x v').mpr hav⟩
          simp only [Q₀, DQ, mem_right, Sum.inr.injEq, exists_eq_left']
          exact ⟨hvi, fun h => hav.2.1 h.1⟩
    have hncard : Set.ncard {v | Aup.allowed x v} =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v => Aup.allowed x v).card := by
      rw [← Set.ncard_coe_finset]
      congr 1
      ext v
      simp
    rw [hQ, candidates, Finset.card_map]
    have hr : rho ≤ Set.ncard {v | Aup.allowed x v} := hreserve x hx.1 hx.2.1
    rw [hncard] at hr
    exact hrho.trans hr

theorem RebalancingResidualCandidacy {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}
    [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (X : Finset VH) (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)
    (Br : BlowUpInstance r {x : VH // x ∉ X} {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}
      (H.induce {x : VH | x ∉ X}) (G.induce {v : VG | v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) R)
    (Ar : CandidacySystem Br) (m : ℕ) (ε d ε' d' L J η rho : ENNReal)
    (hsource : ∀ x, Br.sourceCluster x = B.sourceCluster x.1)
    (hhost : ∀ v, Br.hostCluster v = B.hostCluster v.1)
    (hallowed : ∀ x v, Ar.allowed x v ↔ (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x.1 v.1)
    (hleft : ∀ i, Fintype.card {x : {x : VH // x ∉ X} // Br.sourceCluster x = i} = m)
    (hright : ∀ i, Fintype.card {v : {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun} //
      Br.hostCluster v = i} = m)
    (hEq : ∀ i, Fintype.card {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i} =
      Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i})
    (hSR : CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d)
    (hX : ∀ i, ((X.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤ L)
    (himage : ∀ i, (((X.image f.toFun).filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).card :
      ENNReal) ≤ L)
    (hbuffer : ∀ i, (((Finset.univ.filter fun x => x ∉ X ∧ ∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y).filter
      fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card : ENNReal) ≤ J)
    (hJ : J ≤ η * m) (hε' : 0 < ε') (hε'top : ε' < ⊤)
    (hthreshold : ∀ i, ε * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} ≤ ε' * m)
    (hdensity : (d' - ε') + η / ε' ≤ d - ε)
    (hdegree : ∀ i, (d' - ε') * m ≤
      (d - ε) * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - L - J)
    (hrho : (d' - ε') * m ≤ rho)
    (hreserve : ∀ x, x ∉ X → (∃ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y) →
      rho ≤ Set.ncard {v : VG | (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x v}) :

RebalancingResidualCandidacy.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Fix $i$, and use the sum-vertex representation in
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}. The original left and right parts
are the copies of $X_i$ and $V_i$ in $V(H)\oplus V(G)$. They form a
lower-super-regular pair by assumption. Let $D_L$ be the left copy of
$X\cap X_i$, $D_R$ the right copy of $f(X)\cap V_i$, and let $E_i$ be the
left copy of $E\cap X_i$. These sets lie in the asserted original parts;
$E_i$ is disjoint from $D_L$ because the definition of $E$ excludes $X$.
Define the updated sum-vertex graph by the relation $A_f$ in
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}. For opposite tags its adjacency is exactly
that allowed relation: the forward relation supplies the edge, the
reverse relation has impossible tags, and unequal tags exclude loops.
This observation applies also to the original candidacy graph.

For $x\in X_i\setminus(X\cup E)$, no vertex of $X$ is a neighbor of $x$.
For unused $v\in V_i\setminus f(X)$, expanding the updated relation
therefore gives $A_f(x,v)\iff A(x,v)$: both exclusions hold and every
extra neighbor condition is vacuous. This verifies both directions of
the ordinary-row equality required by
\noderef{ExceptionalLeftLowerSuperRegular}.
For $x\in E\cap X_i$, every updated candidate lies in
$V_i\setminus f(X)$, by the original-candidacy and unused-host clauses
of the updated relation and cluster respect in \noderef{CandidacySystem}.
Hence the entire candidate set is bijective with its updated neighbors
in the residual right part. The reserve hypothesis and
$(d'-\varepsilon')m\leq\rho$ give the required exceptional-row degree.

The two ambient residual parts have size $m$: the literal subtype
projections and the restricted-map identities identify them with the
residual fibers. Since $|X_i|=|V_i|$, the displayed threshold assumption
transfers both thresholds. The exceptional fraction follows from
$|E_i|\leq J\leq\eta m$. The density margin is an assumption.
For the left-degree margin, the stronger assumed degree inequality
implies $(d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)|V_i|-L$ by deleting
the nonnegative $J$ loss, and replacing $L$ by $|D_R|\leq L$ weakens
the required bound. For the right-degree margin use $|X_i|=|V_i|$ and
$|D_L|\leq L$, $|E_i|\leq J$ to get
\[
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)|X_i|-|D_L|-|E_i|.
\]
Antitonicity of truncated subtraction justifies both replacements.
All hypotheses of \noderef{ExceptionalLeftLowerSuperRegular} have thus
been verified, giving lower-super-regularity of this ambient updated pair.

Finally project the sum of the two complement subtypes into the original
sum universe, preserving tags. This is injective and sends each residual
fiber exactly onto its ambient residual part. On opposite tags the
assumed exact relation identifies adjacency in both directions. On equal
tags both graphs have no edges. Thus the product projection bijects
filtered ordered edge sets, and projections biject filtered neighborhoods.
Their cardinalities, and the denominators in \noderef{PairDensity}, agree.
Both strict regularity thresholds and both degree clauses in
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} consequently transfer without change.
This proves \noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular} for $A_r$ in every fiber.
\end{proof}
RebalancingResidualCandidacy.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Residual candidacy with exceptional rows]
Let $B,A$ be a finite blow-up instance with equal source and host fiber
sizes and lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular candidacy. Let $f$ be a
partial compatible embedding on $X$, and let $B_r,A_r$ live on the
literal complement subtypes with induced graphs, unchanged reduced
graph, restricted cluster maps, and allowed relation exactly $A_f$.
Suppose both residual fibers have size $m$. Put
$E=\{x\notin X:\exists y\in X,\ xy\in E(H)\}$.
Suppose the deleted source and host counts in every fiber are at most
$L$, the count $|E\cap X_i|$ is at most $J$, and $J\leq\eta m$.
Assume $0<\varepsilon'<\infty$ and, for every $i$,
\[
 \varepsilon|V_i|\leq\varepsilon'm,\qquad
 (d'-\varepsilon')+\eta/\varepsilon'\leq d-\varepsilon,\qquad
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)|V_i|-L-J.
\]
Finally suppose $(d'-\varepsilon')m\leq\rho$ and every $x\in E$ has
at least $\rho$ updated candidates in the original host universe.
Then $A_r$ is lower-$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular candidacy for $B_r$.
\end{lemma}

RebalancingResidualGeometry.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Compatibility in \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} and cluster respect
in \noderef{CandidacySystem} give $c_G(f(x))=c_H(x)$ for every $x\in X$.
Consequently $f(X)\cap V_i=f(X\cap X_i)$: cluster respect gives one
inclusion, and writing a vertex in the left side as $f(x)$ gives the other.
Injectivity on $X$ makes this restriction a bijection. Thus the two removed
fiber counts agree, and subtraction from $|X_i|=|V_i|$ leaves size $m$
on both sides (the hypothesis $m\leq |V_i|$ makes natural subtraction exact).
Restrict the cluster maps to the literal complements. The independence
and reduced-support fields of \noderef{BlowUpInstance} are inherited:
an induced edge is an original edge, and distinct subtype vertices have
distinct ambient values. Capacity follows from the equal residual counts.
These fields define $B_r$. Define $A_r(x,v)$ to be
$(\noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}\ B\ A\ X\ f)(x,v)$. Its cluster respect is
the cluster respect of that updated system. The two cluster-map identities
and both directions of the allowed-relation equivalence hold by
construction. Nothing replaces either residual set by an abstract copy.
\end{proof}
RebalancingResidualGeometry.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Exact residual geometry]
Let $B$ be a finite blow-up instance with candidacy system $A$, equally
large source and host fibers, and let $f$ be a partial compatible embedding
on $X$. Suppose $m\leq |V_i|$ and $|X\cap X_i|=|V_i|-m$ for every $i$.
On the literal complement subtypes $Y=V(H)\setminus X$ and
$W=V(G)\setminus f(X)$ there exist a blow-up instance $B_r$ on the induced
graphs and the unchanged reduced graph, and a candidacy system $A_r$,
whose cluster maps are restrictions of those of $B$ and whose allowed
relation is exactly the restriction of $A_f$. Both residual fibers have
size $m$. In addition,
$|f(X)\cap V_i|=|X\cap X_i|$ for every $i$.
\end{lemma}
