    (A : CandidacySystem B) (X : Finset VH) (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)
    (Br : BlowUpInstance r {x : VH // x ∉ X} {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}
      (H.induce {x : VH | x ∉ X}) (G.induce {v : VG | v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) R)
    (m : ℕ) (ε d ε' d' L : ENNReal)
    (hmap : ∀ v, Br.hostCluster v = B.hostCluster v.1)
    (hcard : ∀ i, Fintype.card {v : {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun} //
      Br.hostCluster v = i} = m)
    (hSR : InstanceLowerSuperRegular B ε d)
    (hremoved : ∀ i, (((X.image f.toFun).filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).card :
      ENNReal) ≤ L)
    (hthreshold : ∀ i, ε * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} ≤ ε' * m)
    (hdensity : d' - ε' ≤ d - ε)
    (hdegree : ∀ i, (d' - ε') * m ≤
      (d - ε) * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - L) :
    InstanceLowerSuperRegular Br ε' d' := by
RebalancingResidualHost.name: RebalancingResidualHost
RebalancingResidualHost.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Fix an edge $ij$ of the unchanged reduced graph. By
\noderef{InstanceLowerSuperRegular} its original host pair is
lower-super-regular. Write $U=V_i$, $W=V_j$ and
$D_U=f(X)\cap V_i$, $D_W=f(X)\cap V_j$.
These deletion sets are subsets of the corresponding parts.
The subtype projection identifies each residual fiber bijectively with
the ambient part minus its deletion set, so both residual parts have
cardinality $m$.

First verify the lower-regularity premise of
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularDeletionSlicing}. For subsets
$P\subseteq U\setminus D_U$, $Q\subseteq W\setminus D_W$ with
$|P|>\varepsilon'm$ and $|Q|>\varepsilon'm$, the threshold assumptions
give $|P|>\varepsilon|U|$ and $|Q|>\varepsilon|W|$.
The first clause of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} and
\noderef{LowerRegularPair} therefore give density at least
$d-\varepsilon\geq d'-\varepsilon'$ in the original graph.
The assumed degree inequalities and $|D_U|,|D_W|\leq L$ give
\[
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)|U|-|D_U|,
 \qquad (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)|W|-|D_W|,
\]
by antitonicity of truncated subtraction in the deleted amount.
All hypotheses of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularDeletionSlicing} are now
verified; it supplies lower-super-regularity of the ambient residual pair.

To transfer it to the literal subtype graph, use the subtype value map
from $S=V(G)\setminus f(X)$ into $V(G)$. This map is injective, and
adjacency in $G[S]$ is exactly adjacency of the images in $G$.
The exact fiber-image equalities established above identify the images
of the two residual fibers with $U\setminus D_U$ and $W\setminus D_W$.
The reverse implication of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPairEmbedding}
therefore transfers the ambient lower-super-regularity to the subtype
pair. Doing this for every edge of $R$ proves
\noderef{InstanceLowerSuperRegular} for $B_r$.
\end{proof}
RebalancingResidualHost.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Residual host lower super-regularity]
Let $B,A$ be a finite blow-up instance with candidacy system and let $f$
be a partial compatible embedding on $X$. Let $B_r$ be an instance on
the literal complement subtypes with induced source and host graphs and
the unchanged reduced graph, whose host map is the original host map
restricted to the complement and whose host fibers have size $m$.
Suppose $B$ has host lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regularity, at most $L$
vertices are removed from each host fiber, and, for every $i$,
\[
 \varepsilon|V_i|\leq\varepsilon'm,\qquad
 d'-\varepsilon'\leq d-\varepsilon,\qquad
 (d'-\varepsilon')m\leq(d-\varepsilon)|V_i|-L.
\]
Then $B_r$ has host lower-$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regularity.
\end{lemma}
RebalancingResidualHost.title: RebalancingResidualHost

RebalancingRestrictionEstimates.lean_proof:
classical
  have hhalf : d / 2 ≤ d := by
    simpa using ENNReal.div_le_div_left (show (1 : ENNReal) ≤ 2 by norm_num) d
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i j hij U hU W hW hUt hWt
    exact (tsub_le_tsub hhalf hεa).trans
      ((hhost hij).1 U hU W hW
        ((mul_le_mul_left hεa _).trans_lt hUt)
        ((mul_le_mul_left hεa _).trans_lt hWt))
  · intro i
    exact ⟨(mul_le_mul_left (tsub_le_tsub_left hεa 1) _).trans (hsize i).1,
      (hsize i).2.trans (mul_le_mul_left (add_le_add_right hεa 1) _)⟩
  · intro x
    let i := B.sourceCluster x
    let L : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
      ∃ y : VH, z = Sum.inl y ∧ B.sourceCluster y = i
    let Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
      ∃ v : VG, z = Sum.inr v ∧ B.hostCluster v = i
    let C : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p q =>
      ∃ y : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl y ∧ q = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed y v
    letI : DecidableRel C.Adj := Classical.decRel _
    have hleft : Sum.inl x ∈ L := by
      simp only [L, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact ⟨x, rfl, rfl⟩
    have hadj (v : VG) : C.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inr v) ↔ A.allowed x v := by
      simp [C, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
    have hQ : Q.card = Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} := by
      rw [Fintype.card_subtype]
      symm
      apply Finset.card_bij (fun v _ => Sum.inr v)
      · intro v hv
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hv
        exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, v, rfl, hv⟩
      · intro v hv w hw heq
        exact Sum.inr_injective heq
      · intro z hz
        obtain ⟨v, rfl, hv⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hz).2
        exact ⟨v, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hv⟩, rfl⟩
    have hneighbors : (Q.filter fun z => C.Adj (Sum.inl x) z).card =
        Set.ncard {v : VG | A.allowed x v} := by
      rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card', Set.toFinset_setOf]
      symm
      apply Finset.card_bij (fun v _ => Sum.inr v)
      · intro v hv
        have hav : A.allowed x v := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2
        apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        refine ⟨?_, (hadj v).mpr hav⟩
        apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        exact ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, v, rfl, (A.cluster_respecting hav).symm⟩
      · intro v hv w hw heq
        exact Sum.inr_injective heq
      · intro z hz
        obtain ⟨hzQ, hzadj⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hz
        obtain ⟨v, rfl, hv⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hzQ).2
        exact ⟨v, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, (hadj v).mp hzadj⟩, rfl⟩
    have hdeg := (hcand i).2.1 (Sum.inl x) hleft
    change (d - ε) * (Q.card : ENNReal) ≤
      ((Q.filter fun z => C.Adj (Sum.inl x) z).card : ENNReal) at hdeg
    rw [hQ, hneighbors] at hdeg
    exact (hdegree i).trans hdeg
RebalancingRestrictionEstimates.lean_statement:
theorem RebalancingRestrictionEstimates {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}
    [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R)
    (A : CandidacySystem B) (n : ℕ) (ε d a : ENNReal)
    (hεa : ε ≤ a)
    (hhost : InstanceLowerSuperRegular B ε d)
    (hcand : CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d)
    (hsize : ∀ i, (1 - ε) * n ≤ Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} ∧
      (Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} : ENNReal) ≤ (1 + ε) * n)
    (hdegree : ∀ i, (d / 2) * n ≤
      (d - ε) * Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i}) :
    InstanceLowerRegular B a (d / 2) ∧
    (∀ i, (1 - a) * n ≤ Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} ∧
      (Fintype.card {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} : ENNReal) ≤ (1 + a) * n) ∧
    (∀ x, (d / 2) * n ≤ Set.ncard {v : VG | A.allowed x v}) := by
RebalancingRestrictionEstimates.name: RebalancingRestrictionEstimates
RebalancingRestrictionEstimates.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For an edge $ij$ of the reduced graph, \noderef{InstanceLowerSuperRegular}
gives the original lower-super-regular host pair. Its first clause in
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} is lower regularity.
Take subsets of its two parts of sizes strictly greater than $a|V_i|$
and $a|V_j|$. Since $\varepsilon\leq a$, these sizes are also strictly
greater than the original $\varepsilon$ thresholds. Thus
\noderef{LowerRegularPair} gives density at least $d-\varepsilon$.
Because $d/2\leq d$ and $\varepsilon\leq a$, monotonicity of truncated
subtraction gives $d/2-a\leq d-\varepsilon$.
This is precisely \noderef{InstanceLowerRegular} at $(a,d/2)$.
The size-window conclusions follow from $1-a\leq1-\varepsilon$
and $1+\varepsilon\leq1+a$, multiplying by nonnegative $n$.

For any vertex $x$, put $i=c_H(x)$. In the sum-vertex graph defining
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}, the vertex $\mathrm{inl}(x)$ lies
in the left $i$th part. The left-degree clause of
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} gives at least
$(d-\varepsilon)|V_i|$ neighbors in the right part. That right part is
bijective with $V_i$ by $v\mapsto\mathrm{inr}(v)$.
For opposite tags, expanding the defining relation of the graph shows
that adjacency of $\mathrm{inl}(x)$ and $\mathrm{inr}(v)$ is exactly
$A(x,v)$: the forward orientation is this relation, the reverse
orientation cannot have the stipulated tags, and the endpoints are distinct.
Moreover \noderef{CandidacySystem} forces every allowed $v$ into $V_i$.
Thus the filtered neighbor set is bijective with the entire original
candidate set of $x$. Its cardinality is at least
$(d-\varepsilon)|V_i|\geq(d/2)n$, as required.
\end{proof}
RebalancingRestrictionEstimates.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Estimates for the small restricted source]
Let $B,A$ be a finite blow-up instance with candidacy system, host and
candidacy lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regularity, and host-size window
$(1-\varepsilon)n\leq |V_i|\leq(1+\varepsilon)n$. Suppose $\varepsilon\leq a$
and $(d/2)n\leq(d-\varepsilon)|V_i|$ for every $i$.
Then the host is lower-$(a,d/2)$-regular, its sizes lie in the window
$(1-a)n\leq |V_i|\leq(1+a)n$, and every original source vertex has at
least $(d/2)n$ original candidates.
\end{lemma}
RebalancingRestrictionEstimates.title: RebalancingRestrictionEstimates

RectangleFactorCutLowerBound.lean_proof:
have ha := Finset.card_le_card hA
  have hb := Finset.card_le_card hB
  have h := hrect (U \ A) Finset.sdiff_subset (W \ B) Finset.sdiff_subset
  rw [Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hA, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hB, ← hsize] at h
  by_cases hab : A.card + B.card ≤ U.card
  · have hd : U.card - A.card + (U.card - B.card) - U.card =
        U.card - (A.card + B.card) := by omega
    rw [hd] at h
    have he : U.card = A.card + B.card + (U.card - (A.card + B.card)) := by omega
    have hm := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => k * x) he
    simp only [Nat.mul_add] at hm
    omega
  · have hle : U.card ≤ A.card + B.card := by omega
    have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left k hle
    rw [Nat.mul_add] at hm
    omega
RectangleFactorCutLowerBound.lean_statement:
theorem RectangleFactorCutLowerBound {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (k : ℕ)
    (hsize : U.card = W.card)
    (hrect : ∀ X ⊆ U, ∀ Y ⊆ W,
      k * (X.card + Y.card - U.card) ≤
        ((X ×ˢ Y).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).card)
    (A B : Finset V) (hA : A ⊆ U) (hB : B ⊆ W) :
    k * U.card ≤ k * A.card +
      (((U \ A) ×ˢ (W \ B)).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).card + k * B.card := by
RectangleFactorCutLowerBound.name: RectangleFactorCutLowerBound
RectangleFactorCutLowerBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$. The subset hypotheses give $a,b\leq n$ and
$|U\setminus A|=n-a$, $|W\setminus B|=n-b$. If $a+b\leq n$, applying
the rectangle inequality to these two complements gives
$e_G(U\setminus A,W\setminus B)\geq k(n-a-b)$. Adding $ka+kb$ yields
$kn$. If $a+b>n$, already $ka+kb=k(a+b)\geq kn$, and the edge count
is nonnegative. This also covers $n=0$ and $k=0$.
\end{proof}
RectangleFactorCutLowerBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Rectangle inequalities bound the cut expression]
Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $U,W$ be finite sets with
$|U|=|W|=n$. Let $k\in\mathbb N$ and suppose
$k\max\{0,|X|+|Y|-n\}\leq e_G(X,Y)$ for every $X\subseteq U$ and
$Y\subseteq W$. Then, for every $A\subseteq U$ and $B\subseteq W$,
\[
 kn\leq k|A|+e_G(U\setminus A,W\setminus B)+k|B|.
\]
\end{lemma}
RectangleFactorCutLowerBound.title: RectangleFactorCutLowerBound

ReducedSquareColoring.lean_proof:
classical
  intro r D R _ hD
  let S : SimpleGraph (Fin r) :=
    { Adj := fun i j => i ≠ j ∧
        (R.Adj i j ∨ ∃ k, R.Adj i k ∧ R.Adj k j)
      symm := by
        intro i j h
        refine ⟨h.1.symm, ?_⟩
        rcases h.2 with h | ⟨k, hik, hkj⟩
        · exact Or.inl h.symm
        · exact Or.inr ⟨k, hkj.symm, hik.symm⟩
      loopless := ⟨fun i h => h.1 rfl⟩ }
  have hdegree (v : Fin r) : R.degree v ≤ D :=
    (R.degree_le_maxDegree v).trans hD
  have hsdegree (v : Fin r) : S.degree v ≤ D ^ 2 := by
    let block : Fin r → Finset (Fin r) :=
      fun u => insert u ((R.neighborFinset u).erase v)
    have hblock (u : Fin r) (hu : u ∈ R.neighborFinset v) :
        (block u).card = R.degree u := by
      have hv : v ∈ R.neighborFinset u := by
        exact (R.mem_neighborFinset _ _).2 ((R.mem_neighborFinset _ _).1 hu).symm
      have hnot : u ∉ (R.neighborFinset u).erase v := by
        simp
      change (insert u ((R.neighborFinset u).erase v)).card = R.degree u
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hnot]
      exact Finset.card_erase_add_one hv
    have hsub : S.neighborFinset v ⊆ (R.neighborFinset v).biUnion block := by
      intro w hw
      have hw' : v ≠ w ∧ (R.Adj v w ∨ ∃ k, R.Adj v k ∧ R.Adj k w) :=
        (S.mem_neighborFinset _ _).1 hw
      apply Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
      rcases hw'.2 with hvw | ⟨u, hvu, huw⟩
      · exact ⟨w, (R.mem_neighborFinset _ _).2 hvw, Finset.mem_insert_self _ _⟩
      · refine ⟨u, (R.mem_neighborFinset _ _).2 hvu, Finset.mem_insert_of_mem ?_⟩
        exact Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hw'.1.symm, (R.mem_neighborFinset _ _).2 huw⟩
    calc
      S.degree v = (S.neighborFinset v).card := rfl
      _ ≤ ((R.neighborFinset v).biUnion block).card := Finset.card_le_card hsub
      _ ≤ ∑ u ∈ R.neighborFinset v, (block u).card := Finset.card_biUnion_le
      _ = ∑ u ∈ R.neighborFinset v, R.degree u := Finset.sum_congr rfl hblock
      _ ≤ ∑ _u ∈ R.neighborFinset v, D := Finset.sum_le_sum fun u _ => hdegree u
      _ = R.degree v * D := by
        rw [Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul]
        rfl
      _ ≤ D * D := Nat.mul_le_mul_right D (hdegree v)
      _ = D ^ 2 := (pow_two D).symm
  let q := D ^ 2 + 1
  have hq : 0 < q := Nat.zero_lt_succ _
  -- Extend a colouring of a finite set by choosing outside its forbidden image.
  have hcolour (s : Finset (Fin r)) :
      ∃ c : Fin r → Fin q,
        ∀ i ∈ s, ∀ j ∈ s, S.Adj i j → c i ≠ c j := by
    induction s using Finset.induction_on with
    | empty =>
        exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, hq⟩, by simp⟩
    | @insert a s ha ih =>
        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := ih
        let forbidden := ((S.neighborFinset a) ∩ s).image c
        have hcard : forbidden.card < (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin q)).card := by
          calc
            forbidden.card ≤ ((S.neighborFinset a) ∩ s).card := Finset.card_image_le
            _ ≤ (S.neighborFinset a).card := Finset.card_le_card Finset.inter_subset_left
            _ ≤ D ^ 2 := hsdegree a
            _ < (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin q)).card := by simp [q]
        obtain ⟨b, _, hb⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_notMem_of_card_lt_card hcard
        have hbne (j : Fin r) (hj : j ∈ s) (hadj : S.Adj a j) : b ≠ c j := by
          intro heq
          apply hb
          exact Finset.mem_image.mpr
            ⟨j, Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨(S.mem_neighborFinset _ _).2 hadj, hj⟩,
              heq.symm⟩
        refine ⟨fun i => if i = a then b else c i, ?_⟩
        intro i hi j hj hij
        by_cases hia : i = a
        · subst i
          have hja : j ≠ a := hij.ne.symm
          have hjs : j ∈ s := (Finset.mem_insert.mp hj).resolve_left hja
          simpa only [if_pos rfl, if_neg hja] using hbne j hjs hij
        · have his : i ∈ s := (Finset.mem_insert.mp hi).resolve_left hia
          by_cases hja : j = a
          · subst j
            simpa only [if_pos rfl, if_neg hia] using (hbne i his hij.symm).symm
          · have hjs : j ∈ s := (Finset.mem_insert.mp hj).resolve_left hja
            simpa only [if_neg hia, if_neg hja] using hc i his j hjs hij
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hcolour Finset.univ
  refine ⟨q, hq, le_rfl, c, ?_⟩
  intro i j hne hadj
  exact hc i (Finset.mem_univ _) j (Finset.mem_univ _) ⟨hne, hadj⟩
ReducedSquareColoring.lean_statement:
theorem ReducedSquareColoring :
    ∀ {r D : ℕ} (R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)) [DecidableRel R.Adj],
      R.maxDegree ≤ D →
      ∃ q : ℕ, 0 < q ∧ q ≤ D ^ 2 + 1 ∧
        ∃ colour : Fin r → Fin q,
          ∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, i ≠ j →
            (R.Adj i j ∨ ∃ k : Fin r, R.Adj i k ∧ R.Adj k j) →
            colour i ≠ colour j := by
ReducedSquareColoring.name: ReducedSquareColoring
ReducedSquareColoring.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Form the square graph $S$ on $V(R)$ by joining two distinct vertices when
they are adjacent in $R$ or have a common neighbour in $R$.  Fix $v$.
There are at most $D$ neighbours of $v$ in $R$.  For each such neighbour
$u$, there are at most $D-1$ vertices other than $v$ adjacent to $u$.
Every neighbour of $v$ in $S$ is either one of the first set or belongs to
one of the latter sets.  Hence
$\deg_S(v)\leq D+D(D-1)=D^2$.  (Repeated vertices only decrease the size of
the union.)

Order the finite vertex set arbitrarily and colour it greedily.  When a
vertex is reached, at most $D^2$ colours have appeared on its already
coloured $S$-neighbours, so one of $D^2+1$ colours remains available.
Taking $q=D^2+1$ (which is positive) proves the asserted map and bound.
If two same-coloured vertices were adjacent in $R$, they would be adjacent
in $S$; if their $R$-neighbourhoods met, their common neighbour would again
make them adjacent in $S$.  Both contradict properness, proving the final
consequences.
\end{proof}
ReducedSquareColoring.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Proper colouring of the reduced square]
Let $R$ be a finite simple graph of maximum degree at most $D$.  There are
$q\leq D^2+1$ nonempty available colours and a map
$c:V(R)\to[q]$ such that distinct vertices at distance at most two in $R$
receive different colours.  Consequently, vertices in one colour class are
nonadjacent and have pairwise disjoint $R$-neighbourhoods.
\end{lemma}
ReducedSquareColoring.title: ReducedSquareColoring

RefinedLowerSuperRegularTransfer.lean_proof:
classical
  have hkpos : 0 < k := hk
  have htwo : (2 : ENNReal) ≤ 4 * (k : ENNReal) ^ 2 + 2 := le_add_left le_rfl
  have h2ε : 2 * ε ≤ θ := (mul_le_mul_left htwo ε).trans hsmall
  have hεθ : ε ≤ θ := by
    calc
      ε ≤ 2 * ε := by
        simpa using mul_le_mul_left (by norm_num : (1 : ENNReal) ≤ 2) ε
      _ ≤ θ := h2ε
  let S (p : Fin r × Fin k) := Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p
  let F (p : Fin r × Fin k) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p
  let T (p : Fin r × Fin k) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p
  have hcap (p) : (F p).card = (S p).card := hcapacity p
  have hcap' (p) : (T p).card = (S p).card := hcapacity' p
  have hnsize (p) : n ≤ 2 * k * (S p).card := by
    have hq : 2 ≤ n / k := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hn
    have hs : n / k ≤ (S p).card := by
      rcases hsize p with h | h <;> dsimp [S] <;> omega
    have hrem := Nat.mod_lt n hkpos
    have hdecomp := Nat.mod_add_div n k
    have hstep : n ≤ k * (n / k + 1) := by nlinarith
    calc
      n ≤ k * (n / k + 1) := hstep
      _ ≤ k * (2 * (n / k)) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left k (by omega)
      _ ≤ k * (2 * (S p).card) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left k (Nat.mul_le_mul_left 2 hs)
      _ = 2 * k * (S p).card := by ring
  have hthresh (p) : ε * n ≤ θ * (S p).card := by
    calc
      ε * n ≤ ε * (2 * k * (S p).card) :=
        mul_le_mul_right (by exact_mod_cast hnsize p) ε
      _ = (2 * k * ε) * (S p).card := by ring
      _ ≤ θ * (S p).card := mul_le_mul_left hthreshold _
  have hloss (p) : 2 * k * ε * n + 2 * ε * (S p).card ≤ θ * (S p).card := by
    calc
      2 * k * ε * n + 2 * ε * (S p).card ≤
          2 * k * ε * (2 * k * (S p).card) + 2 * ε * (S p).card :=
        add_le_add (mul_le_mul_right (by exact_mod_cast hnsize p) _) le_rfl
      _ = ((4 * (k : ENNReal) ^ 2 + 2) * ε) * (S p).card := by ring
      _ ≤ θ * (S p).card := mul_le_mul_left hsmall _
  -- Additive inequalities avoid cancellation or finiteness assumptions on d.
  have htransfer (p) (P : VG → Prop) [DecidablePred P]

theorem RefinedLowerSuperRegularTransfer {r k : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}
    [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R)
    (A : CandidacySystem B) (σ : VH → Fin r × Fin k)
    (f f' : VG → Fin r × Fin k) (ε θ d : ENNReal) (n : ℕ)
    (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hn : 2 * k ≤ n) (hθ : θ < 1)
    (hsmall : (4 * (k : ENNReal) ^ 2 + 2) * ε ≤ θ)
    (hthreshold : 2 * k * ε ≤ θ)
    (hσ : ∀ x, (σ x).1 = B.sourceCluster x)
    (hf : ∀ v, (f v).1 = B.hostCluster v)
    (hf' : ∀ v, (f' v).1 = B.hostCluster v)
    (hcard : ∀ i,
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => B.sourceCluster x = i).card = n ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => B.hostCluster v = i).card = n)
    (hsize : ∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / k ∨
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / k + 1)
    (hcapacity : ∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card)
    (hcapacity' : ∀ p, (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card)
    (hchange : ∀ p, (((Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p) ∆
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = p)).card : ENNReal) ≤ 2 * k * ε * n)
    (hsource : ∀ x j, (d - 2 * ε) *
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun v => f v = (B.sourceCluster x, j)).card : ENNReal) ≤
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun v =>
        f v = (B.sourceCluster x, j) ∧ A.allowed x v).card : ENNReal))
    (hhostdegree : ∀ v i j, R.Adj (B.hostCluster v) i →
      (d - 2 * ε) * ((Finset.univ.filter fun w => f w = (i, j)).card : ENNReal) ≤
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun w => f w = (i, j) ∧ G.Adj v w).card : ENNReal))
    (hcandidatedegree : ∀ v, (d - 2 * ε) *
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = f' v).card : ENNReal) ≤
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = f' v ∧ A.allowed x v).card : ENNReal))
    (hhost : InstanceLowerSuperRegular B ε d)
    (hcand : CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d) :
    (∀ p q, R.Adj p.1 q.1 →
      LowerSuperRegularPair G (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p)
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = q) θ d) ∧
    (∀ p,
      let L : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
        ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ σ x = p
      let Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
        ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ f' v = p
      let C : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b =>
        ∃ x v, a = Sum.inl x ∧ b = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed x v
      letI : DecidableRel C.Adj := Classical.decRel _

RefinedLowerSuperRegularTransfer.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The displayed smallness bound implies $\varepsilon\leq\theta<1$,
so $\varepsilon$ is finite. Also $m\geq n/(2k)>0$.
For a refined capacity $s\geq m$,
$\varepsilon n\leq2k\varepsilon s\leq\theta s$.
Each source or corrected host bin is contained in its original bin,
by its projection identity. Thus the original lower regularity
transfers to the refined parts by \noderef{LowerRegularRestriction}.
For candidacy use the disjoint tagged copies; their inclusions and
cardinalities are precisely the ordinary fiber inclusions and sizes.
Original lower regularity is supplied by
\noderef{InstanceLowerSuperRegular} and
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}, unpacked with
\noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}.

For any fixed vertex and any predicate specifying its neighbors,
its old neighbor count is at most its new neighbor count plus the
bin symmetric-difference size. Indeed old neighbors not still in
the new bin inject into the old bin minus the new bin, a subset
of the symmetric difference. The two capacities are equal.
Consequently, from an old degree bound $(d-2\varepsilon)s$,
the new count is at least $(d-2\varepsilon)s-2k\varepsilon n$
in real notation when $d$ is finite and $d>2\varepsilon$.
Since $n\leq2ks$, the loss is at most $4k^2\varepsilon s$,
and this gives degree at least $(d-\theta)s$ on both host
orientations and for every refined source vertex into its host bin.
The host estimates apply to all original vertices, including those
which changed bins. The hypothesis on the assigned source bin
directly supplies reverse candidacy degrees; weakening
$2\varepsilon\leq\theta$ gives the desired lower bound.
Tagging preserves these degree counts: an edge from an inl endpoint
to an inr endpoint is exactly an allowed pair, with no reversed-tag
branch, so all degree clauses of \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}
hold. Together with the transferred regularity this proves both claims.

For completeness this argument remains valid with all extended
parameters in the statement. If $d$ is finite and $d\leq\theta$,
the requested degree lower endpoint is zero and no real subtraction
is needed. If $d>\theta$, it is a finite positive endpoint and the
calculation above applies. If $d=\top$ and any original required
pair or candidacy cluster exists, its positive opposite cardinality
$n$ and finite $\varepsilon$ would make its prescribed minimum degree
infinite, contradicting the finite neighbor count. Thus with $d=\top$
there can be no such original pair or candidacy cluster; the asserted
families are vacuous. Densities in the finite-$d$ cases are the same
ordered-edge ratios before and after taking tagged copies, by
\noderef{PairDensity}. Empty index sets are also vacuous.
\end{proof}
RefinedLowerSuperRegularTransfer.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Lower super-regularity after sampling and correction]
Let $B,A$ have $r$ original source and host clusters of common size $n$,
with lower $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular host and candidacy pairs.
Let $k\geq1$, $n\geq2k$, and let $\sigma$ refine the source map into
fibers of sizes $m$ or $m+1$, $m=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$. Let $f,f'$
refine the host map with exactly the same capacities. Suppose each
$f'$-bin differs from its $f$-bin in at most $2k\varepsilon n$ positions.
Suppose every source vertex has degree at least $(d-2\varepsilon)$
times the bin size into every $f$-bin of its original cluster;
every original host vertex has the same bound into every $f$-bin
of each adjacent original cluster; and every host vertex has at least
$(d-2\varepsilon)$ times the size of its assigned $\sigma$-bin
as candidacy degree into that source bin. Assume
\[
 \theta<1,\qquad (4k^2+2)\varepsilon\leq\theta,
 \qquad 2k\varepsilon\leq\theta.
\]
Then every refined host pair whose original indices are adjacent in
$R$ is lower $(\theta,d)$-super-regular, and every corresponding
tagged source/$f'$-host candidacy pair is lower
$(\theta,d)$-super-regular. Counts and parameters use extended
nonnegative reals, with truncated lower endpoints.
\end{lemma}

theorem RegularBipartiteMatchingCount :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (F : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel F.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
      (hUW : Disjoint U W) (n k : ℕ), U.card = n → W.card = n →
      (∀ u ∈ U, (W.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card = k) →
      (∀ w ∈ W, (U.filter fun u => F.Adj u w).card = k) →
      ((k : ENNReal) / (n : ENNReal)) ^ n * (n.factorial : ENNReal) ≤
        ({f : U → W | PerfectMatching F U W hUW f}.ncard : ENNReal) := by
RegularBipartiteMatchingCount.name: RegularBipartiteMatchingCount
RegularBipartiteMatchingCount.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
If $n=0$, both parts are empty. There is one function $U\to W$,
it is bijective, and all edge conditions are vacuous. Thus by
\noderef{PerfectMatching} there is exactly one perfect matching.
In extended nonnegative reals $(k/0)^0=1$, independently of $k$,
and $0!=1$, proving the assertion. Suppose $n>0$.
If $k=0$, the lower bound is $0^n n!=0$, so the assertion is immediate.
Henceforth $k>0$ too.

Choose bijections $e_U:U\to\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ and
$e_W:W\to\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, possible because both finite sets have size $n$.
Let $A_{ij}$ be the indicator that $e_U^{-1}(i)e_W^{-1}(j)$ is an edge.
For fixed $i$, summing the indicators over $j$ counts precisely the
neighbors in $W$ of $e_U^{-1}(i)$: the indexing bijection visits each vertex
of $W$ once. The degree hypothesis makes this sum $k$. The analogous
argument on columns uses the right-degree hypothesis and also gives $k$.
All entries of $A$ are nonnegative. By
\noderef{AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount}, $\operatorname{per}(A)$ is
the natural matching cardinality $M$, cast to $\mathbb R$.
This cited identity uses Mathlib's permutation orientation, so no choice
of row-versus-column convention is being suppressed.

By \noderef{RegularMatrixNormalization}, $B=A/k$ is nonnegative with
all row and column sums one, and
$\operatorname{per}(A)=k^n\operatorname{per}(B)$.
Apply the checked imported theorem
\texttt{EgorychevFalikmanFormalization.VanDerWaerdenPermanentInput}.
It states that for any real $n\times n$ matrix $B$, the hypotheses
$B_{ij}\ge0$ for every $i,j$, $\sum_jB_{ij}=1$ for every $i$, and
$\sum_iB_{ij}=1$ for every $j$ imply
\[
 \operatorname{per}(B)\ge\frac{n!}{n^n}.
\]
All three hypotheses are exactly the conclusions of
\noderef{RegularMatrixNormalization} established above for $B=A/k$.
Thus this is an application of the proved permanent bound, not an appeal
to a bibliographic citation.
Multiply by $k^n>0$ and use the normalization and count identities:
\[
 M=\operatorname{per}(A)\ge k^n\frac{n!}{n^n}
   =(k/n)^n n!.
\]
This last calculation is in $\mathbb R$, with positive denominator $n^n$.
Both $M$ and the lower bound are nonnegative and finite. Apply the monotone
map $\mathrm{ofReal}:\mathbb R\to\mathrm{ENNReal}$. For nonnegative real
arguments it preserves finite products and powers; division by the
positive real integer $n$ becomes division by its finite nonzero
$\mathrm{ENNReal}$ cast. The natural casts of $k,n,n!$, and $M$ agree with
their real casts followed by $\mathrm{ofReal}$. Consequently the resulting
inequality is exactly the stated one, not merely a real-valued variant.
\end{proof}
RegularBipartiteMatchingCount.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Matching count in a regular bipartite graph]
Let $F$ be a finite bipartite graph with disjoint parts $U,W$ of size $n$.
If every vertex on both sides has degree $k$ across the two parts, then $F$
has at least
\[
 (k/n)^n n!
\]
perfect matchings.  The assertion uses the conventions $0^0=1$ and
$0!=1$, so it also includes the empty graph on two empty parts.
\end{lemma}

  have hb0 : ∀ S, 0 ≤ b S := fun S => Nat.cast_nonneg _
  have hc0 : ∀ S, 0 ≤ c S := fun S => Nat.cast_nonneg _
  have hac : ∀ S, a S ≤ c S := fun S =>
    Nat.cast_le.mpr (Finset.card_le_card Finset.inter_subset_right)
  have hbc : ∀ S, b S ≤ c S := fun S =>
    Nat.cast_le.mpr (Finset.card_le_card Finset.inter_subset_right)
  have hsum_inter : ∀ X : Finset V,
      (∑ S ∈ P.parts, ((X ∩ S).card : ℝ)) = X.card := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    intro X
    have hpair : (P.parts : Set (Finset V)).PairwiseDisjoint (fun S => X ∩ S) := by
      intro S hS T hT hST
      exact (P.supIndep.pairwiseDisjoint hS hT hST).mono
        Finset.inter_subset_right Finset.inter_subset_right

      rw [← Finset.card_biUnion hpair, ← Finset.inter_biUnion]
      change (X ∩ P.parts.biUnion id).card = X.card
      rw [P.biUnion_parts, Finset.inter_univ]

    simpa only [a, hU] using hsum_inter U
  have hb : (∑ S ∈ P.parts, b S) = n := by
    simpa only [b, hW] using hsum_inter W
  have hc : (∑ S ∈ P.parts, c S) = 2 * n := hsum
  have hbadU : (∑ S ∈ P.parts, if ¬γ * c S ≤ a S then a S else 0) ≤
      2 * γ * n := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ S ∈ P.parts, γ * c S := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro S hS
        split_ifs with h
        · exact mul_nonneg hγ.le (hc0 S)
        · exact (lt_of_not_ge h).le
      _ = _ := by rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hc]; ring
  have hbadW : (∑ S ∈ P.parts, if ¬γ * c S ≤ b S then b S else 0) ≤
      2 * γ * n := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ S ∈ P.parts, γ * c S := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro S hS
        split_ifs with h
        · exact mul_nonneg hγ.le (hc0 S)
        · exact (lt_of_not_ge h).le
      _ = _ := by rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hc]; ring
  have hareaU : (∑ ST ∈ R,
      if ¬γ * c ST.1 ≤ a ST.1 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) ≤
      2 * γ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    calc
      _ = ∑ S ∈ P.parts,
          (if ¬γ * c S ≤ a S then a S else 0) * n := by
        change (∑ ST ∈ P.parts ×ˢ P.parts,
          if ¬γ * c ST.1 ≤ a ST.1 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) = _
        rw [Finset.sum_product]
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro S hS
        by_cases h : ¬γ * c S ≤ a S
        · simp only [h, not_false_eq_true, if_true, ← Finset.mul_sum, hb]
        · simp only [h, if_false, Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_mul]
      _ = (∑ S ∈ P.parts, if ¬γ * c S ≤ a S then a S else 0) * n :=
        (Finset.sum_mul _ _ _).symm
      _ ≤ (2 * γ * n) * n := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbadU hnr.le
      _ = _ := by ring
  have hareaW : (∑ ST ∈ R,
      if ¬γ * c ST.2 ≤ b ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) ≤
      2 * γ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by

        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

      if ST.1 = ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) ≤
      6 / (l : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by

    calc

  -- The causes may overlap; their nonnegative indicators overcount the complement.
  have hpoint : ∀ ST ∈ R,
      (if ST ∉ E then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) ≤
        (if ¬γ * c ST.1 ≤ a ST.1 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) +
        (if ¬γ * c ST.2 ≤ b ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) +
        (if ST ∈ P.nonUniforms G α then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) +
        (if ST.1 = ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) := by
    intro ST hST
    have hp : ST.1 ∈ P.parts ∧ ST.2 ∈ P.parts := Finset.mem_product.mp hST

      exact ite_nonneg hweight (le_refl 0)
    have hW0 : 0 ≤ (if ¬γ * c ST.2 ≤ b ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) := by
      exact ite_nonneg hweight (le_refl 0)
    have hN0 : 0 ≤ (if ST ∈ P.nonUniforms G α then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) := by
      exact ite_nonneg hweight (le_refl 0)
    have hD0 : 0 ≤ (if ST.1 = ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) := by
      exact ite_nonneg hweight (le_refl 0)
    by_cases hnot : ST ∉ E
    · rw [if_pos hnot]
      have hcauses : ST.1 = ST.2 ∨ ¬γ * c ST.1 ≤ a ST.1 ∨
          ¬γ * c ST.2 ≤ b ST.2 ∨ ST ∈ P.nonUniforms G α := by

        push Not at h
        rcases h with ⟨hD, hU, hW, hN⟩

      · rw [if_pos hU]
        linarith only [hW0, hN0, hD0]
      · rw [if_pos hW]
        linarith only [hU0, hN0, hD0]
      · rw [if_pos hN]
        linarith only [hU0, hW0, hD0]
    · rw [if_neg hnot]
      linarith only [hU0, hW0, hN0, hD0]
  change (∑ ST ∈ R.filter (fun ST => ST ∉ E), a ST.1 * b ST.2) ≤ _
  rw [Finset.sum_filter]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ ST ∈ R,
        ((if ¬γ * c ST.1 ≤ a ST.1 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) +
        (if ¬γ * c ST.2 ≤ b ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) +
        (if ST ∈ P.nonUniforms G α then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0) +
        (if ST.1 = ST.2 then a ST.1 * b ST.2 else 0)) :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum hpoint

      rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      linarith only [hareaU, hareaW, hareaN, hareaD]

theorem RegularExtractionIneligibleArea
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
    (n l : ℕ) (γ α : ℝ)
    (hU : U.card = n) (hW : W.card = n)
    (hl : 1 ≤ l) (hγ : 0 < γ) (hα : 0 < α)
    (P : Finpartition (Finset.univ : Finset V))
    (heq : P.IsEquipartition) (hlP : l ≤ P.parts.card)
    (hPn : P.parts.card ≤ n)
    (htotal : (Finset.univ : Finset V).card = 2 * n)
    (hunif : P.IsUniform G α)
    (hsize : ∀ S ∈ P.parts, (S.card : ℝ) ≤ 3 * n / P.parts.card)
    (E : Finset (Finset V × Finset V))
    (hE : ∀ S T, (S, T) ∈ E ↔
      S ∈ P.parts ∧ T ∈ P.parts ∧ S ≠ T ∧ G.IsUniform α S T ∧
      γ * S.card ≤ ((U ∩ S).card : ℝ) ∧
      γ * T.card ≤ ((W ∩ T).card : ℝ)) :
    (∑ ST ∈ (P.parts.product P.parts).filter (fun ST => ST ∉ E),
      (((U ∩ ST.1).card : ℝ) * (W ∩ ST.2).card)) ≤
      (4 * γ + 9 * α + 6 / (l : ℝ)) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by

RegularExtractionIneligibleArea.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $a_S=|U\cap S|$, $b_S=|W\cap S|$, and $c_S=|S|$.
The parts are disjoint and cover all vertices. Intersecting with $U$
or $W$ preserves disjointness and gives a cover of that set. Consequently
$\sum_S a_S=\sum_S b_S=n$ and $\sum_S c_S=2n$.
All three quantities are nonnegative, and $a_S,b_S\leq c_S$.

For a nonsubstantial $U$ chunk, $a_S<\gamma c_S$. Hence
$\sum_{S:a_S<\gamma c_S}a_S\leq\gamma\sum_S c_S=2\gamma n$.
Summing its rectangle areas over all $T$ multiplies this bound by
$\sum_T b_T=n$, giving $2\gamma n^2$. The identical argument with
$b_T<\gamma c_T$ gives another $2\gamma n^2$.

Let $N$ be the set of ordered distinct nonuniform pairs. Its cardinality
is at most $\alpha m(m-1)\leq\alpha m^2$. For each such pair,
$a_Sb_T\leq c_Sc_T\leq(3n/m)^2$. Since $m\geq l\geq1$,
division by $m$ is legitimate, and the total area over $N$ is at most
$\alpha m^2(3n/m)^2=9\alpha n^2$.

The diagonal area satisfies
\[
 \sum_S a_Sb_S\leq\sum_S c_S^2
 \leq (3n/m)\sum_S c_S=6n^2/m\leq6n^2/l.
\]
Finally, every pair outside $E$ is diagonal, has a nonsubstantial chunk
on at least one side, or is distinct and nonuniform. Pointwise its area
is at most the sum of the four corresponding nonnegative area indicators.
This does not require these causes to be disjoint: repetitions increase
the bound. Summing and using the four estimates proves the claim.
\end{proof}
RegularExtractionIneligibleArea.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Area of ineligible partition rectangles]
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $U,W$ be vertex sets of size $n$.
Let $\mathcal P$ be an equipartition of the full vertex set, which has size
$2n$, and put $m=|\mathcal P|$. Suppose $1\leq l\leq m\leq n$,
$\gamma,\alpha>0$, every part has size at most $3n/m$, and
$\mathcal P$ is $\alpha$-uniform: at most $\alpha m(m-1)$ ordered
distinct pairs of parts fail $\alpha$-uniformity.
Let $E$ consist exactly of pairs $(S,T)$ of parts satisfying $S\ne T$,
$\alpha$-uniformity, $\gamma|S|\leq|U\cap S|$, and
$\gamma|T|\leq|W\cap T|$. Then
\[
 \sum_{(S,T)\in(\mathcal P\times\mathcal P)\setminus E}
 |U\cap S||W\cap T|
 \leq (4\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)n^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

RegularExtractionParameters.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Set $h=\min\{\eta/100,1/100\}$, $\gamma=h^4/100$,
$\alpha=\gamma^2/4$, and $l=\lceil100/h^4\rceil$.
Then $0<h\leq1/100$, $h<\eta$, $0<\gamma<1$,
$0<\alpha\leq\gamma/4$, $\alpha\leq\gamma^2$, $l\geq1$,
and $1/l\leq\gamma$. Put
$M=\max\{1,l,\operatorname{SzemerediRegularity.bound}(\alpha,l)\}$
and $\varepsilon=\min\{\eta/2,\gamma/(2M)\}$.
The two entries of this last minimum are positive, so
$0<\varepsilon<\eta$ and $\varepsilon M\leq\gamma/2<\gamma$.
The required upper bounds on $l$ and the regularity bound hold by
the definition of $M$.

To check the margin, $\alpha\leq\gamma/4$ and $1/l\leq\gamma$
give $6\gamma+9\alpha+6/l\leq(57/4)\gamma<15\gamma$.
Also $2\alpha\leq h^4/200$. Consequently
\[
 2\alpha+\frac{6\gamma+9\alpha+6/l}{h^2}
 \leq h^4/200+15h^2/100
 \leq31h^2/200<h/4.
\]
The middle inequality uses $h\leq1$, and the last uses
$0<h\leq1/100$.

$n_0\geq16\log4/h^4$ and
$n_0^2\geq16\log4/h^4$. Such an integer exists because $h>0$;
for example take a ceiling exceeding the first quantity and its
square root. For $n\geq n_0$ we have
$n\log4\leq h^4n^2/16$ and $h^4n^2/16\geq\log4$.
Using $4^n=\exp(n\log4)$, the expression in the statement is at most
$2\exp(-h^4n^2/16)\leq2\exp(-\log4)=1/2<1$.
This proves the uniform cutoff as well as all scalar conditions.
\end{proof}
RegularExtractionParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform extraction parameters]
For every real $0<\eta<1$, there exist reals $h,\gamma,\alpha,\varepsilon$
and natural numbers $l,M,n_0$ such that
\[
 0<h<\eta,\quad h\leq1/100,\quad
 0<\gamma\leq1,\quad 0<\alpha\leq\gamma,\quad\alpha\leq\gamma^2.
\]
\[
 0<\varepsilon<\eta,\quad \varepsilon M<\gamma,\quad
 1\leq l\leq M,\quad
 \operatorname{SzemerediRegularity.bound}(\alpha,l)\leq M,
 \quad1\leq n_0,\quad M\leq n_0,
\]
\[
 2\alpha+\frac{6\gamma+9\alpha+6/l}{h^2}<h/4,
 \qquad
 2\,4^n\exp(-h^4n^2/8)<1\quad(n\geq n_0).
\]
All choices depend only on $\eta$.
\end{lemma}

RegularExtractionPartitionGeometry.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The disjoint cover gives $|V|=2n$. The equipartition condition says
that sizes of parts differ by at most one. Their sum is $2n$, so each
size lies between $\lfloor2n/m\rfloor$ and $\lceil2n/m\rceil$:
if a size were below the floor, every size would be at most the floor,
with at least one strictly below it, contradicting the sum; the
argument for the ceiling is the reverse inequality. Since
$1\leq l\leq m\leq M\leq n$, it follows that
$|S|\geq2n/m-1\geq n/m$ and $|S|\leq2n/m+1\leq3n/m$.
In particular $n>0$, $m>0$, and every part is nonempty.

Define $E$ by the four conditions in the statement, restricted to
$\mathcal P\times\mathcal P$. A substantial chunk, for example
$U\cap S$ of size at least $\gamma|S|$, has size at least
$\gamma n/m\geq\gamma n/M>\varepsilon n$. Here $M>0$ and
$n>0$, and the strict last inequality is precisely
$\varepsilon M<\gamma$. Thus for every eligible pair the assumed
lower density bound applies to its chunks and gives $D_{ST}\geq d>0$.
Both chunks are nonempty. The number of edges is at most the
Cartesian-product size, so $D_{ST}\leq1$.

For the smaller sets in the statement,
$|A|>\gamma|U\cap S|\geq\gamma^2|S|\geq\alpha|S|$, and the
same holds for $B,T$. Moreover the chunks themselves have size at
least $\gamma|S|\geq\alpha|S|$, and similarly on the other side.
The actual uniformity condition is the subset test with weak size
thresholds $\alpha|S|,\alpha|T|$ and a strict error $\alpha$.
Applying it once to $A,B$ and once to the two chunks bounds each
density's distance from $d_G(S,T)$ by $\alpha$. The triangle
inequality gives the strict error $2\alpha$ asserted above.

It remains to count all ineligible positions. Nonsubstantial
$U$ chunks have total size at most
$\gamma\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}|S|=2\gamma n$; multiplying by $|W|=n$
bounds all rectangles with such a chunk by $2\gamma n^2$.
Nonsubstantial $W$ chunks cost at most another $2\gamma n^2$.
The definition of $\mathcal P$ being $\alpha$-uniform bounds the
number of ordered distinct nonuniform pairs by $\alpha m(m-1)$.
Each rectangle for such a pair has area at most $(3n/m)^2$, so
their total area is at most $9\alpha n^2$. This counts ordered
pairs, not unordered pairs, exactly as required for $U\times W$.
The diagonal pairs cost at most
\[
 \sum_S |U\cap S||W\cap S|
 \leq\sum_S|S|^2
 \leq(3n/m)\sum_S|S|=6n^2/m\leq6n^2/l.
\]
Every ineligible pair either has a nonsubstantial chunk, is a
distinct nonuniform pair, or is diagonal. Summing the three bounds
therefore covers every ineligible position. Repeated coverage can
only increase the upper bound, proving the stated area inequality.
\end{proof}
RegularExtractionPartitionGeometry.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Equitable extraction geometry]
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let disjoint sets $U,W$ cover its
vertex set, with $|U|=|W|=n$. Let $1\leq l$, $M\leq n$, and let real
parameters satisfy $\varepsilon,d,\gamma,\alpha>0$, $\gamma\leq1$,
$\alpha\leq\gamma$, $\alpha\leq\gamma^2$, and
$\varepsilon M<\gamma$. Assume $d_G(A,B)\geq d$ whenever
$A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq W$, and $|A|,|B|>\varepsilon n$.
Let $\mathcal P$ be a partition of the entire vertex set into nonempty
parts whose sizes differ by at most one, with
$l\leq m=|\mathcal P|\leq M$. Assume at most $\alpha m(m-1)$ ordered
distinct pairs of parts fail $\alpha$-uniformity. Here $(S,T)$ is
$\alpha$-uniform precisely when every $A\subseteq S$, $B\subseteq T$
with $|A|\geq\alpha|S|$, $|B|\geq\alpha|T|$ satisfies
$|d_G(A,B)-d_G(S,T)|<\alpha$, with zero density when a denominator
is zero.
Then every part $S$ satisfies $n/m\leq|S|\leq3n/m$.
There is a set $E\subseteq\mathcal P\times\mathcal P$ consisting
exactly of pairs $(S,T)$ with $S\ne T$, $(S,T)$ $\alpha$-uniform,
$|U\cap S|\geq\gamma|S|$, and $|W\cap T|\geq\gamma|T|$.
For $(S,T)\in E$, put $D_{ST}=d_G(U\cap S,W\cap T)$. Then
$d\leq D_{ST}\leq1$. For $A\subseteq U\cap S$, $B\subseteq W\cap T$
with $|A|>\gamma|U\cap S|$, $|B|>\gamma|W\cap T|$,
\[
 |d_G(A,B)-D_{ST}|<2\alpha.
\]
Finally the total area of the ineligible rectangles satisfies
\[
 \sum_{(S,T)\in(\mathcal P\times\mathcal P)\setminus E}
       |U\cap S||W\cap T|
 \leq (4\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)n^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

    ENNReal.ofReal_pow hnonneg, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, hcoef] using hENN
RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal

theorem RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound :
    ∀ ε d κ : ENNReal, 0 < ε → 0 < d → d ≤ 1 → κ * κ = ε →
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
        (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
        (U W S T : Finset V) (hST : Disjoint S T) (n y : ℕ),
        n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n →
        RegularPair G U W ε d → S ⊆ U → T ⊆ W →
        S.card = y → T.card = y → κ * n ≤ y →
        ({f : S → T | PerfectMatching G S T hST f}.ncard : ENNReal) ≤
          (d + ε + 3 * κ) ^ y * (y.factorial : ENNReal) := by
RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound.name: RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound
RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $c=d+\varepsilon+3\kappa$ and let $m$ denote the number of perfect
matchings. If $c\ge1$, take $n_0=0$. The hypotheses $|S|=|T|=y$ and
\noderef{PerfectMatchingBijectionBound} give $m\le y!$, and
$c^y\ge1$ gives $m\le c^y y!$. This argument also covers $y=0$ and
infinite parameter values; the zeroth power is one.

Assume now $c<1$. All parameters are finite: $d,\varepsilon$ are bounded
by $c$, and $3\kappa\le c$ bounds $\kappa$. The identity
$\kappa^2=\varepsilon>0$ implies $\kappa>0$, and $c<1$ implies
$\kappa<1/3$. Consequently $\varepsilon=\kappa^2<\kappa$.
Conversion to real numbers preserves these finite nonnegative
parameters, their sums, products, inequalities, and powers. In the rest
of this branch use real notation for them, and put $D=d+\varepsilon>0$.

Apply \noderef{FactorialRootExceptionalProduct} to $D,\kappa$, obtaining
a positive integer $y_0$ depending only on those parameters. Choose an
integer $n_0>y_0/\kappa+1$. For $n\ge n_0$ and $y\ge\kappa n$ we have
$n>0$ and $y>y_0$. In particular $y>0$, so the empty induced graph
cannot occur in this branch.

Index $S$ and $T$ by $\{0,\ldots,y-1\}$, and write
$r_i=|N_G(e_S^{-1}(i))\cap T|$. Each $r_i\le y$, since its neighbor set
is a subset of $T$. To bound the exceptional indices, note that
$\varepsilon=\kappa^2<\kappa<1/3$, so $\varepsilon\le1$.
Since $n>0$, we have
$|T|=y\ge\kappa n>\varepsilon n=\varepsilon|W|$.
Apply \noderef{RegularPairUpperTail} with left part $U$, right part $W$,
and tested subset $T$, using the given regularity and $d\le1$.
It bounds the full $U$-tail
$B=\{v\in U:|N_G(v)\cap T|>(d+\varepsilon)y\}$ by
$|B|\le\varepsilon|U|=\varepsilon n$.
Let $A=\{v\in S:|N_G(v)\cap T|>(D+\kappa)y\}$.
Since $S\subseteq U$ and $(D+\kappa)y\ge Dy$, we have $A\subseteq B$.
The indexing bijection $e_S^{-1}$ restricts to a bijection from
$\{i:r_i>(D+\kappa)y\}$ onto $A$, so its cardinality $k$ equals $|A|$.
All thresholds are finite: $d+\varepsilon$ is finite, and all set
cardinalities are natural numbers. Their finite extended-real products
convert to the displayed real products, and strict comparison is
preserved by this conversion. Thus the real inequality defining $A$
implies the extended-real inequality defining $B$; converting the
extended-real tail bound back to reals gives
\[
 k=|A|\le |B|\le\varepsilon n
   =\kappa^2 n\le\kappa y,
\]
where the last step multiplies $\kappa n\le y$ by $\kappa>0$.

For the matching-product bound use \noderef{BregmanMatchingDegreeProduct}.
Its natural-number matrix has entry one exactly on the edges between
the indexed parts. Its zero-one hypothesis holds entrywise, its row
supports have cardinalities $r_i$, and its permanent is $m$ after the
natural-to-real cast, by \noderef{AdjacencyPermanentMatchingCount}.
That adapter applies the two branches of the checked imported theorem
\texttt{EntropyMethodsFormalization.BregmanMinc}. If a row has degree
zero, it gives $m=0$, and the assertion follows from nonnegativity.
Otherwise it gives
\[
 m\le\prod_{i=0}^{y-1}(r_i!)^{1/r_i}.
\]
All degrees are now positive and at most $y$, the exceptional count is
at most $\kappa y$, and $y\ge y_0$. Hence
\noderef{FactorialRootExceptionalProduct} gives
\[
 \prod_i(r_i!)^{1/r_i}\le(D+3\kappa)^y y!.
\]
In that estimate the increasing factorial roots bound exceptional rows
by $(y!)^{1/y}$; ordinary and low-degree rows are bounded by
$(y!)^{1/y}xe^{\delta_y}$, where
$x=D+2\kappa$ and $\delta_y=(\log y+1)/(\kappa y)$.
The positive margin
$\log((x+\kappa)/x)-\kappa\log(1/x)$ absorbs both this factorial loss
and the at most $\kappa y$ exceptional rows. Thus the regularity and
factorial losses, not just the imported permanent inequality, are
accounted for.

Combining the inequalities proves the real bound $m\le c^y y!$.
Apply the order-preserving map from nonnegative real numbers to
extended nonnegative real numbers. It preserves the products and
powers here and sends the natural-number count and factorial to their
usual casts. Since $c$ is finite it recovers precisely the original
coefficient. This yields the stated extended-real inequality. The
choice of $n_0$ involves only $D,\kappa$ and hence only the stipulated
parameters, and is uniform over the graph, the parts, and the subsets.
\end{proof}
RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Upper enumeration in large induced subgraphs]
For every $\varepsilon>0$ and $0<d\le1$ there is $n_0$ such that the following holds.  Let $G[U,W]$ be an $(\varepsilon,d)$-regular pair with $|U|=|W|=n\ge n_0$.  If $S\subseteq U$, $T\subseteq W$, $S\cap T=\varnothing$, $|S|=|T|=y$, and $y\ge\sqrt\varepsilon n$, then the number of perfect matchings in $G[S,T]$ is at most
\[
 (d+\varepsilon+3\sqrt\varepsilon)^y y!.
\]
Here a missing edge can only reduce the number, so the assertion also applies to any balanced subgraph induced by prescribed subsets of the two parts.
\end{lemma}
RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound.title: RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound

RegularMatrixNormalization.lean_proof:
dsimp only
  have hkR : (k : ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.ne_of_gt hk)
  refine ⟨fun i j => div_nonneg (hA i j) (Nat.cast_nonneg _), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    rw [← Finset.sum_div, hrow, div_self hkR]
  · intro j
    rw [← Finset.sum_div, hcol, div_self hkR]
  · have hscale : (k : ℝ) • (fun i j => A i j / (k : ℝ)) = A := by
      ext i j
      simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      exact mul_div_cancel₀ (A i j) hkR
    simpa only [Fintype.card_fin] using
      (Matrix.permanent_smul (fun i j => A i j / (k : ℝ)) (k : ℝ)).symm.trans
        (congrArg Matrix.permanent hscale) |>.symm
RegularMatrixNormalization.lean_statement:
open scoped BigOperators

theorem RegularMatrixNormalization {n : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hA : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ A i j)
    (hrow : ∀ i, ∑ j, A i j = (k : ℝ))
    (hcol : ∀ j, ∑ i, A i j = (k : ℝ)) :
    let B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ := fun i j => A i j / k
    (∀ i j, 0 ≤ B i j) ∧ (∀ i, ∑ j, B i j = 1) ∧
    (∀ j, ∑ i, B i j = 1) ∧
    Matrix.permanent A = (k : ℝ) ^ n * Matrix.permanent B := by
RegularMatrixNormalization.name: RegularMatrixNormalization
RegularMatrixNormalization.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Division by the positive real number $k$ preserves nonnegativity.
Finite sums commute with division, so every row and column sum becomes
$k/k=1$. Entrywise $A=kB$. For each permutation in Mathlib's permanent
there are exactly $n$ factors; factoring $k$ from each gives
$\prod_j A_{\sigma(j),j}=k^n\prod_jB_{\sigma(j),j}$.
Summing proves the identity, also for the empty product.
\end{proof}
RegularMatrixNormalization.title: RegularMatrixNormalization

RegularPair.lean_proof:
∀ U ⊆ V₁, ∀ W ⊆ V₂,
    ε * (V₁.card : ENNReal) < (U.card : ENNReal) →
    ε * (V₂.card : ENNReal) < (W.card : ENNReal) →
      d - ε ≤ PairDensity G U W ∧ PairDensity G U W ≤ d + ε
RegularPair.lean_statement:
def RegularPair {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (V₁ V₂ : Finset V) (ε d : ENNReal) : Prop :=
RegularPair.name: RegularPair
RegularPair.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}
Let $G$ be a simple graph on an arbitrary vertex type, let $V_1,V_2$ be arbitrary finite vertex subsets, and let $\varepsilon,d$ be arbitrary extended nonnegative reals.  The ordered pair $(V_1,V_2)$ is an $(\varepsilon,d)$-regular pair if every finite $U\subseteq V_1$ and $W\subseteq V_2$ satisfying $|U|>\varepsilon|V_1|$ and $|W|>\varepsilon|V_2|$ has
\[
d-\varepsilon\leq d_G(U,W)\leq d+\varepsilon,
\]
where density is as in \noderef{PairDensity}.  The paper uses this predicate for finite ambient graphs, disjoint cluster fibers, $\varepsilon>0$, and $0<d<1$.
\end{definition}
RegularPair.title: RegularPair

RegularPairGoodCodegrees.lean_proof:
classical
  intro V _ G _ U W n ε d hU hW hε hsr
  by_cases hn : n = 0
  · have hWempty : W = ∅ := Finset.card_eq_zero.mp (hW.trans hn)
    simp only [hWempty, Finset.empty_product, Finset.filter_empty,
      Finset.card_empty, Nat.cast_zero, zero_le]
  simpa only [hW] using
    SuperRegularCodegreeExceptionalBound G U W n ε d hU hn hε hsr
RegularPairGoodCodegrees.lean_statement:
theorem RegularPairGoodCodegrees :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      (U W : Finset V) (n : ℕ) (ε d : ENNReal),
      U.card = n → W.card = n → 2 * ε < d →
      SuperRegularPair G U W ε d →
      (((W ×ˢ W).filter fun z =>
          let C := (U.filter fun u => G.Adj u z.1 ∧ G.Adj u z.2).card
          (C : ENNReal) < (d - 2 * ε) ^ 2 * n ∨
            (d + 2 * ε) ^ 2 * n < (C : ENNReal)).card : ENNReal) ≤
        2 * ε * n ^ 2 := by
RegularPairGoodCodegrees.name: RegularPairGoodCodegrees
RegularPairGoodCodegrees.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
If $n=0$, then $W$ is empty and there are no ordered pairs to count.
If $n>0$, apply \noderef{SuperRegularCodegreeExceptionalBound} with
the given $U,W,n,\varepsilon,d$.  Its hypotheses are exactly the
super-regularity, $|U|=n$, positivity of $n$, and $2\varepsilon<d$
assumed here.  It bounds the bad ordered pairs, with the same
common-neighborhood window, by $2\varepsilon|W|^2$.
Substituting $|W|=n$ gives $2\varepsilon n^2$, as required.
\end{proof}
RegularPairGoodCodegrees.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Good codegrees in a regular pair]
Let $G[U,W]$ be an $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular pair, where $|U|=|W|=n$ and $2\varepsilon<d$.  Then at most $2\varepsilon n^2$ ordered pairs $(w,w')\in W^2$ fail
\[
 (d-2\varepsilon)^2n\le |N(w)\cap N(w')\cap U|
 \le (d+2\varepsilon)^2n.
\]
\end{lemma}
RegularPairGoodCodegrees.title: RegularPairGoodCodegrees

RegularPairLowerTail.lean_proof:
classical
  let T := L.filter fun v => ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) <
    (d - ε) * S.card
  change (T.card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * L.card
  by_contra hbound
  have hTsize : ε * L.card < T.card := lt_of_not_ge hbound
  have hTzero : (T.card : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt ((zero_le _).trans_lt hTsize)
  have hSzero : (S.card : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt ((zero_le _).trans_lt hsize)
  have hTnonempty : T.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by exact_mod_cast
    ((zero_le _).trans_lt hTsize : (0 : ENNReal) < T.card))
  have hdenzero : (T.card : ENNReal) * S.card ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero hTzero hSzero
  have hdenfinite : (T.card : ENNReal) * S.card ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by simp) (by simp)
  have hsum : (∑ v ∈ T, ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal)) <
      ∑ _v ∈ T, (d - ε) * S.card := by
    apply ENNReal.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty hTnonempty
    intro v hv
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2
  have hdensity : PairDensity G T S < d - ε := by
    unfold PairDensity
    apply (ENNReal.div_lt_iff (Or.inl hdenzero) (Or.inl hdenfinite)).mpr
    rw [FilteredProductRowCount T S G.Adj]
    simpa only [Nat.cast_sum, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, mul_comm,
      mul_left_comm] using hsum
  exact (not_lt_of_ge (hreg T (Finset.filter_subset _ _) S hS hTsize hsize).1) hdensity
RegularPairLowerTail.lean_statement:
theorem RegularPairLowerTail {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (L R S : Finset V) (ε d : ENNReal) (_hε : ε ≤ 1) (_hd : d ≤ 1)
    (hreg : RegularPair G L R ε d) (hS : S ⊆ R)
    (hsize : ε * R.card < S.card) :
    ((L.filter fun v => ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) <
      (d - ε) * S.card).card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * L.card := by
RegularPairLowerTail.name: RegularPairLowerTail
RegularPairLowerTail.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $T$ be the displayed strict lower tail. Suppose, for contradiction, that $|T|>\varepsilon|L|$.
Both $T$ and $S$ are nonempty because these thresholds are nonnegative, so $|T||S|$ is positive and finite.
By \noderef{FilteredProductRowCount}, the ordered edge count between $T$ and $S$ is
$e_G(T,S)=\sum_{v\in T}|N_G(v)\cap S|$.
Each summand is strictly less than $(d-\varepsilon)_+|S|$.
Summing over the nonempty set $T$ gives
$e_G(T,S)<(d-\varepsilon)_+|T||S|$.
Dividing by the positive finite denominator and using \noderef{PairDensity} gives
$d_G(T,S)<(d-\varepsilon)_+$.
On the other hand, $T\subseteq L$ and $S\subseteq R$ satisfy both strict thresholds, so \noderef{RegularPair} gives $d_G(T,S)\geq(d-\varepsilon)_+$, a contradiction.
Thus $|T|\leq\varepsilon|L|$.
No positivity of $\varepsilon$ was used: when the endpoint is zero the strict lower tail is simply empty.
\end{proof}
RegularPairLowerTail.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Lower exceptional tail of a regular pair]
Let $G$ be a graph and $L,R$ finite vertex sets, and let $\varepsilon,d\in[0,1]$.
Suppose $G[L,R]$ is $(\varepsilon,d)$-regular, and $S\subseteq R$ satisfies $|S|>\varepsilon|R|$.
Then
\[
 |\{v\in L:|N_G(v)\cap S|<(d-\varepsilon)_+|S|\}|\leq\varepsilon|L|.
\]
The difference is truncated subtraction in the extended nonnegative reals.
\end{lemma}
RegularPairLowerTail.title: RegularPairLowerTail

RegularPairUpperTail.lean_proof:
classical
  let T := L.filter fun v => (d + ε) * S.card <
    ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal)
  change (T.card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * L.card
  by_contra hbound
  have hTsize : ε * L.card < T.card := lt_of_not_ge hbound
  have hTzero : (T.card : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt ((zero_le _).trans_lt hTsize)
  have hSzero : (S.card : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt ((zero_le _).trans_lt hsize)
  have hTnonempty : T.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by exact_mod_cast
    ((zero_le _).trans_lt hTsize : (0 : ENNReal) < T.card))
  have hdenzero : (T.card : ENNReal) * S.card ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero hTzero hSzero
  have hdenfinite : (T.card : ENNReal) * S.card ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by simp) (by simp)
  have hsum : (∑ _v ∈ T, (d + ε) * S.card) <
      ∑ v ∈ T, ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal) := by
    apply ENNReal.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty hTnonempty
    intro v hv
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2
  have hdensity : d + ε < PairDensity G T S := by
    unfold PairDensity
    apply (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt (Or.inl hdenzero) (Or.inl hdenfinite)).mpr
    rw [FilteredProductRowCount T S G.Adj]
    simpa only [Nat.cast_sum, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, mul_comm,
      mul_left_comm] using hsum
  exact (not_lt_of_ge (hreg T (Finset.filter_subset _ _) S hS hTsize hsize).2) hdensity
RegularPairUpperTail.lean_statement:
theorem RegularPairUpperTail {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (L R S : Finset V) (ε d : ENNReal) (_hε : ε ≤ 1) (_hd : d ≤ 1)
    (hreg : RegularPair G L R ε d) (hS : S ⊆ R)
    (hsize : ε * R.card < S.card) :
    ((L.filter fun v => (d + ε) * S.card <
      ((S.filter fun z => G.Adj v z).card : ENNReal)).card : ENNReal) ≤ ε * L.card := by
RegularPairUpperTail.name: RegularPairUpperTail
RegularPairUpperTail.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $T$ be the displayed strict upper tail. If $|T|>\varepsilon|L|$, then $T$ and $S$ are nonempty and $|T||S|$ is positive and finite.
By \noderef{FilteredProductRowCount}, $e_G(T,S)=\sum_{v\in T}|N_G(v)\cap S|$.
Summing the strict inequalities defining $T$ over this nonempty set gives
$e_G(T,S)>(d+\varepsilon)|T||S|$.
By division by the positive finite product and \noderef{PairDensity}, $d_G(T,S)>d+\varepsilon$.
But $T\subseteq L$ and $S\subseteq R$ meet the strict size thresholds in \noderef{RegularPair}, which gives $d_G(T,S)\leq d+\varepsilon$.
This contradiction proves the non-strict cardinality bound.
The argument includes $\varepsilon=0$, since no division by $\varepsilon$ occurs.
\end{proof}
RegularPairUpperTail.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Upper exceptional tail of a regular pair]
Let $G$ be a graph and $L,R$ finite vertex sets, and let $\varepsilon,d\in[0,1]$.
Suppose $G[L,R]$ is $(\varepsilon,d)$-regular, and $S\subseteq R$ satisfies $|S|>\varepsilon|R|$.
Then
\[
 |\{v\in L:|N_G(v)\cap S|>(d+\varepsilon)|S|\}|\leq\varepsilon|L|.
\]
\end{lemma}
RegularPairUpperTail.title: RegularPairUpperTail

RegularSubgraph.lean_proof:
classical
  intro η d hη hη1 hd hd1
  have hηfin : η ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hη1
  have hdfin : d ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hd1
  have hηR : 0 < η.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hη.ne' hηfin
  have hdR : 0 < d.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hd.ne' hdfin
  have hηR1 : η.toReal < 1 := by
    simpa using (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hηfin (by simp)).mpr hη1
  have hdR1 : d.toReal < 1 := by
    simpa using (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hdfin (by simp)).mpr hd1
  obtain ⟨h, γ, α, ε, l, M, n₀, hh, hhη, hh100, hγ, hγ1, hα,
    hαγ, hαγγ, hε, hεη, hεM, hl, hlM, hbound, hn₀, hMn₀, hmargin, hcut⟩ :=
    RegularExtractionParameters η.toReal hηR hηR1
  refine ⟨ENNReal.ofReal ε, n₀, ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hε, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_iff_lt_toReal hε.le hηfin).mpr hεη
  intro V _ _ G _ U W n hn hU hW hUW hcover _ hlow
  have hMn : M ≤ n := hMn₀.trans hn
  have hnpos : 0 < n := lt_of_lt_of_le (by omega : 0 < n₀) hn
  have hnr : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hnpos
  have hV : Fintype.card V = n + n := by
    have hc := Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hUW
    rw [hcover, Finset.card_univ, hU, hW] at hc
    exact hc
  have hlV : l ≤ Fintype.card V := by rw [hV]; omega
  have hlower : ∀ A ⊆ U, ∀ B ⊆ W,
      ε * n < (A.card : ℝ) → ε * n < (B.card : ℝ) →
      d.toReal ≤ (G.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) := by
    intro A hAU B hBW hA hB
    have hApos : 0 < A.card := by
      have : (0 : ℝ) < A.card := (mul_pos hε hnr).trans hA
      exact_mod_cast this
    have hBpos : 0 < B.card := by
      have : (0 : ℝ) < B.card := (mul_pos hε hnr).trans hB
      exact_mod_cast this
    have hAen : ENNReal.ofReal ε * (U.card : ENNReal) < A.card := by
      apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mp
      simpa only [hU, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hε.le,
        ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hA
    have hBen : ENNReal.ofReal ε * (W.card : ENNReal) < B.card := by
      apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mp
      simpa only [hW, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hε.le,
        ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hB
    have hdens := PairDensityReal G A B (Finset.card_pos.mp hApos) (Finset.card_pos.mp hBpos)
    have hb := hlow A hAU B hBW hAen hBen
    rw [ENNReal.add_sub_cancel_right (by simp)] at hb
    rw [← hdens.2.1]
    exact (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal hdfin hdens.1).mpr hb
  obtain ⟨P, heq, hlP, hPM, hunif⟩ := szemeredi_regularity G hα hlV
  have hPM' : P.parts.card ≤ M := hPM.trans hbound
  obtain ⟨_, E, hEP, _, hD, hslice, harea⟩ :=
    RegularExtractionPartitionGeometry G U W n l M ε d.toReal γ α hU hW hUW hcover
      hl hMn hε hdR hγ hγ1 hα hαγ hαγγ hεM hlower P heq hlP hPM' hunif
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hzero, _, _, _, hmeanAll⟩ :=
    WeightedRectangleExpectation G U W n l d.toReal γ α hU hW hdR hdR1.le
      hγ hα P E hEP hD hslice harea
  have hmean := hmeanAll h hh hmargin
  obtain ⟨H, hHdec, hHG, _, hsample⟩ :=
    SimultaneousUnequalRetention G U W n h hnpos hh hU hW hUW p hp hzero (hcut n hn)
  letI := hHdec
  refine ⟨H, hHdec, hHG, ?_⟩
  intro A hAU B hBW hA hB
  have hAR : η.toReal * n < (A.card : ℝ) := by
    have hc := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mpr hA
    simpa only [hU, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hc
  have hBR : η.toReal * n < (B.card : ℝ) := by
    have hc := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mpr hB
    simpa only [hW, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hc
  have hAh : h * n < (A.card : ℝ) :=
    (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hhη hnr).trans hAR
  have hBh : h * n < (B.card : ℝ) :=
    (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hhη hnr).trans hBR
  have hApos : (0 : ℝ) < A.card := (mul_pos hh hnr).trans hAh
  have hBpos : (0 : ℝ) < B.card := (mul_pos hh hnr).trans hBh
  have hareaPos : (0 : ℝ) < (A.card : ℝ) * B.card := mul_pos hApos hBpos
  have hm := hmean A hAU B hBW hAh hBh
  have hs := hsample A hAU B hBW hAh hBh
  have ht := abs_sub_le
    ((((A.product B).filter fun e => H.Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ))
    (∑ e ∈ A.product B, p e) (d.toReal * A.card * B.card)
  have herr : |(((A.product B).filter fun e => H.Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) -
      d.toReal * A.card * B.card| < (h / 2) * A.card * B.card := by
    linarith only [hm, hs, ht]
  have hsmall : (h / 2) * A.card * B.card < η.toReal * A.card * B.card := by
    have : h / 2 < η.toReal := by linarith only [hh, hhη]
    exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right this hApos) hBpos
  have hnonA : A.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by exact_mod_cast hApos)
  have hnonB : B.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by exact_mod_cast hBpos)
  obtain ⟨hfinite, hreal, hquot⟩ := PairDensityReal H A B hnonA hnonB
  have hlo : d.toReal - η.toReal ≤ (PairDensity H A B).toReal := by
    rw [hreal, hquot]
    apply (le_div_iff₀ hareaPos).mpr
    have he := (abs_lt.mp herr).1
    nlinarith only [he, hsmall]
  have hhi : (PairDensity H A B).toReal ≤ d.toReal + η.toReal := by
    rw [hreal, hquot]
    apply (div_le_iff₀ hareaPos).mpr
    have he := (abs_lt.mp herr).2
    nlinarith only [he, hsmall]
  constructor
  · by_cases hηd : η ≤ d
    · apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hfinite).mp
      simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le hηd hdfin] using hlo
    · simpa only [tsub_eq_zero_of_le (le_of_not_ge hηd)] using
        (zero_le (PairDensity H A B))
  · apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal hfinite (by finiteness)).mp
    simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_add hdfin hηfin] using hhi
RegularSubgraph.lean_statement:
theorem RegularSubgraph :
    ∀ ε' d : ENNReal, 0 < ε' → ε' < 1 → 0 < d → d < 1 →
      ∃ ε : ENNReal, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < ε' ∧
        ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
          (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (n : ℕ),
          n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n → Disjoint U W →
          U ∪ W = Finset.univ →
          (∀ ⦃u v⦄, G.Adj u v →
            (u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ W) ∨ (u ∈ W ∧ v ∈ U)) →
          LowerRegularPair G U W ε (d + ε) →
          ∃ G' : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G'.Adj,
            G' ≤ G ∧ RegularPair G' U W ε' d := by
RegularSubgraph.name: RegularSubgraph
RegularSubgraph.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $\eta=\varepsilon'_{\mathbb R}$ and $d_{\mathbb R}$ for the real
values of the prescribed parameters. They are positive and less than one,
since the original parameters lie strictly between zero and one. Apply
\noderef{RegularExtractionParameters} to $\eta$ to obtain
$h,\gamma,\alpha,\varepsilon,l,M,n_0$ with all the scalar conditions
in that statement. In particular $0<\varepsilon<\eta$, $1\leq n_0$,
$M\leq n_0$, $\varepsilon M<\gamma$,
\[
 2\alpha+(6\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)/h^2<h/4,\qquad
 2\,4^n\exp(-h^4n^2/8)<1\quad(n\geq n_0).
\]
Use the extended-nonnegative-real image of this $\varepsilon$ as the
existential witness. These choices depend only on $\varepsilon'$, hence
in particular only on the two prescribed parameters.

Fix an input graph and its bipartition with $n\geq n_0$. Then
$n>0$, $M\leq n$, and the disjoint cover gives $|V|=2n$.
For $A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq W$ of size strictly greater than
$\varepsilon n$, the input \noderef{LowerRegularPair} condition gives
\[
 (d+\varepsilon)-\varepsilon\leq\operatorname{PairDensity}(G,A,B).
\]
The parameter $\varepsilon$ is finite, so the extended subtraction
cancels to $d$. Both tested sets are nonempty. By
\noderef{PairDensityReal}, their density is finite and its real value
is the usual rational edge density viewed in $\mathbb R$.
Consequently
\[
 d_G(A,B)\geq d_{\mathbb R}\quad
       (|A|,|B|>\varepsilon n).                         \tag{1}
\]
Real and extended-real cardinality thresholds agree here, since
all parameters and cardinalities are finite.

Since $l\leq M\leq n\leq |V|$ and $\alpha>0$, apply
Mathlib's \texttt{szemeredi\_regularity} from
\texttt{Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Lemma} on the entire vertex set.
This gives an equipartition $\mathcal P$ with
$l\leq m=|\mathcal P|\leq
\operatorname{SzemerediRegularity.bound}(\alpha,l)\leq M$ and
$\mathcal P$ $\alpha$-uniform. Apply
\noderef{RegularExtractionPartitionGeometry} with this same partition,
the disjoint cover, and (1). Its scalar hypotheses hold by the
parameter choice, including $\alpha\leq\gamma$ and
$\alpha\leq\gamma^2$. It yields $n/m\leq|S|\leq3n/m$ for every
part and the eligible ordered pair set $E$. For each $(S,T)\in E$,
the chunk density $D_{ST}=d_G(U\cap S,W\cap T)$ belongs to
$[d_{\mathbb R},1]$, and its restriction to intersections larger
than their $\gamma$ thresholds changes by less than $2\alpha$.
The total ineligible area is at most
$(4\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)n^2$. This statement explicitly includes
nonsubstantial chunks, ordered distinct nonuniform pairs, and
diagonal rectangles.

Apply \noderef{WeightedRectangleExpectation} to $\mathcal P,E$ and
these local bounds.
It gives a function $p:V\times V\to[0,1]$, zero on nonedges and
outside $U\times W$. For an edge in an eligible rectangle it is
$d_{\mathbb R}/D_{ST}$, a valid probability because
$0<d_{\mathbb R}\leq D_{ST}$; in every other rectangle it is one.
The unique parts of each endpoint determine the rectangle.
The function is used only in the canonical $U$-to-$W$ orientation.
Put
\[
 \mu(A,B)=\sum_{(a,b)\in A\times B}p(a,b).
\]
The weighted-expectation statement pays both the ineligible area
and the additional small-intersection strips. Specialize its final
conditional conclusion to the chosen $h>0$ and its scalar margin to get
\[
 |\mu(A,B)-d_{\mathbb R}|A||B||<(h/4)|A||B|
        \quad(|A|,|B|>hn).                             \tag{2}
\]

The cutoff supplied by the parameters is precisely the strict
hypothesis of \noderef{SimultaneousUnequalRetention}. Apply that
node to $G,U,W,n,h,p$. It gives a graph $G'$ on the same entire
vertex set, with decidable adjacency and $G'\leq G$, retaining
the weight-one edges, for which all large tests simultaneously obey
\[
 |e_{G'}(A,B)-\mu(A,B)|\leq(h/4)|A||B|
        \quad(|A|,|B|>hn).                             \tag{3}
\]
Its finite product law has one trial for each canonically oriented
undirected edge; the probabilities were validated before forming
that law. The simultaneous conclusion uses all subset tests, not
only tests consisting of partition parts.

Now let $A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq W$ be any of the tests in
\noderef{RegularPair} for $\varepsilon'$. Their real sizes satisfy
$|A|,|B|>\eta n>hn$, because $h<\eta$ and $n>0$.
Combining (2) and (3) by the triangle inequality gives
\[
 |e_{G'}(A,B)-d_{\mathbb R}|A||B||<(h/2)|A||B|.
\]
The two cardinalities are positive, so divide by their product.
By \noderef{PairDensityReal} this gives
$|d_{G'}(A,B)-d_{\mathbb R}|<h/2<\eta$.
In particular the real density belongs to
$[d_{\mathbb R}-\eta,d_{\mathbb R}+\eta]$.

All tested densities are finite by \noderef{PairDensityReal}.
Thus the upper real inequality converts to
$\operatorname{PairDensity}(G',A,B)\leq d+\varepsilon'$.
If $\varepsilon'\leq d$, finite extended subtraction has real value
$d_{\mathbb R}-\eta$, so the lower real inequality converts to
$d-\varepsilon'\leq\operatorname{PairDensity}(G',A,B)$.
If instead $d\leq\varepsilon'$, the truncated lower endpoint is zero
and the same conclusion follows from nonnegativity.
These are every required strict-threshold test of
\noderef{RegularPair}. The graph has the original vertex type,
including isolated vertices, and is contained in $G$, so it is the
required spanning subgraph. No minimum-degree hypothesis was used.
\end{proof}
RegularSubgraph.title: RegularSubgraph

RegularityAfterDensityLoss.lean_proof:
intro V _ _ G H _ _ W₁ W₂ ε δ η ρ hε hsum hreg hloss
  unfold RegularPair at hreg ⊢
  intro U hU W hW hsizeU hsizeW
  have hsizeUε : ε * (W₁.card : ENNReal) < (U.card : ENNReal) :=
    (mul_le_mul_right' hε (W₁.card : ENNReal)).trans_lt hsizeU
  have hsizeWε : ε * (W₂.card : ENNReal) < (W.card : ENNReal) :=
    (mul_le_mul_right' hε (W₂.card : ENNReal)).trans_lt hsizeW
  obtain ⟨hlower, hupper⟩ := hreg U hU W hW hsizeUε hsizeWε
  obtain ⟨hmono, hbounded⟩ := hloss U hU W hW hsizeU hsizeW
  constructor
  · calc
      δ - η ≤ δ - (ε + ρ) := tsub_le_tsub_left hsum δ
      _ = (δ - ε) - ρ := (tsub_tsub δ ε ρ).symm
      _ ≤ PairDensity G U W - ρ := tsub_le_tsub_right hlower ρ
      _ ≤ PairDensity H U W := tsub_le_iff_tsub_le.mp hbounded
  · exact hmono.trans (hupper.trans (add_le_add le_rfl hε))
RegularityAfterDensityLoss.lean_statement:
theorem RegularityAfterDensityLoss :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel H.Adj]
      (W₁ W₂ : Finset V) (ε δ η ρ : ENNReal),
      ε ≤ η → ε + ρ ≤ η → RegularPair G W₁ W₂ ε δ →
      (∀ U ⊆ W₁, ∀ W ⊆ W₂,
        η * W₁.card < U.card → η * W₂.card < W.card →
        PairDensity H U W ≤ PairDensity G U W ∧
        PairDensity G U W - PairDensity H U W ≤ ρ) →
      RegularPair H W₁ W₂ η δ := by
RegularityAfterDensityLoss.name: RegularityAfterDensityLoss
RegularityAfterDensityLoss.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Fix such $U,W$.  Since $\varepsilon\leq\eta$, their two size inequalities also exceed the $\varepsilon$-thresholds, so $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-regularity of $G$ gives
\[
 \delta-\varepsilon\leq d_G(U,W)\leq\delta+\varepsilon.
\]
The assumed monotonicity gives $d_H(U,W)\leq\delta+\varepsilon\leq\delta+\eta$.  For the other side, truncated subtraction in the ordered additive monoid of extended nonnegative reals gives
\[
 d_H(U,W)\geq d_G(U,W)-\rho\geq(\delta-\varepsilon)-\rho
 \geq\delta-(\varepsilon+\rho)\geq\delta-\eta.
\]
Thus both inequalities required by \noderef{RegularPair} hold for every admissible $U,W$, which is the assertion.
\end{proof}
RegularityAfterDensityLoss.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Regularity after bounded density loss]
Let $(W_1,W_2)$ be $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-regular in a graph $G$.  Let $H$ be another graph, let $\varepsilon\leq\eta$, and let $\varepsilon+\rho\leq\eta$.  Suppose that whenever $U\subseteq W_1$ and $W\subseteq W_2$ have $|U|>\eta|W_1|$ and $|W|>\eta|W_2|$, one has
\[
 d_H(U,W)\leq d_G(U,W),\qquad d_G(U,W)-d_H(U,W)\leq\rho.
\]
Then $(W_1,W_2)$ is $(\eta,\delta)$-regular in $H$.
\end{lemma}
RegularityAfterDensityLoss.title: RegularityAfterDensityLoss
