RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound.lean_proof:
let t : ℝ := k / q
  have ht : 0 ≤ t := div_nonneg hk hq.le
  have htq : t * q = k := div_mul_cancel₀ _ hq.ne'
  have htratio : t < 1 / η := by
    exact (div_lt_div_iff₀ hq hη).mpr (by simpa only [mul_comm, mul_one] using hlarge)
  have hpt : 0 ≤ p := hδ.trans hδp
  have hcenterId : (∑ u ∈ U, (d u - p * q) ^ 2) =
      (∑ u ∈ U, (d u) ^ 2) - 2 * p * q * (∑ u ∈ U, d u) +
        (U.card : ℝ) * p ^ 2 * q ^ 2 := by
    calc
      _ = ∑ u ∈ U, ((d u) ^ 2 - 2 * p * q * d u + (p * q) ^ 2) := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro u hu
        ring
      _ = _ := by
        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
        simp only [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
        ring
  have hcenter : (∑ u ∈ U, (d u - p * q) ^ 2) ≤
      (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 *
        (4 * p * δ + δ ^ 2 + 12 * p * δ * (p - δ) * t + 6 * δ * t ^ 2) := by
    have hscale := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hfirst
      (show 0 ≤ 2 * p * q by positivity)
    calc
      _ = _ := hcenterId
      _ ≤ ((U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 * (p + δ) ^ 2 + 6 * δ * k ^ 2 * U.card) -
          2 * p * q * ((q - 6 * δ * k) * (p - δ) * U.card) +
          (U.card : ℝ) * p ^ 2 * q ^ 2 := by linarith only [hsecond, hscale]
      _ = _ := by rw [← htq]; ring
  have hδ1 : δ ≤ 1 := hδp.trans hp
  have hsmall0 : 4 * p * δ + δ ^ 2 ≤ 5 * δ := by
    nlinarith only [mul_nonneg hδ (sub_nonneg.mpr hp), mul_nonneg hδ (sub_nonneg.mpr hδ1)]
  have hsmall1 : p * (p - δ) ≤ 1 := by
    nlinarith only [hp, mul_nonneg hpt (sub_nonneg.mpr hp), mul_nonneg hpt hδ]
  have hsmall2 : 12 * p * δ * (p - δ) * t ≤ 12 * δ * t := by
    have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsmall1 (show 0 ≤ 12 * δ * t by positivity)
    convert this using 1 <;> ring
  have hcoefficient : 4 * p * δ + δ ^ 2 + 12 * p * δ * (p - δ) * t + 6 * δ * t ^ 2 ≤
      δ * (5 + 12 * t + 6 * t ^ 2) := by linarith only [hsmall0, hsmall2]
  have hcenter' : (∑ u ∈ U, (d u - p * q) ^ 2) ≤
      δ * (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 * (5 + 12 * t + 6 * t ^ 2) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ _ := hcenter
      _ ≤ (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 * (δ * (5 + 12 * t + 6 * t ^ 2)) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcoefficient (by positivity)
      _ = _ := by ring
  have hηt : η * t ≤ 1 := by
    have := (lt_div_iff₀ hη).mp htratio
    simpa only [mul_comm] using this.le
  have hηsq : η ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
    nlinarith only [hη1, mul_nonneg hη.le (sub_nonneg.mpr hη1)]
  have hηsqt : η ^ 2 * t ≤ 1 := by
    nlinarith only [hηt, mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hη1) (mul_nonneg hη.le ht)]
  have hηsqt2 : η ^ 2 * t ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
    nlinarith only [hηt, mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg hη.le ht) (sub_nonneg.mpr hηt)]
  have hpoly : η ^ 2 * (5 + 12 * t + 6 * t ^ 2) ≤ 23 := by
    nlinarith only [hηsq, hηsqt, hηsqt2]
  calc
    _ ≤ η ^ 2 * (δ * (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 * (5 + 12 * t + 6 * t ^ 2)) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcenter' (sq_nonneg _)
    _ = (δ * (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2) * (η ^ 2 * (5 + 12 * t + 6 * t ^ 2)) := by ring
    _ ≤ (δ * (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2) * 23 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpoly (by positivity)
    _ = _ := by ring
RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound.lean_statement:
theorem RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound {A : Type*} (U : Finset A) (d : A → ℝ)
    (q k δ p η : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hk : 0 ≤ k)
    (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hδp : δ ≤ p) (hp : p ≤ 1) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η ≤ 1)
    (hlarge : η * k < q)
    (hfirst : (q - 6 * δ * k) * (p - δ) * U.card ≤ ∑ u ∈ U, d u)
    (hsecond : (∑ u ∈ U, (d u) ^ 2) ≤
      (U.card : ℝ) * q ^ 2 * (p + δ) ^ 2 + 6 * δ * k ^ 2 * U.card) :
    η ^ 2 * (∑ u ∈ U, (d u - p * q) ^ 2) ≤ 23 * δ * U.card * q ^ 2 := by
RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound.name: RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound
RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $t=k/q\geq0$. Then $k=tq$ and $t<1/\eta$, since $q>\eta k$ and
$q,\eta$ are positive. Expanding the square, and using $p,q\geq0$ to
substitute the first-moment lower bound into the negative term, gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2
 &=\sum_{u\in U}d_u^2-2pq\sum_{u\in U}d_u+mp^2q^2\\
 &\leq mq^2(p+\delta)^2+6\delta k^2m
       -2pq(q-6\delta k)(p-\delta)m+mp^2q^2\\
 &=mq^2\bigl(4p\delta+\delta^2
       +12p\delta(p-\delta)t+6\delta t^2\bigr).
\end{align*}
The bounds $p\leq1$ and $\delta\leq1$ imply
$4p\delta+\delta^2\leq5\delta$. Also
$0\leq p-\delta\leq1$ and $0\leq p\leq1$, so
$p(p-\delta)\leq1$. Multiplying this inequality by the nonnegative
$12\delta t$ bounds the third term by $12\delta t$. As $mq^2\geq0$, we obtain
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2\leq\delta mq^2(5+12t+6t^2).
\]
Finally $\eta^2\leq1$, $\eta^2t=\eta(\eta t)\leq1$, and
$\eta^2t^2=(\eta t)^2\leq1$, using $0<\eta\leq1$ and $0\leq\eta t<1$.
Thus $\eta^2(5+12t+6t^2)\leq5+12+6=23$.
Multiplication of the preceding variance estimate by $\eta^2$, followed
by multiplication of this last scalar bound by $\delta mq^2\geq0$,
proves the claimed inequality. The argument also applies when $m=0$
or $\delta=0$, since no division by either is used.
\end{proof}
RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Variance bound from restricted degree moments]
Let $U$ be a finite set, let $(d_u)_{u\in U}$ be real numbers, and write $m=|U|$.
Let $q>0$, $k\geq0$, $0\leq\delta\leq p\leq1$, and $0<\eta\leq1$ with
$q>\eta k$. Suppose that
\[
 (q-6\delta k)(p-\delta)m\leq\sum_{u\in U}d_u,
 \qquad
 \sum_{u\in U}d_u^2\leq mq^2(p+\delta)^2+6\delta k^2m.
\]
Then
\[
 \eta^2\sum_{u\in U}(d_u-pq)^2\leq23\delta mq^2.
\]
\end{lemma}
RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound.title: RestrictedDegreeVarianceBound

RestrictedPartialEmbeddingTransport.lean_proof:
classical
  let liftX (x : VH) (hx : x ∈ X) : {x // x ∈ S} := ⟨x, hXS hx⟩
  let extend (t : PartialCompatibleEmbedding Bs As T) :
      PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X :=
    { toFun := fun x => if hx : x ∈ X then t.toFun (liftX x hx) else g x
      injOn := by
        intro x hx y hy hxy
        change x ∈ X at hx
        change y ∈ X at hy
        have heq : t.toFun (liftX x hx) = t.toFun (liftX y hy) := by
          simpa [hx, hy] using hxy
        exact congrArg Subtype.val
          (t.injOn ((hT _).mpr hx) ((hT _).mpr hy) heq)
      map_adj := by
        intro x y hx hy hxy
        simpa only [dif_pos hx, dif_pos hy] using
          t.map_adj (x := liftX x hx) (y := liftX y hy)
            ((hT _).mpr hx) ((hT _).mpr hy) hxy
      compatible := by
        intro x hx
        simpa only [dif_pos hx] using
          (hallowed (liftX x hx) _).mp (t.compatible _ ((hT _).mpr hx)) }
  have hext (t : PartialCompatibleEmbedding Bs As T) (x : VH) (hx : x ∈ X) :
      (extend t).toFun x = t.toFun (liftX x hx) := by
    simp only [extend, dif_pos hx]
  have himage (t : PartialCompatibleEmbedding Bs As T) :
      X.image (extend t).toFun = T.image t.toFun := by
    ext v
    constructor
    · rintro hv
      obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hv
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨liftX x hx, (hT _).mpr hx, (hext t x hx).symm⟩
    · rintro hv
      obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hv
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x.1, (hT x).mp hx, hext t x.1 ((hT x).mp hx)⟩
  have hupdate (t : PartialCompatibleEmbedding Bs As T) (x : {x // x ∈ S})
      (v : VG) : (UpdatedCandidacy B A X (extend t)).allowed x.1 v ↔
        (UpdatedCandidacy Bs As T t).allowed x v := by
    change (x.1 ∉ X ∧ v ∉ X.image (extend t).toFun ∧ A.allowed x.1 v ∧
      ∀ y ∈ X, H.Adj x.1 y → G.Adj v ((extend t).toFun y)) ↔
      (x ∉ T ∧ v ∉ T.image t.toFun ∧ As.allowed x v ∧
      ∀ y ∈ T, (H.induce (S : Set VH)).Adj x y → G.Adj v (t.toFun y))
    rw [himage t]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hx, hv, ha, he⟩
      refine ⟨fun ht => hx ((hT x).mp ht), hv, (hallowed x v).mpr ha, ?_⟩
      intro y hy hxy
      have hyX := (hT y).mp hy
      simpa only [hext t y.1 hyX] using he y.1 hyX hxy
    · rintro ⟨hx, hv, ha, he⟩

RestrictedPartialEmbeddingTransport.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For a sampled restricted map $t$, define $F_t(x)=t(\langle x,x\in S\rangle)$
when $x\in X$, and $F_t(x)=g(x)$ otherwise. Injectivity on $X$ follows from
injectivity on $T$ and injectivity of the subtype inclusion. The induced
source graph has exactly the original edges between its vertices, so
edge preservation on $X$ follows from edge preservation on $T$.
The assumed candidacy equivalence transfers compatibility on $X$.
These are all fields of \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding}.
The two images are exactly equal, $F_t(X)=t(T)$: send $x\in X$ to its
subtype lift for one inclusion, and send a vertex of $T$ to its ambient
value for the other.

For $x\in S$, expand \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}. The exclusion $x\notin X$
is equivalent to its lift not lying in $T$. The unused-host exclusion is
identical by the image equality. Original candidacy transfers by assumption.
For every embedded neighbor $y\in X$, its lift belongs to $T$, induced
adjacency is original adjacency, and $F_t(y)=t(y)$. Conversely every
$y\in T$ arises this way. Thus both directions of the updated-candidacy
equivalence hold, and the two candidate sets are literally equal, with
equal cardinalities, including exactly the same removed image.

Push $\nu$ forward by $t\mapsto F_t$ to define $\mu$. The law on restrictions
to $X$ is the restriction of the original law on $S$ along the injection
$X\hookrightarrow S$: equality holds pointwise on all coordinates of $X$,
and the two iterated PMF pushforwards therefore agree.
Apply \noderef{VertexSpreadRestriction} to this injection. This proves
spread on $X$; it asserts no spread for the fixed values outside $X$.
Finally the support of a PMF pushforward is the image of its support.
Every supported $F$ therefore has a sampled preimage $t$; transfer its
reserve by the candidate-set equality just proved. This also covers
noninjective pushforwards: no selection of a unique preimage is needed.
\end{proof}
RestrictedPartialEmbeddingTransport.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Transport of a restricted partial law]
Let $B,A$ be a finite blow-up instance and candidacy system, let $X\subseteq S$
be source subsets, and let $B_S,A_S$ be an instance on the literal subtype
$S$ with induced source graph, unchanged host and reduced graphs, and
$A_S(x,v)\iff A(x,v)$. Let $T\subseteq S$ consist exactly of the subtype
vertices whose ambient value belongs to $X$, and fix a function
$g:V(H)\to V(G)$. Suppose a law $\nu$ on partial compatible embeddings
of $T$ has $q$-spread total-map law on $S$ and, for every sampled map,
at least $\rho$ updated candidates at every vertex of $S\setminus T$.
Then there is a law $\mu$ on ambient partial compatible embeddings of $X$
whose restrictions to $X$ are $q$-spread. Every $f$ with $\mu(f)\ne0$ has
at least $\rho$ ambient updated candidates at every $x\in S\setminus X$.
All host values are allowed in both spread assertions.
\end{lemma}

RestrictedRowEdgeLowerBound.name: RestrictedRowEdgeLowerBound
RestrictedRowEdgeLowerBound.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Fix $x\in A$.  Its related elements in $W$ partition into those in $B$
and those in $W\setminus B$.  The second set has cardinality at most
$|W\setminus B|=|W|-|B|$.  Since the two cardinalities sum to at least
$D$, the cardinality of the first set is at least $D-(|W|-|B|)$.
Sum this inequality over $x\in A$.  By
\noderef{FilteredProductRowCount}, the sum of the restricted row
cardinalities is exactly the edge count on the left, and the sum of the
constant lower bound is $|A|(D-(|W|-|B|))$.
\end{proof}
RestrictedRowEdgeLowerBound.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Edge count after restricting the opposite part]
Let $A\subseteq X$ and $B\subseteq W\subseteq Y$ be finite sets, let
$P\subseteq X\times Y$ be a relation, and let $D$ be real.  If every
$x\in A$ has at least $D$ related elements in $W$, then
\[
 |\{(x,y)\in A\times B:P(x,y)\}|\geq
 |A|\bigl(D-(|W|-|B|)\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

      {ω | ¬ RetentionCountControl G L R q ξ η ω} ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal
        (2 * (L.card + R.card : ℝ) * Real.exp (-2 * ξ ^ 2 * min (L.card : ℝ) R.card) +
         2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (L.card + R.card) *
           Real.exp (-2 * ξ ^ 2 * η.toReal ^ 2 * L.card * R.card)) := by
RetentionBadEventUnion.name: RetentionBadEventUnion
RetentionBadEventUnion.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
For a left vertex $v$, its tested coordinate set
$A(\{v\},R)$ is a subset of $\{v\}\times R$, so its size is at most $b$.
Apply \noderef{IndependentRetentionConcentration} with $m=b$:
the probability of violating that degree test is at most
$2e^{-2\xi^2b}\leq2e^{-2\xi^2s}$. A right vertex has a coordinate
set of size at most $a$ and the same argument with $m=a$ gives the
same final bound. Summing over the $a+b$ tested vertices gives the
first term in $B_{\xi,h}$. Empty coordinate sets are explicitly allowed
by that concentration node.

For a tested rectangle $U\subseteq L,W\subseteq R$, the thresholds
are equivalent to $|U|>ha$, $|W|>hb$. This conversion is valid because
$\eta$ and the finite cardinalities are finite. Also $h>0$, since
$0<\eta<\infty$. Thus both subset sizes are positive, and
$m=|U||W|>h^2ab>0$. Its edge coordinate set is a subset of $U\times W$
and hence has size at most $m$. The concentration node with this $m$
gives failure probability at most
$2e^{-2\xi^2m}\leq2e^{-2\xi^2h^2ab}$.
There are exactly $2^a$ subsets of $L$ and $2^b$ subsets of $R$: each
subset is specified by its membership bits. Hence there are at most
$2^{a+b}$ tested rectangles, even when no rectangle passes the
thresholds. Sum the last bound over the tested rectangles for the
second term in $B_{\xi,h}$.

By the definition in \noderef{RetentionCountControl}, its complement
is the union of precisely these vertex and rectangle failure events.
For a finite family $E_1,\ldots,E_N$, the pointwise inequality
$1_{\cup E_j}\leq\sum_j1_{E_j}$, integrated against $\mu_q$, proves
the union bound; no independence between different tests is required.
All tests use the same law and the same coordinate function $\omega$.
All events are measurable on this finite discrete space and have
finite probability by \noderef{IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw}
specialized to the constant coordinate probabilities $q_i=q$. Thus taking
real probabilities, adding the displayed nonnegative bounds, and then
applying $\operatorname{ofReal}$ is legitimate and yields exactly the
stated extended-real bound.
\end{proof}
RetentionBadEventUnion.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Finite union bound on all retention tests]
Let $G$ be a finite graph, $L,R$ nonempty finite parts, $0\leq q\leq1$,
$\xi>0$, and $0<\eta<\infty$. Put $a=|L|$, $b=|R|$, $s=\min(a,b)$,
and $h=\eta.\operatorname{toReal}$. On the single sample space of
\noderef{IndependentEdgeSample}, the probability of failing
\noderef{RetentionCountControl} is at most
\[
B_{\xi,h}(a,b)=2(a+b)e^{-2\xi^2s}
       +2\,2^{a+b}e^{-2\xi^2h^2ab}.
\]
The inequality is in the extended nonnegative reals, using
$\operatorname{ofReal}(B_{\xi,h}(a,b))$ on the right.
\end{lemma}
RetentionBadEventUnion.title: RetentionBadEventUnion

RetentionCountControl.lean_proof:
(∀ v ∈ L, let I := (({v} : Finset V).product R).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2
    |(IndependentRetentionCount I ω : ℝ) - q * I.card| ≤ ξ * R.card) ∧
  (∀ w ∈ R, let I := (L.product {w}).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2
    |(IndependentRetentionCount I ω : ℝ) - q * I.card| ≤ ξ * L.card) ∧
  (∀ U ⊆ L, ∀ W ⊆ R,
    η * (L.card : ENNReal) < (U.card : ENNReal) →
    η * (R.card : ENNReal) < (W.card : ENNReal) →
    let I := (U.product W).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2
    |(IndependentRetentionCount I ω : ℝ) - q * I.card| ≤ ξ * (U.card * W.card))
RetentionCountControl.name: RetentionCountControl
RetentionCountControl.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}[Simultaneous retention count control]
For $G,L,R$, real $q,\xi$ and extended nonnegative $\eta$, say that a
sample $\omega$ has retention count control if all the following hold,
where $A(U,W)$ is the original ordered-edge set and $K$ is the count of
\noderef{IndependentRetentionCount}:
\[
|K_{A(\{v\},R)}-q|A(\{v\},R)||\leq\xi|R|\quad(v\in L),
\qquad
|K_{A(L,\{w\})}-q|A(L,\{w\})||\leq\xi|L|\quad(w\in R),
\]
and, for every $U\subseteq L,W\subseteq R$ with
$|U|>\eta|L|,|W|>\eta|R|$,
\[
|K_{A(U,W)}-q|A(U,W)||\leq\xi|U||W|.
\]
All counts and errors in these inequalities are real numbers. The size
thresholds are interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals.
\end{definition}
RetentionCountControl.title: RetentionCountControl

Mathlib multivariate polynomial
\[

An empty product is one. Permanents below are Mathlib's

    [DecidableRel F₁₂.Adj] [∀ k, DecidableRel (F₁₃ k).Adj]
    [∀ k, DecidableRel (F₂₃ k).Adj]
    (W₁ W₂ : Finset V) (_h₁₂ : Disjoint W₁ W₂) (W₃ : K → Finset V)

SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph.name: SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph
SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph.tex_statement:
\begin{definition}
Let $W_1,W_2$ be disjoint finite vertex sets, let $F'_{12}$ be a graph, and let $K$ be a finite family of arbitrary finite vertex sets $W_3^k$.  For each $k\in K$, let $F_{13}^k$ and $F_{23}^k$ be graphs, and fix errors $\varepsilon_k$ and densities $d_{13}^k,d_{23}^k$.  The simultaneous good-edge graph is the graph supported on $(W_1,W_2)$ in which, for $x\in W_1$ and $v\in W_2$, $xv$ is an edge exactly when it is an edge of $F'_{12}$ and, simultaneously for every $k\in K$,
\[
 (d_{13}^kd_{23}^k-2\varepsilon_k)|W_3^k|\leq
 |N_{F_{13}^k}(x)\cap N_{F_{23}^k}(v)\cap W_3^k|
 \leq(d_{13}^kd_{23}^k+2\varepsilon_k)|W_3^k|.
\]
There are no other edges.  Disjointness ensures that this definition cannot acquire an edge by testing the displayed condition with the two endpoint roles reversed.  This is the graph denoted $F_{12}$ in the equal-size induction step of the paper; the equal-size applications additionally assume $|W_1|=|W_2|=|W_3^k|=n$.
\end{definition}
SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph.title: SimultaneousGoodEdgeGraph

SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement.lean_proof:
classical
  intro Delta η c d hDelta hη hη1 hc hcd hd1
  obtain ⟨θ, N, hθ, hθη, hN, hextract, hextractCand⟩ :=
    NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction η c d hη hη1 hc hcd hd1
  have hηfin : η ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hη1
  have hθ1 : θ < 1 := hθη.trans hη1
  have hθfin : θ ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hθ1
  have hk : 1 ≤ Delta ^ 2 := by
    exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (pow_ne_zero 2 (by omega))
  have hηR : 0 < η.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hη.ne' hηfin
  have hηR1 : η.toReal < 1 := by
    simpa using (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal hηfin (by simp)).mpr hη1
  have hθR : 0 < θ.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hθ.ne' hθfin
  obtain ⟨e, he, heη, he1, heksmall, heθ, hethreshold, horders⟩ :=
    HostRefinementParameters (Delta ^ 2) N η.toReal θ.toReal hk hηR hηR1 hθR
  let ε := ENNReal.ofReal e
  have hε : 0 < ε := ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr he
  have hεη : ε < η := (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_iff_lt_toReal he.le hηfin).mpr heη
  have hε1 : ε < 1 := by
    simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_one] using
      (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1)).mpr he1
  have hεsmall : ε < 1 / (8 * (Delta ^ 2 : ℕ) ^ 2 : ENNReal) := by
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by simp [ε]) (by finiteness)).mp
    simpa only [ε, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal he.le, ENNReal.toReal_div,
      ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_natCast,
      ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_one] using heksmall
  have hsmall : (4 * ((Delta ^ 2 : ℕ) : ENNReal) ^ 2 + 2) * ε ≤ θ := by
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hθfin).mp
    rw [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_add (by finiteness) (by finiteness)]
    simpa only [ε, ENNReal.toReal_mul,
      ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal he.le,
      ENNReal.toReal_natCast, ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] using heθ
  have hthreshold : 2 * ((Delta ^ 2 : ℕ) : ENNReal) * ε ≤ θ := by
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (by finiteness) hθfin).mp
    simpa only [ε, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_pow,
      ENNReal.toReal_ofReal he.le, ENNReal.toReal_natCast,
      ENNReal.toReal_ofNat] using hethreshold
  refine ⟨ε, hε, hεη, ?_⟩
  intro r
  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ := horders r
  refine ⟨n₀, ?_⟩
  intro n hn VH VG _ _ _ _ H H' G R R' _ _ _ _ _ B A B₀
    hcard hHH' hσproj hRproj hsize hhost hcand
  obtain ⟨hn2, hnN, htailR⟩ := hn₀ n hn
  by_cases hr : r = 0
  · subst r
    let G' : SimpleGraph VG := ⊥
    letI : DecidableRel G'.Adj := Classical.decRel _
    let B' : BlowUpInstance (0 * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G'
        (R'.comap finProdFinEquiv.symm) := {
      sourceCluster := B₀.sourceCluster
      hostCluster := B₀.hostCluster
      source_independent := B₀.source_independent
      capacity := B₀.capacity
      reduced_support := B₀.reduced_support }
    let A' : CandidacySystem B' := {
      allowed := fun _ _ => False
      cluster_respecting := fun h => h.elim }
    refine ⟨G', inferInstance, B', A', bot_le, (fun _ => rfl), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro v
      exact (B.hostCluster v).elim0
    · intro x v h
      exact h.elim
    · intro p
      exact p.1.elim0
    · intro i j h
      exact (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1.elim0
    · intro i
      exact (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1.elim0
  let σ : VH → Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2) := fun x => finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster x)
  have hXeq (p : Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)) :
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p) =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun x => B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p) := by
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, σ,
      finProdFinEquiv.symm_apply_eq]
  have hsizeσ (p : Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)) :
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨
      (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1 := by
    simpa only [hXeq] using hsize p
  have htail : 2 * (r : ℝ) * (Delta ^ 2 : ℕ) * (r + 1) * n *
      Real.exp (-((ε.toReal / (2 * (Delta ^ 2 : ℕ))) ^ 2 /
        (2 * (1 + ε.toReal / (6 * (Delta ^ 2 : ℕ))))) * n) < 1 := by
    simpa only [ε, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal he.le] using htailR
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hcapacity, hsource, hhostdegree⟩ :=
    PrescribedHostPartitionSample B A σ ε d n hk hn2 hε hε1 hd1
      hσproj hcard hsizeσ hhost hcand htail
  obtain ⟨f', hf', hcapacity', hchange, hcandidatedegree⟩ :=
    HostExceptionalCorrection B A σ f ε d n hk hn2 hε hεsmall hd1
      hσproj hf hcard hsizeσ hcapacity hcand
  obtain ⟨hhostlow, hcandlow⟩ := RefinedLowerSuperRegularTransfer B A σ f f' ε θ d n
    hk hn2 hθ1 hsmall hthreshold hσproj hf hf' hcard hsizeσ
    hcapacity hcapacity' hchange hsource hhostdegree hcandidatedegree hhost hcand
  have hhostsize (p : Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2)) :
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p).card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p).card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1 := by
    rw [hcapacity' p]
    exact hsizeσ p
  have hhostextract : ∀ p q, R'.Adj p q →
      ∃ F : SimpleGraph VG, ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
        F ≤ G ∧ (∀ ⦃u v⦄, F.Adj u v →
          (f' u = p ∧ f' v = q) ∨ (f' u = q ∧ f' v = p)) ∧
        SuperRegularPair F (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p)
          (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = q) η c := by
    intro p q hpq
    have hdis : Disjoint (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p)
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = q) := by
      apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
      intro v hvp hvq
      have hpqeq := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hvp).2.symm.trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hvq).2
      exact R'.ne_of_adj hpq hpqeq
    obtain ⟨F, hFdec, hFG, hFcross, hFreg⟩ := hextract G _ _ (n / (Delta ^ 2)) hnN
      hdis (hhostsize p) (hhostsize q) (hhostlow p q (hRproj p q hpq))
    refine ⟨F, hFdec, hFG, ?_, hFreg⟩
    intro u v huv
    simpa only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] using hFcross huv
  obtain ⟨G', hG'dec, hG'G, hG'support, hG'reg⟩ :=
    CrossPairSubgraphAssembly G R' f' η c hhostextract
  letI := hG'dec
  have hVeq (j : Fin (r * Delta ^ 2)) :
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => finProdFinEquiv (f' v) = j) =
        (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = finProdFinEquiv.symm j) := by
    ext v
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      finProdFinEquiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
  let B' : BlowUpInstance (r * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G'
      (R'.comap finProdFinEquiv.symm) := {
    sourceCluster := B₀.sourceCluster
    hostCluster := fun v => finProdFinEquiv (f' v)
    source_independent := B₀.source_independent
    capacity := by
      intro j
      change Fintype.card {x : VH // B₀.sourceCluster x = j} ≤
        Fintype.card {v : VG // finProdFinEquiv (f' v) = j}
      simp only [Fintype.card_subtype, hVeq, hcapacity', hXeq,
        finProdFinEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
      exact le_rfl
    reduced_support := B₀.reduced_support }
  have hcandextract : ∀ j : Fin (r * Delta ^ 2),
      let L : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
        ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ B'.sourceCluster x = j
      let Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
        ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ B'.hostCluster v = j
      let C : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b =>
        ∃ x v, a = Sum.inl x ∧ b = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed x v
      ∃ F : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG), ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
        F ≤ C ∧ SuperRegularPair F L Q η c := by
    intro j
    let p := finProdFinEquiv.symm j
    let L : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ σ x = p
    let Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z => ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ f' v = p
    let C : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b =>
      ∃ x v, a = Sum.inl x ∧ b = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed x v
    letI : DecidableRel C.Adj := Classical.decRel _
    have hLmap : L = (Finset.univ.filter fun x => σ x = p).map
        ⟨Sum.inl, Sum.inl_injective⟩ := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp [L]
    have hQmap : Q = (Finset.univ.filter fun v => f' v = p).map
        ⟨Sum.inr, Sum.inr_injective⟩ := by
      ext z
      cases z <;> simp [Q]
    have hLsize : L.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ L.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1 := by
      simpa only [hLmap, Finset.card_map] using hsizeσ p
    have hQsize : Q.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ Q.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1 := by
      simpa only [hQmap, Finset.card_map] using hhostsize p
    have hdis : Disjoint L Q := by
      apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
      intro z hz hw
      obtain ⟨x, rfl, hx⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hz).2
      obtain ⟨v, hv, hvp⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hw).2
      exact Sum.inl_ne_inr hv
    obtain ⟨F, hFdec, hFC, hFsupport, hFreg⟩ :=
      hextractCand C L Q (n / (Delta ^ 2)) hnN hdis hLsize hQsize (hcandlow p)
    refine ⟨F, hFdec, hFC, ?_⟩
    simpa only [L, Q, B', σ, p, finProdFinEquiv.symm_apply_eq,
      finProdFinEquiv.apply_symm_apply,
      finProdFinEquiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply] using hFreg
  obtain ⟨A', hA'A, hA'reg⟩ := TaggedCandidacyAssembly B A B' η c hcandextract
  refine ⟨G', hG'dec, B', A', hG'G, (fun _ => rfl), ?_, @hA'A, ?_, ?_, hA'reg⟩
  · intro v
    simpa only [B', finProdFinEquiv.symm_apply_apply] using hf' v
  · intro p
    change (Finset.univ.filter fun x => B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun v => finProdFinEquiv (f' v) = finProdFinEquiv p).card ∧ _
    simp only [hVeq, finProdFinEquiv.symm_apply_apply, hcapacity', hXeq]
    exact ⟨trivial, hsize p⟩
  · intro i j hij
    have hreg := hG'reg (finProdFinEquiv.symm i) (finProdFinEquiv.symm j) hij
    simpa only [B', hVeq] using hreg
SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement.lean_statement:
theorem SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement :
    ∀ (Delta : ℕ) (ε' d' d : ENNReal), 1 ≤ Delta → 0 < ε' → ε' < 1 →
      0 < d' → d' < d ^ 2 / 2 → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ ε : ENNReal, 0 < ε ∧ ε < ε' ∧
      ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ,
      ∀ (n : ℕ), n₀ ≤ n →
      ∀ {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
        [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
        {H H' : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
        {R' : SimpleGraph (Fin r × Fin (Delta ^ 2))}
        [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel H'.Adj] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
        [DecidableRel R.Adj] [DecidableRel R'.Adj]
        (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
        (B₀ : BlowUpInstance (r * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G
          (R'.comap finProdFinEquiv.symm)),
        (∀ i,
          (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = i).card = n ∧
          (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = i).card = n) →
        H ≤ H' →
        (∀ x, (finProdFinEquiv.symm (B₀.sourceCluster x)).1 = B.sourceCluster x) →
        (∀ p q, R'.Adj p q → R.Adj p.1 q.1) →
        (∀ p,
          let s := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B₀.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p
          s.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ s.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1) →
        InstanceLowerSuperRegular B ε d → CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d →
        ∃ (G' : SimpleGraph VG) (_ : DecidableRel G'.Adj)
          (B' : BlowUpInstance (r * Delta ^ 2) VH VG H' G'
            (R'.comap finProdFinEquiv.symm)) (A' : CandidacySystem B'),
          G' ≤ G ∧
          (∀ x, B'.sourceCluster x = B₀.sourceCluster x) ∧
          (∀ v, (finProdFinEquiv.symm (B'.hostCluster v)).1 = B.hostCluster v) ∧
          (∀ {x v}, A'.allowed x v → A.allowed x v) ∧
          (∀ p,
            let X := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B'.sourceCluster x = finProdFinEquiv p
            let V := Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B'.hostCluster v = finProdFinEquiv p
            X.card = V.card ∧
              (X.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) ∨ X.card = n / (Delta ^ 2) + 1)) ∧
          InstanceSuperRegular B' ε' d' ∧ CandidacySuperRegular B' A' ε' d' := by

SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The hypotheses imply $0<d\leq1$ and $0<d'<d^2/2\leq1/2$,
so $d,d',\varepsilon'$ are finite. Apply
\noderef{NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction} with output error
$\varepsilon'$, output density $d'$, and input density $d$.
It supplies $0<\theta<\varepsilon'$ and a cutoff $N\geq1$,
with a contained extraction on any two disjoint parts of sizes
$m$ or $m+1$, for $m\geq N$, from lower $(\theta,d)$-super-regularity.
The same numerical witnesses are used for host graphs and graphs
on the disjoint tagged union of the two vertex types.

Put $k=\Delta^2\geq1$. Apply \noderef{HostRefinementParameters}
to $k,N$ and the real values of $\varepsilon',\theta$. Write $e$
for its witness and set $\varepsilon=\operatorname{ofReal}(e)$.
Then $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon'$ and $\varepsilon<1$. In the
finite real interpretation the usable inequalities are
\[
 \varepsilon<1/(8k^2),\qquad
 (4k^2+2)\varepsilon\leq\theta,\qquad
 2k\varepsilon\leq\theta.
 \tag{1}
\]
Only $\Delta,\varepsilon',d',d$ have been used in choosing this
$\varepsilon$. After $r$ is specified, the same parameter node
gives $n_0$ such that every $n\geq n_0$ satisfies
\[
 n\geq2k,\quad m=\lfloor n/k\rfloor\geq N,\quad
 2rk(r+1)n\exp(-cn)<1,\qquad
 c=\frac{(\varepsilon/(2k))^2}{2(1+\varepsilon/(6k))}>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
This uses the actual positive hypergeometric decay rate, not the
sharper martingale estimate; only $n_0$ depends on $r$.

Fix the input instance and the prescribed intermediate instance $B_0$.
If $r=0$, the source and host maps of
\noderef{BlowUpInstance} take values in an empty type, so there are
no vertices. Use the empty host graph and empty allowed relation,
and copy the source and host maps and structural fields of $B_0$.
Containment holds, all fiber and super-regularity families are
vacuous, and both projection identities hold. Henceforth assume $r>0$.

Identify the refined index set with $[r]\times[k]$ via the given
finite-index equivalence. Let $\sigma$ be the prescribed source map
of $B_0$ in these coordinates, and write
$X_p=\sigma^{-1}(p)$ and $s_p=|X_p|$.
The given source projection makes the fibers $X_{(i,j)}$ partition
the original $X_i$, and the size hypothesis gives $s_p\in\{m,m+1\}$.
In particular $m\geq n/(2k)$, from $n\geq2k$ and the floor bound.

Apply \noderef{PrescribedHostPartitionSample} with this $\sigma$,
the original instance and candidacy system, their lower
super-regularity hypotheses, and the cutoff (2). Its conclusion
gives a host map $f$ projecting to the original map and bins
$W_p=f^{-1}(p)$ of sizes exactly $s_p$. For every original source
vertex $x$ and every bin $(i,j)$ in its original cluster, it gives
\[
 \deg_A(x,W_{(i,j)})\geq(d-2\varepsilon)s_{(i,j)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
For every original host vertex $v$ and every bin $(i,j)$ of an
adjacent original cluster, it likewise gives
\[
 \deg_G(v,W_{(i,j)})\geq(d-2\varepsilon)s_{(i,j)}.
 \tag{4}
\]
These are estimates on every original host vertex, irrespective of
which bin it occupies. The sampling node uses the uniform subset
law and the checked hypergeometric tail; no assertion about uniform
perfect matchings is used.

Apply \noderef{HostExceptionalCorrection} with $f,\sigma$, the
original candidacy lower super-regularity, and the first margin
in (1). It returns a map $f'$ with the same original-cluster
projection and the same exact capacities. Write $V_p=(f')^{-1}(p)$.
Its statement gives, separately for every bin,
\[
 |V_p\mathbin{\triangle}W_p|\leq2k\varepsilon n,
 \tag{5}
\]
and, for every host vertex $v$,
\[
 \deg_A(v,X_{f'(v)})\geq(d-2\varepsilon)|X_{f'(v)}|.
 \tag{6}
\]
The correction puts exceptional vertices into suitable source bins;
it does not presume that all original hosts were good for all fixed
source bins. In particular (6) supplies the reverse candidacy
orientation that randomizing the host bins alone would not give.

All hypotheses of \noderef{RefinedLowerSuperRegularTransfer} now
hold: the original lower host and candidacy pairs, the two projections,
the capacities, the complete sampled degree families (3)--(4),
the correction loss (5), the assigned-bin bound (6), and the last
two scalar margins in (1). It gives lower $(\theta,d)$-super-regularity
on every refined host pair with adjacent original indices, and on
every corresponding tagged candidacy pair. The threshold transfer
inside that result uses $\varepsilon n\leq2k\varepsilon s_p
\leq\theta s_p$; its degree loss is at most
$2k\varepsilon n\leq4k^2\varepsilon s_p$.
The two conclusions therefore include both degree orientations
and all the requisite strict subset tests.

If $pq$ is a required refined host edge, its original indices are
adjacent by hypothesis, so the host conclusion just obtained applies.
Also $p\neq q$ because the reduced graph is simple; hence $V_p,V_q$
are disjoint fibers. Their sizes lie in $\{m,m+1\}$ and $m\geq N$.
Apply \noderef{NearEqualSuperRegularExtraction} to obtain a graph
$F_{pq}\subseteq G$, with edges only between $V_p,V_q$, which is
$(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular on them.
For candidacy form the symmetric graph of the original allowed
relation on the disjoint tagged union of the vertex types, as in
\noderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}. The tagged copies of $X_p,V_p$
are disjoint and have cardinalities $s_p,s_p$: the respective
tag maps biject the ordinary fibers with these sets.
The candidacy conclusion of the transfer node thus permits the
same extraction, giving a contained graph on each tagged pair
with the prescribed output parameters. The extraction result
handles the unequal host sizes by padding, extraction, and dummy
deletion, but returns only edges on the original types.

Use \noderef{CrossPairSubgraphAssembly} to assemble the host
extractions into a single graph $G'\subseteq G$. Its statement
supplies super-regularity on every required refined pair and reduced
support. Its proof selects only one graph per unordered required
pair; crossing support guarantees that on that pair the union
agrees exactly with that selected graph, including every degree
and subset-edge count.

Define $B'$ by copying the source map, source independence, and
reduced support from $B_0$, and by taking host map $f'$ followed by
the finite-index equivalence. Its capacities are equalities, since
$|V_p|=s_p=|X_p|$; converting a finite fiber cardinality to the
cardinality of its subtype changes nothing. These fields give
a \noderef{BlowUpInstance} on $H',G'$ and the same refined reduced
graph. The source map agrees exactly with $B_0$'s, and the
host projection agrees exactly with the original host map.

Apply \noderef{TaggedCandidacyAssembly} to $B,A,B'$ and the
tagged extractions. It gives a \noderef{CandidacySystem} $A'$
for $B'$ contained in $A$ and satisfying
\noderef{CandidacySuperRegular} with error $\varepsilon'$ and
density $d'$. The selected source and host fiber indices already
agree on a refined candidacy pair, so its tagged assembled relation
agrees exactly with its selected extracted graph.
Finally the host super-regular pairs, rewritten under the same
index equivalence, are precisely
\noderef{InstanceSuperRegular} for $B'$.

All final graphs are spanning on the original finite types;
no dummy vertex or tagged host copy remains in the host graph.
The final size alternative is the original one for $B_0$,
and no step altered $H'$ or the prescribed source refinement.
The scalar conversions in (1)--(2) are between finite quantities.
All graph predicates and transfer assertions use extended
nonnegative reals, so every possibly negative output endpoint is
the truncated zero bound, not an unproved real-subtraction inequality.
Containments and exact counts are unchanged by these conversions.
\end{proof}
SimultaneousHostCandidacyRefinement.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous host and candidacy refinement]
Fix $\Delta\geq1$ and $0<\varepsilon'<1$, $0<d'<d^2/2$ with $d\leq1$.  There is $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon'$, depending only on these displayed parameters, such that for every $r$ there is $n_0$ for which the following holds for $n\geq n_0$.  Let $(H,G,R,(X_i),(V_i),(A^i))$ be a lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular blow-up instance with lower-super-regular candidacy graphs, with $|X_i|=|V_i|=n$.  Suppose $H'$ extends $H$, its source clusters refine each $X_i$ into $\Delta^2$ parts of sizes $\lfloor n/\Delta^2\rfloor$ or one larger, and its refined reduced graph $R'$ satisfies
\[
 (i,j)(i',j')\in E(R')\quad\Longrightarrow\quad ii'\in E(R).
\]
Then the host clusters can be partitioned simultaneously into corresponding parts $V_{i,j}$, and there are a spanning subgraph $G'\subseteq G$ and candidacy subgraphs $A'^{i,j}\subseteq A^i[X_{i,j},V_{i,j}]$, such that $|X_{i,j}|=|V_{i,j}|$ and every required host pair and every candidacy graph is $(\varepsilon',d')$-super-regular.  The source refinement is unchanged, and both refined cluster maps project exactly to the original cluster maps.
\end{lemma}

classical
  let E := (U.product W).filter fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2
  let I := {e // e ∈ E}
  let q : I → ℝ≥0 := fun e => ⟨p e.val, (hp e.val).1⟩
  have hq : ∀ e, q e ≤ 1 := fun e => by exact_mod_cast (hp e.val).2
  let μ := Measure.pi (fun e => (PMF.bernoulli (q e) (hq e)).toMeasure)
  obtain ⟨hμ, hi, he, hs⟩ := IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw q hq
  change IsProbabilityMeasure μ at hμ
  letI := hμ
  let X : I → (I → Bool) → ℝ := fun e ω => if ω e then 1 else 0
  let Y : I → (I → Bool) → ℝ := fun e ω => X e ω - p e.val
  have hind : iIndepFun Y μ := by
    exact hi.comp (fun e x => x - p e.val) (fun _ => measurable_id.sub_const _)
  have hsg : ∀ e, HasSubgaussianMGF (Y e) (1 / 4) μ := hs
  let H : (I → Bool) → SimpleGraph V := fun ω =>
    { Adj := fun u w => G.Adj u w ∧
        ((∃ he : (u, w) ∈ E, ω ⟨(u, w), he⟩ = true) ∨
         (∃ he : (w, u) ∈ E, ω ⟨(w, u), he⟩ = true))
      symm := by
        intro u w huv
        exact ⟨huv.1.symm, huv.2.symm⟩
      loopless := ⟨fun u huu => G.loopless.irrefl u huu.1⟩ }
  have hcontain (ω) : H ω ≤ G := fun _ _ huv => huv.1
  have hcross (ω : I → Bool) (u) (hu : u ∈ U) (w) (hw : w ∈ W) :
      (H ω).Adj u w ↔ ∃ he : (u, w) ∈ E, ω ⟨(u, w), he⟩ = true := by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, h | h⟩
      · exact h
      · obtain ⟨hwu, _⟩ := h
        have hwU := (Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hwu).1).1
        exact False.elim (Finset.disjoint_left.mp hUW hwU hw)
    · rintro ⟨huw, hω⟩
      exact ⟨(Finset.mem_filter.mp huw).2, Or.inl ⟨huw, hω⟩⟩
  let s : Finset V → Finset V → Finset I := fun A B =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun e => e.val ∈ A.product B
  have hsum (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W)
      (f : V × V → ℝ) :
      ∑ e ∈ s A B, f e.val =
        ∑ e ∈ (A.product B).filter (fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2), f e := by
    apply Finset.sum_bij (fun e _ => e.val)
    · intro e hem
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨(Finset.mem_filter.mp hem).2, (Finset.mem_filter.mp e.property).2⟩
    · intro e he f hf hef
      exact Subtype.ext hef
    · intro e hem
      obtain ⟨heAB, heG⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hem
      obtain ⟨heA, heB⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp heAB
      have heE : e ∈ E := Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hAU heA, hBW heB⟩, heG⟩
      exact ⟨⟨e, heE⟩, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, heAB⟩, rfl⟩
    · intro e hem
      rfl
  have hcount (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W) (ω : I → Bool) :
      (((A.product B).filter fun e => (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) =
        ∑ e ∈ s A B, X e ω := by
    let f : V × V → ℝ := fun e => if he : e ∈ E then X ⟨e, he⟩ ω else 0
    have hsf : ∑ e ∈ s A B, X e ω = ∑ e ∈ s A B, f e.val := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro e hem
      simp only [f, dif_pos e.property]
      rfl
    rw [hsf, hsum A B hAU hBW f]
    have hfull : ∑ e ∈ (A.product B).filter (fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2), f e =
        ∑ e ∈ A.product B, f e := by
      apply Finset.sum_filter_of_ne
      intro e hem hf
      by_contra hg
      have hnE : e ∉ E := fun heE => hg (Finset.mem_filter.mp heE).2
      exact hf (dif_neg hnE)
    rw [hfull, ← Finset.sum_boole]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro e hem
    obtain ⟨heA, heB⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hem
    have hc := hcross ω e.1 (hAU heA) e.2 (hBW heB)
    by_cases heE : e ∈ E
    · simp only [f, dif_pos heE, X]
      have hc' : (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2 ↔ ω ⟨e, heE⟩ = true := by
        refine ⟨fun hadj => ?_, fun hω => hc.mpr ⟨heE, hω⟩⟩
        obtain ⟨heE', hω⟩ := hc.mp hadj
        exact hω
      simp only [hc']
    · have hnot : ¬(H ω).Adj e.1 e.2 := fun hadj =>
        (hc.mp hadj).elim (fun he _ => heE he)
      simp only [hnot, if_false, f, dif_neg heE]
  have hmean (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W) :
      ∑ e ∈ s A B, p e.val = ∑ e ∈ A.product B, p e := by
    rw [hsum A B hAU hBW p]
    apply Finset.sum_filter_of_ne
    intro e hem hne
    by_contra hg
    exact hne (hzero e hg)
  have htrials (A B : Finset V) : (s A B).card ≤ A.card * B.card := by
    have hinj : Function.Injective (fun e : I => e.val) := Subtype.val_injective
    have hsub : (s A B).image (fun e => e.val) ⊆ A.product B := by
      intro e he
      obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp he
      exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2
    have := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rwa [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj, Finset.product_eq_sprod,
      Finset.card_product] at this

    {ω | h * n < (AB.1.card : ℝ) ∧ h * n < (AB.2.card : ℝ) ∧
      (h / 4) * AB.1.card * AB.2.card < |∑ e ∈ s AB.1 AB.2, Y e ω|}
  have htail (AB : Finset V × Finset V) :
      μ.real (bad AB) ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) := by
    by_cases hA : h * n < (AB.1.card : ℝ)
    · by_cases hB : h * n < (AB.2.card : ℝ)
      · let N : ℝ := (AB.1.card : ℝ) * AB.2.card
        have hhn : 0 < h * (n : ℝ) := mul_pos hh (by exact_mod_cast hn)
        have hapos : 0 < (AB.1.card : ℝ) := hhn.trans hA
        have hbpos : 0 < (AB.2.card : ℝ) := hhn.trans hB
        have hN : 0 < N := mul_pos hapos hbpos
        have hr : ((s AB.1 AB.2).card : ℝ) ≤ N := by
          dsimp only [N]
          exact_mod_cast htrials AB.1 AB.2
        have ht : 0 ≤ (h / 4) * N := by positivity
        have hbound := FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail μ Y (s AB.1 AB.2) hind
          (fun e _ => hsg e) N ((h / 4) * N) hN hr ht
        have hsub : bad AB ⊆ {ω | (h / 4) * N < |∑ e ∈ s AB.1 AB.2, Y e ω|} := by
          intro ω hω
          change (h / 4) * N < |∑ e ∈ s AB.1 AB.2, Y e ω|
          simpa only [N, mul_assoc] using hω.2.2
        have heq : -2 * ((h / 4) * N) ^ 2 / N = -h ^ 2 * N / 8 := by
          field_simp
          <;> ring
        have hNlo : h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ N := by
          calc
            h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 = (h * n) * (h * n) := by ring
            _ ≤ (AB.1.card : ℝ) * AB.2.card :=
              mul_le_mul hA.le hB.le hhn.le hapos.le
        have hexp : -h ^ 2 * N / 8 ≤ -h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8 := by
          nlinarith only [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hNlo (sq_nonneg h)]
        rw [heq] at hbound
        exact (measureReal_mono hsub).trans
          (hbound.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hexp) (by norm_num)))
      · have hempty : bad AB = ∅ := by
          ext ω
          simp only [bad, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
          exact fun hω => hB hω.2.1
        rw [hempty, measureReal_empty]
        positivity
    · have hempty : bad AB = ∅ := by
        ext ω
        simp only [bad, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
        exact fun hω => hA hω.1
      rw [hempty, measureReal_empty]
      positivity
  let tests := U.powerset.product W.powerset
  have htests : (tests.card : ℝ) = (4 : ℝ) ^ n := by
    change ((U.powerset.product W.powerset).card : ℝ) = (4 : ℝ) ^ n
    simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.card_product, Finset.card_powerset, hU, hW,
      Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat]
    rw [← mul_pow]
    norm_num
  let failure := ⋃ AB ∈ tests, bad AB
  have hfail : μ.real failure < 1 := by
    calc
      μ.real failure ≤ ∑ AB ∈ tests, μ.real (bad AB) :=
        measureReal_biUnion_finset_le tests bad
      _ ≤ ∑ _AB ∈ tests, 2 * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum (fun AB _ => htail AB)
      _ = 2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) := by
        rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, htests]
        ring
      _ < 1 := hcut
  have hone : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ e : I, p e.val = 1 → ω e = true := by
    apply ae_all_iff.mpr
    intro e

        measurableSet_eq_fun (measurable_pi_apply e) measurable_const
      have hiint : (∫ ω, X e ω ∂μ) = μ.real {ω : I → Bool | ω e = true} := by
        have hfun : X e = {ω : I → Bool | ω e = true}.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) := by
          ext ω
          simp only [X, Set.indicator, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
        rw [hfun]
        exact integral_indicator_one hm
      have hprob : μ.real {ω : I → Bool | ω e = true} = 1 := by
        rw [← hiint]
        exact (he e).trans hpone
      have hnull : μ {ω : I → Bool | ω e ≠ true} = 0 := by
        apply (measureReal_eq_zero_iff).mp
        change μ.real {ω : I → Bool | ω e = true}ᶜ = 0
        rw [probReal_compl_eq_one_sub hm, hprob, sub_self]
      have ha : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ω e = true := ae_iff.mpr hnull
      exact ha.mono (fun ω hω _ => hω)
    · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun ω h => False.elim (hpone h))
  obtain ⟨ω, hgood, hωone⟩ : ∃ ω, ω ∉ failure ∧
      ∀ e : I, p e.val = 1 → ω e = true := by
    have hm : MeasurableSet failure := by
      exact Set.to_countable failure |>.measurableSet
    have hpos : μ failureᶜ ≠ 0 := by
      apply (measureReal_eq_zero_iff).not.mp
      rw [probReal_compl_eq_one_sub hm]
      linarith only [hfail]
    obtain ⟨ω, hω, hωone⟩ := μ.exists_mem_of_measure_ne_zero_of_ae hpos (ae_restrict_of_ae hone)
    exact ⟨ω, hω, hωone⟩
  refine ⟨H ω, inferInstance, hcontain ω, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u hu w hw huw hpone
    have hem : (u, w) ∈ E := Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hu, hw⟩, huw⟩
    exact (hcross ω u hu w hw).mpr ⟨hem, hωone ⟨(u, w), hem⟩ hpone⟩
  · intro A hAU B hBW hA hB
    have hm : (A, B) ∈ tests := Finset.mem_product.mpr
      ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.mpr hAU, Finset.mem_powerset.mpr hBW⟩
    have hnobad : ω ∉ bad (A, B) := fun hb =>
      hgood (Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨(A, B), Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨hm, hb⟩⟩)
    have hb : |∑ e ∈ s A B, Y e ω| ≤ (h / 4) * A.card * B.card := by
      by_contra! hb
      exact hnobad ⟨hA, hB, hb⟩
    rw [hcount A B hAU hBW ω, ← hmean A B hAU hBW]
    simpa only [Y, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] using hb

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

theorem SimultaneousUnequalRetention
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
    (n : ℕ) (h : ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) (hh : 0 < h)
    (hU : U.card = n) (hW : W.card = n) (hUW : Disjoint U W)
    (p : V × V → ℝ) (hp : ∀ e, 0 ≤ p e ∧ p e ≤ 1)
    (hzero : ∀ e, ¬G.Adj e.1 e.2 → p e = 0)
    (hcut : 2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) < 1) :
    ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel H.Adj,
      H ≤ G ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U, ∀ w ∈ W, G.Adj u w → p (u, w) = 1 → H.Adj u w) ∧
      (∀ A ⊆ U, ∀ B ⊆ W, h * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
        h * n < (B.card : ℝ) →
        |(((A.product B).filter fun e => H.Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) -
          ∑ e ∈ A.product B, p e| ≤ (h / 4) * A.card * B.card) := by
SimultaneousUnequalRetention.name: SimultaneousUnequalRetention
SimultaneousUnequalRetention.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Index the trials by the oriented existing edges
$I=\{(u,w)\in U\times W:G(u,w)\}$. Disjointness gives a unique
$U$-to-$W$ orientation to each undirected edge meeting both sets.
For $e\in I$, its given weight lies in $[0,1]$, so
\noderef{IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw} supplies the finite product
Bernoulli probability law, with independent coordinate indicators of
expectation $p(e)$ and centered subgaussian parameter $1/4$.
For an outcome, take exactly the selected undirected edges from $I$
on the original vertex set, deleting any edges outside this list.
This graph is simple and contained in $G$; it retains vertices even
if they are isolated. Its finite edge list makes adjacency decidable.

Fix one tested pair $A,B$. Its count is the sum of the indicators
indexed by $I_{AB}=I\cap(A\times B)$, and its expectation is the
sum of their weights. This is the weight sum on all of $A\times B$,
since nonedge weights are zero. Put $r=|I_{AB}|$ and $N=|A||B|$.
We have $r\leq N$ and $N>h^2n^2>0$. For completeness, the
subgaussian conclusion gives the following tail bound without any
equal-probability assumption. Independence yields
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\bigl(s(Z-\mathbb EZ)\bigr)\leq\exp(rs^2/8)
 \quad(s\in\mathbb R).
\]
If $r>0$, Markov's inequality for this nonnegative exponential,
with $s=4t/r$, bounds the upper tail at $t>0$ by
$\exp(-2t^2/r)$. Applying the same argument to the negative centered
sum bounds the lower tail identically. Thus the probability of
$|Z-\mathbb EZ|>t$ is at most $2\exp(-2t^2/r)$, which is at most
$2\exp(-2t^2/N)$ because $r\leq N$. If $r=0$, the discrepancy
is identically zero and the failure probability is zero.
Taking $t=(h/4)N$ therefore bounds the failure probability by
\[
 2\exp(-h^2N/8)\leq2\exp(-h^4n^2/8).
\]
There are $2^n$ subsets of each side, hence $4^n$ subset pairs;
restricting to large pairs does not increase this number. For a
finite family of events, the indicator of the union is bounded by
the sum of their indicators. Integrating gives the finite union
bound, so the probability of any failed test is at most the
left side of the assumed strict cutoff and is strictly less than one.

A trial of weight one succeeds with probability one. The finite
intersection of these probability-one success events still has
probability one, so removing their null complement from the good
test event leaves positive probability. In a finite probability
space a positive-probability event is nonempty. Choose an outcome
in this intersection. Its graph retains all weight-one edges and
satisfies every asserted weak discrepancy bound simultaneously.
\end{proof}
SimultaneousUnequalRetention.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous unequal retention]
Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, let $U,W$ be disjoint
sets of size $n>0$, and let $h>0$. Let $p:V\times V\to[0,1]$ be zero
on nonedges. Assume
\[
 2\,4^n\exp(-h^4n^2/8)<1.
\]
There is a graph $H$ on the same entire vertex set, with decidable
adjacency, contained in $G$, retaining every edge from $U$ to $W$ of
weight one, such that for all $A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq W$ with
$|A|,|B|>hn$,
\[
 \left|e_H(A,B)-\sum_{(a,b)\in A\times B}p(a,b)\right|
 \leq(h/4)|A||B|.
\]
\end{lemma}
SimultaneousUnequalRetention.title: SimultaneousUnequalRetention

SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow.lean_proof:
have hkfinite : (k : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.natCast_ne_top k
  have hkzero : (k : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hk
  have hp : p ≤ 2 * ε := by
    have hpk : p * k ≤ 2 * ε * k := by
      calc
        p * k ≤ (a : ENNReal) + ε * k := by
          apply tsub_le_iff_right.mp
          simpa only [ENNReal.sub_mul (fun _ _ => hkfinite)] using halower
        _ ≤ ε * k + ε * k := add_le_add hasmall le_rfl
        _ = 2 * ε * k := by ring
    exact (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_right hkzero hkfinite).mp hpk
  have hpq : p * q ≤ 2 * ε := by
    have hpq' : p * q ≤ p := by simpa only [mul_one] using mul_le_mul_left' hq p
    exact hpq'.trans hp
  constructor
  · simp only [tsub_eq_zero_of_le hpq, zero_mul, zero_le]
  · calc
      (c : ENNReal) ≤ a := by exact_mod_cast hca
      _ ≤ ε * k := hasmall
      _ ≤ (p * q + 2 * ε) * k := by
        apply mul_le_mul_right'
        calc
          ε ≤ ε + ε := le_add_right le_rfl
          _ = 2 * ε := by ring
          _ ≤ p * q + 2 * ε := le_add_left le_rfl
SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow.lean_statement:
theorem SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow (ε p q : ENNReal) (k a c : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≠ 0) (_hε : ε ≤ 1) (_hp : p ≤ 1) (hq : q ≤ 1)
    (halower : (p - ε) * k ≤ a) (hasmall : (a : ENNReal) ≤ ε * k)
    (hca : c ≤ a) :
    (p * q - 2 * ε) * k ≤ c ∧ (c : ENNReal) ≤ (p * q + 2 * ε) * k := by
SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow.name: SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow
SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $k$ is finite, the lower degree bound gives $pk\leq a+\varepsilon k\leq2\varepsilon k$ by distributivity of multiplication over truncated subtraction.
The positive finite factor $k$ can be cancelled, giving $p\leq2\varepsilon$.
Then $pq\leq p\leq2\varepsilon$ because $q\leq1$, so the lower window endpoint is zero.
For the upper bound, $c\leq a\leq\varepsilon k\leq(pq+2\varepsilon)k$ by nonnegativity and monotonicity.
There is no division by $\varepsilon$, and all steps remain valid when $\varepsilon=0$.
\end{proof}
SmallNeighborhoodCodegreeWindow.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Small neighborhoods have no bad codegrees]
Let $\varepsilon,p,q\in[0,1]$, and let $k,a,c$ be nonnegative integers with $k>0$.
If $(p-\varepsilon)_+k\leq a\leq\varepsilon k$ and $c\leq a$, then
$(pq-2\varepsilon)_+k\leq c\leq(pq+2\varepsilon)k$.
The subscript $+$ denotes truncated subtraction, $(x-y)_+=\max\{x-y,0\}$.
\end{lemma}

theorem SourceClusterPadding :
    ∀ {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
      [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
      {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG}
      [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
      {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} [DecidableRel R.Adj]
      (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
      [DecidableRel A.allowed] (ε η d : ENNReal),
      0 < ε → ε ≤ η * η → η ≤ 1 → d ≤ 1 →
      CandidacyLowerSuperRegular B A ε d →
      ∃ (Hp : SimpleGraph (PaddedSource B)),
      ∃ _hHp : DecidableRel Hp.Adj,
      ∃ Bp : BlowUpInstance r (PaddedSource B) VG Hp G R,
      ∃ Ap : CandidacySystem Bp,
      ∃ _hAp : DecidableRel Ap.allowed,
        (∀ x y : VH, Hp.Adj (Sum.inl x) (Sum.inl y) ↔ H.Adj x y) ∧
        (∀ z w, Hp.Adj z w → ∃ x y : VH, z = Sum.inl x ∧ w = Sum.inl y) ∧
        (∀ x : VH, Bp.sourceCluster (Sum.inl x) = B.sourceCluster x) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin r) (k : Fin (Fintype.card
            {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - Fintype.card
            {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i})),
          Bp.sourceCluster (Sum.inr ⟨i, k⟩) = i) ∧
        (∀ v, Bp.hostCluster v = B.hostCluster v) ∧
        (∀ x v, Ap.allowed (Sum.inl x) v ↔ A.allowed x v) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin r) (k : Fin (Fintype.card
            {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = i} - Fintype.card
            {x : VH // B.sourceCluster x = i})) (v : VG),
          Ap.allowed (Sum.inr ⟨i, k⟩) v ↔ B.hostCluster v = i) ∧
        (∀ i, Fintype.card {z : PaddedSource B // Bp.sourceCluster z = i} =
          Fintype.card {v : VG // Bp.hostCluster v = i}) ∧
        Hp.maxDegree ≤ H.maxDegree ∧

          InstanceLowerSuperRegular Bp δ d) ∧

        (∀ φ : SimpleGraph.Copy Hp G, CompatibleEmbedding Bp Ap φ →
          ∃ ψ : SimpleGraph.Copy H G, CompatibleEmbedding B A ψ ∧
            ∀ x, ψ x = φ (Sum.inl x)) ∧
        (∀ (q : ENNReal) (μ : PMF {φ : SimpleGraph.Copy Hp G // CompatibleEmbedding Bp Ap φ}),
          VertexSpreadOn (μ.map fun φ => fun z => φ.1 z) q Set.univ →
          ∃ ν : PMF {ψ : SimpleGraph.Copy H G // CompatibleEmbedding B A ψ},
            VertexSpreadOn (ν.map fun ψ => fun x => ψ.1 x) q Set.univ) := by

SourceClusterPadding.tex_proof:
egin{proof}
For each $i$, capacity in 
oderef{BlowUpInstance} gives $|X_i|\leq|V_i|$.  Adjoin the $|V_i|-|X_i|$ vertices in the $i$th dummy summand of 
oderef{PaddedSource}, assign them to $i$, and give them no edges in $H^+$.  Extend $A^i$ by joining every new row completely to $V_i$; all allowed pairs remain within corresponding source and host clusters, as required by 
oderef{CandidacySystem}.  The source fibers now have size $|X_i|+(|V_i|-|X_i|)=|V_i|$.  Since no source edge was introduced, source independence and reduced support persist, old degrees are unchanged, dummy degrees are zero, and $\Delta(H^+)\leq\Delta(H)$.  The host data are unchanged, so host lower super-regularity in the sense of 
oderef{InstanceLowerSuperRegular} is preserved literally.

Fix a candidacy pair, which is lower-$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular by the hypothesis and 
oderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}, and use its lower-regularity clause from 
oderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}.  Put $M=|X_i|$, $N=|V_i|$, and let $S\subseteq X_i^+$ and $T\subseteq V_i$ have $|S|>\eta N$ and $|T|>\eta N$, the test thresholds of 
oderef{LowerRegularPair} for the padded pair.  Write $S_0=S\cap X_i$ and $S_D=S\setminus X_i$.  If $|S_0|>\varepsilon M$, original lower regularity in 
oderef{LowerRegularPair} gives at least $(d-\varepsilon)|S_0||T|$ old edges, using the edge-count interpretation of density in 
oderef{PairDensity}, and the dummy rows contribute $|S_D||T|$; since $d\leq1$ and $\varepsilon\leq\eta$, the sum is at least $(d-\eta)|S||T|$.  Otherwise $|S_0|\leq\varepsilon M$, and
\[
 |S_0|/|S|<\varepsilon N/(\eta N)\leq\eta.
\]
Thus the complete dummy rows alone contribute at least $(1-\eta)|S||T|\geq(d-\eta)|S||T|$.  This explicitly covers subsets mixing old and dummy rows.  Dividing the edge bound by $|S||T|$ as in 
oderef{PairDensity} proves the padded lower-regularity clause of 
oderef{LowerRegularPair}.

The degree clauses of 
oderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} give old left degrees at least $(d-\varepsilon)N\geq(d-\eta)N$, and dummy degrees are $N$.  If $K=N-M$, every right degree is at least $(d-\varepsilon)M+K$.  After subtracting $(d-\eta)N$, the remainder is
$(\eta-\varepsilon)M+(1-d+\eta)K\geq0$.  Hence the padded pair is lower-$(\eta,d)$-super-regular by 
oderef{LowerSuperRegularPair}; since this holds for every $i$, the padded candidacy system satisfies 
oderef{CandidacyLowerSuperRegular}.

Restrict a padded embedding to the original summand.  Injectivity is inherited, exact inducedness gives preservation of source edges, and the old-row candidacy equivalence gives compatibility in the sense of 
oderef{CompatibleEmbedding}.  Push any law forward by restriction.  By 
oderef{CylinderEvent}, the inverse image of a cylinder on distinct original vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ is exactly the padded cylinder on $\operatorname{inl}(x_1),\ldots,\operatorname{inl}(x_s)$, so its probability remains at most $q^s$ by the padded law's 
oderef{VertexSpreadOn} hypothesis.  The same hypothesis gives $q\leq1$, unchanged under restriction, so all clauses of 
oderef{VertexSpreadOn} hold for the pushed-forward law.  This proves the embedding and spread-transfer clauses.
\end{proof}
