      apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal hz (by finiteness)).mp
      simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul,
        ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (add_nonneg hc.le hη.le),
        ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hu
  refine ⟨G, hGdec, hGH, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro X hXU Y hYW hXen hYen
    have hX : η * n < (X.card : ℝ) := by
      have hr := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mpr hXen
      simpa only [hU, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hη.le,
        ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hr
    have hY : η * n < (Y.card : ℝ) := by
      have hr := (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mpr hYen
      simpa only [hW, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hη.le,
        ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hr
    have hxne : X.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by
      have hr := lt_trans (mul_pos hη hnR) hX
      exact_mod_cast hr)
    have hyne : Y.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by
      have hr := lt_trans (mul_pos hη hnR) hY
      exact_mod_cast hr)
    obtain ⟨hfin, hd, _⟩ := PairDensityReal G X Y hxne hyne
    obtain ⟨hl, hu⟩ := abs_lt.mp (hdensity X hXU Y hYW hX hY)
    have hconv := hconvert 1 (PairDensity G X Y) hfin
      (by rw [hd]; simp only [Nat.cast_one, mul_one]; linarith only [hl])
      (by rw [hd]; simp only [Nat.cast_one, mul_one]; linarith only [hu])
    simpa only [Nat.cast_one, mul_one] using hconv
  · intro u hu
    obtain ⟨hl, hr⟩ := hdegUR u hu
    rw [hW]
    exact hconvert n ((W.filter fun w => G.Adj u w).card : ENNReal) (by simp)
      (by simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hl)
      (by simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hr)
  · intro w hw
    obtain ⟨hl, hr⟩ := hdegWR w hw
    rw [hU]
    have he : U.filter (fun u => G.Adj u w) = U.filter (fun u => G.Adj w u) := by
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro u _
      exact G.adj_comm u w
    rw [he]
    exact hconvert n ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj w u).card : ENNReal) (by simp)
      (by simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hl)
      (by simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_natCast] using hr)
SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration.lean_statement:
theorem SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H F : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj] [DecidableRel F.Adj]
    (U W U₀ W₀ : Finset V) (n : ℕ) (c h η : ℝ)
    (hU : U.card = n) (hW : W.card = n) (hUW : Disjoint U W)
    (hcover : U ∪ W = Finset.univ)
    (hbip : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v →
      (u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ W) ∨ (u ∈ W ∧ v ∈ U))
    (hU₀ : U₀ ⊆ U) (hW₀ : W₀ ⊆ W)
    (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hh : 0 < h)
    (hhc : h ≤ c / 100) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η < 1)
    (h3 : 3 * h < η) (h4 : 4 * h < η)
    (hbudget : 2 * h + 4 * h / η < η) (hfloor : 1 ≤ h * (n : ℝ))
    (hbadU : ((U \ U₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n)
    (hbadW : ((W \ W₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n)
    (hreserveU : ∀ u ∈ U, (7 * c / 4) * n ≤
      ((W.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ))
    (hreserveW : ∀ w ∈ W, (7 * c / 4) * n ≤
      ((U.filter fun u => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ))
    (hFH : F ≤ H)
    (hFsupport : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, F.Adj u v →
      (u ∈ U₀ ∧ v ∈ W₀) ∨ (u ∈ W₀ ∧ v ∈ U₀))
    (hdegU : ∀ u ∈ U₀, (c - 4 * h) * n ≤
      ((W₀.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ∧
      ((W₀.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ≤ (c + 2 * h) * n)
    (hdegW : ∀ w ∈ W₀, (c - 4 * h) * n ≤
      ((U₀.filter fun u => F.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ∧
      ((U₀.filter fun u => F.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ≤ (c + 2 * h) * n)
    (hrect : ∀ A ⊆ U₀, ∀ B ⊆ W₀, h * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
      h * n < (B.card : ℝ) → |(F.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) - c| ≤ 2 * h) :
    ∃ G' : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G'.Adj,
      G' ≤ H ∧ SuperRegularPair G' U W (ENNReal.ofReal η) (ENNReal.ofReal c) := by
SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration.name: SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration
SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $B_U=U\setminus U_0$, $B_W=W\setminus W_0$.
Since $h>0$ and $hn\geq1$, $n>0$ and $1/n\leq h$.
Let $k=\lfloor cn\rfloor$, interpreted as a natural number since
$cn>0$. Then $cn-1\leq k\leq cn$.
For any exceptional vertex in $B_U$, deletion of $B_W$ from
its possible neighbors loses at most $2hn$, so it has at least
$(7c/4-2h)n\geq cn$ neighbors in $W_0$. The last inequality
uses $2h\leq c/50<3c/4$. Likewise every vertex of $B_W$
has at least $cn$ neighbors in $U_0$. Each of these finite
neighbor sets therefore has cardinality at least the integer $k$.
Choose a $k$-element subset for each exceptional vertex.
Define $G'$ by adding to $F$ exactly the edges from these
exceptional vertices to their chosen opposite-core neighbors,
in both orientations. All are edges of $H$. No added edge has
two exceptional endpoints, and no edge is prescribed by two
exceptional vertices. This is a simple graph on the original
vertex set, contained in $H$, with decidable adjacency.

Every exceptional vertex has degree exactly $k$. Every core
vertex gains at most $|B_W|\leq2hn$ neighbors if it is in $U_0$,
or at most $|B_U|\leq2hn$ if it is in $W_0$.
The support condition on $F$ makes its degree into the full
opposite part equal its degree into the opposite core.
Thus core degrees in $G'$ lie in $[(c-4h)n,(c+4h)n]$.
For exceptional degrees use
$k\geq cn-1\geq(c-h)n\geq(c-4h)n$ and
$k\leq cn\leq(c+4h)n$.
Since $4h<\eta$, all opposite-part degrees therefore lie in
$[(c-\eta)n,(c+\eta)n]$ as real inequalities.

For a regularity test take $X\subseteq U,Y\subseteq W$ with
$a=|X|>\eta n$, $b=|Y|>\eta n$. These imply $a,b>0$.
Put $X_0=X\cap U_0,Y_0=Y\cap W_0$. The complement size
bounds and $3h<\eta$ give
$|X_0|\geq a-2hn>hn$, and likewise $|Y_0|>hn$.
The number $R=ab-|X_0||Y_0|$ of tested positions with at least
one exceptional endpoint satisfies
\[
0\leq R\leq|X\cap B_U|b+a|Y\cap B_W|
\leq2hn(a+b)<(4h/\eta)ab.
\]
For the strict last inequality, use $n/a<1/\eta$ and
$n/b<1/\eta$, valid since $n,\eta,a,b>0$.
On the other positions $G'$ agrees with $F$.
The assumed core density bound, after multiplying by
$|X_0||Y_0|>0$, gives
\[
(c-2h)|X_0||Y_0|\leq e_F(X_0,Y_0)
\leq(c+2h)|X_0||Y_0|.
\]
Here $0<c-2h<1$, by $h\leq c/100$ and $c<1$.
At most $R$ added edges occur in $X\times Y$. Consequently
\[
\begin{split}
e_{G'}(X,Y)&\geq(c-2h)(ab-R)
             \geq(c-2h-4h/\eta)ab,\\
e_{G'}(X,Y)&\leq(c+2h)|X_0||Y_0|+R
             \leq(c+2h+4h/\eta)ab.
\end{split}
\]
The budget $2h+4h/\eta<\eta$ and division by $ab>0$ prove
the lower and upper real density inequalities with error $\eta$.

It remains to verify precisely the extended-real predicates.
By \noderef{PairDensityReal}, on these nonempty tested sets the
extended density is finite and its real value equals the density
just bounded. All sizes, degrees, and upper endpoints are finite,
so their real upper inequalities translate directly to extended
upper inequalities. For every lower endpoint, if $c\geq\eta$,
the extended truncated difference has real value $c-\eta$ and
the real lower inequality translates directly, including its
multiplication by the opposite-part size in the degree clauses.
If $c<\eta$, the truncated difference is zero and the extended
lower bounds follow from nonnegativity, without treating a
negative real number as an extended parameter. The size tests
translate exactly as well, since $\eta$ and all sizes are finite.
Thus the density tests are those of \noderef{RegularPair}, and
the two degree clauses are those of \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.
The graph is on the unchanged vertex set throughout, proving the
claimed contained spanning conclusion.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Exceptional-row restoration]
Let $H,F$ be finite simple graphs on the same vertex set, with
disjoint covering parts $U,W$ of size $n$, and with every edge of
$H$ crossing those parts. Let $U_0\subseteq U,W_0\subseteq W$.
Let real numbers $c,h,\eta$ satisfy
\[
0<c<1,\quad0<h\leq c/100,\quad0<\eta<1,\quad
3h<\eta,\quad4h<\eta,\quad2h+4h/\eta<\eta,\quad hn\geq1.
\]
Assume $|U\setminus U_0|,|W\setminus W_0|\leq2hn$;
every vertex of $H$ has at least $7cn/4$ neighbors in the opposite
full part; $F\subseteq H$ has edges only between $U_0,W_0$;
the opposite-core degrees of $F$ lie in $[(c-4h)n,(c+2h)n]$;
and $|d_F(A,B)-c|\leq2h$ whenever
$A\subseteq U_0,B\subseteq W_0$ and $|A|,|B|>hn$.
There is a graph $G'\subseteq H$ on the same vertex set such that
$(U,W)$ is $(\eta,c)$-super-regular, with the parameters regarded
as extended nonnegative reals.
\end{lemma}
SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration.title: SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration

SuperRegularExtractionParameters.lean_proof:
let θ := min η (min ((d ^ 2 / 2) / 100) (η ^ 2 / 1000))
  have hθ : 0 < θ := by dsimp [θ]; positivity
  have hθη : θ ≤ η := min_le_left _ _
  have hθ1 : θ < 1 := hθη.trans_lt hη1
  obtain ⟨h, γ, α, ε, l, M, _, hh, hhθ, hh100, hγ, hγ1, hα,
    hαγ, hαγγ, hε, hεθ, hεM, hl, hlM, hbound, _, _, hmargin, _⟩ :=
    RegularExtractionParameters θ hθ hθ1
  have hhc : h ≤ (d ^ 2 / 2) / 100 := hhθ.le.trans
    ((min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_left _ _))
  have hhη : h ≤ η ^ 2 / 1000 := hhθ.le.trans
    ((min_le_right _ _).trans (min_le_right _ _))
  have hηsq : η ^ 2 ≤ η := by nlinarith only [hη, hη1]
  have h3 : 3 * h < η := by nlinarith only [hhη, hηsq, hη]
  have h4 : 4 * h < η := by nlinarith only [hhη, hηsq, hη]
  have hdiv : 4 * h / η ≤ 4 * η / 1000 := by
    apply (div_le_iff₀ hη).mpr
    nlinarith only [hhη]
  have hfinal : 2 * h + 4 * h / η < η := by
    nlinarith only [hhη, hηsq, hdiv, hη]
  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀, hMn₀, hcut⟩ :=
    ExtractionTailCutoffs (d ^ 2 / 2) h M (by positivity) hh
  exact ⟨h, γ, α, ε, l, M, n₀, hh, hh100, hhc, hhη, h3, h4, hfinal,
    hγ, hγ1, hα, hαγ, hαγγ, hε, hεθ.trans_le hθη, hεM,
    hl, hlM, hbound, hn₀, hMn₀, hmargin, hcut⟩
SuperRegularExtractionParameters.lean_statement:
theorem SuperRegularExtractionParameters (η d : ℝ)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η < 1) (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d < 1) :
    ∃ h γ α ε : ℝ, ∃ l M n₀ : ℕ,
      0 < h ∧ h ≤ 1 / 100 ∧ h ≤ (d ^ 2 / 2) / 100 ∧
      h ≤ η ^ 2 / 1000 ∧ 3 * h < η ∧ 4 * h < η ∧
      2 * h + 4 * h / η < η ∧
      0 < γ ∧ γ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < α ∧ α ≤ γ ∧ α ≤ γ ^ 2 ∧
      0 < ε ∧ ε < η ∧ ε * M < γ ∧
      1 ≤ l ∧ l ≤ M ∧ SzemerediRegularity.bound α l ≤ M ∧
      1 ≤ n₀ ∧ M ≤ n₀ ∧
      2 * α + (6 * γ + 9 * α + 6 / (l : ℝ)) / h ^ 2 < h / 4 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
        1 ≤ h * (n : ℝ) ∧
        4 * n * Real.exp (-(d ^ 2 / 2) ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) < 1 / 4 ∧
        2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) < 1 / 4 ∧
        4 * n * Real.exp (-2 * h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ)) < 1 / 4 ∧
        2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-2 * h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) < 1 / 4 := by
SuperRegularExtractionParameters.name: SuperRegularExtractionParameters
SuperRegularExtractionParameters.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $\theta=\min\{\eta,(d^2/2)/100,\eta^2/1000\}>0$;
then $\theta\leq\eta<1$. Apply \noderef{RegularExtractionParameters}
with $\theta$. Its statement supplies $h<\theta$, $h\leq1/100$,
the displayed positive $\gamma,\alpha,\varepsilon$, the bounds on
$l,M$, and the expectation margin. In particular
$\varepsilon<\theta\leq\eta$, $h\leq(d^2/2)/100$, and
$h\leq\eta^2/1000$. Since $\eta^2\leq\eta$, these imply
$3h<\eta$ and $4h<\eta$. Division by $\eta>0$ gives
$4h/\eta\leq4\eta/1000$ and $2h\leq2\eta/1000$, so
$2h+4h/\eta\leq6\eta/1000<\eta$.
Discard the preliminary order cutoff from that application and apply
\noderef{ExtractionTailCutoffs} with $c=d^2/2>0$, the chosen $h>0$,
and $M$. Its statement gives the required $n_0$, all four strict tail
bounds, and $hn\geq1$. No parameter is chosen from graph data.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularExtractionParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Super-regular extraction parameters]
Let $0<\eta,d<1$ be real. There are real $h,\gamma,\alpha,\varepsilon$
and integers $l,M,n_0$ satisfying
\[
0<h\leq1/100,\quad h\leq(d^2/2)/100,\quad h\leq\eta^2/1000,
\quad3h<\eta,\quad4h<\eta,\quad2h+4h/\eta<\eta;
\]
\[
0<\gamma\leq1,\quad0<\alpha\leq\gamma,\quad\alpha\leq\gamma^2,
\quad0<\varepsilon<\eta,\quad\varepsilon M<\gamma;
\]
\[
1\leq l\leq M,\quad\operatorname{SzemerediRegularity.bound}(\alpha,l)\leq M,
\quad1\leq n_0,\quad M\leq n_0,
\quad2\alpha+(6\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)/h^2<h/4.
\]
For every integer $n\geq n_0$, $hn\geq1$ and the four expressions
\[
4n e^{-(d^2/2)^2n/8},\quad2\,4^n e^{-h^4n^2/8},\quad
4n e^{-2h^2n},\quad2\,4^n e^{-2h^4n^2}
\]
are each less than $1/4$. All choices depend only on $\eta,d$.
\end{lemma}
SuperRegularExtractionParameters.title: SuperRegularExtractionParameters

SuperRegularInitialSample.lean_proof:
classical
  have hn : 0 < n := by omega
  have hnr : 0 < (n : ℝ) := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hn
  have htotal : Fintype.card V = 2 * n := by
    simpa only [Finset.card_univ] using
      (hcover ▸ Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hUW).trans (by rw [hU, hW]; omega)
  obtain ⟨P, heq, hlP, hPb, hunif⟩ :=
    szemeredi_regularity G (l := l) hα (by omega)
  obtain ⟨_, E, hEP, _, hD, hslice, harea⟩ :=
    RegularExtractionPartitionGeometry G U W n l M ε d γ α hU hW hUW hcover
      hl hMn hε hd hγ hγ1 hα hαγ hαγγ hεM hlower P heq hlP
      (hPb.trans hbound) hunif
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hzero, _, hformula, _, happrox⟩ :=
    WeightedRectangleExpectation G U W n l d γ α hU hW hd hd1.le hγ hα
      P E hEP hD hslice harea
  have hpedge (u) (hu : u ∈ U) (w) (hw : w ∈ W) (huw : G.Adj u w) :
      d ≤ p (u, w) := by
    have hSu : P.part u ∈ P.parts := P.part_mem.mpr (Finset.mem_univ _)
    have hTw : P.part w ∈ P.parts := P.part_mem.mpr (Finset.mem_univ _)
    have huS : u ∈ U ∩ P.part u :=
      Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hu, P.mem_part (Finset.mem_univ _)⟩
    have hwT : w ∈ W ∩ P.part w :=
      Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨hw, P.mem_part (Finset.mem_univ _)⟩
    rw [hformula _ hSu _ hTw _ huS _ hwT huw]
    split_ifs with he
    · have hden := hD _ _ he
      have hpos := hd.trans_le hden.1
      apply (le_div_iff₀ hpos).mpr
      exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hden.2 hd.le).trans_eq (mul_one d)
    · exact hd1.le
  have hexpect := happrox h hh hmargin
  let c : ℝ := d ^ 2 / 2
  have hc : 0 < c := by dsimp [c]; positivity
  -- Each original edge has one coordinate, oriented from U to W.
  let E0 := (U.product W).filter fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2
  let I := {e // e ∈ E0}
  let q : I → ℝ≥0 := fun e => ⟨p e.val, (hp e.val).1⟩
  have hq : ∀ e, q e ≤ 1 := fun e => by exact_mod_cast (hp e.val).2
  let μ := Measure.pi (fun e => (PMF.bernoulli (q e) (hq e)).toMeasure)
  obtain ⟨hμ, hi, _, hs⟩ := IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw q hq
  change IsProbabilityMeasure μ at hμ
  letI := hμ
  let X : I → (I → Bool) → ℝ := fun e ω => if ω e then 1 else 0
  let Y : I → (I → Bool) → ℝ := fun e ω => X e ω - p e.val
  have hind : iIndepFun Y μ :=
    hi.comp (fun e x => x - p e.val) (fun _ => measurable_id.sub_const _)
  have hsg : ∀ e, HasSubgaussianMGF (Y e) (1 / 4) μ := hs
  let H : (I → Bool) → SimpleGraph V := fun ω =>
    { Adj := fun u w => G.Adj u w ∧
        ((∃ he : (u, w) ∈ E0, ω ⟨(u, w), he⟩ = true) ∨
         (∃ he : (w, u) ∈ E0, ω ⟨(w, u), he⟩ = true))
      symm := by
        intro u w huv
        exact ⟨huv.1.symm, huv.2.symm⟩
      loopless := ⟨fun u huu => G.loopless.irrefl u huu.1⟩ }
  have hcontain (ω) : H ω ≤ G := fun _ _ huv => huv.1
  have hcross (ω : I → Bool) (u) (hu : u ∈ U) (w) (hw : w ∈ W) :
      (H ω).Adj u w ↔ ∃ he : (u, w) ∈ E0, ω ⟨(u, w), he⟩ = true := by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨_, h | h⟩
      · exact h
      · obtain ⟨hwu, _⟩ := h
        have hwU := (Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hwu).1).1
        exact False.elim (Finset.disjoint_left.mp hUW hwU hw)
    · rintro ⟨huw, hω⟩
      exact ⟨(Finset.mem_filter.mp huw).2, Or.inl ⟨huw, hω⟩⟩
  let s : Finset V → Finset V → Finset I := fun A B =>
    Finset.univ.filter fun e => e.val ∈ A.product B
  have hsum (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W)
      (f : V × V → ℝ) :
      ∑ e ∈ s A B, f e.val =
        ∑ e ∈ (A.product B).filter (fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2), f e := by
    apply Finset.sum_bij (fun e _ => e.val)
    · intro e hem
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨(Finset.mem_filter.mp hem).2, (Finset.mem_filter.mp e.property).2⟩
    · intro e he f hf hef
      exact Subtype.ext hef
    · intro e hem
      obtain ⟨heAB, heG⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hem
      obtain ⟨heA, heB⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp heAB
      have heE : e ∈ E0 := Finset.mem_filter.mpr
        ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hAU heA, hBW heB⟩, heG⟩
      exact ⟨⟨e, heE⟩, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, heAB⟩, rfl⟩
    · intro e hem
      rfl
  have hcount (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W) (ω : I → Bool) :
      (((A.product B).filter fun e => (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) =
        ∑ e ∈ s A B, X e ω := by
    let f : V × V → ℝ := fun e => if he : e ∈ E0 then X ⟨e, he⟩ ω else 0
    have hsf : ∑ e ∈ s A B, X e ω = ∑ e ∈ s A B, f e.val := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro e hem
      simp only [f, dif_pos e.property]
      rfl
    rw [hsf, hsum A B hAU hBW f]
    have hfull : ∑ e ∈ (A.product B).filter (fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2), f e =
        ∑ e ∈ A.product B, f e := by
      apply Finset.sum_filter_of_ne
      intro e hem hf
      by_contra hg
      have hnE : e ∉ E0 := fun heE => hg (Finset.mem_filter.mp heE).2
      exact hf (dif_neg hnE)
    rw [hfull, ← Finset.sum_boole]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro e hem
    obtain ⟨heA, heB⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hem
    have hcross' := hcross ω e.1 (hAU heA) e.2 (hBW heB)
    by_cases heE : e ∈ E0
    · simp only [f, dif_pos heE, X]
      have hcross'' : (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2 ↔ ω ⟨e, heE⟩ = true := by
        refine ⟨fun hadj => ?_, fun hω => hcross'.mpr ⟨heE, hω⟩⟩
        obtain ⟨heE', hω⟩ := hcross'.mp hadj
        exact hω
      simp only [hcross'']
    · have hnot : ¬(H ω).Adj e.1 e.2 := fun hadj =>
        (hcross'.mp hadj).elim (fun he _ => heE he)
      simp only [hnot, if_false, f, dif_neg heE]
  have hmean (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W) :
      ∑ e ∈ s A B, p e.val = ∑ e ∈ A.product B, p e := by
    rw [hsum A B hAU hBW p]
    apply Finset.sum_filter_of_ne
    intro e hem hne
    by_contra hg
    exact hne (hzero e hg)
  have htrials (A B : Finset V) : (s A B).card ≤ A.card * B.card := by
    have hinj : Function.Injective (fun e : I => e.val) := Subtype.val_injective
    have hsub : (s A B).image (fun e => e.val) ⊆ A.product B := by
      intro e he
      obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp he
      exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2
    have := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rwa [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj, Finset.product_eq_sprod,
      Finset.card_product] at this
  have hrowcard (F : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel F.Adj] (u : V) :
      ((({u} : Finset V).product W).filter fun e => F.Adj e.1 e.2).card =
        (W.filter fun w => F.Adj u w).card := by
    have he : ((({u} : Finset V).product W).filter fun e => F.Adj e.1 e.2) =
        ({u} : Finset V).product (W.filter fun w => F.Adj u w) := by
      ext e
      simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product,
        Finset.mem_singleton]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨rfl, hw⟩, ha⟩
        exact ⟨rfl, hw, ha⟩
      · rintro ⟨rfl, hw, ha⟩
        exact ⟨⟨rfl, hw⟩, ha⟩
    rw [he, Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.card_product]
    simp
  have hcolcard (F : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel F.Adj] (w : V) :
      ((U.product ({w} : Finset V)).filter fun e => F.Adj e.1 e.2).card =
        (U.filter fun u => F.Adj u w).card := by
    have he : ((U.product ({w} : Finset V)).filter fun e => F.Adj e.1 e.2) =
        (U.filter fun u => F.Adj u w).product ({w} : Finset V) := by
      ext e
      simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product,
        Finset.mem_singleton]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨hu, he⟩, ha⟩
        rw [he] at ha
        exact ⟨⟨hu, ha⟩, he⟩
      · rintro ⟨⟨hu, ha⟩, he⟩
        rw [← he] at ha
        exact ⟨⟨hu, he⟩, ha⟩
    rw [he, Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.card_product]
    simp
  have hmeanlo (A B : Finset V) (hAU : A ⊆ U) (hBW : B ⊆ W) :
      d * (((A.product B).filter fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) ≤
        ∑ e ∈ s A B, p e.val := by
    rw [hsum A B hAU hBW p]
    calc
      _ = ∑ _e ∈ (A.product B).filter (fun e => G.Adj e.1 e.2), d := by
        simp [mul_comm]
      _ ≤ _ := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro e he
        obtain ⟨heAB, heG⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp he
        obtain ⟨heA, heB⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp heAB
        exact hpedge e.1 (hAU heA) e.2 (hBW heB) heG
  have hrowmean (u) (hu : u ∈ U) : 2 * c * n ≤ ∑ e ∈ s {u} W, p e.val := by
    have hlo := hmeanlo {u} W (Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hu) (Finset.Subset.refl _)
    rw [hrowcard] at hlo
    have hdeg := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hdegU u hu) hd.le
    dsimp only [c]
    nlinarith only [hlo, hdeg]
  have hcolmean (w) (hw : w ∈ W) : 2 * c * n ≤ ∑ e ∈ s U {w}, p e.val := by
    have hlo := hmeanlo U {w} (Finset.Subset.refl _) (Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hw)
    rw [hcolcard] at hlo
    have hdeg := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hdegW w hw) hd.le
    dsimp only [c]
    nlinarith only [hlo, hdeg]
  let badU : V → Set (I → Bool) := fun u =>
    {ω | c * n / 4 < |∑ e ∈ s {u} W, Y e ω|}
  let badW : V → Set (I → Bool) := fun w =>
    {ω | c * n / 4 < |∑ e ∈ s U {w}, Y e ω|}
  have hdegreeTail (A B : Finset V) (hr : (s A B).card ≤ n) :
      μ.real {ω | c * n / 4 < |∑ e ∈ s A B, Y e ω|} ≤
        2 * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) := by
    have ht : 0 ≤ c * (n : ℝ) / 4 := by positivity
    have hb := FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail μ Y (s A B) hind
      (fun e _ => hsg e) n (c * n / 4) hnr (Nat.cast_le.mpr hr) ht
    have heq : -2 * (c * (n : ℝ) / 4) ^ 2 / n = -c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8 := by
      field_simp
      ring
    rwa [heq] at hb
  have htailU (u) : μ.real (badU u) ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) := by
    apply hdegreeTail
    simpa only [Finset.card_singleton, one_mul, hW] using htrials {u} W
  have htailW (w) : μ.real (badW w) ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) := by
    apply hdegreeTail
    simpa only [Finset.card_singleton, mul_one, hU] using htrials U {w}
  let bad : Finset V × Finset V → Set (I → Bool) := fun AB =>
    {ω | h * n < (AB.1.card : ℝ) ∧ h * n < (AB.2.card : ℝ) ∧
      (h / 4) * AB.1.card * AB.2.card < |∑ e ∈ s AB.1 AB.2, Y e ω|}
  have htail (AB : Finset V × Finset V) :
      μ.real (bad AB) ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) := by
    by_cases hA : h * n < (AB.1.card : ℝ)
    · by_cases hB : h * n < (AB.2.card : ℝ)
      · let N : ℝ := (AB.1.card : ℝ) * AB.2.card
        have hhn : 0 < h * (n : ℝ) := mul_pos hh hnr
        have hapos : 0 < (AB.1.card : ℝ) := hhn.trans hA
        have hbpos : 0 < (AB.2.card : ℝ) := hhn.trans hB
        have hN : 0 < N := mul_pos hapos hbpos
        have hr : ((s AB.1 AB.2).card : ℝ) ≤ N := by
          dsimp only [N]
          exact_mod_cast htrials AB.1 AB.2
        have ht : 0 ≤ (h / 4) * N := by positivity
        have hbound := FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail μ Y (s AB.1 AB.2) hind
          (fun e _ => hsg e) N ((h / 4) * N) hN hr ht
        have hsub : bad AB ⊆ {ω | (h / 4) * N < |∑ e ∈ s AB.1 AB.2, Y e ω|} := by
          intro ω hω
          change (h / 4) * N < |∑ e ∈ s AB.1 AB.2, Y e ω|
          simpa only [N, mul_assoc] using hω.2.2
        have heq : -2 * ((h / 4) * N) ^ 2 / N = -h ^ 2 * N / 8 := by
          field_simp
          ring
        have hNlo : h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ N := by
          calc
            h ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 = (h * n) * (h * n) := by ring
            _ ≤ (AB.1.card : ℝ) * AB.2.card :=
              mul_le_mul hA.le hB.le hhn.le hapos.le
        have hexp : -h ^ 2 * N / 8 ≤ -h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8 := by
          nlinarith only [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hNlo (sq_nonneg h)]
        rw [heq] at hbound
        exact (measureReal_mono hsub).trans
          (hbound.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hexp) (by norm_num)))
      · have hempty : bad AB = ∅ := by
          ext ω
          simp only [bad, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
          exact fun hω => hB hω.2.1
        rw [hempty, measureReal_empty]
        positivity
    · have hempty : bad AB = ∅ := by
        ext ω
        simp only [bad, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
        exact fun hω => hA hω.1
      rw [hempty, measureReal_empty]
      positivity
  let tests := U.powerset.product W.powerset
  have htests : (tests.card : ℝ) = (4 : ℝ) ^ n := by
    change ((U.powerset.product W.powerset).card : ℝ) = (4 : ℝ) ^ n
    simp only [Finset.product_eq_sprod, Finset.card_product, Finset.card_powerset, hU, hW,
      Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat]
    rw [← mul_pow]
    norm_num
  let degreeFailure := (⋃ u ∈ U, badU u) ∪ (⋃ w ∈ W, badW w)
  let rectangleFailure := ⋃ AB ∈ tests, bad AB
  have hfinite {β : Type _} (t : Finset β) (f : β → Set (I → Bool))
      (b : ℝ) (hf : ∀ i ∈ t, μ.real (f i) ≤ b) :
      μ.real (⋃ i ∈ t, f i) ≤ t.card * b := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ t, μ.real (f i) := measureReal_biUnion_finset_le t f
      _ ≤ ∑ _i ∈ t, b := Finset.sum_le_sum hf
      _ = t.card * b := by simp [nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hdfail : μ.real degreeFailure < 1 / 4 := by
    calc
      _ ≤ μ.real (⋃ u ∈ U, badU u) + μ.real (⋃ w ∈ W, badW w) :=
        measureReal_union_le _ _
      _ ≤ (U.card : ℝ) * (2 * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8)) +
          W.card * (2 * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8)) :=
        add_le_add (hfinite U badU _ (fun u _ => htailU u))
          (hfinite W badW _ (fun w _ => htailW w))
      _ = 4 * n * Real.exp (-c ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) := by rw [hU, hW]; ring
      _ < 1 / 4 := hdegreeCut
  have hrfail : μ.real rectangleFailure < 1 / 4 := by
    calc
      _ ≤ (tests.card : ℝ) * (2 * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8)) :=
        hfinite tests bad _ (fun AB _ => htail AB)
      _ = 2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n * Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) := by
        rw [htests]
        ring
      _ < 1 / 4 := hrectangleCut
  let failure := degreeFailure ∪ rectangleFailure
  -- Select only after bounding both families under the same product law.
  have hfail : μ.real failure < 1 := by
    have hb : μ.real failure ≤ μ.real degreeFailure + μ.real rectangleFailure :=
      measureReal_union_le _ _
    linarith only [hb, hdfail, hrfail]
  obtain ⟨ω, hgood⟩ : ∃ ω, ω ∉ failure := by
    have hm : MeasurableSet failure := (Set.to_countable failure).measurableSet
    have hpos : μ failureᶜ ≠ 0 := by
      apply (measureReal_eq_zero_iff).not.mp
      rw [probReal_compl_eq_one_sub hm]
      linarith only [hfail]
    exact nonempty_of_measure_ne_zero hpos
  have hgoodU (u) (hu : u ∈ U) : |∑ e ∈ s {u} W, Y e ω| ≤ c * n / 4 := by
    apply le_of_not_gt
    intro hb
    apply hgood
    exact Or.inl (Or.inl (Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨u, Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨hu, hb⟩⟩))
  have hgoodW (w) (hw : w ∈ W) : |∑ e ∈ s U {w}, Y e ω| ≤ c * n / 4 := by
    apply le_of_not_gt
    intro hb
    apply hgood
    exact Or.inl (Or.inr (Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨w, Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨hw, hb⟩⟩))
  refine ⟨H ω, inferInstance, hcontain ω, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u hu
    have hcount' := hcount {u} W (Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hu)
      (Finset.Subset.refl _) ω
    rw [hrowcard (H ω) u] at hcount'
    have hb := (abs_le.mp (hgoodU u hu)).1
    simp only [Y, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] at hb
    have hm := hrowmean u hu
    rw [← hcount'] at hb
    change (7 * c / 4) * n ≤ _
    linarith only [hb, hm]
  · intro w hw
    have hcount' := hcount U {w} (Finset.Subset.refl _)
      (Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hw) ω
    rw [hcolcard (H ω) w] at hcount'
    have hb := (abs_le.mp (hgoodW w hw)).1
    simp only [Y, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] at hb
    have hm := hcolmean w hw
    rw [← hcount'] at hb
    change (7 * c / 4) * n ≤ _
    linarith only [hb, hm]
  · intro A hAU B hBW hA hB
    have hm : (A, B) ∈ tests := Finset.mem_product.mpr
      ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.mpr hAU, Finset.mem_powerset.mpr hBW⟩
    have hb : |∑ e ∈ s A B, Y e ω| ≤ (h / 4) * A.card * B.card := by
      apply le_of_not_gt
      intro hb
      apply hgood
      exact Or.inr (Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨(A, B), Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨hm, hA, hB, hb⟩⟩)
    have hsample : |(((A.product B).filter fun e => (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) -
        ∑ e ∈ A.product B, p e| ≤ (h / 4) * A.card * B.card := by
      rw [hcount A B hAU hBW ω, ← hmean A B hAU hBW]
      simpa only [Y, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] using hb
    have hex := hexpect A hAU B hBW hA hB
    have hdiscrep : |(((A.product B).filter fun e => (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) -
        d * A.card * B.card| < (h / 2) * A.card * B.card := by
      have ht := abs_sub_le
        (((A.product B).filter fun e => (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ)
        (∑ e ∈ A.product B, p e) (d * A.card * B.card)
      linarith only [ht, hsample, hex]
    have hAp : 0 < (A.card : ℝ) := (mul_pos hh hnr).trans hA
    have hBp : 0 < (B.card : ℝ) := (mul_pos hh hnr).trans hB
    have hden : 0 < (A.card : ℝ) * B.card := mul_pos hAp hBp
    have hid : ((H ω).edgeDensity A B : ℝ) - d =
        ((((A.product B).filter fun e => (H ω).Adj e.1 e.2).card : ℝ) -
          d * A.card * B.card) / ((A.card : ℝ) * B.card) := by
      simp only [SimpleGraph.edgeDensity_def, SimpleGraph.interedges_def,
        Rat.cast_div, Rat.cast_mul, Rat.cast_natCast, Finset.product_eq_sprod]
      field_simp
    rw [hid, abs_div, abs_of_pos hden]
    apply (div_lt_iff₀ hden).mpr
    simpa only [mul_assoc] using hdiscrep

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

theorem SuperRegularInitialSample
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
    (n l M : ℕ) (ε d h γ α : ℝ)
    (hU : U.card = n) (hW : W.card = n) (hUW : Disjoint U W)
    (hcover : U ∪ W = Finset.univ)
    (hbip : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, G.Adj u v →
      (u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ W) ∨ (u ∈ W ∧ v ∈ U))
    (hl : 1 ≤ l) (hlM : l ≤ M) (hMn : M ≤ n)
    (hbound : SzemerediRegularity.bound α l ≤ M)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d < 1) (hh : 0 < h)
    (hγ : 0 < γ) (hγ1 : γ ≤ 1) (hα : 0 < α)
    (hαγ : α ≤ γ) (hαγγ : α ≤ γ ^ 2) (hεM : ε * M < γ)
    (hmargin : 2 * α + (6 * γ + 9 * α + 6 / (l : ℝ)) / h ^ 2 < h / 4)
    (hdegreeCut : 4 * n * Real.exp (-(d ^ 2 / 2) ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) / 8) < 1 / 4)
    (hrectangleCut : 2 * (4 : ℝ) ^ n *
      Real.exp (-h ^ 4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 8) < 1 / 4)
    (hlower : ∀ A ⊆ U, ∀ B ⊆ W, ε * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
      ε * n < (B.card : ℝ) → d ≤ (G.edgeDensity A B : ℝ))
    (hdegU : ∀ u ∈ U, d * n ≤ ((W.filter fun w => G.Adj u w).card : ℝ))
    (hdegW : ∀ w ∈ W, d * n ≤ ((U.filter fun u => G.Adj u w).card : ℝ)) :
    ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel H.Adj,
      H ≤ G ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U, (7 * (d ^ 2 / 2) / 4) * n ≤
        ((W.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ)) ∧
      (∀ w ∈ W, (7 * (d ^ 2 / 2) / 4) * n ≤
        ((U.filter fun u => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ)) ∧
      (∀ A ⊆ U, ∀ B ⊆ W, h * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
        h * n < (B.card : ℝ) → |(H.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) - d| < h / 2) := by
SuperRegularInitialSample.name: SuperRegularInitialSample
SuperRegularInitialSample.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $1\leq l\leq M\leq n$, $n>0$. The covering disjoint parts
give $|V|=2n$, so $l\leq|V|$. Apply
Mathlib's \texttt{szemeredi\_regularity} from
\texttt{Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Lemma} with $\alpha,l$, obtaining
an equipartition $\mathcal P$ with
$l\leq|\mathcal P|\leq\operatorname{SzemerediRegularity.bound}(\alpha,l)\leq M$
which is $\alpha$-uniform. Apply
\noderef{RegularExtractionPartitionGeometry} with the stated lower
density assumption. Its statement supplies the eligible set
$E\subseteq\mathcal P\times\mathcal P$, densities
$d\leq D_{ST}=d_G(U\cap S,W\cap T)\leq1$, the slicing error
$2\alpha$, and ineligible area at most $(4\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)n^2$.
These are exactly the three hypotheses needed by
\noderef{WeightedRectangleExpectation}. Obtain its weight $p$, zero
on nonedges and outside $U\times W$, with $0\leq p\leq1$.
For every original crossing edge, its endpoints belong to unique
parts $S,T$. The weight formula says $p=d/D_{ST}$ on eligible
rectangles, and $p=1$ otherwise. On an eligible rectangle
$0<d\leq D_{ST}\leq1$, so $p\geq d$; on an ineligible rectangle
the same inequality follows from $d<1$. Thus every original
crossing edge has retention probability at least $d$.
The final clause of \noderef{WeightedRectangleExpectation}, with
the assumed margin, gives
\[
\left|\sum_{(a,b)\in A\times B}p(a,b)-d|A||B|\right|
<(h/4)|A||B|\quad (|A|,|B|>hn).                 \tag{1}
\]

Index the independent trials by the original edges oriented from
$U$ to $W$, one trial per undirected edge. Take their finite
Bernoulli product law with probabilities $p$.
\noderef{IndependentUnequalEdgeSampleLaw} gives a probability
measure, independent coordinate indicators of means $p$, and
centered indicators of subgaussian parameter $1/4$.
Translation of independent indicators by their constant means
preserves independence. In an outcome include precisely the
successful edges, in both orientations, on the original vertex
set. This defines a simple graph contained in $G$; its crossing
edge counts are the corresponding sums of indicators.

For any vertex its opposite-part degree is a sum of at most $n$
distinct trials. Its mean is at least
$d\deg_G(v)\geq d^2n=2cn$. Apply
\noderef{FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail} with $N=n>0$ and
$t=cn/4>0$ to its centered sum. The probability that its degree
differs from its mean by more than $cn/4$ is at most
$2e^{-c^2n/8}$. There are $2n$ vertices, so the union of these
degree bad events has probability at most $4ne^{-c^2n/8}<1/4$.
This bound includes empty trial sets, for which the centered
sum is zero.

For each $A\subseteq U,B\subseteq W$ with $|A|,|B|>hn$, put
$N=|A||B|>h^2n^2>0$. There are at most $N$ trials in its edge
count. Apply \noderef{FiniteIndependentSubgaussianTail} with
$t=(h/4)N$. Its bad event has probability at most
$2e^{-h^2N/8}\leq2e^{-h^4n^2/8}$.
The number of pairs of subsets is $2^n2^n=4^n$, so the union
of all rectangle bad events has probability at most
$2\,4^n e^{-h^4n^2/8}<1/4$.
Both types of bad events use the same sample law. Their union
has probability less than $1/2$, hence its complement has positive
probability and contains an outcome. Fix it and call the graph $H$.
Its degrees are at least $2cn-cn/4=7cn/4$ simultaneously on both
sides. For a tested rectangle its sampled count differs from its
mean by at most $(h/4)|A||B|$. Combining this weak bound with
the strict inequality (1) gives discrepancy from $d|A||B|$
strictly less than $(h/2)|A||B|$. Dividing by the positive
$|A||B|$ gives the stated density error. All graphs have the
original vertex type and finite decidable adjacency; containment
and the original bipartition are preserved.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularInitialSample.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Joint weighted extraction sample]
Let $G$ be a finite bipartite graph on the disjoint covering parts
$U,W$, with $|U|=|W|=n$. Let integers and real parameters satisfy
\[
1\leq l\leq M\leq n,\quad\operatorname{SzemerediRegularity.bound}(\alpha,l)\leq M,
\quad\varepsilon,h,\gamma,\alpha>0,\quad0<d<1,
\]
\[
\gamma\leq1,\quad\alpha\leq\gamma,\quad\alpha\leq\gamma^2,
\quad\varepsilon M<\gamma,
\quad2\alpha+(6\gamma+9\alpha+6/l)/h^2<h/4.
\]
Put $c=d^2/2$, and assume
\[
4n e^{-c^2n/8}<1/4,\qquad2\,4^n e^{-h^4n^2/8}<1/4.
\]
Suppose $d_G(A,B)\geq d$ for every $A\subseteq U,B\subseteq W$
with $|A|,|B|>\varepsilon n$, and every vertex has at least $dn$
neighbors in the opposite part. There is a graph $H$ on the same
vertex set with $H\subseteq G$, opposite-part degrees at least
$7cn/4$ on both sides, and
\[
|d_H(A,B)-d|<h/2\qquad
(A\subseteq U,\ B\subseteq W,\ |A|,|B|>hn).
\]
\end{lemma}

classical
  have card (S : Finset V) : (S.image e).card = S.card :=
    Finset.card_image_of_injective S hinj
  have density (P Q : Finset V) (hP : P ⊆ L) (hQ : Q ⊆ R) :
      PairDensity H (P.image e) (Q.image e) = PairDensity G P Q := by
    have edges :
        (((P.image e).product (Q.image e)).filter fun p => H.Adj p.1 p.2) =
        ((P.product Q).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).image (Prod.map e e) := by
      change (((P.image e) ×ˢ (Q.image e)).filter _) = _
      rw [← Finset.prodMap_image_product, Finset.filter_image]
      congr 1
      apply Finset.filter_congr
      intro p hp
      obtain ⟨hp, hq⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hp
      exact hadj p.1 (hP hp) p.2 (hQ hq)
    unfold PairDensity
    rw [edges, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (hinj.prodMap hinj), card, card]
  have left (x : V) (hx : x ∈ L) :
      ((R.image e).filter fun y => H.Adj (e x) y).card =
        (R.filter fun y => G.Adj x y).card := by
    rw [Finset.filter_image]
    have hh : R.filter (fun y => H.Adj (e x) (e y)) =
        R.filter (fun y => G.Adj x y) :=
      Finset.filter_congr fun y hy => hadj x hx y hy
    rw [hh, card]
  have right (y : V) (hy : y ∈ R) :
      ((L.image e).filter fun x => H.Adj x (e y)).card =
        (L.filter fun x => G.Adj x y).card := by
    rw [Finset.filter_image]
    have hh : L.filter (fun x => H.Adj (e x) (e y)) =
        L.filter (fun x => G.Adj x y) :=
      Finset.filter_congr fun x hx => hadj x hx y hy
    rw [hh, card]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro P hP Q hQ hsizeP hsizeQ
    let P0 := L.filter fun x => e x ∈ P
    let Q0 := R.filter fun x => e x ∈ Q
    have pull (S : Finset V) (A : Finset W) (hA : A ⊆ S.image e) :
        (S.filter fun x => e x ∈ A).image e = A := by
      ext y
      constructor
      · rintro hy
        obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hy
        exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).2
      · intro hy
        obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp (hA hy)
        exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hx, hy⟩, rfl⟩
    have hp : P0.image e = P := pull L P hP
    have hq : Q0.image e = Q := pull R Q hQ
    rw [← hp, card, card] at hsizeP
    rw [← hq, card, card] at hsizeQ
    rw [← hp, ← hq, density P0 Q0 (Finset.filter_subset _ _) (Finset.filter_subset _ _)]
    exact hG.1 P0 (Finset.filter_subset _ _) Q0 (Finset.filter_subset _ _)
      hsizeP hsizeQ
  · intro x hx
    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
    simpa only [card, left a ha] using hG.2.1 a ha
  · intro y hy
    obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hy
    simpa only [card, right b hb] using hG.2.2 b hb
SuperRegularPairEmbedding.lean_statement:
theorem SuperRegularPairEmbedding
    {V W : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq W]
    (e : V → W) (hinj : Function.Injective e)
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (L R : Finset V) (eps d : ENNReal)
    (hadj : ∀ x ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ R, H.Adj (e x) (e y) ↔ G.Adj x y)
    (hG : SuperRegularPair G L R eps d) :
    SuperRegularPair H (L.image e) (R.image e) eps d := by
SuperRegularPairEmbedding.name: SuperRegularPairEmbedding
SuperRegularPairEmbedding.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
By injectivity, $|e(S)|=|S|$ for every finite $S\subseteq V$.
For $P\subseteq L$, $Q\subseteq R$, the map $(x,y)\mapsto(e(x),e(y))$
is a bijection between their ordered edge sets: injectivity gives
uniqueness of preimages, and the assumed adjacency equivalence gives
both edge preservation and edge reflection. Hence the edge counts
and, by \noderef{PairDensity}, the densities of these rectangles agree.
For arbitrary $P'\subseteq e(L)$, $Q'\subseteq e(R)$, take
$P=\{x\in L:e(x)\in P'\}$ and $Q=\{y\in R:e(y)\in Q'\}$.
Their images are exactly $P',Q'$. Their sizes equal the sizes of those
images, so the strict rectangle-size hypotheses in
\noderef{RegularPair} pull back exactly. Apply the regularity clause
of \noderef{SuperRegularPair} and the density identity to obtain both
density bounds on $P',Q'$.
For a left vertex $e(x)$ with $x\in L$, the map $y\mapsto e(y)$ is
a bijection from its neighbours in $R$ to the neighbours of $e(x)$
in $e(R)$. The right-neighbour count is identical. Likewise, for
$e(y)$ with $y\in R$, its neighbours in $e(L)$ correspond exactly
to the neighbours of $y$ in $L$. Applying the two degree clauses of
\noderef{SuperRegularPair}, and replacing the part sizes by their equal
image sizes, proves both degree windows and completes the proof.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularPairEmbedding.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Super-regularity under a part embedding]
Let $e:V\to W$ be injective, $G,H$ graphs on $V,W$, and $L,R$ finite
parts of $V$. Suppose $H(e(x),e(y))$ holds if and only if $G(x,y)$
for every $x\in L$, $y\in R$. If $(G;L,R)$ is
$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular, then $(H;e(L),e(R))$ is
$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular. No surjectivity on the ambient type
is assumed.
\end{lemma}
SuperRegularPairEmbedding.title: SuperRegularPairEmbedding

theorem SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion
    {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (L R A B : Finset V) (m : ℕ) (τ η c : ℝ)
    (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η ≤ 1)
    (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hc1 : c ≤ 1) (hsmall : 4 * τ ≤ η)
    (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hfloor : 4 ≤ η * m)
    (hAL : A ⊆ L) (hBR : B ⊆ R)
    (hA : m ≤ A.card) (hB : m ≤ B.card)
    (hLA : L.card ≤ A.card + 1) (hRB : R.card ≤ B.card + 1)
    (hG : SuperRegularPair G L R (ENNReal.ofReal τ) (ENNReal.ofReal c)) :
    SuperRegularPair G A B (ENNReal.ofReal η) (ENNReal.ofReal c) := by
SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion.name: SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion
SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $|A|,|B|\geq1$, we have $|L|\leq2|A|$ and
$|R|\leq2|B|$. Thus $\tau|L|\leq\eta|A|$ and
$\tau|R|\leq\eta|B|$. Every strict regularity test for $A,B$
is therefore a test for $L,R$. Its ordered-edge count and density
are the same, and the interval with error $\tau$ is contained in
the interval with error $\eta$. This gives \noderef{RegularPair}.

For either degree orientation, denote the original opposite part by
$S$, its retained subset by $T$, and the old and retained neighbor
counts by $a,b$. Since $|S\setminus T|\leq1$, we have
$b\leq a\leq b+1$. Put $k=|T|$ and $s=|S|$; then
$k\leq s\leq k+1$, $\eta k\geq4$, and $\tau k\leq\eta k/4$.
The degree bounds in \noderef{SuperRegularPair} give
$(c-\tau)s\leq a\leq(c+\tau)s$ as real inequalities:
if the first endpoint is negative, the first inequality is automatic.
If $c\geq\eta$, then $c-\tau\geq0$ and
\[
 b\geq(c-\tau)s-1\geq(c-\tau)k-1\geq(c-\eta)k,
\]
because $(\eta-\tau)k\geq3\eta k/4\geq3$.
If $c<\eta$, the required truncated lower bound is zero.
For the upper bound, $\tau\leq1$ and $c\leq1$ give
\[
 b\leq(c+\tau)(k+1)\leq(c+\tau)k+2\leq(c+\eta)k.
\]
Apply this argument at every vertex of $A$ with $S=R,T=B$, and
at every vertex of $B$ with $S=L,T=A$. These are both required
degree intervals, completing the three clauses of super-regularity.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Deleting at most one vertex from each part]
Let $G$ be a simple graph with finite parts $L,R$ and subsets
$A\subseteq L,B\subseteq R$. Let $m\geq1$ be an integer with
$|A|,|B|\geq m$, $|L|\leq|A|+1$, and $|R|\leq|B|+1$.
For real parameters suppose $0\leq\tau$, $0<\eta\leq1$,
$0\leq c\leq1$, $4\tau\leq\eta$, and $\eta m\geq4$.
If $(L,R)$ is $(\tau,c)$-super-regular, then $(A,B)$ is
$(\eta,c)$-super-regular. All parameters in the pair predicates
are interpreted as extended nonnegative reals, with truncated lower endpoints.
\end{lemma}
SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion.title: SuperRegularPairOneVertexDeletion

    simpa [ENNReal.toReal_mul, e, δ] using h

    ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le hεle hdtop

    simp [e, δ]

          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro u hu
          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
          intro w hw

        simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, hU] using
          (lt_of_not_ge hAsmall)
      have hBgt : ε * (W.card : ENNReal) < (B.card : ENNReal) := by
        apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal
          (ENNReal.mul_ne_top hεtop (by simp)) (by simp)).mp
        simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, hW] using
          (lt_of_not_ge hBsmall)

        (Or.inl (ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by simp) (by simp)))).mp hdensity

          (ENNReal.mul_ne_top (ne_top_of_le_ne_top hdtop tsub_le_self)
            (ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by simp) (by simp))) (by simp)).mpr hedge
        simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, hsub] using h

          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hkhi (by linarith)

        (k : ℝ) * ((A.card : ℝ) + B.card - n) := by
      rw [Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_sub hdefpos.le, Nat.cast_add]
    have hnatReal : ((k * (A.card + B.card - n) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        (((A.product B).filter fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2).card : ℝ) := by
      rw [hcast]
      exact hreal
    exact_mod_cast hnatReal
  obtain ⟨F, hFG, hFU, hFW⟩ :=
    (BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion G U W hUW k (hU.trans hW.symm)).mpr hcuts
  refine ⟨k, F, hFG, ?_, hFU, hFW⟩
  apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal
    (ENNReal.mul_ne_top (ne_top_of_le_ne_top hdtop tsub_le_self) (by simp))
    (by simp)).mp
  simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_natCast, hsubtwo] using hklo

theorem SuperRegularSpanningFactor :
    ∀ ε d : ENNReal, 0 < ε → 2 * ε < d → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
        (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
        (hUW : Disjoint U W) (n : ℕ), n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n →
        SuperRegularPair G U W ε d →
        ∃ (k : ℕ) (F : SimpleGraph V), F ≤ G ∧
          (d - 2 * ε) * (n : ENNReal) ≤ (k : ENNReal) ∧
          (∀ u ∈ U, {w | w ∈ W ∧ F.Adj u w}.ncard = k) ∧
          (∀ w ∈ W, {u | u ∈ U ∧ F.Adj u w}.ncard = k) := by
SuperRegularSpanningFactor.name: SuperRegularSpanningFactor
SuperRegularSpanningFactor.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Because $d\leq1$ and $2\varepsilon<d$, both parameters are finite real
numbers despite being represented as extended nonnegative reals.  Choose
$n_0$ so large that $\varepsilon n\geq2$ for $n\geq n_0$, and fix such an
$n$.  By \noderef{SuperRegularPair}, the super-regular hypothesis supplies
the $\operatorname{RegularPair}$ clause used below for the large--large
density estimate, together with the two opposite-side degree bounds used in
the two small-side cases.  Put
\[
 q=(d-2\varepsilon)n,qquad k=\lceil q\rceil.
\]
Then $k\geq q$.  Also $k<q+1\leq(d-\varepsilon)n$, the last inequality
following from $1\leq\varepsilon n$.  We verify the cut condition of
\noderef{BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion}.

Fix $A\subseteq U$ and $B\subseteq W$, write $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$, and put
$s=a+b-n$.  There is nothing to prove if $s\leq0$, so assume $s>0$.
First suppose $a>\varepsilon n$ and $b>\varepsilon n$.  Regularity gives
\[
 e_G(A,B)\geq(d-\varepsilon)ab.
\]
Indeed the definition of density says
$e_G(A,B)=d_G(A,B)ab$, and neither $a$ nor $b$ is zero.  The elementary
identity
\[
 ab-n(a+b-n)=(n-a)(n-b)\geq0
\]
gives $ab\geq ns$.  Since $k\leq(d-\varepsilon)n$, it follows that
$e_G(A,B)\geq(d-\varepsilon)ns\geq ks$.

Suppose next that $a\leq\varepsilon n$.  Since $s>0$, write $b=n-t$ with
$0\leq t<a$.  Every vertex of $A$ has at least $(d-\varepsilon)n$
neighbours in $W$, and at most $t$ of them lie in $W\setminus B$.  Thus
\[
 e_G(A,B)\geq a((d-\varepsilon)n-t).
\]
If $a\leq k$, then
\[
 a((d-\varepsilon)n-t)-k(a-t)
 =a((d-\varepsilon)n-k)+t(k-a)\geq0.
\]
Here both terms are nonnegative because $k\leq(d-\varepsilon)n$.  If
$a>k$, the same affine expression is decreasing in $t$, so it is bounded
below by its value at $t=a$ (even though the actual integer satisfies
$t<a$).  That value is $a((d-\varepsilon)n-a)$, which is nonnegative since
$a\leq\varepsilon n<(d-\varepsilon)n$ by $2\varepsilon<d$.
Thus $e_G(A,B)\geq k(a-t)=ks$ in either subcase.

The case $b\leq\varepsilon n$ is identical with $U,W$ interchanged, using
the minimum-degree condition on vertices of $B$.  The remaining possibility
has already been treated by regularity.  Therefore every cut inequality
holds, and \noderef{BipartiteRegularFactorCriterion} supplies the desired
spanning $k$-regular subgraph.  Its construction uses only edges of $G$, and
the ceiling choice gives the stated extended-nonnegative-real inequality
after coercing the natural number $k$.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularSpanningFactor.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Regular factor in a super-regular pair]
For every $0<\varepsilon$ and $2\varepsilon<d\leq1$, there is $n_0$ such
that, whenever $n\geq n_0$ and $G[U,W]$ is an
$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular pair with $|U|=|W|=n$, it contains a
spanning $k$-regular subgraph for some natural number $k$ satisfying
$k\geq(d-2\varepsilon)n$.
\end{lemma}
SuperRegularSpanningFactor.title: SuperRegularSpanningFactor

      apply (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal (by finiteness) (by simp)).mp

  obtain ⟨H, hHdec, hHG, hreserveU, hreserveW, hrectH⟩ :=

  letI := hHdec
  obtain ⟨U₀, W₀, hU₀, hW₀, hbadU, hbadW, hcoreU, hcoreW⟩ :=
    SuperRegularTypicalCore H U W n d.toReal h hnpos hh hh1 hU hW hrectH
  have hcoreRect : ∀ A ⊆ U₀, ∀ B ⊆ W₀,
      h * n < (A.card : ℝ) → h * n < (B.card : ℝ) →

    intro A hA B hB

  obtain ⟨F, hFdec, hFH, hFsupport, hFdegU, hFdegW, hrectF⟩ :=
    SuperRegularCoreSample H U₀ W₀ n d.toReal h hnpos hdR hdR1 hh

SuperRegularSubgraph.lean_statement:
-- The partition input comes from szemeredi_regularity through SuperRegularInitialSample.

theorem SuperRegularSubgraph :
    ∀ ε' d : ENNReal, 0 < ε' → ε' < 1 → 0 < d → d < 1 →
      ∃ ε : ENNReal, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < ε' ∧
        ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
          (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V) (n : ℕ),
          n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n → Disjoint U W →
          U ∪ W = Finset.univ →
          (∀ ⦃u v⦄, G.Adj u v →
            (u ∈ U ∧ v ∈ W) ∨ (u ∈ W ∧ v ∈ U)) →
          LowerSuperRegularPair G U W ε (d + ε) →
          ∃ G' : SimpleGraph V, ∃ _ : DecidableRel G'.Adj,
            G' ≤ G ∧ SuperRegularPair G' U W ε' (d ^ 2 / 2) := by
SuperRegularSubgraph.name: SuperRegularSubgraph
SuperRegularSubgraph.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $\varepsilon',d<1$, both extended nonnegative parameters are
finite. Write $\eta,d_R$ for their real values; then
$0<\eta,d_R<1$, and converting them back recovers
$\varepsilon',d$. Put $c=d_R^2/2>0$, so $c<1$.
Apply \noderef{SuperRegularExtractionParameters} to $\eta,d_R$.
Its statement chooses $h,\gamma,\alpha,\varepsilon,l,M,n_0$
depending only on these two parameters, with
$0<\varepsilon<\eta$, $1\leq l\leq M\leq n_0$, the regularity
bound, the expectation margin, $h\leq1/100$, $h\leq c/100$,
$3h<\eta$, $4h<\eta$, and $2h+4h/\eta<\eta$.
For every $n\geq n_0$, it also gives $hn\geq1$ and the four
tail cutoffs less than $1/4$. Use the extended nonnegative value
of this $\varepsilon$ as the theorem's witness. Its strict
positivity and comparison with $\varepsilon'$ follow from the
real inequalities, since all parameters are finite.

Fix any input graph and $n\geq n_0$. Then $n>0$ and $M\leq n$.
Unpack the input using \noderef{LowerSuperRegularPair} and
\noderef{LowerRegularPair}, with parameters given by the extended
values of $\varepsilon$ and $d_R+\varepsilon$. Since these values
are finite, the truncated difference
$(d_R+\varepsilon)-\varepsilon$ equals the extended value of $d_R$.
For $A\subseteq U,B\subseteq W$ with
$|A|,|B|>\varepsilon n$, all cardinalities and parameters are finite,
so taking real values identifies these strict tests with the
extended tests $|A|>\varepsilon|U|$, $|B|>\varepsilon|W|$.
Moreover $|A|,|B|>\varepsilon n\geq0$, so both tested sets are
nonempty. The lower-regularity clause therefore gives an extended
density at least $d_R$. By \noderef{PairDensityReal}, this density
is finite and its real value is $d_G(A,B)$. Taking real values
gives $d_G(A,B)\geq d_R$.
For $u\in U$, the first degree clause, after the same cancellation,
gives the extended inequality
$d_R|W|\leq|N_G(u)\cap W|$. Both sides are finite; taking real
values and using $|W|=n$ gives $d_Rn\leq|N_G(u)\cap W|$ in
$\mathbb R$. For $w\in W$, the second clause similarly gives
$d_R|U|\leq|N_G(w)\cap U|$, hence the real bound
$d_Rn\leq|N_G(w)\cap U|$ using $|U|=n$.
Apply \noderef{SuperRegularInitialSample} using these
bounds, the partition parameters, expectation margin, and the
first two tail cutoffs. Its statement supplies a spanning
$H\subseteq G$ with opposite-part minimum degrees at least
$7cn/4$ and
\[
|d_H(A,B)-d_R|<h/2\quad(|A|,|B|>hn).
\]
Since $h\leq1/100<1$, \noderef{SuperRegularTypicalCore} applies
and gives $U_0\subseteq U,W_0\subseteq W$, complements of sizes
at most $2hn$, and core degrees in
$[(d_R-3h)n,(d_R+h)n]$ on both sides. The same density bound
holds for tests inside the core, because those sets are still
subsets of $U,W$.

The core parts are disjoint and have cardinalities at most $n$.
Apply \noderef{SuperRegularCoreSample} with their degree
intervals, inherited density tests, and the third and fourth
tail cutoffs. Its statement gives a graph $F\subseteq H$ on
the original vertex set, with edges only between the core
parts, core degrees in $[(c-4h)n,(c+2h)n]$, and core rectangle
density error at most $2h$.

All hypotheses of \noderef{SuperRegularExceptionalRestoration}
are now available: the disjoint covering full parts, inherited
bipartition of $H$, minimum-degree reserve $7cn/4$, the two
exceptional-size bounds, $F$'s containment and support, its
core degree and rectangle bounds, and the scalar and floor
margins listed above. Its statement yields a spanning
$G'\subseteq H$ which is $(\eta,c)$-super-regular in the
extended nonnegative predicates. Transitivity gives
$G'\subseteq G$. Finally the extended value of $\eta$ equals
$\varepsilon'$, and the extended value of $d_R^2/2$ equals
$d^2/2$: real conversion commutes with powers and division
by the positive finite number $2$. Thus this is precisely the
required super-regularity. All graphs use the same vertex
set and have decidable adjacency, and the choices of
$\varepsilon,n_0$ preceded the choice of the graph.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularSubgraph.title: SuperRegularSubgraph

SuperRegularTypicalCore.lean_proof:
classical
  have hnr : (0 : ℝ) < n := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hn
  have hhn : h * (n : ℝ) < n := by nlinarith only [hh1, hnr]
  have hcount : ∀ A R : Finset V,
      ((H.interedges A R).card : ℝ) =
        ∑ a ∈ A, ((R.filter fun r => H.Adj a r).card : ℝ) := by
    intro A R
    simp only [SimpleGraph.interedges_def, Finset.card_eq_sum_ones,
      Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_product, Nat.cast_sum, Nat.cast_ite,
      Nat.cast_one, Nat.cast_zero]
  have hdensity : ∀ A R : Finset V, 0 < (A.card : ℝ) → R.card = n →
      (H.edgeDensity A R : ℝ) * ((A.card : ℝ) * n) =
        ((H.interedges A R).card : ℝ) := by
    intro A R hA hR
    simp only [SimpleGraph.edgeDensity_def, Rat.cast_div, Rat.cast_mul,
      Rat.cast_natCast, hR]
    exact div_mul_cancel₀ _ (mul_pos hA hnr).ne'
  have typical : ∀ L R : Finset V, L.card = n → R.card = n →
      (∀ A ⊆ L, h * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
        |(H.edgeDensity A R : ℝ) - d| < h / 2) →
      ∃ L₀ : Finset V, L₀ ⊆ L ∧ ((L \ L₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n ∧
        ∀ v ∈ L₀, (d - h) * n ≤ ((R.filter fun w => H.Adj v w).card : ℝ) ∧
          ((R.filter fun w => H.Adj v w).card : ℝ) ≤ (d + h) * n := by
    as_aux_lemma =>
    intro L R _ hR htest
    let low := L.filter fun v => ((R.filter fun w => H.Adj v w).card : ℝ) < (d - h) * n
    let high := L.filter fun v => (d + h) * n < ((R.filter fun w => H.Adj v w).card : ℝ)
    have hlow : (low.card : ℝ) ≤ h * n := by
      by_contra! hlarge
      have hpos : 0 < (low.card : ℝ) := (mul_pos hh hnr).trans hlarge
      have hdens := (abs_lt.mp (htest low (Finset.filter_subset _ _) hlarge)).1
      have hsum : ((H.interedges low R).card : ℝ) ≤
          (d - h) * n * low.card := by
        rw [hcount]
        calc
          _ ≤ ∑ _v ∈ low, (d - h) * n := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun v hv =>
            (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2.le)
          _ = _ := by simp [mul_comm]
      have hprod := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right
        (show d - h / 2 < (H.edgeDensity low R : ℝ) by linarith only [hdens])
        (mul_pos hpos hnr)
      rw [hdensity low R hpos hR] at hprod
      have hgap := mul_pos hh (mul_pos hpos hnr)
      nlinarith only [hsum, hprod, hgap]
    have hhigh : (high.card : ℝ) ≤ h * n := by
      by_contra! hlarge
      have hpos : 0 < (high.card : ℝ) := (mul_pos hh hnr).trans hlarge
      have hdens := (abs_lt.mp (htest high (Finset.filter_subset _ _) hlarge)).2
      have hsum : (d + h) * n * high.card ≤
          ((H.interedges high R).card : ℝ) := by
        rw [hcount]
        calc
          _ = ∑ _v ∈ high, (d + h) * n := by simp [mul_comm]
          _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun v hv => (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2.le)
      have hprod := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right
        (show (H.edgeDensity high R : ℝ) < d + h / 2 by linarith only [hdens])
        (mul_pos hpos hnr)
      rw [hdensity high R hpos hR] at hprod
      have hgap := mul_pos hh (mul_pos hpos hnr)
      nlinarith only [hsum, hprod, hgap]
    let L₀ := L \ (low ∪ high)
    refine ⟨L₀, Finset.sdiff_subset, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have hsub : L \ L₀ ⊆ low ∪ high := by
        intro v hv
        obtain ⟨hvL, hvnot⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hv
        by_contra hvbad
        exact hvnot (Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hvL, hvbad⟩)
      have hcard : (L \ L₀).card ≤ low.card + high.card :=
        (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans (Finset.card_union_le _ _)
      have hcardR : ((L \ L₀).card : ℝ) ≤ (low.card : ℝ) + high.card := by
        exact_mod_cast hcard
      linarith only [hcardR, hlow, hhigh]
    · intro v hv
      obtain ⟨hvL, hvnot⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hv
      constructor
      · by_contra! hsmall
        exact hvnot (Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hvL, hsmall⟩))
      · by_contra! hlarge
        exact hvnot (Finset.mem_union_right _ (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hvL, hlarge⟩))
  obtain ⟨U₀, hU₀, hbadU, hfullU⟩ := typical U W hU hW
    (fun A hA hsize => hrect A hA W (by rfl) hsize (by simpa only [hW] using hhn))
  obtain ⟨W₀, hW₀, hbadW, hfullW⟩ := typical W U hW hU (by
    intro B hB hsize
    have ht := hrect U (by rfl) B hB (by simpa only [hU] using hhn) hsize
    simpa only [SimpleGraph.edgeDensity_comm] using ht)
  have deletion : ∀ R R₀ : Finset V, ∀ v : V,
      ((R.filter fun w => H.Adj v w).card : ℝ) ≤
        ((R₀.filter fun w => H.Adj v w).card : ℝ) + (R \ R₀).card := by
    intro R R₀ v
    have hsub : R.filter (fun w => H.Adj v w) ⊆
        (R₀.filter fun w => H.Adj v w) ∪ (R \ R₀) := by
      intro w hw
      obtain ⟨hwR, hvw⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hw
      by_cases hw₀ : w ∈ R₀
      · exact Finset.mem_union_left _ (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hw₀, hvw⟩)
      · exact Finset.mem_union_right _ (Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hwR, hw₀⟩)
    exact_mod_cast (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans (Finset.card_union_le _ _)
  refine ⟨U₀, W₀, hU₀, hW₀, hbadU, hbadW, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u hu
    have hfull := hfullU u hu
    have hloss := deletion W W₀ u
    have hmono : ((W₀.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ≤
        ((W.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ) := by
      exact_mod_cast Finset.card_le_card (Finset.filter_subset_filter _ hW₀)
    constructor
    · nlinarith only [hfull.1, hloss, hbadW]

theorem SuperRegularTypicalCore
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
    (n : ℕ) (d h : ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) (hh : 0 < h) (hh1 : h < 1)
    (hU : U.card = n) (hW : W.card = n)
    (hrect : ∀ A ⊆ U, ∀ B ⊆ W, h * n < (A.card : ℝ) →
      h * n < (B.card : ℝ) → |(H.edgeDensity A B : ℝ) - d| < h / 2) :
    ∃ U₀ W₀ : Finset V, U₀ ⊆ U ∧ W₀ ⊆ W ∧
      ((U \ U₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n ∧
      ((W \ W₀).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * h * n ∧
      (∀ u ∈ U₀, (d - 3 * h) * n ≤
        ((W₀.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ∧
        ((W₀.filter fun w => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ≤ (d + h) * n) ∧
      (∀ w ∈ W₀, (d - 3 * h) * n ≤
        ((U₀.filter fun u => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ∧
        ((U₀.filter fun u => H.Adj u w).card : ℝ) ≤ (d + h) * n) := by

SuperRegularTypicalCore.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $L_U$ consist of vertices of $U$ of degree into $W$ strictly
less than $(d-h)n$, and $T_U$ those of degree strictly greater
than $(d+h)n$. If $|L_U|>hn$, then $L_U$ is nonempty and
$|W|=n>hn$ since $h<1$ and $n>0$. Summing its strict degree
bounds gives
$e_H(L_U,W)<(d-h)n|L_U|$. Dividing by $n|L_U|>0$ yields
$d_H(L_U,W)<d-h$, contradicting the assumed density error
$<h/2$, which implies density $>d-h/2>d-h$.
Thus $|L_U|\leq hn$. If $|T_U|>hn$, summing its strict
upper-exceptional degree inequalities yields
$d_H(T_U,W)>d+h$, contradicting density $<d+h/2<d+h$.
Thus $|T_U|\leq hn$ as well.

Define $L_W,T_W$ using degrees from $W$ into $U$.
The same argument applies to the tests $(U,L_W)$ and $(U,T_W)$:
symmetry of adjacency gives
$e_H(U,L_W)=\sum_{w\in L_W}\deg_H(w;U)$, and likewise for
$T_W$. The test with $U$ is legitimate since $|U|=n>hn$.
It follows separately that $|L_W|,|T_W|\leq hn$.

Take $U_0=U\setminus(L_U\cup T_U)$ and
$W_0=W\setminus(L_W\cup T_W)$. Their complements have size
at most the sum of the two corresponding exceptional sizes,
hence at most $2hn$ on each side. A vertex in $U_0$ has full
degree into $W$ in $[(d-h)n,(d+h)n]$. Passing to $W_0$ deletes
at most $|W\setminus W_0|\leq2hn$ neighbors. Thus its core
degree is at least $(d-h)n-2hn=(d-3h)n$ and at most $(d+h)n$.
For vertices of $W_0$, delete at most $|U\setminus U_0|\leq2hn$
neighbors instead. This proves both stated core degree intervals.
No degree conclusion was inferred solely from one exceptional
set: the lower and upper exceptional sets were each bounded on
both sides, and the opposite-side deletion was paid explicitly.
\end{proof}
SuperRegularTypicalCore.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Typical-row core estimates]
Let $H$ be a finite simple graph, let $|U|=|W|=n>0$, and let
$d\in\mathbb R$, $0<h<1$. Assume
\[
|d_H(A,B)-d|<h/2\quad
(A\subseteq U,\ B\subseteq W,\ |A|,|B|>hn).
\]
There are $U_0\subseteq U,W_0\subseteq W$ with
$|U\setminus U_0|,|W\setminus W_0|\leq2hn$ such that each
vertex of either core part has between $(d-3h)n$ and $(d+h)n$
neighbors in the opposite core part in $H$.
\end{lemma}
SuperRegularTypicalCore.title: SuperRegularTypicalCore

      (μ.map fun f => fun x : {x : VH // x ∈ X} => f.toFun x.1) q Set.univ)
    (hres : ∀ f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X, μ f ≠ 0 →
      let Y := {x : VH // x ∉ X}
      let W := {v : VG // v ∉ X.image f.toFun}
      ∃ Br : BlowUpInstance r Y W
          (H.induce {x : VH | x ∉ X})
          (G.induce {v : VG | v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) R,
      ∃ Ar : CandidacySystem Br,
        (∀ x : Y, Br.sourceCluster x = B.sourceCluster x.1) ∧
        (∀ v : W, Br.hostCluster v = B.hostCluster v.1) ∧
        (∀ (x : Y) (v : W), Ar.allowed x v ↔
          (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x.1 v.1) ∧
        ∃ ν : PMF {φ : SimpleGraph.Copy
            (H.induce {x : VH | x ∉ X})
            (G.induce {v : VG | v ∉ X.image f.toFun}) // CompatibleEmbedding Br Ar φ},
          VertexSpreadOn (ν.map fun φ => fun x => φ.1 x) q Set.univ) :

SupportedResidualComposition.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Use the meanings of partial compatibility, updated candidacy and full
compatibility in \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding},
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacy} and \noderef{CompatibleEmbedding} throughout.
Restrict $\mu$ to its positive-mass support; this changes neither total mass
nor any event probability. For each supported $f$, choose one of the residual
instances and one residual law $\nu_f$ from the hypothesis. The choices are
made separately; no uniqueness of residual instances or total partial maps
is asserted. Given a sample $g$ from $\nu_f$, define
\[
 F_{f,g}(x)=\begin{cases}f(x)&x\in X,\\g(x)&x\notin X,\end{cases}
\]
where the latter value is included from the literal complement $W_f$ into
$V(G)$. The first block is injective by partial compatibility and the second
by the definition of a graph Copy. Their images are disjoint, since the
second lies outside $f(X)$. Thus $F_{f,g}$ is injective.
Edges with both endpoints in $X$ are preserved by $f$, and edges with both
endpoints in $Y$ by $g$ and the definition of induced graph. For a crossing
edge $xy$ with $x\in X,y\in Y$, compatibility of $g$ and the stipulated
updated-candidacy equivalence imply $G(F_{f,g}(y),f(x))$. Symmetry supplies
the other orientation. Hence all edges are preserved. Original candidacy
holds on $X$ by partial compatibility. On $Y$ it follows from the original
candidacy conjunct of updated candidacy. Consequently $F_{f,g}$ is a
compatible full Copy for every sample in these laws, not only almost surely.

Mix these laws with weights $\mu(f)$ on supported $f$, obtaining a law on
compatible full Copies. This is a probability law because each conditional
law has mass one and $\sum_{f:\mu(f)\ne0}\mu(f)=1$. This support-indexed
mixture avoids assigning residual laws to impossible states. Equivalently,
one can extend the resulting full-Copy kernel arbitrarily to zero-mass
states using any supported state's law; their contributions are zero.
There is a supported state because a probability law has total mass one.

Here is the joint-cylinder calculation, including the dependence on $f$.
Use \noderef{CylinderEvent} and \noderef{VertexSpreadOn}. Fix distinct
sources $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ and targets $v_1,\ldots,v_s\in V(G)$, and split
their index set into $I=\{i:x_i\in X\}$ and its complement $J$.
Write $a=|I|$, $b=|J|$, so $a+b=s$. Let $E_X$ be the event that
$f(x_i)=v_i$ for every $i\in I$. Its probability is at most $q^a$ by the
given spread law on restrictions to $X$; reindexing $I$ by $[a]$ preserves
distinctness. For a fixed supported $f$, if any target $v_j$, $j\in J$,
does not belong to $W_f$, the conditional joint-cylinder probability is
zero. Otherwise regard all these targets as elements of $W_f$. Distinctness
of the corresponding sources in $Y$ allows the residual spread bound,
so their conditional cylinder probability is at most $q^b$.
If $f\notin E_X$ the joint cylinder is impossible. Therefore its probability
under the mixture is at most
\[
 \sum_{f:\mu(f)\ne0}\mu(f)\mathbf1_{E_X}(f)q^b
 =\Pr_\mu(E_X)q^b\leq q^a q^b=q^s.
\]
All sums are of nonnegative terms, so grouping and multiplying them is valid;
the function space is finite as well. Zero-mass states contribute zero even
when distinct total partial maps have the same restriction to $X$. No
identification of those maps or unjustified conditioning is used. This is
the support-indexed bind version of the cylinder argument in
\noderef{VertexSpreadSequential}. The hypothesis on the first-stage law
also supplies $q\leq1$, including for empty source types. Packaging the
glued maps as Copies and compatible subtypes does not change their values
or cylinder probabilities. The required spread assertion follows.
\end{proof}
SupportedResidualComposition.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}
Let $B$ be a finite blow-up instance with source $H$, host $G$, reduced graph
$R$ on $[r]$, and candidacy system $A$. Fix $X\subseteq V(H)$ and a law
$\mu$ on partial compatible embeddings with domain $X$. Suppose the law of
their restrictions to $X$ is $q$-vertex-spread on all of $V(G)$.
For every $f$ with $\mu(f)\ne0$, put
$Y=V(H)\setminus X$ and $W_f=V(G)\setminus f(X)$. Suppose there are a
blow-up instance $B_f$ on the induced graphs $H[Y],G[W_f]$ with reduced
graph $R$, and a candidacy system $A_f$, whose cluster maps are exactly the
restrictions of the original maps, and such that
\[
 A_f(y,v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (\mathrm{UpdatedCandidacy}(B,A,X,f))(y,v).
\]
Suppose moreover that each such residual instance has a law on compatible
full embeddings $H[Y]\hookrightarrow G[W_f]$ that is $q$-vertex-spread
on all of $W_f$. Then there is a $q$-vertex-spread law on compatible full
embeddings $H\hookrightarrow G$.
\end{lemma}

theorem TaggedCandidacyAssembly {r s : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}
    [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H H' : SimpleGraph VH} {G G' : SimpleGraph VG}
    {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)} {R' : SimpleGraph (Fin s)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (B' : BlowUpInstance s VH VG H' G' R') (η c : ENNReal)
    (hpair : ∀ j : Fin s,
      let L : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
        ∃ x, z = Sum.inl x ∧ B'.sourceCluster x = j
      let Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
        ∃ v, z = Sum.inr v ∧ B'.hostCluster v = j
      let C : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b =>
        ∃ x v, a = Sum.inl x ∧ b = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed x v
      ∃ F : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG), ∃ _ : DecidableRel F.Adj,
        F ≤ C ∧ SuperRegularPair F L Q η c) :
    ∃ A' : CandidacySystem B',
      (∀ ⦃x v⦄, A'.allowed x v → A.allowed x v) ∧
      CandidacySuperRegular B' A' η c := by
TaggedCandidacyAssembly.name: TaggedCandidacyAssembly
TaggedCandidacyAssembly.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Choose one supplied graph $F_j$ for each refined index $j$.
Declare $(x,v)$ allowed in $A'$ exactly when the two refined
cluster indices agree and $F_j$ joins $\mathrm{inl}(x)$ to
$\mathrm{inr}(v)$, where $j$ is the source index. The first
condition proves cluster-respecting, so this is a system as defined
by \noderef{CandidacySystem}. Containment of $F_j$ in the original
tagged graph proves the pair was originally allowed: on endpoints
with these tags, the forward branch of the symmetric relation graph
is precisely $A(x,v)$ and the backward branch is impossible.

For a fixed refined index $j$ and endpoints in its source and host
fibers, the two refined indices already agree and the source index
equals $j$. Therefore the new tagged relation graph agrees exactly
with $F_j$ on the relevant crossing edges. By
\noderef{SuperRegularPairEmbedding}, specialized to the injective
identity map on the tagged vertex type, with source graph $F_j$ and
target the tagged graph of $A'$, this transfers its super-regularity.
The crossing-edge equivalence above is the required adjacency hypothesis;
the identity images of both finite fibers are the original fibers.
The parameters $\eta,c$ are unchanged, including infinite values, and
the argument also applies to empty fibers. Applying this for
every index gives \noderef{CandidacySuperRegular}. No off-pair
edges of any selected graph enter this comparison, and no union of
independently chosen graphs is taken on one candidacy pair.
All maps and graphs retain the original vertex types; classical
decidability of the finite relations supplies the required instances.
\end{proof}
TaggedCandidacyAssembly.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Assembly of tagged candidacy extractions]
Let $B,A$ be a blow-up instance with candidacy system and let $B'$
be another blow-up instance on the same source and host vertex types,
with possibly different graphs and cluster index set. Suppose for
each cluster of $B'$ there is a graph on the disjoint tagged union
of the source and host types, contained in the symmetric tagged
graph of the original allowed relation, and
$(\eta,c)$-super-regular on that cluster's tagged source and host
fibers. There is a candidacy system $A'$ for $B'$ contained in $A$
whose every cluster pair is $(\eta,c)$-super-regular.
\end{lemma}
TaggedCandidacyAssembly.title: TaggedCandidacyAssembly

ThinningCountInterval.lean_statement:
theorem ThinningCountInterval (d ε ρ η : ENNReal)
    (hd : d ≠ ⊤) (hε : ε ≠ ⊤) (hρ : ρ ≠ ⊤) (hη : η ≠ ⊤)
    (hεd : ε ≤ d) (hηρ : η ≤ ρ) (q ξ : ℝ) (hq : 0 ≤ q)
    (hqd : q * d.toReal = ρ.toReal) (herr : q * ε.toReal + ξ ≤ η.toReal)
    (m a b : ℕ)
    (hold : (d - ε) * m ≤ (a : ENNReal) ∧ (a : ENNReal) ≤ (d + ε) * m)
    (hdev : |(b : ℝ) - q * a| ≤ ξ * m) :
    (ρ - η) * m ≤ (b : ENNReal) ∧ (b : ENNReal) ≤ (ρ + η) * m := by
ThinningCountInterval.name: ThinningCountInterval
ThinningCountInterval.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
All scalar parameters and natural counts are finite. Since
$\epsilon\leq d$, the real conversion of $d-\epsilon$ is the ordinary
difference; similarly for $\rho-\eta$. Thus convert the given interval
to real inequalities and multiply both sides by the nonnegative $q$.
The absolute-value inequality says $qa-\xi m\leq b\leq qa+\xi m$.
Combining gives
\[
(\rho-(q\epsilon+\xi))m\leq b
\leq(\rho+(q\epsilon+\xi))m.
\]
Since $m\geq0$ and $q\epsilon+\xi\leq\eta$, enlarge this interval
to the stated one. Finite real conversion preserves and reflects order,
so converting back proves the assertion, without dividing by $m$.
\end{proof}
ThinningCountInterval.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Deterministic count error transfer]
Let $d,\epsilon,\rho,\eta$ be finite extended nonnegative reals with
$\epsilon\leq d$, $\eta\leq\rho$. Let $q\geq0,\xi$ be real numbers
such that $qd=\rho$ and $q\epsilon+\xi\leq\eta$, where these scalar
identities use real conversions. For natural numbers $m,a,b$, if
\[
(d-\epsilon)m\leq a\leq(d+\epsilon)m,
\qquad |b-qa|\leq\xi m,
\]
then $(\rho-\eta)m\leq b\leq(\rho+\eta)m$ in the extended
nonnegative reals. This includes $m=0$.
\end{lemma}
ThinningCountInterval.title: ThinningCountInterval

have hηρ : η < ρ := by
    calc
      η = 1 * η := by simp
      _ ≤ 10 * η := mul_le_mul_left (by norm_num) _
      _ < ρ := hsmall
  have hDtop : D ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top (by simp) hD
  have hρtop : ρ ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hρD
  have hηtop : η ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hηρ
  have hβtop : β ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_lt hβη
  have hξle : ξ ≤ η := by
    calc
      ξ ≤ (ρ / D) * β + ξ := le_add_left le_rfl
      _ = 1 * ((ρ / D) * β + ξ) := by simp
      _ ≤ 4 * ((ρ / D) * β + ξ) := mul_le_mul_left (by norm_num) _
      _ ≤ η := hbudget
  have hξtop : ξ ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top hηtop hξle
  have hDpos : 0 < D.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos (hρ.trans hρD).ne' hDtop
  have hηpos : 0 < η.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos (hβ.trans hβη).ne' hηtop
  have hξpos : 0 < ξ.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hξ.ne' hξtop
