ThinningRealParameters.lean_statement:
open scoped NNReal

theorem ThinningRealParameters (β D ρ η ξ : ENNReal)
    (hβ : 0 < β) (hβη : β < η) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hρD : ρ < D) (hD : D ≤ 1)
    (hξ : 0 < ξ) (hbudget : 4 * ((ρ / D) * β + ξ) ≤ η) (hsmall : 10 * η < ρ) :
    D ≠ ⊤ ∧ β ≠ ⊤ ∧ ρ ≠ ⊤ ∧ η ≠ ⊤ ∧ ξ ≠ ⊤ ∧ η < ρ ∧ β ≤ D ∧
    0 < η.toReal ∧ 0 < ξ.toReal ∧ ∃ q : ℝ≥0, q ≤ 1 ∧
      (q : ℝ) * D.toReal = ρ.toReal ∧ (q : ℝ) * β.toReal + ξ.toReal ≤ η.toReal := by
ThinningRealParameters.name: ThinningRealParameters
ThinningRealParameters.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since $\eta\leq10\eta<\rho<D\leq1$, these three scalars and $D$ are
finite, and $\eta<\rho$. The inequality $\beta<\eta$ gives finiteness
of $\beta$ and $\beta<D$. Nonnegativity gives
$\xi\leq(\rho/D)\beta+\xi\leq4((\rho/D)\beta+\xi)\leq\eta$, so $\xi$
is also finite. Positive finite extended nonnegative reals have positive
real conversions, establishing the asserted positivity and also
$D.\operatorname{toReal}>0$.
Set $q=\rho.\operatorname{toReal}/D.\operatorname{toReal}$. Finite real
conversion preserves $\rho<D$, hence $0\leq q\leq1$, and multiplication
by the positive denominator proves $qD.\operatorname{toReal}
=\rho.\operatorname{toReal}$. The quotient $\rho/D$ is finite because
its numerator is finite and its denominator is positive. Thus every
sum and product in the budget is finite, and converting that budget
to real numbers gives $4(q\beta.\operatorname{toReal}
+\xi.\operatorname{toReal})\leq\eta.\operatorname{toReal}$.
The parenthesized quantity is nonnegative; removing the factor four
proves the required error inequality.
\end{proof}
ThinningRealParameters.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Finite scalar normalization for thinning]
Suppose the extended nonnegative scalars satisfy
$0<\beta<\eta$, $0<\rho<D\leq1$, $\xi>0$,
$4((\rho/D)\beta+\xi)\leq\eta$, and $10\eta<\rho$.
Then $D,\beta,\rho,\eta,\xi$ are all finite, $\eta<\rho$, $\beta\leq D$,
and the real conversions of $\eta,\xi$ are positive. There is a
nonnegative real $q\leq1$ such that
$qD.\operatorname{toReal}=\rho.\operatorname{toReal}$ and
$q\beta.\operatorname{toReal}+\xi.\operatorname{toReal}
\leq\eta.\operatorname{toReal}$.
\end{lemma}
ThinningRealParameters.title: ThinningRealParameters

UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison.lean_proof:
classical
  let κ := Real.sqrt ε
  let D := d + ε + 3 * κ
  let b := d - 2 * ε
  have hκ : 0 < κ := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hε
  have hκsq : κ * κ = ε := by
    simpa only [pow_two] using Real.sq_sqrt hε.le
  have hκsmall : κ < 1 / 4 := by nlinarith
  have hD : 0 < D := by dsimp [D]; positivity
  have hb : 0 < b := sub_pos.mpr hεd
  have htwo : (2 : ENNReal) * ENNReal.ofReal ε = ENNReal.ofReal (2 * ε) := by
    rw [ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by norm_num)]
    norm_num
  have he : 0 < ENNReal.ofReal ε := ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hε
  have hdE : 0 < ENNReal.ofReal d := ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hd
  have hd1E : ENNReal.ofReal d ≤ 1 := by
    simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_one] using ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal hd1
  have hεdE : 2 * ENNReal.ofReal ε < ENNReal.ofReal d := by
    rw [htwo]
    exact (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff hd).mpr hεd
  have hκsqE : ENNReal.ofReal κ * ENNReal.ofReal κ = ENNReal.ofReal ε := by
    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul hκ.le, hκsq]
  have hbE : ENNReal.ofReal d - 2 * ENNReal.ofReal ε = ENNReal.ofReal b := by
    rw [htwo, ← ENNReal.ofReal_sub d (by positivity)]
  have hDE : ENNReal.ofReal d + ENNReal.ofReal ε + 3 * ENNReal.ofReal κ =
      ENNReal.ofReal D := by
    dsimp [D]
    rw [ENNReal.ofReal_add (by positivity) (by positivity),
      ENNReal.ofReal_add hd.le hε.le, ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by norm_num)]
    norm_num
  obtain ⟨n₁, hn₁⟩ := MatchingEnumeration (ENNReal.ofReal ε) (ENNReal.ofReal d)
    he hεdE hd1E
  obtain ⟨n₂, hn₂⟩ := RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound (ENNReal.ofReal ε)
    (ENNReal.ofReal d) (ENNReal.ofReal κ) he hdE hd1E hκsqE
  refine ⟨max 1 (max n₁ n₂), by omega, ?_⟩
  intro V _ _ G _ U W hUW n hn hU hW hreg S T hS hT hM A
  letI := hM
  have hnpos : 0 < n := by omega
  have hs : S.card ≤ n := (Finset.card_le_card hS).trans_eq hU
  have ht : T.card ≤ n := (Finset.card_le_card hT).trans_eq hW
  let M := {f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}
  let X : (U → W) → ℕ := fun f =>
    (Finset.univ.filter fun u : U => u.1 ∈ S ∧ (f u).1 ∈ T).card
  let K : ℕ → ℝ := fun y => if κ * (n : ℝ) ≤ (y : ℝ) then
    D ^ y * (y.factorial : ℝ) else (y.factorial : ℝ)
  have hK (y : ℕ) : 0 ≤ K y := by
    dsimp [K]
    split_ifs <;> positivity
  have htotal : b ^ n * (n.factorial : ℝ) ≤ (M.ncard : ℝ) := by
    have hh := hn₁ G U W hUW n (by omega) hU hW hreg
    rw [hbE, ← ENNReal.ofReal_pow hb.le,
      ← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (pow_nonneg hb.le n),
      ← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast] at hh
    exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (Nat.cast_nonneg _)).mp hh
  have htotalpos : 0 < (M.ncard : ℝ) :=
    lt_of_lt_of_le (mul_pos (pow_pos hb n) (by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos n)) htotal
  have hrect (L R : Finset V) (hLR : Disjoint L R) (y : ℕ)
      (hL : L ⊆ U) (hR : R ⊆ W) (hLc : L.card = y) (hRc : R.card = y) :
      ({f : L → R | PerfectMatching G L R hLR f}.ncard : ℝ) ≤ K y := by
    dsimp [K]
    split_ifs with hlarge
    · have hlargeE : ENNReal.ofReal κ * n ≤ y := by
        rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul hκ.le]
        exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_natCast.mpr hlarge
      have hh := hn₂ G U W L R hLR n y (by omega) hU hW hreg.1
        hL hR hLc hRc hlargeE
      rw [hDE, ← ENNReal.ofReal_pow hD.le,
        ← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast y.factorial,
        ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (pow_nonneg hD.le y), ← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast] at hh
      exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (by positivity)).mp hh
    · exact_mod_cast PerfectMatchingBijectionBound G L R hLR y hLc hRc
  -- A bijection forces the three feasibility inequalities for its intersection size.
  have hfeasible (f : U → W) (hf : PerfectMatching G U W hUW f) :
      X f ≤ S.card ∧ X f ≤ T.card ∧ T.card - X f ≤ n - S.card := by
    let F : V → V := fun u => if hu : u ∈ U then (f ⟨u, hu⟩).1 else u
    have hFu (u : U) : F u.1 = (f u).1 := by simp [F, u.2]
    have hF : Set.BijOn F (U : Set V) (W : Set V) := by
      refine Set.BijOn.mk ?_ ?_ ?_
      · intro u hu
        rw [hFu ⟨u, hu⟩]
        exact (f ⟨u, hu⟩).2
      · intro u hu v hv huv
        have heq : f ⟨u, hu⟩ = f ⟨v, hv⟩ :=
          Subtype.ext ((hFu ⟨u, hu⟩).symm.trans (huv.trans (hFu ⟨v, hv⟩)))
        exact congrArg (fun a : U => a.1) (hf.1.1 heq)
      · intro v hv
        obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hf.1.2 ⟨v, hv⟩
        exact ⟨u.1, u.2, (hFu u).trans (congrArg (fun b : W => b.1) hu)⟩
    have hx : (S.filter fun u => F u ∈ T).card = X f := by
      symm
      apply Finset.card_bij (fun u _ => u.1)
      · intro u hu
        obtain ⟨_, huS, huT⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hu
        exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨huS, (hFu u).symm ▸ huT⟩
      · intro u hu v hv huv
        exact Subtype.ext huv
      · intro v hv
        obtain ⟨hvS, hvT⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hv
        refine ⟨⟨v, hS hvS⟩, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hvS, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
        simpa only [F, dif_pos (hS hvS)] using hvT
    have hp := FourRectangleMatchingPartition U W S T F hF hS hT n (X f) hU hW hx
    have ha := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hp.1
    have hb' := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hp.2.1
    have he' := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hp.2.2.2.1
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [← ha.2]
      exact Finset.card_le_card ha.1
    · rw [← hb'.2]
      exact Finset.card_le_card hb'.1
    · rw [← he'.2, ← hU, ← Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hS]
      exact Finset.card_le_card he'.1
  have hmass (x : ℕ) : 0 ≤ HypergeometricMass n S.card T.card x := by
    unfold HypergeometricMass
    split_ifs <;> positivity
  have hpoint (x : ℕ) :
      ({f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f ∧ X f = x}.ncard : ℝ) /
        (M.ncard : ℝ) ≤
      Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * MatchingConcentrationCorrection d ε) *
        HypergeometricMass n S.card T.card x := by
    by_cases hx : x ≤ S.card ∧ x ≤ T.card ∧ T.card - x ≤ n - S.card
    · let y : Fin 4 → ℕ := ![x, S.card - x, T.card - x, n - S.card - (T.card - x)]
      have hy : ∑ i, y i = n := by
        rw [Fin.sum_univ_four]
        dsimp [y]
        omega
      have hp := FourRectangleSmallOrderProduct κ D n y hκ hκsmall hD hnpos hy
      rw [Fin.prod_univ_four, Fin.prod_univ_four] at hp
      change K x * K (S.card - x) * K (T.card - x) *
        K (n - S.card - (T.card - x)) ≤
        D ^ n * Real.exp (-3 * κ * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (min D 1)) *
          ((x.factorial : ℝ) * ((S.card - x).factorial : ℝ) *
            ((T.card - x).factorial : ℝ) * ((n - S.card - (T.card - x)).factorial : ℝ)) at hp
      let C : ℝ := (S.card.choose x : ℝ) * (T.card.choose x : ℝ) *
        ((n - T.card).choose (S.card - x) : ℝ) *
        ((n - S.card).choose (T.card - x) : ℝ)
      let F : ℝ := (x.factorial : ℝ) * ((S.card - x).factorial : ℝ) *
        ((T.card - x).factorial : ℝ) * ((n - S.card - (T.card - x)).factorial : ℝ)
      let E := Real.exp (-3 * κ * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (min D 1))
      have hC : 0 ≤ C := by dsimp [C]; positivity
      have hF : 0 < F := by dsimp [F]; positivity
      have hfiber := FourRectangleMatchingFiberBound G U W S T hUW n x hU hW
        hS hT hx.1 hx.2.1 hx.2.2 K (fun z _ => hK z) hrect
      have hnum :
          ({f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f ∧ X f = x}.ncard : ℝ) ≤
          C * (D ^ n * E * F) :=
        hfiber.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hp hC)
      have hcoef : D ^ n * E / b ^ n =
          Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * MatchingConcentrationCorrection d ε) := by
        have hpw : (D / b) ^ n = Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (D / b)) := by
          rw [Real.exp_nat_mul, Real.exp_log (div_pos hD hb)]
        calc
          D ^ n * E / b ^ n = (D / b) ^ n * E := by rw [div_pow]; ring
          _ = Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (D / b) +
              (-3 * κ * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (min D 1))) := by
            rw [hpw, ← Real.exp_add]
          _ = _ := by
            congr 1
            dsimp [MatchingConcentrationCorrection, D, b, κ]
            ring
      have hcancel : C * F / (n.factorial : ℝ) =
          HypergeometricMass n S.card T.card x := by
        rw [HypergeometricMass, if_pos hx.1]
        exact FourRectangleFactorialCancellation n S.card T.card x hs ht
          hx.1 hx.2.1 hx.2.2
      calc
        _ ≤ C * (D ^ n * E * F) / (b ^ n * (n.factorial : ℝ)) :=
          div_le_div₀ (by positivity) hnum (by positivity) htotal
        _ = (D ^ n * E / b ^ n) * (C * F / (n.factorial : ℝ)) := by ring
        _ = _ := by rw [hcoef, hcancel]
    · have hempty : {f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f ∧ X f = x} = ∅ := by
        apply Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr
        rintro f ⟨hf, hfx⟩
        exact hx (hfx ▸ hfeasible f hf)
      have hzero : HypergeometricMass n S.card T.card x = 0 := by
        unfold HypergeometricMass
        by_cases hxs : x ≤ S.card
        · rw [if_pos hxs]
          by_cases hxt : x ≤ T.card
          · have hbad : n - T.card < S.card - x := by omega
            rw [Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt hbad, Nat.cast_zero, mul_zero, zero_div]
          · rw [Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt (not_le.mp hxt), Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul, zero_div]
        · rw [if_neg hxs]
      rw [hempty, Set.ncard_empty, Nat.cast_zero, zero_div, hzero, mul_zero]
  change (PMF.uniformOfFintype {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}).toOuterMeasure
    {f | X f.1 ∈ A} ≤ _
  have hevent :
      (PMF.uniformOfFintype {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}).toOuterMeasure
        {f | X f.1 ∈ A} =
      ENNReal.ofReal (∑ x ∈ A,
        ({f : {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f} | X f.1 = x}.ncard : ℝ) /
          (Fintype.card {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f} : ℝ)) := by
    have hc : Fintype.card
        ({f : {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f} | X f.1 ∈ A} : Set _) =
        ∑ x ∈ A,
          {f : {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f} | X f.1 = x}.ncard := by
      simp only [Fintype.card_subtype, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card']
      simpa using (Finset.sum_card_fiberwise_eq_card_filter
        (Finset.univ : Finset {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f})
        A (fun f => X f.1)).symm
    rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFintype_apply, hc]
    rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, ← ENNReal.ofReal_natCast,
      ← ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos (by
        exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos
          (α := {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}))]
    congr 1
    rw [Nat.cast_sum, Finset.sum_div]
  rw [hevent]
  apply (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (mul_nonneg (Real.exp_nonneg _)
    (Finset.sum_nonneg fun x _ => hmass x))).mpr
  have hc : Fintype.card {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f} = M.ncard := by
    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
    exact Nat.card_coe_set_eq M
  have hfib (x : ℕ) :
      {f : {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f} | X f.1 = x}.ncard =
        {f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f ∧ X f = x}.ncard := by
    calc
      _ = ({f : U → W | X f = x} ∩
          {f : U → W | PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}).ncard :=
        Set.ncard_subtype (fun f : U → W => PerfectMatching G U W hUW f)
          {f : U → W | X f = x}
      _ = _ := by
        congr 1
        ext f
        exact and_comm
  simp only [hc, hfib]
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => hpoint x
UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison.lean_statement:
theorem UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison (d ε : ℝ)
    (hd : 0 < d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 16) (hεd : 2 * ε < d) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 0 < n₀ ∧
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
      (hUW : Disjoint U W) (n : ℕ),
      n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n →
      SuperRegularPair G U W (ENNReal.ofReal ε) (ENNReal.ofReal d) →
      ∀ (S T : Finset V), S ⊆ U → T ⊆ W →
      ∀ (hM : Nonempty {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f})
        (A : Finset ℕ),
        (UniformPerfectMatching G U W hUW hM).toOuterMeasure
          {f | (Finset.univ.filter fun u : U =>
            u.1 ∈ S ∧ (f.1 u).1 ∈ T).card ∈ A} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * MatchingConcentrationCorrection d ε) *
          ∑ x ∈ A, HypergeometricMass n S.card T.card x) := by
UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison.name: UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison
UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Put $\kappa=\sqrt\varepsilon>0$ and $D=d+\varepsilon+3\kappa>0$.
Embed these finite nonnegative parameters in extended nonnegative reals.
Then $\kappa^2=\varepsilon$, $0<\varepsilon$, $0<d\le1$, and
$2\varepsilon<d$ still hold in that arithmetic.
Take $n_0$ to be at least one and at least both thresholds supplied by
\noderef{MatchingEnumeration} and
\noderef{RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound}, the latter with parameter
$\kappa$. These thresholds depend only on $d,\varepsilon$, not on any
subsets or orders. The super-regular hypothesis supplies regularity by
the definition \noderef{SuperRegularPair}.

Let $M$ be the total matching count. The first cited enumeration statement
gives $M\ge(d-2\varepsilon)^n n!>0$. All these real quantities are finite,
so this is also precisely the real inequality obtained from its
extended-nonnegative-real statement. For any balanced induced rectangle
of order $y$ with left set in $U$ and right set in $W$, the second cited
statement gives at most $D^y y!$ matchings when $y\ge\kappa n$.
For $y<\kappa n$ use the bound $y!$: by
\noderef{PerfectMatching}, every matching is a bijection between its
parts, and there are exactly $y!$ bijections. This elementary count
follows by assigning the first image in $y$ ways and inducting on the
remaining $y-1$ elements; at $y=0$ the unique empty map gives $0!=1$.
Thus the function $K(y)=D^y y!$ for $y\ge\kappa n$, and $K(y)=y!$
otherwise, is nonnegative and bounds all the rectangles required by
\noderef{FourRectangleMatchingFiberBound}.

Consider a feasible $x$, meaning $x\le s,t$ and $t-x\le n-s$.
The four orders in that fiber lemma are
$y_1=x,y_2=s-x,y_3=t-x,y_4=n-s-(t-x)$; they sum to $n$.
Since $\varepsilon<1/16$, $\kappa<1/4$.
Not all four orders can be smaller than $\kappa n$, since their sum
would then be less than $4\kappa n<n$. Let $I$ be the small orders and
$q=\sum_{i\in I}y_i$. Then $|I|\le3$ and $0\le q\le3\kappa n$.
The four rectangle bounds multiply to
\[
 D^{n-q}\prod_i y_i!
 \le D^n\exp(-3\kappa n\log\min(D,1))\prod_i y_i!.
\]
For $D\ge1$, $D^{n-q}\le D^n$ and $\log\min(D,1)=0$.
For $0<D<1$, write $D^{n-q}=D^n\exp(-q\log D)$ and use
$q\le3\kappa n$ and $-\log D>0$. This proves the estimate in both
cases; zero orders contribute $0!=1$ and no density power, as required.

Divide the fiber count from \noderef{FourRectangleMatchingFiberBound}
by $M\ge(d-2\varepsilon)^n n!>0$ and use
\noderef{FourRectangleFactorialCancellation}. This gives
\[
 {M_x\over M}\le
 \left({D\over d-2\varepsilon}\right)^n
 \exp(-3\kappa n\log\min(D,1))
 {\binom t x\binom{n-t}{s-x}\over\binom n s}
 =e^{nL(d,\varepsilon)}H(n,s,t,x).
\]
The equality uses the definitions
\noderef{MatchingConcentrationCorrection} and
\noderef{HypergeometricMass}, and the identity $a^n=e^{n\log a}$
for positive real $a$. Every denominator here is positive.

For an infeasible $x$ no such matching exists: a bijection has at most
$s$ and at most $t$ images in the intersection, while its $t-x$ remaining
preimages of $T$ must fit in $U\setminus S$, of size $n-s$.
The hypergeometric mass is also zero. If $x>s$ this is the explicit
zero clause of its definition; if $x\le s$ but $x>t$, $\binom t x=0$;
otherwise $t-x>n-s$ is equivalent to $s-x>n-t$, and the other binomial
coefficient vanishes. In particular $x>n$ has zero fiber and zero mass.
This proves the pointwise comparison for every natural $x$.

By \noderef{UniformPerfectMatching}, every member of the finite matching
set has mass $1/M$, so the event $X=x$ has probability $M_x/M$.
The events $X=x$ for distinct $x\in A$ are disjoint. Finite additivity
therefore makes $\Pr(X\in A)$ their sum. Sum the pointwise inequality
over $A$ and factor out $e^{nL(d,\varepsilon)}$, obtaining the assertion.
All masses and both finite sums are nonnegative and finite, so embedding
this real calculation into extended nonnegative reals preserves it.
\end{proof}
UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform matching fibers versus hypergeometric masses]
Fix real $0<d\le1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/16$ with $2\varepsilon<d$.
There is a positive integer $n_0$ such that the following holds uniformly
for all finite graphs $G$, disjoint $U,W$ of size $n\ge n_0$, and
$S\subseteq U$, $T\subseteq W$. Suppose $G[U,W]$ is
$(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular (parameters embedded into extended
nonnegative reals) and its perfect-matching set is nonempty.
Under \noderef{UniformPerfectMatching}, write $X=|f(S)\cap T|$,
$s=|S|$, $t=|T|$. For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers,
\[
 \Pr(X\in A)\le e^{nL(d,\varepsilon)}\sum_{x\in A}H(n,s,t,x),
\]
with $L$ and $H$ defined by \noderef{MatchingConcentrationCorrection}
and \noderef{HypergeometricMass}. The real nonnegative upper bound is
embedded into extended nonnegative reals in the measure inequality.
\end{lemma}
UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison.title: UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison

intro d α β η hd hd1 hα hα1 hβ hβ1 hη
  classical
  by_cases hηtop : η = ⊤
  · subst η
    refine ⟨1, by norm_num, ?_⟩
    intro ε hε hε₀
    refine ⟨0, by norm_num, 1, ?_⟩
    intro V _ _ G _ U W hUW n hn hU hW hreg S T hS hT hs ht hM
    have hn0 : (n : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast (Nat.ne_of_gt hn)
    simp only [ENNReal.top_mul hn0, ENNReal.sub_top, zero_le, add_top, le_top,
      and_self, Set.setOf_true]
    rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply, Set.indicator_univ, PMF.tsum_coe]
    exact tsub_le_self
  · have hdtop : d ≠ ⊤ := ne_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hd1 (by simp))
    have hdr : 0 < d.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hd.ne' hdtop
    have hd1r : d.toReal ≤ 1 := by
      simpa using ENNReal.toReal_mono (by simp : (1 : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤) hd1
    have hηr : 0 < η.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hη.ne' hηtop
    let γ : ℝ := η.toReal ^ 2 / (4 * (1 + η.toReal / 3))
    have hγ : 0 < γ := by
      dsimp [γ]
      positivity

      (MatchingConcentrationCorrectionAbsorption d.toReal hdr hd1r).2 γ hγ
    refine ⟨ENNReal.ofReal ε₀, ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hε₀, ?_⟩
    intro ε hε hεle
    have hεtop : ε ≠ ⊤ := ne_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hεle ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top)
    have hεr : 0 < ε.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hε.ne' hεtop
    have hεler : ε.toReal ≤ ε₀ := by
      have := ENNReal.toReal_mono ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top hεle
      simpa [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hε₀.le] using this
    have hεsmall : ε.toReal < 1 / 16 := lt_of_le_of_lt hεler hsmall
    have hεd : 2 * ε.toReal < d.toReal := by linarith
    obtain ⟨nCount, hnCount, hcompare⟩ :=
      UniformMatchingHypergeometricComparison d.toReal ε.toReal hdr hd1r
        hεr hεsmall hεd
    refine ⟨ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-γ / 2)), ?_, max nAbs nCount, ?_⟩
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_one).2 (Real.exp_lt_one_iff.mpr (by linarith))
    · intro V _ _ G _ U W hUW n hn hU hW hreg S T hS hT hs ht hM
      have hpmfComplements (p : PMF {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f})
          (B : Set {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}) :
          p.toOuterMeasure B + p.toOuterMeasure Bᶜ = 1 := by
        as_aux_lemma =>
        rw [PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_fintype, PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_fintype,
          ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
        calc
          _ = ∑ f, p f := by
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro f _
            by_cases hf : f ∈ B <;> simp [Set.indicator, hf]

      have hnAbs' : nAbs ≤ n := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) hn
      have hnCount' : nCount ≤ n := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) hn
      have hnpos : 0 < n := lt_of_lt_of_le hnAbs hnAbs'
      have hsle : S.card ≤ n := hU ▸ Finset.card_le_card hS
      have htle : T.card ≤ n := hW ▸ Finset.card_le_card hT
      let A := (Finset.range (n + 1)).filter (fun x : ℕ =>
        η.toReal * n < |(x : ℝ) - (S.card : ℝ) * T.card / n|)
      have hcount := hcompare G U W hUW n hnCount' hU hW
        (by simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hdtop, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hεtop]
          using hreg) S T hS hT hM A
      have htail := HypergeometricTwoTail n S.card T.card hnpos hsle htle η.toReal hηr
      have hcorrection := (habs ε.toReal hεr hεler).2 n hnAbs'
      have hdecay :
          Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * MatchingConcentrationCorrection d.toReal ε.toReal) *
            (∑ x ∈ A, HypergeometricMass n S.card T.card x) ≤
          Real.exp (-γ / 2) ^ n := by
        calc
          _ ≤ Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * MatchingConcentrationCorrection d.toReal ε.toReal) *
              (2 * Real.exp (-(η.toReal ^ 2 / (2 * (1 + η.toReal / 3))) * n)) :=
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left htail (Real.exp_pos _).le
          _ = 2 * Real.exp ((n : ℝ) *
              (MatchingConcentrationCorrection d.toReal ε.toReal - 2 * γ)) := by
            rw [← mul_assoc, mul_comm (Real.exp _) 2, mul_assoc, ← Real.exp_add]
            congr 2
            dsimp [γ]
            field_simp
            ring
          _ ≤ _ := hcorrection
      have hfailure := hcount.trans (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal hdecay)
      rw [ENNReal.ofReal_pow (Real.exp_pos _).le] at hfailure
      have hn0 : (n : ENNReal) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hnpos.ne'
      have hmfin : (S.card : ENNReal) * T.card / n ≠ ⊤ :=
        ENNReal.div_ne_top (ENNReal.mul_ne_top (by simp) (by simp)) hn0
      have hηnfin : η * (n : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤ :=
        ENNReal.mul_ne_top hηtop (by simp)

          (((S.card : ENNReal) * T.card / n - η * n ≤ (x : ENNReal)) ∧

theorem UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration :
    ∀ d α β η : ENNReal,
      0 < d → d ≤ 1 → 0 < α → α ≤ 1 →
      0 < β → β ≤ 1 → 0 < η →
      ∃ ε₀ : ENNReal, 0 < ε₀ ∧ ∀ ε : ENNReal, 0 < ε → ε ≤ ε₀ →
      ∃ c : ENNReal, c < 1 ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ,
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
        (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (U W : Finset V)
        (hUW : Disjoint U W) (n : ℕ),
        n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n →
        SuperRegularPair G U W ε d →
        ∀ (S T : Finset V), S ⊆ U → T ⊆ W →
        α * n ≤ S.card → β * n ≤ T.card →
        ∀ (hM : Nonempty {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f}),
          let μ := UniformPerfectMatching G U W hUW hM
          μ.toOuterMeasure {f |
              ((S.card : ENNReal) * T.card / n - η * n ≤
                ((Finset.univ.filter fun u : U => u.1 ∈ S ∧ (f.1 u).1 ∈ T).card : ENNReal)) ∧
              (((Finset.univ.filter fun u : U => u.1 ∈ S ∧ (f.1 u).1 ∈ T).card : ENNReal) ≤
                (S.card : ENNReal) * T.card / n + η * n)} ≥ 1 - c ^ n := by
UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration.name: UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration
UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write $s=|S|$, $t=|T|$, and $X=|\sigma(S)\cap T|$.  For a possible value $x$, a matching counted by $X=x$ splits into matchings on four balanced rectangles of orders
\[
 y_1=x,\quad y_2=s-x,\quad y_3=t-x,\quad y_4=n-s-t+x.
\]
Choosing their vertex sets first gives
\[
 M(G,x)\le {s\choose x}{t\choose x}{n-t\choose s-x}{n-s\choose t-x}
             \prod_{i=1}^4 M(y_i).                                 \tag{1}
\]
We will decrease $\varepsilon_0$ whenever necessary, in particular so that
$2\varepsilon<d$, and take $n_0$ at least the maximum of the thresholds in
\noderef{RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound} and \noderef{MatchingEnumeration}.
For $y_i\ge\sqrt\varepsilon n$, \noderef{RegularInducedMatchingUpperBound} gives
$M(y_i)\le D^{y_i}y_i!$, where $D=d+\varepsilon+3\sqrt\varepsilon$; for a smaller $y_i$ use $M(y_i)\le y_i!$.  At most three of the four $y_i$ can be small unless $n<4\sqrt\varepsilon n$, which is excluded by taking $\varepsilon_0<1/16$.  Since $D$ is bounded below by $d/2$ after decreasing $\varepsilon_0$, all omitted powers cost at most
$\min(D,1)^{-3\sqrt\varepsilon n}$.  Here are the details, including rectangles
of order zero.  Let $I=\{i:y_i<\sqrt\varepsilon n\}$ and
$q=\sum_{i\in I}y_i$.  The trivial estimate is valid also for $y_i=0$, since
the empty rectangle has exactly one matching and $0!=1$.  Moreover
$|I|\le3$ and hence $0\le q\le3\sqrt\varepsilon n$.  The product of all four
matching estimates is therefore at most
\[
 D^{n-q}\prod_{i=1}^4y_i!
 \le D^n\min(D,1)^{-3\sqrt\varepsilon n}\prod_{i=1}^4y_i! .
\]
Indeed, if $D\ge1$, then $D^{n-q}\le D^n$ and the minimum is $1$; if
$0<D\le1$, then
$D^{n-q}=D^nD^{-q}\le D^nD^{-3\sqrt\varepsilon n}$.  This also covers
$q=0$ without interpreting any missing rectangle separately.

By \noderef{MatchingEnumeration}, the denominator is at least
$(d-2\varepsilon)^n n!$.  Divide (1) by it.  The factorial cancellation can
be checked directly: substituting
$y_1=x,y_2=s-x,y_3=t-x,y_4=n-s-t+x$ into the four binomial coefficients gives
\[
 {s\choose x}{t\choose x}{n-t\choose s-x}{n-s\choose t-x}
 {\prod_i y_i!\over n!}
 ={{t\choose x}{n-t\choose s-x}\over {n\choose s}}.
\]
(If one of the $y_i$ is zero, the same identity holds because $0!=1$.)
Consequently
\[
 \Pr[X=x]\le R(\varepsilon)^n
 { {t\choose x}{n-t\choose s-x}\over {n\choose s}},
 \qquad
 R(\varepsilon):={D\over d-2\varepsilon}
                  \min(D,1)^{-3\sqrt\varepsilon}.                 \tag{2}
\]
This factor tends to $1$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.  Indeed,
$D\to d$, so $D/(d-2\varepsilon)\to1$.  Also $D\ge d/2>0$, and hence
$\log\min(D,1)$ remains bounded and converges to $\log d$ (with value $0$
when $d=1$).  Thus
$-3\sqrt\varepsilon\log\min(D,1)\to0$, proving that the second factor tends
to $1$.  In particular $\log R(\varepsilon)\to0$, uniformly in $s,t,x$.

The fraction in (2) is the mass of a hypergeometric variable $Y$ obtained by
choosing a uniformly random $s$-subset of an $n$-set having $t$ marked
elements.  Put $p=t/n$ and $m=sp=st/n$.  We first prove the moment estimate
needed for both tails.  For every real $\lambda$, let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ consist
of $t$ copies of $e^\lambda$ and $n-t$ copies of $1$.  Directly expanding over
the uniformly chosen subset gives
\[
 \mathbb E e^{\lambda Y}
 ={e_s(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\over {n\choose s}},                         \tag{3}
\]
where $e_s$ is the $s$-th elementary symmetric sum.

For completeness, we prove the elementary-symmetric mean inequality used
here.  For arbitrary nonnegative $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, replacing two entries
$a_i,a_j$ by their common average leaves every term of $e_s$ containing
neither or exactly one of them unchanged in total, while it replaces the
factor $a_i a_j$ in the remaining terms by
$((a_i+a_j)/2)^2\ge a_i a_j$.  Thus this averaging cannot decrease $e_s$ and
preserves the arithmetic mean.  Repeatedly average a largest and a smallest
entry.  The sum of squared deviations from the mean decreases, and its only
possible limit is zero: if the limiting deviation were positive, the range
would stay bounded below, so every further averaging would decrease the sum
of squared deviations by a fixed positive amount.  Continuity of $e_s$ then yields
\[
 {e_s(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\over {n\choose s}}
 \le \left({a_1+\cdots+a_n\over n}\right)^s.
\]
Applied to (3), this proves, for every real $\lambda$ (positive or negative),
\[
 \mathbb E e^{\lambda Y}\le(1-p+pe^\lambda)^s,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E e^{\lambda(Y-m)}
 \le \exp\bigl(m(e^\lambda-1-\lambda)\bigr),                      \tag{4}
\]
where the second inequality uses $\log(1+z)\le z$.

We now derive the two tails separately.  For $\lambda>0$, Markov's inequality
and (4) give
$\Pr(Y\ge m+u)\le
\exp(m(e^\lambda-1-\lambda)-\lambda u)$.  If $m>0$, choosing
$\lambda=\log(1+u/m)$ gives exponent $-m h(u/m)$, where
$h(z)=(1+z)\log(1+z)-z$.  The elementary inequality
$h(z)\ge z^2/(2(1+z/3))$ for $z\ge0$ follows by differentiating the
difference twice: its second derivative is
$1/(1+z)-27/(z+3)^3\ge0$, since
$(z+3)^3-27(z+1)=z^3+9z^2\ge0$, and both its value and first derivative
vanish at zero.  This gives the first bound below.  If $m=0$, then $Y=0$ and the assertion
is immediate.  For the lower tail take $\lambda<0$.  Since
$e^\lambda-1-\lambda\le\lambda^2/2$ for $\lambda\le0$ (compare second
derivatives, using $e^\lambda\le1$, and the common value and derivative at
zero), Markov applied to
$e^{\lambda(Y-m)}$ and the choice $\lambda=-u/m$ give the second bound when
$m>0$; again $m=0$ is immediate.  We have proved, for $u\ge0$,
\[
 \Pr(Y\ge m+u)\le e^{-u^2/(2(m+u/3))},\qquad
 \Pr(Y\le m-u)\le e^{-u^2/(2m)}.                                 \tag{5}
\]

Sum (2) over the two tails $|x-st/n|>\eta n$.  The hypergeometric masses in
(2) sum to the corresponding probabilities, so no additional count of
possible values is needed.  Since $m\le n$, (5) gives
\[
 \Pr(|X-st/n|>\eta n)
 \le 2\exp\{n\log R(\varepsilon)-\eta^2n/(2(1+\eta/3))\}.         \tag{6}
\]
Choose $\varepsilon_0$ so that
$\log R(\varepsilon)<\eta^2/(4(1+\eta/3))$ throughout
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$.  Then (6) is at most
$2e^{-\gamma n}$ with $\gamma=\eta^2/(4(1+\eta/3))>0$.
Enlarge $n_0$ so that $2e^{-\gamma n}\le e^{-\gamma n/2}$ for
$n\ge n_0$, and take $c=e^{-\gamma/2}<1$.  Every choice made depends only on
$d$ and $\eta$ (and hence is certainly allowed to depend on
$d,\alpha,\beta,\eta$), not on $S,T,s,t$; this proves the asserted
simultaneous uniformity.  The lower bounds involving $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are
therefore harmless restrictions on the sets, rather than ingredients in the
large-rectangle threshold.
\end{proof}
UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform matching set-image concentration]
Fix $0<d\le1$, lower density bounds $0<\alpha,\beta\le1$, and an error $\eta>0$.  There is $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, whenever $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, there are $c<1$ and $n_0$ with the following property.  If $G[U,W]$ is an $(\varepsilon,d)$-super-regular pair with $|U|=|W|=n\ge n_0$, $S\subseteq U$, $T\subseteq W$, $|S|\ge\alpha n$, $|T|\ge\beta n$, and $\sigma$ is a uniformly random perfect matching of $G$, then
\[
 \Pr\left(\left||\sigma(S)\cap T|-{|S||T|\over n}\right|>\eta n\right)\le c^n.
\]
The same $c,n_0$ work simultaneously for all permitted sizes and choices of $S,T$.
\end{lemma}
UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration.title: UniformMatchingSetImageConcentration

classical

  have h2 : 2 * ε < d := lt_of_le_of_lt
    (mul_le_mul_right' (by norm_num : (2 : ENNReal) ≤ 4) ε) h4
  obtain ⟨Cm, hCm, hCmtop, nm, hm⟩ := MatchingManyEdges ε d hε h2 hd
  obtain ⟨Cs, hCs, hCstop, ns, hs⟩ := MatchingSwitching ε d hε h4 hd
  have hdtop : d ≠ ⊤ := ne_top_of_le_ne_top ENNReal.one_ne_top hd
  have hdpos : 0 < d := lt_of_le_of_lt bot_le h4
  have hdR : 0 < d.toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hdpos.ne' hdtop
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := exists_nat_gt (2 / d.toReal)
  have hr2 : 2 ≤ d.toReal * (r : ℝ) := by
    have ht := (div_lt_iff₀ hdR).mp hr
    nlinarith
  let C : ENNReal := max Cs (Cm ^ r)
  have hC : 1 ≤ C := hCs.trans (le_max_left _ _)
  have hCtop : C ≠ ⊤ := by
    simp only [C, ne_eq, max_eq_top]

  have hns : ns ≤ n := (le_max_right nm ns).trans ((le_max_left _ _).trans hn)

  have hCn : C ≤ n := by
    apply (ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal hCtop (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top n)).mp
    have hh : (m : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast (show m < n by omega)
    simpa using (hmC.trans hh).le

  by_cases hzero : μ.toOuterMeasure (CylinderEvent x y) = 0

        (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top s)).mpr hlarge

        have hu := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hr2 (Nat.cast_nonneg n)

    have hmass (A : Set (U → W)) : μ.toOuterMeasure A ≤ 1 := by

      exact (μ.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff _).mpr (Set.subset_univ _)
    have hprefix : ∀ k (hk : k ≤ s), μ.toOuterMeasure (E k hk) ≤ (C / n) ^ k := by
      intro k
      induction k with
      | zero =>
          intro hk
          simpa only [pow_zero] using hmass (E 0 hk)
      | succ k ih =>
          intro hks
          have hk : k ≤ s := by omega
          let z : Fin s := ⟨k, by omega⟩
          have hsplit : E (k + 1) hks =

            constructor

              · exact ha ⟨i.val, hi⟩
              · have hi' : i.val = k := by omega

              apply le_antisymm _ bot_le
              rw [hsplit]

            rw [hnext]
            exact bot_le

              intro a b hab
              exact Fin.ext (congrArg (fun i : Fin s => i.val) hab)

            have hynew : y z ∉ Set.range (y ∘ idx k hk) := by
              rintro ⟨i, hi⟩
              have hh := congrArg Fin.val (hy hi)

      ext a
      rfl
    simpa only [hfull] using hprefix s le_rfl
UniformPerfectMatchingSpread.lean_statement:
theorem UniformPerfectMatchingSpread :
    ∀ ε d : ENNReal, 0 < ε → 4 * ε < d → d ≤ 1 →
      ∃ C : ENNReal, 1 ≤ C ∧ C ≠ ⊤ ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
        [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
        (U W : Finset V) (hUW : Disjoint U W) (n : ℕ),
        n₀ ≤ n → U.card = n → W.card = n → SuperRegularPair G U W ε d →
        ∀ h : Nonempty {f : U → W // PerfectMatching G U W hUW f},
          VertexSpreadOn ((UniformPerfectMatching G U W hUW h).map Subtype.val)
            (C / n) Set.univ := by
UniformPerfectMatchingSpread.name: UniformPerfectMatchingSpread
UniformPerfectMatchingSpread.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The inequality $4\varepsilon<d$ implies $2\varepsilon<d$. Take finite
constants $C_{\rm many},C_{\rm sw}\geq1$ and their order thresholds from
\noderef{MatchingManyEdges} and \noderef{MatchingSwitching}, respectively.
Since $d>0$, choose a positive integer $r$ with $dr\geq2$, and set
\[
 C=\max\{C_{\rm sw},C_{\rm many}^r\}.
\]
This constant is finite and at least one. Choose $n_0$ at least both support
thresholds, at least one, and greater than $C$. Thus $n\geq n_0$ implies
$n>0$ and $C/n\leq1$. Fix such an instance and any supplied witness that
the finite type of perfect matchings is nonempty. Use that witness to form
the uniform distribution of \noderef{UniformPerfectMatching}, and denote
its image on maps $U\to W$ by $\mu$.

Fix distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_s\in U$ and arbitrary
$y_1,\ldots,y_s\in W$. Write $E_s$ for their cylinder event as defined in
\noderef{CylinderEvent}. If $\mu(E_s)=0$, the desired inequality holds.
Otherwise, some map in the support of $\mu$ belongs to $E_s$: on a finite
space an event of positive mass contains an atom of positive mass. Every
map in this support comes from a perfect matching by
\noderef{UniformPerfectMatching}. By \noderef{PerfectMatching}, it is
bijective and every pair $x f(x)$ is an edge. Consequently all prescribed
pairs are edges and the $y_i$ are distinct, since the $x_i$ are distinct.
Thus the prescriptions form a matching. This also explains why repeated
right endpoints or nonedges have zero cylinder probability.

If $s\geq dn/2$, \noderef{MatchingManyEdges} gives
\[
 \Pr[x_i y_i\in M\ (1\leq i\leq s)]\leq C_{\rm many}^{n}/n^s
 \leq C_{\rm many}^{rs}/n^s\leq C^s/n^s=(C/n)^s,
\]
because $rs\geq rdn/2\geq n$, $C_{\rm many}\geq1$, and
$C_{\rm many}^r\leq C$.

If $s<dn/2$, for $0\leq k\leq s$ let $E_k$ be the cylinder imposing just
the first $k$ prescriptions, and put $p_k=\mu(E_k)$. We prove
$p_k\leq(C/n)^k$ by induction. The empty cylinder $E_0$ is the whole map
space, so $p_0=1=(C/n)^0$; this includes the case $s=0$.
For $k<s$, the first $k$ pairs form a matching $N_k$ of size
$k\leq s<dn/2$, and neither endpoint of $x_{k+1}y_{k+1}$ is covered by
$N_k$, by distinctness on both sides. Moreover
$E_{k+1}=E_k\cap\{f:f(x_{k+1})=y_{k+1}\}$.
If $p_k=0$, containment $E_{k+1}\subseteq E_k$ gives $p_{k+1}=0$.
If $p_k>0$, it is finite because $\mu$ is a probability distribution.
Applying \noderef{MatchingSwitching} with this prefix and fresh edge gives
\[
 p_{k+1}/p_k\leq C_{\rm sw}/n\leq C/n.
\]
Multiplication by the finite nonzero $p_k$ and the induction hypothesis yield
\[
 p_{k+1}\leq(C/n)p_k\leq(C/n)^{k+1}.
\]
At $k=s$ this proves the required cylinder inequality. Together with
$C/n\leq1$, it is exactly \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} on the entire codomain $W$.
\end{proof}
UniformPerfectMatchingSpread.title: UniformPerfectMatchingSpread

UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw.lean_proof:
classical
  -- PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFinset_apply interprets this counting ratio as probability.
  by_cases hxs : x ≤ s
  · have hcount : ((S.powersetCard s).filter fun U => (U ∩ T).card = x).card =
        ((T.powersetCard x).product ((S \ T).powersetCard (s - x))).card := by
      apply Finset.card_bij (fun U _ => (U ∩ T, U \ T))
      · intro U hU
        obtain ⟨hUS, hUcard⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hU).1
        have hUx := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hU).2
        apply Finset.mem_product.mpr
        refine ⟨Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨Finset.inter_subset_right, hUx⟩,
          Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
        · intro v hv
          obtain ⟨hvU, hvT⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hv
          exact Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hUS hvU, hvT⟩
        · have hsum := Finset.card_sdiff_add_card_inter U T
          change (U \ T).card = s - x
          omega
      · intro U _ W _ hUW
        have hi : U ∩ T = W ∩ T := congrArg Prod.fst hUW
        have hd : U \ T = W \ T := congrArg Prod.snd hUW
        calc
          U = (U ∩ T) ∪ (U \ T) := by
            ext v
            simp only [Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_sdiff]
            tauto
          _ = (W ∩ T) ∪ (W \ T) := by rw [hi, hd]
          _ = W := by
            ext v
            simp only [Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_sdiff]
            tauto
      · intro P hP
        obtain ⟨hP1, hP2⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hP
        obtain ⟨hP1T, hP1card⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hP1
        obtain ⟨hP2ST, hP2card⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hP2
        have hP2T : Disjoint P.2 T := by
          apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
          intro v hvP hvT
          exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp (hP2ST hvP)).2 hvT
        have hdis : Disjoint P.1 P.2 :=
          (hP2T.symm).mono_left hP1T
        have hi : (P.1 ∪ P.2) ∩ T = P.1 := by
          rw [Finset.union_inter_distrib_right, Finset.inter_eq_left.mpr hP1T,
            Finset.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hP2T, Finset.union_empty]
        have hd : (P.1 ∪ P.2) \ T = P.2 := by
          ext v
          constructor
          · intro hv
            obtain ⟨hvP, hvT⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hv
            rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hvP with hv1 | hv2
            · exact (hvT (hP1T hv1)).elim
            · exact hv2
          · intro hv
            exact Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_union_right _ hv,
              (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp (hP2ST hv)).2⟩
        refine ⟨P.1 ∪ P.2, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr
          ⟨?_, ?_⟩, by simpa only [hi] using hP1card⟩, ?_⟩
        · exact Finset.union_subset (hP1T.trans hTS)
            (hP2ST.trans Finset.sdiff_subset)
        · rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdis, hP1card, hP2card]
          omega
        · exact Prod.ext hi hd
    rw [hcount]
    have hprod := Finset.card_product (T.powersetCard x) ((S \ T).powersetCard (s - x))
    change (Finset.product (T.powersetCard x) ((S \ T).powersetCard (s - x))).card =
      (T.powersetCard x).card * ((S \ T).powersetCard (s - x)).card at hprod
    rw [hprod]
    simp only [Finset.card_powersetCard,
      Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset hTS, Nat.cast_mul, HypergeometricMass, if_pos hxs]
  · have hzero : ((S.powersetCard s).filter fun U => (U ∩ T).card = x) = ∅ := by
      apply Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr
      intro U hU
      have hcard := (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hU).1).2
      have hx := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hU).2
      have hle := Finset.card_le_card (Finset.inter_subset_left : U ∩ T ⊆ U)
      omega
    simp only [hzero, Finset.card_empty, Nat.cast_zero, zero_div,
      HypergeometricMass, if_neg hxs]
UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw.lean_statement:
theorem UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (S T : Finset V) (hTS : T ⊆ S) (s : ℕ) (hs : s ≤ S.card) (x : ℕ) :
    (((S.powersetCard s).filter fun U => (U ∩ T).card = x).card : ℝ) /
        ((S.powersetCard s).card : ℝ) =
      HypergeometricMass S.card s T.card x := by
UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw.name: UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw
UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
There are $\binom{|S|}{s}>0$ such subsets, including when $S$ is
empty (then $s=0$). If $x>s$, none has intersection size $x$, and
the defining conditional branch of \noderef{HypergeometricMass}
is zero. If $x\leq s$, the map
$U\mapsto(U\cap T,U\setminus T)$ is a bijection between the
subsets being counted and pairs consisting of an $x$-subset of $T$
and an $(s-x)$-subset of $S\setminus T$. Its inverse is union;
the two chosen sets are disjoint, their union has size $s$, and its
intersection with $T$ is exactly the first chosen set. The number
of pairs is
$\binom{|T|}{x}\binom{|S|-|T|}{s-x}$, since $T\subseteq S$.
This also gives zero in the infeasible cases, by the vanishing of
the relevant binomial coefficient. Divide by the positive total
number to obtain the formula in \noderef{HypergeometricMass}.
For interpretation as probability, Mathlib's \texttt{PMF.toOuterMeasure\_uniformOfFinset\_apply}
says that the uniform finite law assigns exactly this fraction to
the event. The proof of the equality itself is the counting bijection,
so no tail or independence assumption is being used.
\end{proof}
UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[The uniform subset intersection law]
Let $T\subseteq S$ be finite sets and $s\leq |S|$. For every
nonnegative integer $x$, the fraction of $s$-subsets $U$ of $S$
with $|U\cap T|=x$ equals $H(|S|,s,|T|,x)$, the mass defined
in \noderef{HypergeometricMass}.
\end{lemma}
UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw.title: UniformSubsetIntersectionLaw

def UpdatedCandidacyCluster {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]

classical

    apply Finset.image_congr

  change (x ∉ X ∧ v ∉ X.image f.toFun ∧ A.allowed x v ∧
      ∀ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y → G.Adj v (f.toFun y)) ↔
    (x ∉ X ∧ v ∉ X.image g.toFun ∧ A.allowed x v ∧
      ∀ y ∈ X, H.Adj x y → G.Adj v (g.toFun y))
  rw [himage]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hx, hv, ha, he⟩
    refine ⟨hx, hv, ha, ?_⟩
    intro y hy hxy
    rw [← h y hy]
    exact he y hy hxy
  · rintro ⟨hx, hv, ha, he⟩
    refine ⟨hx, hv, ha, ?_⟩
    intro y hy hxy

theorem UpdatedCandidacyCongruence {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*}
    [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B) (X : Finset VH)
    (f g : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ X, f.toFun x = g.toFun x) :
    ∀ x v, (UpdatedCandidacy B A X f).allowed x v ↔
      (UpdatedCandidacy B A X g).allowed x v := by
UpdatedCandidacyCongruence.name: UpdatedCandidacyCongruence
UpdatedCandidacyCongruence.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Since the two maps agree on $X$, their image sets $f(X)$ and $g(X)$
are equal: an element represented by $f(y)$ with $y\in X$ is also
$g(y)$, and conversely. Expand \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}.
The source condition $x\notin X$, the unoccupied-image condition
$v\notin f(X)=g(X)$, and the original candidacy condition $A(x,v)$
are identical. For each $y\in X$ adjacent to $x$, the final host-edge
condition is identical because $f(y)=g(y)$. Thus every conjunct agrees,
proving the equivalence for all $x,v$. No values outside $X$ enter
any of these conditions.
\end{proof}
UpdatedCandidacyCongruence.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Unused stored values do not change updated candidacy]
Let $f,g$ be partial compatible embeddings on the same finite set $X$
in a blow-up instance with candidacy system $A$. If $f(x)=g(x)$ for
every $x\in X$, then $A_f$ and $A_g$, as defined in
\noderef{UpdatedCandidacy}, have exactly the same allowed pairs $(x,v)$.
\end{lemma}
UpdatedCandidacyCongruence.title: UpdatedCandidacyCongruence

UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension.lean_proof:
classical
  have hsub : X ⊆ X' := by rw [hdom]; exact Finset.subset_union_left
  have source (y : VH) (hy : B.sourceCluster y = j) : y ∉ X :=
    fun hx => hun y hy (hsub hx)
  have oldHost (v : VG) (hv : B.hostCluster v = j) : v ∉ X.image f.toFun := by
    rintro hm
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hfx⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hm
    have hc := A.cluster_respecting (f.compatible x hx)
    rw [hfx, hv] at hc
    exact source x hc hx
  have newHost (v : VG) (hv : B.hostCluster v = j) : v ∉ X'.image h.toFun := by
    rintro hm
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hfx⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hm
    have hc := A.cluster_respecting (h.compatible x hx)
    rw [hfx, hv] at hc
    exact hun x hc hx
  refine ⟨?_, fun y hy => ⟨fun _ => source y hy, fun _ => hun y hy⟩,
    fun v hv => ⟨fun _ => oldHost v hv, fun _ => newHost v hv⟩⟩
  ext p
  change (B.sourceCluster p.1 = j ∧ B.hostCluster p.2 = j ∧
    p.1 ∉ X' ∧ p.2 ∉ X'.image h.toFun ∧ A.allowed p.1 p.2 ∧
      ∀ x ∈ X', H.Adj p.1 x → G.Adj p.2 (h.toFun x)) ↔
    (B.sourceCluster p.1 = j ∧ B.hostCluster p.2 = j ∧
    p.1 ∉ X ∧ p.2 ∉ X.image f.toFun ∧ A.allowed p.1 p.2 ∧
      ∀ x ∈ X, H.Adj p.1 x → G.Adj p.2 (f.toFun x))
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hs, ht, _, _, ha, hadj⟩
    refine ⟨hs, ht, source p.1 hs, oldHost p.2 ht, ha, ?_⟩
    intro x hx hpx
    simpa only [hag x hx] using hadj x (hsub hx) hpx
  · rintro ⟨hs, ht, _, _, ha, hadj⟩
    refine ⟨hs, ht, hun p.1 hs, newHost p.2 ht, ha, ?_⟩
    intro x hx hpx
    rw [hdom] at hx
    rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hx with hx | hx
    · simpa only [hag x hx] using hadj x hx hpx
    · have hr := B.reduced_support hpx
      rw [hs, hY x hx] at hr
      exact (hji hr).elim

theorem UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension
    {r : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (X Y X' : Finset VH) (f : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)
    (h : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X') (i j : Fin r)
    (hdom : X' = X ∪ Y) (hY : ∀ y ∈ Y, B.sourceCluster y = i)
    (hun : ∀ y, B.sourceCluster y = j → y ∉ X')
    (hji : ¬R.Adj j i) (hij : j ≠ i)
    (hag : ∀ x ∈ X, h.toFun x = f.toFun x) :
    UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X' h j = UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A X f j ∧
    (∀ y, B.sourceCluster y = j → (y ∉ X' ↔ y ∉ X)) ∧
    (∀ v, B.hostCluster v = j →
      (v ∉ X'.image h.toFun ↔ v ∉ X.image f.toFun)) := by
UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension.name: UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension
UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
The source equivalence follows because both domains avoid cluster $j$.
Neither image meets its host cluster: by compatibility in
\noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} and the cluster-respecting clause
of \noderef{CandidacySystem}, an image in host cluster $j$ would have
its preimage in source cluster $j$, contrary to the domain assumption.
This proves the host equivalence as well.
In \noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}, all cluster, domain, image, and
original-allowed conditions therefore agree. The old adjacency
constraints agree because $h=f$ on $X$. A possible new constraint is
indexed by $y\in Y$ and an edge $xy\in H$ with $x$ in cluster $j$.
The reduced-support property of \noderef{BlowUpInstance} would make
$ji$ an edge of $R$, which is excluded. Thus there are no new
constraints on this cluster, proving equality of the updated sets.
\end{proof}
UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Non-neighbour candidacy is unchanged]
Let $f$ be a compatible partial embedding on $X$ and $h$ one on
$X'=X\cup Y$, agreeing on $X$. Suppose all vertices of $Y$ lie in source
cluster $i$, source cluster $j$ is disjoint from $X'$, $j\ne i$, and
$ji\notin E(R)$. Then the true updated candidacy sets of $j$ at $f$
and $h$ are equal. For every source vertex of $j$, being outside $X'$
is equivalent to being outside $X$; for every host vertex of $j$, being
outside $h(X')$ is equivalent to being outside $f(X)$.
\end{lemma}
UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension.title: UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension

VariableSizeInductionBase.lean_proof:
classical
  have host_nonempty (x : VH) : Nonempty {v : VG // B.hostCluster v = B.sourceCluster x} := by
    have hs : 0 < Fintype.card {y : VH // B.sourceCluster y = B.sourceCluster x} :=
      Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨⟨x, rfl⟩⟩
    exact Fintype.card_pos_iff.mp (lt_of_lt_of_le hs (B.capacity (B.sourceCluster x)))
  let f0 : PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A ∅ :=
    { toFun := fun x => (Classical.choice (host_nonempty x)).val
      injOn := by intro x hx; simp at hx
      map_adj := by intro x y hx; simp at hx
      compatible := by intro x hx; simp at hx }
  let μ := PMF.pure f0
  refine ⟨μ, hq, hdegree, hcolour, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j hj
    simp at hj
  · simp
  · refine ⟨hC, ?_⟩
    intro s x y hx hy
    cases s with
    | zero =>
      have hc : CylinderEvent x y = Set.univ := by
        ext f
        simp [CylinderEvent]
      rw [hc, pow_zero]
      exact le_of_eq ((PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff _ _).mpr (Set.subset_univ _))
    | succ s =>
      exact False.elim (Finset.notMem_empty _ (x ⟨0, Nat.succ_pos s⟩).property)
  · intro f hf j hj hr
    let L : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
      ∃ x : VH, z = Sum.inl x ∧ B.sourceCluster x = j
    let Q : Finset (VH ⊕ VG) := Finset.univ.filter fun z =>
      ∃ v : VG, z = Sum.inr v ∧ B.hostCluster v = j
    let P : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
      ∃ x : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl x ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧ A.allowed x v
    let W : SimpleGraph (VH ⊕ VG) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p s =>
      ∃ x : VH, ∃ v : VG, p = Sum.inl x ∧ s = Sum.inr v ∧
        (x, v) ∈ UpdatedCandidacyCluster B A ∅ f j
    letI : DecidableRel P.Adj := Classical.decRel _
    letI : DecidableRel W.Adj := Classical.decRel _
    -- Restriction preserves every edge count used by super-regularity on these parts.
    have hadj : ∀ p ∈ L, ∀ s ∈ Q, W.Adj p s ↔ P.Adj p s := by
      intro p hp s hs
      obtain ⟨x, rfl, hx⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hp).2
      obtain ⟨v, rfl, hv⟩ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hs).2
      simp [W, P, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj, UpdatedCandidacyCluster, UpdatedCandidacy,
        hx, hv]
    have hleft : ∀ p ∈ L, Q.filter (fun s => W.Adj p s) =
        Q.filter (fun s => P.Adj p s) := by
      intro p hp
      ext s
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
      exact and_congr_right fun hs => hadj p hp s hs
    have hright : ∀ s ∈ Q, L.filter (fun p => W.Adj p s) =
        L.filter (fun p => P.Adj p s) := by
      intro s hs
      ext p
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
      exact and_congr_right fun hp => hadj p hp s hs
    have hdens : ∀ U ⊆ L, ∀ V ⊆ Q, PairDensity W U V = PairDensity P U V := by
      intro U hU V hV
      have he : (U.product V).filter (fun p => W.Adj p.1 p.2) =
          (U.product V).filter (fun p => P.Adj p.1 p.2) := by
        ext p
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
        refine and_congr_right fun hp => ?_
        obtain ⟨hu, hv⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hp

      unfold PairDensity

    have hsuper : SuperRegularPair W L Q (epsilon 0) d := by

      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro U hU V hV hu hv

      · intro p hpL

        exact hp.2.1 p hpL

      and_true, not_false_eq_true, hdensity]

VariableSizeInductionBase.lean_statement:
theorem VariableSizeInductionBase
    {r q : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
    [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
    {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}
    [DecidableRel R.Adj]
    (B : BlowUpInstance r VH VG H G R) (A : CandidacySystem B)
    (colour : Fin r → Fin q) (epsilon density : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (D : ℕ) (d C : ENNReal) (n : ℕ)
    (hq : 0 < q) (hdensity : density 0 = d) (hC : C / n ≤ 1)
    (hdegree : ∀ j : Fin r,
      (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin r => R.Adj j k).card ≤ D)
    (hcolour : ∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, i ≠ j →
      (R.Adj i j ∨ ∃ k : Fin r, R.Adj i k ∧ R.Adj k j) →
      colour i ≠ colour j)
    (hA : CandidacySuperRegular B A (epsilon 0) d) :
    ∃ μ : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A ∅),
      ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon density D C n 0 ∅ ∅ μ := by
VariableSizeInductionBase.name: VariableSizeInductionBase
VariableSizeInductionBase.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
We first justify a total representative for the empty-domain embedding;
its values outside the empty domain impose no embedding constraints.
For each source vertex $x$, its source fibre at
$j=B.\mathrm{sourceCluster}(x)$ is nonempty. Capacity in
\noderef{BlowUpInstance} says that the corresponding host fibre has at
least this cardinality, and hence is nonempty. Choose a host vertex from
that fibre for each $x$, obtaining a total function $f_0:V_H\to V_G$.
If $V_H$ is empty this is instead the unique empty function, also when
$V_G$ is empty. Injectivity on the empty domain, edge preservation on that
domain, and candidacy compatibility there are vacuous. Thus $f_0$ defines
an element of \noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} with domain
$\varnothing$. Put $\mu$ equal to its point mass.

The round is legal because $q>0$. The degree and colouring clauses are
the assumptions, and the touched-set clause is vacuous. No colour is
negative, so the domain selected by colour less than zero or membership
in the empty touched set is empty. To check \noderef{VertexSpreadOn},
the bound $C/n\leq1$ is assumed. For a positive number $s$ of prescribed
vertices there is no map from $\operatorname{Fin}(s)$ to the empty domain,
so there is no such cylinder to test. For $s=0$ the cylinder is the entire
function space, has probability one, and the bound is $(C/n)^0=1$.

For the only supported outcome $f_0$ and any cluster $j$, both the
exposure finset and the touched-neighbour finset are empty. Their
cardinalities are zero, so the bounds by $D$ and by one hold and the
required witness error is $\varepsilon_0$ with density $p_0=d$.
There are no used source or host vertices. By \noderef{UpdatedCandidacy},
the updated allowed relation at the empty domain is exactly $A.allowed$:
both exclusions and the universal embedded-neighbour condition are
vacuous. By \noderef{UpdatedCandidacyCluster}, the updated cluster graph
is therefore precisely the original candidacy graph of cluster $j$.

More explicitly, take $W_j$ to be the graph whose edges are the allowed
pairs between the left copy of $X_j$ and the right copy of $V_j$, with
all other vertices isolated. Its containment in the updated cluster
graph is equality. The graph used in \noderef{CandidacySuperRegular}
may retain allowed pairs for other clusters, but on the parts
$L_j=\operatorname{inl}(X_j)$ and $Q_j=\operatorname{inr}(V_j)$ its
edges are exactly those of $W_j$. Indeed an allowed pair respects
clusters by \noderef{CandidacySystem}; restricting its source to $X_j$
automatically restricts its host to $V_j$. Thus all degrees into these
parts and all edge counts between their subsets are identical.
Expanding \noderef{SuperRegularPair} and \noderef{RegularPair} transfers
the asserted $(\varepsilon_0,d)$-super-regularity to $W_j$ on these
exact parts. This supplies every witness clause, using the original
candidacy graphs and no thinning. All clauses of
\noderef{ColourRoundInvariant} are now verified.
\end{proof}
VariableSizeInductionBase.tex_statement:
\begin{lemma}[Initial colour-round law]
Let $B$ be a finite blow-up instance with candidacy system $A$ and reduced
graph $R$ on $[r]$. Fix $q>0$, a colouring $c:[r]\to\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$,
sequences $\varepsilon,p:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty]$, $D,n\in\mathbb N$,
and $d,C\in[0,\infty]$. Assume $p_0=d$, $C/n\leq1$, every reduced
vertex has at most $D$ neighbours, and distinct reduced vertices that are
adjacent or have a common neighbour have different colours.
Suppose \noderef{CandidacySuperRegular} holds with parameters
$(\varepsilon_0,d)$. Then there is a law $\mu$ on
\noderef{PartialCompatibleEmbedding} with empty domain satisfying
\[
 \mathcal I(0,\varnothing;\varnothing,\mu)
\]
of \noderef{ColourRoundInvariant}, with parameters $(\varepsilon,p,D,C,n)$.
\end{lemma}
VariableSizeInductionBase.title: VariableSizeInductionBase

VariableSizeInductionIteration.lean_proof:
classical
  intro r VH VG _ _ _ _ H G _ R _ B A hsizes hmax hG hA hsaturating
  let Q := Delta ^ 2 + 1
  have hQ : 0 < Q := Nat.zero_lt_succ _
  obtain ⟨q, _, hqQ, colour0, hcolour0⟩ := ReducedSquareColoring R hmax
  let colour : Fin r → Fin Q := fun j => Fin.castLE hqQ (colour0 j)
  have hcolour : ∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, i ≠ j →
      (R.Adj i j ∨ ∃ k : Fin r, R.Adj i k ∧ R.Adj k j) →
      colour i ≠ colour j := by
    intro i j hij hadj heq
    exact hcolour0 hij hadj (Fin.castLE_injective hqQ heq)
  have hdegree (j : Fin r) :
      (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin r => R.Adj j k).card ≤ Delta := by
    have hneighbors : (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin r => R.Adj j k) =
        R.neighborFinset j := by
      ext k
      simp
    rw [hneighbors]
    exact (R.degree_le_maxDegree j).trans hmax
  let completedDomain (s : ℕ) : Finset VH := Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH =>
    (colour (B.sourceCluster x)).val < s ∨
      B.sourceCluster x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin r => (colour j).val = s)
  have complete (s : ℕ) (hs : s < Q)
      (X : Finset VH) (μ : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X))
      (hμ : ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon p Delta C n s ∅ X μ) :
      ∃ ν : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A (completedDomain s)),
        ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon p Delta C n s
          (Finset.univ.filter fun j : Fin r => (colour j).val = s)
          (completedDomain s) ν := by
    obtain ⟨hepsilon, hepsilon1, hsqrt, hregloss, hdegloss, htheta,
      hrho, hd, hdcomp, hgap, homega⟩ := hstatic s hs
    obtain ⟨hmatching, hfourgraphs⟩ := hthresholds s hs
    obtain ⟨hinv, hstrict, hpaddingDegree, hpaddingRegularity,
      houtputDegree, houtputRegularity⟩ := hreserve s hs
    have step := VariableSizeInductionStep B A colour theta p epsilon rho
      zeta omega hatZeta Delta d C a n s cert hs hepsilon hepsilon1
      hdegree hcolour hsizes hG hsaturating ha ha1 hC hfailure
      hsqrt hregloss hdegloss htheta hrho hd hdcomp hrec hgap homega
      hmatching hfourgraphs hinv hstrict hpaddingDegree hpaddingRegularity
      (fun x hx => ⟨houtputDegree, houtputRegularity⟩)
    obtain ⟨K, _, hK⟩ := ColourClassSequentialCompletion B A colour epsilon p
      Delta C n s step ∅ X μ (by simp) hμ
    exact ⟨μ.bind K, hK⟩
  have start (s : ℕ) (hs : s < Q) :
      ∃ (X : Finset VH) (μ : PMF (PartialCompatibleEmbedding B A X)),
        ColourRoundInvariant B A colour epsilon p Delta C n s ∅ X μ := by
    induction s with
    | zero =>
      obtain ⟨μ, hμ⟩ := VariableSizeInductionBase B A colour epsilon p
        Delta d C n hQ hp hC hdegree hcolour hA
      exact ⟨∅, μ, hμ⟩
    | succ s ih =>
      have hsold : s < Q := by omega
      obtain ⟨X, μ, hμ⟩ := ih hsold
      obtain ⟨ν, hν⟩ := complete s hsold X μ hμ
      exact ⟨completedDomain s, ν,
        ColourRoundReset B A colour epsilon p Delta C n s
          (completedDomain s) ν hs (hstatic s hsold).1 hν⟩
  have hlast : Delta ^ 2 < Q := Nat.lt_succ_self _
  obtain ⟨X, μ, hμ⟩ := start (Delta ^ 2) hlast
  have hfinal := complete (Delta ^ 2) hlast X μ hμ
  have hfull : completedDomain (Delta ^ 2) = Finset.univ := by
    ext x
    simp only [completedDomain, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
    have hbound : (colour (B.sourceCluster x)).val ≤ Delta ^ 2 :=
      Nat.le_of_lt_succ (colour (B.sourceCluster x)).isLt
    exact iff_true_intro (lt_or_eq_of_le hbound)

  obtain ⟨ν, hν⟩ := hfinal
  exact ⟨colour, ν, hν⟩
VariableSizeInductionIteration.lean_statement:
theorem VariableSizeInductionIteration
    (d : ENNReal) (Delta : ℕ)
    (p rho epsilon omega theta zeta hatZeta : ℕ → ENNReal)
    (cert : InductionApplicationCertificate Delta (Delta ^ 2 + 1) d
      theta p epsilon rho zeta omega hatZeta)
    (a C : ENNReal) (n : ℕ)
    (hp : p 0 = d)
    (hrec : ∀ x, x < Delta → p (x + 1) = rho x * (d / 2))
    (ha : 0 < a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (hC : C / n ≤ 1)
    (hfailure : Delta * (1 - a) ^ n ≤ (2 : ENNReal)⁻¹)
    (hstatic : ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
      epsilon s ≤ epsilon (s + 1) ∧ epsilon (s + 1) ≤ 1 ∧
      2 * (zeta s) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta s ∧
      zeta s + Delta * (zeta s) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta s ∧
      zeta s + 2 * Delta * zeta s ≤ theta s ∧
      (∀ x, x ≤ Delta → 0 < theta s ∧ 4 * theta s < rho x) ∧
      (∀ x, x ≤ Delta → 2 * zeta s < rho x ∧ 2 * zeta s < 1 - rho x) ∧
      2 * zeta s < d / 2 ∧ 2 * zeta s < 1 - d / 2 ∧
      (∀ x, x < Delta →
        p (x + 1) + epsilon s + 1 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ p x) ∧
      omega (s + 1) < epsilon (s + 1))
    (hthresholds : ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
      (∀ x, x ≤ Delta →
        cert.witnessThinningThreshold s x ≤ n ∧
        cert.hostThinningThreshold s ≤ n ∧
        cert.matchingThreshold s x ≤ n ∧
        cert.matchingExistenceThreshold s x ≤ n ∧
        cert.matchingConstant s x ≤ C / 2) ∧
      (∀ x y, x ≤ Delta → y ≤ Delta →
        cert.fourGraphsThreshold s x y ≤ n ∧
        a ≤ cert.fourGraphsConstant s x y))
    (hreserve : ∀ s, s < Delta ^ 2 + 1 →
      (n : ENNReal)⁻¹ ≤ hatZeta s ∧
      hatZeta s < zeta s ∧
      hatZeta s + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ zeta s ∧
      hatZeta s + 1 / (zeta s * (n : ENNReal)) ≤ zeta s ∧
      omega (s + 1) + 2 / (n : ENNReal) ≤ epsilon (s + 1) ∧
      omega (s + 1) + 1 / (epsilon (s + 1) * (n : ENNReal)) ≤
        epsilon (s + 1)) :

\begin{proof}
The corrected paper processes each finite colour class sequentially and
then changes only the round bookkeeping. We give that finite execution,
leaving all local graph and probability estimates to the stated local
transition.

By \noderef{ReducedSquareColoring}, choose $q>0$, $q\leq Q$, and a
colouring $c_0:[r]\to\operatorname{Fin}(q)$ separating distinct adjacent
vertices and distinct vertices with a common neighbour. Define
$c(j)=\operatorname{Fin.castLE}(q\leq Q)(c_0(j))$.
This lift does not change the natural-number value of any colour.
It is injective on colour values: equality after lifting gives equality
of the original values and hence, by extensionality of finite indices,
equality in $\operatorname{Fin}(q)$. Thus $c$ satisfies precisely the
square-colouring separation used below. It takes values in
$\operatorname{Fin}(Q)$; unused colours are allowed. For each reduced
vertex $j$, the finset $\{k:R.Adj(j,k)\}$ has cardinality
$\deg_R(j)\leq\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$. This supplies the local per-vertex
degree hypothesis; it is valid also when there are no reduced vertices.

We next verify the one-cluster transition for any legal round $s<Q$.
Apply \noderef{VariableSizeInductionStep} with the substitution
\[
 (\theta,\mathrm{density},\epsilon,\rho,\eta,\omega,\xi)
       =(\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\widehat\zeta),
 \qquad D=\Delta,\quad q=Q.
\]
Use exactly the given certificate $\mathcal K$. Its type is the
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate} type required by this
substitution, with independent exposure and round indices.
The round bound is $s<Q$; the first displayed round inequalities give
$\varepsilon_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}$ and $\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1$.
The derived degree bounds and the lifted square colouring give the next
two hypotheses. The assumed source/host size equalities give both
alternatives $n,n+1$ and the balance condition required there.
The given \noderef{InstanceSuperRegular} hypothesis has exactly error
$\varepsilon_0$ and density $d$, and the assumed
\noderef{SaturatingSourcePair} supplies its source-matching hypothesis.

The assumptions $0<a\leq1$, $C/n\leq1$, and
$\Delta(1-a)^n\leq1/2$ give the three constant/size bounds.
The three square-root and linear loss bounds give the simultaneous
good-edge inequalities. For every $x\leq\Delta$, the next display
gives $0<\theta_s$, $4\theta_s<\rho_x$, and both density and complementary
density bounds for $2\zeta_s$; the two corresponding host bounds
are also explicitly assumed. The recursion supplies
$p_{x+1}=\rho_x(d/2)$ for every $x<\Delta$, and the assumed density-gap
inequality supplies $p_{x+1}+\varepsilon_s+1/n\leq p_x$.
The output comparison is $\omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}$.
All four scalar thinning/matching thresholds and the comparison
$M_{s,x}\leq C/2$ are given for every exposure $x\leq\Delta$.
For every ordered pair $x,y\leq\Delta$ the Four Graphs threshold and
$a\leq a_{s,x,y}$ are given, without requiring $x\leq y$.

The final two displays give respectively the inner reserve
$n^{-1}\leq\widehat\zeta_s$, its strict inequality
$\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s$, the two padding inequalities, and both
output degree/regularity slack inequalities. The last two are
independent of $x$ and so hold for each $x\leq\Delta$ as required.
This checks every numerical and instance hypothesis of the local step.
Consequently, for every current touched set $T\subseteq B_s$, domain
$Z$, and actual law $\nu$ satisfying $\mathcal I(s,T;Z,\nu)$, and for
every $i\in B_s\setminus T$, that node supplies the total kernel
$\kappa$ preserving all old maps on $Z$, the conditional new-cluster
spread bound, and the new invariant for the actual law
$\nu\mathbin{\mathrm{bind}}\kappa$. This is exactly the transition
hypothesis of \noderef{ColourClassSequentialCompletion}. It does
not resample the past or condition on success for the whole class.

Put $P_s=\{j:c(j)<s\}$ and let $Z_s$ be its union of source clusters.
Since $Q\geq1$, \noderef{VariableSizeInductionBase} applies at zero:
$p_0=d$, $C/n\leq1$, the degree and colouring bounds hold, and the
given \noderef{CandidacySuperRegular} provides the original witnesses.
It gives a specified law $\nu_0$ with
$\mathcal I(0,\varnothing;Z_0,\nu_0)$, where $Z_0=\varnothing$.

Induct over $s=0,\ldots,Q-1$. Starting with a specified law
$\nu_s$ satisfying $\mathcal I(s,\varnothing;Z_s,\nu_s)$, apply
\noderef{ColourClassSequentialCompletion} to the just verified local
transition. Retain its composite kernel $K_s$ and its completed law
$\bar\nu_s=\nu_s\mathbin{\mathrm{bind}}K_s$, on the exact domain
\[
 \bar Z_s=\{x:c(B.\mathrm{sourceCluster}(x))<s
                   \text{ or }c(B.\mathrm{sourceCluster}(x))=s\}.
\]
The node gives $\mathcal I(s,B_s;\bar Z_s,\bar\nu_s)$ for that very law,
and preservation of every previously embedded map. Its empty-class
case is included: the kernel is the point-mass identity after identifying
equal domains, rather than an additional probabilistic step.
If $s+1<Q$, apply \noderef{ColourRoundReset} with
$\varepsilon_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}$ to this completed law.
It supplies $\mathcal I(s+1,\varnothing;\bar Z_s,\bar\nu_s)$ without
changing the domain or the law. The identity
\[
 c(j)<s\ \text{or}\ c(j)=s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c(j)<s+1
\]
identifies $\bar Z_s=Z_{s+1}$, so use the same law, with only this
domain identification, as $\nu_{s+1}$. This completes the induction at
every intermediate boundary. The construction binds only the successive
local kernels, so it retains their recursively produced law throughout.

At $s=Q-1$ do not reset. Every colour value is less than $Q$, hence is
either less than $Q-1$ or equal to $Q-1$. Therefore
$\bar Z_{Q-1}=V_H$. This holds even if the last class is empty.
Identify the last law with a PMF on
$\mathcal E(V_H)=\operatorname{PartialCompatibleEmbedding}(B,A,V_H)$
without changing any underlying function. The completed invariant is
precisely $\mathcal I(Q-1,B_{Q-1};V_H,\bar\nu_{Q-1})$.
The witness clause now has no unembedded cluster, and the domain,
colouring, degree and spread clauses remain the completed invariant's
clauses. Set $\mu=\bar\nu_{Q-1}$. This proves the claimed final state
and its \noderef{VertexSpreadOn} bound. When $Q=1$ the same argument
consists of the base and the single class completion, with no reset;
no round-$Q$ invariant is ever introduced.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite execution of the colour-round induction]
Fix $d,a,C\in[0,\infty]$, $\Delta,n\in\mathbb N$, and put $Q=\Delta^2+1$.
Fix exposure sequences $p,\rho$ and round sequences
$\varepsilon,\omega,\theta,\zeta,\widehat\zeta$, all mapping $\mathbb N$
to $[0,\infty]$, and a certificate $\mathcal K$ of
\noderef{InductionApplicationCertificate} for
$(\Delta,Q,d,\theta,p,\varepsilon,\rho,\zeta,\omega,\widehat\zeta)$.
Assume
\[
 p_0=d,\qquad p_{x+1}=\rho_x(d/2)\ (x<\Delta),\qquad
 0<a\leq1,\quad C/n\leq1,\quad \Delta(1-a)^n\leq\tfrac12.
\]
For every round $s<Q$ assume all of the following inequalities:
\[
 \varepsilon_s\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}\leq1,\qquad
 2\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+\Delta\sqrt{\zeta_s}\leq\theta_s,\quad
 \zeta_s+2\Delta\zeta_s\leq\theta_s,
\]
\[
 0<\theta_s,\quad4\theta_s<\rho_x,\quad
 2\zeta_s<\rho_x,\quad2\zeta_s<1-\rho_x\qquad(x\leq\Delta),
\]
\[
 2\zeta_s<d/2,\quad2\zeta_s<1-d/2,\quad
 p_{x+1}+\varepsilon_s+1/n\leq p_x\ (x<\Delta),\quad
 \omega_{s+1}<\varepsilon_{s+1}.
\]
Writing the certificate fields as $N^{\rm wit}_{s,x},N^{\rm host}_s,
N^{\rm mat}_{s,x},N^{\rm exist}_{s,x},M_{s,x},
N^{\rm FG}_{s,x,y},a_{s,x,y}$, assume
\[
 N^{\rm wit}_{s,x},N^{\rm host}_s,N^{\rm mat}_{s,x},
 N^{\rm exist}_{s,x}\leq n,\quad M_{s,x}\leq C/2\qquad(x\leq\Delta),
\]
\[
 N^{\rm FG}_{s,x,y}\leq n,\quad a\leq a_{s,x,y}
 \qquad(x,y\leq\Delta).
\]
Finally assume, for every $s<Q$,
\[
 n^{-1}\leq\widehat\zeta_s<\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+2/n\leq\zeta_s,\quad
 \widehat\zeta_s+1/(\zeta_sn)\leq\zeta_s,
\]
\[
 \omega_{s+1}+2/n\leq\varepsilon_{s+1},\qquad
 \omega_{s+1}+1/(\varepsilon_{s+1}n)\leq\varepsilon_{s+1}.
\]
Then the following holds for every finite blow-up instance $B$ with
candidacy system $A$ and reduced graph on $[r]$. Suppose
$|X_j|=|V_j|\in\{n,n+1\}$ for every $j$, $\Delta(R)\leq\Delta$,
\noderef{InstanceSuperRegular} and \noderef{CandidacySuperRegular} hold
with $(\varepsilon_0,d)$, and \noderef{SaturatingSourcePair} holds on
every reduced edge. There are a colouring $c:[r]\to\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$
and a specified law $\mu$ on compatible partial embeddings with domain
all of $V_H$ such that
\[
 \mathcal I(Q-1,B_{Q-1};V_H,\mu),\qquad
 B_{Q-1}=\{j:c(j)=Q-1\},
\]
in the sense of \noderef{ColourRoundInvariant}, with
$(\varepsilon,p,\Delta,C,n)$. In particular the full-domain restricted
maps have the $(C/n)$-vertex-spread bound. The final round is $Q-1$,
not $Q$.
\end{lemma}

theorem VariableSizeInductionStep :
    ∀ {r q : ℕ} {VH VG : Type*} [Fintype VH] [Fintype VG]
      [DecidableEq VH] [DecidableEq VG]
      {H : SimpleGraph VH} {G : SimpleGraph VG} {R : SimpleGraph (Fin r)}

      (cert : InductionApplicationCertificate D q d
        theta density epsilon rho eta omega xi),

      epsilon round ≤ epsilon (round + 1) →
      epsilon (round + 1) ≤ 1 →
      (∀ j : Fin r, (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin r => R.Adj j k).card ≤ D) →
      (∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, i ≠ j →
        (R.Adj i j ∨ ∃ k : Fin r, R.Adj i k ∧ R.Adj k j) →
        colour i ≠ colour j) →
      (∀ j : Fin r,
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n ∨
         (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card = n + 1) ∧
        (Finset.univ.filter fun x : VH => B.sourceCluster x = j).card =
          (Finset.univ.filter fun v : VG => B.hostCluster v = j).card) →
      InstanceSuperRegular B (epsilon 0) d →
      (∀ ⦃i j : Fin r⦄, R.Adj i j → SaturatingSourcePair B i j) →

      eta round + D * (eta round) ^ (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ theta round →
      eta round + 2 * D * eta round ≤ theta round →

        2 * eta round < rho x ∧ 2 * eta round < 1 - rho x) →
      2 * eta round < d / 2 →
      2 * eta round < 1 - d / 2 →

        cert.hostThinningThreshold round ≤ n ∧

VariableSizeInductionStep.tex_proof:
\begin{proof}
Package the displayed certificate and numerical inequalities as the data
record of \noderef{ColourRoundStepParameters}; every field is one of the
hypotheses, with exactly the original sequences and the same certified round
bound \(q\). The signature and all parameter dependencies are unchanged.

Fix \(f\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)\). By
\noderef{ColourRoundUntouchedGeometry}, the current cluster and every
future neighbour tested at it have no neighbour in \(S\). Their stored
witnesses therefore have the common error \(\varepsilon_t\); the exposure
indices \(x_i,x_j\) remain independent, with \(x_i\le D\) and \(x_j<D\).
The latter lemma also gives the exact exposure increment and the at-most-one
touched-neighbour bound after adding \(i\).

Apply \noderef{ColourRoundMatchingPreparation} to this supported \(f\),
the original host super-regularity, the saturating source pairs, and the
numerical record. It uses the actual witness and host thinning guarantees,
the simultaneous retained-edge estimate, and the ordered Four-Graphs
guarantees, explicitly at \(t<q\) and the two separate exposure bounds.
The density upper bounds used there follow from
\(2\zeta_t<1-\rho_x\) and \(2\zeta_t<1-d/2\).
Its transport components are
\noderef{EqualSizeSourceWitnessTransport},
\noderef{CurrentExtraSourceWitnessTransport}, and
\noderef{FutureExtraSourceWitnessTransport}.
They keep the parts of sizes \(n\) or \(n+1\) and the codegree windows
normalised by the actual future part.
In the current-extra case the source map has only the residual domain:
the artificial row is inserted before testing and deleted after Four
Graphs. In the future-extra case the unmatched future row is deleted
before testing; the output is transported to the exact residual source
part, and a subset of the genuine unchanged old row is restored.
Each transport uses both exact-image equivalences and proves containment
in the true updated candidacy graph, not equality with that graph.

The preparation supplies a local raw law \(\nu_0\), an event \(E\) with
probability at least one half and a supported member, and the conditioned
law \(\nu_f=\nu_0(\,\cdot\mid E)\).
Its restriction to the new cluster is \(C/n\)-vertex-spread, and every
supported local embedding has the required contained witness for each
future neighbour, for every compatible lift agreeing with \(f\) on the
old domain. The conditioning concerns this one current-cluster matching
only, not a global event for the colour class.

These are precisely the pointwise input hypotheses of
\noderef{ColourRoundKernelAssembly}. That lemma lifts through
\noderef{ExtendUpdatedPartialEmbedding}, uses a supported input's law
as filler outside the old support to produce a total kernel, and checks
all the invariant clauses. Non-neighbours keep their old true candidacy
sets and witnesses by \noderef{UpdatedCandidacyNonneighborExtension};
the touched and untouched errors are preserved separately.
The conclusion of \noderef{ColourRoundKernelAssembly} includes the
full joint spread clause for the very law
\(\mu\mathbin{\mathrm{bind}}\kappa\), as part of its asserted
colour-round invariant.
Thus the kernel has both asserted support properties and its exact bind
law satisfies the new colour-round invariant, as required.
\end{proof}
